items.headline: Mamukelashvili contributed 11 points (4-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound and one assist over 24 minutes during Sunday's 131-125 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Mamukelashvili provided an offensive spark off the bench, reaching double figures while connecting on two shots from beyond the arc. His ability to stretch the floor gives him a role in Los Angeles' second unit, but his limited rebounding and secondary production restrict his fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili closed Wednesday's 103-87 victory over the Clippers with 13 points (6-15 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals over 30 minutes off the bench.
items.story: With Luka Doncic (back) and Ziaire Williams (foot) in street clothes, Mamukelashvili saw his biggest workload of the season and delivered solid numbers. The eight boards were a season high, and through five games (all off the bench), the journeyman big is averaging 10.2 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.0 threes and 1.4 combined steals and blocks in 24.2 minutes, shooting 51.4 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili recorded 17 points (6-9 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one block over 24 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Mamukelashvili provided an early spark off the bench, scoring 13 points in the first half, capped by a buzzer-beating three. The big man finished as the Lakers' third-leading scorer, and his ability to stretch the floor gives Los Angeles a different look behind Walker Kessler. If Mamukelashvili keeps shooting like this, he could push for more minutes in the frontcourt rotation.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili chipped in nine points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds and one block over 21 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Mamukelashvili is averaging 7.0 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 22.3 minutes per game as the backup to Ziaire Williams and Walker Kessler in the frontcourt. Mamukelashvili will continue to provide solid contributions in three-pointers and rebounds for the revamped Lakers, but his upside is limited as a reserve.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili registered 15 points (5-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block across 21 minutes in Friday's 121-106 preseason loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Mamukelashvili delivered one of Los Angeles' most productive performances, leading the team in rebounds and finishing just two boards shy of a double-double while tying Luka Doncic for third in scoring. The versatile big man caught fire from beyond the arc during the second half, knocking down consecutive three-pointers in the third quarter before adding another early in the fourth. Mamukelashvili's ability to stretch the floor and contribute across multiple categories could help him compete for a consistent role in the Lakers' frontcourt rotation, and he seems set to earn regular playing time during the season, either as one of Walker Kessler's backups or alongside him at power forward.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili posted 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt), seven rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 101-89 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Mamukelashvili led the Lakers' bench in minutes and was active on the perimeter, making two of his three-point attempts. He's become one of the most reliable pieces of Los Angeles' rotation as the season opener approaches.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili tallied 19 points (7-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block across 21 minutes in Thursday's 114-110 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Mamukelashvili gave the Lakers a lift off the bench, scoring 11 points in the first half and hitting two late threes in the third quarter to restore a double-digit lead. While he's pushing for one of the open starting spots alongside Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler, Mamukelashvili will likely run with the second unit once the season gets underway.

items.headline: Mamukelsahvili isn't starting Thursday's preseason game against the Kings, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Mamukelashvili drew the start in Tuesday's exhibition against Golden State, and he made the most of his opportunity by finishing with 15 points in 18 minutes. However, the big man will head back to a bench role Thursday as Kevon Looney gets a chance to start at center.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili produced 15 points (6-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one block over 18 minutes in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Luka Doncic (rest) and Austin Reaves (ankle) were inactive for Tuesday's exhibition, so Mamukelashvili got all the shots he wanted on offense. It'll be interesting to see how he fits in the rotation in Los Angeles, but if he's able to secure a 25-plus-minute role, he could have some value as a three-point specialist.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili will start in Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Lakers have seven players inactive for Tuesday's exhibition, so Mamukelashvili could see reasonable minutes. Joining him in the first unit will be Bronny James, Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia and Adou Thiero.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili finished with eight points (3-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt), five assists, one rebound and two steals in 19 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason win over Sacramento.
items.story: Mamukelashvili showed off his versatility in his Lakers debut, with his five assists ranking second on the team. The 27-year-old is coming off a career-best 2025-26 regular season with Toronto and should have a consistent role in Los Angeles' frontcourt after signing a four-year deal during the offseason.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili is among the options for the Lakers' final starting spot, though Jovan Buha of Buha's Block has reservations about his defensive fit.
items.story: Buha questioned whether a lineup featuring Luka Doncic, Mamukelashvili and Walker Kessler would have sufficient quickness and athleticism defensively. Mamukelashvili should nevertheless get an opportunity to compete for the job during camp and the preseason, though Jake LaRavia and Ziaire Williams appear to be the more likely candidates entering the competition.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili registered 22 points (6-18 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 7-7 FT), six rebounds, four assists and two steals in 37 minutes during Georgia's 98-90 win over Portugal in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Mamukelashvili tied for the team lead in boards Monday. The Lakers have a massive void to fill in their starting lineup following the departure of LeBron James, but Mamukelashvili may have to settle for a reserve role behind Jake LaRavia to begin the year. Mamukelashvili averaged a career-high 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game during the 2025-26 regular season for Toronto.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili recorded 17 points (6-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals in 36 minutes during Georgia's 101-74 win over Montenegro in Friday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Mamukelashvili delivered an impressive all-around performance without committing a turnover, continuing a productive offseason ahead of his first campaign with the Lakers. The 27-year-old is coming off the best season of his career, averaging 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists during the regular season for Toronto before signing with Los Angeles in July. Walker Kessler is projected to handle most of the minutes at center, but Mamukelashvili's shooting and playmaking offer a different skill set and could earn him minutes at both frontcourt spots.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili signed a four-year, $52 million deal with the Lakers on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Lakers make another huge splash after just acquiring Walker Kessler. Mamukelashvili likely had a considerable market after a career-best season in Toronto. Across 80 regular-season games, Mamukelashvili averaged 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists in 21.9 minutes per game. In Los Angeles, he's poised for a consistent role in a frontcourt that lost LeBron James and Rui Hachimura this offseason.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili declined his $2.8 million player option for 2026-27, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: This was a widely expected transaction, with Mamukelashvili putting together a career season in 2025-26. Across 80 regular-season contests, he produced averages of 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists on 52.3 percent shooting from the field. He's expected to have a strong market heading into free agency.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili closed Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with six points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT) in nine minutes.
items.story: While his minutes began to dip during the playoffs, Mamukelashvili was a pretty big part of Toronto's rotation earlier this year. Over 80 regular-season appearances (13 starts), the fifth-year big man averaged 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists in 21.9 minutes per game. Mamukelashvili has a player option for 2026-27, and it remains to be seen if he'll settle for that or opt to explore free agency.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili chipped in 12 points (5-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and one steal over 21 minutes during Monday's 115-105 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: With Jakob Poeltl being ineffective once again, the Raptors leaned heavily on Mamukelashvili and Collin Murray-Boyles off the bench. With the team starting a 2-0 deficit, lineup/rotation changes could be on the table for Toronto.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili ended with three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), eight rebounds, two assists and one steal in 20 minutes during Saturday's 126-113 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Mamukelashvili was quiet on the scoring end in this contest, although he at least made up for it by falling just two rebounds shy of the double-digit mark. With Jakob Poeltl likely to remain at about 20 minutes of playing time in Game 2 on Monday, Mamukelashvili should continue to see a solid role on the second unit.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili chipped in 17 points (5-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one steal in 25 minutes during Friday's 112-95 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Mamukelashvili operated as the Raptors' top big man off the bench behind starting center Jakob Poeltl due to the absence of Collin Murray-Boyles (neck). Mamukelashvili took advantage of the expanded role and ended up finishing as the Raptors' leading scorer. He will likely see a decrease in minutes in Sunday's regular-season finale against the Nets, assuming Murray-Boyles is cleared to return.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili (knee) has been upgraded to available for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Mamukelashvili is good to go Tuesday, which effectively puts the Raptors at full strength. The big man is worth streaming in most fantasy leagues, as Mamukelashvili has averaged 14.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 2.3 three-pointers in 22.6 minutes per contest over his last seven games.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili (knee) has been upgraded to probable for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Mamukelashvili was initially listed as questionable for Tuesday's game, but now it appears likely that he'll be active. Check back for official confirmation on his status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili (knee) is listed as questionable for Tuesday's game against Miami.
items.story: Mamukelashvili is in danger of missing his first game since Jan. 14 due to left knee soreness. With Collin Murray-Boyles (quadriceps) also questionable, the Raptors could be thin in the frontcourt, which would open the door for guys like Trayce Jackson-Davis, Jonathan Mogbo and Jamison Battle to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili finished Sunday's 139-87 win over the Magic with 19 points (8-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds and three steals in 21 minutes.
items.story: Although he saw slightly fewer minutes than Jakob Poeltl, Mamukelashvili was the third-leading scorer in this contest for Toronto and made the most of his action. He's been excellent over his last seven games, posting averages of 14.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.9 three-pointers in 20.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Mamukelashvili made a spot start last time out, but now that Jakob Poeltl (back) is available, Mamukelashvili will come off the bench. The 26-year-old is averaging 9.7 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.6 assists across 19.9 minutes per game as a reserve this season.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili logged 23 points (9-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, two assists, one block and five steals over 32 minutes during Monday's 143-127 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Getting the start in place of Jakob Poeltl (back), Mamukelashvili produced his best scoring effort since Dec. 20, when he dropped 24 points on the Celtics. The journeyman center is on his third NBA team in five seasons, but he's found a fairly steady role in the Raptors' frontcourt, playing 20-plus minutes in five of the last 10 games while averaging 10.6 points, 4.4 boards, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.2 threes in 21.0 minutes a contest.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against Utah, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With Jakob Poeltl (back) inactive, Mamukelashvili will step into the starting lineup at center. In 12 starts this season, the big man is averaging 15.3 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 30.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili chipped in four points (1-1 FG, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 14 minutes during Friday's 121-115 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Mamukelashvili continues to struggle, scoring in single digits for the fifth time in the past six games. Outside of a 17-point performance in a win over the Bulls, it's been rough going for Mamukelshvili, a far cry from what he was delivering earlier in the season. In 14 appearances over the past month, he has been outside the top 200, averaging 8.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers in 18.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Mamukelashvili made a spot start in Toronto's most recent game, but he'll move aside now that Jakob Poeltl (illness) is healthy. Mamukelashvili is averaging 9.8 points and 4.5 rebounds per game this season as a reserve.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili supplied eight points (3-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and two steals over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 113-99 loss to Houston.
items.story: With Jakob Poeltl sidelined due to illness, Mamukelashvili was inserted into the starting lineup. While the 30 minutes were encouraging, his production was largely underwhelming. For those who picked him up, he is worth holding with the Raptors on the first night of a back-to-back. However, beyond that, he is likely nothing more than a stream-level player.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili will start Tuesday's game against the Rockets, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With Jakob Poeltl (illness) and Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) unavailable, Mamukelashvili will enter the starting five for the first time since Jan. 25. As a starter this season (11 games), the big man has averaged 16.0 points, 6.6 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 30.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili closed with 11 points (5-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 24 minutes during Thursday's 115-107 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Although Jakob Poeltl started yet again, Mamukelashvili saw plenty of minutes off the bench at both frontcourt slots. Collin Murray-Boyles has been sidelined by a thumb sprain, and that has allowed Mamukelashvili to play an expanded role in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili provided seven points (3-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and one steal over 16 minutes during Saturday's 134-125 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Mamukelashvili was limited again, despite the fact that Collin Murray-Boyles was sidelined with an ongoing thumb issue. While it has been mostly a productive season for Mamukelashvili, it appears as though his time as a standard league asset may have come to an end. He should at least remain on the radar, but as we approach the pointy end of the season, his nightly production just isn't cutting it.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili notched two points (1-2 FG) and three rebounds over 14 minutes during Wednesday's 110-107 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Mamukelashvili scored no more than eight points for the fourth time in the past five games, continuing to serve as the third-string center. While his recent production has been far from ideal, managers may want to hit pause before cutting bait. Collin Murray-Boyles was forced from Wednesday's game due to an ongoing thumb issue, which could result in Mamukelashvili getting a bump, at least in the short term.

items.headline: Mamukelashvili ended with seven points (3-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds and one block in 16 minutes during Thursday's 110-101 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Mamukelshvili has been a welcome surprise for fantasy managers this season, flirting with top 100 value for much of the past three months. However, with Collin Murray-Boyles and Jakob Poeltl now seemingly healthy, it appears as though Mamukelashvili could be on the outside looking in when it comes to meaningful playing time. He remains a soft hold for now, although if his minutes continue to dip, managers should have no hesitation in moving on from him.

items.headline: Bona won't start Monday's game against the Bulls, Keith Pompey of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: With Joel Embiid (foot) back in the lineup, Bona will slide to the second unit. In six appearances off the bench this season, the big man has averaged 1.5 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 12.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bona will start in Saturday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: With Joel Embiid (foot) sidelined for the second game of a back-to-back, Bona will enter the starting lineup. The 23-year-old started 18 times during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 6.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.0 blocks over 21.4 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: Bona recorded one point (0-1 FG, 1-2 FT), one rebound and one block over four minutes during Wednesday's 114-109 win over the Pacers.
items.story: Coming off his best performance of the season, Bona barely touched the floor Wednesday, logging just four minutes. With Joel Embiid back in the rotation, Bona's role basically evaporated. Outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons on Sunday, Bona has averaged just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances. He should only be viewed as a potential streaming candidate, if and when Embiid is missing.

items.headline: Bona supplied six points (3-5 FG), 13 rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal across 25 minutes during Sunday's 106-93 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Bona made a significant impact on the defensive end, pairing a game-high 13 rebounds with three blocks while collecting five offensive boards. The 23-year-old benefited from Joel Embiid's absence and Philadelphia's depleted frontcourt, making a strong case for additional playing time. Bona offers intriguing short-term fantasy value for managers seeking rebounds and blocks, though his opportunities could diminish once Embiid returns.

items.headline: Bona produced three rebounds, one assist and one block across 10 minutes during Tuesday's 106-100 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: Bona was available after dealing with a left foot sprain during the preseason, but his role was minimal behind Joel Embiid, who logged 33 minutes. The reserve center made his presence felt defensively with a block, though he didn't receive any offensive opportunities. Bona's fantasy value remains heavily dependent on additional playing time, particularly when Embiid is unavailable.

items.headline: Bona (foot) is available for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Across 71 regular-season games (18 starts) in 2025-26, Bona averaged 4.8 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.2 blocks, providing solid rim protection and defense behind Joel Embiid and the departed Andre Drummond. With Drummond now in New York and Ariel Hukporti (Achilles) already out for the season, Bona is primed to earn the backup center spot and has the opportunity to see a career high in minutes in 2026-27, especially when considering Embiid's health concerns over the last several years.

items.headline: Bona (foot) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Bona missed the preseason due to the foot issue, but he was able to get in a full practice Sunday, so he appears to be trending in the right direction. If Bona is cleared for Tuesday's season opener, he'll play limited minutes behind Joel Embiid.

items.headline: Bona (foot) was a full participant in Sunday's practice, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: Bona didn't suit up in the preseason due to a foot injury, though this update bodes well for his status ahead of Tuesday's regular-season opener versus the Knicks. The big man will likely have a chance to carve out a meaningful role behind Joel Embiid to begin the season, especially if Dominick Barlow (back) misses time.

items.headline: Bona (foot) remains out for Friday's preseason finale against the Celtics, but he's getting closer to a return, Kyle Neubeck of AllPHLY.com reports.
items.story: Bona has yet to appear in the preseason and will now miss the final exhibition. He did go through practice Thursday, however, giving him a chance to suit up for Opening Night as the backup center.

items.headline: Bona (foot) practiced in a limited fashion Monday, per Ky Carlin of USA Today.
items.story: Bona is already expected to miss Friday's preseason finale against Boston, but he's still aiming to be ready for the start of the regular season. Once healthy, Bona is in line to serve as the No. 2 center behind Joel Embiid.

items.headline: Bona (left foot) isn't expected to play in either of Philadelphia's next two preseason games against Brooklyn and Boston, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Bona has yet to practice during training camp while recovering from the foot injury he suffered during FIBA competition. With Ariel Hukporti (Achilles) out indefinitely, Philadelphia will be particularly thin at center until Bona is cleared to return.

items.headline: Bona (foot) will not play in Monday's preseason opener against New York, Chris Hine of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: Bona has been sidelined by a foot sprain suffered during FIBA competition and has yet to practice during training camp. Coach Nick Nurse recently expressed optimism that Bona could return for a couple of Philadelphia's preseason contests, making his status worth monitoring over the coming days.

items.headline: 76ers coach Nick Nurse said Bona (foot) will be re-evaluated in a couple days, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Bona has been recovering from a foot sprain he suffered during the offseason. According to Nurse, there's a chance Bona could be back for a portion of the preseason. He is currently penciled in as Joel Embiid's backup for the upcoming season.

items.headline: Bona (foot) will be re-evaluated at the start of training camp, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports.
items.story: Bona suffered a foot sprain this offseason, clouding his ability to participate in camp later this month. It's unclear if his status for Opening Night is in serious doubt, as he does have about a month until the regular season begins. Until Bona is cleared to retake the floor, Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti should handle the backup center reps.

items.headline: Bona recorded eight points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-6 FT), 10 rebounds and three blocks in 18 minutes during Turkey's 110-73 win over Iceland in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 23-year-old averaged 4.8 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 17.4 minutes across 71 regular-season appearances for Philadelphia in 2025-26. Bona remains on the 76ers' roster entering 2026-27, but the presence of Joel Embiid and offseason addition Ariel Hukporti could make consistent playing time difficult to come by.

items.headline: Bona supplied seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), two rebounds and one block across 10 minutes during Sunday's 144-114 loss to New York in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: With Joel Embiid having his workload managed throughout the year, Bona wound up making a career-high 18 starts during the regular season while averaging 4.8 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 17.4 minutes per contest over 71 games. Andre Drummond is an unrestricted free agent this offseason, so Bona could take another step forward in 2026-27 as the top backup center behind Embiid.

items.headline: Bona finished with two points (2-4 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 16 minutes in Wednesday's 108-102 loss to New York in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Joel Embiid (hip, ankle) didn't suit up for this contest, so Bona saw more action after logging just four minutes in Game 1. While the 23-year-old came off the bench behind Andre Drummond and generated only two points, he still made a difference on the glass, collecting six offensive boards, as well as on the defensive end. With the Knicks now up 2-0 in the series, both clubs will head to Philadelphia for Game 3 on Friday night. If Embiid plays, Bona likely won't be on the floor much. However, if Embiid misses another game, Bona should remain involved, potentially re-entering the starting lineup.

items.headline: Bona will come off the bench during Sunday's Game 4 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Celtics, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Bona will come off the bench due to Joel Embiid (abdomen) returning to the lineup. Bona has posted averages of 4.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 19.3 minutes per contest across three games in the postseason thus far, but he will likely see a smaller role in Embiid's return.

items.headline: Bona notched zero points (0-4 FG), three rebounds and one block over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 victory over the Celtics in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Bona started for the sixth straight game, although he continues to offer very little on either end of the floor. During that six-game stretch, Bona has averaged just 2.3 points, 3.2 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 17.3 minutes per game. While there is a chance we will see Joel Embiid (abdomen) before the series is done, Bona may need to have to have more of an impact moving forward.

items.headline: Bona produced two points (0-1 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and three blocks over 16 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 Play-In Game victory over the Magic.
items.story: Bona remained in the starting lineup, filling in for Joel Embiid (appendicitis), who remains sidelined indefinitely. Despite blocking three shots, Bona served mainly as the backup behind Andre Drummond, who himself had a fantastic night. Should Embiid be forced to miss Sunday's game against Boston, expect Bona to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Bona will start Thursday's game against Houston.
items.story: Joel Embiid (illness) is out, so Bona will re-enter the starting lineup versus the Rockets. In 15 starts this season, the 23-year-old has averaged 6.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, 0.7 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.0 steals across 22.3 minutes.

items.headline: Bona (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the 76ers' 115-102 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: For the first time since Jan. 9, Bona was left out of the Philadelphia rotation, with head coach Nick Nurse turning to Andre Drummond to handle the backup minutes at center behind starter Joel Embiid. The 76ers won't necessarily prioritize Drummond over Bona moving forward, but neither player will be in line for extensive playing time whenever Embiid is available. Philadelphia will head into its final back-to-back set of the season Thursday and Friday versus the Rockets and Pacers, respectively, so with Embiid likely to rest for one of those games, Bona should resurface in the rotation in short order.

items.headline: Bona won't start Friday's game against Minnesota, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports.
items.story: Bona got the spot start in Wednesday's win over the Wizards, though he'll retreat to the bench with Joel Embiid (illness) back in the lineup. Bona has averaged 3.8 points and 4.2 rebounds across 14.6 minutes per game over his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Bona will start in Wednesday's game against Washington.
items.story: With Joel Embiid (illness) ruled out, Bona will draw the start. In 14 starts during the campaign, the 23-year-old has averaged 6.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, 0.7 assists, 1.2 blocks and 0.9 steals while shooting 52.2 percent from the field in 22.4 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Bona will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against the Bulls, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Joel Embiid (oblique) is back and starting, so Bona will retreat to the second unit. As a reserve this season, Bona owns averages of 4.4 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game.

items.headline: Bona provided eight points (2-3 FG, 4-4 FT), 10 rebounds and two steals in 20 minutes during Thursday's 139-118 win over the Kings.
items.story: Bona should continue to start at center and provide lower-end fantasy value until Joel Embiid (oblique) is finally cleared to return. Bona has averaged 6.6 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.1 blocks and 0.8 steals in 22.6 minutes per tilt in his last eight games (all starts), shooting 51.2 percent from the floor during this period.

items.headline: Bona (back) is available for Sunday's game against the Trail Blazers, Noah Levick of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.story: Bona carried a questionable tag into Sunday's contest due to a back injury, but he will be able to play through it. Bona has started each of the last five games, averaging 7.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 blocks in 26.6 minutes per contest over that stretch.

items.headline: Bona (back) is questionable for Sunday's game versus the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Bona could get hit with a maintenance day on the second leg of a back-to-back set, and with Andre Drummond (back) also questionable, the 76ers could be very thin up front Sunday. Check back for official word on Bona's status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Bona amassed nine points (2-5 FG, 5-5 FT), 10 rebounds, three blocks and one steal across 33 minutes during Saturday's 104-97 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Bona was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a back injury and drew the start at center with Joel Embiid (oblique) and Andre Drummond (back) both sidelined. Bona was energetic on the defensive end of the floor and posted his ninth game of the season with at least three blocks. He has started each of the Sixers' last five games, and over that span he has averaged 7.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 blocks over 26.5 minutes per game. Bona should remain in the Sixers' starting five for as long as Drummond and Embiid are sidelined.

items.headline: Bona (back) will play Saturday against the Nets, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: With Andre Drummond (back) and Joel Embiid (oblique) out, Bona will start at center and should play heavy minutes. As a starter this season (eight games), Bona has averaged 5.9 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.7 stocks in 22.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Bona (back) is questionable for Saturday's game versus the Nets.
items.story: Bona sat out Thursday's loss to the Pistons due to a back issue, and with Saturday's game being the first of a back-to-back set, he could be headed for his second straight absence. Check back for official word on Bona's status closer to Saturday's tipoff.

items.headline: Bona, who has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Detroit, is being considered day-to-day after scans on his back came back clean, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: Bona was sent for imaging after experiencing back soreness, but the results shows that he's managed to avoid a serious injury. The Sixers will presumably re-evaluate the big man again Friday to get a better idea of his availability for Saturday's clash against the Nets.

items.headline: Bona (back) is out for Thursday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Bona was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest and will join Joel Embiid (oblique) on the shelf. Andre Drummond (back) is questionable, so the 76ers may need guys like Dominick Barlow and Trendon Watford to step up.

items.headline: Bona is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against Detroit due to back soreness.
items.story: Bona is at risk of missing his first game since Jan. 9 as he tends to a back issue. If Bona were to sit Thursday, Andre Drummond would assume starting center duties, while Dominick Barlow and Trendon Watford could see some action at the five spot.

items.headline: Bona finished Monday's 115-101 loss to the Cavaliers with eight points (4-10 FG) and seven rebounds over 26 minutes.
items.story: Despite starting for the third straight game, Bona continues to offer very little in terms of tangible production. In his three recent starts, he has averaged just 8.0 points, 5.7 rebounds and 0.7 blocks, well below what fantasy managers would have expected. While the numbers are far from exciting, he remains a viable streaming option, given the favorable schedule and the fact that Joel Embiid could miss the entire week due to an ongoing oblique injury.

items.headline: Bona will start Wednesday's game against the Jazz, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Andre Drummond started Philadelphia's last two games due to Joel Embiid (oblique) being sidelined, though Bona will get the starting nod at center Wednesday. As a starter this season (four games), the second-year big man has averaged 4.8 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.3 combined steals-plus-blocks in 20.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Bona closed Tuesday's 131-91 loss to San Antonio with six points (2-3 FG, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and two assists over 22 minutes.
items.story: Bona continues to do very little with his time on the court, failing to take advantage of the fact that Joel Embiid is currently dealing with an oblique injury. In seven appearances over the past two weeks, Bona has put up just 6.0 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.1 blocks, logging 18.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Bona finished Saturday's 126-111 loss to the Pelicans with four points (1-2 FG, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist and one block across 21 minutes.
items.story: Bona grabbed double-digit rebounds for just the second time this season, continuing to serve as the backup center, despite the fact that Joel Embiid is currently sidelined due to ongoing knee issues. Andre Drummond appears to have the front-running for the starting spot until Embiid is cleared to return. With that said, Bona still has some limited fantasy value for anyone seeking rebounds and blocks.

items.headline: Bona is not in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Hawks, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: The 76ers are instead rolling with Andre Drummond in the absence of Joel Embiid (shin/knee) on Thursday. Bona has averaged 4.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.1 blocks in 14.2 minutes per tilt in his last eight games off the bench.

items.headline: Wade won't start Monday's game against Chicago, Keith Pompey of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: LeBron James (back) is back in the starting five, pushing Wade to the second unit. Over five regular-season appearances (four starts), Wade's averaging 3.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 2.0 steals in 27.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Wade finished Friday's 98-93 win over New York with two rebounds, one assist and three steals in 27 minutes.
items.story: Wade was moved into the 76ers' starting lineup Friday due to the absence of Jaylen Brown (knee), but the former barely showed up on the box score and didn't attempt a shot. Wade has taken only one shot over his last two games, and his lack of shooting gives him little fantasy value even in the deepest of leagues. He would likely revert to a bench role if Brown is cleared to play against the Hornets on Saturday.

items.headline: Wade will start Friday's game against the Knicks, Noah Levick of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.story: With Jaylen Brown (knee) sidelined, Wade will get the starting nod for the third time in Philadelphia's last four games. In two starts this season, Wade has averaged 7.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 steals and 1.0 blocks in 32.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Wade will come off the bench in Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Wade started the past two games with Joel Embiid and LeBron James alternating rest days on a back-to-back set, but with those two back in action Wednesday evening, Wade will return to a reserve role. Wade averaged 32.6 minutes as a starter, but he'll likely be working with minutes in the 20s as a member of the second unit.

items.headline: Wade contributed seven points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals in 37 minutes during Sunday's 106-93 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Wade drew the start and logged substantial playing time with Philadelphia's frontcourt shorthanded, though he attempted just four shots. His defensive contributions helped offset the limited scoring, but his low offensive usage makes him difficult to trust outside deeper fantasy formats. Wade could continue seeing significant minutes while the Sixers deal with injuries up front.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is available and starting Saturday's game against the Bucks, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Wade will return from a two-game absence due to a sprained ankle and enter the starting lineup in LeBron James' (back) stead. Wade will be joined in the first unit by Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid in the front end of this back-to-back set.

items.headline: Wade is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Bucks due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: Wade is in jeopardy of missing a third straight game to begin the regular season. If the veteran forward is unable to suit up, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker would be candidates to see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is out for Thursday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: After sitting out Philadelphia's 106-100 victory over the Knicks on Opening Night, Wade will have to watch from the sidelines once again. In his absence, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker could see a slight uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) participated in Thursday's morning shootaround, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Wade remains day-to-day with his ankle sprain after missing the season opener. The 76ers have listed him as questionable, but his availability Thursday morning bodes well for his chances.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is questionable for Thursday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Wade is aiming to make his 76ers debut Thursday. His eventual return from an ankle sprain could slightly cut into Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's minutes on the wing.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is out for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: The former Cavalier, who signed with the 76ers in the offseason following seven seasons in Cleveland, will have to wait at least one more game to make his debut with Philadelphia. Wade averaged 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.2 three-pointers made on 36.2 percent shooting in 2025-26 across 59 regular-season appearances (38 starts). With him on the shelf for the 2026-27 Opening Night, expect Justin Edwards, Rayan Rupert and Jabari Walker to see their roles increased slightly.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday's season opener versus the Knicks, per Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com.
items.story: With back-to-back missed practices, Wade appears to be on the wrong side of the questionable tag. Justin Edwards and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope would have a chance to enter the streaming mix in deep leagues if Wade is out.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) did not practice Monday, according to 76ers reporter Paul Hudrick.
items.story: Wade has been sidelined since picking up the injury in Friday's preseason finale. He was limited to individual work Monday and appears to be questionable at best for Opening Night against the Knicks.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) didn't participate in Sunday's practice, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Wade didn't return to Friday's preseason finale after injuring his ankle in the first half, and his status for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Knicks is up in the air. If the 29-year-old forward is forced to miss time, Justin Edwards and Jabari Walker could see increased burn.

items.headline: Wade suffered an ankle injury in the first half of Friday's 125-120 preseason loss to the Celtics and did not return, per Kyle Neubeck of AllPHLY.com. He had zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two assists and one steal over 13 minutes.
items.story: Head coach Nick Nurse wasn't overly concerned but chose to keep Wade off the floor for the remainder of the contest. The 29-year-old, who signed with the 76ers in the offseason, can be considered questionable ahead of the team's Opening Night meeting with the Knicks. If Wade can't suit up Tuesday, Justin Edwards, Jabari Walker and Dominick Barlow (back) would be candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Wade will come off the bench in Friday's preseason finale against the Celtics, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Wade started for the resting LeBron James in Saturday's preseason loss to Boston, but James is active and starting for Friday's preseason finale. Wade could make sense as a three-point streamer this season on occasions James receives a maintenance day, but it'll be tough for him to impact fantasy leagues while the 76ers are at full strength.

items.headline: Wade is in the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Wade will get the start Saturday since the 76ers are resting players such as Jaylen Brown and LeBron James. Wade started in 38 of his 59 regular-season appearances with the Cavaliers in 2025-26, but he'll likely be a bench player when Philadelphia is healthy in 2026-27.

items.headline: Wade isn't in the starting lineup for Thursday's preseason game against the Nets.
items.story: Wade drew the start in the preseason opener with the Sixers electing to rest several key contributors. However, he'll retreat to the bench Thursday with LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey all back in action.

items.headline: Wade will start Monday's preseason game against the Knicks.
items.story: LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey are all sitting out the preseason opener for rest purposes, opening the door for Wade to enter the first unit. He'll be joined in the starting five by Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Ariel Hukporti.

items.headline: Wade said recently he wants to play hard, bring energy and make a difference on the defensive side of the ball for the 76ers in the 2026-27 campaign, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: "My focus during the year will be playing hard and making a difference one-on-one defensively," Wade said. "My stats may not wow a lot of people, but my energy and impact in the game will." After going undrafted in 2019 and spending the first seven years of his career with Cleveland, Wade agreed to a four-year, $38.7 million pact with Philadelphia on June 30. The club traded for Jaylen Brown the next day and signed LeBron James in late July, so Wade figures to operate off the bench behind the star forwards. The 29-year-old is known for taking on challenging defensive assignments and is a career 36.7 percent shooter from three-point range. He'll likely carve out a meaningful role for the 76ers given his versatility on the defensive end, though he shouldn't be expected to stuff the stat sheet. Over 59 regular-season appearances (38 starts) with the Cavaliers in 2025-26, he averaged 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.2 triples, 0.7 steals and 0.4 blocks in 22.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Wade agreed to a four-year, $39 million contract with the 76ers on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Wade spent the first seven years of his career in Cleveland, most recently averaging 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 0.4 blocks and 0.7 steals while shooting 36.2 percent from deep across 22.3 minutes in 59 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. Although the 29-year-old forward hasn't been a steady contributor throughout his career, he'll still provide valuable depth for the Sixers, considering he's capable of contributing on both ends of the floor while being used interchangeably as a starter or reserve.

items.headline: Wade closed with zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound, one assist, one block and two steals in 12 minutes during Monday's 130-93 loss to New York in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Finals.
items.story: The Cavaliers were blown out of this contest, resulting in a lower workload for Wade. The forward appeared in 59 regular-season contests for the Cavaliers, posting averages of 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 three-pointers in 22.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wade won't start Monday's Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Knicks.
items.story: Max Strus will get the starting nod in Monday's do-or-die matchup, pushing Wade to the second unit for the fourth time this postseason. Over three playoff appearances off the bench, the 29-year-old forward has averaged 7.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, 0.7 assists and 0.7 steals across 23.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wade provided three points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt), three rebounds and three assists over 21 minutes during Thursday's 109-93 loss to the Knicks in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Finals.
items.story: Despite continuing to start, Wade has been mostly a non-factor on both ends of the floor, a trend that continued Thursday. Through 16 playoff appearances, Wade has scored double digits only twice, with both of those being 10-point performances. He has also recorded just 10 steals, four of which came in the opening two games against Toronto.

items.headline: Wade will start Tuesday's Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Knicks.
items.story: Max Strus got the starting nod over Wade in Sunday's Game 7 win over Detroit in the Eastern Conference Semifinals, though the latter will return to the starting five Tuesday. Wade has averaged 4.7 points and 4.2 rebounds across 23.4 minutes per game over 14 postseason appearances (11 starts) in 2026.

items.headline: Wade won't start Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Pistons.
items.story: Max Strus will get the starting nod in Sunday's do-or-die matchup, pushing Wade to the second unit. The 29-year-old forward has averaged 3.2 points and 3.8 rebounds in 22.7 minutes per contest across six second-round appearances.

items.headline: Wade had three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and three rebounds across 22 minutes during Friday's 115-94 loss to Detroit in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Wade's three-pointer in the second quarter was the only shot he made in Friday's loss, and his minus-16 point differential was the third-worst mark on the Cavaliers behind Donovan Mitchell (minus-25) and Evan Mobley (minus-24). Wade averaged just 5.8 points per game during the regular season, but that number has dropped to 4.7 points per game in the playoffs, and he has tallied only six points over the Cavaliers' last four playoff games. The winner of Sunday's Game 7 will advance to the Eastern Conference Finals to face the Knicks.

items.headline: Wade will start Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Raptors.
items.story: After coming off the bench in each of the last two games, Wade will get the starting nod over Max Strus in Sunday's do-or-die matchup. Over four starts in the series, Wade has averaged 5.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 25.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wade will come off the bench for Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Raptors, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: With the Cavaliers dropping two straight games in this series, the team will shift Max Strus into the first unit. Wade is averaging 5.0 points and 4.5 rebounds in 25.3 minutes through four postseason games.

items.headline: Wade closed Sunday's 93-89 loss to the Raptors in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with seven points (3-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and five rebounds over 28 minutes.
items.story: Despite a considerable workload, Wade wasn't able to make a huge impact on the stat sheet. Through four postseason games, he's averaging 5.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 25.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's Game 1 against the Raptors.
items.story: Wade was one of several key contributors who sat out Cleveland's regular-season finale, but he's set to return for the start of the playoffs. He averaged 5.7 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 21.0 minutes per tilt over his final 10 regular-season appearances (all starts).

items.headline: Wade (ankle) won't play Sunday against the Wizards.
items.story: The Cavs will sit out their entire starting lineup for Sunday's regular-season finale, so guys like Max Strus, Jaylon Tyson and Craig Porter could see massive upticks in usage. This is just a maintenance day for Wade, so he should get cleared when the playoffs begin.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) produced eight points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 21 minutes during Wednesday's 122-116 win over the Hawks.
items.story: Wade took back his spot in the starting five Wednesday after he had missed the Cavaliers' previous seven games due to a sprained ankle. He took on a relatively standard minutes load in his return, so his playing time shouldn't be expected to dramatically increase over Cleveland's final two contests of the regular season. Through 58 appearances, Wade is averaging 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 three-pointers in 22.4 minutes.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is available and starting in Wednesday's game against Atlanta, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: Wade will suit up after missing the Cavaliers' last seven games because of an ankle injury. He will also start over Max Strus. In 36 starts this season, Wade has averaged 6.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.8 steals across 23.0 minutes.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: The questionable tag is an upgrade to Wade's status and gives him a chance to end a seven-game absence due to a right ankle sprain. His return would likely create a bit of a logjam on the wing for the likes of Keon Ellis, Sam Merrill and Max Strus, especially if Jaylon Tyson (toe) also suits up.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is out for Monday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Wade is struggling to shake off this ankle injury and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered doubtful for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) won't play Sunday against the Pacers.
items.story: Wade continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, which is not encouraging. For now, he should be considered doubtful for Monday's meeting in Memphis.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) won't be available to play in the Cavaliers' upcoming three-game road trip, according to Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: The Cavaliers have upcoming games against the Jazz, Lakers and Warriors, but Wade won't suit up for any of those contests and therefore will extend his current string of absences to five games, at minimum. It's currently uncertain when Wade will be able to return from his ankle injury, and while he's out of commission, Keon Ellis and Max Strus should see an increase in playing time.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Wade will miss a second consecutive matchup while nursing a right ankle sprain. Sam Merrill started in his place Wednesday and should be considered the favorite to do so again Friday in Wade's place.

items.headline: Wade won't play Wednesday versus the Heat due to a right ankle sprain, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Wade tweaked his ankle during his pregame routine, but the Cavs are calling it a precautionary absence, so there's a chance he could be available for Friday's rematch with Miami. Keon Ellis and Sam Merrill could see some extra minutes with Wade out Wednesday.

items.headline: Wade finished Thursday's 115-110 victory over Chicago with zero points (0-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), seven rebounds and one assist in 19 minutes.
items.story: Despite the absence of Donovan Mitchell (eye), Wade wasn't able to take advantage of his opportunity with a microscopic usage rate. He remains a deep-league fantasy asset at best with averages of 6.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.1 three-pointers in 21.2 minutes over his last seven games.

items.headline: Wade posted 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt) and five rebounds across 26 minutes during Sunday's 130-120 loss to Dallas.
items.story: Wade remains a key part of Cleveland's rotation, but his fantasy upside is quite limited. Over his last five appearances, he's averaging 20.9 minutes per contest with 7.0 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists on 51.9 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Wade supplied 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt), 10 rebounds, two assists and one block in 20 minutes during Monday's 115-101 win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Wade recorded his first double-double of the season, a welcome sight for anyone holding him in deeper formats. Despite having carved out a starting role, Wade has been far from a must-roster player, averaging just 7.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.7 three-pointers in seven appearances over the past month.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: As expected, Wade will suit up for a second consecutive contest following a three-game absence due to a right ankle sprain. Over six appearances since the All-Star break, the 29-year-old forward has averaged 6.2 points and 4.5 rebounds in 21.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Wade returned from a three-game absence Sunday and logged 21 minutes with seven points and three rebounds. His ankle responded well, and the Cavaliers are anticipating that he will play the second leg of the back-to-back set.

items.headline: Wade (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Boston, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
items.story: Wade missed the Cavaliers' last three games due to a right ankle sprain. He earned the probable tag for Sunday's game after logging a full practice Friday, and the seventh-year pro has progressed enough in his recovery to return. Wade will likely start in his return due to the absence of Jarrett Allen (knee), with the former joining Evan Mobley in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Hachimura (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: The 28-year-old forward will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a left quadriceps contusion, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Heat. With Hachimura and Derrick Jones both sidelined, Kobe Sanders, Baba Miller and Gradey Dick are all candidates for increased playing time, especially if Max Strus (foot) operates under a minutes restriction in his regular-season debut with the Clippers.

items.headline: Hachimura amassed a team-high 24 points (10-16 FG, 4-7 3Pt) and seven rebounds over 30 minutes during Sunday's 124-112 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: The 24 points were a season high for Hachimura, as were the four made three-pointers. The veteran forward is seeing career-high shot volume to begin his first campaign with the Clippers, but Sunday's performance was the first time in five games he shot better than 50 percent from the floor. So far in 2026-27, Hachimura is averaging 13.4 points, 6.0 boards, 2.4 threes and 1.0 steals in 30.0 minutes.

items.headline: Hachimura ended with 12 points (4-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds and two steals across 26 minutes during Friday's 127-101 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Hachimura has struggled to adjust to a more prominent offensive role with the Clippers this season, as shown by the fact that he's scored more than 15 points just once in four appearances, despite averaging 12.3 field-goal attempts per game. His starting role and usage rate should keep him relevant in most formats, but this isn't the start of the season many envisioned for the veteran forward.

items.headline: Hachimura (quadriceps) is available to play in Friday's game against Minnesota, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Hachimura didn't play in Wednesday's 103-87 loss to the Lakers. He was upgraded to probable Friday but has since been cleared to suit up versus the Timberwolves. With Hachimura available and returning to the starting lineup, Kobe Sanders will presumably retreat to the bench.

items.headline: Hachimura (quadriceps) is probable for Friday's game against Minnesota, per Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com.
items.story: Hachimura is set to return from a two-game absence with quadriceps soreness. Kobe Sanders is likely to revert to a bench role Friday, and fewer minutes should be available to Gradey Dick.

items.headline: Hachimura (quadriceps) is questionable for Friday's game against Minnesota, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Hachimura is in jeopardy of missing a second straight game due to left quad soreness. If the 28-year-old forward is ultimately ruled out, Kobe Sanders, Gradey Dick and Baba Miller would be candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Hachimura (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Hachimura didn't practice Tuesday and will be held out of Wednesday's contest due to left quad soreness. His next opportunity to play will come Friday at Minnesota. In the meantime, Kobe Sanders and Gradey Dick are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Hachimura totaled 16 points (5-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, one assist and two steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 125-117 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Hachimura had some good moments in his first game against this former team. He tied for second on the Clippers in scoring and tied for the team lead in rebounds. Hachimura signed a two-year, $28 million deal with Los Angeles' other team over the summer, and he should keep getting heavy minutes at power forward while the Clippers are shorthanded.

items.headline: Hachimura registered 10 points (3-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-5 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 win over Sacramento.
items.story: After jumping ship from the Lakers to the crosstown-rival Clippers over the summer, Hachimura opened the new season in a starting position with his new squad. As long as he stays in the first unit, the veteran forward should be able to supply late-round fantasy value.

items.headline: Hachimura tallied 16 points (5-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, two steals and one assist across 24 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over Denver.
items.story: Hachimura put together a solid effort in the victory, leading Los Angeles in scoring while tying four teammates for the team lead in rebounds. After spending the past three-and-a-half seasons with the Lakers, Hachimura inked a two-year, $28 million contract with their crosstown rival and is in line to start at power forward for the Clippers during the regular season.

items.headline: Hachimura scored 14 points (3-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 7-7 FT) while adding three rebounds, an assist and a steal across 19 minutes in Saturday's 114-106 preseason loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Hachimura earned half of his scoring output from the charity stripe, but he still made his presence felt in a limited cameo, although no starter outside of Cam Christie played more than 20 minutes. Hachimura is expected to be the Clippers' starting power forward once the regular season starts, so it makes sense for the team to monitor his workload during the preseason.

items.headline: Hachimura racked up 21 points (8-11 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and one block across 15 minutes in Sunday's 104-101 preseason win over the Warriors.
items.story: Hachimura had the hot hand early, and despite logging just 15 minutes, his 21 points were a game-high figure. He's making a strong case to open the year as a starter with Brandon Ingram (Achilles) sidelined, and he could be a solid source of points and triples this season.

items.headline: Hachimura will start in Sunday's preseason game against the Warriors, but he will be limited to the first half of play, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Joining Hachimura in the first unit for Sunday's exhibition will be Darius Garland, Max Strus, Derrick Jones and Isaiah Jackson. Brandon Ingram (Achilles) won't be ready for Opening Night, so Hachimura could begin the season as a starter.

items.headline: Hachimura recorded 29 points (11-14 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, two assists, three steals and one block in 28 minutes during Japan's 106-78 win over Saudi Arabia in Thursday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Hachimura was nearly flawless in his return to international competition while committing zero turnovers. The 28-year-old will begin a new chapter in 2026-27 after signing a two-year, $28 million contract with the Clippers this offseason. Hachimura shot a career-best 44.3 percent from three-point range with the Lakers last season and should provide the Clippers with another capable floor spacer. However, the wing depth could make consistent fantasy production difficult to come by. He'll likely compete with players such as Max Strus for minutes and isn't guaranteed a starting role heading into training camp.

items.headline: The arrival of Max Strus creates another source of competition for Hachimura in Los Angeles.
items.story: Strus' ability to space the floor and function without the ball should make him an easy fit around the Clippers' primary creators, potentially costing Hachimura some opportunities depending on how the rotation shakes out. Hachimura can still carve out a significant role with his size and scoring ability, but the Clippers' depth makes a major fantasy breakout less likely.

items.headline: Hachimura signed a two-year, $28 million contract with the Clippers on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After spending the past three-plus seasons with the Lakers, Hachimura will remain in Los Angeles on a two-year pact with the Clippers. The 28-year-old forward figures to see meaningful playing time but isn't guaranteed a starting role with his new club. Over 68 regular-season appearances (41 starts) in 2025-26, he averaged 11.5 points and 3.3 rebounds across 28.3 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Hachimura notched 25 points (9-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block in 43 minutes during Monday's 115-110 loss to Oklahoma City in Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: It was Hachimura's best scoring effort of the playoffs, but it wasn't enough to keep the Lakers' season alive as they got swept out of the second round. The 28-year-old forward averaged 17.5 points, 4.0 boards, 3.3 threes, 1.7 assists and 1.5 combined steals and blocks over 10 games this postseason while shooting 54.9 percent from the floor and 56.9 percent from beyond the arc, a strong performance that should only boost his value on the open market as he heads into free agency.

items.headline: Hachimura logged 21 points (7-14 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal over 39 minutes during the Lakers' 131-108 loss to the Thunder on Saturday in Game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Hachimura paced the Lakers with 16 of his team-high 21 points in the first half, though he went just 2-for-7 from the floor in the second. It was the second time in the playoffs that he connected on five three-pointers after not reaching that mark in any contest during the regular season. The Lakers enter Game 4 down 3-0 in the series, and a loss could be Hachimura's last outing with the team, as he'll enter the offseason an unrestricted free agent.

items.headline: Hachimura produced 18 points (7-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 37 minutes during Tuesday's 108-90 loss to the Thunder in Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Even with Austin Reaves back in the starting five for the Lakers, it was Hachimura who gave LeBron James the most support on the offensive end of the court. Hachimura has scored in double digits in every game of the playoffs so far while draining multiple three-pointers in six of seven contests. During that stretch, he's averaged 16.1 points, 3.7 boards, 2.9 threes, 1.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 38.3 minutes while shooting 54.2 percent from the floor and 57.1 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Hachimura totaled 21 points (8-15 FG, 5-7 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists and one block over 35 minutes during Friday's 98-78 victory over the Rockets in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: It was the second time in the series that Hachimura scored 20-plus points, and he finished as the Lakers' second-leading scorer behind LeBron James (28 points). Hachimura will finish the first round of the Western Conference playoffs having averaged 15.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 2.8 threes and 1.0 steals over 38.5 minutes per game. The Lakers will face the Thunder in the semifinals.

items.headline: Hachimura logged 22 points (8-14 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal across 44 minutes during Friday's 112-108 overtime victory over the Rockets in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hachimura had his best game of the playoffs thus far, scoring 22 points and knocking down four triples. It's all hands on deck for the Lakers right now, with multiple role players stepping up on a nightly basis. Now with a 3-0 series lead, Los Angeles will look to wrap things up when the two teams meet again Sunday.

items.headline: Hachimura had 13 points (5-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt), five rebounds and two assists in 43 minutes during Tuesday's 101-94 victory over Houston in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hachimura logged a considerable workload in the Game 2 win, although he didn't make a huge impact on the box score. Through two playoff games, he's averaging 13.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 42.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hachimura produced 22 points (8-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds and one steal across 29 minutes during Sunday's 131-107 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: With no Luka Doncic (hamstring) or Austin Reaves (oblique) in the lineup, and with LeBron James logging only 17 minutes, Hachimura co-led the Lakers in scoring alongside Deandre Ayton. With Doncic and Reaves not expected to be a factor in the early stages of the playoff series against the Rockets, Hachimura will be tasked with playing a big role on offense as a scorer behind James. Hachimura averaged 11.5 points per game across 68 appearances (41 starts) in 2025-26, but that number increased marginally to 13.4 points per contest when he was part of the first unit.

items.headline: Hachimura had 15 points (7-10 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 0-3 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block across 26 minutes during Tuesday's 123-87 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: With no Luka Doncic (hamstring), Austin Reaves (oblique) or LeBron James (foot) in the lineup, Hachimura led the Lakers in scoring on the night. The 28-year-old has scored in double digits in four of the last five games (three starts), averaging 13.6 points, 4.0 boards, 1.4 threes and 1.0 combined blocks and steals in 25.6 minutes while shooting 60.0 percent from the floor. Hachimura will likely continue to see elevated usage to close out the regular season as the Lakers focus on getting their stars healthy for the playoffs.

items.headline: Hachimura produced 21 points (9-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal across 39 minutes during Sunday's 134-128 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: With Luka Doncic (hamstring), Austin Reaves (oblique) and Marcus Smart (ankle) sidelined, Hachimura moved into the starting lineup. He thrived with a 21-point performance, marking his best scoring night since he delivered a 23-point output in a win over the Bulls on Jan. 26. Expect Hachimura to have a sizable role on offense in the final week of the regular season, given he should be a go-to option as long as Doncic and Reaves remain out. Reaves isn't expected back until early May at the earliest, while Doncic's timetable remains uncertain.

items.headline: Hachimura will start in Sunday's game against Dallas, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Lakers are down Luka Doncic (hamstring) and Austin Reaves (oblique), so Hachimura will re-enter the starting lineup. The 28-year-old has started 36 times this season, averaging 12.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.6 steals while shooting 45.3 percent from deep across 31.9 minutes.

items.headline: Hachimura won't start Tuesday's game against the Cavaliers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Luka Doncic back from his one-game suspension, Hachimura will retreat to the second unit. The 28-year-old forward has averaged 6.2 points and 2.2 rebounds across 20.6 minutes per game in his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Hachimura is starting Monday's game against Washington.
items.story: Hachimura will enter the starting lineup with Luka Doncic serving a one-game suspension Monday. Hachimura started four games in a row earlier in the month and averaged 12.5 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 31.0 minutes during this stretch.

items.headline: Hachimura (calf) is available for Friday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Hachimura is ready to end a three-game absence due to right calf injury management, which should slightly eat into the playing time of Jake LaRavia. Across his past five appearances, Hachimura has averaged 5.8 points, 2.4 rebounds and 0.4 steals in 20.4 minutes per game while shooting 54.2 percent from the field.

items.headline: Hachimura (calf) is questionable for Friday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Hachimura is in danger of missing a third consecutive game with what the team is deeming right calf injury management. He'll presumably test out the calf at some point before tipoff, at which time the Lakers will provide another update on his availability.

items.headline: Hachimura (calf) will not play Wednesday against the Pacers.
items.story: Hachimura was previously considered questionable, but he'll miss his second straight contest and can be considered day-to-day moving forward. With Marcus Smart (ankle) also out, there will be plenty of minutes available for guys like Jake LaRavia and Luke Kennard.

items.headline: Hachimura (calf) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Hachimura was held out of Monday's game against the Pistons with right calf soreness, and he's now in danger of missing a second straight matchup. He'll presumably get checked out again Wednesday, at which point the Lakers could have an update on his availability.

items.headline: Hachimura is out is out for Monday's game against Detroit with right calf soreness.
items.story: Monday is Hachimura's first absence since the Feb. 28 win over the Warriors. His absence frees up some more playing time for Luke Kennard and Jake LaRavia on the wing versus the Pistons.

items.headline: Hachimura is questionable to play Monday in Detroit due to soreness in his right calf.
items.story: If Hachimura can't play Monday, Jarred Vanderbilt would have the chance to get into the rotation, while Jake LaRavia could also see a slight bump in minutes. Check back for official word on Hachimura's status closer to Monday's tipoff.

items.headline: Walker supplied 12 points (5-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT) and six rebounds across 19 minutes during Saturday's 109-104 win over Charlotte.
items.story: After missing Philadelphia's previous three games with a knee injury, Walker returned and made a noticeable impact with LeBron James and Joel Embiid inactive. Walker posted season-highs in minutes, points and rebounds to help the Sixers win their third straight contest. However, when Philadelphia is healthy, his playing time will shrink substantially.

items.headline: Walker (knee) is available for Saturday's game versus the Hornets, Chris Hine of The Philly Inquirer reports.
items.story: Walker missed the last three games but will return for Saturday's meeting with Charlotte. The 24-year-old has averaged just 6.3 minutes this season. However, with LeBron James (rest), Dominick Barlow (back) and Joel Embiid (foot) sidelined, Walker might see a little more action.

items.headline: Walker (knee) is questionable for Saturday's game in Charlotte.
items.story: Walker has missed the past three games for the 76ers, but this is the first time he's received the questionable tag since going down, which indicates progress. With LeBron James (rest) out, Walker could be in the rotation if he's cleared to play.

items.headline: Walker (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game versus New York.
items.story: Walker will miss a third consecutive contest due to a left knee issue. His next opportunity to suit up will come Saturday at Charlotte in the second leg of this back-to-back set.

items.headline: Walker (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Walker will miss a second consecutive contest due to left knee soreness. According to Ky Carlin of USA Today, the 24-year-old forward didn't practice Tuesday but was able to go through individual on-court workouts. His next chance to play will come Friday against New York.

items.headline: Walker has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pistons due to left knee soreness.
items.story: It was reported after Saturday's win over the Bucks that Walker exited the contest early due to a right knee injury, though he's now listed on the injury report with left knee soreness. With the 24-year-old sidelined, Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope may see increased minutes, while Justin Edwards could enter the rotation.

items.headline: Walker exited Saturday's 127-116 win over the Bucks in the third quarter and did not return due to a right knee injury, Noah Levick of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports. He finished with six points (2-3 FG, 2-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 12 minutes.
items.story: Walker logged a season-high 12 minutes in the absence of LeBron James (back), though the former injured his knee in the third quarter and never checked back in. Walker can be considered questionable for Sunday's game against Detroit until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Walker exited to the locker room in the third quarter of Saturday's game against the Bucks due to an apparent ankle injury, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Walker appeared to turn his ankle before limping to the locker room. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Walker racked up two points (1-1 FG) and one rebound in four minutes during Thursday's 114-106 win over Cleveland.
items.story: Walker was barely involved in Philadelphia's rotation, making his only field-goal attempt during a brief appearance off the bench. With the 76ers boasting considerable frontcourt depth, the 24-year-old forward faces an uphill battle for consistent minutes and fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Walker recorded 13 points (4-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds and two steals across 19 minutes in Friday's 125-120 preseason loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Walker provided a productive performance off Philadelphia's bench to close out a strong preseason. Although Walker struggled with his long-range shot -- an issue that also affected him in the 2025-26 regular season -- he compensated with solid defensive activity and four rebounds. His 13 points were the most among Philadelphia's reserves, and Walker's ability to contribute in multiple categories could help his case for a regular rotation role, though his fantasy value remains dependent on consistent minutes.

items.headline: Walker will come off the bench in Friday's preseason finale against the Celtics, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Walker started in Saturday's preseason loss to the Celtics with Philly resting Joel Embiid, but Embiid is back and starting for the preseason finale. Walker is not expected to be a major factor in the rotation for the 76ers this season as long as the starters are healthy.

items.headline: Walker totaled 14 points (6-11 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds and two assists in 27 minutes during Saturday's 144-106 preseason loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Walker finished behind VJ Edgecombe for the team high in points, doing so while picking up his second double-digit scoring performance of the preseason. The 2022 No. 57 overall pick spent his first three seasons with the Trail Blazers before suiting up for the 76ers during the 2025-26 campaign. Walker appeared in 64 regular-season games for Philadelphia, and while he managed to start six times, he averaged just 2.5 points and 3.3 rebounds over 14.0 minutes per outing in those appearances.
