Plowden, a Bowling Green product, played in six regular-season games with the Hawks during the 2024-25 campaign, averaging 7.2 points and 1.8 rebounds across 12 minutes per game while shooting 64.0 percent from the floor and 52.9 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: The Hawks traded Plowden to the Suns as part of a historic seven-team trade that became official Sunday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Plowden played in six games for the Hawks during the 2024-25 campaign. The Bowling Green product averaged 7.2 points and 1.8 rebounds across 12 minutes per game, shooting 64 percent from the field and 52.9 percent from deep.

items.headline: Plowden, who is on a two-way contract with the Hawks, is ineligible for the NBA Playoffs.
items.story: Plowden appeared in a total of six games for the Hawks, averaging 7.2 points and 1.8 rebounds in 12.0 minutes. He was much more involved for the College Park Skyhawks in the G League, posting averages of 15.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.1 steals, 0.9 blocks and 2.2 three-pointers across 29 appearances.

items.headline: Plowden registered two points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) in one minute during Thursday's 133-109 victory over Brooklyn.
items.story: Plowden suited up for just the fifth time all season, all of which have been garbage-time appearances bar one. It's clear Plowden is on the outside looking in when it comes to rotational minutes, averaging 5.2 points in 8.1 minutes this season.

items.headline: Plowden was transferred from the G League's College Park Skyhawks to Atlanta on Monday.
items.story: With College Park missing out on the G League playoffs, Plowden will join the Hawks in the NBA to provide some depth to the roster. The rookie swingman is logging 16.5 minutes per game over two appearances with Atlanta in 2024-25, but it's unclear what kind of role he'll have to close out the season.

items.headline: Plowden didn't play in Sunday's 126-108 G League loss to the Rio Grande Valley Vipers due to a right elbow strain.
items.story: The right elbow strain is a new injury for Plowden, and his next chance to suit up will come in the parent club's game against Memphis on Monday. The swingman has received the majority of his playing time in the G League, appearing in only two outings with the Hawks since signing a two-way contract with the club in December.

items.headline: The Hawks transferred Ploweden from the G League's College Park Skyhawks on Friday.
items.story: Plowden recorded 11 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, one assist and one block in 22 minutes during Thursday's 123-122 overtime G League loss to the Maine Celtics. Plowden will now get an opportunity to crack the Hawks' NBA rotation during Saturday's matchup with Boston.

items.headline: Dunn supplied six points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block across 14 minutes during Monday's 125-114 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Dunn appears to have beaten out the likes of Haywood Highsmith, Rasheer Fleming and Koa Peat for a rotation spot with the Suns. However, Dunn's fantasy appeal is likely to remain limited while the team's wings and forwards are healthy.

items.headline: Dunn will come off the bench in Friday's preseason finale versus Utah, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Miles Bridges (ankle) is back and starting following a two-game layoff, so Dunn will head back to the second unit. As a reserve this preseason, Dunn is averaging 3.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 19.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Dunn registered 15 points (6-6 FG, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, two blocks and one steal over 23 minutes during the Suns' 123-103 preseason loss to the Spurs on Wednesday.
items.story: Dunn got the start Wednesday while the Suns rested all of their projected starters, and the third-year pro stepped up by co-leading the team in both points and blocks. He averaged 19.4 minutes per game off the bench during the 2025-26 regular season, though Dunn played less than 10 minutes in five of the Suns' six playoff games. He figures to be the most likely candidate to enter Phoenix's starting five if Miles Bridges (ankle) were to miss time.

items.headline: Dunn will start in Saturday's preseason game against the Spurs, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Dunn is getting the start with Miles Bridges (ankle) unavailable for Saturday's exhibition. As a starter last season, Dunn averaged 9.3 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.3 triples and 1.3 steals per game.

items.headline: Dunn recorded four points (2-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block in 23 minutes during Wednesday's 124-117 preseason loss to Chicago.
items.story: Dunn made his presence felt defensively, leading Phoenix's reserves in playing time while contributing across several statistical categories. His defensive versatility could help him secure a consistent rotation role, though limited offensive production may restrict his fantasy upside.

items.headline: The Suns exercised Dunn's fourth-year option for 2027-28 on his rookie contract Thursday.
items.story: This was the expectation as Dunn plays out the final year of his rookie deal in 2027-28 ahead of restricted free agency the following year. He figures to be contending for a bench role with the likes of Jordan Goodwin, Haywood Highsmith, Rasheer Fleming and perhaps even rookie first-rounder Koa Peat at training camp this fall.

items.headline: Dunn could be restricted to a reserve role next year after Phoenix acquired Miles Bridges from Charlotte this summer.
items.story: The Suns may have lost Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale this offseason, but they signed sharpshooter Luke Kennard in addition to receiving Bridges in a trade with the Hornets. Dunn opened 2025-26 as a starter before being phased out of Phoenix's rotation entirely during the playoffs, ultimately averaging a pedestrian 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 19.4 minutes per game over 70 appearances (16 starts) during the regular season. Dunn figures to be battling for a bench role with the likes of Jordan Goodwin, Haywood Highsmith, Rasheer Fleming and perhaps even rookie first-rounder Koa Peat at training camp this fall.

items.headline: Dunn amassed zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) in one minute during Monday's 131-122 loss to the Thunder in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Despite opening the year in a starting role, the second-year forward was unable to hold down a spot in the Phoenix first unit this year. Dunn averaged 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 19.4 minutes per game over 70 appearances (16 starts) during the regular season.

items.headline: Dunn won't start Tuesday's Play-In Tournament game against Portland, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Dunn got the spot start in Sunday's regular-season finale but will retreat to the bench Tuesday. The second-year forward isn't guaranteed significant playing time but could pick up a few extra minutes due to Grayson Allen (hamstring) being out.

items.headline: Dunn totaled 20 points (8-11 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, five assists and one block over 25 minutes during Sunday's 135-103 victory over the Thunder.
items.story: Dunn exploded in his second straight start, scoring a season-best 20 points in a blowout road victory. He'll close the regular season averaging 5.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 19.4 minutes across 70 appearances (16 starts). Despite the strong showing Sunday, Dunn is likely to see a decrease in playing time in Tuesday's Play-In Tournament matchup against the Trail Blazers or beyond if the Suns advance deeper into the postseason.

items.headline: Dunn is in the Suns' starting lineup against the Lakers on Friday.
items.story: Dunn has seen his playing time fluctuate as of late, but he'll make his 15th start of the season due to the absence of Haywood Highsmith (knee). Dunn's last start took place Feb. 26 against the Lakers, when he played 26 minutes and finished with 10 points, four rebounds, one assist and one steal in a 113-110 win.

items.headline: Dunn (coach's decision) didn't receive any playing time Tuesday in the Suns' 115-111 loss to the Magic.
items.story: With Grayson Allen (knee) and Dillon Brooks (hand) back in action after one- and 18-game absences, respectively, Dunn was bumped out of the rotation while head coach Jordan Ott went with Royce O'Neale and Rasheer Fleming as the team's backup forwards. Dunn had played at least 17 minutes in each of his last six appearances, averaging 8.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.2 three-pointers while shooting 59.5 percent from the field over that stretch.

items.headline: Dunn (groin) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Saturday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Dunn is set to return after a one-game absence, but with Grayson Allen back, it could be tough for Dunn to find meaningful run. Dunn is averaging 5.9 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game this season.

items.headline: Dunn (groin) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Dunn was added to the injury report shortly before tipoff, and he's since been downgraded to out with right groin soreness. Jordan Goodwin and Rasheer Fleming look to be in line for more minutes with Dunn sidelined.

items.headline: Dunn is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets due to right groin soreness, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: Dunn was an extremely late addition to the injury report, which isn't a positive sign ahead of tipoff at 11:00 p.m. ET. If the second-year forward is ultimately ruled out, Rasheer Fleming would likely see increased playing time.

items.headline: Dunn closed with 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals across 27 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 120-98 win over the Raptors.
items.story: The second-year forward made an impact at the defensive end, with his four combined steals and blocks being his best effort at that end of the court since Jan. 27. Dunn has played at least 20 minutes in three straight games as Phoenix deals with injuries to its frontcourt, averaging 9.7 points, 6.3 boards, 2.0 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.7 threes in 23.3 minutes over that span.

items.headline: Dunn recorded 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 23 minutes during Saturday's 108-105 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Dunn had his best night in quite some time, recording double-digit scoring for the first time in his past 10 games, while also adding a pair of defensive stats. While this was certainly an encouraging performance, his recent lack of production cannot be overlooked. In 14 games over the past month, he has been barely a top-300 player, averaging 5.0 points and 4.5 rebounds in 19.3 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Dunn (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Friday's 122-115 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Dunn had been seeing his playing time trend down recently, but Friday marked the first time all season that the second-year forward failed to see any action for non-injury reasons. Though he's regarded as a versatile defender, Dunn's perimeter shooting hasn't developed as the Suns had hoped, as he's converting on just 32.6 percent of his three-point attempts on the season. Now that the Suns are at full strength on the wing and at forward sans Dillon Brooks (hand), Dunn looks like he could find himself outside of the rotation more often than not while head coach Jordan Ott prioritizes Grayson Allen, Haywood Highsmith and Rasheer Fleming in the second unit.

items.headline: Dunn won't start against the Kings on Tuesday.
items.story: With Devin Booker (hip) back in action following a four-game absence, Dunn will retreat to the second unit. Over eight outings off the bench in February, the second-year forward averaged 4.1 points and 3.1 rebounds across 15.9 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Dunn will start Sunday's game against the Trail Blazers, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Dunn will make his first start since Nov. 21 due to Dillon Brooks (hand) being out of the lineup. Dunn has seen at least 20 minutes in each of his last three appearances, averaging 2.3 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 22.0 minutes per game over that stretch.

items.headline: Dunn registered nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and four steals in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 106-102 victory over the Nets.
items.story: The four steals were one short of a season high for Dunn, whose 21 minutes were also his most since Jan. 7. Dunn hasn't scored in double figures since Nov. 16 and has seen single-digit minutes in two of his last four games, so he's not doing enough to warrant much attention in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Dunn recorded three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound and one assist over 17 minutes during Monday's 126-117 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Dunn continues to play a secondary role off the bench, having logged fewer than 20 minutes in six straight games. Even when he has been afforded starter-level minutes, Dunn has been unable to produce at a standard league level. In his current role, he holds very little value outside of deeper formats.

items.headline: Dunn logged seven points (3-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and one steal over 12 minutes during Friday's 112-107 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Dunn logged a season-low 12 minutes, though he was productive during his limited run. He led the second unit in assists, dishing out at least three dimes for the first time since Dec. 20. Dunn hasn't scored in double figures since Nov. 16 and doesn't offer much fantasy value outside of some solid performances on the glass. Still, he had totaled only two rebounds in his past two games entering Friday's tilt. If and when the team returns to full strength, the second-year forward could struggle to earn significant burn on a nightly basis.

items.headline: Dunn chipped in five points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT) and one rebound in 16 minutes during Monday's 100-97 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Dunn failed to produce anything of note, another in a string of underwhelming performances. After opening the season as a starter, Dunn has since shifted to a bench role, averaging 5.3 points and 4.9 rebounds in 19.9 minutes per game over his last 11 appearances.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is available for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Dunn will return from a two-game absence due to a right knee injury, which will likely leave fewer minutes available for the likes of Rasheer Fleming, Isaiah Livers and Jordan Goodwin. Dunn has averaged 5.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 20.2 minutes per game across nine outings during December.

items.headline: Dunn is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers due to a right knee contusion.
items.story: Dunn is in jeopardy of missing his third straight outing due to the right knee injury he sustained in Friday's win over the Pelicans. If the second-year forward remains sidelined, Rasheer Fleming and Jordan Goodwin are candidates for increased playing time. Across nine appearances in December, Dunn has averaged 5.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 20.2 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Dunn is out for Monday's game against the Wizards due to right knee soreness.
items.story: The forward will be trying to end a two-game absence during Wednesday's contest against the Cavaliers. Dunn's absence solidifies Royce O'Neale's streaming value in all fantasy leagues Monday, with Grayson Allen (knee) and Jalen Green (hamstring) out.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Dunn could miss a second straight game due to right knee soreness. If he is unable to play, Jordan Goodwin and Rasheer Fleming could see increased roles.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is out for Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Dunn is dealing with right knee soreness and won't suit up for the second leg of this back-to-back set. His next chance to play will come against the Wizards on Monday.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Dunn is dealing with right knee soreness following Friday's win over New Orleans and is in jeopardy of missing Saturday's rematch. If the second-year forward is unable to suit up, Rasheer Fleming and Jordan Goodwin are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Dunn (knee) is available to return to Friday's game against the Pelicans, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Dunn exited to the locker room in the second quarter due to a right knee issue but is available to return for the second half. He posted three points, three rebounds and one assist across seven minutes in the first half before heading to the tunnel.

items.headline: Dunn exited to the locker room after sustaining an apparent right knee injury in the second quarter of Friday's game against the Pelicans, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: Dunn grabbed at his right knee and limped to the locker room with 9:52 remaining in the second quarter. If the second-year forward is unable to return, Rasheer Fleming and Jordan Goodwin are candidates for increased playing time for the remainder of the game.

items.headline: Dunn supplied seven points (2-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal over 20 minutes during Saturday's 119-116 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Dunn continues to provide very little outside of defensive stats, scoring single digits for the ninth straight game. During that time, he has averaged just 4.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 19.7 minutes per game. At this stage, he should be viewed as nothing more than a defensive streaming option.

items.headline: Dunn amassed two points (1-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt), eight rebounds and four assists across 24 minutes during Monday's 108-105 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Dunn hasn't been much of a scoring factor since returning from a wrist injury that sidelined him for five games, averaging 4.0 points on shooting just 31.3 percent from the field in his last three appearances. However, he has been a force defensively, averaging 6.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in that span, and he will likely remain with the second unit in the foreseeable future despite starting 11 games this season.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) registered six points (3-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), eight rebounds, two steals and one assist across 21 minutes in Monday's 125-108 win over the Lakers.
items.story: The defensive-minded forward made his return Monday after missing the Suns' previous five games with a right wrist sprain. He didn't appear to be operating with any restrictions, given that he nearly reached his season-long average in minutes (23.8 per game). Dunn could be in line for a slight uptick in playing time in Phoenix's next game Friday in Houston, if both Devin Booker (groin) and Grayson Allen (illness) aren't available.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) has been cleared to play Monday against the Lakers, Shane Young of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Dunn will make his first appearance since Nov. 21 after recovering from a right wrist sprain. He'll presumably be deployed off the bench Monday and could have his minutes monitored closely in his first game back.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) is probable for Monday's game against the Lakers, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: It appears that Dunn will be returning from a five-game absence Monday evening, which could result in Royce O'Neale heading back to the second unit and Nigel Hayes-Davis could drop from the rotation entirely. Check back for official confirmation on Dunn's status closer to Monday's tip.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) is out for Saturday's game against the Nuggets, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Dunn will be sidelined for a fifth straight contest due to a right wrist sprain, meaning the Suns will be thin in terms of depth once again. They're also missing Isaiah Livers (hip), Jalen Green (hamstring) and Mark Williams (calf). Dunn will aim to return to the hardwood when the Suns take on the Lakers on Monday.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Dunn has missed the Suns' last four games due to a right wrist sprain, but he has a chance to return during Saturday's contest. His return would be timely, given that Isaiah Livers (hip) has been ruled out for the game.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) is out for Friday's game against the Thunder, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Dunn will miss a fourth consecutive game while nursing a right wrist sprain, and there's no clarity as to when he might return to the hardwood. Jordan Goodwin and Isaiah Livers will likely continue to see more minutes as long as Dunn remains out.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Dunn is set to miss a third consecutive game due to a right wrist sprain, and his next opportunity to play is Friday against the Thunder. Jordan Goodwin and Isaiah Livers will likely continue to see more rotational minutes for as long as Dunn is sidelined.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) will not play Monday against the Rockets.
items.story: Dunn will miss his second game in a row Monday due to a right wrist sprain. His next chance to play comes Wednesday against the Kings. In Dunn's absence, guys like Isaiah Livers and Jordan Goodwin could see an increase in minutes.

items.headline: Dunn (wrist) is out for Sunday's game against the Spurs, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: Dunn will miss his first game of the season due to a right wrist sprain. His absence could open up more minutes for Isaiah Livers and Jordan Goodwin.

items.headline: Pritchard is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee due to a right shoulder contusion, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Pritchard's status is uncertain after he struggled in Monday's loss to Houston, finishing with four points on 0-for-7 shooting across 30 minutes. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also questionable and Devin Carter (illness) ruled out, Boston could be shorthanded Wednesday. Pritchard's availability should become clearer closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Pritchard finished Monday's 109-93 loss to the Rockets with four points (0-7 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 30 minutes.
items.story: Pritchard couldn't buy a basket, missing all seven of his field-goal attempts while finishing with a team-worst minus-17 rating. Despite the shooting struggles, he logged 30 minutes off the bench with Paul George (rest) unavailable, suggesting his role remains secure. Pritchard should have opportunities to bounce back, but his offensive inconsistency has been frustrating for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Pritchard had 30 points (9-17 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 9-9 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals across 35 minutes during Friday's 125-111 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Pritchard scored 20 of his game-high 30 points in the first half, which was a big reason why the Celtics entered the break with a 29-point lead. He did his scoring from all over the floor, and his nine made free throws were a career high. Pritchard's scoring production has been inconsistent over the first five games of the regular season, but he's the offensive spark plug that the Celtics rely on, especially when one of Jayson Tatum and Paul George is not on the floor.

items.headline: Pritchard registered 28 points (10-16 FG, 7-10 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, four assists and two steals across 22 minutes during Monday's 134-99 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Pritchard caught fire from beyond the arc, connecting on seven three-pointers while leading Boston in scoring despite coming off the bench. The veteran guard was particularly effective during the third quarter, helping the Celtics pull away in a lopsided victory. Pritchard's explosive shooting ability gives him considerable fantasy upside, though his production could fluctuate depending on his playing time.

items.headline: Pritchard finished with 17 points (4-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 7-8 FT), four rebounds and one assist in 27 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Pritchard matched Derrick White for Boston's second-highest scoring total despite the former coming off the bench. The guard generated much of his offense at the charity stripe, converting seven of eight attempts while committing zero turnovers. His 28-minute workload suggests he'll remain a significant part of the Celtics' backcourt rotation, although his limited playmaking in the opener was less encouraging for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Pritchard (rest) is expected to play in Tuesday's game versus Detroit.
items.story: Pritchard didn't play in Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over Philadelphia but is on track to be on the floor when the Celtics begin the 2026-27 campaign versus the Pistons. The 2020 No. 26 overall pick is coming off his best season in 2025-26, averaging 17.0 points, 3.9 rebounds and 5.2 assists across 32.4 minutes per contest in 79 regular-season games, including 50 starts. With Jaylen Brown now in Philadelphia, there is room for Pritchard to take over as the No. 3 offensive option behind Paul George and Jayson Tatum, giving him more than enough upside for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Pritchard (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Pritchard and the rest of Boston's regulars won't be available for the final exhibition but should be good to go for the regular-season opener against the Pistons on Tuesday. Pritchard provided seven points (3-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 11 assists and three rebounds over 29 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over Charlotte.

items.headline: Pritchard provided seven points (3-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 11 assists and three rebounds over 29 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 114-93 preseason win over Charlotte.
items.story: The 28-year-old guard had trouble getting his own shot to fall, but he led the Celtics in assists on the night while tying Jayson Tatum for the team lead in minutes. Pritchard posted better numbers last season than he did in 2024-25, when he won the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year award, averaging a career-best 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 boards, along with 2.7 threes in 32.4 minutes over 79 regular-season games, and he should be the engine of the second unit once again in 2026-27.

items.headline: Pritchard signed a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension with the Celtics on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Pritchard's extension includes a mutual option for the 2029-30 campaign. The 28-year-old guard is coming off the best statistical year of his career, averaging 17.0 points, 5.2 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 0.7 steals across 32.4 minutes per game in 79 regular-season appearances (50 starts). Regardless of whether the 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year starts, he figures to play a sizable role for the Jaylen Brown-less Celtics.

items.headline: Pritchard posted 25 points (7-12 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), seven assists and four rebounds over 24 minutes during Saturday's 144-106 preseason win over the 76ers.
items.story: Pritchard helped the Celtics race out to a commanding lead in the second quarter with 11 points, nine of which came on three triples. The seventh-year point guard has been the Celtics' offensive spark plug the last few seasons, and he operated in a starting role for most of last year during Jayson Tatum's absence. Pritchard is expected to revert to a rotational role now that Tatum is back, but with Jaylen Brown now in Philadelphia and Paul George in Boston, Pritchard could be the Celtics' second offensive option on most nights.

items.headline: Pritchard (rest) said he'll play in Saturday's preseason game against the 76ers, Jay King of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Most of Boston's regular players rested during the preseason opener, including Pritchard, but the veteran point guard will make his debut Saturday. He's coming off a career-best season during which he averaged 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds across 79 regular-season games (50 starts).

items.headline: Pritchard (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: This appears to be a scheduled rest day for Pritchard, as the Celtics are sitting a number of their regular rotation players. He'll have an opportunity to suit up for Saturday's exhibition against the 76ers.

items.headline: Pritchard said Monday that he's focused on making incremental improvements across the board rather than dramatically changing his game heading into the 2026-27 season, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: The veteran guard mentioned becoming more efficient while improving his production as a scorer, facilitator, rebounder and defender. Pritchard is coming off a career year in which he averaged 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds across 79 regular-season appearances, and he should be an even more important piece of Boston's backcourt this season with Jaylen Brown out of the picture.

items.headline: Pritchard could benefit from additional offensive opportunities after Boston dealt Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia, John Schuhmann of NBA.com reports.
items.story: Although Paul George is expected to step into a starting role, Brown's departure creates extra ball-handling and scoring chances throughout the rotation, potentially allowing Pritchard to build on last season's breakout campaign. Increased minutes in three-guard lineups could help preserve his fantasy relevance despite George's arrival.

items.headline: Pritchard racked up 13 points (5-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 39 minutes during Saturday's 109-100 loss to Philadelphia in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Pritchard logged 39 minutes in Game 7, his most of the series. Although the 28-year-old was productive, he once again struggled from three-point range. With Boston now eliminated from the playoffs, the Celtics may need to make some adjustments in order to remain competitive moving ahead. Pritchard, who has a couple of years left on his current contract, is coming off a solid 2025-26 campaign, averaging a career-best 17.0 points, 3.9 rebounds and 5.2 assists across 32.4 minutes in 79 regular-season appearances. Unless the Celtics receive a substantial offer, it's hard to imagine the team parting ways with the 2025 Sixth Man of the Year. Still, Pritchard might benefit from a change of scenery if he can carve out a stable role as a starter for a new club.

items.headline: Pritchard contributed 32 points (12-21 FG, 6-12 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal over 35 minutes during Sunday's 128-96 win over the 76ers in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Pritchard was on fire during Game 4, drilling six three-pointers on the way to a convincing victory. Most recently, Pritchard has performed as an effective sixth man for the Celtics. He started 50 games amid various injury scenarios that plagued the team, but he seems best suited as a spark plug with the second unit off the bench. He experienced career highs in almost every major category in this sixth season and has been invaluable to the team as it strives to bring another title back to Boston.

items.headline: Pritchard ended with 15 points (5-12 FG, 5-10 3Pt), four rebounds and two assists over 33 minutes during Friday's 108-100 victory over Philadelphia in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Pritchard delivered an improved effort, landing a number of crucial three-pointers down the stretch. While this was an encouraging performance, Pritchard has been far from his best during the series, averaging just 10.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 2.3 three-pointers across three games.

items.headline: Pritchard racked up four points (2-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt), five rebounds and five assists over 27 minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the 76ers in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Pritchard couldn't get anything going Tuesday, scoring just four points on 2-for-8 shooting. Boston was likely caught off guard in the loss, with numerous players delivering below expectations. With the series now tied at 1-1, The Celtics will be looking to turn things around when they line up again for Game 3 on Friday.

items.headline: Pritchard (foot) isn't listed on the injury report for Sunday's Game 1 against the 76ers.
items.story: Pritchard was held out of Boston's regular-season finale due to left foot plantar fasciitis, though he's set to return to action Sunday. The 28-year-old guard averaged 17.2 points, 5.3 assists and 2.8 rebounds across 30.3 minutes per tilt off the bench over his final six regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Pritchard (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Orlando, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: Pritchard drew the doubtful tag for Sunday's regular-season finale due to left foot plantar fasciitis, and he'll indeed be sidelined as the Celtics prepare for their playoff run. The sixth-year guard started in a career-high 50 regular-season games, but he returned to a bench role in early February after Anfernee Simons (wrist) was traded to the Bulls in exchange for Nikola Vucevic (finger). Pritchard was still effective in his sixth-man role, and across 31 outings (two starts) since Feb. 3, he averaged 17.5 points, 5.0 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 2.9 threes over 32.0 minutes per game while connecting on 41.7 percent of his field-goal attempts from beyond the arc. Dalano Banton, Max Shulga and Baylor Scheierman will all handle more responsibilities against Orlando in Pritchard's absence.

items.headline: Pritchard is listed as doubtful for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Magic due to left foot plantar fasciitis, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: The Celtics locked their spot as the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference after their blowout win against the Pelicans on Friday. With nothing to play for Sunday, Boston will rest its entire starting lineup, and it looks like Pritchard will also not play against Orlando. If that's indeed the case, Pritchard will end the 2025-26 regular season averaging career highs in points (17.0), assists (5.2), rebounds (3.9) and minutes (32.4). Max Shulga, Dalano Banton, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and other deep rotational players for the Celtics should all see extended action Sunday.

items.headline: Pritchard ended Friday's 144-118 victory over the Pelicans with 21 points (7-14 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, 10 assists and one steal in 30 minutes.
items.story: Pritchard posted his fifth double-double of the season Friday, taking advantage of some extra usage left behind by the absence of Jayson Tatum (Achilles). Over his last seven contests, Pritchard has averaged 17.0 points, 4.6 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 3.3 three-pointers in 29.7 minutes per game while shooting 50.0 percent from deep.

items.headline: Pritchard posted 23 points (10-20 FG, 3-8 3Pt), six assists and three rebounds across 36 minutes in Thursday's 112-106 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: With Jaylen Brown (Achilles) out, Pritchard was far more aggressive on the offensive end Thursday. The 28-year-old guard led Boston's second unit in points and was the team's second-leading scorer behind Jayson Tatum (24), who struggled with efficiency. Pritchard also finished second on the club in assists and three-pointers made.

items.headline: Pritchard racked up 12 points (4-8 FG, 4-7 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists in 30 minutes during Tuesday's 113-102 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Pritchard scored double digits for the 12th straight game, albeit only just. With Boston now mostly healthy, Pritchard has reverted to a bench role, although his playing time still reflects that of a starter. While he hasn't necessarily taken any major steps forward this season, Pritchard has become a reliable producer, averaging 16.9 points, 5.1 assists and 2.6 three-pointers through 77 games.

items.headline: Pritchard won't start Monday's game against the Hawks, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: With Derrick White (knee) back in the lineup, Pritchard will retreat to the second unit. The 28-year-old guard has averaged 19.6 points, 3.6 assists and 3.2 rebounds across 31.6 minutes per game over his last five outings off the bench.

items.headline: Pritchard amassed 28 points (10-18 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds, six assists and one steal over 37 minutes during Sunday's 114-99 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Pritchard has played very well filling in for Jaylen Brown (Achilles) over the past two games, scoring a total of 64 points on 23-for-41 shooting to go with eight triples and 10 assists. If Derrick White (knee) and Brown are forced to spend another game on the inactive list Monday, Pritchard will make for an attractive target in daily fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Pritchard will start Sunday's game against the Hornets, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: With Derrick White (knee) out, Pritchard will enter the first unit Sunday. As a starter this season (49 games), he has averaged 16.7 points, 5.2 assists and 4.3 rebounds in 32.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Pritchard posted 36 points (13-23 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds and four assists across 35 minutes in Friday's 109-102 win over the Hawks.
items.story: With Jaylen Brown (Achilles) sidelined, Pritchard saw increased usage and erupted for a game-high 36 points. The 28-year-old guard has been somewhat inconsistent as a scorer in March, though he has now scored in double figures in six straight games. Friday's contest marked the first time he has reached the 20-point threshold since March 2 and his first time dropping at least 30 since Feb. 22. He also knocked down at least six triples for the sixth time this season while leading the second unit in assists and rebounds.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams will be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a left quad contusion. His next chance to play will come Thursday against Miami. Will Richard and De'Anthony Melton could see a bump in minutes in Williams' stead.

items.headline: Williams (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams is dealing with a left quadriceps contusion and could sit out the back end of this back-to-back set. If the 26-year-old guard is unable to suit up, Will Richard and De'Anthony Melton could see increased burn.

items.headline: Williams ended with 17 points (7-11 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block across 25 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 124-112 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: The 26-year-old guard played more than 20 minutes for the second time in seven games so far this season, and both times the extra run has come while Stephen Curry (rest) wasn't in the lineup. In those two contests (one start), Williams has averaged 18.5 points, 4.0 assists, 3.0 boards, 2.0 threes and 1.0 steals in 24.5 minutes, giving him some DFS appeal the next time Curry gets a night off.

items.headline: Williams tallied 11 points (4-11 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and an assist across 14 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Williams reached double figures despite playing fewer than 15 minutes, demonstrating an aggressive offensive approach with 11 field-goal attempts. His reserve role remains the main obstacle to consistent production, but he could be a decent waiver pickup if he gets an expanded role. Williams has scored in double digits in three of his five appearances this season despite shooting 34.1 percent from the floor and 33.3 percent from deep.

items.headline: Williams will come off the bench Monday night against Denver, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Williams will rotate back to the bench with Stephen Curry returning from a rest day Saturday. Williams has totaled 18 points in 27 minutes over his first two games off the bench this season.

items.headline: Williams (back) is available for Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Williams was deemed probable Sunday due to left lower-back soreness, but he's been cleared to play and should see minutes off the bench in the Warriors' backcourt. He started against Phoenix on Saturday in a game where the Warriors rested several starters and posted 20 points with five assists, so he's likely to see a relatively voluminous role with the second unit.

items.headline: Williams is probable for Monday's game against the Nuggets due to left lower back soreness.
items.story: The back issue seems to be new for Williams, but he is expected to play through it Monday. Williams got a spot start Saturday against the Suns due to Golden State resting many players, and he made the most of the opportunity, recording 20 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 8-11 FT), five assists, three rebounds and two steals in 24 minutes.

items.headline: Williams accumulated 20 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 8-11 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals over 24 minutes during Saturday's 131-122 loss to the Suns.
items.story: With Golden State opting to rest a number of players, Williams was inserted into the starting lineup for the first time this season. He certainly made the most of his opportunity, finishing as one of three Warriors players to score at least 20 points. While this is likely just a one-off, it is worth keeping an eye on Williams' role moving forward. Should Golden State's trajectory continue downward, there is a scenario in which Williams could see more run later in the season.

items.headline: Williams will start Saturday's game against Phoenix, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: With Stephen Curry (rest) out, Williams will draw his first regular-season start with the Warriors. Through two regular-season games, he's averaging 9.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 2.0 steals in 13.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Williams ended with 14 points (3-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 7-7 FT), four rebounds, three assists and three steals over 18 minutes during Wednesday's 127-105 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Williams led the team in steals Wednesday and paced the second unit in scoring. It's hard to gauge how the Warriors will divvy up the minutes in more competitive games, but it looks like Williams will be a regular member of the rotation off the bench.

items.headline: Williams closed Saturday's 111-106 preseason win over the Kings with 19 points (7-8 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), one assist and one steal across 17 minutes.
items.story: After starting Wednesday's loss to Portland, Williams shifted to the second unit Saturday. He still torched the nets off the bench and finished as Golden State's second-leading scorer behind Yaxel Lendeborg (23 points). Williams has scored in double figures in all four of the Warriors' preseason outings thus far, and he's making a strong case for additional minutes to open the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Williams will come off the bench in Saturday's preseason game against the Kings.
items.story: Stephen Curry is back and starting after skipping Wednesday's exhibition, so Williams will return to a reserve role. However, with Curry set to play just the first half of Saturday's exhibition, Williams should still see quality minutes.

items.headline: Williams played 18 minutes in Wednesday's preseason loss to the Trail Blazers, scoring 17 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-4 FT) while adding four assists, three rebounds and one steal.
items.story: Golden State rested most of its key rotation players, leaving Williams as one of the more experienced members of the starting five, and the 26-year-old guard stepped up with an efficient performance. The former Maverick is expected to be a consistent part of the second unit after signing a one-year deal with the Warriors in August.

items.headline: Williams will start in Wednesday's exhibition against the Trail Blazers, Jason Quick of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Warriors are resting nine players for Wednesday's exhibition, so Williams could see major minutes in a starting role. Joining him in the first unit for Wednesday's game will be Will Richard, Malevy Leons, Dalen Terry and Charles Bassey.

items.headline: Williams posted 10 points (3-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, an assist and a steal across 18 minutes during Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Williams hopes to catch on with the Warriors after three seasons with the Mavericks, and although his speed and playmaking are unquestioned, he's buried on the depth chart and unlikely to make an impact. One possible advantage is Stephen Curry's advancing age, which could give him extra possessions in back-to-backs, but Williams is far from fantasy-relevant at this point.

items.headline: Williams has made an early impression on the Warriors with his speed and ability to put pressure on opposing defenses, Monte Poole of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Williams recorded 11 points (4-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal in 16 minutes during Sunday's preseason loss to the Clippers. Coach Steve Kerr has called Williams the fastest player he's coached with Golden State, and his ability to attack in transition and off high pick-and-rolls could give the Warriors a dimension they've lacked in recent seasons.

items.headline: Williams has been impressive during training camp, with head coach Steve Kerr praising his speed and ability as a "defensive pest," Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Kerr called Williams the "fastest guy we've ever had," and he's seemingly made a positive impression with the Warriors thus far after signing a one-year deal with the club in late August. The 26-year-old guard was productive for the Mavericks in 2025-26, averaging 13.0 points, 3.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.9 steals across 22.2 minutes per contest in 66 regular-season outings (15 starts). He'll likely fight to carve out a rotational role and figures to compete for playing time with the likes of De'Anthony Melton, Gary Payton and Will Richard.

items.headline: Williams signed a one-year, $2.6 million deal with the Warriors on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Williams is coming off a successful campaign with the Mavericks. Across 66 regular-season appearances, he averaged 13.0 points, 3.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.5 three-pointers. Minutes won't be easy to come by in Golden State, however, so he's likely going to be an emergency depth option.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is unavailable for Sunday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Williams will now miss a fourth consecutive contest, marking the end of a career-best 2025-26 campaign. Without the 26-year-old, extra minutes will presumably be absorbed by Ryan Nembhard and AJ Johnson. Williams started 15 of his 66 appearances, averaging 13.0 points, 3.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 22.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is doubtful to play Sunday versus Chicago.
items.story: Williams is set to sit out his fourth consecutive game Sunday. Check back for official word on his status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Williams (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Spurs.

With Williams sidelined and Klay Thompson also out with an illness, the Mavericks' depth will be severely tested on Friday. Ryan Nembhard, AJ Johnson, and John Poulakidas should all see increased opportunities.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is listed as doubtful for Friday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Williams is still under the weather and is expected to miss his third straight game Friday. If the 26-year-old guard is ruled out, there would be more minutes available for Ryan Nembhard and John Poulakidas.

items.headline: Williams (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams will miss both halves of this back-to-back set due to an illness, and his next opportunity to play will come Friday in San Antonio. With the 26-year-old point guard out, Ryan Nembhard and AJ Johnson are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Williams didn't play Tuesday against the Clippers, and barring a miracle, he's likely to sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set Wednesday as well. With Williams expected to be out, Ryan Nembhard should be in line to see more minutes in the backcourt.

items.headline: Williams (illness) won't play Tuesday versus the Clippers, Farbod Esnaashari of SI.com reports.
items.story: With Williams unavailable, Ryan Nembhard and AJ Johnson will have a chance to get back into the rotation. For now, Williams should be considered questionable for Wednesday's game in Phoenix.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Williams was previously listed as questionable, but it appears he will miss the front end of this back-to-back set. His absence could open things up for Ryan Nembhard in the backcourt.

items.story: Williams put up 13 points in 25 minutes Sunday against the Lakers but is in danger of sitting Tuesday after popping up on the injury report. The Mavericks should have a better idea of his status closer to game time.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Williams was a late addition to the injury report with the probable tag, but now we have official confirmation that he'll be out there. Over the past three games, Williams has delivered averages of 18.7 points, 4.7 assists and 1.7 steals per contest.

items.headline: Williams (illness) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Williams recently popped up on the injury report because of an illness. However, the probable designation suggests he is expected to suit up versus Los Angeles. If the 26-year-old suffers a setback and can't play, Ryan Nembhard will likely see more minutes from off the bench.

items.headline: Williams ended with 23 points (7-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-11 FT), two rebounds, five assists and two steals across 26 minutes during Friday's 138-127 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Williams reached the 20-point mark for the first time since Jan. 24, and this was his best scoring output since he delivered 26 points in a loss to the Warriors on Christmas Day. Williams has been very productive off the bench and has scored in double digits in 11 of his last 12 outings with the second unit, a stretch in which he's averaging 12.8 points, 2.9 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game.

items.headline: Williams accumulated 15 points (4-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and two steals over 28 minutes during Monday's 124-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Williams has been a steady contributor off the bench for the Mavericks, and he's scored in double digits in all but one of his 17 appearances since the All-Star break. The bench role limits his upside a bit, but Williams can fill the stat sheet every time he steps on the hardwood, so he's a valuable option to target in most formats if he's available.

items.headline: Williams (concussion) supplied 11 points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-7 FT), six assists and two rebounds across 19 minutes during Wednesday's 142-135 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Williams made his return to action after missing the previous three games due to a concussion. Though head coach Jason Kidd has been reluctant to use Williams as a full-time starter, the fifth-year guard still looks poised to remain a regular part of the rotation as the season winds down. While his production of late has been adequate, Williams doesn't necessarily need to be viewed as a must-roster player. Since moving back to a bench role March 6, Williams has averaged 10.9 points, 3.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds, 0.8 blocks, 0.6 three-pointers and 0.5 steals in 19.1 minutes per contest while shooting 47.1 percent from the field.

items.headline: Williams (concussion) is available for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets, Brad Townsend of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Williams will return from a three-game absence due to a concussion. His return could spell fewer minutes for Ryan Nembhard and Klay Thompson.

items.story: Williams has missed Dallas' last three games while in the league's concussion protocol, though he has been upgraded to questionable and could return in Denver. If the 26-year-old guard remains sidelined, Ryan Nembhard and Klay Thompson will likely see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Williams (concussion) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Williams will miss a third consecutive game as he remains in the league's concussion protocol. Ryan Nembhard figures to see his minutes tick up as a result, and Williams' next chance to return will come Wednesday against the Nuggets.

items.story: Williams is in danger of missing his third straight contest. If he isn't available, Ryan Nembhard will likely absorb most of the minutes from off the bench.

items.headline: Williams (concussion) is out for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Williams was unable to shake his doubtful tag for this contest. With this news, Max Christie and Ryan Nembhard could be a bit more involved for Dallas.

items.headline: Williams is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Hawks due to a concussion.
items.story: The guard is unlikely to pass the league's concussion protocol in time for Wednesday's action. With Williams likely sidelined, Max Christie is in the streaming mix in shallow fantasy leagues and Ryan Nembhard in deeper setups.

items.story: Williams' night ended prematurely after taking a hit to the side of his head. The guard had a minimal impact in Monday's contest, though it's unclear when he sustained the hit, and it likely played a role in him logging just five minutes. items.story: Williams has scored in double figures in 12 straight appearances, missing only one game during that stretch while averaging 15.0 points, 4.6 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.2 stocks with 51/31/79 shooting splits. He's come off the bench in four straight contests, but his 28 minutes Thursday snapped a three-game streak of playing fewer than 20 minutes, and it was his most playing time since Feb. 24.

items.headline: Grimes contributed seven points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds and four assists in 23 minutes during Monday's 138-117 win over the Heat.
items.story: It's been a rather disappointing start to the year for Grimes, who had been penciled in as a starter for the Lakers during the preseason but has since watched Matisse Thybulle win the job. Grimes has scored in double digits just once in his past six appearances, averaging only 8.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 26.3 minutes per game for the season.

items.headline: Grimes won't start Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Luka Doncic (back) is in the lineup following a one-game absence, pushing Grimes to the second unit. In four appearances off the bench this season, he's averaging 7.0 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists across 24.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Grimes finished Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers with 23 points (7-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 9-11 FT), five assists, four steals and three rebounds across 38 minutes.
items.story: With Luka Doncic (back) unavailable for the second leg of this back-to-back set, Grimes got the starting nod for the first time this season. The 26-year-old shooting guard led the Lakers in minutes en route to team- and season-high marks in points, assists and steals. He's now scored in double figures in three of the Lakers' five regular-season games thus far.

items.headline: Grimes will start Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Luka Doncic (back) sidelined, Grimes will get the starting nod for the first time this season. Through four regular-season outings, he's averaging 7.0 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 24.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Grimes provided three points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and one assist in 20 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 win over Utah.
items.story: After scoring in double figures in each of the Lakers' first two contests to begin 2026-27, Grimes deferred to Collin Sexton, who finished with 13 points in 20 minutes off the bench. The 26-year-old is averaging 8.7 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists in 26.0 minutes a night to begin his tenure in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Grimes will come off the bench in Friday's game against Denver, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Grimes is projected to start at small forward to open the season. He will come off the bench Friday in the final preseason game before the Opening Night meeting with the Warriors on Wednesday.

items.headline: Grimes supplied nine points (4-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), six assists, one steal and one block across 26 minutes in Tuesday's 101-89 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Grimes stayed in the starting lineup and did more as a distributor, posting a preseason-high six assists, though his three turnovers were part of a 29-turnover night for the Lakers. He has started all four exhibitions and appears set to open the season alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves.

items.headline: Grimes supplied 12 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two steals in 29 minutes during Thursday's 114-110 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Grimes reached double figures for the third straight preseason game, though six turnovers took some shine off his night. He's started all three exhibitions after signing a four-year, $60 million deal, and it's looking increasingly likely that coach JJ Redick will roll with him as one of the starting wings alongside Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler.

items.headline: Grimes logged 12 points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three assists, a rebound and a steal in 23 minutes during Tuesday's 124-98 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Grimes is in an interesting spot after coming over from Philadelphia, as the starting wing role seems ripe for the taking. Inserting Grimes there would put the Lakers at a height disadvantage against most teams, which is why rookie Cameron Carr will immediately enter the conversation at the position. Los Angeles' lineup scheme is unique, with Luka Doncic assuming a multi-pronged role in the offense, and while pairing Grimes and Austin Reaves with the All-Star isn't entirely unreasonable, there's no question that it's the Lakers' most uncertain position heading into the regular season.

items.headline: Grimes finished with 16 points (5-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and one assist in 19 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Grimes drew the start with Austin Reaves (ankle) and Collin Sexton (lower body) unavailable and didn't commit a turnover during an efficient Lakers debut. The 26-year-old is competing for a starting spot and should have a significant role regardless of where he ultimately lands in the rotation.

items.headline: Grimes wants to establish himself as a starter during training camp, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: According to Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com, Grimes also said that he takes pride in his defense and will be ready to guard the opposing team's best player on a nightly basis, which should help him secure a regular starting role. Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler are all essentially locked in as starters to begin the season, though head coach JJ Redick will have training camp and the preseason to evaluate the final two spots. Grimes is coming off a productive 2025-26 season with Philadelphia, averaging 13.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 0.9 steals in 29.4 minutes per game across 75 regular-season outings (19 starts). He shot a career-low 33.4 percent from three-point range last season but is still a career 36.6 percent shooter from deep.

items.headline: Grimes is viewed as a lock to occupy one of the Lakers' starting spots entering training camp, according to Jovan Buha of Buha's Block.
items.story: Grimes is expected to join Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler as four established members of the starting five, leaving only one position unsettled. The offseason addition should complement Doncic and Reaves with his perimeter defense and ability to operate away from the ball, putting Grimes in line for a substantial role in his first season with Los Angeles.

items.headline: Grimes figures to have an opportunity to fill the two-way role the Lakers need on the perimeter, with his defensive ability potentially being just as important as his production on the offensive end, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Grimes is an athletic, aggressive guard capable of applying pressure at the point of attack, while his physicality and activity should give Los Angeles another option against opposing perimeter scorers. Grimes' willingness to attack offensively also adds another dimension beyond his spot-up shooting, though his overall impact could depend heavily on the makeup of the starting five.

items.headline: Grimes agreed to a four-year, $60 million deal with the Lakers on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The Lakers continue to add some firepower to their roster after acquiring Walker Kessler, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Sexton. Grimes will likely be a key part of the second unit in Los Angeles with his ability to play multiple positions. During the 2025-26 regular season, Grimes averaged 13.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 0.9 steals in 29.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Grimes posted six points (2-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt) and one block in 16 minutes during Sunday's 144-114 loss to the Knicks in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Following an impressive finish to 2024-25 with Philadelphia, Grimes ended up settling for a one-year deal with the 76ers for 2025-26 and turned in an up-and-down campaign. It remains to be seen if he'll command a multi-year deal ahead of 2026-27, whether it be with Philadelphia or elsewhere. Over 75 regular-season games, Grimes averaged 13.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 0.9 steals and 1.7 three-pointers in 29.4 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Grimes produced seven points (1-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal over 24 minutes during Wednesday's 108-102 loss to the Knicks in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Grimes led the bench in minutes once again. However, he didn't do much with the opportunity, contributing only seven points. With a combined 12 points in the last two games, the 25-year-old will look to turn it around in Game 3 on Friday night. While Grimes can get hot from a production standpoint, his volatility on the scoring end doesn't make him an appealing option for fantasy managers, even with the potential for more offensive opportunities if Joel Embiid (hip, ankle) misses another game.

items.headline: Grimes produced three points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds and four assists over 26 minutes during Saturday's 109-100 win over the Celtics in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Grimes logged 26 minutes off the bench in this contest, more than the rest of the reserves combined. However, he scored only three points, his second-lowest mark of the postseason. The 25-year-old averaged 7.1 points, 3.4 rebound and 2.3 assists across 22.4 minutes in the series with the Celtics. While Grimes should continue to get plenty of work in the second round versus the Knicks, his lack of consistency on the scoring end is an issue for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Grimes ended with 18 points (5-8 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds and one block over 24 minutes during Tuesday's 113-97 victory over Boston in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Grimes built on his previous effort, scoring 18 points Tuesday, the most he has scored thus far in the playoffs. After struggling in the opening three games, he has now notched a total of 30 points in his past two appearances, providing the 76ers with a much-needed offensive threat off the bench. He will look to continue on an upward trend when the two teams meet again in Game 6, this time on Philadelphia's home court.

items.headline: Grimes recorded two points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one block in 15 minutes during Friday's 108-100 loss to the Celtics in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Grimes has chosen the worst time to go cold from the floor, having now scored a total of just 15 points during this series. During that three-game span, he has averaged just 5.0 points and 1.0 three-pointers in 20.1 minutes per contest. If Philadelphia hopes to force the series into a sixth or even seventh game, the team will likely need more from Grimes.

items.headline: Grimes logged six points (2-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one block over 21 minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 victory over the Celtics in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Grimes continues to be more of a passenger than a valuable contributor, scoring no more than seven points for the sixth time in his past eight games. While this was an impressive road victory, Grimes may have to find something on the offensive end if Philadelphia hopes to push Boston all the way. The two teams will now head to Philadelphia for Game 3 on Friday.

items.headline: Grimes ended with 20 points (7-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Sunday's 126-106 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: With most of the first unit taking a seat in the second half, Grimes was able to take over the backcourt and show his stuff. Grimes would likely be a starter for most teams in the league, and he displayed his playmaking in 19 starting appearances this season. We may not see much from Grimes in Tuesday's Play-In Game against Orlando, but he'll provide solid second-unit support when needed. Grimes finishes the regular season with averages of 13.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 0.9 steals over 75 games played.

items.headline: Grimes supplied 20 points (7-16 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds and one steal over 26 minutes off the bench during Thursday's 113-102 loss to Houston.
items.story: It's the first time since March 21 that the fifth-year guard has scored at least 20 points. Grimes has returned to the second unit with Tyrese Maxey back in action, and over the last seven games off the bench, he's averaging just 9.4 points, 3.0 boards, 1.4 assists and 1.1 threes in 25.0 minutes.

items.headline: Grimes contributed 11 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and four assists in 32 minutes during Monday's 119-109 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Grimes logged 32 minutes in the loss, continuing to play a meaningful role despite the fact that Philadelphia is running with a relatively injury-free rotation. While it does appear as though he could flirt with 28 minutes per game moving forward, his fantasy value is likely to be limited to streaming, as opposed to being a must-roster player.

items.headline: Grimes won't start Saturday's game against the Hornets, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: With Tyrese Maxey (finger) back in the lineup following a 10-game absence, Grimes will retreat to the second unit. Over six appearances off the bench since the All-Star break, the 25-year-old guard has averaged 12.2 points, 2.5 assists and 2.2 rebounds across 26.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Grimes logged 13 points (5-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists, three steals and three blocks over 31 minutes during the 76ers' 157-137 win over the Bulls on Wednesday.
items.story: Grimes filled up the box score in Wednesday's blowout win, especially on the defensive end of the floor, where he set a season high with six combined steals and blocks. He took a bit of a step back offensively, scoring less than 15 points for just the third time in his last 10 outings, but that was to be expected due to the returns of both Joel Embiid (oblique) and Paul George (suspension). Even as the fourth option, Grimes demonstrated his value to the Sixers on both ends of the floor as the team looks to improve its standing ahead of the Eastern Conference playoffs.

items.headline: Grimes (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Bulls, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: An illness prevented Grimes from playing against the Thunder on Monday. The fifth-year pro has recovered enough to return Wednesday, and while he's started in each of his last 11 outings, it's unclear what his role will look like moving forward due to the return of Paul George from a 25-game suspension.

items.headline: Grimes is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Bulls with an illness.
items.story: After missing Monday's loss to the Thunder, Grimes is looking to keep his absence to a one-game minimum. items.headline: Grimes (illness) won't play Monday against Oklahoma City, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
