items.headline: Grimes closed with 25 points (9-15 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), five rebounds and four assists across 36 minutes during Saturday's 126-116 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Grimes has embraced the role of being one of the 76ers' primary offensive weapons alongside VJ Edgecombe due to the absence of star players like Tyrese Maxey (finger), Joel Embiid (oblique) and Paul George (suspension). The numbers back Grimes, as he has scored at least 25 points in four of his last five appearances. Since moving to the starting lineup on March 3, Grimes is averaging 20.1 points per game, and he should continue to handle a sizable workload on offense as long as the aforementioned star trio remains out.

items.headline: Grimes logged 27 points (10-20 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds and seven assists across 32 minutes during Thursday's 139-118 victory over the Kings.
items.story: The fifth-year guard continues to shine for the injury-depleted 76ers. Grimes has started 10 straight games and scored in double digits in nine straight, averaging 21.6 points, 4.4 boards, 3.2 assists, 1.3 threes and 1.0 steals in 34.1 minutes over that latter stretch.

items.headline: Grimes chipped in 31 points (11-22 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 40 minutes during Sunday's 109-103 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The 76ers were without star players Tyrese Maxey (finger), Joel Embiid (oblique) and Paul George (suspension), but Grimes stepped up and not only carried Philadelphia to victory, but he posted a season-high mark in scoring. Grimes has scored 20-plus points in four of his last six appearances, a stretch in which he's averaging 23.2 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game.

items.headline: Grimes posted 28 points (10-22 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 7-7 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal over 34 minutes during Saturday's 104-97 win over the Nets on Saturday.
items.story: The Nets attempted to make a late run in the fourth quarter, but Grimes kept the 76ers afloat with 15 of his game-high 28 points coming in the fourth quarter. Grimes has struggled from three-point range of late (2-for-18 from beyond the arc over his last three outings), but the fifth-year pro is working in an elevated role on offense due to the absences of Tyrese Maxey (finger), Kelly Oubre (elbow) and Paul George (suspension). Grimes has started each of the Sixers' last seven games, and over that span he has averaged 18.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.0 steals over 33.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Grimes logged 23 points (6-16 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 11-13 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals over 35 minutes during the 76ers' 139-129 win over the Grizzlies on Tuesday.
items.story: Grimes struggled from deep, but he was rewarded for his aggressiveness with a season-high 11 made free throws. He's scored at least 23 points in two of his last three outings, and the fifth-year pro should continue to operate in an expanded role due to the absences of Tyrese Maxey (finger), Joel Embiid (oblique) and Paul George (suspension).

items.headline: Spencer won't start Monday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Ty Jerome (back) is back in the lineup, sending Spencer to the second unit. The sharpshooter has averaged 8.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 0.8 steals while shooting 58.8 percent from downtown across 18.0 minutes per game in five appearances off the bench this season.

items.headline: Spencer closed Saturday's 136-105 victory over the Kings with 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt), five rebounds, 13 assists and one steal in 25 minutes.
items.story: Spencer made his first start of the regular season Saturday due to the absence of Ty Jerome (back). Spencer answered the call by tying a career high in assists en route to his first double-double of the season and seventh of his three-year NBA career. He would likely revert to a bench role against the Pelicans on Monday if Jerome is cleared to return.

items.headline: Spencer is in the Grizzlies' starting lineup against the Kings on Saturday.
items.story: Spencer has come off the bench in each of the first five games of the regular season, but he'll get his first start of the 2026-27 campaign Saturday due to the absence of Ty Jerome (back). Spencer is averaging 8.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.0 threes and 0.8 steals over 18.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer produced eight points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 23 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 win over Portland.
items.story: Spencer registered season highs in both boards and dimes Thursday, leading the second unit in the latter category. Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal believes Spencer has leapfrogged Scotty Pippen in the backcourt rotation hierarchy, so Spencer's stock in fantasy looks to be very much on the rise.

items.headline: Spencer posted 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 16 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 win over Sacramento.
items.story: With Ty Jerome taking the league by storm in the early going, Spencer is falling behind in the race for minutes at point guard. Spencer should continue battling with Scotty Pippen for backup playing time.

items.headline: Spencer tallied 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-3 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 19 minutes in Friday's 117-98 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Spencer was perfect from three-point range off the bench, posting his best scoring night of the preseason. The third-year guard started 20 games for Memphis last season, but he's expected to begin the 2026-27 campaign in the second unit behind Cedric Coward.

items.headline: Spencer finished with eight points (2-3 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 14 minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason win over Atlanta.
items.story: Spencer came off the bench and shared the floor with Scotty Pippen for a portion of the contest, continuing an experiment Memphis utilized during training camp. Spencer is among several players competing for starting and rotation opportunities and offers valuable shooting after hitting 44.8 percent of his threes during the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Spencer is in the mix for a spot in the Grizzlies' starting five to begin the 2026-27 season, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen are competing for the starting point guard job with Ja Morant now in Portland, though there's also a battle for starting spots on the wings in Memphis. Cedric Coward, Jerami Grant and Jaylen Wells are all competing with Spencer for a role in the first unit. The 26-year-old shot an impressive 44.8 percent from beyond the arc in 2025-26, averaging 11.1 points and 2.0 triples per game across 72 regular-season games (20 starts). Spencer also averaged 5.6 assists per tilt and could operate as a secondary playmaker in the Grizzlies' starting five. Regardless, he should continue seeing a sizable role for a rebuilding Memphis squad.

items.headline: Spencer (back) should have a significant role next season after the Grizzlies traded Ja Morant to the Trail Blazers this offseason.
items.story: Memphis has a three-way competition brewing for No. 1 point guard duties ahead of training camp, featuring Scotty Pippen (toe), Ty Jerome (ankle) and Spencer. Even if he fails to seize a starting position to open the year, Spencer is far more likely than D'Angelo Russell to play meaningful minutes in the backcourt off the bench for the rebuilding Grizzlies. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (finger) also agreed to a buyout with Memphis on Saturday, further improving Spencer's chances of claiming a big role with the second unit.

items.headline: Spencer (back) will not play in Sunday's season finale against the Rockets.
items.story: Spencer will end his campaign with three consecutive absences. Overall, it was a breakout season for the second-year pro, who set career highs essentially across the board. In his 23.8 minutes per game, Spencer averaged 11.1 points, 5.6 assists and 2.5 rebounds.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is listed as out ahead of Friday's game in Utah.
items.story: Spencer has missed three of the Grizzlies' last four games. At this point, it would be surprising to see him suit up for the season finale versus the Rockets on Sunday. With Walter Clayton (hip) and Javon Small (thigh) both questionable, Jahmai Mashack and Adama Bal may be the featured options out of the backcourt.

items.headline: Spencer (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Spencer continues to deal with lower-back soreness and will miss his third game this month. His next chance to play will come Friday in Utah. In the meantime, Lucas Williamson, Adama Bal and Rayan Rupert are candidates for increased playing time for the injury-riddled Grizzlies.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is available for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Spencer is suiting up for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Over his last nine appearances (three starts), Spencer has averaged 9.8 points, 5.7 assists, 1.9 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 23.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game in Milwaukee.
items.story: Spencer is in danger of missing his second straight game, which could result in major minutes for Adama Bal. Check back for official word on Spencer's status closer to Sunday's tipoff.

items.headline: Spencer is out for Friday's game against the Raptors due to low back soreness.
items.story: Spencer has put together two straight solid performances, but he'll be forced to the sidelines Friday after picking up a back injury. Jahmai Mashack and Walter Clayton could pick up increased minutes as a result of Spencer's absence.

items.headline: Spencer will start Monday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Spencer didn't play in Saturday's 125-124 win over the Bulls. However, he will suit up Monday and make his first start since March 13. In 17 starts this season, the 2024 No. 53 overall pick has averaged 11.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 8.4 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.7 steals across 29.1 minutes.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is not listed on the injury report for Monday's matchup with the Suns.
items.story: Spencer is set to return from a one-game absence, and he should see quality minutes with Ty Jerome (ankle) out and Javon Small (back) not expected to play. Spencer has handed out a total of 17 dimes over his past two appearances, while committing just two turnovers.

items.headline: Spencer (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: As expected, Spencer will miss Saturday's contest due to lower-back soreness, and his next opportunity to play will come Monday against Phoenix. The Grizzlies will be extremely shorthanded against Chicago, so Rayan Rupert, Jahmai Mashack (ankle/nose) and DeJon Jarreau will likely see increased minutes.

items.headline: Spencer (ankle) is doubtful for Saturday's game against Chicago.
items.story: The Grizzlies might be running with a skeleton crew Saturday. With Walter Clayton (ankle) questionable and Ty Jerome (ankle) out, Javon Small may be running things in the backcourt to begin the contest. DeJon Jarreau and Rayan Rupert might also need to get more involved off the bench.

items.headline: Spencer accumulated 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), three rebounds, 10 assists, one block and three steals over 29 minutes during Friday's 119-109 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Spencer missed all six of his shot attempts during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, but he scored efficiently in this one and got some extra minutes with Ty Jerome (ankle) missing another game. As long as Jerome is sidelined, Spencer should be a reliable source of dimes.

items.headline: Spencer (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Spencer was held out of Monday's loss to Atlanta due to back soreness, though he's set to return to action Wednesday. Over his last five appearances (one start), the second-year guard has averaged 10.0 points, 4.2 assists, 1.8 three-pointers, 1.6 rebounds and 1.0 steals across 23.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is out for Monday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Spencer has officially been downgraded to out due to back soreness. The Grizzlies will be awfully thin in the backcourt Monday with Spencer, Cedric Coward (personal), Javon Small (back) and Jahmai Mashack (ankle) all unavailable. It'll presumably be up to Rayan Rupert, DeJon Jarreau and Walter Clayton to pick up the slack.

items.headline: Spencer is doubtful for Monday's game in Atlanta due to lower-back soreness.
items.story: It looks like Spencer will be joining Ja Morant (elbow) and Jahmai Mashack (ankle) on the inactive list for Monday's game, which should result in more minutes for Walter Clayton and Javon Small. Check back for official confirmation on Spencer's status closer to Monday's tipoff.

items.headline: Spencer is not in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Spencer started Friday against the Pistons and poured in an efficient 19 points but will revert to a reserve role Monday as the Grizzlies are slated to start Walter Clayton, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Rayan Rupert and Olivier-Maxence Prosper. Spencer has come off the bench in 46 of his 63 appearances this season, averaging 11.5 points, 4.4 assists and 2.3 rebounds in 22.2 minutes per contest as a reserve.

items.headline: Spencer will start against Detroit on Friday.
items.story: With Jaylen Wells (shoulder) out, Spencer will step into the starting lineup for the third time since the All-Star break. As a starter this season (16 games), the sharpshooter has averaged 10.8 points, 8.6 assists and 3.8 rebounds across 28.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is available for Friday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Spencer is no longer on the injury report after missing the front end of this back-to-back set. Spencer may be hard to trust in fantasy hoops, given Memphis' volatile rotations and injury reports, but Walter Clayton (ankle) is doubtful Friday, Scotty Pippen (toe) is done for the season, and it's unclear when or if Ja Morant (elbow) will suit up again, opening the door for Spencer to see decent minutes as a resreve against Detroit.

items.headline: Spencer (back) is out for Thursday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Spencer was tagged as questionable on the Grizzlies' injury report leading up to Thursday's clash, and he'll join several of his teammates in sitting out against Dallas. Memphis will be forced to lean on Javon Small, Jahmai Mashack and Rayan Rupert in the backcourt as a result.

items.headline: Spencer is questionable for Thursday's game against the Mavericks due to lower-back soreness.
items.story: Spencer is at risk of missing the first leg of this back-to-back. The Grizzlies could need each of Javon Small, Jahmai Mashack and Rayan Rupert to play a significant role in the backcourt Thursday.

items.headline: Spencer is not in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Ty Jerome (calf) is back in the starting five for the Grizzlies on Tuesday, forcing Spencer to the second unit. Spencer has averaged 12.3 points, 4.0 assists and 3.0 rebounds in 22.9 minutes per tilt in his last six games off the bench.

items.headline: Spencer will start Monday's game against the Nets.
items.story: The Grizzlies have only eight players available for the front end of this back-to-back set, so Spencer will get the starting nod for just the second time since the beginning of February. As a starter this season (15 games), the sharpshooter has averaged 11.1 points, 8.6 assists and 3.9 rebounds across 29.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer recorded 10 points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one steal over 24 minutes during Tuesday's 117-110 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: The Grizzlies are expected to be very shorthanded for the second leg of this back-to-back set Wednesday against Portland, catapulting Spencer onto the streaming radar. Across 15 fill-in starts this season, he's averaging 11.1 points, 8.6 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 0.7 steals and 1.9 three-pointers.

items.headline: Spencer supplied 25 points (9-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal across 25 minutes in Friday's 124-105 win over Dallas.
items.story: After totaling 12 points on 31.3 percent shooting from the field over his previous three outings, Spencer bounced back with a game-high 25 points in this one. He was the only player to score more than 16 and reached the 20-point mark for the second time this month. The sharpshooter hasn't logged fewer than 20 minutes since Jan. 18 and will likely continue to see significant playing time regardless of whether he starts. While Friday's scoring outburst is encouraging, Spencer had failed to reach double-digit points in five of his previous six appearances entering the contest.

items.headline: Spencer is not in the Grizzlies' starting lineup against the Warriors on Wednesday.
items.story: Spencer started in Monday's loss to the Kings, when he finished with seven points, three rebounds, three assists and one steal over 22 minutes. He'll come off the bench for Wednesday's contest while the Grizzlies go with a starting five of Ty Jerome, Jaylen Wells, Javon Small, GG Jackson and Olivier-Maxence Prosper.

items.headline: Spencer is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Spencer will draw his first start since Jan. 30 with Cedric Coward (knee) still sidelined. In 14 starts this season, the 25-year-old is averaging 11.4 points, 9.0 assists and 3.9 rebounds in 29.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Spencer supplied two points (1-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt), four rebounds and four assists over 24 minutes during Monday's 114-113 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Spencer matched his season low with two points, continuing to play off the bench behind Ty Jerome. Despite what has been a breakout campaign, Spencer's long-term fantasy value remains somewhat of a mystery. He now has plenty of competition for playing time, having to deal with the likes of Jerome, Scottie Pippen, Walter Clayton (calf) and eventually, Ja Morant (elbow). Spencer remains a soft hold in standard formats, although it wouldn't be surprising to see him let go in a few spots, given the uncertainty.

items.headline: Spencer (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Spencer missed Saturday's game due to a right ankle injury, but he will return to the lineup Monday. Over his last five games, he holds averages of 15.0 points, 4.6 assists and 2.2 rebounds in 25.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Spencer (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Portland, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Spencer will miss the tail end of the Grizzlies' back-to-back set due to a sore right ankle. The 25-year-old's absence could mean more opportunities for Walter Clayton, Jahmai Mashack or Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Spencer's next chance to play will come Monday at Golden State.

items.headline: Spencer (ankle) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Spencer is dealing with right ankle soreness and is in jeopardy of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set. If the 25-year-old guard isn't cleared to suit up, Walter Clayton, Jahmai Mashack and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope would likely see increased playing time, especially if Cedric Coward (shoulder) and Jaylen Wells (shoulder) are downgraded from doubtful to out.

items.headline: Spencer amassed 18 points (7-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five assists, one block and two steals across 26 minutes off the bench during Friday's 135-115 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The second-year guard led Memphis in scoring on the night, coming off the bench for a fourth straight game. The team's backcourt is getting crowded even with Ja Morant (elbow) still sidelined, as Ty Jerome (calf) made his season debut Jan. 31 and Scotty Pippen (toe) followed Friday, and the Grizzlies seem more comfortable having Spencer in the second unit. Over the last three games in that role, he's averaged 18.0 points, 5.0 assists, 2.7 threes and 2.3 boards in 26.0 minutes.

items.headline: Spencer won't start against the Timberwolves on Saturday.
items.story: With Ty Jerome (calf) entering the starting five in his regular-season debut, Spencer will slide to the second unit. In 31 appearances off the bench so far this season, the sharpshooter has averaged 11.9 points, 4.1 assists, 2.4 three-pointers and 2.1 rebounds while shooting 50.7 percent from downtown in 21.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Spencer contributed 16 points (6-7 FG, 4-4 3Pt), one rebound and three assists over 24 minutes during Friday's 114-106 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Spencer was uber-efficient Friday evening, with his first, and only miss, not coming until midway through the fourth quarter. The sophomore guard has been heating up over the past four games, churning out top-80 value behind averages of 11.5 points, 8.3 assists and 2.0 triples per contest.

items.headline: Spencer finished with five points (1-5 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, 13 assists, one block and one steal in 27 minutes during Monday's 108-99 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Spencer matched his season-best mark of 13 assists, a figure he's reached three times this campaign. This wasn't Spencer's best night shooting the ball, but he looks poised to have some solid fantasy appeal in the absence of Ja Morant (elbow). Across 12 starts this season, Spencer holds averages of 11.7 points, 9.8 assists, 4.5 rebounds and 1.9 three-pointers in 30.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hopkins won't start Wednesday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: The rookie forward started the last two games in Cameron Johnson's (ankle) absence, though it'll be Trevon Brazile who replaces Johnson in the first unit Wednesday. Hopkins is still likely to see meaningful burn with the Nuggets shorthanded.

items.headline: Hopkins had 13 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 31 minutes during Monday's 134-114 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Hopkins delivered an efficient scoring performance in his starting role, reaching double figures for Denver while committing zero turnovers. However, the forward offered little production outside the scoring column and finished without a steal or block. Hopkins' substantial playing time is encouraging, but he'll need to contribute more consistently across multiple categories to establish reliable fantasy value.

items.headline: Hopkins will start Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: With Cameron Johnson (ankle) sidelined, Hopkins will draw his first career start. The rookie second-rounder has logged just two minutes over one appearance so far this season.

items.headline: Hopkins signed a two-way contract with Denver on Wednesday.
items.story: Hopkins was the No. 49 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. With this transaction, he will be allowed to develop at his own pace with a lot of reps in the G League.

items.headline: Hopkins (rest) won't play in Sunday's Summer League game against the Raptors, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Hopkins will sit out the Nuggets' Summer League finale. Over four Las Vegas Summer League appearances, he averaged 18.0 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.5 steals and 0.8 blocks in 25.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hopkins finished with 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and two steals in 27 minutes during Thursday's 108-101 loss to Portland.
items.story: Hopkins shot the basketball with efficiency Thursday and tied Trevon Brazile for the team lead in rebounds. He's provided solid production for the Nuggets lately, scoring in double figures while racking up seven or more boards in each of his last three Summer League appearances.

items.headline: Hopkins notched 14 points (6-14 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one steal in 27 minutes during Tuesday's 106-103 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: Hopkins continues to play well in Las Vegas, reaching double figures in scoring while doing a nice job on the glass. The second-round pick is an intriguing prospect, but it'll be tough for him to carve out a rotation role while Cameron Johnson and Aaron Gordon remain healthy.

items.headline: Hopkins produced 16 points (6-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 24 minutes in Saturday's 101-82 Summer League win over Minnesota.
items.story: Hopkins came up empty from beyond the arc but was otherwise excellent in Denver's lopsided victory. Of his seven rebounds, three came on the offensive glass. After pouring in 24 points Friday, the second-round rookie is off to an encouraging start in the Las Vegas Summer League.

items.headline: Hopkins totaled 24 points (9-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-6 FT), four rebounds, three steals and two blocks over 26 minutes during Friday's 97-86 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Rockets.
items.story: The 2026 second-round pick led the Nuggets' Summer League squad in scoring, and he racked up five stocks in just 26 minutes of play. Hopkins will look to keep rolling Saturday versus the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Hopkins was selected by the Nuggets with the No. 49 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Hopkins made stops at Kentucky and Providence before spending his final collegiate year at St. John's. He appeared in 37 regular-season games for the Red Storm in 2025-26, averaging 13.6 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 0.3 blocks and 1.1 steals while shooting 36.3 percent from deep across 28.8 minutes. The 24-year-old is a capable scorer and defender, though his limited athleticism might limit his growth as a professional, at least early in his career. The Nuggets are still a championship-caliber club, considering the team is made up of veterans Nikola Jokic, Aaron Gordon and Jamal Murray, among others. As a result, unless Hopkins exceeds expectations throughout Summer League and training camp, he may not see consistent playing time in 2026-27. Still, with Gordon, Murray and Cameron Johnson known for having issues staying off the injury report, Hopkins' services might be needed at some point.

items.headline: Curry posted 34 points (9-21 FG, 5-13 3Pt, 11-12 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Golden State's 116-113 win over Phoenix on Monday.
items.story: Curry dazzled in his return from a one-game absence, as the 38-year-old got the night off in the Warriors' first night of a back-to-back on Sunday. He finished as the team leader in minutes while tallying game-high figures in scoring and three-pointers, helping Golden State earn a fifth straight victory after starting the season 0-3. The Warriors only play two more games this week, so Curry will likely suit up for the remaining tilts, both of which are at home.

items.headline: Curry (rest) is available Monday against the Suns.
items.story: After getting a planned maintenance day Sunday for the first leg of this back-to-back set, Curry is ready to roll. Looking ahead, Golden State's next back-to-back set begins Nov. 18.

items.headline: Curry (rest) won't play Sunday against the Clippers, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Sunday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so Curry will receive a maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Suns. De'Anthony Melton could draw the start sans Curry, and Brandin Podziemski will be more involved in the offense.

items.headline: Curry recorded 31 points (11-23 FG, 8-14 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal over 31 minutes during Friday's 112-95 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Curry passed Dominique Wilkins for 18th place on the NBA's all-time scoring list during the fourth quarter. With Jimmy Butler III (knee) and Moses Moody (knee) sidelined, the Warriors are leaning on Curry even more than usual, and they'll host the Clippers on Sunday.

items.headline: Curry contributed 44 points (11-27 FG, 6-16 3Pt, 16-16 FT), eight rebounds, six assists and two steals across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: After shooting a perfect 8-for-8 from the field for 24 points in his last time out, Curry was far more aggressive hunting his shot Wednesday. Although he didn't deliver his most efficient performance from the floor, the superstar guard got to the charity stripe often and scored his most points since Dec. 14, 2025. He contributed in other areas as well, tying for the team lead in rebounds. Curry also tied for second on the Warriors in assists and tallied multiple steals for the third time across four regular-season appearances thus far.

items.headline: Curry accumulated 24 points (8-8 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals across 27 minutes during Monday's 134-114 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Curry delivered a flawless shooting performance, making all eight of his field-goal attempts and all five of his free throws. The veteran guard scored 21 of his 24 points in the second half, helping Golden State pull away for its first victory of the season. Curry returned to the lineup after sitting out Saturday's loss to Phoenix and should continue serving as the Warriors' primary offensive weapon.

items.headline: Curry (rest) is not listed on the injury report and is available to play Monday against the Nuggets.
items.story: Curry didn't play Saturday against the Suns due to rest, but the star floor general isn't listed on Sunday's injury report, so he should be available to suit up Monday. That means Brandon Williams, who started at point guard versus Phoenix, should return to the bench. Curry is averaging 23.5 points per game despite shooting a mere 29.4 percent from three-point range in his two appearances this season.

items.headline: Curry (rest) won't play Saturday against the Suns.
items.story: Curry told reporters after Friday's loss to the Grizzlies that he will "probably not" play Saturday, and the star floor general won't suit up in the second leg of this back-to-back set. With Curry out, a committee of De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard, Brandon Williams and Gary Payton will cover his minutes in the Warriors' backcourt. Curry will aim to return against the Nuggets on Monday.

items.headline: Curry told reporters after Friday's loss to the Grizzlies that he will "probably not" play against the Suns on Saturday, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Curry played 30 minutes during Friday's game against Memphis, finishing with 24 points (5-15 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 11-11 FT), four assists and two rebounds in a 111-108 loss. Brandin Podziemski (back) won't play Saturday, and if Curry joins him on the bench in street clothes, then De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard, Brandon Williams and Gary Payton would all be candidates to enter the Warriors' starting lineup.

items.headline: Curry tallied 23 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 7-7 FT), two rebounds, an assist and two steals across 21 minutes in Wednesday's 127-105 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Curry scored 20 points in the first half but was held to just three in the third quarter before sitting out the fourth. His limited minutes were largely a product of the lopsided score, though his workload will be worth monitoring after an injury-shortened 2025-26 regular season. Still, this 21-minute outing confirmed that Curry remains Golden State's primary offensive option. His scoring and three-point volume should sustain his fantasy value.

items.headline: Curry (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Curry injured his ankle during practice Sunday. He carried a probable designation ahead of this contest, but he now officially has the green light to suit up. While Curry's presence could mean less work for others, there are still minutes available due to the absence of Brandin Podziemski (back). As a result, De'Anthony Melton and Gui Santos should be more involved than originally projected.

items.headline: Curry (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Curry suffered an ankle injury during Sunday's practice. Head coach Steve Kerr didn't seem overly concerned, though the multi-time All-Star will carry an injury designation ahead of Opening Night versus Los Angeles. If Curry suffers a setback and can't get on the floor, De'Anthony Melton would presumably see even more action, considering Brandin Podziemski (back) has already been ruled out.

items.headline: Curry (ankle) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Lakers, per Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: Head coach Steve Kerr said Monday that the star guard is fine and was a full participant Monday after leaving Sunday's practice with an ankle sprain. It remains to be seen if Curry will carry an injury designation into Wednesday's opener, but fantasy managers can plan on having him available in any event.

items.headline: Curry sustained a right ankle injury during Sunday's practice but is expected to be fine, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Curry exited practice for the locker room Sunday due to a non-contact right ankle injury, but initial indications suggest it is nothing serious. Early reports suggested it could be a right knee injury for Curry, who missed 27 games last season for that same reason, so clarification that it is a minor ankle injury is a positive development. Still, Curry's health will be worth monitoring ahead of Wednesday's regular-season opener.

items.headline: Curry appeared to suffer a right knee injury during Sunday's open practice, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Curry appeared to sustain a non-contact right knee injury before leaving for the locker room during Sunday's open practice. The star guard missed 27 games last season with an injury to the same knee. The Warriors kick off the regular season Wednesday against the Lakers.

items.headline: Curry finished Friday's 128-118 preseason win over Portland with 20 points (7-19 FG, 3-11 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five assists, four rebounds and one steal over 26 minutes.
items.story: Curry and most of the other Warriors prominent players took to the floor for Friday's exhibition contest, which was the team's final tune-up before the regular-season opener against the Lakers on Wednesday. Entering his 18th season, Curry will once again shoulder the bulk of the offensive responsibilities, especially since Jimmy Butler (knee) is not expected to return to action until the calendar flips over to 2027.

items.headline: Curry tallied 11 points (3-9 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Tuesday's 101-89 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Curry's shot wasn't falling consistently, but the more important development was his workload, as he logged his most minutes of the preseason after being held to roughly 14 minutes per game. Coach Steve Kerr will likely keep Curry at this usage level as the season opener approaches.

items.headline: Curry (rest) is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason matchup with the Kings, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Curry is back after sitting out Wednesday's exhibition for rest, but he will be limited to the first half of Saturday's preseason game. Joining him in the first unit will be Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green.

items.headline: Curry generated 16 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five assists and two rebounds across 14 minutes in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Curry made the most of his limited court time, drilling three shots beyond the arc in short order. Curry won't travel with the team to Portland, and the veteran's preseason participation is expected to be very limited to avoid injury and keep him fresh for the regular season.

items.headline: Curry will be limited to "around 20 minutes" in Tuesday's preseason game against the Lakers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Curry is starting again Tuesday but will be limited to roughly 20 minutes of work. However, the multi-time All-Star won't travel with the team to Portland for Wednesday's game, the second of back-to-back outings.

items.headline: Curry logged 10 points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and a steal in 12 minutes during Sunday's 104-101 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Curry understandably saw limited action in the team's preseason opener, but he made the most of his minutes, leading the starting five with 10 points on efficient shooting. Curry will likely continue to see limited minutes throughout the preseason to preserve his health for the regular season. The star guard played in just 43 regular-season games in 2025-26.

items.headline: Lendeborg logged 16 points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 8-9 FT), five rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Monday's 116-113 win over the Suns.
items.story: Lendeborg followed Sunday's career-high 37-point performance with another productive outing, overcoming a difficult shooting night by getting to the free-throw line nine times. The rookie also contributed across multiple categories and played a key role in Golden State's comeback, including a late block on Jalen Green. Lendeborg's expanding offensive responsibilities make him an intriguing fantasy option.

items.headline: Lendeborg tallied 37 points (13-19 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six assists, four rebounds and one steal over 34 minutes in a 124-112 win over the Clippers on Sunday.
items.story: Lendeborg scored 24 of his game-high 37 points between the second and third quarters of Sunday's game, and he picked up the scoring responsibilities in the absence of Stephen Curry (rest). Sunday was Lendeborg's second game of 30-plus points, and he has scored at least 26 points in four of his last five outings. In that five-game span, he has averaged 25.2 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 3.2 threes over 32.0 minutes per contest. The rookie 11th-overall pick has given the Warriors exactly what they need on offense, especially in the absence of Jimmy Butler (knee), who is not expected to make his 2026-27 debut until the new calendar year.

items.headline: Lendeborg posted 26 points (11-20 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Lendeborg has surpassed even the most optimistic expectations early in the season, scoring at least 25 points in three straight games. His 20 field-goal attempts and 35-minute workload were particularly encouraging, highlighting his growing role in Golden State's offense as the No. 2 option behind Stephen Curry, who scored 44 points in this win. Lendeborg's scoring and rebounding potential give him considerable fantasy upside, and he's averaging a robust 22.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and a combined 1.6 steals-plus-blocks in his first five appearances.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) is available for Wednesday's game in Minnesota, as expected.
items.story: The rookie was able to get through shootaround and his pregame routine without issue, and there's been no discussion of any minutes limitations, so make sure you've got him active. Lendeborg is averaging 21.8 points, 9.3 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 2.3 triples, 1.0 steals and 0.5 blocks per game this season.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) is trending toward playing Wednesday against the Timberwolves, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Lendeborg went through shootaround without issue and is currently going through his pregame routine, so we should have official confirmation on his status shortly. With Lendeborg expected to play, Georges Niang loses his streaming appeal.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) went through Wednesday's morning shootaround, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: The standout rookie remains officially listed as questionable for Wednesday's tilt versus Minnesota. However, he appears to be trending in the right direction.

items.headline: Lendeborg (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: The rookie standout is in danger of missing his first game of the season Wednesday with foot soreness. With the Warriors already short on forward options, Georges Niang could be thrust into an expanded role if Lendeborg cannot play.

items.headline: Lendeborg totaled 31 points (9-19 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 12-13 FT), 12 rebounds, six assists and one block in 31 minutes during Monday's 134-114 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Lendeborg put together the best final line of his young NBA career, propelling Golden State to a comfortable victory. The rookie forward has shown promise as a scorer, especially over his last two games, racking up 57 total points over this short stretch. Coach Steve Kerr noted after the game that he was particularly impressed with Lendeborg's performance in the win. "Basically, in all the critical moments of the game, we put the ball in his hands. And for a rookie to be that advanced already, it's extremely rare," said Kerr, per Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle.

items.headline: Lendeborg accumulated 18 points (4-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 9-12 FT), 13 rebounds, six assists and three steals in 37 minutes during Friday's 111-108 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: After a more subdued NBA debut on Wednesday, Lendeborg flashed his full array of skills in his second game. The 11th overall pick in the 2026 Draft tied Brandin Podziemski for second on the team in scoring while pacing the Warriors in boards and tying for the lead in assists and steals, all while getting to the free-throw line with regularity. Lendeborg will have his ups and downs as a rookie, but Golden State seems committed to giving him plenty of court time to speed his development.

items.headline: Lendeborg contributed 12 points (5-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds, two assists and a steal across 29 minutes in Wednesday's 127-105 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Lendeborg's 29 minutes were an encouraging sign for the role he's expected to have in the Warriors' rotation. However, his modest peripheral production and inefficient free-throw shooting limited his fantasy impact. With the Warriors missing several established contributors, mainly Jimmy Butler (knee) and Moses Moody (knee), as well as Brandin Podziemski (back) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness), Lendeborg should get consistent playing time in the coming weeks, but his production needs to increase to be a valuable option in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Head coach Steve Kerr confirmed Monday that Lendeborg will start Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Lakers, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: This was the expectation throughout the preseason, given the rookie forward started most of Golden State's exhibition contests. Lendeborg is expected to hold down the fort at small forward at least until Jimmy Butler finishes his ACL rehab at some point later this year.

items.headline: Lendeborg finished Friday's 128-118 win over the Trail Blazers with 17 points (6-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-5 FT), five assists, four rebounds, two steals and one block over 26 minutes.
items.story: Lendeborg finished the preseason logging 17 points in back-to-back games and was tied with Brandin Podziemski as the Warriors' second-leading scorer Friday behind Stephen Curry (20 points). Lendeborg was the Warriors' 11th-overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft and will likely have a sizable role for at least the first couple of months of his rookie season while Jimmy Butler (knee) is sidelined.

items.headline: Lendeborg recorded 17 points (5-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-9 FT), five rebounds, four assists and two steals across 26 minutes in Tuesday's preseason matchup against the Lakers.
items.story: Lendeborg briefly exited after tweaking his ankle but was able to return to the contest, an encouraging sign regarding the severity of the issue. The rookie forward delivered a well-rounded performance despite the injury scare, contributing across multiple categories while committing just one turnover.

items.headline: Head coach Steve Kerr plans to start Lendeborg to begin the season, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area.
items.story: Both Jimmy Butler (knee) and Moses Moody (knee) are expected to be on the shelf for an extended period to open 2026-27, and Lendeborg is primed to help pick up the slack to start the year. The rookie first-rounder will be looking to make a case to remain a full-time starter and carries plenty of upside in the later rounds of fantasy drafts.

items.headline: Lendeborg produced 23 points (10-14 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, six assists, two steals and one block over 24 minutes in Saturday's 111-106 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: After a lackluster preseason debut, Lendeborg has caught fire over the past two games, scoring efficiently while bringing a little bit of everything to the box score. He should start for the Warriors right away and makes for an intriguing late-round target on draft day.

items.headline: Lendeborg (rest) is in the Warriors' starting lineup against the Kings on Saturday, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Lendeborg was rested for Wednesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, but the rookie first-rounder will be in the Warriors' starting five for Saturday's contest. The Michigan product is attempting to carve out a consistent role for himself for the 2026-27 season, and he has a path to do so seeing as both Jimmy Butler (knee) and Moses Moody (knee) are expected to be sidelined for a sizable chunk of the upcoming campaign.

items.headline: Lendeborg (rest) is out for Wednesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: The rookie is one of several Warriors not making the trip for maintenance reasons. He produced 17 points (7-11 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds and two assists across 21 minutes in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers and continues to impress the coaching staff.

items.headline: Lendeborg registered 17 points (7-11 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds and two assists across 21 minutes in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Lendeborg appears to have an inside track to start with the first unit once the season gets underway. The 2026 first-round pick finds himself in one of the best situations among this season's pack of rookies, as Draymond Green's advancing age and several frontcourt injuries will all play in the Michigan product's favor.

items.headline: Henderson finished with 14 points (4-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, one assist and three steals over 31 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Aside from his four turnovers, Henderson played well in his first start of the season, providing a scoring punch for Portland while doing a nice job of disrupting passing lanes. Ja Morant (hamstring) will miss at least the next four weeks, so Henderson should be locked in as a starter for Portland. He's someone to consider grabbing off the waiver wire.

items.headline: Henderson will move into the starting lineup for Saturday's game in Utah, Trail Blazers' reporter Sean Highkin reports.
items.story: Henderson is replacing the injured Ja Morant (hamstring) in the first unit, so it'll be interesting to see how he fares with the increased opportunity. Per 36 minutes this season, Henderson is averaging 14.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.0 three-pointers per game.

items.headline: Henderson (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Henderson will shed his questionable tag due to left ankle soreness and suit up in Los Angeles. The fourth-year guard is averaging 9.5 points in 20.0 minutes per tilt through two regular-season games.

items.headline: Henderson is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Lakers due to left ankle soreness.
items.story: Henderson is evidently dealing with some soreness following Friday's matchup in Sacramento. The Blazers should have a better idea of his availability after watching him go through shootaround and warmups ahead of Tuesday's tipoff.

items.headline: Henderson provided 15 points (7-14 FG, 1-6 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 19 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 124-83 victory over the Suns.
items.story: While all five Portland starters scored in double digits during the rout, Henderson was the only member of the second unit to deliver 10-plus points. The fourth-year guard is firmly behind Damian Lillard and Ja Morant on the backcourt depth chart to begin the season and is working off the bench with Jrue Holiday, but after a strong training camp and preseason, Henderson could be poised to thrive in that role.

items.headline: Henderson logged 17 points (7-16 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two assists, one rebound, one steal and one block over 19 minutes during Portland's 128-118 preseason loss to Golden STate.
items.story: Henderson had a poor night from beyond the arc, but he was accurate enough on other parts of the floor to finish as the Trail Blazers' third-leading scorer behind Damian Lillard (23 points) and Ja Morant (19 points). Lillard and Morant are projected to be the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt for the 2026-27 season, with Henderson and veteran Jrue Holiday (rest) coming off the bench.

items.headline: Henderson will come off the bench in Friday's preseason finale against the Warriors, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Ja Morant will replace Henderson in the first unit for Friday's final exhibition game. As a reserve this preseason, Henderson is averaging 10.5 points, 3.0 assists and 2.5 triples per contest.

items.headline: Henderson supplied nine points (3-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists and one rebound in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 110-98 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Portland wanted to take a look at Ja Morant out of the second unit, giving Henderson the chance to start Tuesday. It's hard to envision a player of Morant's caliber coming off the bench once the games begin to count, but this at least appears to be a fluid backcourt situation.

items.headline: Henderson will start Tuesday's preseason game against the Kings, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Henderson will step into the starting five for the first time this preseason. He'll be joined in the first unit by Damian Lillard, Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan.

items.headline: Henderson recorded 14 points (4-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three assists and two steals across 16 minutes off the bench in Monday's 119-66 preseason win over the London Lions.
items.story: Henderson was particularly effective from beyond the arc, knocking down four of his five attempts while tying Toumani Camara for the team lead in scoring. The 22-year-old guard also contributed defensively with two steals and committed just one turnover. His perimeter shooting was an encouraging development, though Portland's crowded backcourt could make consistent playing time difficult to secure. Damian Lillard was rested Monday.

items.headline: Henderson finished with nine points (3-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block over 17 minutes in Wednesday's 123-118 preseason win over the Warriors.
items.story: Although most of the attention is on Ja Morant and Damian Lillard in Portland's revamped backcourt, Henderson should continue to play a prominent role off the bench this season. Henderson averaged a career-high 14.2 points despite playing a career-low 24.9 minutes per game last regular season.

items.headline: Henderson is in jeopardy of moving back to a bench role after Portland acquired Ja Morant in a trade this offseason.
items.story: Henderson closed the 2025-26 campaign as a starter after missing the first half of the season with a torn hamstring. Not only do the Trail Blazers now have Morant in the mix, but Damian Lillard (Achilles) is also a candidate to jump into the starting lineup in his 2026-27 return to the floor. Until Portland makes its backcourt plans a bit clearer, Henderson is a difficult player to rank from a fantasy perspective ahead of the new year.

items.headline: Henderson finished Tuesday's 114-95 loss to San Antonio in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with five points (2-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and two rebounds over 17 minutes.
items.story: After a strong start to the series, Henderson scored a total of five points on 2-for-13 shooting in the final two games. Injuries derailed his third NBA season, limiting him to 30 regular-season appearances with averages of 14.2 points, 3.7 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.9 three-pointers in 24.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Henderson chipped in zero points (0-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt), two assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 114-93 loss to the Spurs in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Henderson couldn't hit the side of a barn, missing all seven of his shot attempts as the Trail Blazers fell behind 3-1 in the series. The forgettable performance was in stark contrast to the first three games of the series for Henderson, as he averaged 23.3 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.0 steals while shooting 56.5 percent, including 52.2 percent from behind the arc. Given that body of work, Henderson should have a solid chance of bouncing back in a potential elimination scenario for Portland in Game 5.

items.headline: Henderson produced 21 points (8-18 FG, 5-10 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 36 minutes during Friday's 120-108 loss to San Antonio in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: It was another impressive performance from long range for Henderson, who has come out firing for the Blazers in the series. Over his first three career playoff contests, the third-year guard is averaging 23.3 points, 4.0 threes, 2.0 boards, 1.3 assists and 1.0 steals while shooting a blistering 52.2 percent (12-for-23) from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Henderson amassed 31 points (11-17 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 4-6 FT), one rebound, one steal and one block across 38 minutes in Tuesday's 106-103 Game 2 win over the Spurs in the first round of the playoffs.
items.story: Henderson turned in an efficient performance en route to a game- and season-best 31 points across the regular season and playoffs. Additionally, the 22-year-old point guard became the youngest Trail Blazers player to score at least 30 points in the playoffs. He also knocked down a game-high five triples and is shooting 7-for-13 from beyond the arc through two first-round matchups. He'll look to remain productive in Friday's Game 3 in Portland as the Trail Blazers aim to take a 2-1 series lead.

items.headline: Henderson racked up 18 points (7-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Sunday's 111-98 loss to the Spurs in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Making his ninth straight start, the third-year guard was second on the Trail Blazers in scoring behind Deni Avdija's 30 points. Henderson has become a more efficient scorer during his latest starting stint, and over that nine-game stretch, he's averaging 15.4 points, 3.2 assists, 2.4 boards, 2.1 threes and 1.3 steals while shooting a respectable 46.2 percent from the floor and 40.4 percent from long distance.

items.headline: Henderson closed Sunday's 122-110 victory over the Kings with 15 points (6-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, four assists and two steals over 27 minutes.
items.story: Henderson started in each of the Trail Blazers' last seven games and posted solid numbers, averaging 16.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.3 steals per game while shooting 40 percent from beyond the arc. Regardless of whether he starts or comes off the bench, Henderson should play a big role in the Blazers' upcoming playoff run, starting with the Play-In Game against the Suns on Tuesday.

items.headline: Henderson had 20 points (7-20 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 38 minutes during Wednesday's 112-101 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: For the fifth time this campaign, Henderson reached 20 points for the Trail Blazers. Across 28 total appearances, he holds averages of 14.4 points, 3.8 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.9 three-pointers on 41.4 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Henderson closed Tuesday's 114-104 victory over the Clippers with 15 points (5-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 29 minutes.
items.story: The Trail Blazers employed a smaller lineup amid Jerami Grant's (calf) absence, running Henderson alongside Jrue Holiday in the backcourt for a second consecutive game. The move has reaped significant benefits with two convincing victories. Shaedon Sharpe's (calf) extended absence has opened a window for Henderson to show his potential after fading into the woodwork for most of the season behind Holiday. The team will likely ride with this successful scheme until Grant returns.

items.headline: Henderson ended Sunday's 123-88 win over the Wizards with 21 points (6-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 8-9 FT), three rebounds and seven assists in 25 minutes.
items.story: With Jerami Grant (calf) sidelined, Henderson made his fourth start of the campaign and made the most of his opportunity despite the limited workload -- the Trail Blazers put this game to bed early. Over his last eight appearances, Henderson holds averages of 14.4 points, 3.9 assists, 2.6 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.5 three-pointers in 24.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Henderson is in the Trail Blazers' starting lineup against the Wizards on Sunday, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: With Jerami Grant (calf) sidelined, Henderson will make his fourth start of the season Sunday (and third since March 4). Over his last five outings, Henderson has averaged 13.8 points, 3.0 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 1.6 threes and 2.2 steals over 24.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Henderson closed with 23 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one steal over 24 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 130-99 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: It was the third time in the last 10 games that Henderson produced 20-plus points, with Wednesday's effort pacing the Trail Blazers. The third-year guard is averaging 16.6 points, 3.3 assists, 2.8 boards, 2.5 threes and 1.1 steals over that stretch while shooting 47.2 percent from long distance, a remarkable hot streak for a player with a career 34.0 percent mark from three-point range.

items.headline: Henderson notched 13 points (4-9 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, four assists and four steals across 24 minutes during Monday's 134-99 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: The four swipes were a season high for Henderson, who continues to be an effective sixth man for the Trail Blazers. Over his last nine contests, the third-year guard has averaged 15.9 points, 3.2 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 1.1 steals and 2.4 three-pointers in 24.6 minutes per game while shooting 47.8 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Henderson posted 25 points (8-14 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one block in 30 minutes off the bench during Friday's 124-114 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: The 25 points tied Jrue Holiday for the team scoring lead on the night. Henderson is still searching for consistency, especially when it comes to his shooting, but he's at least flashing the upside that made him the third overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft. In 11 games (three starts) since the All-Star break, Henderson is averaging 14.0 points, 3.6 assists, 2.8 boards and 1.9 threes.

items.headline: Henderson closed Sunday's 131-111 victory over the Pacers with 28 points (10-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal over 26 minutes.
items.story: Henderson was one of the main reasons why the Blazers secured a comfortable 20-point blowout win Sunday. The electric floor general didn't start after being part of the first unit in the past two contests, but he responded with his best game of the season thus far. Henderson made his debut Feb. 6 but has been very consistent, scoring in double digits in 10 of his 13 appearances. He's averaging 12.9 points, 2.8 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game, so he should carry some fantasy appeal as long as he stays healthy, regardless of his role.

items.headline: Henderson won't start Sunday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: With Deni Avdija (back) returning to action, Henderson will slide to the second unit. Over nine appearances off the bench this season, the 22-year-old point guard has averaged 12.9 points, 4.8 assists and 3.1 rebounds in 23.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Henderson closed with eight points (3-11 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal across 24 minutes during Wednesday's 122-114 victory over Memphis.
items.story: Henderson moved into the starting lineup for just the second time since returning from injury, although the promotion failed to improve what has been a tough couple of weeks. In seven appearances during that time, he has averaged just 11.4 points, 4.0 assists and 1.0 three-pointers, leaving him outside the top-300 players in nine-category leagues.

items.headline: Henderson will start Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: With Deni Avdija (back), Shaedon Sharpe (lower leg) and Kris Murray (illness) all unavailable, Henderson will get the starting nod for the second time this season. During his lone start in Thursday's win over Chicago, the third-year guard posted 12 points, four assists and three rebounds in 24 minutes.

items.headline: Henderson will move to the bench for Saturday's game against Charlotte, Sam Perley of the Hornets' official site reports.
items.story: This is an expected move with Donovan Clingan returning from a one-game absence. Henderson is expected to maintain a sizable role off the bench.

items.headline: Henderson will start Thursday in Chicago.
items.story: This will be Henderson's first start of the season, and it'll be Toumani Camara, Jrue Holiday, Jerami Grant and Kris Murray joining him in the first unit for Thursday's game. Henderson is coming off a 19-point game and will draw a favorable matchup against the Bulls, so he's on the radar as a potential streamer if you need some points and dimes.

items.headline: Henderson ended with 19 points (7-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds and five assists over 29 minutes off the bench during Tuesday's 124-121 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: The points and boards were both season highs for Henderson, albeit in just seven appearances. The third-year guard missed the first three-plus months of the campaign due to a hamstring injury, and he returned in the nick of time as Shaedon Sharpe (calf) went down in early February and could be sidelined into April. Henderson is no longer playing with a minutes restriction, and his workload and usage could both be near starter levels as he fills sixth-man duties for the Blazers.

items.headline: Henderson will no longer operate under a minutes restriction, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: Henderson was cleared to make his 2025-26 debut Feb. 6 after recovering from a torn left hamstring that he suffered in late September during an offseason workout. He has averaged 20.0 minutes per game in his four outings, but the third-year guard has been given the green light to increase his playing time moving forward.

items.headline: Henderson had 15 points (4-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one rebound, four assists and one steal in 20 minutes off the bench during Thursday's 135-119 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Playing both halves of a back-to-back for the first time since recovering from a torn hamstring and making his season debut Feb. 6, Henderson saw a muted workload but put together a productive night. The third-year guard will likely remain with the second unit on the other side of the All-Star break as long as Jrue Holiday remains healthy, but Henderson at least appears to be ready to make a consistent contribution.

items.headline: Henderson is available for Thursday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Henderson recorded 18 points (5-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 133-109 loss to the Timberwolves, and it was widely assumed that he would be held out for injury maintenance Thursday. However, it appears that he has the green light, but it's fair to expect a modest workload at best.

items.headline: Okorie registered two points (2-2 FT) across two minutes during Sunday's 106-93 victory over Philadelphia.
items.story: Okorie made his NBA regular-season debut Sunday, scoring his first points at the charity stripe. The rookie first-rounder is unlikely to see meaningful playing time early on unless Cade Cunningham or Daniss Jenkins miss time.

items.headline: Okorie (coach's decision) didn't play during Tuesday's 121-113 win over the Celtics.
items.story: While the Pistons traded up in the draft to acquire Okorie's services earlier this year, the team doesn't look to be ready to throw the rookie first-rounder into the fire. Okorie appears to have more fantasy value in dynasty leagues.

items.headline: Okorie logged 14 points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one assist and one steal over nine minutes during the Pistons' 129-125 preseason win over the Raptors on Friday.
items.story: Okorie didn't see the floor until the fourth quarter, but he made an immediate impact off the bench by scoring 14 of the Pistons' 36 points in the period to help stave off a late comeback attempt by the Raptors. Okorie was the 17th overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft and made a good impression on Detroit's coaching staff during the Summer League and training camp. That said, it's hard to see a clear path to playing time for the rookie out of Stanford, as he's behind both Cade Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins on the depth chart.

items.headline: Okorie supplied 14 points (6-15 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six assists, one rebound and one steal across 27 minutes in Saturday's 114-108 preseason loss to the Wizards in overtime.
items.story: Okorie was the only player to log more than 21 minutes for Detroit. Although he struggled from beyond the arc, the rookie point guard still led the Pistons in scoring and assists. He has totaled 21 points and seven assists over 37 minutes in two preseason games.

items.headline: Coach J.B. Bickerstaff has been impressed by Okorie so far in camp and wants the guard to continue to gain experience against NBA-caliber talent in the preseason, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: Okorie hit the game-winning bucket during Monday night's preseason game against the Suns as the team continues to evaluate where the young guard will fit into the rotation. Bickerstaff has been particularly impressed by Okorie's maturity and poise, and his ability to take care of the basketball. The 19-year-old was selected by the Pistons with the No. 17 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and is in a position to earn regular minutes off the bench behind Cade Cunningham.

items.headline: Okorie posted 27 points (8-19 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 28 minutes during the Pistons' 101-87 Summer League loss to the Heat on Friday.
items.story: Okorie made most of his scoring impact just before and after halftime, scoring 21 of his game-high 27 points across the second and third quarters of Friday's game. The rookie first-rounder has been solid across his five outings in the Summer League and figures to compete with Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Isaiah Joe and Gary Harris for backcourt minutes off the bench behind starters Cade Cunningham and Duncan Robinson.

items.headline: Okorie finished with 14 points (5-18 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 32 minutes in Monday's 86-75 Summer League loss to the Knicks.
items.story: After Okorie combined for nine steals in his first two Summer League appearances, he cooled off Monday. While the 2026 No. 17 overall pick has certainly demonstrated his ability on the defensive end, it has been a different story on offense, with Okorie shooting 28.5 percent from the field in his previous two Summer League games while going 0-for-7 from deep during that span.

items.headline: Okorie posted 14 points (5-17 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-5 FT), six assists, three rebounds and seven steals over 31 minutes during the Pistons' 103-94 Summer League win over the Cavaliers on Sunday.
items.story: Okorie finished as the Pistons' fourth-leading scorer despite his inefficiencies from the field, but he more than made up for it on the defensive side of the floor, where he accounted for seven of the team's 13 steals. Okorie was selected by the Pistons with the No. 17 pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, and strong play on defense should earn him consistent minutes in his rookie season, with his main competition for playing time coming from Daniss Jenkins and Isaiah Joe.

items.headline: Okorie tallied 20 points (8-16 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four assists, two steals and one rebound across 30 minutes in Thursday's 101-93 Summer League loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Okorie delivered an efficient performance and finished as Detroit's second-leading scorer, albeit in a losing effort. The rookie point guard was also one of two Pistons players to log multiple steals. The Stanford product could see rotational minutes right away in 2026-27, though he'll likely compete for playing time with Daniss Jenkins and Isaiah Joe.

items.headline: The Thunder selected Okorie with the No. 17 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and traded his rights to the Grizzlies, who then traded his rights to the Pistons, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Detroit moved up from No. 21 and packaged three second-round picks to acquire Okorie, who powered Stanford's offense during his lone collegiate campaign. The guard averaged 23.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.6 steals in 35.0 minutes per contest across 31 starts during the 2025-26 season. He earned All-ACC First Team honors and showcased his scoring prowess by reaching the 30-point mark eight times. The Pistons are set at point guard with superstar Cade Cunningham, but Okorie figures to provide a spark off the bench during his rookie campaign.

items.story: The Mavericks currently have P.J. Washington, Santi Aldama, rookie Morez Johnson and Martin competing for opportunities at power forward. At the same time, several other wings can also slide between positions. Martin's experience and two-way versatility do give him some hope, but the competition for minutes limits his fantasy ceiling entering the season.

He's played fewer than 16 minutes in five straight appearances.

items.story: Sharp made all three of his attempts from beyond the arc, providing efficient bench scoring in Sacramento's first win of the campaign. He also chipped in defensively, but his limited shot volume and uncertain night-to-night workload make him difficult to trust outside deeper fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Sharp racked up three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound and one block across 14 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: The rookie second-rounder has somewhat surprisingly nailed down a rotation spot in the early going with the rebuilding Kings. That's perhaps due to Ben Simmons going down for the season with an Achilles injury, but Sharp isn't quite yet on fantasy radars in most leagues.

items.headline: Sharp recorded 11 points (3-9 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 2-5 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 21 minutes during Thursday's 114-110 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Sharp provided Sacramento with perimeter scoring off the bench, accounting for all three of his field goals from beyond the arc. Although he struggled at the free-throw line, the rookie guard demonstrated his willingness to shoot from distance and avoided committing a turnover. Sharp will look to build on the performance as he competes for a spot in Sacramento's regular-season backcourt rotation.

items.headline: Sharp faces increased competition for playing time after the Kings signed Ben Simmons to a one-year deal Friday.
items.story: Although Russell Westbrook is out of the picture now, Ben Simmons will return to The Association and figures to see a steady role in the Kings' rotation thanks to his defensive versatility and playmaking. Along with fellow rookie Alex Karaban, Sharp isn't guaranteed a meaningful role to begin his professional career. However, the No. 45 overall pick out of Houston could see increasingly steady minutes as the season progresses, depending on whether the Kings trade some of their veterans.

items.headline: Sharp tallied 16 points (5-12 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three assists, two rebounds, three steals and one block over 30 minutes during the Kings' 92-90 Summer League win over the Hornets on Friday.
items.story: Sharp scored 13 of his team-high 16 points in the first half, with the rookie second-rounder being one of six Kings players to score in double digits in Friday's victory. He also made his mark defensively with three steals, an area of his game that has really stood out so far in the Summer League. Zach LaVine (hand), Malik Monk (personal) and Nique Clifford (rest) are all ahead of Sharp on the Kings' depth chart, but Sharp could earn himself a consistent role in the rotation with a strong summer, training camp and preseason.

items.headline: Sharp racked up 23 points (7-12 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, four steals and one block over 23 minutes during Tuesday's 115-83 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Nets.
items.story: It was the Sharp and Darius Acuff Show on Tuesday, as the rookie duo combined for 49 of Sacramento's 83 points. Sharp caught fire from deep, knocking down a game-high six three-pointers, and he was a disruptive force on the defensive end, finishing with six stocks. However, with little offensive support from the rest of the roster, the Kings were blown out for the second straight game in Las Vegas.

items.headline: The Kings selected Sharp with the No. 45 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

items.story: Thiero will miss the Lakers' final two exhibition games for "maintenance." It's unclear if he'll be good to go for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Thiero (undisclosed) is being managed for "maintenance," per Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: Thiero's practice reps are limited by an undisclosed issue. His status is uncertain for Friday's preseason finale against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Thiero (undisclosed) is out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Thiero is among several Lakers players who have been ruled out, though the team hasn't specified the reason for his absence. Coach JJ Redick indicated that the young forward remains day-to-day, leaving open the possibility of a return for Friday's preseason finale against Denver.

items.headline: Thiero tallied seven points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-3 FT) and four rebounds across 17 minutes during Tuesday's 124-98 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: After an encouraging Summer League campaign, coach JJ Redick intends to give the 6-foot-8 Arkansas product every opportunity to be a key support piece for the Lakers this season. Unlike other spots in LA's rotation, Thiero's position is a bit more wide open, with Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Jarred Vanderbilt all competing for time. Although he shouldn't be considered a viable fantasy option right now, Thiero has the potential to be a bigger contributor.

items.headline: Thiero is in the starting lineup for Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Lakers are playing on the second leg of a back-to-back preseason set, so there's no reason to play most of their starters. Thiero is vying for a spot in the frontcourt rotation, so he'll aim to make the most of this opportunity.

items.headline: Thiero finished Saturday's 92-88 Summer League loss to Golden State with 18 points (6-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and three steals over 26 minutes.
items.story: It was an efficient performance from Thiero, who made all nine of his shots between the field and the charity stripe while leading the Lakers in points, rebounds and steals. It was Thiero's first double-double of the Summer League and his most points in a game since July 10 against the Thunder (20). The 2025 second-rounder averaged just 6.0 minutes per game across 25 regular-season games in his rookie year, but he'll have the opportunity to earn a larger, more consistent role for himself in training camp and in the preseason.

items.headline: Thiero posted 15 points (4-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 26 minutes in Saturday's 91-70 Summer League win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Behind a 34-point outburst from Arthur Kaluma, Thiero finished as the Lakers' second-leading scorer in the blowout win. He has now scored in double figures in four consecutive outings dating back to the California Classic Summer League. After averaging 1.9 points and 1.1 rebounds in 6.0 minutes per contest across 25 regular-season appearances as a rookie, the second-year wing will look to carve out a larger role during the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Thiero (wrist) finished with 20 points (8-14 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-5 FT), four rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 96-84 Summer League win over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Thiero had been battling a wrist injury heading into this contest. However, not only did he suit up and get the start, but he also finished with a game-high 20 points. The 2025 No. 36 overall pick averaged 1.9 points, 1.1 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.1 blocks and 0.3 steals over 6.0 minutes in 25 regular-season appearances for the Lakers in 2025-26. If Thiero continues to play well during Summer League, he might be able to climb the depth chart heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Thiero (wrist) will start in Friday's Summer League game against Oklahoma City, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Thiero had been dealing with a wrist injury, but he'll get the start to open Los Angeles' Las Vegas stint. The 22-year-old appeared in 25 regular-season games for the Lakers in 2025-26, averaging 1.9 points, 1.1 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.1 blocks and 0.3 steals across 6.0 minutes.

items.headline: Thiero did not play in Monday's 88-84 California Classic Summer League win over the Spurs due to a right wrist injury, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
