items.story: Lakers' Summer League head coach Ty Abbott said he's hopeful that Thiero will be available for their first game in Las Vegas against the Thunder on Friday, so for now, he can be considered questionable for that one. The good news is that it doesn't sound like Thiero is dealing with anything too serious.

items.headline: Thiero recorded 13 points (3-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-7 FT), three rebounds, three steals and two assists in 28 minutes during Sunday's 93-91 double-overtime win over the Heat at the California Classic Summer League.
items.story: Thiero put together a solid all-around performance Sunday despite struggling from the floor. He stood out defensively, logging a game-high three steals. Through two Summer League games, Thiero is averaging 11.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 steals and 2.0 assists in 24.5 minutes per contest. One area in which he has struggled thus far is efficiency, as he has shot just 31.6 percent from the field on 19 attempts.

items.headline: Thiero produced zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over three minutes during Monday's 115-110 loss to Oklahoma City in Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Los Angeles' second-round rookie was used sparingly by the Lakers in 2025-26, logging a total of 25 regular-season appearances for an average of 6.0 minutes per contest. Depending on how many changes the team makes this offseason, Thiero could be in a better spot to compete for minutes in 2026-27.

items.headline: Thiero was ejected from Sunday's Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Rockets, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Thiero got tied up with Aaron Holiday late in the fourth quarter, leading to both of them getting ejected. He concludes the contest with three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 FT). in six minutes.

items.headline: Thiero (face) returned to Tuesday's game against the Thunder with 7:54 remaining in the third quarter, per the broadcast.
items.story: Thiero took an elbow to the face in the second quarter and immediately headed back to the locker room. However, he was eventually cleared to return and will likely continue to play meaningful minutes the rest of the way for the banged-up Lakers.

items.headline: Thiero exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Tuesday's game against the Thunder due to an apparent facial injury, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: Thiero caught an elbow to the face from Chet Holmgren and headed straight back to the locker room with a towel on his face. Thiero should be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Thiero from the G League's South Bay Lakers on Sunday.
items.story: Since their last game Thursday, the Lakers have lost Austin Reaves (oblique) and Luka Doncic (hamstring) to long-term injuries, and with Marcus Smart (ankle) joining them on the sideline for Sunday's game in Dallas, Thiero was summoned from the G League to provide reinforcement. Even if he's included in the rotation Sunday, Thiero likely won't be in store for enough minutes to make a meaningful fantasy impact.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is available for Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Thiero will be available off the bench after three straight absences. He's not guaranteed any minutes, however.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is out for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Thiero will miss a third straight game due to a left knee injury. His absence doesn't figure to impact the rotation. His next chance to suit up comes Tuesday against the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) won't play Friday versus the Nets.
items.story: Thiero will miss his second straight game due to the knee issue, but he's a negligible part of the rotation anyway. His next chance to suit up will come Monday against the Wizards.

items.headline: Thiero (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Thiero is not usually in the rotation for the Lakers, so his absence won't have many fantasy implications. He's made only four appearances since playing double-digit minutes against the Spurs on Feb. 10.

items.headline: Thiero is questionable for Wednesday's game against Indiana due to left knee soreness.
items.story: It's unclear as to when this injury popped up for Thiero, who logged two minutes Monday night against Detroit. He's appeared in three games for the Lakers in March, so even if he is cleared to play, he's unlikely to be much of a factor.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Thiero from the G League's South Bay Lakers on Sunday, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Thiero and Kobe Bufkin were both inactive for Saturday's 105-104 win over the Magic, but the two will rejoin the Lakers ahead of their next game Monday in Detroit. Thiero hasn't typically been included in the rotation when the Lakers are at full strength, but he could be needed to handle some minutes if Rui Hachimura (calf) and Marcus Smart (ankle) -- both of whom are listed as questionable -- are unable to play Monday.

items.headline: The Lakers assigned Thiero to the G League's South Bay Lakers on Friday, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Thiero continues to bounce back and forth between the G League and the NBA. The rookie forward has a much clearer path to consistent developmental reps with South Bay.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Thiero from the G League's South Bay Lakers on Saturday.
items.story: Thiero will be available off the bench for the Lakers' game Saturday against the Nuggets but isn't expected to be featured in the rotation. He suited up for the G League club Friday and played 31 minutes in South Bay's 125-106 win over the Iowa Wolves, finishing with 20 points (7-12 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block.

items.headline: Garland ended with 16 points (5-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and eight assists in 36 minutes during Monday's 125-118 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Garland led the Clippers in assists but struggled with his efficiency, committing seven turnovers while shooting just 35.7 percent from the field. He also failed to record a steal or block and finished with a team-worst minus-16 rating. The substantial workload and playmaking opportunities remain encouraging, though his turnovers significantly diminished his fantasy production.

items.headline: Garland notched 24 points (10-22 FG, 4-8 3Pt), five assists, two rebounds and one steal across 31 minutes in Friday's 127-101 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Garland turned in an efficient performance and tied for the game-high mark in scoring, reaching the 20-point mark for the third time across five regular-season appearances. He also matched his season high in three-pointers made after shooting 3-for-11 from downtown in his previous two contests. Additionally, the star point guard finished second on the team in assists and has dished out at least five dimes in four straight games.

items.headline: Garland racked up 16 points (7-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt), four rebounds and 11 assists across 36 minutes during Sunday's 108-101 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Garland led the Clippers in scoring and recorded his first double-double of the season, though he struggled from beyond the arc and committed six turnovers against Oklahoma City's aggressive defense. With Brandon Ingram (Achilles) and Max Strus (foot) sidelined, Garland continues to handle substantial offensive responsibilities, giving him a strong opportunity to produce points and assists despite his early-season efficiency issues.

items.headline: Garland amassed 26 points (9-19 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six assists and one steal across 37 minutes during Friday's 125-117 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Garland had another strong scoring night, leading the Clippers with 26 points after dropping 30 in the opener, but his nine turnovers weren't encouraging. With Bradley Beal (knee), Brandon Ingram (heel) and Max Strus (foot) all sidelined, the offense runs through Garland as the Clippers start a rebuilding season. Next up is a tough road test at Oklahoma City on Sunday.

items.headline: Garland accumulated 30 points (11-19 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-8 FT), one rebound, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 victory over the Kings.
items.story: The 26-year-old thrived as the focal point of the Clippers' offense in the absence of Bradley Beal (knee) and Brandon Ingram (Achilles), leading all scorers on the night in an efficient performance. Garland could be headed for career-high shot volume until his big-name teammates get healthy, giving him a chance to reach the 20 points per game plateau for the fourth time.

items.headline: Garland supplied 14 points (5-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, seven assists and a steal over 23 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Garland tied for the game lead in assists, though he committed four turnovers during the victory. Los Angeles acquired Garland from Cleveland in February in a deal for James Harden. Garland was dealing with a toe injury at the time of the trade, which limited his availability and production throughout the 2025-26 campaign. His healthy start this fall is an encouraging sign for a Clippers squad scrambling to fill the production void left by Kawhi Leonard.

items.headline: Garland recorded 11 points (4-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and four assists across 19 minutes in Saturday's 114-106 preseason loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Garland struggled to find his shooting rhythm, but he contributed as a facilitator, leading the Clippers' starters with four assists while committing just one turnover. The veteran guard played fewer than 20 minutes as Los Angeles distributed playing time throughout its roster, but fantasy managers shouldn't be worried about the limited playing time. He's penciled in as the starting floor general ahead of the regular-season opener against the Kings on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Garland recorded 15 points (4-4 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six assists and three rebounds in 15 minutes during Sunday's 104-101 preseason win over the Warriors.
items.story: Garland was extremely efficient in his brief appearance, accounting for 15 points on only four field-goal attempts while committing just one turnover. The veteran guard is coming off a 2025-26 regular season in which he averaged 18.8 points and 6.7 assists per game, and he remains firmly entrenched as one of the Clippers' primary offensive initiators.

items.headline: Garland will start in Sunday's preseason opener against the Warriors, but he will only play the first half of the game, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Garland is headed into his first full season in Los Angeles with expectations he'll shoulder a heavy load offensively now that Kawhi Leonard is in Toronto. The veteran guard was limited to 45 total regular-season games in the 2025-26 campaign while splitting his time between the Cavaliers and Clippers, but Garland is healthy entering the new campaign.

items.headline: Head coach Ty Lue has been very impressed with Garland's offseason, per Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com.
items.story: Lue also notes he'll push Garland when needed, so it sounds like the Clippers are planning to give the star guard all the usage he can handle amid Brandon Ingram's (Achilles) absence. Provided he stays healthy after playing a career-low 45 regular-season games last year, Garland has the upside for a career campaign with a rebuilding Los Angeles team.

items.headline: Garland could face more competition for ballhandling duties at point guard after the Clippers drafted Keaton Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Garland came off the bench just twice for the Clippers last year, and that was likely done to ease him back into action due to nagging toe injuries. It's hard to envision the star guard seeing a noticeable decline in playing time due to the addition of Wagler, and Los Angeles must believe the two guards will mesh well alongside one another in the long run. If Wagler starts at shooting guard right away, his presence could help alleviate some of the ballhandling duties on Garland's plate.

items.headline: Garland finished with 21 points (8-15 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 31 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Garland battled foul trouble all night, eventually fouling out in the dying minutes. Although his numbers were fine, he never really found any rhythm, ultimately contributing to what was a devastating loss. With that said, his end to the season was certainly a positive one, positioning him to play a major role next season. In six games over the final two weeks, he averaged 17.0 points, 30. rebounds, 5.7 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.7 three-pointers.

items.headline: Garland racked up 16 points (5-16 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and three steals over 41 minutes during Friday's 116-97 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Garland rejoined the first unit after sitting out Wednesday's game against the Thunder. Garland has averaged 20.2 points, 6.4 assists and 2.4 rebounds since joining the Clippers. While his point total suffered, Garland exceeded his usual production in the secondary categories. For the Clippers to achieve maximum success, Garland needs to get closer to Kawhi Leonard's production, and a few of his lines have shown the potential to get there.

items.headline: Garland (toe) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Friday's game against the Trail Blazers, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Garland was held out of Wednesday's matchup against Oklahoma City due to left toe injury management, but he's been given the green light to return Friday. He's averaging 16.7 points, 2.3 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.0 steals through three April appearances.

items.headline: Garland has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder due to left toe injury management.
items.story: Garland will sit out the second half of this back-to-back set, though he'll likely return for Friday's game in Portland. With the 26-year-old point guard out, Jordan Miller and John Collins are candidates to step into the starting five. Kobe Sanders and Kris Dunn could also see increased playing time in Garland's absence.

items.headline: Garland had 22 points (9-18 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, four assists, one block and one steal over 28 minutes during Tuesday's 116-103 win over Dallas.
items.story: The Clippers got out to a hot start, with Garland making a solid contribution right away. He quieted down while the Mavericks cut into the Clippers' significant lead, but the rest of the team rallied to put the game out of reach. Garland's most glaring deficiency in recent games is in the assist column. The point guard has amassed only 17 assists over the past four games, well below his seasonal average of 6.7 assists per game.

items.headline: Garland finished with 20 points (7-17 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 37 minutes during Tuesday's 114-104 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Garland logged a high shot volume but had trouble finding the bottom of the basket during the defeat. Although Garland has been generally productive, his scoring results have been wildly erratic, alternating between prolific totals and underwhelming performances. Although assists have padded his fantasy totals, the team needs more consistency from the guard down the stretch.

items.headline: Garland (lower leg) will start the second half of Friday's game against the Pacers, Lauren Rosen of FanDuel Sports Network SoCal reports.
items.story: Garland exited to the locker room late in the second quarter after appearing to step on a camera operator's foot. However, the 26-year-old point guard has been cleared to return for the second half.

items.headline: Garland exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Friday's game against the Pacers due to an apparent left lower-leg injury, Farbod Esnaashari of SI.com reports.
items.story: Garland appeared to step on a camera operator's foot late in the second quarter. He briefly played through the issue before exiting to the locker room, and he can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Garland finished with 24 points (9-16 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 119-94 win over Toronto.
items.story: Garland has been slightly inconsistent of late, but the floor general seems to be finding his footing in Los Angeles while learning how to play with Kawhi Leonard. Garland has scored at least 20 points in seven of his last nine outings dating back to March 7, a stretch in which he's averaging a loaded line of 23.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 7.2 assists and 1.2 steals per game.

items.headline: Garland ended Saturday's 138-131 overtime win over Dallas with 41 points (15-24 FG, 8-12 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, 11 assists, one block and one steal in 39 minutes.
items.story: Garland was cleared to return for Saturday's game after a one-game absence due to left toe injury management. The veteran point guard made a big impact in his return, becoming the first Clippers player in franchise history with 40-plus points, 10-plus assists and seven-plus three-pointers in a game. This is the kind of production the Clippers were envisioning from Garland after acquiring him from the Cavaliers in early February in exchange for James Harden. Since making his Clippers debut March 2, Garland has averaged 21.4 points, 7.0 assists, 2.3 rebounds, 3.9 threes and 1.1 steals over 28.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Garland (toe) is off the injury report for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: After sitting out Thursday's loss to the Pelicans due to left toe injury management, Garland is ready to return Saturday. Kris Dunn appears headed back into a reserve role versus Dallas. Over his last six appearances, Garland has averaged 21.3 points, 7.0 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 28.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Garland (toe) will not play Thursday against the Pelicans.
items.story: As expected, Garland will be rested for the second leg of this back-to-back set. The guard produced 13 points (6-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt), one rebound, six assists and one steal in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 124-109 loss to the Pelicans. Kris Dunn and Jordan Miller could step into larger roles as a result Thursday.

items.headline: Garland produced 13 points (6-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt), one rebound, six assists and one steal in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 124-109 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Garland played through a questionable tag Wednesday for the front end of this back-to-back set, and a maintenance day could be on the table Thursday. Since joining the Clippers, he's averaging 19.0 points, 6.5 assists, 2.3 rebounds, 1.1 steals and 3.4 three-pointers in 27.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Garland (toe) will play in Wednesday's game against the Pelicans, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: Wednesday is the first half of a back-to-back set with New Orleans, so Garland's presence might mean a maintenance day is coming Thursday. The star guard has averaged 19.9 points, 6.6 assists, 2.4 rebounds, 1.1 steals and 3.7 three-pointers in 27.0 minutes per game over seven contests for the Clippers so far, shooting 46.4 percent from deep.

items.headline: Garland is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans due to left toe injury management.
items.story: The Clippers are considering sitting Garland down Wednesday for the first half of this back-to-back. Expect another update on his availability closer to game time.

items.headline: Garland collected 25 points (9-21 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, 10 assists and two steals in 32 minutes during Monday's 119-115 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Garland pieced together yet another impressive all-around performance, but it wasn't enough to will LA to a victory. He scored 20-plus points for a fifth straight game and recorded his first double-double since returning from a right big toe sprain by making his mark as a facilitator. The Clippers will gear up for a back-to-back set later in the week, so it's possible that Garland will sit either Wednesday or Thursday in an effort to keep him healthy.

items.headline: Garland (toe) amassed 25 points (9-20 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 30 minutes during Saturday's 118-109 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Garland returned as expected for the tail end of the back-to-back. The upcoming schedule shows an upcoming back-to-back set against the Pelicans beginning on Wednesday, so there's a possibility that Garland could sit for one of those contests. He should be ready for Monday's game against the Spurs. The team would need Garland's production if Kawhi Leonard's (ankle) injury warrants a multi-game absence, and that could create a scenario where the Clippers start Garland despite the recent trend.

items.headline: Garland (toe) is available for Saturday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Garland did not play in the front end of the Clippers' back-to-back set against the Bulls on Friday while managing a lingering left toe injury, but the veteran point guard will be available for Saturday's Western Conference clash. Over his last three outings, Garland has averaged 21.7 points, 6.3 assists, 2.0 rebounds, 4.3 threes and 1.3 steals over 26.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Garland is out for Friday's game against the Bulls due to left toe injury management, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Garland will take a seat Friday after playing in three straight games for LA. The Clippers have shown a tendency to start Kris Dunn at point guard when Garland isn't available, so that option should be on the table versus Chicago.

items.headline: Garland amassed 21 points (8-13 FG, 5-9 3Pt), one rebound, six assists and two steals in 23 minutes during Wednesday's 153-128 victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Garland didn't debut for the Clippers until March 2 and made his first start last Saturday in a win over the Grizzlies. The Clippers have gone 3-0 with Garland as a starter, and the former Cavaliers floor general has posted excellent numbers so far with averages of 21.7 points, 6.3 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals per game. Garland has scored at least 21 points in his three starts while shooting 46.9 percent from the floor and 50 percent from three, so the arrow is definitely pointing up for him.

items.headline: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
items.story: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. He was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Edwards will undergo arthroscopic right knee surgery and is expected to miss up to two months, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: This is a tough blow after a torrid start to the season for Edwards, and it looks like we might not see him again until 2027. Ayo Dosunmu will likely be elevated to a starting role while Edwards is sidelined, while LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga will see a bump in usage. There will also be more minutes available for Terrence Shannon, Bones Hyland and Cody Williams.

items.headline: Edwards (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Edwards has been playing through knee pain this season, but it hasn't impacted his numbers, as he's already had two 40-plus-point performances. However, it's possible he could get hit with a maintenance day against the 1-3 Warriors. If Edwards is out, Ayo Dosunmu would have a chance to start, and there would be more minutes available for Terrence Shannon and Bones Hyland.

items.headline: Edwards totaled 47 points (19-34 FG, 5-15 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks in 41 minutes during Monday's 127-125 overtime loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: The Timberwolves weren't sure Edwards was going to suit up Monday, as the team was pondering a maintenance day for the star guard, but he was given the green light to play and put on a show. He turned in a game-high 47 points and reached the 40-point threshold for the second time through four games to open the new campaign. However, it wasn't quite enough to carry Minnesota to a victory, with Donovan Mitchell leading the charge for Cleveland to spoil Edwards' big night.

items.headline: Edwards (knee) is available for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: The Timberwolves were considering a maintenance day for the superstar guard, but Edwards is suiting up for the second end of this back-to-back set. He should be able to handle a normal workload Monday, barring any setbacks.

items.headline: Edwards (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Minnesota is considering giving the superstar guard the night off for the second half of this back-to-back set. Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon would both have added fantasy appeal if Edwards sits out Monday.

items.headline: Edwards produced 15 points (5-23 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and four steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 115-93 victory over Orlando.
items.story: After a red-hot opening game, Edwards came crashing back to earth Friday with a highly inefficient shooting performance. While it wasn't his night offensively, he did manage to record a game-high four steals, salvaging what was an otherwise underwhelming effort. The fact Minnesota easily accounted for Orlando despite Edwards' struggles bodes well for the season ahead. As for Edwards, he will look to get back on track in a matchup against the Raptors on Sunday.

items.headline: Edwards ended with 45 points (16-29 FG, 9-17 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 33 minutes in Wednesday's 131-106 victory over Miami.
items.story: Edwards was dominant Wednesday, setting a new franchise Opening Night scoring record to lead the Timberwolves to a victory to begin the 2026-27 campaign. The 2020 No. 1 overall pick averaged a career-best 28.8 points along with 5.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.4 steals over 35.0 minutes per contest in 2025-26. However, he appeared in only 61 games, marking the first season of his career with fewer than 72 appearances. Edwards has MVP potential, and while he'll face heavy competition for the award, he could at least be a finalist at the end of the year, assuming he stays healthy.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: The Timberwolves rested most of their projected regular-season rotation Wednesday, though Edwards should be back in action Wednesday. The star shooting guard appeared in four games this preseason, averaging 19.8 points, 2.3 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 0.8 steals across 22.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the Bulls, Chuck Swirsky of the Bulls Radio Network reports.
items.story: Edwards, Rudy Gobert, LaMelo Ball and Ayo Dosunmu all appear to be resting Friday. Edwards should be good to go for the regular-season opener against the Heat on Wednesday.

items.headline: Edwards ended with 20 points (5-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 9-9 FT), three assists and two steals over 28 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Edwards had trouble finding the net Wednesday. However, he has been known to have occasional shooting slumps throughout his career, so his performance against Detroit shouldn't be a cause for concern. The 2020 No. 1 overall pick had his best year in 2025-26, averaging 28.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.4 steals across 35.0 minutes, though he appeared in fewer than 72 regular-season games (61) for the first time since entering the NBA.

items.headline: Edwards closed with 26 points (8-16 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 25 minutes in Monday's 122-104 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Edwards returned from a one-game absence for rest purposes and looked fantastic, knocking down a game-high five triples en route to finishing as the game's leading scorer. The star guard has scored in double figures in all three of his preseason appearances, though Monday marked his heaviest workload yet, surpassing the 20-minute mark while also reaching 20-plus points for the first time.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) is in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason matchup with the Knicks.
items.story: Edwards is back after a one-game absence, but he'll likely still have his minutes limited, with this being the preseason. He's played well in his first two preseason games and looks comfortable sharing the floor with LaMelo Ball.

items.headline: Edwards (rest) is not available for Saturday's preseason game against Miami.
items.story: Both Edwards and LaMelo Ball (rest) will get a breather Saturday while Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon form the Timberwolves' starting backcourt. In Edwards' last appearance against the Pacers on Wednesday, he finished with 19 points, one rebound and one assist over 20 minutes in a 123-112 loss. His next opportunity to play is Monday against New York.

items.headline: Edwards recorded 19 points (5-10 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), one rebound and one assist in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 123-112 preseason loss to Indiana.
items.story: Edwards was efficient from beyond the arc, connecting on four of five three-point attempts while playing limited minutes. The star guard continues to benefit from Minnesota's revamped offensive attack, with LaMelo Ball providing another playmaking option in the backcourt.

items.headline: Da Silva ended with 23 points (9-14 FG, 5-8 3Pt), 10 rebounds and two assists across 35 minutes during Sunday's 108-97 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Following a quiet showing in Friday's 121-114 win over Toronto, da Silva erupted for his first double-double of the season Sunday. The 23 points and 10 rebounds were season highs for the 25-year-old, while the boards matched a career high he recorded back in January of 2025. Orlando will continue to rely on da Silva's production off the bench while Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) remain sidelined.

items.headline: Da Silva logged 20 points (8-10 FG, 4-5 3PT, 0-3 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 loss to Toronto.
items.story: The Magic struggled on both ends of the floor Wednesday, but da Silva managed to lead his team in scoring on only 10 field-goal attempts. He's connected on at least four three-pointers in three of the first four games of the regular season and has gone 14-for-31 (45.2 percent) from beyond the arc in that span. Da Silva's production floor will continue to be elevated for as long as Paolo Banchero (ankle) is on the shelf.

items.headline: Da Silva closed Sunday's 111-102 victory over the Knicks with 19 points (7-13 FG, 5-9 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one block over 27 minutes.
items.story: Anthony Black made his season debut Sunday, but Paolo Banchero is facing an extended absence with a high-ankle sprain and Jalen Suggs left Sunday's game early with a knee injury. Da Silva should remain worth streaming in most fantasy leagues as Orlando's sixth man for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Da Silva notched five points (2-9 FG, 1-7 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 29 minutes during Friday's 115-93 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: It wasn't a great outing for da Silva, as he was unable to replicate what he did during the season opener. His playing time remains solid, logging 29 minutes off the bench in this one. However, as a player whose overall value is built on points and threes, the off nights tend to hurt a little more. At this point, da Silva should be viewed as more of a stream-level player, as opposed to someone who needs to be rostered.

items.headline: The Magic have exercised da Silva's fourth-year rookie-scale team option, keeping him under contract through the 2027-28 season, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: The decision gives Orlando another year of control over the 2024 first-round pick, who has established himself as a versatile forward capable of spacing the floor. Da Silva will continue competing for minutes in a crowded Magic frontcourt, with his fantasy upside largely dependent on securing a consistent rotation role and increasing his offensive involvement.

items.headline: Da Silva recorded 18 points (7-14 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 0-0 FT), three rebounds, five assists and a steal across 20 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Da Silva provided an offensive spark off Orlando's bench, finishing third on the team in scoring while knocking down four three-pointers. The forward was particularly aggressive from beyond the arc, attempting 11 shots from deep and accounting for more than a third of the Magic's three-point attempts among reserves. His perimeter shooting could help him compete for consistent minutes in Orlando's regular-season rotation.

items.headline: Da Silva won't start Tuesday's preseason meeting with Cleveland.
items.story: Desmond Bane is back from his rest day, forcing da Silva back to the second unit. The 25-year-old forward is expected to play a meaningful role off the bench behind Paolo Banchero this season.

items.headline: Da Silva finished with 17 points (6-14 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals over 24 minutes in Sunday's 119-105 preseason loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Da Silva had another productive performance Sunday, with the 2024 No. 18 overall pick now having scored a combined 36 points in his first two preseason appearances. He averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.6 assists across 24.7 minutes in 77 regular-season games, including 34 starts, in 2025-26. While da Silva may not start as often during the 2026-27 campaign if Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner can stay healthy, he should continue to get his share of minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Da Silva will start Sunday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: With Desmond Bane getting the night off for rest purposes, da Silva will join the first unit. Over 25 minutes in Wednesday's preseason-opening win over the Grizzlies, he provided 19 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal.

items.headline: Da Silva logged 19 points (6-16 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 25 minutes off the bench in Wednesday's 122-118 preseason win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Da Silva wasn't very efficient from two-point range but put together a solid performance from beyond the arc en route to a game-high 19 points. The 25-year-old forward also tied for third on the team in rebounds. Da Silva averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals across 24.7 minutes per game in 2025-26, and he figures to serve as Paolo Banchero's primary backup this season.

items.headline: Da Silva ended with nine points (3-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal in 25 minutes during Germany's 96-94 loss to Poland in Tuesday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Da Silva has been staying active this offseason ahead of his third NBA season. The Magic more or less maintained the same core from the 2025-26 campaign, positioning da Silva for a bench role at power forward behind Paolo Banchero to begin the year. Da Silva averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest over 77 regular-season games (34 starts) in 2025-26.

items.headline: Da Silva chipped in zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over eight minutes during Sunday's 116-94 loss to the Pistons in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Even with Franz Wagner (calf) and Jonathan Isaac (knee) sidelined, da Silva was phased out of the Orlando rotation at times during this series. It was still a positive 2025-26 campaign overall for the second-year forward, who averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per tilt over 77 regular-season games (34 starts).

items.headline: Da Silva posted 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt) and six rebounds over 23 minutes during Friday's 93-79 loss to the Pistons in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: After barely featuring for much of the first-round series, da Silva logged 23 minutes Friday, scoring double-digit points for the first time in the playoffs. Although the second-year forward had a solid outing, Orlando is going to need a lot more from its stars and role players alike if it hopes to put an end to Detroit's season in Game 7 on Sunday. Through six games, da Silva has averaged just 4.8 points and 3.3 rebounds in 16.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva racked up four points (2-2 FG) and two rebounds across 14 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 Play-In Game loss to the 76ers.
items.story: In what was another disappointing performance, da Silva offered very little on either end of the floor. Outside of a brief period in which he put himself firmly on the standard league radar, things haven't gone as planned in recent times. In seven appearances over the past two weeks, da Silva has been well outside the top-300 players in fantasy, averaging just 8.4 points and 3.6 rebounds in 22.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva is not in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Da Silva will return to his regular bench role due to the return of Franz Wagner (ankle) to the first unit. In 40 appearances off the bench this season, da Silva is averaging 8.3 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists across 21.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva will start Monday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: With Franz Wagner (ankle) unavailable for the second half of this back-to-back, da Silva will enter the starting five. As a starter this season (33 games), the second-year forward has averaged 12.0 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 28.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva supplied 19 points (6-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Friday's 138-127 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Paolo Banchero had a subpar showing after finishing with 10 points across 31 minutes Friday, but da Silva stepped up in a big way and finished tied for the third-most points on the Magic with Jalen Suggs -- only Wendell Carter (28 points) and Desmond Bane (27 points) outpaced them. The return of Franz Wagner means da Silva will head to the bench for the rest of the season, and while he can deliver solid fantasy production as long as he stays on the court, the reduced role will clearly have a toll on his fantasy value.

items.headline: Da Silva is not in the Magic's starting lineup against the Hawks on Wednesday, Cody Taylor of USA Today reports.
items.story: Da Silva has started 19 of the Magic's last 21 games (including 13 straight), and over that span, he has averaged 13.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 2.0 threes and 1.0 steals over 30.6 minutes. The second-year pro will retreat to the bench due to the return of Franz Wagner (ankle), but da Silva should continue to operate in a prominent role, especially if the former plays under a minutes restriction.

items.headline: Da Silva accumulated 18 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 32 minutes during Thursday's 121-117 win over the Kings.
items.story: Da Silva continues to take advantage of several injuries in Orlando. He's been a solid source of fantasy value, posting averages of 14.1 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.8 three-pointers over his last 12 games.

items.headline: Da Silva contributed 21 points (9-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt), three rebounds, five assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Monday's 128-126 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: After a number of underwhelming performances, da Silva managed to get things back on track, scoring at least 20 points for the first time in his past six appearances. Although he continues to start, da Silva has struggled to put up consistent numbers, ranking outside the top 110 over the past week. In four games during that time, he has averaged 12.5 points, 0.8 steals and 1.5 three-pointers, making him nothing more than a schedule-based streaming consideration.

items.headline: Da Silva notched 12 points (4-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds across 21 minutes during Saturday's 105-104 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Da Silva continues play a significant role for the Magic amid the ongoing absence of Franz Wagner (ankle). He's started eight straight games, during which da Silva has averaged a serviceable 12.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals in 29.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva ended with seven points (2-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist over 28 minutes during Monday's 124-112 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Despite continuing to play a sizeable role, da Silva was unable to maintain his recent production. In fact, this was arguably his worst performance in the past month, during which he has managed to put up top-40 value in standard leagues. In 14 appearances over that time, he has averaged 12.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.1 steals and 1.7 three-pointers. Despite this effort, he is worth holding for the time being, at least while Anthony Black (abdomen) and Franz Wagner (ankle) are sidelined.

items.headline: Da Silva logged 23 points (8-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one block over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 128-122 victory over the Cavaliers.
items.story: With Franz Wagner (ankle) and Anthony Black (abdomen) sidelined, da Silva continues to take advantage of his extra touches and minutes. Over his last seven games, he's averaging 13.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.3 three-pointers in 30.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva will start Sunday's game against the Bucks, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Da Silva will return to a starting role Sunday due to Anthony Black (back) being out. In his last six starts, da Silva averaged 11.0 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 33.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva is not in the Magic's starting lineup against the Mavericks on Thursday.
items.story: Da Silva has started in the Magic's last six games and has averaged 11.0 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.3 threes over 33.2 minutes per game over that span. He will revert to a bench role for Thursday's contest due to the return of Anthony Black, the latter of whom will start alongside Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane, Paolo Banchero and Wendell Carter.

items.headline: Da Silva posted 19 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals across 37 minutes during Sunday's 106-92 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: The 19 points were da Silva's most since the Nov. 14 win over the Nets. The second-year forward is a player to consider as a streamer in deep leagues for as long as Franz Wagner (ankle) remains on the shelf. Da Silva has started five consecutive contests, averaging 11.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.8 blocks in 34.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva recorded 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-5 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists and two steals in 32 minutes during Tuesday's 110-109 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Da Silva continues to see heavy minutes for Orlando in the absence of Jalen Suggs (back). Over his last three games, da Silva has averaged 10.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.0 steals, 1.0 blocks and 2.3 three-pointers in 33.0 minutes per contest. Suggs remains day-to-day for the Magic, however.

items.headline: Da Silva will start against the Suns on Saturday.
items.story: With Jalen Suggs (back) sidelined, da Silva will join the starting five for the first time since Jan. 22. As a starter this season (14 games), the second-year forward has averaged 10.7 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.0 steals in 25.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva contributed 12 points (4-6 FG, 4-6 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 18 minutes off the bench during Thursday's 131-94 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Sacramento's porous perimeter defense led Orlando to go 27-for-50 (54.0 percent) from three-point range, with da Silva being one of seven Magic players with at least three treys. The second-year forward has had a steady role in the rotation in February, averaging 20.9 minutes off the bench in seven games this month, but he's averaging just 5.7 points, 2.9 boards, 1.4 threes, 1.3 assists and 1.0 combined steals and blocks on the month.

items.headline: Da Silva finished with 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists and three steals in 21 minutes during Wednesday's 133-124 victory over Miami.
items.story: Despite the absence of Franz Wagner (ankle), da Silva remains stuck in a reserve role. Da Silva has come off the bench in six of his last seven contests, during which the forward has averaged a modest 6.9 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.3 assists in 18.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Da Silva will return to the second unit for Saturday's game versus the Cavs.
items.story: Da Silva is getting bumped to the second unit with Jalen Suggs (knee) returning from a lengthy absence, so da Silva's minutes will likely be reduced to the lower-20s Saturday evening. As a reserve this season, da Silva owns averages of 8.7 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.3 triples per contest.

items.headline: Da Silva is starting in Thursday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Da Silva is starting in place of the injured Franz Wagner (ankle) on Thursday. Da Silva has averaged 11.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.0 steals in 26.3 minutes per contest through 13 games as a starter this season.

items.headline: Freeman agreed to a two-way deal with Minnesota on Tuesday, per Sam Amico of HoopsWire.com.
items.story: The Timberwolves just waived Freeman on Saturday, but it didn't take long for the two sides to hash out a new contract. Freeman is likely to spend most of his time with the G League's Iowa Wolves.

items.headline: Freeman (shoulder) was waived by the Timberwolves on Saturday.
items.story: Freeman appeared in three preseason games for Minnesota, averaging 1.3 points and 1.3 rebounds over 5.7 minutes per contest. He does have experience at the NBA level beyond the preseason, so there's a chance he could earn a deep roster spot with a club at some point moving forward.

items.headline: Freeman (shoulder) won't play in Friday's preseason game against Chicago.
items.story: Freeman will miss another preseason contest due to a shoulder injury he sustained in Saturday's 125-124 win over Miami. It's unknown if he will be ready to suit up when the Timberwolves begin the regular season Wednesday versus the Heat.

items.headline: Freeman (shoulder) was unavailable for Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Freeman exited Saturday's contest against Miami due to a right shoulder injury and has since missed two consecutive games. The forward's final opportunity to suit up during the preseason will come Friday against Chicago.

items.headline: Freeman is out for Monday's preseason matchup with the Knicks due to a right shoulder injury.
items.story: Freeman exited Saturday's exhibition with a shoulder injury and will now miss Monday's preseason game. His next chance to get out there will come Wednesday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Freeman agreed to a two-way contract with the Timberwolves on Thursday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Freeman was also on a two-way deal with Minnesota a season ago. He spent the majority of his time playing for the G League's Iowa Wolves, averaging 16.5 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.1 made threes in 39 games.

items.headline: The Timberwolves recalled Freeman from the G League's Iowa Wolves on Monday.
items.story: The move perhaps signals that Minnesota is bracing for Naz Reid (shoulder) to miss some time. Freeman is averaging 35.6 minutes per game over his last six G League games but hasn't yet made his Timberwolves debut.

items.headline: Minnesota recalled Freeman from the G League's Iowa Wolves on Tuesday.
items.story: This transaction comes after he put up 26 points (10-13 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and a block across 27 minutes in Monday's 132-104 G League victory over the Westchester Knicks. With Jaden McDaniels (hip) slated to miss Tuesday's game, Freeman may have an opportunity to play, which would be his first NBA appearance of the season.

items.headline: Freeman agreed to a two-way contract with the Timberwolves on Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
items.story: A second-round pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Freeman was limited to 22 regular-season appearances with the Pacers in 2024-25. He made a strong impression in the Summer League, however, averaging 16.6 points, 9.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks.

items.headline: Freeman tallied 14 points (7-8 FG, 0-3 FT), 10 rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes in Friday's 113-104 Summer League win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Freeman closed out an impressive Summer League showing with another double-double on highly efficient shooting. While the big man is expected to spend significant time in the G League during the 2025-26 season, his strong summer performance -- combined with Myles Turner's departure and Isaiah Jackson's (Achilles) injury status -- could open the door for NBA minutes.

items.headline: Freeman registered 18 points (7-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists and one block in 29 minutes during Thursday's 91-88 Summer League win over the Knicks.
items.story: It was an efficient shooting performance by Freeman, who also turned in a double-double to help lead the Pacers to victory. The two-player is in a position to spend the majority of his time in 2025-26 in the G League. However, it's worth noting that Isaiah Jackson (Achilles) may not be ready for the start of the new year to help fill the void left behind by Myles Turner at center.

items.headline: Freeman tallied 17 points (6-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal across 27 minutes in Monday's 114-105 Summer League loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Freeman notched his second straight double-double Monday, this time finishing with 17 points. He appeared in 22 regular-season games (one start) for the Pacers in 2024-25, averaging 2.1 points and 1.4 rebounds across 8.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Freeman racked up 15 points (4-5 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 11 rebounds, one steal and two blocks across 23 minutes during Saturday's Summer League 104-85 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Freeman missed only one field-goal attempt on his way to recording a double-double Saturday. The Akron product had an impressive bounce-back performance after finishing with only four points and three rebounds in Friday's game against the Magic.

items.headline: Freeman finished with four points (2-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and three rebounds across 11 minutes during Friday's 129-115 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Freeman suited up for the first time in the past 32 games, albeit for a brief appearance. With the Pacers' playoff future now set, there is a chance Freeman could remain in the rotation for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers. Beyond that, he will likely spend the majority of his time spectating from the bench.

items.headline: Freeman (illness) is available for Tuesday's game against Portland.
items.story: The two-way player has overcome an illness and will be available off Indiana's bench Tuesday. However, Freeman hasn't appeared for the Pacers since the Jan. 8 win over Chicago, so it's not a guarantee he'll see the court against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Freeman (illness) is out for Saturday's game versus the Hawks.
items.story: Freeman has been downgraded from questionable to out Saturday due to an illness. However, the rookie big man's absence won't impact Indiana's rotation, as he hasn't seen action at the NBA level since Jan. 8.

items.headline: Freeman (illness) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Freeman is currently battling through an illness, which has put his availability for Saturday's game in jeopardy. The rookie second-round pick last saw NBA regular-season action Jan. 8 against the Bulls.

items.headline: Freeman accumulated one rebound and one block over three minutes during Tuesday's 122-111 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Freeman barely saw the floor again Tuesday, having played more than 10 minutes only twice thus far. Despite dealing with a number of injuries, the Pacers have seen no reason to extend Freeman beyond a depth role. He has scored a total of just 20 points across 13 games, recording a season-high six points against the Rockets.

items.headline: Freeman is not in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Far from surprising here, but Freeman will return to his regular bench with the return of Myles Turner to the starting lineup. Freeman is averaging 9.9 minutes per game in seven outings (one start) this season, so he's not expected to see heavy minutes off the bench with both Turner and Pascal Siakam managing most of the frontcourt minutes.

items.headline: Freeman is in the Pacers' starting lineup for Monday's game against the Raptors, Scott Agness of FieldhouseFiles.com reports.
items.story: With Myles Turner (calf) sidelined and backup big men James Wiseman (Achilles) and Isaiah Jackson (Achilles) done for the year, Freeman will make his first career start Monday. Freeman, the Pacers' second-round selection in the 2024 NBA Draft, has seen sparse playing time this season, but he has a chance to earn a bigger spot in the rotation with a solid outing Monday.

items.headline: Freeman fouled out of Monday's preseason matchup against the Grizzlies with 3:59 remaining in the fourth quarter, Alex Golden of the 'Setting the Pace' podcast reports. Freeman produced six points (3-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
items.story: Freeman was efficient while racking up seven rebounds, tying Myles Turner for the team high. Freeman injured his knee during Thursday's preseason win over the Cavaliers, though he was able to accumulate 24 minutes Monday, so the injury is likely already past him. The 24-year-old's next chance to suit up will come in the Pacers' final preseason game Thursday versus the Hornets.

items.headline: Freeman needed assistance walking to the locker room during Thursday's preseason game against the Cavaliers after suffering an apparent right knee injury, Tony East of SI.com reports.
items.story: Freeman couldn't bend his knee much on his way off the floor and likely headed to the locker room for further evaluation to determine the severity of the injury. Freeman finished the game with nine points (3-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, an assist and a block across 16 minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Freeman and the Pacers agreed on a two-way contract Thursday, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Freeman, who spent five years at Akron, was the 50th overall pick in the 2024 Draft. It's not surprising that he was signed to a two-way contract. He'll spend the majority of the season in the G League getting developmental minutes.

items.headline: The Pacers selected Freeman with the No. 50 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.story: Freeman spent five years at Akron before declaring for the NBA Draft. In 2023-24, he averaged 18.6 points, 12.9 rebounds, 1.7 blocks and 1.6 assists in 35 games. While Freeman has shown impressive rebounding abilities for a 6-foot-7 forward, there is no obvious path for playing time right out of the gate.

items.headline: Kuminga registered eight points (3-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt), 10 rebounds, three assists and four blocks in 33 minutes during Monday's 112-100 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: Kuminga struggled to make an offensive impact but compensated with a season-high four blocks and his first double-digit rebounding performance of the campaign. The forward also connected on two triples, providing valuable production in multiple fantasy categories despite scoring in single digits. His defensive contributions were particularly encouraging, though his modest offensive involvement remains worth monitoring.

items.headline: Kuminga registered 20 points (7-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-5 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Kuminga stepped into a bigger offensive role with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, leading Minnesota in scoring while adding five assists without a turnover. His three triples and two steals added valuable fantasy production, making this one of his most balanced performances of the season. Kuminga could see increased scoring opportunities during Edwards' absence, which should raise his fantasy ceiling considerably.

items.headline: Kuminga notched 10 points (4-10 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 10 rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block across 36 minutes in Monday's 127-125 overtime loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Kuminga recorded his first double-double of the season Monday and has been consistent to open the year, scoring in double digits in every game despite not attempting more than 10 shots in any of his four appearances. Sharing the floor with Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball could continue to limit his scoring opportunities, but since Kuminga is putting up decent numbers in other categories like rebounds and steals, he's delivering solid upside. He's certainly making the most of his opportunity to play consistent starter-level minutes.

items.headline: Kuminga racked up 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 26 minutes during Sunday's 117-94 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Kuminga made the most of his limited shot attempts, knocking down three triples while committing no turnovers. The forward also contributed defensively and finished with a plus-23 rating in his 26 minutes. His efficiency was encouraging, though his fantasy ceiling will depend on whether he can establish a more substantial offensive role alongside Anthony Edwards.

items.headline: Kuminga finished with 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 0-0 FT), a rebound, three assists, four steals and a block across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 131-106 win over the Heat.
items.story: Kuminga's regular-season debut with Minnesota featured limited rebounding but excellent defensive production, with his four steals showing how he can contribute in other areas, since he'll likely hold a secondary role in an offense monopolized by Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball. Kuminga's fantasy outlook will improve if he maintains this playing time and contributes more consistently in peripheral stats, since he's not expected to be a go-to scoring option anytime soon.

items.headline: Kuminga (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: Kuminga joined several other regulars on the inactive list for Friday's preseason finale, but he should play Wednesday. The 24-year-old forward is ready to prove himself in a starting role with Minnesota after signing a two-year, $13 million deal in August.

items.headline: Kuminga (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason game against the Bulls, Alan Horton of the Timberwolves Radio Network reports.
items.story: Kuminga will join several other key contributors on the inactive list in Minnesota's preseason finale. He should be able to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.

items.headline: Kuminga (soreness) recorded 16 points (5-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 22 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: After missing Minnesota's previous two exhibitions due to soreness, Kuminga showed little rust in his return, missing just one field-goal attempt while connecting twice from beyond the arc. His efficient performance and 22-minute workload were positive developments as he works toward being fully ready for the regular season.

items.headline: Kuminga (soreness) is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Detroit.
items.story: Kuminga missed the previous two games due to general soreness but will return to the starting lineup Wednesday. The forward should see a fair amount of playing time in the first half, though his workload may be limited given the exhibition setting.

items.headline: Kuminga (general soreness) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Knicks, Alan Horton of the Timberwolves Radio Network reports.
items.story: "[Kuminga] is dealing with a little bit of bumps and bruises that we're just being overly cautious with," said head coach Chris Finch when asked why Kuminga would miss Monday's exhibition. It sounds like there's a decent chance Kuminga will be able to get back out there for Wednesday's preseason meeting with the Pistons.

items.headline: Kuminga (rest) is not available against the Heat on Saturday.
items.story: Kuminga played in each of the Timberwolves' first two preseason games but will observe Saturday's game from the bench in street clothes. His next chance to play is against the Knicks on Monday.

items.headline: Kuminga finished with two points (1-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt), three assists, one rebound and one steal in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 123-112 preseason loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Kuminga got the starting nod for the second straight game, another indication that he is likely to hold onto that spot when the season proper begins. Although he attempted the second-most shots behind Anthony Edwards and Jaden McDaniels, Kuminga's fantasy flaws were on full display, managing to connect on just one shot from nine attempts. Assuming he is given the green light to start on opening night, Kuminga is worth a look late in drafts, remembering that if and when his shot isn't falling, he has very little to fall back on in terms of peripheral production.

items.headline: Kuminga contributed eight points (2-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and two rebounds across 14 minutes in Monday's 116-97 preseason win over the Bucks.
items.story: Kuminga started at power forward and scored Minnesota's first points of the game, finishing a drive off a feed from Ball. He didn't see much offensive volume after that, but he was efficient when called upon, making all four free throws and committing no turnovers. Kuminga's place in the starting five is particularly notable as Minnesota begins evaluating how its revamped frontcourt will fit together during the preseason, and it wouldn't be surprising if he opens the 2026-27 regular season in a starting role.

items.headline: Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $13 million contract with the Timberwolves on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Kuminga spent most of his career in Golden State before briefly suiting up for Atlanta during the 2025-26 campaign. In 294 career regular-season appearances, the 2021 No. 7 overall pick has averaged 12.2 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists across 22.1 minutes. He isn't the most efficient shooter from deep, but he will add more depth to a team that also acquired LaMelo Ball during the offseason. Kuminga might initially come off the bench, though that could change along the way.

items.headline: The Hawks declined Kuminga's 2026-27 team option Monday, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Kuminga was owed $24.3 million, so this move comes as no surprise. Rowland notes that the Hawks could still explore re-signing him in free agency, as they own his Bird Rights. In 22 games with Atlanta (including the playoffs), Kuminga averaged 12.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Kuminga contributed 11 points (3-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one block in 23 minutes during Thursday's 140-89 loss to the Knicks in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Kuminga closed the chapter on another disappointing season, undoubtedly raising some questions heading into the 2026-27 campaign. Although the trade from Golden State to Atlanta allowed him to play meaningful basketball, his impact was minimal. In 22 games as a Hawk (including playoffs), Kuminga averaged 12.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers, leaving him well outside the top 250 in standard fantasy formats.

items.headline: Kuminga finished with 10 points (3-10 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT) and two rebounds in 25 minutes during Saturday's 114-98 loss to New York in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Kuminga was unable to maintain his recent momentum, struggling from the field while adding little in the peripheral columns. At one point, he missed four consecutive shots during the second quarter yet continued to force things at an inappropriate time. The series is now level at 2-2 heading back to New York. The hope for Atlanta is that Kuminga can play more like he did during the two previous games, both of which were victories for the Hawks.

items.headline: Kuminga supplied 21 points (9-14 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal in 28 minutes during Thursday's 109-108 victory over New York in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Kuminga found success on the offensive end for a second straight appearance. He's scored 40 combined points over that brief stretch, resulting in a pair of victories. This Atlanta squad is clearly dangerous when Kuminga is firing on all cylinders off the bench while CJ McCollum and Jalen Johnson lead the charge with the first unit.

items.headline: Kuminga provided 19 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 35 minutes during Monday's 107-106 victory over New York in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Kuminga nearly matched the output of the New York second unit with 19 points compared to their 20. He's averaging 13.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists through two postseason games, but he's shooting just 16.7 percent from beyond the arc thus far.

items.headline: Kuminga had eight points (3-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds and one assist in 27 minutes during Saturday's 113-102 loss to the Knicks in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Kuminga failed to produce anything of note, despite playing 27 minutes off the bench. Outside of a couple of encouraging performances, Kuminga has been unable to serve as a key contributor for his new team. For Atlanta to have a chance of upsetting New York, Kuminga is going to have to be more of an all-around contributor.

items.headline: Kuminga (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's Game 1 against the Knicks.
items.story: Kuminga will be available for the start of the postseason after sitting out the regular-season finale. In 16 regular-season appearances with the Hawks, he averaged 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 0.9 steals in 22.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Kuminga (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami.
items.story: Kuminga will join several other Hawks players on the sidelines for Sunday's regular-season finale. The 2021 first-rounder was acquired by Atlanta from Golden State in early February, and in 13 outings since March 12, Kuminga has averaged 10.2 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.0 threes and 0.7 steals over 21.0 minutes, establishing himself as a key piece to the Hawks' rotation heading into the postseason. Corey Kispert, Zaccharie Risacher, Buddy Hield and Keaton Wallace should all operate in expanded roles against the Heat.

items.headline: Kuminga (knee) is questionable to face the Heat on Sunday.
items.story: Kuminga could get hit with a maintenance day for Atlanta's final regular-season game, which would open up minutes for Zaccharie Risacher and Corey Kispert. Check back for another update on Kuminga closer to Sunday's tipoff.

items.headline: Kuminga logged 24 points (11-20 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds and three assists over 30 minutes during the Hawks' 122-116 loss to the Cavaliers on Wednesday.
items.story: Kuminga gave the Hawks a much-needed scoring boost off the bench during Wednesday's game, particularly after Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels both fouled out during the fourth quarter. Kuminga finished as the team's second-leading scorer behind Nickeil Alexander-Walker (25 points), and it was the former's first 20-plus-point performance since March 1 against the Trail Blazers. The Hawks will need more games out of Kuminga like Wednesday's if they wish to be competitive in the Eastern Conference playoffs.

items.headline: Kuminga had five points (2-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal over 22 minutes during Monday's 108-105 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Kuminga failed to produce anything of note, although he does appear to have carved out a consistent 20-minute-per-night role for himself. Since arriving in Atlanta, Kuminga has done very little to convince fantasy managers of his value, averaging just 8.5 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers in 11 games over the past month.

items.headline: Coward logged 10 points (3-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds and three assists over 31 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Coward fell just one rebound short of what would have been his third double-double of the season, although as a whole, this was a somewhat underwhelming performance. Despite some inconsistencies, Coward has cobbled together a strong start to the season, averaging 12.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.5 three-pointers, good enough for borderline top-50 value.

items.headline: Coward finished with 16 points (6-12 FG, 4-4 3Pt), 11 rebounds, three assists and one steal across 31 minutes during Monday's 110-105 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Coward recorded his second straight double-double, helping Memphis to its fourth straight victory to begin the season. After missing the second game of the campaign due to a wrist injury, Coward has put that behind him, playing some of the best basketball of his young career. In three appearances thus far, he has averaged 12.7 points, 9.7 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.7 three-pointers, good enough for top-55 value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Coward delivered 15 points (6-11 FG, 3-5 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists and a steal across 32 minutes in Sunday's 123-112 win over the Kings.
items.story: Coward recorded his first double-double of the season and posted another efficient performance while surpassing the 30-minute plateau for the first time in 2026-27. His efficient perimeter shooting also provided a boost. It's still early in the season, but Coward's consistent playing time and rebounding production are encouraging for fantasy managers, although his scoring opportunities could fluctuate alongside Memphis' other offensive options.

items.headline: Coward (wrist) is available for Sunday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Coward sat out Friday's 111-108 win over the Warriors with a left wrist sprain, but he's back in the starting lineup after a one-game absence. He started his lone appearance this season, tallying seven points, seven rebounds, two assists and a block in 28 minutes.

items.headline: Coward (wrist) is questionable for Sunday's game in Sacramento.
items.story: Coward sat out Friday's 111-108 win over the Warriors due to the wrist issue, which resulted in GG Jackson drawing the start, and Jerami Grant saw a minor bump in minutes. It will likely be more of the same if Coward gets ruled out again.

items.headline: Coward (wrist) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Coward will miss Friday's contest due to a left wrist sprain, and his next chance to suit up will come Sunday against Sacramento. With the 23-year-old swingman sidelined, Jerami Grant, Scotty Pippen, Cam Spencer and GG Jackson are all candidates for a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Coward is doubtful for Friday's game against the Warriors due to a left wrist sprain.
items.story: Coward is expected to miss Friday's contest after posting seven points, seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 28 minutes in Wednesday's season-opening win over Utah. If he's ultimately ruled out, Jerami Grant, Cam Spencer and Scotty Pippen would all be candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Coward chipped in seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and one block across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Coward didn't need to shoulder much of the scoring load with Ty Jerome dominating offensively, but the second-year wing made an impact on the glass and finished with a plus-23 rating. His 28-minute workload suggests he'll remain an important part of Memphis' young rotation, though his scoring opportunities could fluctuate depending on the team's other offensive options.

items.headline: The Grizzlies exercised their third-year team option on Coward's contract Tuesday.
items.story: Coward is now officially under contract for the 2027-28 campaign after averaging 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 25.8 minutes per game across 62 regular-season appearances (47 starts) in his rookie season. The 23-year-old swingman will likely begin the 2026-27 season in the Grizzlies' starting five when they host the Jazz on Wednesday.

items.headline: Coward amassed 13 points (5-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and two steals in 26 minutes during Friday's 117-98 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Coward delivered his best preseason performance after failing to reach double figures in scoring in his previous three outings. An excellent fantasy breakout candidate, the second-year wing should be in Memphis' first unit when the regular season tips off.

items.headline: Coward recorded nine points (3-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal across 18 minutes in Monday's 132-123 preseason win over the Hawks.
items.story: Coward drew the start and contributed across the board despite attempting only six shots. The wing's four assists were particularly encouraging, and he tied for second among Memphis players in both rebounds and assists. Coward has generated plenty of fantasy interest heading into the campaign, and his ability to contribute without requiring significant offensive volume gives him multiple avenues toward fantasy relevance. He's in the mix to open the 2026-27 regular season in a starting role, and a solid showing in preseason will boost his case to crack the first unit.

items.headline: Coward appears to be in the mix for a starting role entering the preseason, Damichael Cole of The Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Memphis experimented with several lineup combinations during training camp, with Coward, Jaylen Wells and Jerami Grant among the team's options on the wing. Coward and Wells have already logged significant minutes together, and the second-year wing's ability to fit alongside multiple backcourt combinations could help his chances of securing a prominent role.

items.headline: Coward finished with 19 points (6-10 FG, 5-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, four assists and a block in 27 minutes during Sunday's Las Vegas Summer League championship loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Coward continued his strong play at Summer League on Sunday, matching Cameron Boozer with a team-high 19 points on impressive efficiency. Coward excelled from beyond the arc, connecting on each of his five three-point attempts. The 22-year-old pro will look to take a step forward in his second season after an impressive rookie campaign in which he averaged 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 25.8 minutes per contest across 62 appearances.

items.headline: Coward racked up 28 points (9-19 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block over 28 minutes during Saturday's 101-90 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Rockets.
items.story: Coward was locked in on both ends of the floor, helping the Grizzlies punch their ticket to the Las Vegas Summer League Finals. He finished with a plus-10 rating and committed just one turnover in the convincing victory.

items.headline: Coward finished with 23 points (7-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 24 minutes in Thursday's 96-64 Summer League win over the Hawks.
items.story: Coward recorded a double-double in his first two appearances in the Las Vegas Summer League. Although he hasn't reached that mark since, he finished with 23 points Thursday, his highest-scoring performance during his time in Las Vegas. The 2025 No. 11 overall pick is coming off a quality 2025-26 campaign, averaging 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists over 25.8 minutes in 62 regular-season appearances. As long as Coward can stay healthy, he is expected to build on his production from last season in 2026-27.

items.headline: Coward finished with 17 points (7-23 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block across 27 minutes in Monday's 96-88 Summer League loss to Dallas.
items.story: Coward recorded his second consecutive double-double Monday. However, he continued to struggle shooting the ball and has now gone 3-for-14 from deep in his two Las Vegas Summer League appearances. Turnovers have also been an issue, with the 22-year-old committing eight during that span. Coward is expected to play a prominent role for the Grizzlies during the 2026-27 campaign, so his performances in Las Vegas likely won't affect him one way or another. Memphis plays again Tuesday versus the Warriors, though it wouldn't be surprising if Coward sat out to rest.

items.headline: Coward finished with 17 points (5-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists and two blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 97-96 Summer League victory over Chicago.
items.story: Coward appeared in 62 regular-season games as a rookie in 2025-26, averaging 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 0.4 blocks and 0.6 steals over 25.8 minutes per contest. Since he also played in the Salt Lake City Summer League, it's unclear how much more action he will see during his time in Las Vegas.
