However, even if the 22-year-old doesn't suit up again this summer, he's already expected to hold a prominent role for a Grizzlies team that no longer has Ja Morant on the roster.

items.headline: Coward (rest) has been ruled out for Tuesday's Salt Lake City Summer League game against the Hawks, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: Coward won't suit up for the Grizzlies' final game in Salt Lake City this summer. However, the 22-year-old swingman is expected to return when the Grizzlies open the Las Vegas Summer League against the Bulls on Friday.

items.headline: Coward logged 23 points (9-21 FG, 3-12 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three blocks, one rebound, one assist and a steal in 28 minutes during Monday's 109-100 Utah Summer League loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Coward was aggressive on the offensive end Monday, getting up a game-high 21 shots en route to a game-high 23 points. In addition to scoring, Coward produced on the defensive end, recording three blocks and a steal. Through two games in Summer League, he has averaged 17.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.5 blocks and 1.0 steals in 26.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Coward (back) totaled 11 points (3-13 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, one steal and two blocks across 25 minutes during Saturday's 111-74 Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: Coward missed the final two games of the 2025-26 season with a minor back issue, but suiting up for an exhibition game in Salt Lake City indicates he's fully recovered. Coward couldn't find his footing offensively Saturday, but he did a nice job on defense and attacking the glass. He'll look to bounce back with a more productive offensive outing in Monday's matchup with the Jazz.

items.headline: Coward (back) could potentially have more competition for touches with the Grizzlies selecting Cameron Boozer with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: The second-year pro could spend more time on the wings and in the backcourt after the Grizzlies added considerable frontcourt talent. In addition to Boozer, Memphis also selected forward Karim Lopez in the first round. The Grizzlies' depth may slightly limit his usage, though Coward still offers intriguing long-term upside.

items.headline: Coward (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Houston.
items.story: Coward will miss a second straight game due to lower-back soreness. The rookie first-rounder has impressed this season and will finish the 2025-26 campaign averaging 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists while shooting 47.1 percent from the field in 25.8 minutes per game across 62 regular-season appearances (47 starts).

items.headline: Coward (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Coward will be held out of Friday's contest due to lower-back soreness. The rookie first-rounder's last chance to suit up this season will come Sunday in Houston. With Coward joining a plethora of Memphis players on the inactive list, Adama Bal and Jahmai Mashack should see increased burn.

items.headline: Coward chipped in 27 points (10-17 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal over 22 minutes during Wednesday's 136-119 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Coward has been one of the few bright spots in what has been a lost season for the Grizzlies. The rookie posted his first game with more than 25 points since he scored 28 against the 76ers on Dec. 30. Coward has been consistent overall and has scored in double digits in all but one of his last 10 appearances, a stretch in which he's averaging 15.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game.

items.headline: Coward (back) is available for Monday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: After resting Sunday, Coward is ready to play in the second half of this back-to-back set. Across his last six appearances, the rookie first-rounder has averaged 13.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.2 steals in 26.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Coward (back) won't play Sunday in Milwaukee.
items.story: Coward will receive a maintenance day on the front end of a back-to-back set to rest his ailing back, which could result in a spot-start for Rayan Rupert. For now, Coward should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with the Cavs.

items.headline: Coward (back) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: With Sunday's game being the front end of a back-to-back set, the Grizzlies are leaning towards a maintenance day. With the way the team has handled  rotations in recent weeks, it's not a lock that Coward plays the second leg either.

items.headline: Coward supplied 15 points (5-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT) and one steal across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 130-119 loss to New York.
items.story: Coward scored in double digits for the sixth time in his past seven games, although a lack of peripheral production cannot be overlooked. In 11 appearances over the past month, Coward has averaged 13.6 points, 4.7 rebounds, 0.9 steals and 1.4 three-pointers, making him a fringe standard-league asset, at best.

items.headline: Coward contributed 24 points (10-19 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and four steals across 24 minutes during Saturday's 125-124 victory over Chicago.
items.story: Coward delivered on both ends of the floor, recording a career-high four steals while also scoring at least 20 points for just the sixth time. Although his playing time continues to be slightly underwhelming, he has now suited up in three straight games. The fact that a missed game could be just around the corner is worrying, but for now, he should be held in most leagues.

items.headline: Coward (personal) totaled 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt), four assists and one rebound across 27 minutes during Wednesday's 123-98 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Making his return from a three-game absence due to a personal issue, Coward saw his most minutes since Feb. 2, as the Grizzlies have been gradually ramping him back up after he had previously been sidelined for about three weeks while recovering from a right knee sprain. Coward has scored in double figures in six of his seven appearances since the beginning of March, averaging 13.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.6 triples per game in that span.

items.headline: Coward (personal) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Following a three-game absence for personal reasons, the rookie first-rounder will rejoin the Grizzlies for Wednesday's action. Coward has averaged 13.7 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.5 three-pointers in 23.2 minutes per contest over his last six games.

items.headline: Coward (personal) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Coward will miss a third consecutive contest for personal reasons, and his next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against the Spurs. With the rookie first-rounder remaining sidelined, Javon Small, Walter Clayton and DeJon Jarreau are candidates to see increased minutes.

items.headline: Coward (personal) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: Coward will miss both games of the Grizzlies' back-to-back set while attending to a personal matter, and his next opportunity to play is Monday against the Hawks. Javon Small figures to stay in Memphis' starting lineup due to Coward's absence.

items.headline: Hunter chipped in 19 points (8-18 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter scored 12 of his 19 points in the second quarter and finished Saturday as the Kings' second-leading scorer behind rookie seventh-overall pick Darius Acuff (38). Hunter failed to score in double digits in each of the first three games of the regular season, but over his last three outings, he has averaged 22.3 points per game on 52.3 percent shooting along with 4.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 3.7 threes and 0.7 steals over 34.0 minutes per contest. He'll continue to operate in an elevated role for as long as Keegan Murray (ankle) is out of action.

items.headline: Hunter logged 24 points (8-13 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Hunter finally found his footing, scoring a season-high 24 points, despite another loss. Prior to Tuesday, he had scored a total of 17 points across three games to open the campaign, an indication that this could be considered an outlier. While this was an encouraging shooting performance, fantasy managers certainly shouldn't overreact just yet.

items.headline: Hunter chipped in seven points (2-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter is off to a sluggish start to the new campaign. The forward has yet to score in double digits in any of his first three appearances, but he should be able to hang on to a starting role with the rebuilding Kings going forward.

items.headline: Hunter will start Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Ben Simmons is out for the season with a torn Achilles, opening the door for Hunter to step into the starting five. The 28-year-old appeared in only two games after being traded to Sacramento last season, and he averaged 13.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.7 steals across 26.1 minutes per contest in 45 regular-season games (25 starts) between the Kings and Cavaliers.

items.headline: Hunter (rest) is available to play in Friday's exhibition against the Spurs, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Hunter missed Tuesday's preseason loss to Portland for maintenance, but he's been cleared for Sacramento's preseason finale. Hunter is averaging 3.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 2.3 turnovers per game this preseason.

items.headline: Hunter (rest) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Hunter will join several other regulars on the inactive list. His final chance to play in the preseason will come Friday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Hunter is not in the Kings' starting lineup against the Warriors on Saturday, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Hunter has started in each of the Kings' first two preseason games, but he'll come off the bench Saturday while Keegan Murray, Ben Simmons and Precious Achiuwa make up Sacramento's starting frontcourt. Hunter logged only three points over 13 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to the Lakers.

items.headline: Hunter finished with three points (3-3 FT) in 13 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason loss to Los Angeles.
items.story: Hunter started at small forward but didn't attempt a field goal during his limited action. The 28-year-old joined Sacramento late last season and appears positioned to open the 2026-27 campaign in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Kings general manager Scott Perry said Monday that Hunter is healthy ahead of training camp, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Hunter appeared in only two regular-season games for Sacramento following his midseason arrival before undergoing season-ending surgery in February to repair a retinal detachment in his left eye. His return to full health clears the way for Hunter to participate in camp and compete for a significant role on the wing in his first full season with the Kings.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) has a major competitor for usage after the Kings took Darius Acuff with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Fantasy managers weren't quite able to get a clear idea about Hunter's role after his move to Sacramento, as the forward made just two appearances for the Kings before undergoing season-ending eye surgery. While Acuff is expected to play a big role and see plenty of ballhandling duties right away, Hunter could still move up the depth chart and benefit from a usage perspective if DeMar DeRozan (hamstring) winds up going elsewhere in 2026-27.

items.headline: Hunter is set to undergo season-ending eye surgery, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: Hunter managed to suit up for only two games for Sacramento before opting to undergo a season-ending procedure on his eye, but this likely won't be something that impacts his status for next year's training camp. He will end his 2025-26 campaign with averages of 13.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.7 triples in 26.1 minutes per game across 45 regular-season outings (25 starts) between Cleveland and Sacramento. With the 28-year-old forward sidelined, Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) has been ruled out for Saturday's game in San Antonio.
items.story: Saturday will mark Hunter's fifth consecutive game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Memphis. Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden will continue to pick up the slack in Hunter's absence.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) is listed as out for Thursday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Hunter is battling a left eye injury that cost him the final three games before the All-Star break and will keep him sidelined coming out of the pause. It's unclear how close he is to returning, but his absence will likely mean more opportunities for Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden. Hunter's next chance to play will come Saturday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) will be reevaluated in about 10 days, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: Hunter has been diagnosed with iritis after being hit in the eye during Friday's game against the Clippers, putting him out until after the All-Star break. Daeqwon Plowden and Nique Clifford are candidates for increased minutes with Hunter sidelined.

items.headline: Hunter (eye) will not play Saturday against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hunter picked up a left eye injury Friday against the Clippers and was unable to return to the contest. With Hunter sidelined, more minutes will be available for Daeqwon Plowden and Nique Clifford on the wings.

items.headline: Hunter won't return to Friday's game against the Clippers due to a left eye injury, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports. He'll finish with six points (1-8 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and one rebound across 25 minutes.
items.story: Hunter checked out of the contest with 2:06 left in the third quarter, and after a brief trip to the locker room, the Kings ruled him out for the remainder of the contest. The 28-year-old forward faces a short turnaround to recover from the eye injury, with the Kings returning to action Saturday versus the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Hunter produced nine points (3-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 26 minutes during Wednesday's 129-125 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter failed to impress during his Sacramento debut, continuing what had been a rough finish to his tenure in Cleveland. After the Cavaliers moved him to a bench role in mid-December, Hunter averaged 12.3 points (on 41.6 percent shooting from the field), 4.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.4 three-pointers and 0.7 steals in 23.4 minutes per game over a stretch of 20 contests before he was dealt to Sacramento. Hunter immediately moved into the starting five for the Kings and took on more minutes than he had been receiving with the Cavaliers, but he showed why his overall fantasy impact in category leagues remains limited when his shots aren't falling in. Though his value should rise with the move to Sacramento, Hunter still looks to be more of a streaming option for points, free-throw percentage and three-pointers in most 12-team leagues rather than a must-roster player.

items.headline: Hunter is in the Kings' starting lineup against the Grizzlies on Wednesday, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Wednesday will be Hunter's first look in a Kings uniform after he was acquired from the Cavaliers on Saturday. The veteran forward's insertion into the starting lineup will result in Precious Achiuwa moving to the bench.

items.headline: Hunter isn't listed on the injury report and is expected to make his debut with the Kings on Wednesday against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hunter didn't join the team in time to play in Sunday's game against Washington after being traded from the Cavs on Sturday, but he's expected to be on the court for Wednesday's clash. The Virginia product averaged 14.0 points, 4.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 43 games this season with Cleveland.

items.headline: Hunter has yet to join the Kings and won't play in Sunday's game against the Wizards, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: Hunter was traded from Cleveland to Sacramento on Saturday in a three-team deal involving the Bulls, and he will have to wait to make his Kings debut. Head coach Doug Christie said Sunday that the plan is for Hunter to practice with the team Tuesday and play against the Grizzlies on Wednesday, per Chris Biderman of The Sacramento Bee. Over 43 regular-season appearances with Cleveland in 2025-26, Hunter averaged 13.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 three-pointers in 26.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Kings acquired Hunter on Saturday in a three-team deal involving the Cavaliers and Bulls, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After a couple weeks of speculation, Hunter will move on from the Cavaliers and will fill an obvious need at forward for Sacramento. As part of the deal, the Bulls will acquire Dario Saric and two second-round draft picks, while the Cavaliers will receive Dennis Schroder, Emanuel Miller and Keon Ellis. With the move to Sacramento, Hunter could see a bump in fantasy appeal with his new team after he had moved into a bench role with Cleveland in mid-December. Over his 43 appearances with Cleveland this season, Hunter averaged 13.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 three-pointers in 26.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hunter recorded 17 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and three steals over 23 minutes during Friday's 126-113 loss to the Suns.
items.story: It was a balanced scoring attack from the Cavaliers on Friday, and Hunter ended up leading the team in that category off the bench while tying a season high with three swipes. He has scored in double digits in each of his last two outings since returning from a knee injury, and he will end the month of January having averaged 12.3 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.4 threes over 22.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hunter (knee) posted 19 points (7-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 21 minutes Wednesday in the Cavaliers' 129-99 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Hunter had been sidelined for the Cavaliers' previous two games due to right knee soreness, but he returned to action Wednesday and excelled as the team's go-to scoring option on the second unit. Prior to getting hurt, Hunter had been held under 20 minutes in his most recent two appearances, but the Cavaliers could call upon him to handle a larger role now that the team has a greater need for secondary scoring behind Donovan Mitchell while Evan Mobley (calf) and Darius Garland (toe) remain sidelined. Hunter could be in store for added usage in the short term as a result, but beyond potentially being a solid source of points, his production in other categories typically leaves much to be desired.

items.headline: Hunter (knee) is available to play Wednesday versus the Lakers.
items.story: Hunter has missed the past two games for the Cavaliers with a sore knee, but he'll return to the floor Wednesday evening, and he could see some more minutes coming his way with Evan Mobley (calf) out. Hunter is averaging 13.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 triples per contest this season.

items.headline: Hunter is probable  for Wednesday's game against the Lakers with right knee soreness.
items.story: Hunter is expected to return from a two-game absence Wednesday. With Evan Mobley (calf) out of the mix, the swingman could see some extra shot attempts fall his direction. Hunter has averaged 12.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 22.0 minutes per tilt in his last five games.

items.headline: Hunter won't play in Monday's game against Orlando due to right knee soreness, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Hunter is out of action for a second consecutive outing. His next chance to play comes Wednesday against the Lakers. With Sam Merrill out for personal reasons, players such as Dean Wade, Craig Porter and Nae'Qwan Tomlin will be asked to step up Monday.

items.headline: Hunter (knee) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Hunter is still dealing with right knee soreness and might miss a second consecutive contest. If the 28-year-old forward remains sidelined, Nae'Qwan Tomlin and Jaylon Tyson would be candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Hunter (knee) won't play Saturday versus the Magic, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Knee soreness will force Hunter to the sidelines for Saturday's game, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's rematch with the Magic. Expect more minutes for Nae'Qwan Tomlin and Larry Nance with Hunter unavailable Saturday.

items.headline: Hunter is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Magic due to right knee soreness.
items.story: It's not a good sign that Hunter was a late addition to Saturday's injury report, and his official status will be known closer to the 7:00 p.m. ET tipoff. Craig Porter and Lonzo Ball would be in line for more minutes off the bench if Hunter is unable to play.

items.headline: Hunter notched four points (1-6 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 13 minutes during Wednesday's 94-87 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Hunter was unable to have a positive impact, scoring no more than four points for the third time in the past six games. Despite a relatively consistent role, Hunter has been a non-factor for the majority of the season, currently sitting outside the top-200 players in standard leagues. At best, he can be streamed in for points and threes.

items.headline: Hunter had 16 points (7-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt), four assists, three rebounds, one block and one steal across 31 minutes during Friday's 117-115 victory over the 76ers.
items.story: Hunter provided a spark off the bench Friday, trailing only Jaylon Tyson in scoring during the Cavaliers' narrow win. After a disappointing two-game stretch of single-digit scoring, Hunter has found his form over the past two contests, averaging 16.5 points, 4.0 assists and 3.5 rebounds on efficient shooting splits. With plenty of moving parts in Cleveland, getting the 28-year-old rolling would be a meaningful boost to the team's overall success.

items.headline: Hunter notched 17 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), four rebounds and four assists across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 133-107 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Hunter scored 17 points in the win, the most he has scored in his past 11 games. His red-hot start to the season is now a mere memory, having struggled to produce at a standard league level for the past month. In 14 games during that time, he has averaged 11.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.3 three-pointers, leaving him outside the top 200.

items.headline: Hunter totaled two points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and three assists over 18 minutes during Monday's 123-112 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Hunter continues to take a backseat for the Cavaliers with Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson comfortably ahead of him. To make matters worse for Hunter, Nae'Qwan Tomlin is trending up as well. With the Cavaliers struggling, Hunter may find himself on the trade block.

items.headline: Hunter logged 12 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and two assists over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 120-116 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Hunter didn't see a big workload Tuesday, and that's been the case a lot lately. With the Cavaliers mostly healthy again, Hunter may struggle to be relevant outside of deeper formats. The emergence of Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson has really kept Hunter's appeal in check this season.

items.headline: Hunter had 16 points (5-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Friday's 113-108 victory over Denver.
items.story: Hunter returned after missing the previous game due to an illness, scoring 16 points, the most he has scored since Dec 22. After a strong start to the season, Hunter has regressed in recent times. In 13 games over the past month, he has averaged just 11.4 points and 1.3 three-pointers, leaving him well outside the top 200 in standard leagues.

items.headline: Hunter (illness) is available for Friday's game against the Nuggets, Ethan Sands of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
items.story: Hunter missed Wednesday's win over the Suns due to an illness and was initially listed as questionable to face Denver. However, he was upgraded to probable Friday morning and has been officially cleared for game action. Hunter has come off the bench in seven straight games, averaging 12.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.7 steals in 25.0 minutes per game during that stretch.

items.headline: Hunter (illness) is probable for Friday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Hunter was previously listed as questionable after missing Wednesday's win over the Suns, but he intends to play through his illness Friday. Hunter is averaging 12.3 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists over his last six outings.

items.headline: Hunter (illness) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Hunter was unable to play in Wednesday's win against the Suns due to an illness, but the veteran forward has a chance to return for Friday's home game. Jaylon Tyson, Dean Wade and Sam Merrill (ankle) will likely continue to see an uptick in minutes if Hunter is not cleared to play.

items.headline: Jenkins logged 14 points (6-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three assists, two rebounds and two steals across 24 minutes in Wednesday's 97-89 win over Charlotte.
items.story: With Ausar Thompson shedding his probable tag to suit up Wednesday, Jenkins came off the bench for a second straight game. The 25-year-old was productive, scoring in double figures for a fourth consecutive contest while bouncing back from a 1-for-6 shooting performance from downtown in the front end of this back-to-back set. He also tallied a season-high mark in steals.

items.headline: Jenkins is not listed in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Jenkins started in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers, finishing with 18 points, eight rebounds, six assists and one block across 38 minutes of action. With Ausar Thompson (ankle) back from a one-game layoff, Jenkins will return to the bench.

items.headline: Jenkins posted 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, six assists and a block across 38 minutes in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Jenkins capitalized on an expanded role with Ausar Thompson (ankle) sidelined, playing a team-high 38 minutes and contributing across several categories. His late three-pointer helped secure Detroit's victory, while his rebounding and playmaking added considerable fantasy value. However, his long-term outlook remains tied to the Pistons' injury situation, as a healthier rotation could reduce his opportunities moving forward.

items.headline: Jenkins will start Sunday's game against the 76ers, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Jenkins gets the start due to Ausar Thompson (ankle) being out. Jenkins holds averages of 7.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 26.0 minutes per contest across two appearances this season.

items.headline: Jenkins posted three points (1-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists in 15 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 win over the Celtics.
items.story: Jenkins knocked down his lone three-point attempt in the second quarter but played a relatively minor role in Detroit's comeback from a 22-point deficit. The reserve guard committed one turnover and four fouls while receiving limited offensive opportunities. After averaging 9.3 points and 3.9 assists over 72 regular-season games last campaign, Jenkins will need a larger workload than Tuesday to replicate that production consistently.

items.headline: Jenkins finished with six points (2-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists, three rebounds and one block across 16 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason win over Minnesota.
items.story: After scoring 12 points in 18 minutes as a starter Saturday, Jenkins had a quieter scoring outing in a reserve role Wednesday. The St. John's product emerged as a key role player last season, averaging 9.3 points, 3.9 assists and 2.3 rebounds in 20.2 minutes across 72 regular-season appearances (19 starts). Heading into the 2026-27 campaign, Jenkins is positioned to serve as the primary backup to star point guard Cade Cunningham.

items.headline: Jenkins is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason game against the Wizards, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: The Pistons won't start Cade Cunningham in Saturday's preseason contest, meaning Jenkins will get the nod at point guard. The former St. John's standout is expected to operate as Cunningham's backup as long as he stays healthy, so he'll get the chance to run with the first-team offense in this game. He averaged 9.3 points and 3.9 assists per game across 72 contests (19 starts) in the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Jenkins finished with five points (2-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), four assists and two rebounds in 18 minutes during Monday's preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Jenkins helped Detroit erase a 19-point deficit and connected on a contested three-pointer to tie the game at the end of the third quarter. After emerging as a rotation contributor last season, the 24-year-old will look to secure consistent reserve minutes in a deeper Detroit backcourt.

items.headline: The Pistons exercised their 2026-27 team option for Jenkins on Monday, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
items.story: This was basically a formality for the Pistons at $4 million. Jenkins was upgraded to a standard contract last season after a string of impressive performances. Across 72 regular-season games, he averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 assists and 2.3 rebounds on 40.8 percent shooting from the field, though he may face competition for backup backcourt minutes from rookie first-round pick Ebuka Okorie.

items.headline: Jenkins ended Sunday's 125-94 loss to Cleveland in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals with 17 points (4-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 7-8 FT), three rebounds and five assists in 34 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins was one of the best stories to come out of Detroit this season. He began the season on a two-way contract, but his stellar play quickly earned him a standard deal. He ended up with 72 regular-season appearances, averaging 9.3 points, 3.9 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 20.2 minutes per contest. He's expected back in Detroit, with the Pistons likely to pick up his team option.

items.headline: Jenkins closed with 19 points (8-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal over 41 minutes during Wednesday's 117-113 overtime loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Jenkins moved into the starting lineup, replacing Duncan Robinson, who was ruled out with a back injury. Jenkins made the most of his opportunity, scoring a postseason-high 19 points, adding three combined steals and blocks. In 12 postseason games, Jenkins has averaged 8.0 points, 2.8 assists and 0.9 three-pointers in 21.1 minutes per game. However, he has now scored double digits in four of the past six games, seeing elevated minutes on a consistent basis.

items.headline: Jenkins will start in Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against Cleveland, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: With Duncan Robinson (back) ruled out, Jenkins will start in Game 5. The 24-year-old started 19 times during the regular season, averaging 17.2 points, 3.6 rebounds, 7.4 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.9 steals across 33.8 minutes in those appearances.

items.headline: Jenkins accumulated 14 points (6-14 FG, 2-5 3Pt), six rebounds and four assists in 26 minutes during Thursday's 107-97 win over the Cavaliers in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Despite continuing to come off the bench, Jenkins has now logged at least 26 minutes in three straight games, running with the closers in both games against the Cavaliers. Although Cleveland typically rolls with a double-big lineup, Jenkins has increased both his playing time and production, with Detroit seemingly taking the initiative when it comes to dictating the flow of the game.

items.headline: Jenkins totaled 12 points (5-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and four steals across 29 minutes during Tuesday's 111-101 win over the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Jenkins logged at least 28 minutes for the second straight game, as Detroit opted to go with a smaller lineup in Game 1 against Cleveland. After a quiet start to the postseason, Jenkins has stepped up in the past two games, averaging 14.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 2.0 steals and 2.0 three-pointers. It appears that he has replaced Isaiah Stewart as the preferred first option off the bench, providing the team with another dynamic scoring option. With that said, should Cleveland's size advantage prove an issue in Game 2, we could see Stewart back in his traditional role, with Jenkins shifting to more of a depth role.

items.headline: Jenkins closed Sunday's 116-94 victory over the Magic in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 16 points (5-8 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, five assists and one block over 29 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins had easily his best game of the postseason, scoring 16 points in 29 minutes and closing the game over Ausar Thompson. Although he has been a consistent part of the rotation, Jenkins has mostly served as a backup to Cade Cunningham. However, he played alongside Cunningham in Sunday's win, providing the team with an additional perimeter threat. Detroit will now face Cleveland in the second round in what figures to be another tight matchup.

items.headline: Jenkins won't start Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: With Cade Cunningham (chest) back in action, Jenkins will retreat to the second unit. Over his last eight appearances off the bench, the 24-year-old guard has averaged 6.3 points, 3.4 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 17.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jenkins closed Saturday's 116-93 victory over Philadelphia with 16 points (4-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 6-7 FT), four rebounds, 14 assists, one block and one steal in 31 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins continues to impress, recording his third double-double of the season. With Cade Cunningham (chest) still sidelined, Jenkins has certainly made the most of his opportunity. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged 19.9 points, 4.4 rebounds, 8.0 assists and 2.3 three-pointers.

items.headline: Jenkins posted 26 points (9-19 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 6-7 FT), five rebounds and eight assists across 37 minutes during Thursday's 113-108 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Jenkins continues to roll on the offensive end, as he led the Pistons in scoring on the way to a hard-fought victory. He's posted 20-plus points in back-to-back games and continues to put up strong numbers across the board while running with the first unit, which is where he'll remain until Cade Cunningham (chest) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Jenkins finished Tuesday's 127-116 win over the Raptors with 21 points (5-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 9-9 FT), five rebounds, five assists and one block over 37 minutes.
items.story: Jenkins attempted just nine shots from the field, but he still reached the 20-point threshold for the sixth time this season thanks to his work at the charity stripe, where he logged career highs in both made and attempted free throws. Jenkins saw his role off the Pistons' bench steadily increase as the season progressed, and he has thrived in a starting role while filling in for the injured Cade Cunningham (chest). Jenkins has started in each of the Pistons' last eight games, and over that span he has averaged 18.5 points, 6.9 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 2.1 threes over 36.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Jenkins notched 15 points (7-17 FG, 1-5 3Pt), four rebounds, six assists and two steals across 36 minutes during Monday's 114-110 overtime loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Jenkins continues to fill in effectively for the injured Cade Cunningham (chest) in the Pistons' starting lineup. The second-year guard has averaged 19.7 points, 7.5 assists, 4.7 rebounds and 2.2 three-pointers in 36.5 minutes per tilt in his last six games, essentially making Jenkins a must-roster player as the fantasy season winds down.

items.headline: Jenkins supplied 19 points (6-12 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, nine assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Thursday's 129-108 win over New Orleans.
items.story: Jenkins has supplied the Pistons with plenty of offensive firepower since entering the starting lineup. He's put up 19 or more points in four of five starts since stepping into the first unit for Cade Cunningham (chest), and he's done so by also finding his teammates for buckets. Jenkins is averaging 19.8 points, 3.6 rebounds and 8.0 assists during this five-game stretch.

items.headline: Jenkins totaled 19 points (6-13 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 6-8 FT), three rebounds, 10 assists and one steal over 45 minutes during Wednesday's 130-129 overtime loss to the Hawks.
items.story: While Jenkins did do a nice job of handing out the dimes, he also set a new career high in turnovers and was responsible for nearly half of Detroit's giveaways in the one-point defeat. The Pistons weren't able to keep their win streak alive Wednesday, but they'll look to get things back on track Thursday against the Pelicans.

items.headline: Jenkins finished Monday's 113-110 win over the Lakers with 30 points (11-18 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight assists and four rebounds over 39 minutes.
items.story: Making his third straight start in the absence of Cade Cunningham (lung), Jenkins scored 10 of his career-high 30 points in the fourth quarter, including a mid-range jumper with 24.6 seconds left in the frame to put the Pistons up for good. After averaging just 3.3 minutes per game across seven NBA outings in 2024-25, Jenkins has thrived when thrust into an expanded role due to Cunningham absences this season. Jenkins had a similarly productive stretch in mid-November, when he averaged 19.3 points, 8.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds, 1.8 threes and 1.5 steals over 34.5 minutes across four consecutive starts. Considering Jenkins is shooting just 40.9 percent from the field on the season, some volatility with his scoring should be expected even while he remains in a high-usage, high-minute starting role. However, he should be an excellent source of counting stats, particularly in the assists category.

items.headline: Jenkins supplied 22 points (7-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 7-7 FT), eight assists, seven rebounds and one steal across 38 minutes in Friday's 115-101 win over the Warriors.
items.story: Getting the start for a second consecutive contest in the absence of Cade Cunningham (chest), Jenkins turned in an efficient overall shooting performance and was Detroit's second-leading scorer. The 24-year-old guard also led all players in assists and rebounds, finishing one board shy of tying his career high. Jenkins has played heavy minutes over the last two games and may continue to see starter-level minutes for the remainder of the campaign, as Cunningham won't be re-evaluated for another two weeks.

items.headline: Green logged 11 points (5-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-6 FT), eight rebounds, eight assists, two blocks and two steals across 36 minutes during Monday's 116-113 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Green struggled with his efficiency, particularly at the charity stripe, but compensated with an impressive all-around performance. He led Phoenix with eight assists while matching Miles Bridges for the team lead in rebounds and contributing four defensive statistics. Green's substantial workload and versatility helped salvage his fantasy production despite the poor shooting.

items.headline: Green produced 20 points (8-13 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one block in 31 minutes during Monday's 125-114 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Green led Phoenix in scoring while converting an efficient 61.5 percent of his field-goal attempts. The 24-year-old guard bounced back from a 12-point performance against Golden State on Saturday, reaching the 20-point mark for the second time in three games to begin the campaign. Green should remain one of Phoenix's primary scoring options alongside Devin Booker, giving him a solid fantasy outlook.

items.headline: Green registered 10 points (4-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one block in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 124-83 loss to Portland.
items.story: Green put together modest production in Wednesday's blowout defeat, which became lopsided early on. The 24-year-old guard endured an injury-ruined 2025-26 campaign, but he has a clean bill of health this year and should get on track before long.

items.headline: Green registered 18 points (6-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), two rebounds, two assists and three steals across 23 minutes in Friday's 119-116 preseason loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Green got off to a strong start and recorded 10 points in the first quarter alone, and he ultimately co-led Phoenix in scoring next to Dillon Brooks. The three steals were encouraging, and he's coming off averaging a career-best 1.1 swipes per game in the 2025-26 regular season, so there might be some upside in that regard. However, his fantasy value will mainly depend on what he does in the scoring column. He averaged 17.8 points per game across 32 regular-season appearances (27 starts) in 2025-26 in an injury-marred campaign. Green's scoring upside remains appealing for fantasy managers, particularly if he can maintain efficient perimeter shooting while contributing defensively during the regular season.

items.headline: Green (rest) is available for Friday's preseason game against the Jazz, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Green was given the night off during Wednesday's loss to San Antonio. However, the 24-year-old guard will return to the lineup for the Suns' preseason finale.

items.headline: Green (rest) won't play Wednesday versus the Spurs, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Green was expected to sit this one out, so the latest update isn't surprising. His final chance to suit up before the start of the regular season will come Friday against Utah.

items.headline: Green did not participate in Wednesday's full morning shootaround and isn't expected to face San Antonio, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Green is among six Suns players expected to miss Wednesday's exhibition contest. The reason for his anticipated absence is likely maintenance-related, leaving Friday's preseason finale against Utah as his next potential opportunity to take the floor.

items.headline: Green recorded 18 points (7-12 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five assists, three rebounds and one steal in 29 minutes during Saturday's 102-98 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: With Devin Booker (rest) sidelined, Luke Kennard (20 points) and Green led the scoring attack for Phoenix. The 24-year-old swingman turned in an efficient shooting performance and tied for the team lead in assists. He's scored in double figures in all three of his preseason appearances in 2026 and has shot 14-for-28 from the field thus far.

items.headline: Green played 22 minutes in Wednesday's preseason loss to the Bulls, scoring 12 points (4-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT) while adding four rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block.
items.story: The former Rocket is heading into his second campaign with the Suns and is mainly hoping to stay healthy in 2026-27 after averaging 25.9 minutes over 32 regular-season games last season due to a hamstring issue. If Green can stay on the court, he should be one of Phoenix's primary offensive threats after topping 20.0 points per game in two of his last three seasons with Houston.

items.headline: Green totaled 11 points (3-6 FG, 4-6 FT, 1-4 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist in 15 minutes during Monday's 109-107 preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Green was one of three Suns players to score double digits, an encouraging sign given all the injury concerns he had last season. While this was obviously a very small sample size, Green looked energized on the offensive end, a positive sign for anyone considering him in drafts. As a result of basically missing the entire 2025-26 campaign, managers are showing caution when it comes to drafting him, typically targeting him well past pick 100. As a player who can routinely put up in excess of 20 points per game, Green makes for a highly valuable late-round target.

items.headline: Green said Monday that improving his playmaking and pace were major focuses during the offseason, with the guard working with Hall of Famer Steve Nash to develop those areas of his game, according to Suns reporter Ethan Kinney.
items.story: Green said Nash has helped him better understand how to read the floor and control the pace of a game, which could prove particularly useful with Phoenix looking to emphasize transition opportunities this season. Green averaged 17.8 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists across 32 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, and growth as a facilitator would add another dimension to his offensive profile.

items.headline: Green could experience a downtick in usage next season after the Suns acquired Miles Bridges from the Hornets this offseason.
items.story: Phoenix is welcoming in a new member of its starting lineup in 2026-27, with Bridges set to replace Royce O'Neale in that role. The Suns effectively replaced Grayson Allen with Luke Kennard, as both players profile similarly as three-point shooters, but Bridges poses a far greater risk to Green's usage than Kennard. Green still figures to slot in as the team's No. 2 scoring option behind Devin Booker, and the former will be looking to bounce back after averaging 17.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.2 three-pointers in 25.9 minutes per game over 32 regular-season appearances amidst an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Green racked up 23 points (10-25 FG, 1-10 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, four assists and four steals in 39 minutes during Monday's 131-122 loss to the Thunder in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Green didn't have the best night shooting the ball, but he still put together an impressive stat line. Injuries derailed his first season in Phoenix, limiting him to 32 regular-season appearances. He posted averages of 17.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.2 three-pointers in 25.9 minutes per contest prior to the playoffs.

items.headline: Green totaled 26 points (8-19 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one steal in 39 minutes during Saturday's 121-109 loss to the Thunder in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Green has been struggling with his shot in this first-round series, converting just 39 percent of his field-goal attempts. The counting stats have been decent, but he'll need to be more efficient to help the Suns avoid elimination in Game 4 on Monday.

items.headline: Green registered 21 points (8-23 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 4-5 FT), five rebounds, three assists and two steals over 41 minutes during Wednesday's 120-107 loss to Oklahoma City in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The fifth-year guard is having trouble finding his shot from the outside against the Thunder's perimeter defense. After a couple of huge performances to close out the regular season, Green is averaging 19.0 points, 5.0 boards, 2.0 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.5 threes to begin the playoffs while shooting just 35.9 percent from the floor and 20.0 percent (3-for-15) from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Green logged 36 points (14-20 FG, 8-14 3Pt), six rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals in 40 minutes during Friday's 111-96 Play-In Game win over the Warriors.
items.story: Green scored at least 35 points for the second straight game, leading Phoenix to a comfortable win over Golden State and propelling the team into the playoffs. While it has been a frustrating season for Green, he appears to be peaking at just the right time. However, he will undoubtedly be a focus for Oklahoma City, meaning his recent production could be hard to maintain.

items.headline: Green finished with 35 points (14-29 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block across 35 minutes in Tuesday's 114-110 loss to the Trail Blazers in the Play-In Tournament.
items.story: Green carried the Suns offensively in a game where Devin Booker was held to 7-for-17 shooting from the field, and the former delivered his best scoring mark of the entire 2025-26 campaign. Green will need to be at his best again when the Suns play in the final game of the Play-In Tournament on Friday, either against the Warriors or Clippers.

items.headline: Green (knee) has been cleared to play in Tuesday's Play-In Game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Green was held out for the final two matchups of the regular season due to a knee issue, but it won't prevent him from suiting up Tuesday. He should be back in the starting lineup in his return, which would bump Amir Coffey back to a bench role.

items.headline: Green (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
items.story: Green will miss a second consecutive game before presumably returning for the Play-In Tournament. As a result, Jamaree Bouyea is in line for an enhanced role, potentially even entering the starting lineup.

items.headline: Green is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Thunder due to right knee soreness.
items.story: Green exited Wednesday's win over Dallas due to a right knee issue and is now in danger of missing a second consecutive contest. If the 24-year-old guard is ruled out for Sunday's regular-season finale, Jamaree Bouyea and Amir Coffey would be candidates for increased playing time. The Suns could be very thin in the backcourt, as Collin Gillespie (shoulder) and Jordan Goodwin (ankle) are questionable, while Devin Booker (ankle) and Grayson Allen (hamstring) have already been ruled out.

items.headline: Green (knee) is unavailable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Green exited Wednesday's 112-107 win over Dallas after logging only four minutes. However, after being listed as questionable heading into this contest, the 24-year-old has been downgraded, giving him one more chance to play before the end of the regular season. With Devin Booker (ankle) also sidelined Friday, Collin Gillespie and Grayson Allen are expected to be the featured options out of the backcourt.

items.headline: Green (knee) is questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Green was unable to return to Wednesday's game after picking up a knee injury, so the fact that he's been upgraded to questionable ahead of Friday's tilt is a promising sign. The team will presumably monitor him closely in shootaround and warmups to determine whether he can step onto the court in LA.

items.headline: Green (knee) exited Wednesday's 112-107 win over the Mavericks in the first quarter and did not return, finishing with zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound in four minutes.
items.story: Green picked up a right knee injury in the opening quarter and was later deemed questionable to return, though he never checked back in. The severity of the injury is unknown, though the 24-year-old guard can be considered questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers until Phoenix offers an update on his status. If he's forced to miss time, Collin Gillespie will likely continue seeing increased playing time.

items.headline: Green is questionable to return to Wednesday's game against Dallas due to a right knee injury.
items.story: Green logged just under four minutes before limping to the locker room in the first quarter. If he's unable to return, Collin Gillespie will likely help pick up the slack the rest of the way.

items.headline: Green exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's game against the Mavericks due to an apparent leg injury, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: Green limped to the locker room after checking out with 8:10 remaining in the opening quarter. If he's unable to return, Collin Gillespie will likely help pick up the slack the rest of the way.

items.headline: Green ended Tuesday's 119-105 loss to the Rockets with 15 points (5-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, one assist and three blocks in 32 minutes.
items.story: Green endured an ice-cold shooting night during the loss and underperformed in every major category. Tuesday was a significant regression for Green, who rattled off two 25-point games against Charlotte and Chicago before facing the Rockets. There's no difference between the seventh and eighth seeds in the Play-In tournament, so the Suns can tolerate an off night from Green for now.

items.headline: Green registered 25 points (11-21 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal over 36 minutes during Sunday's 120-110 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Although he lost the first half of the season due to a lingering hamstring injury, Green is rewarding his patient fantasy managers while looking to finish the year strong. The star guard has averaged 21.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 29.0 minutes per tilt in his last eight games, shooting 51.1 percent from the field over that stretch.

items.headline: Green closed Thursday's 127-107 loss to the Hornets with 25 points (10-19 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and two steals in 34 minutes.
items.story: Green bounced back from a sluggish eight-point showing Tuesday against the Magic by draining 52.6 percent of his field-goal attempts Thursday night. He led the Suns in scoring and was active as a playmaker, as he tied his season high in assists. Green has also been a force on the defensive end of late, recording two steals in three straight matchups.

items.headline: Green totaled eight points (3-10 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, two assists and two steals across 20 minutes during Tuesday's 115-111 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Devin Booker carried the Suns in this tight loss to the Magic, and there's a chance that the outcome could've been different had Green been more accurate with his shot. Green was coming off five straight games with at least 20 points, so this was just a bump in the road for the talented scorer. Green averaged 21.8 points per game while appearing in each of the Suns' 16 games during March.

items.headline: Green supplied 31 points (13-22 FG, 5-11 3Pt), six rebounds and three assists across 22 minutes during Saturday's 134-109 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Green compiled his brilliant total with only 22 minutes on the court. The Suns elected to sit Green and Devin Booker for the entire fourth quarter with the game well in hand, and the former would have almost certainly eclipsed his season high of 36 points if he had stayed in the game. Although hampered by injury for a sizeable chunk of the season, Green has been productive since returning to action. Over 26 games, he's averaged 18.2 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 26.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mogbo supplied seven points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 18 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Keegan Murray sat out Sunday with an ankle injury, allowing Mogbo to play an expanded role. Once the G League season begins, the two-way player is likely to report to the Stockton Kings.

items.headline: Mogbo registered 15 points (5-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists and two steals in 27 minutes during Tuesday's 110-98 preseason loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Mogbo co-led the Kings in scoring and posted one of the game's two double-doubles as Sacramento rested most of its rotation. The two-way forward has strung together productive back-to-back outings, though a crowded frontcourt will make regular minutes hard to come by once the season begins.

items.headline: Mogbo finished with 12 points (5-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists and two steals in 22 minutes during Thursday's 114-110 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Mogbo delivered an encouraging all-around performance, shooting efficiently from the field while contributing on the glass and defensively. The versatile forward also collected two offensive rebounds and committed two turnovers. His ability to contribute across multiple categories could help him earn additional opportunities in Sacramento's frontcourt, though his regular-season fantasy value will depend on securing consistent minutes.

items.headline: Mogbo (rest) totaled nine points (3-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and one steal over 28 minutes in Wednesday's 82-76 Summer League loss to the Celtics.
items.story: After resting Tuesday, Mogbo returned to action Wednesday. He struggled from the field but made his presence felt on the glass, pulling down a team-high 11 rebounds, including five on the offensive end. Mogbo signed a two-way contract with the Kings this offseason after making 40 regular-season appearances with the Raptors during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 1.5 points and 1.7 rebounds in 6.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Mogbo (rest) won't play in Tuesday's Summer League game against the Nets, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: Mogbo will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set for rest purposes. His next opportunity to suit up in Las Vegas will come Wednesday against the Celtics.

items.headline: Mogbo posted 12 points (4-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in 24 minutes during Thursday's 91-85 Summer League win over the Clippers.
items.story: Mogbo is coming off two seasons in Toronto, during which he primarily featured for their G League affiliate. The Kings signed him to a two-way contract July 1, and he's expected to have a prominent role with the Stockton Kings early on.

items.headline: Mogbo (undisclosed) is available and starting Thursday's Summer League game against the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Mogbo didn't play in Monday's California Classic Summer League win over the Bucks, though he'll return to action Thursday. The 24-year-old forward signed a two-way pact with Sacramento earlier this month and will likely spend most of his time with the Kings' G League affiliate, the Stockton Kings, in 2026-27.

items.headline: Mogbo will not play in Monday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks for undisclosed reasons, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Mogbo played both games in the team's back-to-back set over the weekend and will get a night off for the third game in as many days. His next chance to suit up will come Thursday in the Las Vegas Summer League against the Clippers.

items.headline: Mogbo finished with six points (3-5 FG, 0-1 FT), seven rebounds, two steals and five blocks across 32 minutes in Saturday's 79-76 California Classic Summer League victory over the Nets.
items.story: Mogbo wasn't heavily involved offensively, though he got after it on the defensive end by accruing a game-high five blocks to help lead the Kings to a narrow win. Mogbo, the No. 31 overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, spent his first two seasons in Toronto, where he averaged 4.4 points, 1.7 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.3 steals over 14.9 minutes in 103 regular-season contests. While Mogbo has some positive attributes, he will need to improve in several areas if he hopes to earn a meaningful role with the Kings beyond a two-way contract.

items.headline: Mogbo will sign a two-way contract with the Kings, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports Wednesday.
items.story: Previously with the Raptors, Mogbo will become a developmental project for the Kings. Presumably, he will spend the bulk of his time in the G League early on. Mogbo made 40 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 for an average of 6.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Raptors declined their team option on Mogbo's contract for the 2026-27 campaign, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports Monday.
items.story: After spending the first two years of his career in Toronto, Mogbo will enter unrestricted free agency. The 24-year-old forward saw a significant decline in playing time in his second season, averaging 1.5 points and 1.7 rebounds in 6.2 minutes per game across 40 regular-season outings in 2025-26.

items.headline: The Raptors recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Wednesday.
items.story: Mogbo wasn't available for the Raptors' 127-116 loss to Detroit on Tuesday while he was on assignment in the G League, but he'll suit up for the parent club in the second leg of its back-to-back set Wednesday versus the Kings. The second-year big man took the court Tuesday with the 905 in a 120-105 loss to the Motor City Cruise in the first round of the G League playoffs, playing 19 minutes and finishing with four points (2-4 FG), five rebounds and one block.

items.headline: Mogbo supplied eight points (3-5 FG, 2-3 FT), one rebound, two assists, one block and three steals in 17 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 120-98 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl played only 17 minutes in the rout while no Toronto starter saw more than 27 minutes, and Mogbo took advantage of the extra run to set a new season high in steals. The second-year forward has played more than 10 minutes only twice in seven March appearances, and he hasn't scored 10-plus points in any of his 30 NBA games this season, making him tough to roster even as a DFS punt play.

items.headline: Toronto recalled  Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Monday.
items.story: With Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) on the shelf, it looks like the Raptors are summoning Mogbo from the G League to join them on their road trip as emergency frontcourt depth. Mogbo has averaged 1.2 points, 1.5 rebounds and 0.5 assists in 6.0 minutes per contest through 25 regular-season games for Toronto on the campaign.

items.headline: Toronto recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Sunday.
items.story: Mogbo, who has been a key player for the 905, is being recalled to provide emergency depth at the NBA level. Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) continues to manage a lingering injury.

items.headline: The Raptors recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Thursday.
items.story: Mogbo won't stick around with the 905 ahead of their game Thursday against the Cleveland Charge and will instead return to the parent club as it heads into the All-Star break. Though he's not signed to a two-way deal, Mogbo will likely have more G League assignments in his future over the rest of the season since he's been unable to capture a consistent rotation role with Toronto. Over his 23 appearances at the NBA level this season, Mogbo is averaging 1.3 points and 1.6 rebounds in 6.0 minutes.

items.headline: Mogbo amassed zero points (0-2 FT) in one minute during Wednesday's 115-101 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Even with multiple injuries to other players, Mogbo failed to play any sort of meaningful role. It's been a struggle this season, with Mogbo having seen the court on just 16 occasions. In 5.2 minutes per game, he has averaged 1.3 points and 1.2 rebounds.

items.headline: Toronto recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Friday.
items.story: Mogbo has continued to go back and forth between the NBA and G League clubs, serving as a depth option for the main team but getting some meaningful action with the 905. During his last pair of appearances at the G League level, he averaged 9.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game.

items.headline: Toronto recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Tuesday.
items.story: While Mogbo doesn't have much of a role with Toronto, he will continue to split time between the two clubs this season. In 11 NBA appearances, Mogbo is averaging 1.2 points, 1.4 rebounds, 0.5 assists, 0.1 steals and 0.3 blocks across 4.5 minutes.

items.headline: The Raptors assigned Mogbo to the team's G League affiliate Wednesday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca report.
items.story: Mogbo has bounced back and forth between the NBA and G League, and he'll get some burn with Raptors 905. In 11 NBA appearances, Mogbo is averaging 1.2 points and 1.4 rebounds across 4.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Toronto assigned Mogbo to the G League's Raptors 905 on Wednesday.
items.story: With Mogbo unable to break through Toronto's rotation, most of his live reps will continue to come with the 905 for the time being. He posted 20 points (8-11 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, three blocks and two steals in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 win over the G League's Delaware Blue Coats.

items.headline: Mogbo amassed two points (1-1 FG) over four minutes during Friday's 111-86 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Mogbo suited up for just the third time in the past 13 games, continuing to serve as nothing more than a depth piece, typically dusted off during garbage time. Through 10 appearances this season, Mogbo has scored a total of 10 points. Some simple math would tell you that he is averaging 1.0 points per game, which is less than ideal when it comes to potential fantasy value.

items.headline: The Raptors recalled Mogbo from the G League on Friday, Coty Wiles of RaptorsRepublic.com reports.
items.story: Mogbo was sent down to play in a G League game Friday morning, but he'll be back with the NBA club for the team's matchup with Charlotte on Friday night. With the Raptors' frontcourt close to full health, Mogbo may not crack the rotation.

items.headline: Toronto recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Sunday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Mogbo is back with the parent club following an 18-point performance for the G League affiliate Saturday. He'll have a chance to see minutes Sunday in the absence of center Jakob Poeltl (back). Mogbo is currently averaging 0.9 points, 1.3 rebounds and 0.6 assists per contest at the NBA level.

items.headline: Toronto recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Wednesday.
items.story: Mogbo has been well outside the rotation for Toronto this season, appearing in seven games for an average of 5.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Toronto recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Saturday.
items.story: Mogbo last saw NBA regular-season action Nov. 11 against the Nets, but he'll be available off the bench for Sunday's game against the Nets. The second-year pro has appeared in five games for the 905, averaging 11.2 points, 8.2 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.0 blocks and 1.0 steals over 28.3 minutes per game in the G League this season.

items.headline: The Raptors recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Sunday.
items.story: Mogbo will return to the parent club after a two-game stint in the G League. The 2024 second-round pick has averaged just 4.9 minutes per game in seven appearances with the Raptors, and he isn't guaranteed to see the floor in Monday's game against the Hornets.

items.headline: The Raptors recalled Mogbo from the G League's Raptors 905 on Friday.
items.story: Mogbo was sent to the G League on Thursday but promptly rejoined the Raptors' regular roster Friday. The second-year big man's role in Toronto's rotation has diminished, as he's averaging 1.0 points and 1.5 rebounds in 5.5 minutes per game across six appearances this season.

items.headline: Mogbo registered zero points (0-1 FG), two rebounds and two assists across six minutes during Tuesday's 128-100 victory over Milwaukee.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl returned from his injury Tuesday, while Sandro Mamukelashvili continues to see the bulk of the backup center minutes for Toronto. Mogbo is averaging 5.6 minutes across six appearances, and until his role changes, he's safe to ignore in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Mogbo did not attempt a shot but recorded two rebounds and a block over four minutes in Friday's 122-116 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Mogbo seems to be firmly entrenched as a third-string big man behind Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Murray-Boyles (forearm). He will likely only garner significant playing time in the event of injury and/or foul trouble, as seen with Poeltl in Wednesday's contest against Atlanta.

items.headline: Mogbo produced eight points (4-7 FG), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and five turnovers in 19 minutes of Friday's 107-105 preseason win over the Celtics.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl was rested, but Mogbo returned to the bench for Friday's game with Sandro Mamukelashvili getting the starting nod. Mogbo is currently in a battle with Mamukelashvili for the backup center minutes, but it's also possible the Raptors base their center rotation on the matchups.

items.headline: Mogbo will come off the bench during Friday's preseason game against the Celtics.
items.story: After starting in Monday's preseason game against the Nuggets, Mogbo will be in the second unit Friday. Sandro Mamukelashvili will get the nod to start in the frontcourt, with Mogbo coming off the bench and Jakob Poeltl (back) ruled out.

items.headline: Mogbo will start in Monday's preseason game against the Nuggets, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: With Jakob Poeltl (back) sidelined, Mogbo will get the starting nod in Toronto's preseason opener. The 23-year-old appeared in 63 regular-season games (18 starts) in the 2024-25 campaign, during which he averaged 6.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.3 assists across 20.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mogbo (hand) has been ruled out for Thursday's Summer League game against the Warriors, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Mogbo is dealing with a sprained right hand, which will keep him sidelined. It's uncertain whether this injury will keep him out of the rest of the Las Vegas Summer League.

items.headline: Mogbo totaled nine points (4-14 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 14 rebounds, 10 assists and four steals in 35 minutes during Sunday's 125-118 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Mogbo finished as the leader in rebounds and assists, and he was one point shy from registering the second triple-double of his NBA career. The rookie second-round pick had a steady role in the rotation for much of the season and ended up starting in 18 games (including the final five contests of the regular season). Since the beginning of March, Mogbo averaged 8.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.2 steals over 27.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Mogbo produced 17 points (7-16 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, 11 assists and three steals in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 126-96 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Mogbo did his best impression of teammate Scottie Barnes on Wednesday, leading the Raptors with a career-high 10 assists en route to registering the first triple-double of his NBA career. Mogbo has seen his playing time increase since early February and has played at least 24 minutes in each of his last 12 outings. Over that span, the rookie second-round pick has averaged 9.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.0 steals over 28.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cunningham tallied 33 points (13-20 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and five steals in 27 minutes during Detroit's 124-91 victory over Charlotte on Monday.
items.story: It took 27 minutes for Cunningham to record season highs in scoring and steals, as he accounted for a third of Detroit's 15 total swipes on the night. Monday marked Cunningham's second 30-plus-point outing of the year, with both of them coming over his last three games. He'll continue providing fantasy contributions across the board for the 6-1 Pistons.

items.headline: Cunningham finished with 20 points (6-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one block across 28 minutes in Friday's 110-94 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Cunningham had trouble getting some of his shots to fall, but his efforts were still good enough to lead Detroit to its fifth victory of the 2026-27 campaign. The 2021 No. 1 overall pick is now averaging 22.2 points, 7.2 assists, 5.5 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 1.3 blocks over 33.5 minutes per contest in six regular-season appearances. He will likely continue to produce All-Star numbers and stay an all-around contributor, though he's not the most consistent shooter. Turnovers may also remain a concern.

items.headline: Cunningham contributed 30 points (10-22 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 6-8 FT), seven assists, five rebounds and two steals across 39 minutes in Wednesday's 97-89 win over Charlotte.
items.story: Cunningham knocked down a season-high four triples en route to his first 30-point performance of the year. The star point guard also finished second on the club in assists and has yet to dish out fewer than seven dimes in a game this season. Through five regular-season games, he's averaging 22.6 points, 7.8 assists, 5.6 rebounds, 1.4 blocks and 1.2 steals in 34.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cunningham contributed 19 points (7-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-5 FT), nine rebounds, eight assists and one block across 36 minutes in Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: The star floor general didn't deliver his most efficient performance, though he still finished as Detroit's second-leading scorer behind Paul Reed (22 points). Cunningham also tied for the team lead in rebounds and paced all players in assists, dishing out eight dimes for a fourth straight game to begin the regular season. He's averaging 20.8 points, 8.0 assists, 5.8 rebounds, 1.8 blocks and 1.0 steals per game so far this season.

items.headline: Cunningham amassed 26 points (9-19 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-8 FT), eight rebounds, eight assists, two steals and two blocks over 33 minutes in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Cunningham has been oddly inefficient at the charity stripe over the past two games, going 9-for-14 at the line, but that's not a trend we'd expect to continue for a career 84 percent free-throw shooter. Aside from some minor issues at the line and some carelessness with the turnovers, Cunningham has been solid to start the season, averaging 21.3 points, 8.0 assists, 4.7 rebounds, 2.0 triples, 1.3 steals and 2.0 blocks per game.

items.headline: Cunningham contributed 16 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-6 FT), eight assists, three blocks, two rebounds and one steal across 30 minutes in Friday's 128-111 win over the Heat.
items.story: Cunningham wasn't particularly aggressive hunting his shot but was still one of five Pistons players who scored at least 15 points. The star floor general also led all players in blocks and assists, dishing out eight dimes for the second time in as many regular-season outings thus far. Jalen Duren (thigh) and Ausar Thompson (undisclosed) both exited Friday's contest and did not return, so Cunningham could be asked to do more if either misses time.

items.headline: Cunningham posted 22 points (8-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), eight assists, four rebounds, one steal, one block and five turnovers across 35 minutes in Tuesday's 121-113 win over the Celtics.
items.story: The turnovers and three-point shooting weren't great, but Cunningham delivered everywhere else as he guided the Pistons to an Opening Night win on their home floor. The 25-year-old star point guard should again be a reliable source of points, dimes and defensive stats this season.

items.headline: Cunningham recorded 18 points (8-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt), seven assists, one rebound and one steal over 26 minutes in Friday's 129-125 preseason win over the Raptors.
items.story: Cunningham went to work in his limited minutes, and he committed just two turnovers. Cunningham was a top-20 player in fantasy last season with averages of 23.9 points, 5.5 rebounds, 9.9 assists, 2.0 triples, 1.4 steals, 0.8 blocks and 3.7 turnovers per game, and he could be even better in his age-25 season.

items.headline: Cunningham tallied 14 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, nine assists and one steal across 25 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason win over Minnesota.
items.story: Cunningham looked pretty sharp in Wednesday's exhibition as he gears up for his sixth season in the league. The superstar guard may end up as one of the NBA's leaders in turnovers, but he remains worthy of a first-round pick in fantasy drafts this fall.

items.headline: Cunningham (rest) is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Minnesota, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: Cunningham rested Saturday against Washington, but the star guard is back in the starting five for Wednesday's matchup in Minnesota. He should see a fair amount of playing time in the first half but isn't expected to shoulder a heavy workload throughout the exhibition.

items.headline: Cunningham (rest) didn't play in Saturday's 114-108 preseason loss to the Wizards in overtime.
items.story: The star guard wasn't announced in the starting lineup for this contest, with Daniss Jenkins taking his place, but Cunningham didn't even step on the hardwood. This was likely a precautionary move to manage his workload before the start of the regular season, so fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about his absence. His next chance to play in the preseason will come Wednesday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Cunningham is not in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason game against the Wizards, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
items.story: Cunningham isn't in the starting lineup for the Pistons ahead of this preseason contest, and it remains to be seen whether he'll be playing at all. Daniss Jenkins will get the nod at point guard over the MVP candidate.

items.headline: Cunningham finished with 10 points (3-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 16 minutes during Monday's preseason win over Phoenix.
items.story: Cunningham played exclusively in the first half as Detroit kept its franchise guard on a limited workload in the preseason opener.
