His activity level will be worth monitoring as the preseason approaches.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) will return to the Magic on a one-year deal, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports Wednesday.
items.story: The Magic waived Isaac on June 27, but there was always mutual interest in a return. Across 52 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, Isaac produced averages of 2.6 points and 2.5 rebounds in 10.0 minutes per contest before a left knee sprain sidelined him through the end of the season. He's likely going to be facing an uphill battle for playing time in 2026-27, even if he's healthy.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) was waived by the Magic on Saturday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Isaac had been with the Magic since the organization selected him No. 6 overall in the 2017 NBA Draft, but he'll now depart after his effectiveness and role diminished in recent years. Across 52 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, the 28-year-old averaged 2.6 points and 2.5 rebounds in 10.0 minutes per contest before a left knee sprain sidelined him from mid-March through Orlando's Eastern Conference first-round series loss. Isaac will now seek a fresh opportunity elsewhere, and while earning a consistent role may prove challenging, the forward's length and defensive ability may make him an intriguing option for teams looking to bolster their frontcourt depth.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Pistons.
items.story: Isaac hasn't played during this series, so his absence shouldn't catch anyone by surprise. If Orlando manages to advance to the second round, it's unknown if Isaac will be ready to go. However, even if the 28-year-old gets cleared to return at some point this postseason, he likely won't be much of a factor on either end of the floor.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against Detroit.
items.story: Isaac has appeared in only one game in the last two months, so the doubtful designation is hardly a surprise. If the 28-year-old manages to return for Sunday's contest, he may not see any action. If anything, Isaac might only be used sporadically throughout the contest for situational purposes.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Friday's Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs against Detroit.
items.story: As expected, the Magic have downgraded Isaac from doubtful to out for Game 6 due to a left knee sprain. If the Pistons survive Friday and force a Game 7, Isaac wouldn't appear to be in line to be available for that contest either.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is doubtful for Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs Friday against Detroit.
items.story: The Magic are listing Isaac as doubtful with a left knee sprain ahead of a fourth consecutive contest. Jamal Cain is already set to fill in for the injured Franz Wagner (calf) on Friday, so it's possible Tristan da Silva will be needed to pick up a few extra minutes in Game 6.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Pistons.
items.story: As expected, Isaac will miss yet another contest for Orlando. He's likely going to be listed as doubtful for Game 6 on Friday if the Magic don't end the series Wednesday.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is doubtful for Game 5 on Wednesday against the Pistons.
items.story: A sprained left knee has cost Isaac over a month and a half of action, and the oft-injured forward remains unlikely to return in Game 5. With Isaac expected to stay on the shelf, Jamal Cain should remain a fixture off the bench for the Magic on Wednesday.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Game 4 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Pistons on Monday.
items.story: Isaac has been sidelined for a month and a half due to a left knee sprain, and the Magic haven't given any indication that the oft-injured forward's return to the court is at all imminent. Jamal Cain should continue to see some playing time off the bench in Isaac's continued absence Monday.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is doubtful for Monday's Game 4 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Pistons.
items.story: Isaac has not appeared in a game since March 12 due to a left knee injury, and he is unlikely to play Monday. Jamal Cain figures to maintain a role off the bench as long as Isaac is sidelined.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Game 3 against the Pistons on Saturday.
items.story: As expected, Isaac will be a spectator for Saturday's Eastern Conference playoff game due to a left knee sprain that he sustained in mid-March. His next chance to play is Game 4 on Monday, but he appears unlikely to be available for that contest as well.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is doubtful for Game 3 on Saturday against the Pistons.
items.story: Isaac, who hasn't appeared in a game in over a month, is expected to remain a spectator due to a left knee sprain. Jamal Cain should continue to fill Isaac's spot in the rotation and see some playing time off the bench.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Wednesday's Game 2 against the Pistons.
items.story: Isaac has been limited to non-contact drills, so it was a surprise he even had a doubtful tag prior to this. It's unclear if Isaac will be able to play during Round 1, but his next chance to do so will come  Saturday.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is doubtful for Game 2 on Wednesday against the Pistons.
items.story: Isaac, who's limited to non-contact drills at practice, doesn't appear to be ready for game action amid his recovery from a left knee sprain. His expected absence Wednesday should at least keep Jamal Cain in the mix but will otherwise have a minimal impact on Orlando's frontcourt rotation.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) remains limited to non-contact drills at practice, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Based on this update, Isaac appears likely to miss his 21st straight contest in Wednesday's Game 2 against Detroit. Isaac is making progress, but the Magic aren't ready to offer a clear timetable.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Sunday's Game 1 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Pistons.
items.story: Isaac will miss a 20th straight game due to a left knee injury. His next opportunity to suit up comes Wednesday for Game 2.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's Game 1 against the Pistons.
items.story: Isaac is in danger of missing a 20th consecutive contest due to a left knee sprain. If he's ultimately ruled out, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain could see a small bump in playing time.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Hornets.
items.story: Isaac hasn't played since March 12 due to a left knee sprain and will remain sidelined for Friday's win-or-go-home matchup. His continued absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is questionable for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Hornets.
items.story: Isaac has missed over a month now due to a left knee sprain, but the Magic are leaving the door open for the forward to return in a must-win game Friday. If Isaac is ultimately deemed unable to play, Orlando would need Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain to help fill out more playing time in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) won't play in Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the 76ers, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Isaac isn't ready to return Wednesday from a month-long absence with a left knee sprain. His absence should help keep Tristan da Silva in a significant role in the frontcourt against Philadelphia.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the 76ers.
items.story: The oft-injured Isaac last appeared back on March 12, but he'll have an opportunity to overcome a left knee sprain and get back onto the court Wednesday. Isaac would likely have a minutes restriction if he's upgraded to available, which means Jamal Cain should remain at least somewhat involved off the bench in any event.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus Boston.
items.story: Isaac has missed 20 of Orlando's last 21 games, and his status for the Play-In Tournament is also in question. Considering the 28-year-old has averaged only 10.0 minutes per contest throughout the campaign, his absence won't have much of an impact on the Magic's rotation in the final game of the regular season.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Boston, Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com reports.
items.story: Isaac has missed 20 of Orlando's last 21 contests, although he logged only one minute in his only appearance during that span. It's unknown how much action the 28-year-old will receive if he's able to suit up. However, with Orlando looking to avoid the Play-In, it's hard to imagine Isaac getting a prominent role in the season finale if he's available.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Bulls, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Isaac remains without a timetable, and there's been no indication he's close to a return. He can be considered doubtful for Orlando's regular-season finale in Boston on Sunday.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Isaac doesn't have a timetable to return to the floor for Orlando and can be considered week-to-week.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Monday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Isaac remains without a timetable to return. Consider him doubtful for Wednesday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Isaac has no timeline for a return to the court due to a knee sprain. His next chance to play comes Monday against the Pistons, but his return doesn't look to be imminent.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Isaac has no timetable for a return to the floor due to his knee sprain. His next chance to play is Sunday against the Pelicans, but he can be considered doubtful for now.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Isaac remains without a timetable to return to the floor. He can be considered doubtful for Friday's game against the Mavericks.

items.headline: Isaac is out for Tuesday's game against the Suns due to a sprained left knee.
items.story: Isaac has no timetable for a return to the floor due to the sprain. The veteran forward can be tentatively deemed doubtful for future contests until the Magic offer an update to suggest otherwise.

items.headline: Isaac is out for Thursday's game against the Kings due to a sprained left knee.
items.story: Thursday will mark an eighth consecutive absence for Isaac. The veteran forward carries no definitive timeline for his return to the court and can be considered out indefinitely.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Tuesday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Isaac will remain sidelined with a left knee sprain. Orlando has yet to provide an update on his availability moving forward, so he can be considered doubtful for Thursday's matchup with the Kings until more information surfaces.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Isaac has appeared in just one game since March 5 due to a left knee sprain, which he aggravated against the Wizards on March 12. His next chance to play is Tuesday against the Cavaliers, though he can be considered doubtful until the Magic provide a medical update for the veteran big man.

items.headline: Isaac (knee) is out for Saturday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Isaac being ruled out is not a surprise, as the team has yet to provide a timetable for his return. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

items.headline: Hendricks amassed zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and one rebound in seven minutes during Sunday's 123-112 win over the Kings.
items.story: Hendricks entered the Memphis rotation for the first time this season after going unused off the bench for the team's first two games. However, he appears to be well behind Isaiah Stewart (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Monday's game at Utah, Jerami Grant and Quinten Post in the frontcourt pecking order.

items.headline: Hendricks (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 123-103 win over Utah.
items.story: Memphis cruised to an Opening Night victory without needing Hendricks in its rotation. The forward faces competition for frontcourt minutes and will need to establish a more consistent role before generating meaningful fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Hendricks supplied 12 points (5-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds, an assist and a blocked shot in 11 minutes during Wednesday's 122-118 preseason loss to the Magic.
items.story: Hendricks gave Memphis an efficient boost off the bench, but his rebound totals paled in comparison to his preseason debut. After averaging 10.6 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 26 games with Memphis last season, he's projected to play second fiddle to Cameron Boozer at the four spot.

items.headline: Hendricks produced seven points (3-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three steals and one block in 19 minutes during Monday's 132-123 preseason win over the Hawks.
items.story: Hendricks made an impact defensively despite coming off the bench, though he also committed five fouls. He's competing for minutes in a crowded Memphis frontcourt and should continue receiving opportunities throughout the preseason.

items.headline: Hendricks recorded 11 points (3-14 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three blocks in 28 minutes of Tuesday's 96-82 Summer League loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Hendricks, who has three years of NBA experience, will be frustrated with this line. Through two exhibitions, he's shooting 40.0 percent from the field with 11.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists.

items.headline: Hendricks (undisclosed) is available for Tuesday's Summer League game against the Hawks, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: The Grizzlies held Hendricks out of Monday's Salt Lake City Summer League game against the Jazz, but the forward is good to go Tuesday. He should be heavily involved on both ends of the floor for a Grizzlies squad that will be without several key producers.

items.headline: Hendricks (undisclosed) won't play in Monday's Salt Lake City Summer League game against the Jazz, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Hendricks will be held out of Monday's contest but can be considered day-to-day moving forward. His final opportunity to suit up in Salt Lake City this summer will come Tuesday against the Hawks.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) recorded 15 points (5-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 12 minutes during Saturday's 111-74 Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: Hendricks sat out the final two games of the 2025-26 season with a minor thumb injury, but he's since recovered. The third-year forward got whatever he wanted against the Thunder's Summer League squad, missing only one shot in his limited minutes.

items.headline: The Grizzlies' selection of Cameron Boozer with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft creates additional frontcourt competition, but Hendricks (thumb) should still have an opportunity to carve out a significant role entering 2026-27.
items.story: Acquired from Utah in the Jaren Jackson trade, the 22-year-old showed encouraging flashes after arriving in Memphis, averaging double figures while displaying his defensive versatility and floor-spacing ability. Boozer's arrival could reduce some of Hendricks' offensive opportunities, but the former lottery pick remains an intriguing developmental piece as the Grizzlies continue building their young core.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) will not play Sunday against the Rockets.
items.story: The thumb injury will end Hendricks' season, as Sunday marks the final game of 2025-26 for the Grizzlies. The third-year forward was dealt to the Grizzlies from the Jazz mid-season. In his 26 regular-season appearances with Memphis, he averaged 10.6 points, 4.7 rebounds, 1.4 steals, 1.2 assists and 0.8 blocks in 24.1 minutes.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Hendricks will be held out of Memphis' penultimate regular-season game due to a right thumb sprain, and his next opportunity to suit up will come Sunday in Houston. With Olivier-Maxence Prosper (ankle) doubtful, Taj Gibson, Toby Okani and Dariq Whitehead are candidates for increased run in the injury-plagued Memphis frontcourt.

items.headline: Hendricks ended with 16 points (6-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 136-119 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Even though Hendricks has missed three of the Grizzlies' last nine games due to minor injuries, he's been starting regularly when available, and he could be a decent option to stream if you need frontcourt depth late in the season. He's averaging 8.0 points and 5.0 rebounds in 22.7 minutes per game in those six outings, however, so his fantasy upside is still limited despite his starting role.

items.headline: Hendricks will start Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: With Olivier-Maxence Prosper (ankle) unavailable, Hendricks will join the first unit in his return from a one-game absence due to a right thumb sprain. Over 10 starts since the All-Star break, the 22-year-old forward has averaged 7.2 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 24.7 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Hendricks sat out Monday's loss to the Cavaliers -- the second leg of a back-to-back -- due to a right thumb sprain. However, he's set to return to action Wednesday and should play a sizable role with Olivier-Maxence Prosper (ankle) doubtful and GG Jackson (knee) out.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hendricks will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a right thumb sprain. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against the Nuggets. Olivier-Maxence Prosper, Toby Okani and Dariq Whitehead are candidates for increased playing time in Hendricks' stead.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) is doubtful for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: A right thumb sprain is likely to prevent Hendricks from playing Monday. Dariq Whitehead and Toby Okani should soak up more playing time in the frontcourt versus Cleveland.

items.headline: Hendricks will start Friday versus the Raptors.
items.story: Olivier-Maxence Prosper (back) is out, so Hendricks will get the start, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Javon Small, Cedric Coward, Rayan Rupert and GG Jackson. As a starter this season, Hendricks has averaged 5.9 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.

items.headline: Hendricks (finger) is off the injury report for Friday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Following a one-game absence with a finger injury during Wednesday's loss to New York, Hendricks is available for Friday's action. Over his last 10 appearances, the third-year forward has averaged 10.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.2 blocks in 25.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hendricks (finger) has been ruled out ahead of Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Hendricks was initially listed as doubtful, so the latest update just confirms what most had expected. His next chance to play will be Thursday versus Toronto. In the meantime, Tyler Burton could see increased action without Hendricks on the floor.

items.headline: Hendricks (finger) is listed as doubtful ahead of Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Hendricks started Monday's 131-105 loss to Phoenix. However, he likely won't suit up for Wednesday's meeting with the visiting Knicks. Tyler Burton and Rayan Rupert would be candidates to see increased playing time if Hendricks is ultimately ruled out.

items.headline: Hendricks is starting Monday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Hendricks took a seat for Saturday's game against the Bulls due to a thumb injury, but he's been cleared to return and will run with the first unit. He was ineffective as a scorer in his previous two starts, totaling seven points on 3-of-18 shooting from the field over that brief stretch.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Monday's meeting with the Suns.
items.story: Hendricks skipped Saturday's win over the Bulls, with that one being the second game in a back-to-back set, but he'll be back in action Monday evening. As a member of the Grizzlies, Hendricks has recorded averages of 10.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.5 triples, 1.4 steals and 1.0 blocks per contest.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hendricks will take a seat for Saturday's contest. His absence should mean more opportunities for Rayan Rupert and Tyler Burton, while Olivier-Maxence Prosper and GG Jackson handle the brunt of the minutes at the power forward and center positions.

items.headline: Hendricks is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Bulls due to right thumb soreness.
items.story: Hendricks is at risk of missing Saturday's closing end of a back-to-back, as the 22-year-old forward played 30 minutes Friday night. If Hendricks doesn't suit up, Rayan Rupert and Tyler Burton would be in line for more minutes.

items.headline: Hendricks is in the Grizzlies' starting lineup against the Spurs on Wednesday.
items.story: Hendricks has come off the bench in each of the Grizzlies' last two games, but he will start Wednesday alongside Javon Small, Cedric Coward, GG Jackson and Olivier-Maxence Prosper. Hendricks made his last start against the Celtics this past Friday, when he played 29 minutes and finished with 12 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks in a 117-112 loss.

items.headline: Hendricks amassed 14 points (4-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, three assists, one block and three steals over 25 minutes during Saturday's 124-101 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Hendricks moved back to the bench with the return of GG Jackson (knee) to the first unit, but he still found a way to be productive on both ends of the court. Hendricks has scored in double digits in five of his last six games regardless of his role, so he's a player worth keeping close tabs on most formats. If available in your league, he could be a decent addition from the waiver wire.

items.headline: Hendricks isn't part of the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the Hornets, Roderick Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.story: Hendricks drew a start last time out for the shorthanded Grizzlies, but he'll move back to a reserve role with GG Jackson back in action. In his last six games, Hendricks is averaging 12.2 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.2 steals and 1.7 blocks across 25.5 minutes.

items.headline: Hendricks will start Friday versus the Celtics.
items.story: GG Jackson (knee) and Taj Gibson (foot) are out, so Hendricks should see heavy minutes against the Celtics. Javon Small, Ty Jerome, Jaylen Wells and Olivier-Maxence Prosper will round out the first unit for Friday's game.

items.headline: Hendricks finished with 13 points (6-18 FG, 1-10 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist, three blocks and six steals in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 125-118 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Hendricks might have ended with 13 points, but the fact that he needed 18 shots to achieve that mark means he was far from efficient on that end of the floor. The same can't be said about what he delivered defensively, as Hendricks' nine steals-plus-blocks were his best mark of the campaign by a wide margin. Plus, those figures were season highs in each category. Hendricks is averaging 12.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.5 steals, 1.4 assists and 1.2 blocks per game since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Hendricks is not in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hendricks has started two of the past three contests and logged 30 minutes in Friday's start, though he'll revert to a bench role Monday as the Grizzlies roll out a lineup of Walter Clayton, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Rayan Rupert and Olivier-Maxence Prosper. Hendricks has come off the bench in 38 of his 48 appearances this season, averaging 7.0 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 16.8 minutes per contest as a reserve.

items.headline: Hendricks totaled seven points (2-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-5 FT), five rebounds, two blocks and two steals over 30 minutes during Friday's 126-110 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Hendricks moved into the starting lineup for the second time in the past three games, although he was unable to repeat his heroics from the night before. However, while his offensive production was lacking in this one, he has now recorded 12 combined steals-plus-blocks in his past four games. During that time, he has been a borderline top-50 player, averaging 12.5 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.3 steals, 1.8 blocks and 1.8 three-pointers.

items.headline: Hendricks will start Friday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: With GG Jackson (foot) sidelined, Hendricks will join the first unit. As a starter for the Grizzlies this season (three games), the 22-year-old forward has averaged 7.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 24.7 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Hendricks notched 17 points (7-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt), 10 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal in 24 minutes during Thursday's 120-112 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: After minimal production as a starter in Philadelphia on Tuesday, Hendricks was replaced by GG Jackson in the first five Thursday, but the former was still able to be productive. Since the All-Star break, Hendricks has missed two contests, both parts of back-to-back sets, and averaged 12.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.1 blocks and 0.9 steals in 24.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hendricks isn't in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Hendricks started Tuesday's game against Philly, but he'll revert to the bench Thursday with the Grizzlies choosing to see what GG Jackson can do in a starting role. Hendricks logged 26 minutes off the bench Saturday and should see plenty of playing time against Dallas given the fact that he's one of seven active Memphis players for Thursday's tilt.

items.headline: Hendricks logged eight points (3-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block over 25 minutes during the Grizzlies' 139-129 loss to the 76ers on Tuesday.
items.story: Hendricks made his return Tuesday from a one-game absence due to a thumb injury, but he didn't move the needle much in the loss. It was his ninth start of the season (and first since Feb. 21), though whether he remains in the starting lineup over GG Jackson moving forward remains to be seen.

items.headline: Hendricks will start Tuesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Hendricks will return from a one-game absence due to thumb soreness and enter the starting lineup, pushing GG Jackson to the bench. Over two starts for Memphis, Hendricks has averaged 6.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 24.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) is off the injury report for Tuesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Hendricks sat out Monday's loss to the Nets with a thumb injury, but he's good to go Tuesday. Over 12 appearances since joining Memphis, Hendricks has averaged 10.9 points, 4.7 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 23.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hendricks (thumb) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Nets.
items.story: As expected, Hendricks will miss the front end of this back-to-back set due to right thumb soreness. His next opportunity to play will come Tuesday in Philadelphia. With the Grizzlies set to be extremely shorthanded in the frontcourt, GG Jackson, Rayan Rupert and Olivier-Maxence Prosper should all see significant minutes.

items.headline: Hendricks is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against the Nets due to right thumb soreness.
items.story: Hendricks may have picked up the injury during the Grizzlies' 123-120 loss to the Clippers on Saturday, when he finished with 18 points, four rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers over 26 minutes. There are several Memphis players listed on the injury report, so Olivier-Maxence Prosper, Rayan Rupert and GG Jackson are all in line for more minutes in Monday's road tilt.

items.headline: Hendricks logged 18 points (7-8 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals over 26 minutes during the Grizzlies' 123-120 loss to the Clippers on Saturday.
items.story: Hendricks needed only eight shots to finish as the Grizzlies' second-leading scorer behind Ty Jerome (21 points) in Saturday's close loss. Hendricks also contributed on the other end of the floor with four combined steals-plus-blocks, and it was the first time this season that he finished with at least two blocks and two steals in the same game. Over his last six outings, Hendricks has averaged 13.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 2.0 threes, 1.2 blocks and 1.0 steals over 25.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Embiid (foot) is available for Monday's game against the Bulls, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: Embiid will shake off his questionable tag and return from a one-game absence due to right foot plantar fascia injury management. The star big man's return will leave fewer minutes available for the likes of Adem Bona and Jabari Walker. Embiid has reached the 20-point threshold in three of his five regular-season outings, averaging 19.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 1.8 combined steals-plus-blocks in 35.2 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Embiid (foot) is questionable for Monday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Embiid missed Saturday's 109-104 win over Charlotte due to right foot plantar fascia injury management, and he's now in jeopardy of missing a second consecutive game for the same reason. If he's unable to play Monday, Adem Bona will likely earn another start, with Jabari Walker getting additional minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Embiid (foot) is out for Saturday's game in Charlotte.
items.story: It's the second night of a back-to-back set, so Embiid will get hit with a maintenance day. Adem Bona will have the opportunity to start Saturday with Embiid inactive.

items.headline: Embiid closed Friday's 98-93 victory over the Knicks with 10 points (3-12 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, seven assists, one block and one steal in 33 minutes.
items.story: Embiid didn't have a great shooting night Friday, but he did fill up the box score and finished second on the 76ers in assists behind LeBron James (eight). Through five regular-season games, Embiid is averaging 19.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 1.0 blocks over what is currently a career-high 35.2 minutes per contest. It wouldn't be surprising to see the veteran center sit for the second leg of the Sixers' back-to-back set Saturday against the Hornets.

items.headline: Embiid closed Wednesday's 114-109 win over the Pacers with 21 points (9-17 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and one block across 39 minutes.
items.story: Embiid continued his strong start to the season, recording his third double-double in four appearances. He has been a borderline top-50 player thus far, averaging 21.5 points, 10.0 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.8 combined steals and blocks. However, while the production has been fantastic, the fact that he has averaged 35.8 minutes per game could be cause for concern moving forward. He played 39 minutes in Wednesday's win, barely leaving the floor during the second half. If you have reservations when it comes to his long-term availability, now might be a good time to try and execute a sell-high.

items.headline: Embiid (foot) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: The star big man is set to return Wednesday after sitting out the second leg of Philadelphia's most recent back-to-back. With the 76ers back at full strength, Dean Wade and Adem Bona should fall into lesser roles.

items.headline: Embiid has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Detroit due to right plantar fasciitis management.
items.story: Embiid will be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set after posting a 28-point triple-double in Saturday's win over Milwaukee. Adem Bona will likely see a significant bump in minutes in Embiid's stead.

items.headline: Embiid produced 28 points (8-20 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 12-14 FT), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and four turnovers across 36 minutes in Saturday's 127-116 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Embiid notched his first triple-double of the year, setting season highs in points and dimes to go with a plus-18 differential in the win. Embiid said Thursday that he intends to play in only one game of the 76ers' back-to-back set, so managers should be prepared for him to sit out Sunday's meeting with the Pistons.

items.headline: Embiid (rest) is off the injury report for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: The star big man told reporters following Thursday's comeback win over the Cavaliers that he'd play only one half of this back-to-back set, so he's in line to sit out Sunday's showdown with the Pistons as opposed to Saturday. With LeBron James (back) a candidate to miss Saturday's contest, Embiid could have more usage on his plate.

items.headline: Embiid recorded 24 points (8-16 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 7-9 FT), seven rebounds and one assist in 34 minutes during Thursday's 114-106 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Embiid played a critical role in Philly's impressive second-half comeback, finishing second on his squad in scoring behind Tyrese Maxey's team-high 32 points. Embiid was much more polished on the offensive end during his second appearance of the season after going 4-for-15 from the field Tuesday against the Knicks. Embiid stated after Thursday's victory that he'll sit for one of his team's matchups over the weekend, per Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com, though he failed to specify whether he'd sit out the first or second game of the back-to-back. The 76ers are scheduled to face Milwaukee on Saturday and Detroit on Sunday.

items.headline: Embiid ended with 13 points (4-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, six assists, three blocks and two steals in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 106-100 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Embiid tied for fourth place in scoring for the 76ers on Tuesday, but he did lead the team in rebounding while sacrificing some usage to accommodate for the arrivals of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. Embiid endured a start-stop 2025-26 campaign due to various injuries, and the star big man is looking to play at least 60 regular-season games this year for the first time since 2022-23.

items.headline: Embiid finished with 27 points (7-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 11-13 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block over 29 minutes in Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime loss to Boston.
items.story: Embiid didn't play when these two clubs met Saturday but was on the floor for the rematch. He had four turnovers, though he was still the most productive starter overall for Philadelphia on Friday night. The 2023 MVP finished the 2025-26 campaign with averages of 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 steals across 31.6 minutes per contest. However, he was limited to 38 regular-season games. Embiid should still be considered one of the top players in the NBA, but his health will be a significant concern for the rest of his career.

items.headline: Embiid (rest) will play in Friday's preseason finale against Boston, Gary Washburn of The Boston Globe reports.
items.story: Embiid was held out of Saturday's game against Boston for maintenance and there is no injury to report. He will get some final reps Friday ahead of Opening Night.

items.headline: Embiid (rest) is out for Saturday's exhibition against the Celtics, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Head coach Nick Nurse is resting most of the vets for Saturday's exhibition, so Jabari Walker could get all the run he can handle. Embiid should return for Friday's preseason rematch with Boston.

items.headline: Embiid closed with six points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in 24 minutes during Thursday's 114-108 preseason loss to Brooklyn.
items.story: After sitting out the first preseason game, Embiid made his first appearance for the new-look 76ers, turning in an indifferent performance. Although he managed to chip in across the board, he struggled from the field and was careless with the ball, racking up a team-high eight turnovers. It was certainly encouraging to see him suiting up for a preseason game, indicating that he should be ready to go for Opening Night.

items.headline: Embiid (rest) is set to play in Thursday's preseason game against the Nets, per ESPN.com.
items.story: The 76ers are planning to have their entire Opening Night starting lineup available Thursday. Embiid, who sat out the preseason opener, should get some run in the first half while Philadelphia gets its first look at its new-look roster.

items.headline: Embiid (rest) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Knicks, Chris Hine of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: Embiid, LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey and Anfernee Simons, among others, will take a seat for the preseason opener, leaving plenty of usage available for second-year guard VJ Edgecombe and rookie Labaron Philon. It's unclear if Embiid will suit up Thursday in Brooklyn, but the big man's workload will continue to be closely managed during the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Embiid's workload will continue to be closely managed during the 2026-27 season, head coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday, according to Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com.
items.story: Nurse said Philadelphia is already working through plans for Embiid and LeBron James on back-to-backs while mapping out their workloads for the next month. Embiid entered training camp without restrictions and was a full participant in Tuesday's opening practice, but the 76ers' early planning indicates they'll remain cautious with the veteran center despite his encouraging health entering the season.

items.headline: Hyland racked up 19 points (8-16 FG, 3-9 3Pt), eight assists and one steal across 20 minutes during Friday's 127-101 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Hyland finished just two assists shy of a double-double and recorded his second straight game with double-digit points and over 15 minutes of action. It's still early, but the early signs show Hyland could be in line for a bigger role in the backcourt with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Hyland contributed zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and two assists in five minutes during Monday's 127-125 overtime loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hyland barely factored into Minnesota's rotation, making his lone appearance during a brief stretch in the second quarter. The guard has played 15 minutes or fewer in each of his four appearances this season, limiting his fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Hyland (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: Hyland was one of many Timberwolves regulars who sat out the preseason finale, though he should play Wednesday. The 26-year-old guard averaged 8.5 points, 2.6 assists and 1.8 rebounds in 16.6 minutes per game across 71 regular-season appearances (three starts) in 2025-26.

items.headline: Hyland (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason game against Chicago, Alan Horton of the Timberwolves Radio Network reports.
items.story: Hyland will receive Friday night off, joining several other key players on the inactive list for Minnesota. Isaiah Evans and Zyon Pullin will both likely see a significant bump in minutes Friday.

items.headline: Hyland finished Saturday's 125-124 preseason win over the Heat with 23 points (6-9 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds, four assists and three steals over 21 minutes.
items.story: Hyland was moved into the Timberwolves' starting five due to the absences of both Anthony Edwards (rest) and LaMelo Ball (rest). Hyland answered the call by leading Minnesota in points, with most of his damage coming from beyond the arc. The sixth-year pro averaged 16.6 minutes per game while mostly operating in a bench role last season, but Hyland could see a bump in playing time given that Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) will be out for most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Hyland is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason matchup with the Heat.
items.story: Terrence Shannon, Jaylen Clark, Trey Lyles and Joan Beringer will join Hyland in the first unit for Saturday's exhibition. The Timberwolves are sitting out seven players, so Hyland could see quality minutes Saturday.

items.headline: Hyland closed with 10 points (3-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one assist, one steal and one block in 11 minutes during Wednesday's 123-112 preseason loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Hyland was used sparingly off the bench, although he did make the most of his time on the floor, ending as one of five Minnesota players to score double digits. Despite a proven ability to score the basketball, it would appear as though Hyland could struggle to carve out a meaningful role this season. At best, he should be on the streaming radar if and when those ahead of him in the rotation are struck down with injury or illness.

items.headline: Hyland re-signed with the Timberwolves on a one-year minimum deal, according to Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast'.
items.story: Hyland stated that he wanted to return to Minnesota after the Game 6 loss to the Spurs on May 15, and he got his wish Tuesday. Hyland should have a bench role in Minnesota's rotation in 2026-27, but he doesn't figure to play a large role while competing for minutes in a backcourt group led by Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball. Hyland averaged 8.5 points, 1.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 16.6 minutes per tilt across 71 regular-season contests last season.

items.headline: Hyland closed with three points (1-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt) and one rebound over eight minutes during Friday's 139-109 loss to the Spurs in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Hyland saw meaningful minutes off the Timberwolves' bench during the first round of the Western Conference playoffs against the Nuggets. However, he saw his playing time diminish during the second round, and all eight of his minutes in Friday's loss came during garbage time in the fourth quarter. Hyland is an unrestricted free agent but expressed his desire to return to the Timberwolves, as he told reporters Friday that "[Minnesota] feels like where I belong so I definitely want to come back," per Chris Hine of The Minnesota Star Tribune. Hyland averaged 16.6 minutes per game during the regular season while mostly operating off the bench, but if he returns to the Timberwolves for the 2026-27 campaign, he could be in line for an expanded role due to the absence of Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles).

items.headline: Hyland (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Friday in the Timberwolves' 115-108 loss to the Spurs in Game 3 of a Western Conference Semifinals series.
items.story: With Anthony Edwards (41 minutes) and Ayo Dosunmu (32 minutes) both being able to take on full workloads in Game 3, Minnesota didn't have any playing time in the backcourt left over for Hyland, who dropped out of head coach Chris Finch's eight-man rotation. Hyland had appeared in each of the Timberwolves' first eight playoff games, averaging 5.4 points, 1.9 assists, 1.4 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers in 13.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hyland (knee) is available for Thursday's Game 6 against the Nuggets.
items.story: Hyland was carrying a questionable tag prior to this update, but he was able to go through shootaround without any setbacks. With the team shorthanded, Hyland is expected to play a key role Thursday.

items.headline: Hyland is questionable for Game 6 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Nuggets on Thursday due to left knee soreness.
items.story: It's a new injury for Hyland, who shapes up as a true game-time decision for Minnesota's must-win contest. The combo guard would be in line for a fairly big role in the absences of Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles), but the likes of Mike Conley, Terrence Shannon and Kyle Anderson would be needed to help pick up the slack if Hyland is also sidelined Thursday.

items.headline: Hyland (hip) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's Game 1 against the Nuggets.
items.story: Hyland missed Minnesota's last two regular-season games due to a right hip issue, but he's good to go for the start of the playoffs. The 25-year-old guard averaged 14.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.2 steals in 24.4 minutes per contest over five regular-season appearances in April. If Anthony Edwards (knee) is downgraded from questionable to out, Hyland could see a bump in playing time Saturday.

items.headline: Hyland (hip) won't play Sunday against the Pelicans.
items.story: Hyland won't play in the Timberwolves' regular-season finale due to maintenance of a right hip injury, and this will be his second straight absence. The combo guard is expected to be available for the postseason, though. Hyland will end the regular season averaging 8.5 points and 2.6 dimes per game across 71 appearances (three starts).

items.headline: Hyland (hip) is out for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Hyland will miss his first game since Dec. 6 due to soreness in his right hip. Mike Conley and Terrence Shannon could see increased run with this news.

items.headline: Hyland (hip) is questionable for Friday's game against Houston.
items.story: Hyland is in danger of missing his first game since Dec. 6 due to right hip soreness. If the 25-year-old guard is unable to suit up, Mike Conley and Terrence Shannon would be candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Hyland provided 19 points (5-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, seven assists and one steal in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 124-104 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Hyland was sharp with his shot and looked excellent as a playmaker, ending just three assists away from what would've been his first double-double of the season. Hyland has logged over 20 minutes in all but one of his last 11 appearances off the bench and is making the most with that playing time, averaging 15.5 points, 2.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.1 steals per game over that stretch.

items.headline: Hyland ended Sunday's 122-108 loss to the Hornets with 18 points (5-11 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals over 29 minutes.
items.story: With Anthony Edwards (knee) getting the night off, Hyland stepped up in a big way for Minnesota. Edwards seems to be struggling to get back to 100 percent, making Hyland an intriguing streamer to close out the regular season.

items.headline: Hyland registered 21 points (7-14 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and two steals in 30 minutes during Friday's 115-103 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Hyland recorded at least 20 points for the first time in his past five games, rewarding anyone who took a chance on him. While this was certainly an encouraging performance, managers may want to temper their expectations, given that he had scored a total of 32 points in his previous four outings. At best, he can be streamed in on low-volume nights, at least until Jaden McDaniels returns from his knee injury.

items.headline: Hyland closed Saturday's 109-87 loss to the Pistons with six points (2-10 FG, 2-9 3Pt), one rebound and two steals in 26 minutes.
items.story: Hyland struggled from the field for the second straight game, unable to maintain his hot shooting from the four previous outings. Despite stepping into a larger role following the knee injury to Anthony Edwards, Hyland has been a fringe fantasy asset at best, averaging 13.9 points and 2.6 three-pointers in 24.9 minutes per game in seven appearances over the past two weeks.

items.headline: Hyland recorded 23 points (8-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal over 29 minutes during Sunday's 102-92 victory over Boston.
items.story: Hyland has always had the capacity to score off the bench, but he seems to be taking his game to another level. He's scored at least 17 points in his last four appearances and has reached the 20-point plateau twice in that stretch, averaging 20.0 points per game and shooting 44.8 percent from deep. Hyland has scored in double digits in seven of his last eight contests, and the uptick in playing time is directly tied to the absence of Anthony Edwards (knee).

items.headline: Hyland closed Tuesday's 116-104 victory over Phoenix with 22 points (8-14 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, five assists and one steal across 29 minutes.
items.story: Hyland saw at least 25 minutes for the first time in his past 16 games, delivering one of his best performances of the season. With Anthony Edwards set to miss at least a week with a knee injury, it appears as though Hyland is going to play a sizeable role for the foreseeable future. While he won't shoot 57 percent from the floor on most nights, he is certainly on the radar as a short-term addition.

items.headline: Hyland notched 10 points (4-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt), four assists and one steal over 16 minutes during Wednesday's 153-128 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: With the Timberwolves fully healthy, there isn't a clear path to fantasy relevance for Hyland, but he is capable of putting up strong numbers when he gets hot. The combo guard has averaged 9.5 points, 2.2 assists, 0.8 rebounds and 1.8 three-pointers in 15.9 minutes per contest in his last six games, shooting 42.3 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Hyland closed with 18 points (6-7 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 16 minutes during Sunday's 117-108 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: After scoring in single digits in five straight outings, Hyland turned in an extremely efficient performance Sunday. The 25-year-old finished as Minnesota's third-leading scorer and paced the second unit in scoring against the Nuggets, who selected Hyland with the 26th overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft before trading him to the Clippers in February 2023. While Hyland should continue to see meaningful burn off the bench, he typically doesn't offer much in terms of peripheral numbers and has been an inconsistent scorer of late.

items.headline: Hyland had three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), four rebounds and two assists over 15 minutes during Friday's 122-111 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Hyland scored just three points for the second straight game, continuing his recent struggles on the offensive end. In four appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 7.3 points, 3.0 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 14.4 minutes per game. With Ayo Dosunmu now serving as the primary backup behind Donte DiVincenzo, it appears as though Hyland's brief run of relevancy may have some to a grinding halt.

items.headline: Hyland finished with 20 points (8-12 FG, 4-7 3Pt), seven rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals over 26 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 128-126 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: It was Hyland's best scoring effort since Jan. 13, when he dropped a season-high 23 points on the Bucks. However, the fifth-year guard scored in double digits only once during the 10 games in between those ceiling performances, making him little more than a DFS dart throw for fantasy purposes. Over that 12-game stretch, Hyland is averaging 8.3 points, 2.9 assists, 2.5 boards, 1.6 threes and 0.8 steals in 16.6 minutes from the second unit.

items.headline: Hyland ended with 17 points (6-9 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and two steals in 25 minutes during Monday's 108-83 victory over Golden State.
items.story: Hyland received 25 minutes with Anthony Edwards (foot) out of action. Mike Conley struggled as Edwards' direct replacement in the starting lineup, leaving Hyland to produce his third-highest scoring total of the season. Edwards' injury isn't considered serious, and Hyland's numbers will likely regress to normal levels upon the superstar's return.

items.headline: Hyland accumulated five points (2-5 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-3 FT), one rebound and three assists over 16 minutes during Sunday's 111-85 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Similar to Mike Conley, Hyland has seen a very limited role off the bench in Minnesota. Over his last six games, he's playing 13.7 minutes per contest with 6.7 points, 2.8 assists, 1.0 rebounds and 1.2 three-pointers.

items.headline: Hyland ended Friday's 110-105 loss to the Rockets with two points (1-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 0-2 FT) and five assists over 17 minutes.
items.story: Hyland was limited to just two points, unable to replicate his 23-point performance from the previous game. Although he has been able to carve out a regular spot in the rotation, Hyland's production has been sporadic, at best. In 16 appearances over the past month, he has averaged 8.5 points, 3.6 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 17.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hyland finished Sunday's 104-103 win over San Antonio with 10 points (3-8 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one block in 12 minutes.
items.story: After some strong moments in December, Hyland is fading once again. Over his last four games, he's seeing 13.6 minutes per night with 7.5 points, 3.8 assists, 1.8 rebounds and 1.3 three-pointers on 39.3 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Edgecombe notched 21 points (9-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds, five assists, a steal and a block across 33 minutes in Monday's 126-107 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Edgecombe delivered an impressive offensive performance, converting 75 percent of his field-goal attempts en route to his best scoring output of the season while adding five assists and two defensive stats. His 33-minute workload reinforced his established role in Philadelphia's starting backcourt, although his shooting efficiency is unlikely to remain this high consistently. Edgecombe's combination of scoring, playmaking and defensive contributions offers considerable fantasy upside in his second year in the league. He's scored in double digits in five of his last six outings.

items.headline: Edgecombe closed Friday's 98-93 win over New York with 13 points (6-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt), eight rebounds and two assists across 36 minutes.
items.story: Edgecombe finished fourth on the 76ers in scoring, but the second-year guard did the dirty work by hauling in eight boards (six on the defensive end of the floor), which were second-most on the team behind LeBron James (nine). Edgecombe has adjusted to his complementary role nicely, and his production will fluctuate on a night-to-night basis depending on the availability of James, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown (knee) and Tyrese Maxey.

items.headline: Edgecombe (abdomen) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: After fully practicing Tuesday, Edgecombe is ready to return Wednesday following a one-game absence with an abdominal bruise. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope should head back to the bench in Edgecombe's return.

items.headline: Edgecombe (abdomen) practiced in full Tuesday, Keith Pompey of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.story: This is a good sign ahead of Wednesday's game against the Pacers. The second-year guard was unable to suit up Sunday, and if he's unable to return Wednesday, guys like Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope could see increased run.

items.headline: Edgecombe (abdomen) is out for Sunday's game against the Pistons, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Edgecombe sustained an abdominal contusion during Saturday's game against the Bucks, and although he was able to return, he has been ruled out for Sunday's game due to the injury. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons figure to see larger roles in his absence.

items.headline: Edgecombe has been downgraded to questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Pistons due to an abdominal contusion.
items.story: Edgecombe exited Saturday's game briefly and could miss the second half of the team's back-to-back set due to an abdominal injury. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons are candidates for extra minutes if Edgecombe is unable to go.

items.headline: Edgecombe recorded 17 points (5-13 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 13 rebounds, two assists, a steal and two blocks across 30 minutes in Saturday's 127-116 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Edgecombe delivered his first double-double of the season, setting an early personal best with 13 rebounds while connecting on five three-pointers. He has now collected 20 rebounds over his last two games, an encouraging development for a player operating alongside several established scorers, and he's also scored in double digits in back-to-back games. Even though he's likely the fifth option on offense in a star-studded lineup, his versatility and defensive contributions offer multiple paths to fantasy production.

items.headline: Edgecombe (groin) started the second quarter of Saturday's game against the Bucks, per the broadcast.
items.story: Edgecombe took a shot to the groin area and limped to the locker room in the opening quarter. However, the 21-year-old quickly returned to the bench and appears to be good to go for the remainder of the contest.

items.headline: Edgecombe exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Saturday's game against the Bucks due to an apparent groin injury, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Edgecombe took a shot to the groin area and briefly stayed in the game before limping to the locker room. He can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Edgecombe registered 11 points (4-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and three steals across 33 minutes in Thursday's 114-106 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Edgecombe made a significant impact beyond scoring, matching his strong rebounding effort with solid playmaking and defensive contributions, as he co-led the team in both assists and steals. His 33-minute workload was particularly encouraging in a crowded Philadelphia rotation, suggesting he'll continue receiving substantial opportunities. However, his limited scoring efficiency could restrict his fantasy ceiling, making his contributions in assists, rebounds and defensive categories especially important.

items.headline: Edgecombe supplied nine points (4-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal in 35 minutes during Tuesday's 106-100 win over New York.
items.story: Edgecombe drew the start at shooting guard and logged the third-most minutes on Philadelphia's roster, trailing only Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. The second-year guard struggled to establish his perimeter shot and committed four fouls, but his substantial workload suggests he'll remain a prominent part of the 76ers' rotation. Greater offensive involvement will be necessary for Edgecombe to consistently capitalize on those minutes in fantasy.

items.headline: The 76ers exercised the third-year team option on Edgecombe's contract for the 2027-28 season Monday, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports.
items.story: This was the expected move by Philadelphia, and it will result in Edgecombe taking home $12.2 million during the 2027-28 campaign. The 21-year-old will look to take another step forward in 2026-27 playing alongside plenty of veteran talent in Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

items.headline: Edgecombe (rest) is expected to play in Tuesday's regular-season opener against New York.
items.story: Edgecombe should return to action Opening Night after sitting out the Sixers' preseason finale Friday. In three preseason appearances this year, he averaged 14.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.3 steals across 22.7 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Edgecombe (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason game against the Celtics, Chris Hine of The Philly Inquirer reports.
items.story: Edgecombe will get the night off during the Sixers' preseason finale. The second-year swingman should be available for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Knicks.

items.headline: Edgecombe put up 19 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, four assists and four steals over 26 minutes in Saturday's 144-106 preseason loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Edgecombe saw a big uptick in usage with Jaylen Brown (rest), LeBron James (rest) and Joel Embiid (rest) all sitting this one out, and he made the most of the increased opportunity. With new additions Brown and James, Edgecombe could at times find it difficult to assert himself in the offense, but he should do enough with the triples, dimes and defensive stats to remain fantasy-relevant.

items.headline: Edgecombe totaled 11 points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one block in 23 minutes during Thursday's 114-108 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: Edgecombe expectedly took somewhat of a backseat, with Philadelphia rolling out its expected starting five. After tallying seven assists in the preseason opener, Edgecombe was limited to just one assist Thursday. As long as the team is relatively healthy, the impressive sophomore is expected to be the fourth or fifth option on offense. While this doesn't bode well for his upside, he is still worth a look in the later middle rounds of drafts, given the fact that he should step into a larger role any time another member of the starting five misses time.

items.headline: Edgecombe supplied 12 points (4-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and seven assists across 20 minutes in Monday's 120-97 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Edgecombe was one of six Philadelphia players to score in double digits in this preseason opener, and the second-year guard also led the team in assists, showing what he can do when given the keys to a bigger playmaking role. He isn't expected to have the same level of opportunity once the regular season starts, though, as he'll share the court with accomplished playmakers who weren't available for this preseason tune-up, such as LeBron James (rest) and Tyrese Maxey (rest).

items.headline: Edgecombe said Monday that he placed an emphasis on improving his shooting during the offseason while also working on his finishing and ball-handling, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Edgecombe established himself as a significant part of Philadelphia's rotation as a rookie, but improving his perimeter efficiency was an obvious area of focus heading into his second season. He shot 43.6 percent from the field and 35.9 percent from three across 79 regular-season appearances, and continued development as a shooter could make him an even more effective complement to the 76ers' other high-usage options. While Edgecombe's fantasy outlook is somewhat murkier entering 2026-27 after the 76ers added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, James doesn't feel like his presence should take away from the youngster's development. "I don't understand why things would change for him," James said of Edgecombe's role.

items.headline: Edgecombe recorded 25 points (9-16 FG, 7-11 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists during the Bahamas' 100-82 win over Panama in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 21-year-old is coming off a strong first campaign with Philadelphia and earned All-Rookie honors after establishing himself as a key piece of the team's backcourt. However, his fantasy outlook is somewhat murkier entering 2026-27 after the 76ers added LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope during a dramatic roster overhaul.

items.headline: Edgecombe is not on the Bahamas' roster ahead of the FIBA World Cup qualifiers, according to NBA reporter Marc Stein.
items.story: There's no injury to report, and this is likely Edgecombe's decision. Presumably, his focus is going to be on ramping up ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season, when he'll look to build on a breakout rookie season. However, he'll face added competition for usage after the 76ers added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown this offseason.

items.headline: Edgecombe could benefit from entering a veteran-laden environment after Philadelphia added LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Paul Hudrick of Liberty Ballers reports.
items.story: While touches may be harder to come by, Edgecombe will have less pressure to create offense immediately and should continue developing alongside one of the league's deepest rosters. Across 75 regular-season games in 2025-26, Edgecombe averaged 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.4 steals.

items.headline: Carter recorded six points (2-3 FG, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and one steal in 34 minutes during Monday's 103-94 loss to Washington.
items.story: Carter was largely uninvolved offensively despite Orlando playing without Paolo Banchero (ankle), attempting just three shots while finishing one rebound shy of double figures. His 34 minutes were encouraging, but Nikola Vucevic continues to provide competition in the frontcourt. Carter should remain a reliable source of rebounds, though his scoring production could fluctuate significantly.

items.headline: Carter finished with 20 points (6-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and two steals in 39 minutes during Friday's 121-114 win over the Raptors.
items.story: Carter has yet to record his first double-double of the season, and he ended just three boards shy of doing so Friday. He took a step forward offensively, though, as he hit the 20-point mark after scoring a combined 12 points (4-10 FG) in his previous two contests. Carter has reached the 20-point mark in three of his five appearances this season, and he should continue to benefit from an expanded offensive role due to the absences of Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee).

items.headline: Carter chipped in nine points (3-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal in 33 minutes during Sunday's 111-102 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: Carter cooled off a bit Sunday after dropping at least 20 points in two prior appearances, but he came down with a season-high 10 boards. The big man should continue to play a key role at center for the Magic, but fantasy managers should anticipate some regression coming at some point for Carter.

items.headline: Carter put up 20 points (8-9 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 29 minutes in Friday's 115-93 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Carter has been unconscious through the first two games of the season, converting 84.2 percent of his shot attempts and 57.1 percent of his long-range looks. These gaudy percentages aren't sustainable, but managers can certainly appreciate the torrid start to the year. Additionally, offseason addition Nikola Vucevic is clearly no threat to Carter's playing time, as he's logged just nine minutes through the first two games.

items.headline: Carter amassed 22 points (8-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 5-5 FT), seven rebounds and one steal over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Carter scored an efficient 22 points despite the loss, putting to rest any doubts there were regarding his role as the starting center. Seen as his primary competition for playing time, Nikola Vucevic managed just five minutes, while Goga Bitadze saw 12 minutes. While this is only a one-game sample size, it does appear as though Carter should be able to maintain relevance in standard leagues, although expecting 22 points from him on most nights feels unwise.

items.headline: Carter logged 13 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), four rebounds and two assists in 15 minutes during Wednesday's 122-118 preseason win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Carter was Orlando's full-time starting center last season, averaging 11.8 points and 7.4 rebounds, but his outlook is complicated by Nikola Vucevic's return to Orlando. Carter's starting role isn't currently in jeopardy, but the situation is worth monitoring.

items.headline: Carter's outlook becomes more uncertain following Orlando's acquisition of Nikola Vucevic.
items.story: While Carter has served as the Magic's starting center in recent seasons, Vucevic's return could cut into his playing time and potentially shift him into a reduced role depending on how Orlando structures its frontcourt rotation. Carter is likely to remain with the first unit, but his fantasy value may take a hit if the two centers split minutes consistently.

items.headline: Carter contributed 13 points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block over 38 minutes during Sunday's 116-94 loss to Detroit in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Carter logged a season-high 38 minutes, bringing the curtain down on what was a relatively successful season, at least from a personal standpoint. After establishing himself as the starting center on Opening Night, Carter held onto the position for the duration of the season. He finished the regular season with averages of 11.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.8 steals, 0.6 blocks and 0.9 three-pointers in 78 outings. Although his lack of defensive contributions remains an issue, he did average 1.3 blocks per game over the final 15 games of the season, including the playoffs.

items.headline: Carter recorded nine points (3-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two assists and two blocks in 32 minutes before fouling out of Friday's 93-79 loss to Detroit in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Carter scored just nine points for the second straight game as Orlando blew a 24-point lead and eventually fell by 14 points. Through six games, Carter's production has seemingly been a measuring stick for the Magic. In three wins, he has averaged 14.3 points, 11.7 rebounds and 1.3 blocks. In three losses, his numbers have fallen to 7.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game.

items.headline: Carter ended Saturday's 113-105 victory over the Pistons in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 14 points (5-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 17 rebounds, three assists and one block across 37 minutes.
items.story: The 27-year-old center delivered his first double-double in April at a very opportune time, and the 17 boards represented his best performance on the glass since the 2021-22 season. Carter has produced strong numbers in both of the Magic's wins in the series so far, and he's averaging 11.3 points, 9.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.0 steals in 32.7 minutes heading into Game 4 on Monday.

items.headline: Carter recorded 17 points (8-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt), seven rebounds, five assists, one block and two steals over 37 minutes during Sunday's 112-101 victory over the Pistons in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Carter was at his best in the win, chipping in across all major categories as Orlando came out of the blocks with a bang. While his production has been a little up and down throughout the season, Carter has been a consistent part of the rotation. After having limited Jalen Duren to just eight points and seven rebounds, Carter should expect a tougher go of things when the two teams meet again in Game 2.

items.headline: Carter supplied three points (0-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 31 minutes during Sunday's 113-108 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Carter struggled during the loss, scoring just three points, the fewest he has scored since mid-Feb. Despite facing a Boston team minus all of its stars, Orlando failed to get the job done. As punishment, the Magic will now have to face the 76ers in Philadelphia, where the loser will then have to back up against either the Heat or the Hornets.

items.headline: Carter (questionable) is available for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Carter was initially carrying a questionable tag due to a nasal fracture, but the big man will suit up and should handle his regular workload down low. Carter is averaging 13.3 points, 6.9 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game in 19 appearances since the beginning of March.

items.headline: Carter is questionable for Wednesday's game against Minnesota with a nasal fracture.
items.story: Carter didn't return to Monday's win over the Pistons due to the injury. His absence would free up a spot in the starting lineup, which would likely be filled by Goga Bitadze and would also put him in the streaming mix.

items.headline: Carter (neck) didn't return to Monday's game against the Pistons. He finished the night with 12 points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 7-8 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in 18 minutes.
items.story: The timing of this injury is unfortunate for Carter and the Magic, who have three regular-season matchups remaining before gearing up for the playoffs. The team will presumably re-evaluate the 26-year-old Tuesday to determine his status for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.

items.headline: Carter exited Monday's game against the Pistons due to a neck sprain and is doubtful to return.
items.story: The Magic will likely lean on Goga Bitadze down the stretch with Carter presumably shut down for the rest of the night. He can be considered day-to-day leading up to Wednesday's game against Minnesota, assuming he fails to return Monday.

items.headline: Carter finished Friday's 138-127 victory over the Mavericks with 28 points (8-16 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 10-10 FT), six rebounds and three assists across 36 minutes.
items.story: Carter not only led the Magic in scoring in this win, but he also delivered a season-high mark in scoring -- his previous season-best output was a 26-point effort against the Nuggets on Dec. 18. Carter is ending the regular season on a strong note, and even though he tends to operate as the No. 3 or No. 4 option offensively for Orlando, he's making the most of his role. This was the 12th time he's scored in double digits over his last 13 appearances dating back to March 11.

items.headline: Carter recorded 15 points (4-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 6-7 FT), 12 rebounds and two steals across 28 minutes during Tuesday's 115-111 win over the Suns.
items.story: Carter was efficient on both ends of the court and posted his second double-double over the last three games. While Carter's upside on offense is being the team's No. 3 option in a best-case scenario, he ultimately produces enough even in a limited role to be considered a strong fantasy option. Carter ended March scoring in double digits in nine of his last 10 appearances, averaging 13.6 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.0 steals per contest.

items.headline: Carter finished with 10 points (3-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), 11 rebounds, one block and one steal in 35 minutes during Thursday's 121-117 win over the Kings.
items.story: Carter didn't have his best shooting performance, particularly considering that he plays near the rim as a center, but he still posted a decent output. This was his first double-double since March 12, when he had 19 points and 11 rebounds in a win over the Wizards, and his fifth since the All-Star break. It's worth noting that Carter has now scored in double digits in each of his last nine appearances as well.

items.headline: Carter contributed 15 points (4-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 29 minutes before fouling out of Tuesday's 136-131 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Carter continues to play a pivotal role for the Magic, despite the fact that he has yet to really blow up. He has been one of the more underrated players this season, quietly going about his business with very little fanfare. Through 68 games, he has been a top-70 player in nine-category leagues, averaging 11.9 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Carter (ribs) is available for Saturday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Carter will shed a questionable tag to play in Saturday's contest. He had been dealing with a bruised left rib. Carter's return will likely push Goga Bitadze back to the second unit.

items.headline: Carter (ribs) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Carter remains day-to-day after missing Thursday's game against the Hornets. If Orlando's starting center misses another contest, the Magic will likely lean on Goga Bitadze and Moritz Wagner.

items.headline: Washington logged 12 points (2-9 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five rebounds, one assist and two steals across 38 minutes during Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Washington is holding down a starting position at power forward over Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher. Washington has put up at least 10 points in six of his first seven appearances, averaging 13.6 points, 7.7 rebounds and 1.1 assists for the season.

items.headline: Washington supplied 18 points (7-16 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and one block over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 120-96 win over Oklahoma City.
items.story: The veteran forward fell one board short of his second double-double of the season. Washington has been his usual steady self through five games, scoring in double digits in all five games while averaging 16.0 points, 7.8 rebounds, 2.0 threes, 1.2 assists and 1.2 blocks in 33.4 minutes.

While durability is a concern, Washington still has plenty to offer, considering he can play on both ends of the floor while shifting to multiple positions during a given contest. The Mavericks added Johnson and Lawal in the 2026 NBA Draft. items.headline: Lyles amassed seven points (2-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 28 minutes during Friday's 114-97 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Although Lyles fell just three points short of his second double-double of the campaign, he was still able to haul in double-digit rebounds for the first time since a Nov. 18 loss to Atlanta. The 29-year-old veteran big man has quietly been very effective off Sacramento's bench over his last eight appearances, as he's averaged 11.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 0.9 steals and 2.3 threes in 24.9 minutes while shooting 43.9 percent from three-point land.
