Lyles is worth streaming in most fantasy leagues while he's hot, but his upside will remain capped by the presence of a healthy Domantas Sabonis.

items.headline: Lyles chipped in 12 points (4-9 FG, 4-8 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and two steals in 31 minutes during Wednesday's 113-107 win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Lyles' four made threes accounted for 12 of Sacramento's 14 total bench points during Wednesday's victory. While the 29-year-old forward is shooting 39.0 percent from the field this season, he is converting 36.7 percent of his 4.1 three-point attempts per contest.

items.headline: Lyles supplied 20 points (5-8 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 6-8 FT) and eight rebounds in 25 minutes during Thursday's 114-113 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Alex Len proved to be ineffective as Domantas Sabonis' (illness) direct replacement, prompting Lyles to step in and take a larger role. Point-for-point, Lyles has been a better option as Sabonis' fill-in throughout the season, though Len was probably a more logical player to size up against Jalen Duren. Lyles has floor-stretching ability and an accurate perimeter game that Len lacks, making him a more suitable pivot when Sabonis is off the court.

items.headline: Lyles (calf) is listed as available for Sunday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Lyles will play in his second consecutive outing following a 10-game absence due to a right calf strain. It wouldn't come as a surprise if the big man operates under a minutes restriction, meaning Isaac Jones and Alex Len could be in line for a slight uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Lyles (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Pacers.
items.story: Lyles made his return to game action in Saturday's 103-99 loss to the Lakers following a 10-game absence due to a right calf strain. He played 17 minutes off the bench, finishing with three points (1-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds and one steal. Though he didn't experience any reported setbacks in his return, the Kings could still end up holding out Lyles for maintenance purposes in the second leg of a back-to-back set. With Lyles and Domantas Sabonis (ankle) both deemed questionable, Isaac Jones and Alex Len could end up covering most of the minutes at center if neither Lyles nor Sabonis is available.

items.headline: Lyles (calf) is available for Saturday's game versus the Lakers, Deuce Mason of NBC Sports California reports.
items.story: Lyles has been upgraded from questionable to available Saturday after missing Sacramento's last 10 games with a right calf injury. Even with Domantas Sabonis (back) questionable, Lyles will likely operate on a minutes restriction until he's able to handle a full workload.

items.headline: Lyles (calf) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Lyles suffered a Grade 1 right calf strain in late November, and he has been sidelined ever since. In the 10 games prior to his injury, he averaged 7.0 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 23.0 minutes per game. Lyles was initially slated to return Thursday against the Lakers but was added back to the injury report and eventually ruled out. If he's unable to play in Saturday's rematch, his next opportunity would be against the Pacers on Sunday.

items.headline: Lyles (calf) won't play Thursday against the Lakers, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Lyles was added to the injury report earlier in the day and has now been ruled out for Thursday's action. He hasn't seen the court since Nov. 25 due to his current role in the rotation, so his presence shouldn't be missed much.

items.headline: Gordon notched 15 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds and five assists in 29 minutes during Friday's 127-120 win over the Suns.
items.story: Gordon was steady in the victory, and the forward was one of five Nuggets starters to reach double figures. His physicality on both ends remains a key piece of Denver's starting group. He'll look to keep it rolling Monday against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Gordon registered 15 points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 7-8 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists and a steal across 31 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Gordon compensated for a difficult shooting performance by collecting 11 rebounds and converting seven free throws. His double-double was encouraging, particularly after struggling to establish consistent rebounding production earlier in the season. Gordon's ability to contribute on the glass and from the perimeter gives him useful fantasy versatility, although his scoring remains dependent on opportunities alongside Denver's primary offensive options. This was his first double-double of the season and just the second time he has scored in double digits, so the next step is to show more consistency on a game-to-game basis.

items.headline: Gordon was ejected from Monday's game against the Warriors after picking up back-to-back technical fouls, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports. He'll end the night with seven points (2-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 25 minutes.
items.story: The game was already well in hand for Golden State with 8:34 left in the fourth quarter when Gordon's night ended early after disagreeing with a foul call. He couldn't get his shot to fall on the offensive end Monday, and he's now been held to seven points in back-to-back appearances.

items.headline: Gordon totaled 20 points (6-9 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block in 29 minutes during Thursday's 96-84 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Gordon paced Denver in scoring and made treys, but it wasn't enough to help his team secure the victory. He enjoyed an efficient shooting performance, needing only nine attempts from the field to reach the 20-point threshold. This is a strong start to the 2026-27 campaign for Gordon, who averaged 16.2 points and 1.7 made treys over 36 regular-season games a year ago.

items.headline: Gordon (rest) is expected to play in Thursday's regular-season opener against the Thunder.
items.story: Gordon sat out Friday's preseason finale but should return to the lineup in Oklahoma City on Thursday. The veteran forward is coming off an injury-plagued 2025-26 season in which he appeared in only 36 regular-season games (33 starts), averaging 16.2 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.7 assists in 27.9 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Gordon (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the Lakers, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Gordon is being held out of Denver's final preseason game for maintenance purposes, but he should be fine for Thursday's regular-season opener in Oklahoma City. Trevon Brazile will start in Gordon's place Friday evening.

items.headline: Gordon dropped a team-high 25 points (9-12 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT) while adding six rebounds in 23 minutes during Sunday's 133-128 preseason win over the Bulls.
items.story: Denver's starting five all played at least 23 minutes as the team gets ready for Opening Night, and while Gordon stepped up with a strong scoring effort, Nikola Jokic also appeared to be in midseason form with a triple-double. Gordon has had trouble staying on the court the last couple of years, playing a combined 87 regular-season games in 2024-25 and 2025-26, but he's been healthy this preseason and is averaging 18.3 points, 5.0 boards and 2.0 threes in just 16.0 minutes across three exhibition contests.

items.headline: Gordon registered 18 points (5-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 6-7 FT) and five rebounds over 15 minutes in Tuesday's 93-79 preseason win over the Jazz.
items.story: Despite logging just 15 minutes, Gordon led his team in scoring, free-throw attempts and rebounding. He's looked spry this preseason, so he seems ready to bounce back after back-to-back injury-plagued seasons.

items.headline: Gordon totaled 12 points (4-8 FG, 3-3 FT, 1-3 3Pt) and four rebounds in 11 minutes during Sunday's 109-97 preseason loss to Utah.
items.story: Gordon was limited to just 11 minutes, although he looked good, particularly on the offensive end of the floor. After playing just 87  regular-season games over the past two seasons, Gordon has spoken of prioritizing health coming into this season, which can only mean good things for fantasy, at least in terms of his availability. While his best years are probably behind him, Gordon's importance to the Nuggets can't be overstated. His overall skill set doesn't translate particularly well to fantasy, although he is a viable target in the later rounds, even in standard formats.

items.headline: Gordon is focused more on his health in an effort to avoid soft-tissue injuries after two injury-riddled seasons, Bennett Durando of The Denver Post reports.
items.story: "I need to be here much earlier and stay much later," Gordon said. "And I need to invest a lot more time warming up and a lot more time cooling down so I can be available for these guys." After appearing in just 51 regular-season games (42 starts) in the 2024-25 season, the veteran forward played in just 36 outings (33 starts) last regular season. Gordon missed 38 of Denver's 48 games from Nov. 22 to March 5 due to a right hamstring strain, and he also missed time in the team's first-round series loss to Minnesota with a calf injury. However, the 31-year-old is ready to go ahead of the 2026-27 season and seemingly has made his health more of a priority.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) said he got his mind and body right during the offseason, and he's "ready to go" for the 2026-27 season, Harrison Wind of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.story: Gordon labored through a left calf issue during Denver's postseason run last spring, missing three of the Nuggets' final four games in their first-round loss to the Timberwolves. However, he's had plenty of time to recover, and it appears he'll enter training camp at 100 percent. Gordon averaged 27.9 minutes per game last season over 36 regular-season contests, but his playing time could dip this upcoming season due to the arrival of DeMar DeRozan.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) could see more usage for Denver in 2026-27 after Peyton Watson was shipped to Cleveland.
items.story: Much like teammates Christian Braun and Cameron Johnson, Gordon experienced an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign but maintained strong productivity when healthy. Gordon averaged 16.2 points, his most since his time with Orlando, 5.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.7 three-pointers in 27.9 minutes per game over 36 regular-season appearances, and Watson's departure presents one less obstacle for usage.

items.headline: Gordon is out for Thursday's Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs against the Timberwolves, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Gordon attempted to warm up ahead of Thursday's clash, but he's not feeling healthy enough to give it a go. Spencer Jones stepped into the starting lineup in Gordon's place in Game 5 and should be considered the favorite to start again in Game 6.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) is listed as questionable for Thursday's Game 6 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Gordon missed Games 3 and 5 due to left calf tightness and may remain out for Thursday's win-or-go-home matchup. The veteran forward logged only 23 minutes in Game 4, so even if he's cleared to suit up Thursday, he could operate under a minutes restriction.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) has been ruled out for Game 5 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Timberwolves on Monday.
items.story: Gordon struggled at times during Game 4 due to his calf injury, and he simply isn't feeling healthy enough to give it a go Monday night. Spencer Jones drew the start in Gordon's place in Game 3 and will be a candidate to do so again Monday.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) is being considered a true game-time decision ahead of Monday's Game 5 against Minnesota, Alan Horton of the Timberwolves Radio Network reports.
items.story: Gordon managed to return for Saturday's Game 4 and put up nine points in 23 minutes throughout the contest, but it's clear he's not yet over the calf injury. He'll test the calf in pre-game warmups before the Nuggets provide another update on his status for Game 5.

items.headline: Gordon is questionable for Monday's Game 5 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Timberwolves due to left calf tightness.
items.story: Gordon has been dealing with the left calf issue for some time, and he even exited Game 4 briefly due to the issue. If he is unable to go Monday, Tim Hardaway and Spencer Jones could see expanded roles.

items.headline: Gordon closed Saturday's 112-96 loss to Minnesota in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with nine points (4-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt), one rebound and one block in 23 minutes.
items.story: Gordon briefly headed to the locker room with a calf injury but made it back to the bench before the end of the contest. It seemed obvious that Gordon was struggling during a few possessions, and he may not be ready for Monday's elimination game against the Timberwolves. More news should emerge after Monday morning.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) will return to Saturday's Game 4 in Minnesota, Duvalier Johnson of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.story: Gordon briefly exited Saturday's game, but after getting checked on in the locker room, he's been cleared to return. Gordon doesn't appear to be 100 percent healthy, but he's good enough to play.

items.headline: Gordon went back to the locker room during the third quarter of Saturday's Game 4 versus the Timberwolves with an undisclosed injury, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: It's unclear exactly what Gordon is dealing with, but he was playing through a left calf issue, so he may have had a flare-up. We should get more info soon, but if Gordon needs to miss time, that would open up minutes for Tim Hardaway and Spencer Jones.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) will play in Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Timberwolves on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Gordon will shed his questionable tag and return to action after missing Thursday's Game 3 loss due to left calf tightness. The veteran forward has averaged 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 33.0 minutes per contest over two first-round appearances.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) is listed as questionable for Saturday's Game 4 against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Gordon is in danger of missing a second straight game due to left calf tightness. If the veteran forward is not cleared to play, Spencer Jones, Tim Hardaway and Zeke Nnaji would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) has been ruled out for Game 3 against the Timberwolves on Thursday, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Gordon was originally added to the injury report as probable after dealing with some calf tightness following Game 2, but he was downgraded to questionable earlier in the day Thursday and has now been ruled out. Look for Spencer Jones and Tim Hardaway to see more run in the frontcourt in Gordon's absence.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) is questionable for Game 3 on Thursday against Minnesota.
items.story: The Nuggets originally deemed Gordon probable due to left calf tightness, so it's unclear if he suffered a setback during morning shootaround Thursday. If the veteran forward is ultimately downgraded to out, Bruce Brown could find himself being more involved in Game 3.

items.headline: Gordon (calf) is listed as probable for Thursday's Game 3 against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Gordon is dealing with left calf tightness but is still likely to suit up for Game 3 in Minnesota. Through two first-round games, the veteran forward has averaged 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 33.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Gordon posted 17 points (5-10 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 6-8 FT), eight rebounds and three assists over 29 minutes during Saturday's 116-105 victory over the Timberwolves in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Gordon did an excellent job of containing Julius Randle, holding Minnesota's star power forward to just 16 points on 7-for-16 shooting. He was shoved by Randle late in the match and landed hard on his rear, but despite some grimacing, he played through it and finished the game. Gordon should be fine for Game 2 on Monday.

items.headline: Gordon (hamstring) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's Game 1 against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Gordon missed Denver's last two regular-season games due to right hamstring injury management, but he's good to go for the start of the playoffs. The veteran forward appeared in four regular-season outings in April, during which he averaged 12.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 30.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Gordon (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Gordon will miss a second straight game due to right hamstring injury management, though he should be good to go for the start of the postseason. He'll finish the 2025-26 regular season with averages of 16.2 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.7 assists across 27.9 minutes per game in 36 appearances (33 starts). David Roddy and Julian Strawther will likely see increased playing time in Gordon's absence Sunday.

items.headline: Jerome recorded 40 points (14-22 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, five assists and two steals in 37 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime loss to New Orleans.
items.story: Jerome looked sharp Monday following a one-game absence due to a back issue. He pieced together a spectacular shooting performance and has already reached the 40-point threshold twice in six games so far this season. However, his heroics weren't enough to lead his team to a comeback victory, resulting in the Grizzlies' first loss of the campaign.

items.headline: Jerome (back) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Jerome didn't play in the 136-105 victory over the Kings on Saturday, though he will return from his one-game layoff for Monday's meeting with the Pelicans. With Jerome cleared to play, Cam Spencer will presumably head back to the bench. However, since Scotty Pippen (back) is doubtful, Spencer should see more minutes than usual.

items.headline: Jerome (back) won't play in Saturday's game versus Sacramento, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Jerome has been battling a nagging back injury, and it will force him to miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Scotty Pippen (back) also sidelined, Cam Spencer is the favorite to start at the one.

items.headline: Jerome (back) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Kings.
items.story: This isn't the first mention of Jerome's nagging back issue, though it didn't stop him from suiting up for the 124-103 win over the Trail Blazers on Thursday. The 29-year-old has played at an All-Star level in his five regular-season appearances in 2026-27, averaging 25.8 points, 2.2 rebounds and 5.8 assists -- all career highs -- along with 1.0 steals in 29.8 minutes per contest. If Jerome can't get on the floor Saturday versus Sacramento, Cam Spencer and Scotty Pippen (back) are candidates for more minutes.

items.headline: Jerome (back) is available for Thursday's game at Portland.
items.story: Jerome was added to the injury report less than an hour before tipoff, though he was cleared to play after going through pregame warmups. The veteran guard has been spectacular through four regular-season games, averaging 29.8 points, 6.5 assists, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 triples and 0.8 steals in 31.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jerome is questionable for Thursday's game against the Trail Blazers due to back tightness.
items.story: Jerome was added to the injury report less than one hour before tipoff, so it appears the back issue recently popped up. The team should have another update on his availability shortly.

items.headline: Jerome posted 31 points (8-17 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 14-14 FT), four rebounds, six assists and a steal across 32 minutes in Sunday's 123-112 win over the Kings.
items.story: Jerome continued his impressive start to the season, reaching the 30-point mark for the second time in three games. His perfect 14-for-14 performance at the free-throw line compensated for a difficult night from beyond the arc, while his six assists showed he's more than just a scoring threat out of the backcourt. He's had at least 25 points and five dimes in his first three outings of the season, and while he was widely seen as a breakout candidate for the 2026-27 campaign, these numbers are surpassing even the most optimistic expectations.

items.headline: Jerome racked up 28 points (11-22 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), two rebounds, five assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Friday's 111-108 win over Golden State.
items.story: The 28 points led all scorers on the night, as Jerome cooled off only slightly from his dazzling 45-point performance in the Grizzlies' opener. The 29-year-old point guard is taking on a much bigger role in his second season with Memphis now that Ja Morant is out of the picture, and so far he's seizing the opportunity. Jerome won't keep shooting 59.8 percent from the floor, but as long as he's attempting more than 20 shots a game, his fantasy value will skyrocket.

items.headline: Jerome finished with 45 points (17-25 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 6-7 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and one block across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 123-103 win over Utah.
items.story: Jerome wasn't messing around to kick off the 2026-27 campaign, reaching a new career high in scoring while simultaneously setting a franchise Opening Night scoring record. The 29-year-old ended the 2025-26 campaign by averaging a career-best 19.7 points in 15 regular-season games with the Grizzlies. While Jerome will have difficulty maintaining Wednesday's level of production throughout the rest of the 2026-27 campaign, there's reason to believe he is on the cusp of a career year.

items.headline: Jerome contributed 17 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and three steals over 22 minutes in Friday's 117-98 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Jerome is locked in as Memphis' starting point guard, and he was impressive throughout the preseason, scoring efficiently while flashing his playmaking upside. The 29-year-old could be in for a career year with the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Jerome tallied 16 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four assists and one rebound over 14 minutes during Friday's 104-100 preseason win over the Bulls.
items.story: All of Jerome's production came in the first half, as the veteran point guard sat out for last two quarters. He was limited to just 15 regular-season games last year due to ankle and calf injuries, but now that Ja Morant is in Portland, Jerome figures to start alongside Cedric Coward in Memphis' backcourt, with Scotty Pippen and Cam Spencer providing depth.

items.headline: Jerome tallied 17 points (7-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four assists and one rebound over 19 minutes in Wednesday's 122-118 preseason loss to the Magic.
items.story: Jerome scored efficiently, did a nice job distributing the rock and finished without committing a single turnover. He's looked great as Memphis' starting point guard through the first two preseason games and could be primed for a breakout season.

items.headline: Jerome registered 12 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five assists and one block across 15 minutes in Monday's 132-123 preseason win over the Hawks.
items.story: Jerome started at point guard and did a good job running Memphis' offense, leading the team with five assists while reaching double figures on only eight shots. He committed three turnovers but otherwise made good use of his limited playing time before sitting out the second half. Jerome should have an opportunity to handle significant playmaking responsibilities in Memphis' backcourt, and it wouldn't be surprising if he's the Grizzlies' starting point guard once the 2026-27 regular season begins.

items.headline: Jerome is emerging as a potential option at point guard for the Grizzlies, Damichael Cole of The Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: With Memphis still sorting through its point guard depth chart, it's possible that Jerome is in pole position to begin the season as Memphis' top point guard in favor of Scotty Pippen. Health has long been a major obstacle for Jerome, but he's certainly shined in his starting opportunities over the past several years. Dating back to 2020-21, the 29-year-old has averaged 18.6 points, 5.3 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 steals in just 25.6 minutes per contest across 25 regular-season starts in his career.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) moved up the depth chart earlier this offseason when Portland acquired Ja Morant in a trade with the Grizzlies.
items.story: Scotty Pippen (toe) appears to be the early favorite for the starting spot at point guard, but there's no denying how effective Jerome was when healthy in 2025-26.  Across 15 regular-season appearances, Jerome averaged a hyper-efficient 19.7 points, 5.7 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.1 steals in just 22.6 minutes per game. Pippen underwent a toe procedure in March, so it remains to be seen if he'll be cleared for full participation in training camp this fall.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) is out for Sunday's season finale against the Rockets.
items.story: Jerome will end the 2025-26 season having missed 11 games in a row. He didn't make his season debut until Jan. 31 and didn't play more than three consecutive games all year. Still, when he took the floor, he played well. Across his 15 appearances, the guard averaged 19.7 points, 5.7 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 22.6 minutes.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Utah.
items.story: Jerome will log another absence due to a left ankle sprain. He'll have one final opportunity to return for the regular-season finale Sunday in Houston.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game versus Denver.
items.story: A left ankle sprain will cost Jerome a ninth consecutive contest. With Memphis wrapping up the final stretch of a losing season, Walter Clayton and Rayan Rupert should see plenty of action at point guard Wednesday.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) is out for Monday's game versus Cleveland.
items.story: A left ankle sprain is costing Jerome an eighth consecutive contest. Walter Clayton and Rayan Rupert should see plenty of reps at point guard Monday.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) won't play Sunday in Milwaukee.
items.story: This will be Jerome's seventh straight game on the sidelines, and it's not encouraging that he continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff. After Sunday's match, the Grizzlies will have just four games remaining on their schedule.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) is listed as out for Friday's game in Toronto.
items.story: Jerome has missed the last five games because of a sprained left ankle. With Memphis not going anywhere near the playoffs, it's unknown if he will be back on the floor again this season. With Cam Spencer (back) also out Friday, Javon Small, Walter Clayton and Jahmai Mashack should absorb most of the minutes in the backcourt.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Jerome is in line for his fifth straight absence while rehabbing from a left ankle sprain. The fact that he's been ruled out a full day ahead of Wednesday's game is likely a sign that he's not all that close to a return. With only six games remaining in the regular season after Wednesday, it's unknown if he'll get healthy in time to appear down the stretch, especially with little to play for.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) remains out for Monday's game against Phoenix,.
items.story: Jerome will miss another contest because of a sprained left ankle. However, with only eight games remaining on the schedule before the Grizzlies call it a year, it's unknown if Jerome will be back this season. With a loaded injury report for Memphis once again, Cam Spencer and Cedric Coward will likely handle most of the work in the backcourt versus the Suns. Walter Clayton (ankle) could also factor into the equation, although he's currently listed as questionable.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) won't play Saturday versus the Bulls.
items.story: The Grizzlies injury report remains extensive. With Cam Spencer (back) doubtful and Walter Clayton (ankle) questionable, Javon Small and Cedric Coward may see most of the minutes in the backcourt, with extended action potentially on tap for DeJon Jarreau and Rayan Rupert.

items.headline: Jerome (ankle) won't play Friday versus the Rockets.
items.story: Jerome is set to sit out his second straight game, but he may be able to get back on the court for Saturday's matchup with the Bulls. Javon Small will have a chance for another start Friday with Jerome unavailable, while Walter Clayton and Cam Spencer should see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Jerome is out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: Jerome will continue his recent trend of sitting out every other game or so as the team aims to keep him healthy, though this time he's being listed with a left ankle injury. Walter Clayton is a candidate to start at point guard in Jerome's place Wednesday.

items.headline: Sanders registered 26 points (8-17 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one block in 38 minutes during Monday's 125-118 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Sanders took full advantage of a spot start Monday and filled in admirably for Rui Hachimura (quadriceps). The 24-year-old Sanders led the Clippers in the scoring department with the help of a team-high five triples, which is also his best mark of the young season. He's now 9-for-17 from deep over his last two matchups.

items.headline: Sanders is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Raptors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Rui Hachimura (quadriceps) is sitting out Monday, which opens up a spot in the starting five for Sanders. This marks the 24-year-old's second start of the new campaign. He finished with nine points, four rebounds and three steals in 27 minutes in his first start of the year Wednesday against the Lakers.

items.headline: Sanders totaled 16 points (6-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt), three rebounds and one steal in 30 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 124-112 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: The four made threes were a career high for Sanders, while the 16 points were a season high. The second-year forward has scored in double digits just twice in six games (one start) to begin the season, averaging 8.5 points, 3.0 boards, 2.0 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.5 threes in 23.2 minutes, but his role and usage figure to increase while Max Strus (foot) and Derrick Jones (knee) are on the shelf.

items.headline: Sanders isn't starting Friday against the Timberwolves, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Sanders will return to his regular bench role with Rui Hachimura (calf) back in the starting five. Sanders is averaging 6.3 points and 2.3 rebounds per game in three appearances off the bench this season.

items.headline: Sanders will be in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game versus the Lakers, per Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: Rui Hachimura is dealing with a calf issue, and the Clippers are planning for Sanders to make his first start of the season in his place. Last regular season, Sanders averaged 10.6 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 27.3 minutes per contest covering 16 games as a starter.

items.headline: Sanders finished with 12 points (4-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 20 minutes during Sunday's 108-101 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Sanders was one of three Clippers to tally double figures in scoring off the bench in what was his most productive game so far in 2026-27. With Rui Hachimura struggling with his shot early in the season (26.3/31.6/55.6 shooting splits), Sanders could earn more opportunities going forward.

items.headline: Sanders (hip) was a full participant in Saturday's practice and is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Kings, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Sanders didn't suit up during the preseason due to a hip injury, though he's expected to play when the Clippers host the Kings on Wednesday. The 24-year-old swingman could see increased playing time to begin the regular season, as Brandon Ingram (Achilles), Bradley Beal (knee) and Max Strus (foot) are all expected to miss an extended period.

items.headline: Sanders (hip) won't play in Wednesday's preseason game against the Nuggets, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: While Sanders isn't available for the Clippers' final preseason game, the team is optimistic he will be cleared to suit up for Opening Night against the Kings. With Max Strus (foot), Bradley Beal (knee) and Brandon Ingram (Achilles) all sidelined to begin the 2026-27 campaign, Sanders might be in line for a more prominent role. The 24-year-old appeared in 68 regular-season games as a rookie in 2024-25, starting 16 of them and averaging 7.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists over 19.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Sanders (hip) was limited to individual player development work and did not take part in five-on-five activity Wednesday, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports. Azarly adds that the Clippers said Sanders is day-to-day.
items.story: With Sanders having already missed the Clippers' preseason opener due to a left hip impingement, his continued limitations in practice suggest he still isn't back to full activity. The day-to-day designation keeps him in play to suit up at some point this preseason, but his availability for upcoming exhibition action remains uncertain until he resumes five-on-five work.

items.headline: Sanders won't play in Sunday's preseason game against the Warriors due to a left hip impingement, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: It's unclear when Sanders began dealing with the hip issue, though it'll keep him out of the Clippers' preseason opener. He will also be limited to individual work during Saturday's practice, per Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com. Sanders' next opportunity to suit up during the preseason will come next Saturday against the Raptors.

items.headline: Sanders could have a clearer path to playing time early in the season with Brandon Ingram unavailable for the opener while recovering from a partially torn Achilles and right heel surgery.
items.story: Los Angeles is already dealing with several injuries on the wing, and Sanders is expected to compete for meaningful minutes off the bench. Ingram's absence should give Sanders an opportunity to establish himself in the Clippers' rotation during the opening portion of the campaign. During the 2025-26 regular season, Sanders averaged 7.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists.

items.headline: The Clippers' addition of Max Strus further crowds a wing rotation that already presented Sanders with a difficult path to immediate playing time.
items.story: Strus should command regular minutes because of his shooting and ability to play off the Clippers' primary creators, potentially pushing developmental players such as Sanders further down the depth chart. Sanders therefore projects as more of a long-term option than a player likely to make a fantasy impact.

items.headline: Sanders (rest) did not participate in the Clippers' 128-120 Summer League overtime win over the Timberwolves on Friday.
items.story: Sanders played well in his four Summer League outings and finished strong with 26 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal over 32 minutes against the Wizards on Wednesday. The 2025 second-rounder averaged 19.9 minutes per game across 68 regular-season contests (19 starts) in his rookie year. Sanders could operate in an expanded role in the upcoming season, even with both Brandon Ingram (heel) and Bennedict Mathurin ahead of him on the depth chart.

items.headline: Sanders delivered 26 points (9-17 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, five assists and a steal across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 108-94 Summer League win over the Wizards.
items.story: Sanders saw his scoring numbers increase with each passing game in the Summer League, surpassing the 15-point threshold in the last two and scoring in double digits every time. A second-round pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, Sanders could use a strong showing in the Summer League to grab a rotation spot in 2026-27. He made 68 regular-season appearances as a rookie in 2025-26 while the Clippers dealt with numerous injuries, and the departure of Kawhi Leonard opens up plenty of opportunities.

items.headline: Sanders finished with 18 points (6-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Tuesday's 99-85 Summer League loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Sanders, the No. 50 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, was a sporadic contributor for the Clippers in his 68 regular-season appearances. Still, he had more than a few promising performances, averaging 10.6 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.8 steals over 27.3 minutes in 16 regular-season starts. The players currently projected to start for Los Angeles during the 2026-27 campaign are known for durability issues. As such, Sanders could work his way back into the starting lineup at some point.

items.headline: Sanders totaled 10 points (3-10 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, four assists and four steals in 33 minutes during Thursday's 91-85 Summer League loss to Sacramento.
items.story: The second-year guard struggled to find his perimeter shot but made his presence felt defensively, tying for the game high with four steals. Sanders agreed to a four-year, $11.2 million deal with the Clippers back in June but is facing an uphill battle for minutes in the backcourt.

items.headline: Sanders agreed to a four-year, $11.2 million deal with the Clippers on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Sanders wasn't a consistent producer last season. However, the 2025 No. 50 overall pick displayed flashes of promise by averaging 10.6 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.8 steals while shooting 43.3 percent from deep over 27.3 minutes in 16 regular-season starts. Kawhi Leonard is heading back to Toronto and Darius Garland and Brandon Ingram have struggled to stay healthy over the years, meaning Sanders could get an opportunity to be more active on the scoring end at some point during the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: The Clippers extended Sanders a qualifying offer Monday, per Michael Scotto of USA Today.
items.story: The Clippers declined the team option on Sanders' prior deal, but he could still end up sticking around with Los Angeles. Over 68 regular-season appearances, Sanders averaged 7.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 19.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sanders ended Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game loss to Golden State with three points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and three assists across 11 minutes.
items.story: Sanders was the ninth rotation player for the Clippers as their season came to an end. He made a total of 68 regular-season appearances and was never close to standard-league fantasy appeal with averages of 7.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists.

items.headline: Sanders posted 17 points (5-8 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 24 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 128-110 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: The rookie forward has seen more court time in the last three games as the Clippers wrap up their schedule and prepare for the Play-In Tournament, and Sanders has taken advantage of the opportunity. He's sunk exactly three three-pointers in each contest, averaging 15.0 points, 3.0 threes, 2.3 boards, 2.3 steals and 1.3 assists in 22.7 minutes while shooting 58.3 percent from the floor and 56.3 percent (9-for-16) from beyond the arc. Sanders seems likely to maintain his elevated role over the final two games of the regular season.

items.headline: Sanders supplied 17 points (5-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one assist and four steals over 20 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 138-109 win over the Kings.
items.story: It's only the third time in his last 12 games (one start) that Sanders has scored in double digits, but the three made three-pointers tied his career high. The rookie forward is averaging 7.2 points, 1.3 boards, 1.3 assists, 1.3 threes and 1.3 steals in 15.0 minutes during that 12-game stretch as he struggles to maintain a consistent role in the Clippers' rotation.

items.headline: Sanders provided 19 points (8-10 FG, 3-5 3Pt), three rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal over 26 minutes off the bench during Monday's 129-96 win over the Bucks.
items.story: The 19 points were Sanders' best offensive performance since Jan. 5, when he dropped 20 on the Warriors. The rookie forward has found a fairly consistent role in the Clippers' frontcourt rotation in March, and over his last 10 appearances (four starts), he's averaging 7.6 points, 2.1 boards, 1.7 assists, 1.6 threes and 1.3 steals in 19.7 minutes.

items.headline: Sanders won't start Saturday's game against the Kings, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The rookie second-rounder got the spot start in place of Darius Garland (toe) during Friday's win over Chicago, though Sanders will slide to the second unit with Garland back in action. Sanders has averaged 6.0 points in 11.6 minutes per game over his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Sanders will start Friday's game against the Bulls, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Darius Garland (toe) unavailable for the front end of this back-to-back set, Sanders will get the starting nod. As a starter this season (15 games), the rookie second-rounder has averaged 10.5 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 27.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sanders (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the Clippers' 126-118 win over the Knicks.
items.story: With head coach Tyronn Lue cutting his rotation down from 10 to nine men Monday, Sanders ended up being the odd man out. Sanders had appeared in each of the previous seven games and shot 58.3 percent from the field in 19.4 minutes per contest over that stretch, but it's difficult to see his continuing to receive steady playing time now that Darius Garland has been cleared to play 30-plus minutes. Regaining a spot in the rotation will only become more difficult for Sanders once John Collins (neck) receives the green light to return.

items.headline: Sanders will come off the bench Saturday against the Grizzlies, according to Lauren Rosen of FanDuel Sports Network SoCal.
items.story: The Clippers will start Darius Garland for the first time Saturday. Sanders is likely to maintain a decent role with the second unit for Los Angeles.

items.headline: Sanders is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Warriors, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sanders will return to the starting lineup after coming off the bench in the previous two contests. Across 12 starts, the Nevada product is averaging 11.2 points while shooting 48.1 percent from the field and 39.5 percent from beyond the arc. Darius Garland (toe) is slated to make his team debut Monday, though he'll do so in a reserve role.

items.headline: Sanders will start Sunday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Sanders will start Sunday's contest due to John Collins (head) being out of the lineup. Sanders has seen a declining role over the last six games, culminating in two consecutive games where he did not see the floor. He will get a chance to reinstate himself in the rotation Sunday.

items.headline: Sanders (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Thursday's 115-114 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Though the Clippers upgraded him from a two-way contract to a standard deal over the All-Star break, Sanders ended up dropping out of the rotation for the first time since Nov. 10, ending a streak of 44 consecutive appearances. With Derrick Jones recently returning from an extended injury-related absence and with the Clippers bringing aboard Bennedict Mathurin at the trade deadline to bolster their depth on the wing, Sanders could regularly find himself outside of head coach Tyronn Lue's nine-man rotation. Sanders may at least temporarily reclaim a role in the second unit for Friday's game against the Lakers, as veteran Nicolas Batum (18 minutes Thursday) could be a candidate to rest for the second leg of a back-to-back set.

items.headline: The Clippers and Sanders agreed to a standard contract Saturday, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: Sanders was approaching the 50-game cap for a two-way player, having appeared in 43 NBA games with the Clippers and being active for two others this season. Now on a standard contract, Sanders is officially part of the Clippers' 15-man roster and will have no limitations moving forward. Per Law Murray of The Athletic, the deal includes a team option for the 2026-27 season. Sanders is averaging 7.0 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.7 assists across 21.5 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Sanders is not in the Clippers' starting lineup against the Kings on Friday, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Although Sanders was listed in the starting lineup, it was Derrick Jones who was on the floor at the opening tip. It's unclear what prompted the late change, but it appears as though Sanders will operate in a reserve role Friday.

items.headline: Sanders notched 17 points (7-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and three assists in 34 minutes during Monday's 128-113 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Sanders figures to be a risk-reward option off the waiver wire in the coming days, as the rumor mill regarding a James Harden (personal) trade continues to churn. Sanders and Jordan Miller are top beneficiaries if the trade comes to pass, but the 2025 second-round pick seems to have a slight edge over Miller for the gig at present.

items.headline: Sanders is in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Suns, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Sanders will move into the starting lineup Sunday with James Harden (personal) ruled out, joining Kris Dunn, Kawhi Leonard, John Collins and Ivica Zubac. Across eight starts this season, Sanders is averaging 11.8 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 29.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Sanders is not in the Clippers' starting lineup against the Lakers on Thursday, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Sanders has started in each of the Clippers' last four games and averaged 10.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.5 threes and 1.0 steals over 27.5 minutes per game over that span. He'll revert to a bench role Thursday due to the return of Kawhi Leonard (knee).

items.headline: Sanders logged eight points (3-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist over 22 minutes during Monday's 110-106 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Sanders got the starting nod for a third consecutive contest, though he struggled with efficiency after shooting 53.3 percent from the field across his previous two games. The rookie second-rounder has logged 22 or more minutes in four straight games and could remain in the starting five for as long as Kawhi Leonard (knee) is sidelined.

items.headline: Sanders is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Wizards, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: With John Collins (groin) ruled out late, Sanders will step into the starting five for his fifth start of the season. In his previous four starts, the rookie has taken advantage of the opportunity, averaging 13.5 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 30.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sanders is not in the Clippers' starting lineup against the Knicks on Wednesday, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Sanders was added to the Clippers' starting lineup against the Warriors on Monday after James Harden was ruled out due to a shoulder injury. The former stepped up in a big way, finishing with 20 points, seven rebounds and three assists across 36 minutes, but Sanders will revert to a bench role against New York after Harden was cleared to return.

items.headline: Sanders contributed 20 points (9-16 FG, 2-3 3Pt), seven rebounds and three assists across 36 minutes during Monday's 103-102 victory over Golden State.
items.story: Sanders posted a career-high 20 points while filling in for James Harden (shoulder). The 2025 second-round pick has appeared in 27 games this season, and he's proven to be a steady backup on an aging roster that needs ample support. The Nevada product isn't a worthy fantasy prospect right now, but he's one long-term injury away from more time with the parent club.

items.headline: Sanders is starting Monday's game against the Warriors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Sanders is in line for his first start since Nov. 22, as the Clippers will be without James Harden (shoulder) on Monday. Sanders has had a tough go of late, averaging 4.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists in his last five games.

items.headline: Sanders provided five points (2-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist over 16 minutes during Friday's 119-103 win over Portland.
items.story: Sanders took only two shots but still led Los Angeles' bench in scoring. The rookie second-rounder is still seeing relatively solid playing time but has seen a decline in minutes compared to mid-to-late November. With Derrick Jones (knee) set to return to the lineup against the Pistons on Sunday, Sanders' minutes could take a hit.

items.headline: Sanders racked up five points (2-5 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 30 minutes during Thursday's 122-101 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Sanders was barely able to tie his season-high mark in assists despite playing more minutes than usual due to James Harden's (calf) absence. Sanders is expected to remain a bench option in upcoming action as he looks to end a run of five games without scoring in double figures.

items.headline: Richardson supplied nine points (3-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, five assists and one steal across 29 minutes during Monday's 103-94 loss to Washington.
items.story: Richardson continued to handle an expanded backcourt role with Jalen Suggs (knee) sidelined and Anthony Black (rest) unavailable. Although he struggled from beyond the arc, the young guard contributed five assists without committing a turnover. Richardson should remain a potential short-term streaming option for assists while Orlando is shorthanded, but his fantasy appeal could diminish once the team gets healthy.

items.headline: Richardson contributed four points (2-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt), a rebound and three assists across 26 minutes in Sunday's 108-97 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Richardson struggled to establish an offensive rhythm, missing all four of his three-point attempts while contributing little outside of playmaking. His 26-minute workload provided opportunities, as he continues to start due to the absence of Jalen Suggs (knee), but his lack of production is concerning. Through four starts, Richardson is averaging just 6.0 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game. His inconsistent shooting and modest statistical contributions make him difficult to trust outside deeper formats.

items.headline: Richardson had six points (2-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt) and one rebound over 17 minutes during Sunday's 111-102 win over New York.
items.story: Richardson made his first career start with Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined, though he struggled to make much of an impact offensively. The second-year guard could remain in line for additional opportunities if Jalen Suggs' right knee injury forces him to miss time, but Anthony Black's strong season debut may limit Richardson's upside.

items.headline: Richardson is in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Cody Taylor of USA Today reports.
items.story: Richardson will make his first start of the season Sunday due to the absence of Paolo Banchero (ankle), and the second-year guard will share the backcourt alongside Jalen Suggs, with Desmond Bane and Franz Wagner at the three and four, respectively. Richardson is averaging 4.0 points and 3.0 assists in 14.0 minutes per game in two bench appearances this season.

items.headline: The Magic exercised Richardson's team option Wednesday, per Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel.
items.story: This is an expected transaction after Orlando chose Richardson in the first round of last year's draft. Richardson is cleared to play through a back injury for Opening Night, but he's unlikely to play a significant role Wednesday.

items.headline: Richardson (back) is off the injury report for Wednesday's season opener against the Hawks.
items.story: Richardson is cleared to play through a back injury for Opening Night. However, he's unlikely to play a significant role Wednesday.

items.headline: Richardson (back) is considered day-to-day, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Richardson exited Friday's 136-115 preseason win over Miami due to back soreness. While he hasn't been officially ruled out for Opening Night against Atlanta, it appears there's a chance he won't be available for that game. With Noah Penda (hamstring) ruled out and Franz Wagner (shoulder) dealing with an injury, Tristan da Silva and Anthony Black could see more minutes.

items.headline: Richardson logged seven minutes before exiting Friday's 136-115 preseason win over the Heat due to lower-back soreness. He contributed two rebounds and two assists.
items.story: Head coach Sean Sweeney said that Richardson will be re-evaluated after exiting Friday's contest. He can be considered questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Hawks until the Magic provide an update on his status.

items.headline: Richardson recorded 10 points (4-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and four assists across 23 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Richardson delivered a balanced performance in a reserve role. The young guard's versatility offers promise, although his regular-season fantasy value will depend on securing consistent playing time in Orlando's crowded backcourt, something that's far from a reality right now.

items.headline: Richardson won't start Tuesday's preseason game against Cleveland.
items.story: Jalen Suggs (illness) is back in the lineup for Tuesday's contest, pushing Richardson to the second unit. The second-year guard will continue trying to carve out a steady role ahead of the regular season.

items.headline: Richardson recorded 12 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one steal in 26 minutes as a starter during Sunday's 119-105 preseason loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Richardson made a positive impression in his starting opportunity with Jalen Suggs (illness) and Anthony Black (ankle) out, shooting efficiently from the field while contributing as a playmaker. The young guard also committed just two turnovers despite handling significant minutes, strengthening his case for a meaningful role in Orlando's backcourt rotation.

items.headline: Richardson will start in Wednesday's preseason game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Jalen Suggs (illness) and Anthony Black (ankle) are out for Wednesday's exhibition, so Richardson will start. Desmond Bane, Franz Wagner, Paolo Banchero and Wendell Carter will join Richardson in the first unit for Wednesday's game.

items.headline: Richardson has some obstacles to climb in order to seize an Opening Night role.
items.story: The 2025 first-rounder was not a big part of Orlando's rotation in his rookie season, averaging 10.9 minutes per game over 54 regular-season appearances. With Anthony Black primed to serve as the Magic's sixth man off the bench, Richardson is left to compete with the likes of Jamal Cain, Noah Penda and Jevon Carter for reserve minutes this season.

items.headline: Richardson (rest) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against the Celtics, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Richardson will sit out Orlando's Summer League finale for rest purposes. Over three Las Vegas Summer League appearances, the 20-year-old guard averaged 18.3 points, 4.7 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 30.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Richardson (undisclosed) finished with 25 points (10-15 FG, 3-5 3Pt,1-1 FT), two rebounds, four assists and three steals in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 99-92 Summer League win over the 76ers.
items.story: Richardson was a bright spot in his return from a one-game absence for undisclosed reasons. The 2025 first-rounder is preparing for his second season with the Magic and is aiming to make a case for a reserve role in 2026-27 after hardly being part of the rotation as a rookie.

items.headline: Richardson (undisclosed) will miss Sunday's Las Vegas Summer League game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Richardson will sit out the second leg of a Summer League back-to-back set, but he should return for Wednesday's meeting with the 76ers. TyTy Washington will draw the start in Richardson's absence Sunday, and there should be more minutes available for Keon Johnson.

items.headline: Richardson finished with 15 points (4-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and six assists across 30 minutes in Saturday's 93-88 Summer League win over Miami.
items.story: Richardson scored 15 points in Thursday's 86-74 loss to Charlotte. While he wasn't more productive Saturday, he shot the ball well by going 3-for-5 from behind the arc. The 20-year-old had a quiet rookie campaign in 2025-26, averaging 4.4 points, 1.2 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 0.4 steals over 10.9 minutes in 54 regular-season appearances. Richardson will need to play well this summer, though that still may not improve his chances of earning a more prominent role with the Magic in 2026-27.

items.headline: Richardson finished with 15 points (6-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, four assists and two steals across 30 minutes in Thursday's 86-74 Summer League loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Richardson is coming off an uneventful 2025-26 campaign in which he averaged only 4.4 points, 1.2 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 0.4 steals over 10.9 minutes in 54 regular-season appearances. Even with injuries to some of the starters, the 20-year-old wasn't able to take advantage and mostly served as a depth piece. While Richardson looked good to begin Summer League play, he's still not guaranteed to seize a consistent role in the rotation even if he continues to play well in Las Vegas.

items.headline: Richardson averaged 4.4 points, 1.2 rebounds and 1.1 assists per contest in 54 regular-season games during 2025-26.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder appeared just once during Orlando's seven-game first-round series with Detroit. If the Magic let Jevon Carter walk away this offseason, Richardson would have a better chance of cracking the Opening Night rotation in 2026-27.

items.headline: Richardson finished Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game victory over the Hornets with two points (1-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds and two assists over six minutes.
items.story: Richardson made a brief appearance, taking advantage of the fact that the game was a blowout. It continues what has been mostly a disappointing campaign, with Richardson averaging just 4.4 points in 10.8 minutes per game over 55 contests.

items.headline: Richardson finished with zero points (0-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists in 18 minutes during Sunday's 139-87 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Richardson couldn't find his rhythm Sunday, but he was shooting the ball well heading into the matchup. Across his last five outings, he's hitting 57.1 percent from the field, but he's getting just 10.9 minutes per contest, which keeps him off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: The Magic recalled Richardson from the G League's Osceola Magic on Saturday.
items.story: The rookie first-round pick made his second G League appearance of the season Friday in Osceola's 113-106 win over the Delaware Blue Coats, finishing with 17 points (8-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 32 minutes. Richardson will be available for Orlando's home game versus the Lakers on Saturday but isn't expected to be featured in the rotation.

items.headline: Richardson (back) is available to play Wednesday against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Richardson is all set to return from a two-game absence. He's been used sparingly in recent weeks, but there are more minutes available with Anthony Black (abdomen) on the shelf.

items.headline: Richardson (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Richardson remains day-to-day after missing the past two games for Orlando. He recently lost his rotation spot to Jevon Carter, but more minutes are up for grabs with Anthony Black (abdomen) sidelined.

items.headline: Richardson (back) is unavailable for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Richardson has been ruled out for a second straight game due to back spasms. With Anthony Black (back) also sidelined, Jett Howard and Jevon Carter could see expanded roles.

items.headline: Richardson (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Richardson was unable to play in Saturday's win against Minnesota due to lower-back spasms. The rookie first-rounder has a chance to return for Sunday's contest, and while he's had inconsistent playing time since the All-Star break, Richardson would be in line for a larger role off the bench if Anthony Black (back) was ruled out.

items.headline: Richardson has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves due to lower-back spasms.
items.story: Richardson will miss the front end of the Magic's back-to-back set and look to return for Sunday's road tilt against the Bucks. The rookie first-rounder has seen inconsistent playing time this season and has averaged just 7.2 minutes per game in five outings since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Orlando recalled Richardson from the G League's Osceola Magic on Friday.
items.story: Richardson joined Osceola for its 128-111 win over the Cleveland Charge on Friday, during which he recorded 22 points (9-15 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine assists, three rebounds and one steal in 31 minutes. The rookie first-rounder has totaled just 15 minutes in two appearances over Orlando's last four games, and he isn't guaranteed to see meaningful burn in Sunday's game against Detroit unless multiple key backcourt contributors are sidelined.

items.headline: Richardson (ankle) is available for Friday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Richardson is bothered by a sore left ankle, but he's still healthy enough to play Friday. With Jalen Suggs (knee) sidelined, the expectation is that Richardson and Tyus Jones will share the minutes as the backup point guards behind Anthony Black.

items.headline: Richardson is questionable for Friday's game against the 76ers with left ankle soreness.
items.story: Richardson wasn't on the injury report heading into the Magic's most recent game Wednesday against the Nets, but the sore ankle likely explains why he didn't see any minutes in the 104-103 win. He had received playing time in each of the Magic's prior 12 contests, averaging 8.8 points, 1.9 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.2 three-pointers in 17.7 minutes.

items.headline: Richardson recorded 20 points (7-12 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds and three assists over 26 minutes during the Magic's 120-112 loss to the Wizards on Tuesday.
items.story: Richardson saw most of his playing time in the second half when the game seemed out of reach for the Magic, but the rookie first-rounder ended up leading the team in scoring while contributing to Orlando's late comeback attempt. Richardson has seen extended playing time off the bench in back-to-back games, due in part to the absence of Jalen Suggs (knee). More strong play like Tuesday could earn Richardson more consistent minutes moving forward.

items.headline: Richardson closed with 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), one rebound and four assists over 27 minutes during Sunday's 135-127 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: This was a solid showing for Richardson, as he took advantage of some extra minutes with Jalen Suggs sidelined by an MCL contusion. If Suggs continues to miss time, which wouldn't be a surprise, Richardson could be a name to monitor in deeper formats.

items.headline: Richardson ended Monday's 107-106 loss to the Raptors with seven points (2-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one steal over 20 minutes.
items.story: Richardson is slowly becoming more involved for the Magic in the absence of Franz Wagner (ankle). Over his last seven games, the rookie has played 19.3 minutes per contest with averages of 8.1 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.9 three-pointers. His fantasy appeal remains limited to deeper formats for the time being.

items.headline: Richardson notched 11 points (5-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four rebounds, one block and one steal over 22 minutes during Monday's 120-97 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Richardson's involvement is on the rise, though he's mostly just a deep-league fantasy asset for now. Over his last four outings, Richardson has averaged 9.8 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.5 three-pointers in 18.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Richardson contributed nine points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two assists and one rebound in eight minutes during Saturday's 132-120 loss to New York.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder did not see the floor in the first three quarters but played the last 7:35 with Jalen Suggs (hip) exiting to the locker room and not returning. Richardson impressed during his limited run and ended with a bench-high nine points for Orlando. The Michigan State product is not guaranteed to play meaningful minutes on a nightly basis, though he could see increased playing time if Suggs is forced to miss additional time.

items.headline: Richardson ended Wednesday's 114-112 loss to the Spurs with eight points (3-5 FG, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 16 minutes.
items.story: Richardson seems to have moved up in the depth chart, playing at least 10 minutes in his last three games and averaging 11.0 points, 3.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 0.7 steals and 1.3 threes in that span. Time will tell if this role boost will last, but Richardson is definitely worth monitoring in deeper leagues, especially if an injury were to occur to Orlando's backcourt.

items.headline: Richardson racked up 18 points (7-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes during Sunday's 138-129 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Richardson saw a sizable increase in opportunities given a thin Magic backcourt. He was averaging 4.4 minutes in five November appearances entering Sunday but logged a season-high 21 minutes in the loss, scoring in double figures for the first time in his young NBA career. Richardson could eventually carve out a consistent role in Orlando's rotation, but for the time being, he'll presumably move out of the fold once Jalen Suggs (knee) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Richardson racked up zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one assist over seven minutes during Tuesday's 127-112 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Richardson came up empty in the scoring column for the fifth straight game, having played limited minutes to this point in his young career. While the Magic could certainly do with some reliable shooting, it doesn't appear as though Richardson is on the radar as far as the coaching staff is concerned.

items.headline: Richardson (coach's decision) went unused in Wednesday's 125-121 win over Miami.
items.story: The entire Magic backcourt is healthy for the start of the new season, leaving no room in the rotation for Richardson. The rookie first-round pick out of Michigan State showed some promise during the preseason, but he'll likely have minimal value in redraft leagues unless the Magic are down multiple key guards in a given game.

items.headline: Richardson provided 13 points (4-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, one steal and one turnover in 20 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 120-104 preseason win over Miami.
items.story: Through three preseason outings, Richardson has produced averages of 11.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 2.3 triples per game on 46.2 percent shooting. It's unlikely he'll have fantasy value out of the gates, as he'll likely be playing limited minutes behind Desmond Bane, but Richardson will be a name to watch if Orlando experiences an injury to one of their backcourt players this season.

items.headline: Richardson supplied 13 points (5-11 FG, 3-3 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and one steal across 24 minutes in Saturday's 126-118 preseason win over the Heat.
items.story: Richardson recorded a game-high mark in scoring, with all of his points coming in the third quarter. The No. 25 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft has an opportunity to carve out a role with the Magic in his rookie season, though he'll likely have to compete for minutes off the bench with Anthony Black and Jett Howard. Richardson averaged 12.1 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.9 assists across 25.3 minutes per game in 36 outings during his lone collegiate campaign at Michigan State.

items.headline: Jokic registered 26 points (10-22 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, eight assists, four steals and a block across 35 minutes in Monday's 118-110 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Jokic narrowly missed another triple-double, finishing one rebound and two assists short despite a strong all-around performance. His four steals provided a substantial fantasy boost, helping compensate for relatively inefficient shooting. Jokic remains one of fantasy basketball's most reliable contributors thanks to his exceptional involvement across scoring, rebounding and playmaking, with defensive production offering additional upside. He's averaging 22.0 points, 9.7 rebounds, 9.0 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.3 blocks per game to open the season.

items.headline: Jokic posted 18 points (8-13 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, 10 assists and three steals in 37 minutes during Friday's 127-120 win over Phoenix.
items.story: Jokic didn't need to carry the scoring load Friday, but he still filled the box score effectively. The three-time MVP shot efficiently and picked up three steals while letting the red-hot Jamal Murray and Christian Braun take over. Denver won consecutive games for the first time this season, and Jokic's playmaking remains the engine of the offense.

items.headline: Jokic finished with 21 points (8-13 FG, 5-5 FT), 13 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal across 34 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Jokic ended with his second triple-double of the 2026-27 campaign Wednesday. However, he wasn't perfect, amassing seven turnovers to bring his total to 16 on the year. The multi-time MVP is now averaging 22.0 points, 10.5 rebounds, 9.0 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.8 blocks over 37.1 minutes per contest in his first four regular-season appearances, though he has shot an inefficient 21.7 percent from deep.

items.headline: Jokic logged 19 points (8-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, 11 assists, three blocks and one steal across 35 minutes during Monday's 134-114 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Jokic led the team in assists Monday, setting a season high in dimes in the process. The perennial MVP candidate has logged a pair of double-doubles through three games on the young campaign, posting a full stat line each time out so far.

items.headline: Jokic closed Saturday's 141-135 overtime victory over New Orleans with 35 points (12-23 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 8-8 FT), 15 rebounds, 10 assists, three blocks and two steals over 44 minutes.
items.story: Jokic turned things around after a slow start to the season, at least by his lofty standards, recording his first triple-double of the campaign. For good measure, he added four blocks, an unexpected yet welcome surprise for fantasy managers. There isn't much left to say when it comes to what Jokic can do on a basketball court. Those who invested in him with the first or second pick in drafts should feel at ease with their decision.

items.headline: Jokic contributed 13 points (5-19 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), seven rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal across 35 minutes during Thursday's 96-84 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Jokic started the season with a mediocre performance, at least by his lofty standards. He still managed to chip in across all major categories, providing managers with a sense of reassurance. Up against the might of the Thunder, it's not a total surprise to see Jokic struggling, much like Victor Wembanyama did on Opening Night. Criticism aside, another elite fantasy season seems inevitable, likely ending with a top-three finish in all formats.

items.headline: Jokic posted 17 points (7-8 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 0-0 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 31 minutes in Friday's 121-106 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Jokic delivered another highly efficient performance, missing just one of his eight field-goal attempts while leading the Nuggets in assists and ranking second in rebounds. The star center looks ready to roll ahead of the regular-season opener against the Thunder on Thursday, Oct. 22. Jokic remains arguably the premier fantasy basketball option heading into the regular season, with his combination of scoring, rebounding and assists providing an exceptionally high floor.

items.headline: Jokic logged five points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and a steal over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 122-110 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Jokic had a quiet scoring night in a limited run, though he still led Denver in assists. It was a sharp drop from Monday's win over the Bulls, when he posted 22 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. The three-time MVP hasn't topped 26 minutes in four preseason appearances, so expect his workload to stay light until the games count.

items.headline: Jokic recorded 22 points (8-12, 1-2 3Pt, 5-7 FT), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and a block in 26 minutes during Sunday's 133-128 preseason win over the Bulls.
items.story: Denver elected to play its starters into the second half for the first time this preseason, leading to Jokic producing a highly efficient triple-double while playing three quarters. The star big man led the game in rebounds and assists. Jokic is coming off six straight seasons in which he finished in the top two in MVP voting, and he seems poised for another dominant campaign.

items.headline: Jokic recorded three points (1-1 FG, 1-2 FT), seven assists, three rebounds, one steal and a block in 14 minutes during Sunday's 109-97 preseason loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Jokic played facilitator almost exclusively Sunday, totaling a game-high seven assists while only recording one official field-goal attempt. Despite not looking for his shot, Jokic added to his highlight tape with a crafty behind-the-back pass along the baseline, which resulted in a Cameron Johnson three-pointer. The star big man is expected to retain a limited role throughout the preseason to preserve his health for the regular season.

items.headline: Jokic reiterated Monday that he intends to sign a new contract with the Nuggets next offseason, Brendan Vogt of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.story: "I'm going to sign next year, if they want me," Jokic said, adding that his decision to hold off on an extension this summer was purely business. The three-time MVP passed on a four-year extension worth $278 million and can become eligible for a five-year deal worth approximately $360 million next summer. Jokic has repeatedly expressed his desire to spend the remainder of his career in Denver, so his decision to delay a new deal appears financially motivated rather than an indication that he's considering leaving the Nuggets.

items.headline: Jokic (illness) registered eight points (1-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 6-7 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and one steal in 23 minutes during Serbia's 76-64 win over Italy in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Jokic has been playing through an illness for the Serbian national team, per Harrison Wind of TheDNVR.com, so he hasn't been looking like his usual dominant self on the court. The perennial MVP candidate figures to be well past whatever's ailing him come time for training camp with the Nuggets later this fall, and he's paralleled by only Victor Wembanyama in discussions for the No. 1 overall pick in fantasy circles.

items.headline: Jokic recorded six points (3-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt), 13 rebounds, six assists and three steals in 23 minutes during Serbia's 102-73 win over Iceland in Friday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Jokic attempted only seven shots but impacted the game in his usual fashion as a rebounder and facilitator. The 31-year-old averaged a triple-double for the second consecutive regular season in 2025-26, posting 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 10.7 assists per game while finishing second in MVP voting. Denver has reshaped the supporting cast around him this offseason, but Jokic remains the unquestioned centerpiece of the offense and should once again be among the first players selected in virtually every fantasy format in 2026-27.

items.headline: The Nuggets added another playmaker with the signing of DeMar DeRozan on Friday to pair alongside Jokic to help handle the offensive pressure in 2026-27.
items.story: Jokic averaged a triple-double for the second straight season in 2025-26, though it's possible the addition of DeRozan slightly cuts into his ball-handling responsibilities. Regardless, the presence of DeRozan, a six-time All-Star, as opposed to the more defensive-minded Peyton Watson, should aid Jokic's efficiency as well as his ability to find open looks all around the court in 2026-27.

items.headline: Black will be rested Monday against the Wizards.
items.story: The Magic are listing him out for left ankle injury management, so they are taking a cautious approach for the second leg of this back-to-back set. He finished with 23 points (6-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 10-11 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and two steals over 33 minutes Sunday against Boston. Jase Richardson, Jevon Carter and Jamal Cain could be more involved as a result.

items.headline: Black closed Sunday's 108-97 loss to Boston with 23 points (6-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 10-11 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and two steals over 33 minutes.
items.story: Black tied Tristan da Silva for the team lead in scoring, while the former accounted for more than half of Orlando's 19 free-throw attempts in the loss. It was good to see Black attacking the rim with his three-point shot not falling, and his eight boards also represented a season high.
