items.story: Walsh will get the start to begin the preseason. The 22-year-old is coming off his best campaign in 2025-26, and in 25 regular-season starts, he averaged 7.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 steals over 22.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh is learning from Paul George this offseason on how to expand his offensive game, per Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com.
items.story: After making a career-high 25 starts last regular season, Walsh is looking to take another step forward in 2026-27. He's in contention for a starting spot on the wing with Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Sam Hauser during training camp, which will remain a battle to monitor this fall.

items.headline: Walsh and the Celtics agreed to a three-year, $15 million extension Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Boston previously picked up Walsh's $2.4 million option for the 2026-27 season and now added three more years for their 2023 second-rounder. During the 2025-26 regular season, Walsh appeared in 68 games with averages of 5.4 points, 4.0 rebounds and 0.8 assists.

items.headline: The Celtics picked up their 2026-27 team option for Walsh on Monday, Adam Himmelsbach of The Boston Globe reports.
items.story: This is an expected move by the Celtics. Walsh appeared in 68 regular-season games in 2025-26, posting averages of 5.4 points and 4.0 rebounds in 17.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Walsh logged zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) across five minutes during Saturday's 109-100 loss to Philadelphia in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Despite the absence of Jayson Tatum (knee), Walsh didn't benefit. In fact, he logged a series-low five minutes while going without a point. Although the 2025-26 campaign didn't work out exactly as the team had hoped, Walsh at least saw his production improve, as he averaged a career-best 5.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.7 steals across 17.8 minutes in 68 regular-season appearances (25 starts). While Walsh should hold a stable role in the rotation for the Celtics next season, assuming he remains on the roster, he may have trouble being consistently productive as long as the starters stay healthy.

items.headline: Walsh isn't starting in Sunday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Walsh started in the Celtics' final three contests of the regular season, most recently finishing with nine points, eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in 33 minutes in the 113-108 win over Orlando on April 12. However, with a healthy starting lineup for Boston versus Philadelphia, Walsh will head back to the bench, potentially seeing 10-15 minutes of work in Game 1.

items.headline: Walsh is starting Thursday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Walsh will take the place of Jaylen Brown, who is out Thursday due to left Achilles tendinitis. Walsh started a pair of games down the stretch but failed to score in double figures in either opportunity.

items.headline: Walsh is not in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Heat on Wednesday.
items.story: Walsh started each of the Celtics' last two games, but the third-year wing will revert to a bench role for Wednesday's contest. The Celtics will roll with a starting lineup of Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Sam Hauser, Jayson Tatum and Neemias Queta.

items.headline: Walsh will start in Sunday's game against Charlotte, according to Justin Turpin of WEEI.com.
items.story: The Celtics are down Jaylen Brown (Achilles) and Derrick White (knee), so head coach Joe Mazzulla will turn to Walsh to make his first start since New Year's Day. In 20 starts during the campaign, the 22-year-old is averaging 7.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 0.6 blocks and 1.1 steals across 21.5 minutes.

items.headline: Walsh recorded five points (2-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt), three rebounds, three blocks and one assist across 27 minutes Friday in the Celtics' 109-102 win over the Hawks.
items.story: With Jaylen Brown (Achilles) sitting out Friday, Walsh re-entered the rotation after going unused in each of the Celtics' last six games. Walsh fared well in his low-usage role, knocking down his lone perimeter shot while making his biggest impact at the defensive end. Despite seeing heavy minutes Friday, Walsh could drop back out of the rotation Sunday in Charlotte if Brown is cleared to return to action.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Walsh was sidelined for Friday's 120-100 win over the Mavericks due to an illness, but the third-year pro has recovered enough to return for Sunday's road tilt. His minutes were set to take a sizable hit due to the return of Jayson Tatum, but Walsh could still see some meaningful playing time for the next couple of weeks due to the absence of Nikola Vucevic (finger).

items.headline: Walsh (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Walsh is under the weather and will miss Friday's contest, but he'll look to progress enough in his recovery to be available for Sunday's game against the Cavaliers. Walsh's absence shouldn't impact the Celtics' rotation all that much, seeing as Jayson Tatum (Achilles) has been cleared to make his 2025-26 debut against Dallas.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) is questionable for Friday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Walsh was a very late addition to the injury report. He's been averaging 13.0 minutes over his last seven appearances, and minutes will be hard to come by with Jayson Tatum (Achilles) targeting his debut against Dallas.

items.headline: Walsh ended with four points (2-2 FG, 0-1 FT) and three rebounds over 14 minutes during Wednesday's 103-84 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Walsh logged 14 minutes in the loss, most of which came during garbage time. While it has been a somewhat encouraging season for Walsh, his role in recent times has been less than ideal. In 12 games over the past month, he has seen just 13.8 minutes per game, putting up 4.2 points and 3.5 rebounds. At this point, he should not be rostered in any moderately competitive league.

items.headline: Walsh recorded 16 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and three steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 124-105 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Walsh had been quiet lately, but he turned in his first double-digit scoring night since Jan. 3. His versatility was on full display, and the large margin of victory helped him see additional run. Walsh can deliver when called upon, but his role hasn't been as consistent as it was at the start of the campaign.

items.headline: Walsh (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Friday in the Celtics' 98-96 win over the Heat.
items.story: With Jaylen Brown (hamstring/knee) and Sam Hauser (thumb) returning from one-game absences and with Nikola Vucevic making his Celtics debut, head coach Joe Mazzulla opted to remove Walsh from the rotation. Though defense is Walsh's calling card, his lack of productivity on the offensive end looks as though it cost him his spot in the second unit Friday. Since moving out of the starting five Jan. 3, Walsh has shot just 38.3 percent from the field and 25.8 percent from three-point range in 18 appearances. Walsh's move outside of the rotation may not necessarily be a permanent one, but even if he gets some minutes in the Celtics' next game Sunday versus the Knicks, he shouldn't be expected to deliver much fantasy value.

items.headline: Walsh logged zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) over 10 minutes during Tuesday's 110-100 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: Walsh went scoreless in the win, now serving as nothing more than a depth piece for the Celtics. Outside of a brief run earlier in the season, Walsh seems as though his time as a viable fantasy asset has come and gone. At this point, there is no reason to be holding him, even in deeper formats.

items.headline: Walsh ended with five points (1-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds, one block and one steal over 16 minutes during Friday's 112-93 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Walsh was used sparingly again, playing fewer than 20 minutes for the seventh time in the past eight games. With Sam Hauser seemingly taking hold of the starting power forward position, Walsh has been relegated to a depth role. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 3.4 points and 2.5 rebounds in 14.5 minutes per game, leaving him well outside the top 300 in nine-category formats.

items.headline: Walsh ended with six points (3-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), nine rebounds, one assist and three steals across 26 minutes during Monday's 98-96 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Walsh logged 26 minutes in the loss, which is the most he has played in his past five games. After a stint in the starting lineup, Walsh has since been reduced to a limited role off the bench. In four games over the past week, Walsh has averaged just 1.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 16.0 minutes per game. Given the uncertainty in Boston, there is no reason to consider Walsh a pickup based on this effort.

items.headline: Walsh closed with 13 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), 13 rebounds, two assists and one block across 30 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 146-115 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Shifting to the second unit while Sam Hauser got a start at the four, Walsh produced his second double-double of the season, with the other coming Nov. 20 against the Cavaliers. Walsh's production has been on the decline in the starting five -- he'd failed to score in double digits, or pull down more than seven boards, in seven straight games -- but it's not yet clear if Saturday's effort will be enough for the third-year forward to regain his spot.

items.headline: Walsh is not in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Clippers on Saturday, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Head coach Joe Mazulla will shake up the rotation Saturday, moving Walsh to the bench while Sam Hauser enters the starting five. Walsh has been a mainstay in the Celtics' starting lineup since Nov. 12, but over his last seven outings he has averaged just 4.0 points and 3.4 rebounds over 14.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh chipped in three points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists in 19 minutes during Friday's 140-122 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Walsh returned from a one-game absence due to an Illness, slotting straight back into the starting lineup. The positives end there, however, as Walsh was unable to have any sort of tangible impact on the game. After a brief run of value, it's been slim pickings for Walsh of late, as he's averaging 4.3 points and 4.8 rebounds in 17.7 minutes in his past four appearances.

items.headline: Walsh is in the Celtics' starting lineup against the Pacers on Friday.
items.story: Walsh was cleared to return Friday from a one-game absence due to an illness, and he will reclaim his spot in the starting lineup from Josh Minott. Walsh has averaged 11.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.3 threes and 1.5 steals over 23.3 minutes per game since Dec. 2.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) is available for Friday's game against the Pacers, Zack Cox of the Boston Herald reports.
items.story: Walsh was able to shed a probable tag for this contest. Over his last 16 starts, the forward has provided some low-end fantasy numbers with 8.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.3 steals in 23.9 minutes.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) is probable for Friday's matchup against the Pacers.
items.story: Walsh sat out Boston's most recent game but is expected to be back Friday. He's started 16 straight appearances, averaging 8.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.3 steals in 23.9 minutes.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) won't play Monday against the Pacers, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: Walsh was unable to clear his questionable tag for this contest, but Jaylen Brown (illness) was given the green light. With Walsh out, Sam Hauser, Josh Minott and Hugo Gonzalez could potentially be more involved.

items.headline: Walsh (illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Pacers, Zack Cox of the Boston Herald reports.
items.story: Walsh joins Jaylen Brown as the two Celtics players battling through illnesses, with the latter's ailment preventing him from playing in Saturday's 112-96 win over the Raptors. If Walsh is unable to play Monday, then Sam Hauser and Josh Minott would be the top candidates to enter the Celtics' starting lineup. Walsh has started in each of the Celtics' last 16 games, and over that span he has averaged 8.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.3 steals over 23.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh produced 20 points (8-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds and three steals across 32 minutes during Thursday's 116-101 loss to Milwaukee.
items.story: Walsh continues to thrive since moving into the starting lineup Nov. 12. The 21-year-old forward led both teams with three steals, his second straight game with a trio of swipes, and recorded the second 20-point performance of his career. He's been hyper-efficient as a scorer lately, shooting an impressive 81.1 percent from the field over the past five games while averaging 15.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.0 steals, and 1.0 assists in 26.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh recorded nine points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds and three steals over 26 minutes before fouling out of Sunday's 121-113 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Walsh got the starting nod for a 12th consecutive contest and had an impactful performance on both ends of the floor, despite fouling out with just over two minutes to go in the final quarter. The 21-year-old forward led all players in steals and tied his season-high mark, tallying multiple swipes for the third time in his last five appearances. He also delivered another efficient outing from the field and has shot an impressive 76.5 percent from the floor in that five-game span, during which he has averaged 14.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.2 assists in 27.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Walsh posted 17 points (6-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal over 26 minutes during the Celtics' 126-105 win over the Lakers on Friday.
items.story: Coming off a career-best 22-point performance in Thursday's win over the Wizards, Walsh provided another effective performance during the second leg of the Celtics' back-to-back set Friday. He connected on a career-high four triples, led the Celtics with two blocks and finished with a game-high plus-28 point differential. Boston has a 9-2 record since Walsh permanently entered the starting lineup Nov. 12 against the Grizzlies, and over his last four outings he has averaged 15.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.5 threes, 1.5 steals and 1.3 blocks over 28.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Middleton totaled four points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and two assists across 23 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Middleton exceeded 20 minutes for the first time this season, although he failed to make the most of his opportunity. Thus far,  Middleton has looked like a shell of his former self, offering very little in terms of tangible production. In four appearances, he has averaged 3.0 points and 2.0 rebounds in 16.0 minutes per game. Moving forward, Washington could certainly phase him out of the rotation.

items.headline: Middleton racked up one rebound in 13 minutes during Monday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Middleton failed to attempt a shot during his brief appearance, finishing with a minus-17 rating. The veteran forward has played a limited role off Washington's bench to begin the season, making it difficult for him to provide consistent fantasy value. Unless his minutes increase significantly, Middleton remains an unappealing option outside the deepest leagues.

items.headline: Middleton amassed five points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 14 minutes in Friday's 107-106 preseason loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Middleton made his 2026 preseason debut in the Wizards' final exhibition game. The veteran forward struggled with efficiency but led the second unit in assists. He'll likely compete for playing time with Justin Champagnie and Will Riley behind Anthony Davis in the regular season.

items.headline: Middleton (rest) was unavailable for Monday's 131-122 preseason loss to Brooklyn, Greg Finberg of Wizardscentral.com reports.
items.story: Middleton has yet to play in the preseason as he ramps up his conditioning. The veteran forward's next chance to suit up will come Friday against New Orleans.

items.headline: Middleton did not leave the bench during Saturday's 114-108 preseason win over the Pistons.
items.story: Middleton has yet to play this preseason, but the 35-year-old veteran isn't dealing with an injury. His next chance to get out there will come Monday versus the Nets.

items.headline: Middleton (rest) is trending in the right direction for Saturday's preseason game against Detroit, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
items.story: Middleton is being eased into action to begin the year. His status remains up in the air for Saturday's exhibition after missing Thursday's preseason opener.

items.headline: Middleton (rest) won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Knicks, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Middleton is ramping up for game action. His next chance to play is Saturday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Middleton got in a workout Thursday ahead of his second season with Washington.
items.story: Middleton is in line for a different role with the new-look Wizards this time around, though. The veteran forward started each of his 34 appearances in Washington a year ago before being shipped to Dallas as part of the Anthony Davis trade, and he's positioned initially as Davis' primary backup at power forward heading into training camp. Middleton also routinely sat out one leg of back-to-back sets with the Wizards, so it remains to be seen if the team will have a similar workload management plan in store for him as well.

items.headline: Middleton agreed to a three-year, $17.6 million contract with the Wizards on Tuesday via a sign-and-trade with the Mavericks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Dallas is sending Middleton to the Wizards as part of a six-team deal, per Charania. The veteran forward was traded from Milwaukee to Washington in February 2025 before being sent to the Mavericks last February. Now, he'll return to Washington, where he figures to serve as a veteran presence while providing frontcourt depth behind AJ Dybantsa and Anthony Davis (finger). Over 63 regular-season outings (50 starts) between the Mavericks and Wizards last season, Middleton averaged 10.2 points, 3.7 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 0.7 steals in 22.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Middleton closed Sunday's 149-128 victory over the Bulls with eight points (2-3 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist across six minutes.
items.story: Middleton logged just six minutes with the Mavericks, pulling most of their starters early. Since his trade from Washington, Middleton made 29 appearances for the Mavericks with averages of 10.0 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.2 three-pointers in 21.1 minutes per contest. The veteran will now hit the open market as a free agent.

items.headline: Middleton will start Tuesday against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Middleton will get the spot start with P.J. Washington (elbow) out, and the former will be joined in the first unit by Cooper Flagg, Max Christie, Naji Marshall and Dwight Powell. As a starter this season, Middleton owns averages of 10.6 points, 3.2 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game.

items.headline: Middleton won't start Friday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Naji Marshall will return to the starting lineup following a two-game absence due to an illness, resulting in Middleton retreating to the second unit. The veteran forward has averaged 6.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.0 steals across 16.2 minutes per game over his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Middleton will start Monday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: With P.J. Washington (illness) unavailable, Middleton will step into the starting five following a one-game absence due to an illness. As a starter for Dallas this season (10 games), the veteran forward has averaged 12.1 points, 4.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 25.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Middleton (illness) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Monday's meeting with Minnesota.
items.story: Middleton will be back in action Monday following a one-game stint on the sidelines, which could result in fewer minutes for Klay Thompson. As a member of the Mavericks, Middleton has contributed averages of 11.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.2 triples per contest.

items.headline: Middleton (illness) won't play in Friday's game against Portland.
items.story: Middleton wasn't listed on the injury report throughout the day. However, he popped up due to an illness, subsequently ruling him out. His next chance to play will be Monday against the Timberwolves. While Middleton is out, Klay Thompson should receive all the minutes he can handle off the bench.

items.headline: Middleton had two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists over 12 minutes during Monday's 137-131 overtime loss to Golden State.
items.story: Middleton was playing a sizable role for the Mavericks when he first joined the team, but he's now trending in the wrong direction. Over his last eight games, he's averaging 10.4 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.0 steals across 19.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Middleton supplied six points (2-9 FG, 2-7 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist and two steals over 18 minutes during Monday's 129-111 loss to New Orleans.
items.story: Middleton scored no more than six points for the third straight game, prior to which he erupted for a season-high 35 points. While the talent is still there. Middleton simply can't sustain meaningful production at this point. Even with his 35-point effort, Middleton sits outside the top-150 players in five games over the past week, averaging 13.2 points, 1.0 steals and 2.6 three-pointers.

items.headline: Middleton finished with 35 points (10-17 FG, 8-10 3Pt, 7-7 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two steals in 25 minutes during Thursday's 120-112 victory over Memphis.
items.story: Middleton was getting nearly everything to fall, especially from beyond the arc, where he buried a season-high eight triples. He paced the Mavs in scoring despite being deployed off the bench and even found a way to add production on the defensive end. It's unfair to expect this kind of scoring production from the 34-year-old regularly, but he still shows flashes of elite scoring from time to time.

items.headline: Middleton won't start Tuesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: After 10 straight starts, Middleton is moving to the bench in favor of Naji Marshall. Even as a starter, Middleton averaged 6.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists in only 21.5 minutes over his past two appearances.

items.headline: Middleton ended with 19 points (7-15 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds and seven assists across 32 minutes during Thursday's 115-114 loss to Orlando.
items.story: Middleton put together his best scoring performance since Feb. 22, and he rewarded the Mavs for keeping him in the starting lineup even after the return of Naji Marshall from a bruised finger. However, Middleton has been held to single figures in three of his last six games, so the consistency simply hasn't been there lately from the veteran forward. Production on the offensive end will only become more difficult once Cooper Flagg builds back up to a full workload.

items.headline: Middleton (shoulder) will play Thursday against Sacramento, Ron Harrod Jr. of DLLS Sports reports.
items.story: Middleton was upgraded to probable leading up to tipoff, and he's now been given the green light to play Thursday night. He's averaging 14.0 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists over his last five games.

items.headline: Middleton (shoulder) is probable for Thursday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Middleton was initially considered questionable for this contest. Thursday's game is the front end of a back-to-back set, so a maintenance day could be on the table for Friday.

items.headline: Middleton (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Middleton sustained a right shoulder stinger in Tuesday's game and did not return. Now, the issue puts his availability at risk for Thursday's contest -- the first of a back-to-back set. Middleton has started in each of his last three appearances.

items.headline: Middleton won't return to Tuesday's game against the Nets due to a right shoulder stinger. He finished with six points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal across 12 minutes.
items.story: Middleton was able to finish out the first half but didn't open the third quarter with the rest of the Dallas starters and will sit out the rest of the contest. The Mavericks will likely turn to Klay Thompson and Caleb Martin to pick up the slack in Middleton's absence. Middleton's status will now warrant monitoring heading into Thursday's game against the Kings.

items.headline: Middleton produced 25 points (11-15 FG, 3-5 3Pt), seven rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 30 minutes during Sunday's 134-130 win over the Pacers.
items.story: It was certainly Middleton's best effort since joining the Mavericks and perhaps his finest of the year altogether. The 25 points were a season high for the 34-year-old forward, whose seven dimes were also his most since Nov. 25 with the Wizards. Over his first four outings for Dallas, Middleton has averaged 16.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.5 three-pointers in 25.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Middleton will start Friday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: With Max Christie (ankle) sidelined, Middleton will draw his first start with the Mavericks. The veteran forward has averaged 10.5 points and 3.0 rebounds in 21.5 minutes per tilt over two appearances for Dallas.

items.headline: Middleton contributed eight points (3-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound and one assist across 21 minutes during Thursday's 124-104 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Since joining Dallas, Middleton has seen a very modest role on the wings. Through two appearances, he's averaging 21.5 minutes with 10.5 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists. It's hard to imagine his minutes trending up much after the All-Star break.

items.headline: Middleton (recently traded) isn't listed on the injury report ahead of Tuesday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Middleton is ready to make his Dallas debut after being traded from the Wizards on Wednesday. He figures to plug right into the rotation, presumably logging bench minutes behind P.J. Washington.

items.headline: Middleton (recently traded) is hoping to make his Mavericks debut Tuesday against the Suns, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The Mavericks are in San Antonio on Saturday as part of a lengthy road trip, and Middleton has finally joined the team after being traded from Washington on Wednesday. The veteran forward is aiming to make his team debut Tuesday. Middleton averaged 10.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 3.3 assists across 24.3 minutes per game with the Wizards this season, and he figures to play a sizable role for a Mavericks team that had been in dire need of frontcourt depth.

items.headline: Middleton (recently traded) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Middleton will have to wait at least one more game to make his Mavericks debut, as Wednesday's trade that centered around Anthony Davis (hand/groin) going to the Wizards is yet to be finalized. Middleton's next chance to play is Tuesday against the Suns.

items.headline: Middleton (recently traded) is listed as doubtful for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Middleton was traded to Dallas on Wednesday but is not expected to make his Mavericks debut Saturday. If the veteran forward is ultimately ruled out, his next chance to play would come Tuesday against the Suns.

items.headline: Middleton (recently traded) is out  for Thursday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: The Mavericks' moves prior to Thursday's trade deadline still aren't official, therefore Middleton isn't yet cleared to make his Dallas debut. That could change for Saturday's meeting with San Antonio. With the Mavs shorthanded Thursday, Max Christie, Caleb Martin and Klay Thompson could each push for minutes near the 30s.

items.headline: The Wizards traded Middleton, AJ Johnson, Malaki Branham, Marvin Bagley, two first-round picks and three second-round picks to the Mavericks on Wednesday in exchange for Anthony Davis (finger), Jaden Hardy, D'Angelo Russell (illness) and Dante Exum (knee), Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After being traded from Milwaukee to Washington ahead of last year's deadline, Middleton will now head to Dallas. The veteran forward is on an expiring $33.3 million contract and is set to enter unrestricted free agency this offseason. He isn't guaranteed a starting role in Dallas but will provide a veteran presence for the team if he isn't bought out. In 34 regular-season outings with the Wizards this season, Middleton averaged 10.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 3.3 assists across 24.3 minutes per game. He can be considered doubtful for Thursday against the Spurs.

items.headline: Middleton notched 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds and two assists over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 132-101 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: With the trade deadline approaching, Middleton continues to fortify his value on the market. The veteran forward is averaging 13.3 points, 4.1 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 25.1 minutes per tilt in his last seven games, shooting 42.3 percent from deep. Middleton has started all 34 of his appearances for the Wizards, though his role and fantasy value could be altered if Washington ends up moving the 34-year-old sharpshooter.

items.headline: Middleton (knee) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Kings.
items.story: After missing Friday's loss to the Lakers for maintenance purposes, the veteran wing will be returning to the rotation Sunday. He'll be a name to watch at the upcoming trade deadline with the Wizards rumored to be sellers.

items.headline: Middleton (knee) won't play Friday against the Lakers.
items.story: Middleton will sit out for maintenance-related reasons for the second leg of this back-to-back set. During Thursday's game against the Bucks, Middleton logged 26 minutes with 13 points, six rebounds and four assists.

items.headline: Middleton supplied 19 points (7-14 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists, one block and three steals over 27 minutes during Tuesday's 115-111 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: It was Middleton's best scoring effort since Opening Night, when he dropped 23 points in a revenge game against the Bucks. The veteran forward missed the Wizards' prior contest with a sore foot, and nagging injuries have cost him three games in January, but he may be finding his form. Over his last five appearances, Middleton is averaging 14.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.8 three-pointers, and 1.2 steals in 27.4 minutes.

items.headline: Middleton (foot) is available for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Middleton will shed his questionable tag due to left foot soreness and return from a one-game absence Tuesday. Over nine January appearances, the veteran forward has averaged 9.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 23.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Middleton (foot) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Middleton is in jeopardy of missing his second straight contest, but the veteran remains day-to-day. If he's unable to play, the Wizards could rely more on Will Riley. Bilal Coulibaly (back) is questionable for the Wizards.

items.headline: Middleton (foot) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Middleton will sit out of Saturday's contest while recovering from a left foot injury, and his next opportunity to play is Tuesday against the Trail Blazers. Rookie first-rounder Will Riley will be in the Wizards starting lineup for the first time in his NBA career due to Middleton's absence.

items.headline: Middleton is questionable for Saturday's game against the Hornets due to left foot soreness.
items.story: The Wizards are likely to re-evaluate Middleton closer to Saturday's tipoff. If the veteran forward is unable to play against Charlotte, Justin Champagnie is a prime candidate to join the starting lineup, while Will Riley could handle a more prominent role off the bench.

items.headline: Middleton (illness) is available to play Thursday against Denver.
items.story: Middleton was previously listed as questionable, but he will give it a go Thursday. He's likely to be a big part of the game plan with Bilal Coulibaly (back) set to miss his fourth straight game.

items.headline: Murray dropped 35 points (10-19 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 11-11 FT), five rebounds, six assists, one steal and one block in 39 minutes during Monday's 118-110 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: After erupting for 39 points during Friday's 127-120 win against Phoenix, Murray posted game highs with 35 points and four three-pointers while going a pristine 11-for-11 at the charity stripe. Through six regular-season appearances thus far, he's gone for 35-plus in three of them, each coinciding with his ability to drain four or more triples and earn double-digit free-throw attempts. Murray's scoring heroics were not enough to get the win, but he's clearly found a groove after finishing with six points (2-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT) and six turnovers in the season-opening loss to the Thunder.

items.headline: Murray finished with 39 points (10-18 FG, 7-9 3Pt, 12-15 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block over 37 minutes in Friday's 127-120 win over Phoenix.
items.story: Murray narrowly missed scoring at least 40 points for the second time this season, though it was still a fantastic all-around effort to lead the Nuggets to a win. The 29-year-old is having an All-Star-caliber season, averaging 25.8 points, 5.6 rebounds and 5.6 assists -- all career highs -- along with 1.2 steals over 38.2 minutes per contest in five regular-season games. He's also shot an efficient 53.5 percent from behind the arc.

items.headline: Murray posted 23 points (9-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt), a rebound, six assists and two blocks across 38 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Murray led Denver in scoring and extended his impressive start to the season as a reliable go-to threat alongside Nikola Jokic. Murray was limited to six points in the season-opening loss to the Thunder on Oct. 22, but he's averaged 28.0 points per game while shooting 48.5 percent from three-point range in three games since.

items.headline: Murray recorded 19 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt), six rebounds, eight assists and three steals across 36 minutes during Monday's 134-114 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Murray turned in an efficient performance, shooting 61.5 percent from the field while leading Denver in assists and steals. The veteran guard also connected on three triples and collected six rebounds, providing well-rounded fantasy production despite the lopsided defeat. Murray continues to serve as a primary offensive facilitator alongside Nikola Jokic.

items.headline: Murray accumulated 42 points (12-25 FG, 8-16 3Pt, 10-13 FT), three rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal across 43 minutes during Saturday's 141-135 overtime win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Murray was held to just six points on 2-for-11 shooting in the Nuggets' season-opening loss to the Thunder, but he was nothing short of spectacular Saturday evening, helping his team erase a 23-point deficit. Murray also finished without committing a single turnover in his 43 minutes of floor time, putting a bow on an absolute masterpiece.

items.headline: Murray accumulated six points (2-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and one steal in 37 minutes during Thursday's 96-84 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Murray was ice cold from the field, with him and Nikola Jokic combining to shoot just 7-for-30 from the floor. While he did manage to grab double-digit boards, managers have to feel somewhat disappointed given the fact that a high draft pick was likely spent to get him. With that said, expect to see Murray get back on track when the Nuggets host the Pelicans on Saturday in what is a much more favorable matchup.

items.headline: Murray notched 21 points (8-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, six assists and a steal across 31 minutes in Friday's 121-106 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Murray paced Denver in scoring despite missing his three attempts from long range. The veteran guard compensated by attacking inside the perimeter and converting all five free throws, while his six assists were the second-best mark on the team behind Nikola Jokic's eight. Murray's ability to contribute as both a scorer and playmaker should keep him firmly established as an excellent fantasy option heading into the regular season, and he'll operate as the Nuggets' No. 2 scoring threat behind Jokic.

items.headline: Murray tallied 14 points (6-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt), four rebounds and an assist in 17 minutes during Wednesday's 122-110 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Murray delivered his most efficient preseason outing, hitting six of eight shots in just over a quarter. The veteran guard has played limited minutes this exhibition season and will take on his customary load once the regular season tips off.

items.headline: Murray (personal) is in the starting lineup for Tuesday's preseason contest against the Jazz.
items.story: Murray didn't play in Sunday's preseason opener against Utah, but he gets the nod and is in the starting lineup for this rematch Tuesday. It remains to be seen whether the star guard will have a limited workload in this preseason contest, though that wouldn't be surprising. He's the No. 2 option on offense behind Nikola Jokic and isn't expected to play heavy minutes in the preseason with the start of the 2026-27 regular season just around the corner.

items.headline: Murray is out for Sunday's preseason opener against the Jazz due to personal reasons, Katy Winge of Altitude Sports reports.
items.story: Murray is dealing with a personal matter, but at this point, there's no indication it will affect his status for the regular-season opener. His next chance to play in the preseason will come Tuesday in Utah. Tyus Jones should see an expanded role with Murray unavailable.

items.headline: Murray did not participate in Canada's latest FIBA World Cup qualifying window as he turns his attention toward the upcoming NBA season.
items.story: Murray is coming off a standout 2025-26 campaign with Denver in which he earned his first All-Star and All-NBA selections of his career. The veteran guard remains firmly entrenched as the Nuggets' No. 2 offensive option alongside Nikola Jokic and should continue carrying a substantial scoring and playmaking workload in 2026-27.

items.headline: The Nuggets signed DeMar DeRozan on Friday, giving Murray another competitor for usage in 2026-27.
items.story: There could be a tighter squeeze for usage in Denver this season, as DeRozan is effectively replacing the more defensive-minded Peyton Watson on the roster. Murray should remain the team's clear-cut No. 2 scoring option behind Nikola Jokic, but it remains to be seen if the addition of DeRozan, who should compete for a starting job during training camp, will adversely impact Murray's productivity.

items.headline: Murray posted 12 points (4-17 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, four assists and one block across 40 minutes during Thursday's 110-98 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Murray will be disappointed with his performance in the playoffs, as Minnesota limited him to a 35.7 percent mark from the field and 26.2 percent from beyond the arc. He found plenty of success in the regular season, however. Across 75 appearances, he averaged 25.4 points, 7.1 assists, 4.4 rebounds, 0.9 steals and 3.3 three-pointers.

items.headline: Murray ended Monday's 125-113 win over Minnesota in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with 24 points (9-23 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, seven assists and four steals in 39 minutes.
items.story: Although Murray converted only 39.1 percent of his shots, his secondary numbers helped him record a solid fantasy total. Murray's four steals matched a season high, and he recorded seven assists for the third time in the first-round series. A more accurate shooting evening will be needed from Murray to increase the team's chances of advancing.

items.headline: Murray contributed 30 points (10-25 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, five assists and one block across 42 minutes during Saturday's 112-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Murray scored 11 of his team-high 30 points in the fourth quarter, but his efforts were not enough for the Nuggets to mount a comeback. Murray has scored exactly 30 points in three of four games of the series while also recording at least five rebounds and five assists. The series will return to Denver on Monday, when Murray and the Nuggets will look to embark on coming back from a 3-1 series deficit against a Timberwolves team that will be without Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) and Anthony Edwards (knee) moving forward.

items.headline: Murray recorded 30 points (11-25 FG, 6-14 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 43 minutes during Monday's 119-114 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The 30 points led the Nuggets on the night, the second straight game in which Murray has paced his squad with that exact number. The 29-year-old guard missed the final two games of the regular season while nursing a minor shoulder issue, but he's been plenty productive when he's been on the court over the last month. Murray has scored 30-plus points in six of his last 12 contests, averaging 28.0 points, 7.1 assists, 4.6 boards, 4.3 threes and 1.1 combined steals and blocks during that span.

items.headline: Murray recorded 30 points (7-22 FG, 0-8 3Pt, 16-16 FT), five rebounds and seven assists across 39 minutes during Saturday's 116-105 victory over the Timberwolves in Game 1 of the first round of the playoffs.
items.story: While Murray struggled to get his shot to drop and missed all eight of his three-point attempts, he did an excellent job of creating contact and getting to the charity stripe for easy buckets. He was perfect at the line, committed only two turnovers in his 39 minutes of floor time and ended his evening with a team-best plus-13 differential in the 11-point win.

items.headline: Murray (shoulder) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's Game 1 against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Murray missed Denver's final two regular-season games due to a right shoulder impingement, though he's set to return for the start of the playoffs. The star point guard reached the 20-point threshold in nine of his last 10 regular-season games, averaging 27.6 points, 7.1 assists and 4.3 rebounds across 37.9 minutes per contest during that span.

items.headline: Murray has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Spurs due to a right shoulder impingement.
items.story: Murray will join at least three more of Denver's regular starters on the inactive list for Sunday's regular-season finale, while Nikola Jokic (wrist) is listed as questionable. Murray earned his first All-Star nod in the 2025-26 campaign and will finish the regular season with averages of 25.4 points, 7.1 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 35.4 minutes per game across 75 appearances. Tyus Jones and Jalen Pickett will likely see increased playing time in Murray's stead.

items.headline: Murray (shoulder) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder, per Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com.
items.story: According to head coach David Adelman, the Nuggets have opted to hold out their regular starters for Friday's penultimate regular-season contest. Murray was initially listed as questionable due to a shoulder issue, but he will officially take a seat alongside the rest of the starting five as Denver prioritizes rest ahead of the playoffs. With Murray and the starters sidelined, Bruce Brown, Tyus Jones, and Jalen Pickett are all expected to take on massive workloads against Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Murray (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Along with Nikola Jokic (wrist) and Aaron Gordon (hamstring), Murray is in jeopardy of missing Denver's penultimate regular-season game. If the star point guard is ruled out, Bruce Brown, Jalen Pickett and Tyus Jones would be candidates for increased run.

items.headline: Murray chipped in 26 points (8-17 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 5-5 FT), seven rebounds and five assists over 35 minutes during Wednesday's 136-119 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Murray was coming off back-to-back games in which he didn't surpass 20 points, but he bounced back admirably here and was one of Denver's best players in an easy win. Murray might be the No. 2 option on offense behind Nikola Jokic, who had a triple-double Wednesday, but the guard's impact can't be overlooked. Murray has scored at least 20 points in all but one of his last 10 games, a stretch in which he's averaging 27.6 points, 4.3 rebounds and 7.1 assists per contest.

items.headline: Murray posted 20 points (7-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, seven assists and two blocks over 38 minutes during Monday's 137-132 overtime victory over Portland.
items.story: Murray adeptly directed the offense and pitched in with 20 points while Nikola Jokic and Aaron Gordon got the job done inside. The Nuggets trailed the Trail Blazers heading into the final stanza, but the Nuggets stuck to their game plan and chipped away at Portland's lead. Murray's continued health and regular attendance are essential to the team's rhythm on offense, and he's on pace to hit career-high averages in points (25.4), rebounds (4.4), assists (7.2) and field goal percentage (48.3 percent).

items.headline: Suggs has been diagnosed with a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Suggs suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Knicks when his right knee buckled following a layup attempt. Fortunately, further testing revealed no major structural damage, though the 25-year-old will miss at least two weeks before being re-evaluated. Anthony Black and Jase Richardson could see increased opportunities in Orlando's backcourt during Suggs' absence.

items.headline: Suggs (knee) did not return to Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Suggs exited the game late in the fourth quarter due to a non-contact right knee injury and was unable to return. He concluded the contest with four points (2-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt), six rebounds, six assists and three steals in 33 minutes. Initial reports postgame suggest that Suggs will undergo an MRI in the coming days to determine the extent of the injury.

items.headline: Suggs went down with an apparent right knee injury during Sunday's game against the Knicks and needed to be helped to the locker room, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Suggs couldn't put much pressure at all on his right leg as he was helped back to the locker room, so for now, he should be considered doubtful to return. Anthony Black will likely be elevated to a starting role if Suggs needs to miss time, and there will be more minutes available for Jase Richardson.

items.headline: Suggs racked up six points (2-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals over 32 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Suggs struggled to find any rhythm Wednesday, managing just six points despite playing 32 minutes. He did rack up a pair of steals, providing fantasy managers with some respite. Perhaps the biggest positive to come out of the game was the fact that he played in excess of 30 minutes. Missed games have been a major issue for Suggs throughout his career, up to and including last season. Those who drafted him this season will be hoping he can finally stay on the floor.

items.headline: Suggs supplied nine points (3-4 FG, 3-4 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 13 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason win over Cleveland.
items.story: All three of Suggs' baskets came from beyond the arc, and he pulled down five rebounds despite playing fewer than 13 minutes. He was battling an illness prior, missing over a week of training camp. The efficient perimeter shooting and defensive activity offered a productive snapshot of his two-way contributions before Orlando turns its attention to the regular season.

items.headline: Suggs (illness) is available for Tuesday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Dan Savage of the Magic's official site reports.
items.story: Suggs missed the Magic's first two preseason games while under the weather, though he'll return to action Tuesday. With the 25-year-old floor general back in action, Jase Richardson will likely shift to the second unit.

items.headline: Magic coach Sean Sweeney said Suggs is no longer under the weather, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Sweeney added that Suggs is doing well, but there was no mention of his status for Tuesday's preseason game against the Cavaliers. Suggs' status for Opening Night is not a concern, however.

items.headline: Suggs (illness) is out for Sunday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Suggs has been dealing with an illness lately, and although he has made progress in his recovery, he is not yet ready to play. His next chance to suit up comes Tuesday against the Cavaliers.

items.headline: Magic head coach Sean Sweeney said Suggs (illness) increased his activity level at Saturday's practice and looked more like himself but stated that the team can't "skip steps" in the point guard's recovery, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Suggs has been sick for nearly a week, and while it may not affect his regular-season availability, it has limited his training camp reps. The veteran point guard was sidelined for Orlando's preseason opener last Wednesday, and his status for Sunday's exhibition in Cleveland remains unclear.

items.headline: Suggs (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's preseason game against the Grizzlies, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Suggs has been under the weather for a few days and will miss Orlando's preseason opener, along with Anthony Black (ankle), which sends second-year guard Jase Richardson into the starting lineup. Suggs will have three more chances to suit up during the preseason, with his first opportunity coming Sunday in Cleveland.

items.headline: Suggs remains under the weather but was able to get on the court and run around during Tuesday's practice, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Suggs appears to be progressing after being limited by the illness over the previous few days. His activity level is encouraging, though his status for Wednesday's preseason opener against Memphis remains uncertain.

items.headline: Suggs remains under the weather but appears to be improving, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Coach Sean Sweeney said Sunday that Suggs can do "a little bit, but not much" at the moment, though the expectation is that he'll ramp up his activity soon. With Orlando's preseason opener against Memphis set for Wednesday, Suggs' participation over the next couple of practices should provide a better indication of his availability.

items.headline: Philip Rossman-Reich of Orlando Magic Daily believes Suggs is best utilized as a spot-up shooter and in catch-and-shoot situations.
items.story: Suggs is coming off a disappointing playoff run, having averaged 11.1 points per game on 29.9 percent shooting from the field and 24.1 percent from three-point range last postseason. Rossman-Reich also thinks a healthy Magic team is paramount to maximizing Suggs' strengths in an off-ball role after the guard was forced to operate more on the ball last year due to injuries to Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner. Suggs should see enough playmaking opportunities to be worthy of a late-round pick in fantasy leagues, but the emergence of Anthony Black, who's coming off a breakout 2025-26 campaign, could remain a worrisome presence at point guard for Suggs' managers.

items.headline: Suggs closed Sunday's 116-94 loss to Detroit in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with six points (2-9 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists, two blocks and four steals over 36 minutes.
items.story: Suggs got to work on the defensive end, tallying six combined steals-plus-blocks. However, it was a different story on the offensive end, where he scored just six points, finishing in single digits for the third time in the past four games. Sunday's Game 7 loss brings to an end what was a disappointing season for the Magic, due in large part to the fact that injuries were a constant issue. Suggs continues to be one of the best defensive guards in the league, although he certainly wasn't immune to injuries, missing a total of 25 regular-season games.

items.headline: Suggs finished with 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds, five assists and three steals in 37 minutes during Wednesday's 116-109 loss to the Pistons in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Suggs logged 37 minutes, the most he has played thus far during the playoffs. After another season littered with injuries, Suggs has managed to stay relatively healthy over the past month, appearing in 15 games. As for the playoffs, Suggs has scored double digits in four of his five appearances, averaging 13.0 points, 3.2 assists, 1.8 steals and 2.4 three-pointers.

items.headline: Suggs chipped in 19 points (7-18 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds and four assists in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 98-83 loss to the Pistons in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Suggs led his team in scoring on a night when the Magic struggled mightily, shooting just 33 percent from the field in a blowout loss. After recording four stocks in a Game 1 win Sunday, the point guard finished without a steal or block Wednesday, marking just the eighth time that has occurred this year between the regular season and postseason. Suggs playing at the top of his game will be crucial if Orlando wants to pull off the series upset.

items.headline: Suggs logged 16 points (6-16 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three steals across 36 minutes before fouling out of Sunday's 112-101 win over Detroit in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Suggs played a pivotal role for the Magic, despite eventually fouling out. The biggest impact was, as per usual, on the defensive end, where he tallied four combined steals and blocks, not to mention a number of deflections. The upset win now sees Orlando take a 1-0 series lead over its more fancied opponents, with Game 2 scheduled for Wednesday in Detroit.

items.headline: Suggs recorded 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, six assists and one block in 22 minutes before fouling out of Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Suggs logged modest playing time as Orlando easily accounted for Charlotte, advancing to the first round of the playoffs to face the Pistons. Although Suggs' production was somewhat muted, his impact on the defensive end of the floor was undeniable. He continues to provide Orlando with energy on both ends and will need to be at his best for the Magic to have a chance of pulling off a first-round upset.

items.headline: Suggs accumulated 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-5 3Pt), four assists and two steals over 25 minutes during Wednesday's 132-120 victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Suggs didn't have a lot of touches on offense, but he was extremely sharp with his shot and drained three of his five three-pointers. It was his fourth straight game, and seventh of the last eight, in which he drained two or more treys. Suggs will need to be on point with his three-point shot in the playoffs, as the return of Franz Wagner means his role on offense will be even more secondary, as he'll sit behind Paolo Banchero, Desmond Bane  and the German forward in terms of offensive touches and usage rate.

items.headline: Suggs racked up 12 points (4-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, 12 assists, one block and three steals over 34 minutes during Monday's 123-107 victory over the Pistons.
items.story: Suggs recorded his third double-double of the season, including a season-high 12 assists. When healthy, Suggs has been a revelation this season, putting up top-50 value through 54 appearances, averaging 13.7 points, 5.6 assists, 1.9 steals ad 2.0 three-pointers. At this point in his career, ongoing injury concerns are the only thing holding him back from being a regular top-60 target.

items.headline: Suggs supplied 20 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 6-6 FT), eight rebounds, seven assists and four steals across 38 minutes in Tuesday's 115-111 win over the Suns.
items.story: Suggs turned in a well-rounded performance Tuesday and was Orlando's second-leading scorer, reaching the 20-point mark for the first time since March 12. He also finished third on the team in rebounds and second in assists. Additionally, the 24-year-old point guard made an impact on the defensive end, finishing one swipe shy of tying his season high. Suggs has been inconsistent on the offensive end of late, scoring in double figures in four of his last seven games while reaching the 15-point threshold just once.

items.headline: Suggs amassed eight points (3-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt), four rebounds, four assists and one block in 34 minutes during Thursday's 121-117 win over the Kings.
items.story: Suggs returned to the hardwood after a two-game absence, and while he had a decent stat line, he failed to provide much value as a scoring weapon. This was his sixth consecutive game in which he couldn't reach the 15-point mark, and at this point, it's fair to consider Suggs only a secondary option on offense, well behind the one-two combo of Paolo Banchero and Desmond Bane in terms of usage rate and shooting volume.

items.headline: Suggs (illness) is available for Thursday's game against the Kings, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: After missing two contests with an illness, Suggs is ready to return Thursday. Fewer minutes will be needed from Jamal Cain and Jevon Carter versus Sacramento. Over his last eight appearances, Suggs has averaged 14.9 points, 4.8 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 30.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Suggs (illness) participated in the Magic's morning shootaround but remains questionable for Thursday's game against the Kings, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Head coach Jamahl Mosley said after shootaround that Suggs is "definitely" feeling better, so the guard is trending in the right direction as Thursday's 7 p.m. ET tipoff approaches. Suggs has missed the Magic's last two games while recovering from the illness.

items.headline: Suggs is questionable for Thursday's game against the Kings due to an illness.
items.story: Suggs is at risk of missing a third straight contest with the ailment. If the guard isn't feeling well enough to play Thursday, more playing time at point guard would be open for Jevon Carter and Jamal Cain.

items.headline: Suggs (illness) won't play Tuesday against the Cavaliers, Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com reports.
items.story: Suggs sat out of Monday's matchup after waking up under the weather, and the team has now moved forward with downgrading him to out for the second half of Orlando's back-to-back. Jevon Carter drew the start at point guard Monday and should be in position to do so again in Cleveland.

items.headline: Suggs (illness) is out for Monday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Presumably, Suggs woke up under the weather as he wasn't on the original injury report. Monday's game is the front end of a back-to-back set, so it remains to be seen if he will be cleared in time for Tuesday. As for Monday, the Magic may need to rely heavily on Jevon Carter.

items.headline: Suggs ended with 14 points (5-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, six assists and one steal across 34 minutes during Saturday's 105-104 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Suggs looks to be just about all the way back from a back issue that cost him some time in late February. The fifth-year guard has averaged 14.1 points, 5.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 31.0 minutes per contest in his last seven games, tallying at least one steal in each game.

items.headline: Suggs logged 14 points (5-12 FG, 4-9 3Pt), seven rebounds, six assists, one steal and one block over 33 minutes during the Magic's 113-108 loss to the Thunder on Tuesday.
items.story: Suggs finished Tuesday's game as the Magic's leader in assists and third in scoring behind Paolo Banchero (32 points) and Desmond Bane (16 points). It was the eighth time this season that Suggs connected on at least four three-pointers, and that is an encouraging sign seeing as he was connecting on just 22.2 percent of his three-point attempts (on 6.8 3PA/G) over his four prior outings. The fifth-year guard has averaged 15.1 points, 5.5 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 2.4 threes and 1.6 steals over 29.9 minutes per game since March 1.

items.headline: Suggs provided 28 points (10-17 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, eight assists and two steals over 34 minutes during Thursday's 136-131 overtime victory over Washington.
items.story: Suggs ended just two assists away from recording a double-double in this win, and he delivered at least two tallies in five of the major categories to deliver a loaded line. The floor general has scored in double digits in his seven outings since returning to the starting lineup March 1, averaging 16.4 points, 3.0 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 1.9 steals per game in that span.

items.headline: Robinson accumulated 24 points (8-11 FG, 6-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and three steals over 32 minutes during Monday's 124-91 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Robinson continues to defy logic, putting together arguably the best stretch of his career. Through seven games, he has been a top-30 player in standard leagues, averaging 17.9 points, 2.0 steals and 4.0 three-pointers, shooting 44.6 percent from the field and 88.5 percent from the line. He has connected on at least five triples on four separate occasions, while tallying at least three steals in three straight games. He is a clear must-roster player but should also be viewed as a potential sell-high candidate.

items.headline: Robinson finished with 17 points (5-11 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, two assists and three steals across 26 minutes in Friday's 110-94 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Robinson had an off night shooting the ball from deep but still finished third on the team in scoring behind Cade Cunningham and Ron Holland. The 32-year-old is averaging a career-best 16.8 points and 1.8 steals along with 2.0 rebounds and 2.2 assists over 29.7 minutes per outing in six regular-season appearances. With Jalen Duren (hamstring) sidelined for at least a couple of weeks and Tobias Harris (calf) now in San Antonio, there is room for Robinson to have his most productive year since entering the league in 2018.

items.headline: Robinson finished with 12 points (4-14 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists, a steal and a block across 33 minutes in Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Robinson cooled off considerably after connecting on five three-pointers in each of his previous three appearances, but some kind of regression was widely expected. Despite the shooting woes, the volume shows Robinson has settled into a steady role in the Pistons' offensive scheme, though his limited contributions outside scoring can expose his fantasy volatility, as they did Tuesday. One bad game can happen to anyone, and Robinson should keep thriving as a floor-spacing threat for the Pistons even if his shooting numbers fluctuate.

items.headline: Robinson delivered 21 points (6-12 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 32 minutes in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Robinson has drained exactly five three-pointers in each of his first three outings this season and has cleared the 20-point threshold twice, so he's undoubtedly making the most of his opportunities as a spot-up shooter while playing alongside Cade Cunningham, one of the league's best playmakers. Even though his fantasy production is strongly tied to his perimeter shooting, he's surpassed expectations so far. He averaged just 12.2 points and 2.9 three-pointers made per game in the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Robinson posted 17 points (5-12 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), a rebound, two assists and two steals across 28 minutes in Friday's 128-111 win over the Heat.
items.story: Robinson opened the season with five threes and a 21-point performance against the Celtics on Tuesday, and he delivered another strong showing here while also connecting on five long-range shots. His perimeter shooting remains his primary source of fantasy value, although the two steals provided a welcome boost. Robinson's substantial playing time is encouraging, but his limited contributions elsewhere could make his production heavily dependent on shooting efficiency. So far, so good, though -- he's made 10 of his 19 three-pointers in his first two games of the season.

items.headline: Robinson accumulated 21 points (5-10 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 6-8 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 victory over Boston.
items.story: Robinson started at shooting guard and helped power Detroit's comeback from a 22-point deficit, connecting on a crucial fourth-quarter three-pointer during the Pistons' decisive run. His five triples were tied for the team lead, and his 21 points ranked third behind Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren. Robinson's starting role and high-volume perimeter shooting give him a clear path to fantasy value in three-pointers.

items.headline: Robinson tallied 15 points (5-8 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds and one assist across 24 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason win over Minnesota.
items.story: Robinson caught fire from beyond the arc, drilling four of his five three-point attempts while adding a handful of rebounds in a starting role. His perimeter shooting helped Detroit stretch the floor, and the veteran sharpshooter should remain an important source of three-point production as the Pistons prepare for the regular season.

items.headline: Robinson recorded nine points (3-4 FG, 3-3 3Pt) and one assist in 13 minutes during Monday's 109-107 preseason win over Phoenix.
items.story: Robinson started at shooting guard and knocked down all three of his attempts from beyond the arc before sitting out the second half. The veteran sharpshooter appears positioned to start and should provide valuable spacing around Cade Cunningham.

items.headline: Robinson (back) is available for Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers on Sunday.
items.story: Robinson has been dealing with a back injury of late, but he will be able to suit up Sunday. Robinson shifted to a reserve role for Game 6 after missing Game 5 due to injury, and he will come off the bench again for Game 7.

items.headline: Robinson is listed as questionable for Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers on Sunday due to lower-back soreness.
items.story: Robinson's back injury prevented him from playing in Game 5 on Wednesday, but he was cleared to play in a reserve role for Game 6 on Friday, when he played 20 minutes and finished with 14 points, two rebounds and two assists in a 115-94 win. Through 12 playoff games, Robinson has averaged 11.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 3.2 threes and 1.3 steals over 30.2 minutes per contest. His potential absence would mean more minutes would be available for Marcus Sasser and Javonte Green.

items.headline: Robinson won't start Friday's Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers, Serena Winters of FanDuel Sports Network Ohio reports.
items.story: The sharpshooter will return to action following a one-game absence due to lower-back soreness, though Daniss Jenkins will remain in the starting five. Robinson has averaged 13.8 points, 3.8 three-pointers, 2.5 assists, 2.5 steals and 1.8 rebounds across 32.5 minutes per contest through four second-round appearances.

items.headline: Robinson (back) is available for Friday's Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Robinson sat out Wednesday's Game 5 loss but will shed his questionable tag due to lower-back soreness and suit up in Friday's win-or-go-home matchup. Over four second-round appearances, the sharpshooter has averaged 13.8 points, 3.8 triples, 2.5 assists, 2.5 steals and 1.8 rebounds in 32.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Robinson (back) was present at Friday's morning shootaround, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Robinson was unable to go in Game 5 due to lower-back soreness, but he remains day-to-day with a questionable tag ahead of Game 6. Ausar Thompson could see another massive workload if Robinson is unable to give it a go.

items.headline: Robinson (back) is questionable for Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against Cleveland on Friday, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
items.story: Robinson was unable to go in Game 5 due to lower-back soreness, and he's back on the injury report of Friday's matchup. The Pistons will presumably monitor the sharpshooter closely in shootaround and warmups before issuing another update on his availability for Game 6.

items.headline: Robinson (back) won't play in Wednesday's Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against Cleveland.
items.story: Robinson has played well throughout most of this series, averaging 13.8 points, 1.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 0.3 blocks and 2.5 steals while shooting 57.7 percent from deep across 32.5 minutes. However, the 32-year-old won't suit up for Game 5 because of lower-back soreness. Without Robinson in the equation, Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter (adductor) and Caris LeVert (heel) should see more work.

items.headline: Robinson (back) is questionable for Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals on Wednesday versus Cleveland.
items.story: Robinson is bothered by lower-back soreness, and he could test out the issue during pregame warmups Wednesday before the Pistons update his status. Ausar Thompson and Daniss Jenkins would be needed to help pick up the slack if Robinson is ultimately downgraded to out for Game 5.

items.headline: Robinson notched 15 points (5-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, four assists, one block and five steals in 36 minutes during Saturday's 116-109 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Robinson was effective as usual on offense, leading the Pistons with four makes from beyond the arc while finishing as the team's third-leading scorer behind Cade Cunningham (27 points) and Tobias Harris (21 points). However, Robinson was also effective on the defensive side of the floor with five steals, the most in a game in his NBA career. The veteran sharpshooter is averaging 12.3 points, 2.7 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 3.3 threes and 1.6 steals over 31.2 minutes per game in the postseason.

items.headline: Robinson logged 19 points (7-12 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two assists and two steals over 28 minutes during Tuesday's 111-101 win over the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: The 19 points and five threes were both postseason highs for Robinson, who's drilled at least one triple in eight straight contests. The veteran sharpshooter has averaged 11.4 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.0 steals and 3.0 three-pointers per game in the 2026 playoffs, shooting 40.0 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Robinson recorded 14 points (5-11 FG, 4-9 3Pt), five rebounds and three assists over 36 minutes during Friday's 93-79 victory over the Magic in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Robinson scored in double figures for the fourth time in the past five games, including a series-high four three-pointers. Despite trailing by as much as 24 points in the first half, the Pistons rallied to force a Game 7, which will take place in Detroit on Sunday. Although his production has been somewhat underwhelming, Robinson continues to provide the team with a viable floor-spacer, allowing players like Cade Cunningham to go to work inside.

items.headline: Robinson amassed 10 points (3-9 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals over 32 minutes during Wednesday's 98-83 victory over the Magic in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Robinson didn't have the best shooting performance, but he was terrific on the other end of the floor. The Pistons have tightened up their rotation, with Javonte Green being the only reserve to eclipse 20 minutes Thursday.

items.headline: Robinson ended with nine points (3-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt) and four assists in 26 minutes during Sunday's 112-101 loss to Orlando in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Robinson dealt with foul issues throughout the night, limiting him to just nine points in 26 minutes. As a rhythm shooter, Robinson was simply unable to build any momentum, contributing to the Game 1 loss. Assuming he can stay out of foul trouble, expect to see Robinson more involved when Detroit looks to wrestle back the ascendency Wednesday.

items.headline: Robinson finished Friday's 118-100 win over the Hornets with 19 points (6-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 26 minutes.
items.story: Even though the Pistons' offense was regularly flowing through Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren, it's safe to say Robinson took advantage of his touches to deliver another solid shooting performance. He has scored at least 19 points in three of his past five outings. This was also his fifth consecutive game with three or more three-pointers made, and his ability to stretch the floor is key for the Pistons' offensive scheme, even if that limits his upside in fantasy.

items.headline: Robinson logged 20 points (8-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), one rebound, three assists and one steal in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 137-111 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Robinson (hip) returned after a one-game absence, as Detroit continues to manage its key players heading into the playoffs. In what was certainly a favorable matchup, Robinson went for at least 20 points for the first time in his past 27 games, a welcome sight for anyone still rostering him. As for his overall season value, Robinson continues to be one of the best three-point specialists typically available on waiver wires, averaging 2.9 three-pointers per game thus far.

items.headline: Robinson (hip) will play Wednesday against the Bucks.
items.story: Robinson is set to return from a one-game absence along with Tobias Harris. With this news, Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green could see their minutes take a hit.

items.headline: Robinson (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: As expected after he was downgraded to doubtful, Robinson will miss Monday's contest due to a right hip strain. With the veteran swingman sidelined, Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green are candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Robinson (hip) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game in Orlando.
items.story: After initially being listed as questionable, Robinson is now expected to sit out with a hip strain. Marcus Sasser and Kevin Huerter should see more playing time at shooting guard Monday.

items.headline: Robinson (hip) is listed as questionable for Monday's game in Orlando.
items.story: Robinson has played well of late, most recently finishing with 11 points, two rebounds and two assists while shooting 50.0 percent from deep across 23 minutes in Saturday's 116-93 win over Philadelphia. However, he's in danger of missing Monday's contest because of a strained right hip. If Robinson can't play against the Magic, Kevin Huerter, Caris LeVert and Ronald Holland would likely see more action, with one of those players expected to enter the starting lineup.

items.headline: Robinson posted 15 points (5-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 29 minutes during Thursday's 113-108 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Robinson has been on a tear lately, and this was his seventh straight game with multiple three-pointers made. The eight-year veteran has solidified his position as a starter in the Pistons' backcourt, and his floor-spacing and outside-shooting abilities are vital for the team's offensive scheme. During that impressive seven-game stretch, Robinson is making 47.2 percent of his threes on 7.6 attempts per contest.

items.headline: Robinson registered 19 points (6-9 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two assists, one rebound and one steal over 29 minutes during the Pistons' 127-116 win over the Raptors on Tuesday.
items.story: Robinson sat out  Monday's game against the Thunder due to a right hip strain, but the veteran sharpshooter was cleared to return for the second leg of the Pistons' back-to-back set Tuesday. He gave the Pistons the scoring spark they needed and finished as the team's third-leading scorer behind Jalen Duren (31 points) and Daniss Jenkins (21 points). It was the 11th time this season that Robinson connected on five-plus threes, with three of those games coming in his last eight outings since March 15.

items.headline: Robinson (hip) will play Tuesday against the Raptors.
items.story: Robinson was initially added to the injury report with a probable designation and has since been cleared to take the court Tuesday. He sat out Monday while dealing with a hip injury but is expected to be a full go versus Toronto.

items.headline: Robinson (hip) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Raptors.
