He also connected on three triples and committed just one turnover, providing valuable production across multiple fantasy categories. Bridges continues to handle a substantial workload in the Suns' starting lineup.

items.headline: Bridges chipped in 24 points (10-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal in 37 minutes during Friday's 127-120 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Bridges led Phoenix in scoring and posted a double-double while adding three blocks. The forward has quickly become a key part of the Suns' frontcourt in his first season in Phoenix, and his production was even more important after Dillon Brooks was ejected in the third quarter. He'll try to help Phoenix bounce back Monday at Golden State.

items.headline: Bridges registered 17 points (7-17 FG, 2-10 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Monday's 125-114 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Bridges appears to be settling in nicely with his new team in Phoenix. The forward has watched his production across the board increase in each of his first three games, and Bridges hasn't looked to be hampered at all by a preseason ankle injury.

items.headline: Bridges amassed eight points (3-11 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 124-83 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: It was a quiet team debut for Bridges, who more or less went down with the ship Wednesday. The 28-year-old forward is expected to play a big role as one of Phoenix's secondary scoring options behind Devin Booker, and better days are ahead for Bridges.

items.headline: Bridges (ankle) will play in Friday's preseason game against the Jazz, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges will return to the lineup in Friday's preseason finale after missing two games with an ankle injury. The 28-year-old forward is gearing up for his first regular season with the Suns after averaging 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game across 77 regular-season starts with Charlotte in 2025-26.

items.headline: Bridges (rest) won't play Wednesday against the Spurs, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Bridges and the other veterans on the roster will sit this one out. His final opportunity to get on the floor before the start of the regular season will come Friday versus the Jazz.

items.headline: Bridges isn't expected to play Wednesday against the Spurs after missing Phoenix's full morning shootaround, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges appears headed for a night off alongside several other Suns regulars. Phoenix has one exhibition game remaining Friday against Utah, giving the forward another chance to get minutes before the regular season.

items.headline: Bridges (ankle) won't play in Saturday's preseason game against the Spurs, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: While Bridges won't play Saturday, he was able to practice Friday, so he's trending in the right direction. His next chance to suit up will come Wednesday in a preseason rematch with the Spurs.

items.headline: Head coach Jordan Ott said Friday that Bridges' (ankle) X-rays came back negative, and he participated in Friday's practice, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges exited Wednesday's preseason loss to the Bulls with a right ankle injury and did not return, though this news bodes well for his status ahead of the regular season. Ott added that the team will "be smart" with Bridges moving forward, so it wouldn't be surprising if he missed time during the preseason. The 28-year-old forward can be considered questionable for Saturday's exhibition against San Antonio until the Suns provide an update.

items.headline: Bridges exited Wednesday's 124-117 preseason loss to the Bulls with a right ankle injury and did not return, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Bridges got tangled up fighting for a loose ball and tweaked his ankle, and while he initially tried to play through it, he retreated to the locker room a few possessions later. According to Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic, head coach Jordan Ott said after the game that he believes Bridges is "fine" and thinks there's a chance he could play in Saturday's exhibition against the Spurs.

items.headline: Bridges finished with eight points (3-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal in 14 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Bridges started at power forward and scored Phoenix's first seven points before sitting out the second half with the rest of the starters. His ability to contribute as a scorer, rebounder and secondary playmaker should give him a significant role in Phoenix's revamped rotation.

items.headline: The Hornets traded Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick to the Suns on Sunday in exchange for Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and a 2033 first-round pick, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Bridges should continue to start in Phoenix, but his usage will likely dip, as he'll be competing for touches with the likes of Devin Booker, Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks. Bridges supplied averages of 17.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.9 triples per game this past season with the Hornets, but his offensive role might shrink some with the Suns.

items.headline: Bridges could take on additional offensive responsibilities after Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball, according to Cholo Magsino of Yahoo Sports.
items.story: The veteran forward remains one of the Hornets' most experienced scorers and playmakers, which may increase his importance as the team integrates younger players into larger roles. The addition of Naz Reid could push Bridges to small forward at times, and his long-term future could still depend on whether Charlotte pursues additional roster changes this offseason. Plus, he may lose out on some easy lobs that Ball was known for generating.

items.headline: Bridges ended Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic with 15 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 28 minutes.
items.story: Bridges propelled the Hornets to a 127-126 overtime victory over the Heat in Tuesday's Play-In Game, when he logged 28 points, nine rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 43 minutes, though he was unable to replicate that production in Friday's elimination loss. Bridges was productive to open the 2025-26 season, but his numbers dipped significantly following the All-Star break. Over his final 24 regular-season outings from Feb. 24 to April 12, he averaged 14.6 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.5 threes and 0.8 steals over 28.3 minutes per game. Part of that dip had to do with Bridges taking a back seat to the likes of LaMelo Ball, Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller. Bridges is slated to earn $22.8 million in 2026-27, which is the final year he is under contract with Charlotte.

items.headline: Bridges finished with seven points (3-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and two assists over 24 minutes during Sunday's 110-96 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Bridges was mostly a non-factor in the win, limited to single digits for the first time in his past 10 games. Charlotte will host Miami in the first round of the Play-In Tournament, with the winner moving on to face the winner of Orlando and Philadelphia.

items.headline: Bridges posted 25 points (10-12 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds and seven assists across 34 minutes during Sunday's 122-108 victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Bridges and LaMelo Ball combined for 60 points in the win as the Hornets improved to 43-36 on the season. Bridges has been hot over his last eight games with 17.4 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 28.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Bridges totaled 19 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and four steals across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Bridges posted a strong all-around line after failing to tally either a block or steal in four consecutive games. He shot the basketball with efficiency on the offensive end and set a new season high in steals. Bridges is averaging 15.3 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals over his last four appearances.

items.headline: Bridges notched 14 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds and two assists over 29 minutes during Sunday's 114-99 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Bridges was Charlotte's leading scorer through the first half of action, but the Celtics held him to just four points over the second half. The 27-year-old forward has struggled to make much of an impact over the past four games, posting modest averages of 12.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists per contest.

items.headline: Bridges produced nine points (4-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds and four assists across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 134-90 win over the Kings.
items.story: This was a tame effort by Bridges' standards, with the Hornets utilizing a balanced attack Tuesday in the blowout win. Brandon Miller led all starters in minutes played (27), so Bridges' fantasy managers can write this off as an outlier.

items.headline: Bridges accumulated 11 points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT) and three rebounds in 23 minutes during Thursday's 130-111 win over Orlando.
items.story: This was a quiet outing by Bridges' standards, but the entire starting group saw reduced minutes in the blowout win. Bridges has been solid over his last seven outings, averaging 16.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 30.0 minutes per contest over that stretch.

items.headline: Bridges accumulated 26 points (11-15 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, five assists and one steal over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 117-109 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Bridges finally found some rhythm on the offensive end, scoring at least 20 points for the first time in his past 10 games. It was a welcome return to form for Bridges, who has struggled to put up top-200 value in those 10 games over the past month. While this was an encouraging performance, Charlotte now plays only twice in the next seven days, meaning fantasy managers may have to make some tough decisions when it comes to someone like Bridges.

items.headline: Bridges racked up 16 points (7-16 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes during Sunday's 111-99 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Although Bridges has recorded solid rebounding totals since his return to action, his recent scoring totals have all fallen below his seasonal average. His 16 points matched his best result since coming back from a four-game absence, and his work off the glass should remain steady while the Hornets struggle to find healthy options under the basket.

items.headline: Bridges amassed 12 points (5-13 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two steals over 28 minutes during Friday's 128-120 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Bridges has been mired in a shooting funk over the past three games, going just 11-for-36 from the floor and 3-for-15 from three-point range. Four of his five makes Friday evening were dunks, and he didn't convert anything outside of six feet from the rim. The Hornets will draw another difficult matchup against the Suns on Sunday, so it could be tough for Bridges to bust out of this slump in that one.

items.headline: Hauser totaled two points (1-6 FG, 0-5 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 19 minutes during Monday's 109-93 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Hauser failed to connect on any of his five three-point attempts as Boston struggled from long range, shooting just 28.6 percent as a team. The sharpshooter has a narrow fantasy profile built primarily around perimeter scoring, making outings like Monday's particularly damaging to his value.

items.headline: Hauser finished with 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 20 minutes during Monday's 134-99 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Hauser connected on three triples for the second time in three games to begin the season, providing efficient perimeter scoring off Boston's bench. However, he offered limited production outside of points and rebounds. His value remains concentrated in three-point shooting, making him more appealing in deeper fantasy formats.

items.headline: Hauser chipped in 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 18 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Hauser provided efficient perimeter scoring off Boston's bench, knocking down three of his five attempts from beyond the arc without committing a turnover. He finished with a plus-five rating despite the loss, though his 18-minute workload suggests his fantasy contributions will depend heavily on three-point shooting rather than consistent opportunities in other categories.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is expected to play in Tuesday's game against Detroit.
items.story: Hauser didn't play in Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over Philadelphia, though that was the case with most of the team's core performers. The 28-year-old averaged 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists, all career highs, in 78 regular-season games, including 49 starts, during the 2025-26 campaign. Hauser could be in line for an even better season, especially if Paul George, Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and Payton Pritchard miss time.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is not suiting up for Friday's preseason game against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Hauser and other prominent Celtics players, like Jayson Tatum, Paul George and Derrick White, will rest for Friday's preseason finale. The Celtics will open their regular season Tuesday against the Pistons, and Hauser is once again expected to operate in a rotational role off the bench, though he'll be competing against the likes of Jordan Walsh, Baylor Scheierman (rest), Hugo Gonzalez and Ron Harper for playing time.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is available for Saturday's preseason contest against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: Hauser didn't play in the preseason win over the Cavaliers on Thursday, but he'll be able to log minutes off the bench in this contest. Hauser has a strong grip on a rotation spot, and a good showing in the preseason could boost his chances to earn consistent playing time once the regular season starts. He's projected to open the campaign as the backup small forward behind Paul George.

items.headline: Hauser (rest) is out for Thursday's preseason game against the Cavaliers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: The Celtics are resting several players ahead of this preseason game, and that includes Hauser, who's expected to have a sizable role in the rotation this season. His next chance to play will come against the 76ers on Saturday.

items.headline: Hauser's role could become more secure following Boston's offseason shakeup with the team swapping Jaylen Brown for Paul George and other assets, John Schuhmann of NBA.com reports.
items.story: While George is expected to absorb most of Brown's minutes, George's recent durability concerns may create additional opportunities for Hauser on the wing throughout the season. Hauser should continue to provide elite three-point shooting, with his fantasy value receiving a boost whenever George requires maintenance days or misses time.

items.headline: Hauser closed Saturday's 109-100 loss to the 76ers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist over 30 minutes.
items.story: The Celtics inexplicably brought Neemias Queta and Hauser off the bench in favor of Ron Harper and Luka Garza, but the experiment did not last long with Harper and Garza combining for 13 total minutes. Hauser closed the 2025-26 regular season with 78 appearances and averages of 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 three-pointers in 24.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser won't start Saturday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: The Celtics will shake up their starting five in this do-or-die matchup, with Neemias Queta and Hauser both heading to the bench. The sharpshooter has scored six or fewer points in four of the last five games, shooting 34.6 percent from deep during that span.

items.headline: Hauser notched six points (2-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 22 minutes during Sunday's 128-96 win over the 76ers in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hauser continues to play a relatively modest role in this series. Through four games, he's shooting 38.5 percent from the field with averages of 7.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 23.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is not on the Celtics' injury report for Game 1 against the 76ers on Sunday.
items.story: Hauser managed a lingering back injury during the regular season and was sidelined for the Celtics' regular-season finale against the Magic on April 12, but the fifth-year sharpshooter will be available for Game 1 on Sunday. Hauser finished the 2025-26 regular season averaging 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 threes over 24.8 minutes per game, starting in 49 of 78 games.

items.headline: Hauser (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
items.story: As expected, Hauser will join several other Celtics players on the sidelines for Sunday's regular-season finale, but he should be available for the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs. He'll end the 2025-26 regular season averaging 9.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 threes over 24.8 minutes per game across 78 outings (49 starts). Hauser connected on 39.3 percent of his three-point attempts, which is the first time in his five-year NBA career that he did not shoot above the 40.0 percent mark. Boston will lean more heavily on Dalano Banton, Max Shulga, Jordan Walsh, Baylor Scheierman and Ron Harper against Orlando.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Magic, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: With the Celtics set to rest a lot of their regular rotation guys for Sunday's regular-season finale, there will be plenty of minutes and shots available for Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Jordan Walsh. Check back for official confirmation on Hauser's status closer to Sunday's tipoff.

items.headline: Hauser posted 24 points (8-13 FG, 8-12 3Pt), six rebounds and four assists in 28 minutes during Friday's 144-118 victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Hauser stepped up in the absence of Jayson Tatum (Achilles), scoring a team-high 24 points. The sharpshooter is scorching the nets from deep ahead of the postseason, shooting 52.6 percent from deep in his last six games while averaging 13.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 3.3 three-pointers per contest.

items.headline: Hauser (back) has been cleared to play in Friday's game against the Pelicans, per Jay King of The Athletic.
items.story: As expected, Hauser will push through his probable tag and suit up for the second leg of a back-to-back set despite lingering low-back spasms. With Jayson Tatum getting the night off to rest, Hauser could be in line for a slight uptick in usage and shot attempts.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is probable for Friday's game against the Pelicans, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: With Jayson Tatum resting and Jaylen Brown (Achilles) considered questionable, Hauser could see a bump in touches against the Pelicans, making him worth a stream for managers in need of three-pointers. He's appeared in 27 straight games, averaging 9.0 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 26.0 minutes during that stretch.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is available for Thursday's game against the Knicks, Zack Cox of the Boston Herald reports.
items.story: Hauser has appeared in 26 straight games (25 starts), and he could see increased usage Thursday due to Jaylen Brown (Achilles) being out. Derrick White (knee) and Neemias Queta (toe) are also questionable. Hauser is a candidate to rest Friday against the Pelicans, especially if he sees a major workload against New York.

items.headline: Hauser is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks due to low back spasms.
items.story: Hauser has been a key member of the Celtics' starting lineup because of his three-point shooting and floor spacing, so not having him would be a significant blow for Boston. Still, the questionable tag suggests a decision won't be made yet, and a final call on his status could be made closer to Wednesday's tipoff at 7:30 p.m. ET. If Hauser ends up being ruled out, Payton Pritchard and Baylor Scheierman could see increased burn.

items.headline: Hauser ended Wednesday's 147-129 victory over the Heat with 23 points (9-11 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, one block and one steal over 29 minutes.
items.story: Hauser moved back into the starting lineup Wednesday and responded with one of his best games of the campaign. This was his third game with at least 23 points and his 11th game with at least five triples. This has the look of an outlier for fantasy hoops, however, as he's averaging 9.1 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.5 three-pointers across 73 appearances this season.

items.headline: Hauser will start Wednesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: After shifting to a bench role for Monday's matchup against the Hawks, Hauser will rejoin the first unit Wednesday. The sharpshooter has been in a slump recently, averaging just 5.4 points while shooting 30.3 percent from deep in his past eight games. Hauser will look to get back on track and provide his usual floor spacing alongside Jayson Tatum against Miami.

items.headline: Hauser isn't starting Monday's game against Atlanta, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: The Celtics are electing to give Jordan Walsh an opportunity to start Monday, and Hauser will make the corresponding move to the bench. He's averaging 10.4 points and 3.8 rebounds in his last five appearances as a reserve, dating back to a stretch from Dec. 22 to Jan. 1.

items.headline: Hauser closed with nine points (3-9 FG, 3-8 3Pt) and five rebounds across 29 minutes during Wednesday's 119-109 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Hauser remains a streamer strictly for three-pointers in most fantasy leagues, though he's struggling to score at the moment. The sharpshooter has scored in single digits in five consecutive games, failing to knock down a single trey in three of them.

items.headline: Hauser logged two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Monday's 120-112 victory over Phoenix.
items.story: With Jayson Tatum healthy and gobbling up touches in this offense, Hauser's fantasy appeal is going to take a hit. Over his last seven appearances, he's averaging 8.1 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 2.4 three-pointers in 26.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser provided 15 points (5-10 FG, 5-10 3Pt) and four rebounds over 24 minutes during Sunday's 109-98 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Hauser caught fire from beyond the arc and appears to be a good fit alongside Jayson Tatum due to his floor spacing. Hauser won't have a big usage rate, but he will remain a solid three-point specialist in category formats.

items.headline: Hauser ended Monday's 108-81 victory over Milwaukee with 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-8 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 29 minutes.
items.story: Hauser continues to be a steady source of three-pointers in fantasy formats, but his upside is limited elsewhere. Over his last seven games, he's averaging 11.3 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.7 three-pointers in 27.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser closed with 16 points (6-14 FG, 4-10 3Pt), three rebounds and four assists in 29 minutes during Tuesday's 97-81 win over Phoenix.
items.story: Hauser took advantage of some extra touches due to Jaylen Brown being sidelined by a knee issue. Overall this season, Hauser is sitting just inside the top-200 players in standard nine-category formats with averages of 9.3 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.6 three-pointers in 24.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hauser ended Thursday's 121-110 win over Golden State with 16 points (6-10 FG, 4-5 3Pt), three rebounds and five assists over 28 minutes.
items.story: The fifth-year forward put together his best scoring effort since Jan. 23 with an efficient night from long distance. Hauser has drained multiple three-pointers in 17 of 19 appearances since moving into the starting five in early January, averaging 12.3 points, 4.1 boards, 3.3 threes, 1.8 assists and 1.1 combined steals and blocks in 28.3 minutes a game over that stretch.

items.headline: Hauser (back) will play Wednesday against the Bulls, according to Celtics reporter Bobby Manning.
items.story: Hauser will shake off his probable tag for this contest, setting him up to return from a one-game absence. With this news, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh could be less involved for the Celtics.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hauser is on track to return from a one-game absence. If he does get the green light, there will be fewer minutes available for guys like Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

items.headline: Hauser (back) will not play Sunday against the Knicks.
items.story: Hauser was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. With the sharpshooter out of the mix, the Celtics could allot more minutes to Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

items.headline: Hauser (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Hauser is in jeopardy of missing Sunday's contest due to lower-back spasms. If the sharpshooting forward is ultimately ruled out, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Hauser (thumb) is not listed on the injury report for Friday's matchup with the Heat, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: It looks like Hauser will be back in action Friday night following a one-game stint on the sidelines, which should result in fewer minutes for Hugo Gonzalez, Jordan Walsh and Ron Harper. Hauser is averaging 9.2 points and 2.6 triples per game this season.

items.headline: Hauser has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Rockets due to a right thumb strain, Jay King of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Hauser out and Jaylen Brown (hamstring/knee) doubtful, the Celtics are expected to be shorthanded in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Hugo Gonzalez and Jordan Walsh will likely see a significant bump in minutes, while Josh Minott may enter the rotation. Hauser's next opportunity to play will come Friday against Miami.

items.headline: Hauser totaled 12 points (5-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, one assist and one block over 25 minutes during Wednesday's 117-106 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Hauser continues to occupy a significant role for the Celtics, making him worth rostering in most fantasy leagues as long as he stays hot from long distance. Over his last eight contests, the sharpshooter has averaged 16.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 4.3 three-pointers in 29.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hauser contributed 19 points (7-12 FG, 5-10 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 39 minutes during Friday's 130-126 double-overtime win over the Nets.
items.story: The Hauser hot streak stays intact after another sharpshooting performance. He's now up to 46 made threes in the month of Jan. on 95 attempts. Hauser is hitting threes at a 48.4 percent clip this month, leading to a deserved uptick in playing time highlighted by Friday's season-high 39 minutes.

items.headline: Hauser closed Wednesday's 119-104 win over the Pacers with 17 points (6-8 FG, 5-7 3Pt), six rebounds and three assists across 28 minutes.
items.story: Hauser stayed scorching hot from downtown Wednesday, drilling five three-pointers on seven attempts. The 28-year-old forward's 19 made triples over the last three games are the most by a Celtic since Hauser hit 21 over a three-game span during the 2023-2024 season. Since entering the starting lineup Jan. 3, Hauser is averaging 14.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.0 threes, 1.8 assists and 0.7 steals over 27.9 minutes per outing.

items.headline: Hauser popped off for 30 points (10-21 FG, 10-21 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and two turnovers across 30 minutes during Saturday's 132-106 win over the Hawks.
items.story: With all 21 of Hauser's shot attempts coming from beyond the arc, he set a new record for most three-point attempts without any two-point attempts, and he also became the only player in Celtics franchise history to have multiple games with double-digit triples. Hauser has been playing well over the past four games, averaging 18.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 5.5 triples per contest.

items.headline: Flagg ended Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings with 17 points (3-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 11-11 FT), four rebounds, six assists and two steals in 40 minutes.
items.story: With Kyrie Irving resting Monday, the Kings were able to devote most of their defensive attention to Flagg and hold the second-year superstar in check from the field. Flagg is still off to an excellent start overall, averaging 25.2 points, 6.5 assists and 5.7 rebounds per game so far this season.

items.headline: Flagg finished Friday's 116-111 win over the Rockets with 33 points (13-19 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 7-10 FT), nine rebounds, six assists, two steals and one block across 39 minutes.
items.story: Although he struggled from three-point range once again, Flagg turned in another productive all-around performance in Dallas' first NBA Cup game of the year. The star forward erupted for a season-high 33 points and was second on the Mavericks in scoring behind Kyrie Irving (35 points). Flagg also finished second on the team in rebounds and assists. He's posted at least 26 points, six assists and five rebounds in three consecutive contests, though he's shot just 20.0 percent from downtown during that span.

items.headline: Flagg finished with 26 points (10-23 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and eight assists across 33 minutes in Wednesday's 120-96 victory over Oklahoma City.
items.story: Flagg's phenomenal 2026-27 campaign continued Wednesday, with the 2025 No. 1 overall pick scoring over 20 points for the third time this season. He hasn't been consistent shooting the ball, and turnovers have also been somewhat of a concern. However, despite the struggles in those areas, Flagg is still putting up All-Star numbers, and at this rate, his name could be mentioned in MVP conversations throughout the year.

items.headline: Flagg finished Monday's 113-109 win over the Heat with 29 points (12-23 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 11 assists, six rebounds, five steals and two blocks across 40 minutes.
items.story: Flagg returned from a one-game absence due to a left shoulder sprain and stuffed the stat sheet. The star forward tied for the game-high scoring total in an efficient performance from inside the arc and dished out a career-high-tying 11 assists. He also logged a career-best five steals and has supplied at least three swipes in all three of his regular-season appearances thus far.

items.headline: Flagg (shoulder) is active for Monday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Despite being diagnosed with a mild left shoulder sprain that forced him to miss Saturday's loss to the Spurs and being considered a true game-time call by coach Dusty May, Flagg will play versus Miami. It doesn't sound like he'll have any restrictions following the one-game absence, and his return will likely send Zaccharie Risacher back to the bench.

items.headline: Head coach Dusty May said Flagg is a game-time decision for Monday's matchup against the Heat, though May expects the second-year forward to play, Eddie Sefko of the Mavericks' official site reports.
items.story: Flagg suffered a left shoulder sprain in Friday's win over Indiana, though he's trending in the right direction after being held out of Saturday's loss to the Spurs. If the star forward is cleared to return to action, there would be fewer minutes available for guys like Sergio de Larrea, Jett Howard and Zaccharie Risacher.

items.headline: Flagg (shoulder) has been upgraded to probable for Monday against the Heat, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Flagg was carrying a questionable tag prior to this update with his mild shoulder sprain. He made it through the morning shootaround with no setbacks, however, and the Mavericks are now preparing for their star forward to suit up. For now, there's no word of potential restrictions.

items.headline: Flagg (shoulder) was spotted going through Monday's morning shootaround, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Given the circumstances of the injury, it's quite remarkable to see Flagg doing so well. He was diagnosed with a sprain Saturday, but the injury seems to be progressing, and it's being described as a mild issue. He remains listed as questionable on the injury report.

items.headline: Flagg (shoulder) is questionable to play Monday against the Heat.
items.story: The Mavericks diagnosed Flagg with a mild left shoulder sprain Saturday, and the questionable tag suggests a final call on his availability will be made closer to Monday's 7:30 p.m. ET tipoff. With Naji Marshall (illness) already ruled out, Marcus Sasser and Zaccharie Risacher would be the top candidates to start if Flagg is ruled out for Monday's road game.

items.headline: The Mavericks diagnosed Flagg with a mild left shoulder sprain, and the second-year forward will be re-evaluated by medical staff next week, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Flagg took a hard fall during the second quarter of the Mavericks' win against the Pacers on Friday. He was already ruled out for Saturday's game against the Spurs, but it looks like the 2025 first-overall pick will miss at least a couple more games while recovering from his injury. Naji Marshall, Marcus Sasser and Zaccharie Risacher figure to be the top candidates to enter Dallas' starting five for as long as Flagg is sidelined.

items.headline: Head coach Dusty May said Flagg (shoulder) will be evaluated in the next couple of days, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Flagg can presumably be ruled out for Saturday's game against San Antonio after leaving Friday's win over Indiana and not returning. The star forward was hit while in the air and took a hard fall, landing on his left shoulder. With Flagg sidelined, Naji Marshall, Zaccharie Risacher and Marcus Sasser are candidates for increased burn.

items.headline: Flagg won't return to Friday's game against the Pacers due to left shoulder soreness, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Flagg took a hard fall after being fouled on a dunk attempt late in the second quarter and headed to the locker room with 45 seconds remaining in the first half. He did not come out for the second half, with Naji Marshall starting in his place. Flagg was ruled out shortly thereafter, and he will finish with 14 points (4-6 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, six assists, three steals, one block and three turnovers across 17 minutes. For now, he should be considered questionable for Saturday's meeting with the Spurs.

items.headline: Flagg exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Friday's game against Indiana due to an apparent left shoulder injury, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Flagg was hit while he was in the air and landed on his shoulder. He headed to the locker room shortly before halftime and can be considered questionable to return in the second half until the Mavericks provide an update on his status.

items.headline: Flagg closed Wednesday's 128-110 loss to the Rockets with 32 points (10-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 11-13 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals across 33 minutes.
items.story: Flagg was as advertised, getting it done on both ends of the floor despite what ended up being a comprehensive loss. While there is cause for concern when it comes to what Dallas might be able to achieve this season, it's clear that Flagg is going to be leading from the front. His ADP settled in the 6-to-10 range across most fantasy formats, meaning a lot of fantasy managers could have their season riding on his production.

items.headline: The Mavericks exercised the third-year team option on Flagg's contract for the 2027-28 season, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Flagg is coming off an impressive rookie campaign with Dallas, averaging 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.9 blocks across 33.5 minutes per game in 70 regular-season appearances. The second-year forward should operate as one of Dallas' top offensive options alongside Kyrie Irving in 2026-27.

items.headline: Flagg notched 26 points (8-20 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 8-9 FT), 12 rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and two turnovers over 30 minutes in Friday's 135-111 preseason loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Flagg closed out the preseason strong, recording his first double-double to go with a full stat line. Last season's Rookie of the Year has looked great throughout the preseason, averaging 19.7 points, 7.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 1.3 triples, 1.7 steals, 1.0 blocks and 2.0 turnovers in just 24.7 minutes per game, so he appears primed to take a leap in Year 2.

items.headline: Flagg (rest) is available for Friday's preseason game against the Hawks.
items.story: Flagg didn't play in Wednesday's meeting with the Pelicans but will be on the floor to close out the preseason. The 19-year-old appeared in two preseason games, averaging 16.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.0 blocks over 22.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Flagg (rest) won't play Wednesday against the Pelicans, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Flagg is getting Wednesday night off for rest purposes. He'll look to return Friday against the Hawks in what could be a dress rehearsal for the Mavericks.

items.headline: Flagg recorded 14 points (3-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 7-8 FT), four rebounds, seven assists, two steals and a block across 25 minutes in Sunday's 132-115 preseason win over the Rockets in China.
items.story: Flagg struggled with his shot but delivered an impressive playmaking performance, leading Dallas with seven assists and committing just two turnovers. Despite his shooting woes, Flagg still found a way to contribute offensively, getting to the free-throw line eight times. Even with Kyrie Irving in the backcourt, Flagg should be a key playmaking and scoring weapon for the Mavericks ahead of his second year in the league following an impressive rookie season in which he averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 0.9 blocks and 1.2 steals across 33.5 minutes in 70 regular-season games.

items.headline: Flagg recorded 19 points (7-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in 19 minutes during Friday's preseason loss to Houston.
items.story: Flagg was productive in limited action, shooting 50 percent from the field while contributing across multiple categories. The second-year forward also converted all four of his free-throw attempts, offering an encouraging glimpse of his offensive development ahead of the 2026-27 regular season. Flagg figures to remain a central piece of Dallas' offense as the Mavericks work through their revamped rotation.

items.headline: Stewart recorded 24 points (8-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT) and four rebounds across 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 victory over Sacramento.
items.story: Stewart was one of three Grizzlies players who scored 20-plus points during Saturday's blowout win, and he finished second on the team in points behind rookie Cameron Boozer (27). Stewart has scored in double digits in three of his last four outings, and over that span he has averaged 14.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 0.8 blocks and 1.5 threes over 18.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Stewart ended with 18 points (7-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one block across 16 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 victory over Portland.
items.story: Stewart dropped a season-high 18 points, although a lack of peripheral stats continues to be an issue. Having appeared in four games thus far, he has averaged just 9.8 points, 3.5 rebounds and 0.8 blocks in 17.5 minutes per game. Assuming Zach Edey's playing time continues to ramp up, there isn't much hope for Stewart being anything more than a situational streaming consideration.

items.headline: Stewart won't start Monday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: The big man will play in the second leg of this back-to-back set, though Zach Edey (ankle) will return to action and push Stewart to the bench. Stewart is averaging 8.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks across 19.5 minutes per contest in two regular-season appearances (one start) on the campaign.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) is available for Monday's game at Utah.
items.story: Stewart will shed his questionable tag and suit up for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Through two regular-season games (one start), he's averaging 8.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks across 19.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Stewart is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Jazz due to left ankle injury management.
items.story: Stewart may be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set after posting 13 points, five rebounds, two assists, two blocks and a steal across 22 minutes while starting in the absence of Zach Edey (injury management) during Sunday's win over Sacramento. If Stewart is ultimately ruled out, Quinten Post would likely see increased playing time behind Edey.

items.headline: Stewart accumulated 13 points (4-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 22 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Stewart got the start for the resting Zach Edey on Sunday, chipping in a full stat line. Stewart is in line to revert to the bench Monday in Utah.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) is available for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Stewart is set to make his regular-season debut for the Grizzlies, and he should help back up Zach Edey and Cameron Boozer. With Stewart active, Quinten Post's minutes could dip.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Stewart wasn't able to go for Wednesday's opener against the Jazz due to an ankle injury suffered during the preseason, but he's been upgraded to questionable ahead of Friday's clash. The Grizzlies will likely monitor him closely in shootaround and warmups to determine whether he can suit up Friday night.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Stewart has been battling an ankle injury he sustained in the preseason and won't suit up in Memphis' regular-season opener. His next opportunity to make his regular-season debut with his new club will come Friday at Golden State. In the meantime, Taylor Hendricks and Quinten Post are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) is doubtful to play Wednesday against the Jazz.
items.story: Stewart is still recovering from an ankle injury he sustained during the preseason Oct. 5, and it looks like he'll miss Memphis' regular-season opener. With Stewart out of the lineup, Quinten Post should be more involved in the rotation.

items.headline: The Grizzlies announced Friday that Stewart (ankle) will miss at least two weeks.
items.story: Stewart, who was traded from Detroit to Memphis over the summer, sustained a left ankle sprain in the team's preseason opener and is now likely to miss Opening Night. His absence opens the door for Quinten Post to move into the backup center role behind Zach Edey in the interim.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) didn't practice Friday, per Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site.
items.story: Stewart appears to be doubtful for Friday's preseason game in Chicago. He's recovering from a left ankle injury suffered in Memphis' preseason opener.

items.headline: Stewart (ankle) didn't participate in Tuesday's practice and will not play in Wednesday's preseason game against the Magic, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
items.story: Stewart is still being evaluated after sustaining a left ankle injury in Monday's preseason-opening win over the Hawks. The big man's next opportunity to play in the preseason will come against the Bulls on Friday.

items.headline: Stewart exited Monday's 132-123 preseason win over the Hawks in the first quarter and did not return due to a left ankle injury, finishing with one rebound in two minutes.
items.story: Stewart landed on an opposing player's foot and took a hard fall before limping back to the locker room. He was eventually deemed doubtful to return and never checked back in. The big man's next opportunity to play in the preseason will come Wednesday versus Orlando.

items.headline: Stewart is doubtful to return to Monday's preseason game against the Hawks due to a left ankle injury.
items.story: Stewart landed on an opposing player's foot in the opening quarter and limped to the locker room. If he doesn't return, he'll finish with a rebound in only two minutes of action.

items.headline: Stewart (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Monday's preseason game against the Hawks, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Stewart appeared to come down on an opposing player's foot and took a hard fall before limping to the locker room. If he's unable to check back in, Olivier-Maxence Prosper and Taylor Hendricks could see increased playing time for the rest of the way.

items.headline: The Pistons traded Stewart to the Grizzlies on Wednesday in exchange for three second-round draft picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Stewart is coming off a strong 2025-26 campaign, especially on the defensive end, as he averaged 10.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.6 blocks and 1.1 assists across 22.7 minutes per contest in 58 regular-season games (13 starts). The big man will likely command a significant role in the Memphis frontcourt, though he isn't guaranteed a starting spot and could begin the season operating off the bench behind Zach Edey (ankle/elbow) and Cameron Boozer.

items.headline: Stewart recorded three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 FT) across six minutes during Sunday's 125-94 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Stewart played a very minor role in Detroit's postseason run, averaging just 11.8 minutes per contest. He found more success in the regular season, posting averages of 10.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.6 blocks in 22.7 minutes across 58 appearances.

items.headline: Stewart racked up six points (2-2 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 13 minutes during Tuesday's 111-101 win over the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: With Jalen Duren dominating the center minutes for the Pistons, Stewart continues to play a limited role this postseason. Stewart has averaged 4.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.6 blocks in 14.1 minutes per contest across eight games in the 2026 playoffs, shooting 55.0 percent from the field.

items.headline: Stewart accumulated no counting stats across eight minutes during Friday's 93-79 victory over Orlando in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart played himself out of the rotation, logging just eight minutes in the first half. Paul Reed took his place in the second half, contributing to the come-from-behind victory. Although Stewart blocked a career-high eight shots in Game 4, it's been a relatively quiet series thus far. Through six games, he has averaged 4.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.2 blocks in 15.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Stewart amassed eight points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and eight blocks across 17 minutes during Monday's 94-88 loss to the Magic in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart was a bright spot for the Pistons with a career-high eight swats in very limited action. With Detroit facing a 3-1 series deficit, Stewart made a strong case to be more involved going forward.

items.headline: Stewart closed with 10 points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds and two blocks over 16 minutes during Wednesday's 98-83 win over the Magic in Game 2 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart's 16 minutes were eventful, as the big man didn't miss a shot while recording two blocks, though he also committed three turnovers. Turnovers aside, the 24-year-old was far more productive in Game 2 than in Game 1, when he totaled three points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal across 19 minutes. The numbers may fluctuate, but Stewart's role as a physical presence off the bench remains a key part of the Pistons' identity.

items.headline: Stewart supplied three points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal in 19 minutes during Sunday's 112-101 loss to the Magic in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Stewart failed to have any sort of meaningful impact, continuing what has been an underwhelming few games. In fact, in four appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 8.0 points and 1.0 blocks in 15.7 minutes per game. Along with a number of his teammates, Stewart will need to be better should Detroit intend on going deep into the playoffs.

items.headline: Stewart chipped in eight points (3-3 FG, 2-2 FT) and one rebound over 11 minutes during Wednesday's 137-111 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Stewart logged 11 minutes in his return, back in action after missing 13 straight games due to a calf injury. Although he has proven to be a menace on the defensive end, Stewart's role remains limited, serving as the primary backup behind Jalen Duren. As for next season, he will likely be nothing more than a blocks specialist, providing managers with limited value off the waiver wire.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is available for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Stewart will shed his questionable tag and return from a 13-game absence due to a left calf strain. While he may operate under a minutes restriction in his first game back, the big man's return will leave fewer minutes available for Paul Reed.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: A left calf strain has held Stewart out for 13 consecutive contests, but the questionable designation gives him a real chance to return Wednesday. Stewart would likely face a minutes cap if he's upgraded to available, but he would still figure to push Paul Reed for playing time as the backup center behind Jalen Duren.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is out for Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Stewart was temporarily upgraded from out to doubtful earlier in the day Monday, but the team has now officially listed him as out, which will mark his 13th straight absence while on the mend from a left calf strain. The 24-year-old's next chance to take the court will come Wednesday against the Bucks.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game versus Orlando.
items.story: The Pistons are upgrading Stewart from out to doubtful Monday, signaling that he's inching closer to returning from a left calf strain. Paul Reed should remain worth streaming in deep fantasy leagues for at least one more contest.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is listed as out ahead of Monday's game in Orlando.
items.story: Stewart continues to battle a strained left calf, an injury that has caused him to miss Detroit's last 12 contests. Although the 24-year-old resumed on-court basketball activities over a week ago, he won't be back on the floor versus the Magic. With Stewart unavailable, Paul Reed should continue to see the bulk of the minutes from off the bench behind Jalen Duren.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) will remain on the inactive list for Saturday's game in Philadelphia.
items.story: Stewart will miss another game, and while he's slowly making progress, it remains unclear when he might return. Paul Reed will continue to operate as Jalen Duren's primary backup with Stewart sidelined.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Stewart has missed the last 10 contests. Although he has resumed on-court activities, his return date remains a mystery. With Stewart out again, Paul Reed should continue receiving the bulk of the minutes off the bench behind Jalen Duren.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) has been cleared to resume on-court basketball activities, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Stewart has been battling a strained left calf for nearly two weeks, and he's finally been cleared to begin on-court activities. A return for the 24-year-old doesn't seem imminent, but a return before the postseason seems possible.

items.headline: Stewart (calf) is out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: A left calf strain has sidelined Stewart since March 15, though the Pistons are expected to re-evaluate him at some point in the near future. Paul Reed should remain the top backup center Saturday unless Jalen Duren (knee) ends up needing to sit out altogether.

items.headline: The Pistons announced Tuesday that Stewart has been diagnosed with a Grade 1 left calf strain and will be re-evaluated in one week.
items.story: The update isn't especially surprising, given that Pistons head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Sunday that Stewart was without a clear timeline for a return. Bickerstaff also said Stewart has been playing through the injury recently, but it worsened, so the Pistons opted to shut him down. Until Stewart is cleared to play, Paul Reed should remain in the rotation as the backup to starting center Jalen Duren, while forwards Javonte Green and Ronald Holland could see slightly elevated roles.

items.headline: Head coach JB Bickerstaff said Sunday that Stewart (calf) is without a timetable to return, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: "It's something he's been dealing with. It just had been getting worse. He gutted it out [Friday versus Memphis] and I think you could see he was favoring it late," said Bickerstaff of Stewart's calf injury. "It's something we're going to take time with." Stewart missed Sunday's loss to the Raptors, and it doesn't sound like Bickerstaff plans on having him available for Week 21. Stewart is a cut candidate for managers currently battling through the fantasy playoffs.

items.headline: Stewart has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raptors due to a left calf strain.
items.story: The calf injury is a new concern for Stewart, and it's not a positive sign that he's being ruled out a day in advance of tipoff. With the 24-year-old big man unavailable, Paul Reed is expected to see increased burn behind Jalen Duren.

items.headline: Stewart produced 10 points (5-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist and one block across 20 minutes during Friday's 126-110 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Stewart continues to serve up adequate production, although given the current injury situation in Detroit, managers have likely been disappointed. Despite Ausar Thompson's absence due to an ankle injury, Stewart's playing time has remained steady. In seven games over the past two weeks, he has been nothing more than a top-160 player, averaging 10.4 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks in 22.5 minutes per contest over that stretch.

items.headline: Stewart chipped in 10 points (2-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 5-8 FT) and four rebounds across 20 minutes during Saturday's 107-105 loss to the Nets.
items.story: Stewart struggled to find any rhythm, failing to take advantage of what could have been a favorable situation. With Ausar Thompson (ankle) set to miss at least a handful of games, Stewart could find himself moving up in the rotation. While he didn't start Saturday, he could certainly be called upon to move into the opening five should the matchup call for some additional size. Despite this performance, he should at least be on the radar as a short-term addition.

items.headline: Stewart posted 18 points (4-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Thursday's 121-106 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Jalen Duren was limited to 12 minutes in this matchup, but Stewart made the most of his time. The 18-point output was his best scoring mark since Jan. 7, when he had a season-high 31 points in a win over the Bulls. He's now recorded tallies in each of the five major categories in his two outings since returning from a seven-game suspension and should continue to deliver quality minutes off the bench for Detroit. However, his fantasy impact won't be very high due to the nature of his second-unit role.

items.headline: Stewart ended Tuesday's 113-109 loss to the Cavaliers with four points (2-4 FG), two rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 22 minutes.
items.story: This was Stewart's first game back in action after serving his seven-game suspension. He reprised his role as the backup center, pushing Paul Reed completely out of the rotation. Across 49 regular-season appearances, Stewart holds averages of 9.9 points, 5.1 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.7 blocks.

items.headline: Stewart will be suspended for seven games for his involvement in an altercation with Charlotte's Miles Bridges and Moussa Diabate on Monday, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
items.story: The Pistons were anticipating a lengthy suspension and got one for their backup center after he left the bench to aggressively charge Bridges and Diabate. Jalen Duren will be suspended for a pair of games, making Paul Reed a decent pickup in fantasy hoops for the short term. Stewart will be eligible to return against the Cavaliers on March 3.

items.headline: Collins racked up four points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 19 minutes during Monday's 124-91 win over the Hornets.
items.story: Collins scored no more than four points for the fourth straight game, continuing his rough start to the season. Despite seemingly landing in a favorable position this season, Collins has been largely underwhelming. In seven games, he has barely been a top-200 player, averaging 8.4 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.0 blocks and 1.0 three-pointers. At this stage, parting ways with him in standard formats is certainly a viable option.

items.headline: Collins posted four points (2-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt) and two rebounds across 18 minutes during Wednesday's 97-89 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Collins endured a rough shooting performance, missing all three attempts from beyond the arc while failing to contribute any assists or defensive statistics. The veteran forward also committed four personal fouls, which contributed to his limited playing time. His lack of production is concerning for fantasy managers, particularly if his minutes remain inconsistent.

items.headline: Collins registered 16 points (7-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 11 rebounds and two blocks across 34 minutes in Sunday's 106-93 win over the 76ers.
items.story: Collins followed his 23-point performance against Miami with his first double-double of the season, taking advantage of Jalen Duren's absence (hamstring) to play an expanded frontcourt role. Collins should remain productive, although his rebounding opportunities and minutes could decrease once Duren returns. That said, Collins is entrenched as the starting power forward and has done a good job of filling the void left by Tobias Harris (calf), who departed in the offseason to join the Spurs.

items.headline: Collins delivered 23 points (9-15 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 0-0 FT), seven rebounds and an assist across 29 minutes in Friday's 128-111 win over the Heat.
items.story: In a game where Cade Cunningham was limited to 16 points while Jalen Duren (thigh) and Ausar Thompson (undisclosed) left with injuries, Collins stepped up and led the Pistons in scoring. This was also a nice bounce-back effort for the veteran, as he had been limited to just six points in the season-opening win over the Celtics on Tuesday. Look for Collins to have a prominent offensive role for the Pistons as a shooter and floor stretcher.

items.headline: Collins closed Tuesday's 121-113 victory over the Celtics with six points (3-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 25 minutes.
items.story: Collins started for his new team, as expected, but certainly fell short of the mark when it comes to having a sizeable impact. The two combined steals and blocks were nice, but more is going to be expected from him, particularly on the offensive end. Despite the struggles, he remains a clear hold in all formats.

items.headline: Collins logged 12 points (4-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds and one steal over 22 minutes during Friday's 129-125 preseason win over the Raptors.
items.story: Collins co-led the Pistons in rebounds during Friday's preseason finale, and he ended off the first half nicely with eight points in the second quarter. Collins signed a three-year contract with the Pistons on July 1 to replace Tobias Harris, who is in San Antonio. Collins finished the 2025-26 regular season having averaged 13.6 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 0.9 steals over 27.1 minutes per game while connecting on 55.2 percent of his field-goal attempts.

items.headline: Collins finished with 11 points (4-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and two steals in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 128-106 preseason victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: The veteran power forward is replacing Tobias Harris (calf), who jumped ship for San Antonio over the summer, in the starting lineup during his debut campaign with the Pistons. Collins is a strong lob threat and pick-and-roll big man, which should play well with superstar point guard Cade Cunningham. Collins got off to a shaky start last season but experienced a second-half turnaround from Jan. 1 onward, averaging 14.4 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.5 three-pointers per game while shooting 58.1 percent from the field and 45.2 percent from deep across his final 38 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Collins plans to use his versatility to complement Cade Cunningham after joining the Pistons during the offseason, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The veteran forward highlighted Cunningham's playmaking ability and said he wants to generate easy baskets by playing off the star guard. Collins shot 40.6 percent from three-point range during the 2025-26 regular season, and his combination of perimeter shooting and finishing ability should give Cunningham another versatile offensive option.

items.headline: Collins could be the most significant offseason addition for the Pistons, per Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News.
items.story: Collins is replacing Tobias Harris, who left for San Antonio this summer, in the starting lineup this year. The veteran power forward is a strong lob threat and pick-and-roll big man, which could play well with Cade Cunningham running the show at point guard. Collins got off to a rough start last season but experienced a second-half turnaround from Jan. 1 onward, averaging 14.4 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.5 three-pointers per game while shooting 58.1 percent from the floor and 45.2 percent from downtown over his final 38 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Collins agreed to a three-year, $51 million contract with the Pistons on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: With Tobias Harris expected to leave this offseason, the Pistons found a new starting power forward in Collins, who's coming off a down year but has been steady throughout his career. Across nine seasons and three different teams, Collins has averaged 16.2 points, 7.9 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.0 blocks and 0.7 steals while posting 55/37/79 shooting splits.

items.headline: Collins won't start Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Warriors, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: With Kawhi Leonard (ankle) back in the lineup, Collins will slide to the second unit. Over 13 appearances off the bench during the regular season, he averaged 12.8 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 23.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Collins racked up 18 points (8-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and nine rebounds over 21 minutes during Sunday's 115-110 victory over Golden State.
items.story: Ideally, a balanced set of totals from Collins and Brook Lopez would be the best recipe for the Clippers' frontcourt, but the team insists on keeping Derrick Jones and his oft-inconsistent production in the first unit. Collins showed his potential impact by pouring in 18 points in only 21 minutes. The team is likely to revert to the original scheme in the rematch Tuesday night, but Jones went scoreless in 21 minutes against Golden State. A lineup switch could be in store.

items.headline: Collins will start Sunday's game against the Warriors, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Collins will return to the starting lineup Sunday after playing only 13 minutes off the bench during Friday's loss in Portland. As a starter this season (55 games), Collins has averaged 13.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.7 stocks in 28.0 minutes.

items.headline: Collins is not in the Clippers' starting lineup against the Trail Blazers on Friday, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Collins started in Wednesday's 128-110 loss to the Thunder, when he played 27 minutes and finished with 12 points, nine rebounds, three assists and three steals. He'll revert to a bench role for Friday's contest due to the return of Darius Garland (toe).

items.headline: Collins is in the Clippers' starting lineup against the Thunder on Wednesday, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Collins has come off the bench in each of the Clippers' last two games, but he'll return to the starting lineup for Wednesday's contest due to the absence of Darius Garland (toe). Collins started nine consecutive outings from March 16 to April 2, and over that span, he averaged 12.7 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.9 threes and 0.9 steals over 26.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Collins logged 25 points (9-20 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two steals across 24 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 138-109 win over the Kings.
items.story: Shifted to the second unit for the first time since March 14, Collins didn't miss a beat as he tied his season scoring high. The veteran big man has scored in double digits in eight of 11 games since returning in mid-March from a neck strain, averaging 13.5 points, 5.5 boards, 1.3 assists, 1.2 threes and 1.1 steals in 25.8 minutes over that stretch while shooting 53.9 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Collins will come off the bench for Sunday's game in Sacramento, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: The Clippers are going with a small-ball lineup for Sunday's game, bringing Kris Dunn into the first unit and shifting Kawhi Leonard over to power forward, which will result in Collins heading to the bench. As a reserve this season, Collins owns averages of 13.0 points, 4.7 rebounds, 1.1 triples and 1.1 steals per game.

items.headline: Collins went to the locker room during the third quarter of Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers due to an undisclosed injury, but he returned for the start of the fourth, Adam Ausland of Fox Sports Radio reports.
items.story: Ausland notes that Collins appeared to suffer the injury while competing with Brook Lopez for a rebound. Collins checked out of the game with 6:23 remaining in the third period to get evaluated in the locker room. He would later emerge from the tunnel in time to start the final period of play.

items.headline: Collins accumulated 22 points (9-13 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block over 35 minutes during Sunday's 127-113 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: Sunday marked a breakout performance for Collins, who logged his most minutes and points since returning from a recent seven-game absence with a neck strain. The playing time is particularly a sign the power forward is cleared of whatever restrictions the Clippers had in place for Collins of late -- he last played at least 30 minutes back in February.

items.headline: Collins logged five points (2-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt), six rebounds, one assist and two steals in 20 minutes during Friday's 114-113 victory over Indiana.
items.story: Despite continuing to start, Collins has seen his role reduced of late, having logged more than 25 minutes only twice in his past seven appearances. During that time, he has barely been a top-200 player, averaging 10.0 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 24.1 minutes per game. Although he does possess the upside to be a top-70 player, managers are well within their rights to move on from him, given his current role.

items.headline: Collins (ankle) will play Wednesday against the Raptors, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Collins will return to action following a one-game absence due to a left ankle sprain. He'll presumably slot right back into the starting lineup, which would bump Nicolas Batum back to his usual bench role.

items.headline: Collins (ankle) is out for Monday's game against Milwaukee, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Collins will sit out Monday's matchup due to a left ankle sprain. Nicolas Batum and Kobe Sanders should be in line for an uptick in opportunities with Collins sidelined.

items.headline: Collins (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against the Bucks, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: The Clippers initially deemed Collins probable due to a left ankle sprain, so it's possible he suffered a slight setback during Monday's morning shootaround. If Collins is ultimately downgraded to out, the likes of Jordan Miller, Kris Dunn and Nicolas Batum would all be in line for more playing time.

items.headline: Collins is probable for Monday's matchup with Milwaukee due to a left ankle sprain, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Collins is dealing with a minor ankle sprain, but it looks like he plans to play through it Monday. Check back for official confirmation on his status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Collins logged 18 points (7-14 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-3 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and one steal in 28 minutes during Thursday's 105-99 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Collins enjoyed a bigger role on offense due to the absence of Kawhi Leonard (ankle), and the veteran stepped up while ending just two rebounds shy of a double-double. Collins missed seven games in early March due to a neck strain but has looked good since returning to the hardwood, averaging 14.3 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game in four appearances (three starts).

items.story: Collins continues to play at a high level for the Clippers.
