items.headline: Johnson finished Monday's 125-113 win over Minnesota in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with 18 points (8-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and three steals over 36 minutes.
items.story: Johnson bounced back after tepid single-digit scoring totals in Games 3 and 4 against Minnesota. The trade for Johnson has been a net negative for the Nuggets. Michael Porter's impressive totals this season with the Nets probably generate some buyer's remorse within the organization, but Monday's result was more in line with what was expected from Johnson. Denver has fallen behind in this series due to a lack of production from the supporting cast, and the balanced outcome from Johnson and Spencer Jones produced the desired result.

items.headline: Johnson logged nine points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 27 minutes during Saturday's 112-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson's production has slowed in the first round, averaging only 10.0 points, 1.5 assists, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.8 steals over four games against the Timberwolves. Although Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray are propping up the team with stellar production, the two superstars need more help from the supporting cast. Right now, Johnson isn't holding up his end of the bargain. The Nuggets will face elimination Monday night, and the pressure will be on Johnson, Christian Braun and Aaron Gordon to deliver better results.

items.headline: Johnson produced six points (2-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 24 minutes during Thursday's 113-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson couldn't get anything going on the offensive end, although he was certainly not alone, as Denver was soundly beaten by Minnesota on the road. On the whole, it's been a mediocre season for Johnson, who is averaging just 12.1 points and 2.0 three-pointers in 57 total appearances.

items.headline: Johnson ended with 12 points (5-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt) and one assist across 33 minutes during Saturday's 116-105 victory over the Timberwolves in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Johnson logged 33 minutes in Game 1. While he managed to supply 12 points, he didn't contribute much to other statistical categories and struggled from beyond the arc. With a win by the Nuggets to open the series, Johnson will look to turn things around on the offensive end Monday night in Game 2.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is available for Game 1 against Minnesota on Saturday.
items.story: The Nuggets kept Johnson off the court for their final two regular-season games, but they'll have the forward back on the floor for the start of the playoffs. A midseason right knee bone bruise limited Johnson to just 54 appearances in his debut season with Denver, but he did average a solid 12.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.2 three-pointers per contest while shooting 43.1 percent from deep across his final 26 games.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) is out for Sunday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Just like in Friday's win over the Thunder, Johnson will sit out this game due to rest purposes. The veteran forward, who averaged 12.2 points per game while shooting 43.0 percent from deep in 54 regular-season contests, should be ready to roll for the start of the playoffs next week.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Johnson will join fellow starters Christian Braun (ankle), Jamal Murray (shoulder) and Nikola Jokic (wrist) on the bench for Friday's contest. With Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Spencer Jones (hamstring) also ruled out, the Nuggets will turn to Tim Hardaway, Julian Strawther, Bruce Brown, Jalen Pickett and Tyus Jones to alleviate the load.

items.headline: Johnson (rest) is questionable for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Johnson, along with Denver's other four starters, is carrying a questionable tag with the team contemplating some maintenance days. Bruce Brown, Tim Hardaway and Julian Strawther could see expanded roles if multiple players sit out for Denver.

items.headline: Johnson closed with 18 points (8-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 136-119 win over Memphis.
items.story: Johnson might have a secondary role in the Nuggets' offensive scheme, but there's no question the sharpshooting forward is making the most of his opportunities of late. He's scored at least 17 points in each of his last four games, and he'll continue to have tons of scoring touches as long as he stays. Over that four-game stretch, Johnson is making 45.5 percent of his threes on 5.5 attempts per contest.

items.headline: Johnson provided 17 points (6-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds and seven assists in 37 minutes during Monday's 137-132 overtime victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Although injuries and inconsistent totals have plagued Johnson's first season with the Nuggets, he's coming alive at the right time. Over the past 10 games, Johnson has remained steady, averaging 14.2 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.2 steals while maintaining a conversion rate of 52.1 percent during the span. Assuming he stays healthy, Johnson will prop up the wing position with fantasy-worthy numbers in the playoffs.

items.headline: Johnson ended with 19 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, six assists and two steals across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 130-117 win over the Jazz.
items.story: The veteran forward fell one board short of his second double-double of the season, with the first coming way back on Dec. 18 against the Magic. Johnson has scored in double digits in 10 of the last 12 games, averaging 14.7 points, 3.7 rebounds, 2.8 threes, 2.6 assists and 1.1 steals over that span while shooting 54.4 percent from the floor and 48.6 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Johnson (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Johnson exited Sunday's win over the Warriors in the third quarter due to back spasms and did not return. However, he practiced Tuesday and is set to play Wednesday. Over his last five games, the 30-year-old forward has averaged 12.6 points, 2.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.0 steals in 27.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Johnson (back) practiced Tuesday, per Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette.
items.story: Johnson left Sunday's win over the Warriors and didn't return due to a back injury. However, his presence at Tuesday's session is an encouraging sign, and Johnson can be tentatively deemed questionable for Wednesday's game against Utah until the Nuggets release an official injury report.

items.headline: Johnson (back) did not return to Sunday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Johnson left the game in the third quarter and was not able to return. He finished the contest with six points (2-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three assists, one rebound, one steal and a block in 19 minutes. His status for Wednesday's game against the Jazz is now in question.

items.headline: Johnson is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Warriors due to back spasms.
items.story: Johnson left the game for the locker room in the third quarter and is uncertain to return. Tim Hardaway and Bruce Brown could see extra minutes while Johnson is sidelined.

items.headline: Johnson notched 19 points (7-10 FG, 5-7 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and two steals in 28 minutes during Sunday's 128-112 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Johnson couldn't miss to begin Sunday's game, drilling his first five buckets after being limited to just six points on 2-of-7 shooting his last time out. This was Johnson's second straight game with multiple steals, and as a bonus for nine-cat managers, he finished the match without a single turnover.

items.headline: Johnson recorded 18 points (6-8 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds and one assist in 23 minutes during Tuesday's 124-96 win over the 76ers.
items.story: The 30-year-old forward scored at least 15 points for a fourth straight game, a stretch in which Johnson has gone 11-for-20 (55.0 percent) from three-point range. During that hot streak, he's averaging 17.0 points, 3.3 boards, 2.8 threes, 2.3 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks while shooting 63.2 percent.

items.headline: Podziemski supplied 17 points (7-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds and eight assists over 37 minutes during Sunday's 124-112 win over the Clippers.
items.story: The fourth-year guard set new season highs in boards and assists as he came within spitting distance of his first career triple-double. Podziemski has played only five of the Warriors' seven games so far due to back trouble, but he's been productive when on the court, averaging 16.4 points, 5.6 assists, 5.4 boards, 2.2 threes and 1.2 steals in 33.6 minutes and seeing career-high shot volume at 13.0 FG attempts and 6.4 three-point attempts per contest.

items.headline: Podziemski closed Friday's 112-95 win over the Lakers with 21 points (7-15 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 3-5 FT), five rebounds, six assists, one block and two steals in 33 minutes.
items.story: Podziemski gave Golden State a strong secondary scoring option. The guard has taken on a bigger role in the starting lineup due to numerous long-term absences, and his all-around production was key to the comeback. He should keep seeing heavy minutes Sunday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Podziemski amassed 18 points (7-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Monday's 134-114 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Podziemski returned to the starting lineup after sitting out Saturday's contest against Phoenix, delivering an efficient performance while committing zero turnovers. The third-year guard also finished with a team-high plus-35 rating, contributing across multiple categories in Golden State's first victory of the campaign. His combination of rebounds, assists and three-point shooting should keep him relevant in standard fantasy formats.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is no longer listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Podziemski didn't play Saturday against the Suns because of a back issue, but since the shooting guard isn't on the injury report, he should return to the starting lineup Monday. Stephen Curry (rest) is also expected back, so the Warriors could have their starting backcourt against Denver. Podziemski has made just one appearance this season. He finished with 18 points (7-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three assists, two rebounds, three steals and one block in a 111-108 loss to the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) told reporters Friday that he will not play in the second leg of the Warriors' back-to-back set Saturday against the Suns, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Podziemski missed the Warriors' regular-season opener against the Lakers on Wednesday due to back soreness, but he was cleared to play against the Grizzlies on Friday, when he played 33 minutes and finished with 18 points (7-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three assists, two rebounds, three steals and one block in a 111-108 loss. Stephen Curry (rest) is unlikely to play Saturday, so the Warriors' starting backcourt figures to be made up of some combination of De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard, Brandon Williams and Gary Payton. Podziemski's next chance to play is Monday against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is good to go for Friday's game against the Grizzlies, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Podziemski is set to make his regular-season debut after sitting out Opening Night, which will shift De'Anthony Melton back to the second unit. Podziemski is expected to have a significant role in the Warriors' offense this season.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is probable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: The 23-year-old guard was previously listed as questionable, so he's trending in the right direction after missing Opening Night. If Podziemski is cleared to play, De'Anthony Melton would likely see fewer minutes.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Podziemski missed the regular-season opener against the Lakers on Wednesday and is at risk of missing a second consecutive game, but a final call on his availability is expected to be made at some point Friday. If Podziemski isn't able to play, De'Anthony Melton, Gary Payton and Will Richard are all candidates to log more time on the court.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Podziemski will miss Wednesday's regular-season opener due to lower-back soreness, and his next chance to play will come Friday against Memphis. With the 23-year-old guard sidelined, De'Anthony Melton, Gary Payton and Will Richard are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) was unable to practice Tuesday, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
items.story: It was reported on Monday that Podziemski will be listed as questionable for Wednesday's season opener, and Friedell confirmed that remains the case. If the Warriors opt to hold him out, the team could rely more on De'Anthony Melton.

items.headline: Podziemski (back) is questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Lakers, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area.
items.story: The combo guard has had a back issue crop up and missed Monday's practice, leaving his status for the start of the year up in the air. If Podziemski cannot play, De'Anthony Melton appears to be the next man up on the depth chart at shooting guard.

items.headline: Podziemski logged 17 points (4-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five assists, four rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes during Friday's 128-118 preseason win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Podziemski was quiet over the first two quarters of Friday's game before logging 10 points in the third to help the Warriors extend their lead. The fifth-year pro enters the 2026-27 with high expectations, which is reflected by the five-year, $110 million contract extension that he signed with the Warriors last Saturday. He could emerge as the No. 2 option on offense behind Stephen Curry, especially since Jimmy Butler (knee) is not expected to play until the start of the 2027 calendar year.

items.headline: Podziemski posted 17 points (6-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-5 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 26 minutes in Tuesday's 101-89 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Podziemski tied for the team lead in scoring and hit a key fourth-quarter three-pointer set up by a Charles Bassey offensive rebound as Golden State erased a 13-point halftime deficit. After a slow preseason opener, Podziemski has scored 16 or more in two of his last three exhibitions and looks locked into a starting role next to Stephen Curry.

items.headline: Podziemski (rest) is in the Warriors' starting lineup against the Kings on Saturday, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Podziemski sat out Wednesday's exhibition contest against the Trail Blazers, but the fourth-year pro will be on the court for Saturday's game. He's fresh off signing a five-year, $110 million contract extension that is fully guaranteed.

items.headline: Podziemski (rest) and the Warriors agreed to a five-year, $110 million contract extension Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The deal is a fully guaranteed, rookie-scale contract extension that includes a mutual option for the 2031-32 season. Podziemski is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he averaged career highs in points (13.8) and three-pointers (1.9) while starting in 43 of 82 regular-season games. Podziemski figures to start alongside Stephen Curry (rest) in the backcourt to open the 2026-27 season, though that could change once Jimmy Butler (knee) is cleared to return, which likely won't be until after the calendar flips to 2027.

items.headline: Podziemski (rest) won't travel with the Warriors for Wednesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Podziemski is coming off a strong showing in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers, finishing with 16 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in 19 minutes. Golden State is resting several rotation players during the second half of a preseason back-to-back, and Podziemski should have another opportunity to suit up Saturday against Sacramento.

items.headline: Podziemski tallied 16 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block over 19 minutes in Tuesday's 124-98 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Podziemski came out flat with seven points on 2-for-10 shooting in Golden State's preseason opener, but he found his footing against a Lakers team that was resting their stars. Podziemski was generating a lot of buzz at training camp, so it'll be interesting to see if he can keep it going  Wednesday in Portland.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded seven points (2-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 18 minutes during Sunday's 104-101 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Podziemski struggled from the field after earning a starting spot alongside Stephen Curry in Golden State's preseason opener. Despite the poor shooting performance, Podziemski appears positioned for a prominent role after a strong training camp, and coach Steve Kerr recently called him one of the Warriors' best players.

items.headline: Podziemski said at Warriors media day he wants to shoot more threes per game, per Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle.
items.story: Head coach Steve Kerr is in full support as well, offering Podziemski encouragement Wednesday to fire away from downtown. Podziemski opened last season as a part-time starter before moving into a full-time position with the first unit post-All-Star break, averaging 17.5 points, 6.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.0 steals in his final 27 regular-season games, and he could become a lethal threat from deep especially once Jimmy Butler (knee) and Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed) are both in the mix.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 23 points (9-17 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 10 rebounds and one steal over 39 minutes during Friday's 111-96 Play-In Game loss to the Suns.
items.story: Podziemski left it all on the floor, recording his sixth double-double of the season. On the whole, it was a relatively successful season for Podziemski, as he played in all 82 regular-season games and both Play-In tilts. With averages of 14.0 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.9 three-pointers, he is likely to remain on the radar heading into drafts next season.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 30 points (9-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 9-10 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 32 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Stephen Curry (ankle) returned to the starting five Friday, but it was Podziemski who led the way on offense for the Warriors as he paced all scorers on the night while setting a new career high. The third-year guard has dropped 20-plus points in seven of the last 10 games, averaging 21.1 points, 4.8 boards, 3.7 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.0 steals over that stretch as he heads into the regular-season finale Sunday.

items.headline: Podziemski produced 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist across 24 minutes during Thursday's 119-103 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: The 17 points tied Nate Williams for the team lead in the loss. Podziemski has scored in double digits in nine straight games as he tries to keep an injury-depleted Golden State roster afloat heading into the Play-In Tournament, averaging 20.1 points, 5.0 boards, 4.0 assists, 2.6 threes and 1.0 steals over that span while shooting 53.1 percent from the floor and 43.4 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Podziemski finished Tuesday's 110-105 win over Sacramento with 20 points (5-11 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal in 30 minutes.
items.story: The third-year guard continues to roll. Podziemski has scored at least 14 points and drained multiple three-pointers in eight straight games, averaging 20.5 points, 5.5 boards, 4.4 assists, 2.8 threes and 1.1 steals over that stretch while shooting 54.1 percent from the floor and 45.8 percent from long distance.

items.headline: Podziemski ended Thursday's 118-111 loss to Cleveland with 25 points (9-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, four assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: This was one of Podziemski's best games of the season as he recorded his fourth game with at least 25 points, finishing one point shy of his season-best mark. He's been on a tear with 18.3 points, 5.9 rebounds and 4.1 assists over his last eight games, but Stephen Curry (knee) is targeting a return Sunday against Houston.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 23 points (8-14 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals across 32 minutes during Sunday's 116-93 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Podziemski matched Kristaps Porzingis with a team-high 23 points during the loss. While Podziemski has fared well in the starting role at point guard, the gap left by Stephen Curry (knee) is still quite noticeable. The team seems destined to finish at the bottom of the Play-In bracket without his contribution, but Podziemski has helped to keep the team above water. He's averaged 14.5 points, 6.4 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.0 steals since Curry's exit 21 games ago.

items.headline: Podziemski logged 22 points (6-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 7-8 FT), 10 rebounds, seven assists and two steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 131-126 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Podziemski has reached the 20-point mark in three straight games, which marks his longest streak of the season doing so. With Jimmy Butler (knee) and Stephen Curry (knee) sidelined, Podziemski has been forced to embrace a bigger role on offense, but he's certainly thriving in that scenario. He's averaging 16.9 points, 6.5 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 0.9 steals per game in 16 appearances since returning to the starting lineup on a regular basis Feb. 25.

items.headline: Podziemski notched 22 points (6-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 8-8 FT), six rebounds and five assists across 35 minutes during Wednesday's 109-106 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Making his 15th straight start in place of Stephen Curry (knee), Podziemski scored 20-plus points for the second straight game and the sixth time in 13 March contests. On the month, the third-year guard is averaging 16.9 points, 6.1 boards, 4.0 assists, 2.3 threes and 0.9 steals in 33.5 minutes.

items.headline: Podziemski supplied 20 points (8-15 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, six assists, one block and one steal over 40 minutes during Monday's 137-131 overtime win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Podziemski bounced back with a solid total after struggling through a rough four-game stretch where he averaged only 10.0 points. The third-year pro has been indispensable during Stephen Curry's (knee) extended absence. Given the Warriors' playoff position with only 10 games remaining, Podziemski will continue to receive every opportunity to produce, with Curry's regular-season return becoming increasingly unlikely.

items.headline: Podziemski ended Wednesday's 120-99 loss to the Celtics with 10 points (1-8 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 7-10 FT), six rebounds, five assists and one steal in 28 minutes.
items.story: Podziemski couldn't get his shot to drop and finished with a minus-11 plus/minus rating in the blowout loss. The Warriors have now dropped six of their past seven games, and it'll be tough for them to right the ship Friday with a matchup against the 48-18 Pistons.

items.headline: Podziemski chipped in 25 points (8-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 7-9 FT), five rebounds, six assists and two steals across 37 minutes during Sunday's 110-107 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Podziemski was coming off a 25-point effort in Friday's loss to the Timberwolves, and he continues to put up excellent numbers since moving into a starting role. He has started the Warriors' last nine games dating back to Feb. 25, and he's averaging a robust line of 18.4 points, 6.9 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game over that stretch while shooting 38.5 percent from beyond the arc. As long as Stephen Curry (knee) remains sidelined, Podziemski should maintain elevated usage.

items.headline: Podziemski closed Friday's 127-117 loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-17 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 10 rebounds and two assists in 36 minutes.
items.story: The third-year guard led the shorthanded Warriors in scoring, and the roster only got thinner as the night progressed with Al Horford (calf), Quinten Post (ankle) and Seth Curry (thigh) all heading to the locker room early. Podziemski has scored more than 20 points in three of the last six games, averaging 18.8 points, 7.0 boards, 3.8 assists, 3.3 threes and 1.0 steals in 35.7 minutes over that stretch, and it doesn't look like his workload or usage are going to be scaled back any time soon.

items.headline: Podziemski ended Monday's 119-116 loss to the Jazz with 14 points (5-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 0-4 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: Podziemski has strung together four consecutive games with at least 14 points, and he's scored in double figures in 11 of his last 12 contests. The third-year guard should continue to handle extra usage in the absence of Stephen Curry (knee), averaging 16.5 points, 8.1 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.1 steals in 34.0 minutes per tilt in his last 12 games.

items.headline: Podziemski logged 26 points (10-18 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and one assist over 40 minutes during the Warriors' 115-113 overtime win over the Rockets on Thursday.
items.story: Podziemski got off to a slow start to Wednesday's game but finished strong with 10 points in the third quarter and seven more in overtime to help the Warriors snap their two-game losing streak. His 26 points were a season high, and he was one rebound shy from recording his third double-double of the season. Podziemski has started in each of the Warriors' last four games and should remain a starter for as long as Stephen Curry (knee) is sidelined.

items.headline: Podziemski recorded 22 points (9-18 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and three assists in 37 minutes during Monday's 114-101 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Podziemski posted a solid all-around line in the loss, but lackluster performances with the rest of the first unit weren't enough to turn the tide against the Clippers. He was one of only four Warriors to reach double digits in the contest, with only two other players scoring more than 10 points. Although Podziemski has been a great placeholder for Stephen Curry (knee), the team is in desperate need of more production.

items.headline: Podziemski finished with 19 points (6-14 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds and six assists across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 133-112 win over Memphis.
items.story: Podziemski was moved into the starting lineup Wednesday for the 20th time this season (and first since Feb. 3). The third-year pro responded by co-leading the Warriors in rebounds while finishing second in both assists and points. The Warriors' next game takes place Saturday against the Lakers, and it's unclear whether Podziemski will remain in the starting lineup if De'Anthony Melton (knee) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Podziemski is part of the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Podziemski will make his 20th start of the season for Golden State, as the Warriors deal with a slew of injuries. As a starter, Podziemski is averaging 12.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.1 steals across 28.9 minutes.

items.headline: Podziemski had 16 points (7-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 15 rebounds, three assists and two steals over 32 minutes during Tuesday's 113-109 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: For the second straight game, Podziemski pulled down 15 rebounds, matching his career-best mark. He continues to step up for the shorthanded Warriors, and his fantasy upside is trending up while Stephen Curry continues to nurse his knee injury.

items.headline: Podziemski registered 18 points (7-16 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 15 rebounds, nine assists and one steal over 37 minutes during Sunday's 128-117 victory over the Nuggets.
items.story: Podziemski turned in a huge all-around performance, pulling down a career-best 15 rebounds while finishing just one assist shy of his first triple-double. After starting seven straight games to close January and open February, the young guard has recently shifted back to a reserve role, averaging 11.4 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.0 steals in 28.0 minutes per contest over the five games prior to Sunday's outburst.

items.headline: Gafford finished with 20 points (9-10 FG, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, one steal and one block across 26 minutes in Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Gafford has been a scoring machine lately, averaging 19.0 points over his last two outings. The 20 points marked a season-high for the 28-year-old through seven games, and he's now grabbed seven or more boards in five straight contests. Gafford tied Walter Clayton for the team lead in scoring with Kyrie Irving (rest) out and Cooper Flagg finishing 3-for-19 from the field in 40 minutes of play. Gafford offers a reliable fantasy floor and will continue to work as the primary big with Dereck Lively (foot) and Santi Aldama (knee) both sidelined.

items.headline: Gafford amassed 18 points (6-7 FG, 6-9 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 29 minutes during Friday's 116-111 victory over the Rockets.
items.story: The 18 points were a season high for Gafford, who continues to operate without much backup in the paint as Dereck Lively (foot) and Santi Aldama (knee) remain sidelined. Gafford has recorded exactly two blocks in six straight games to begin the season, averaging 8.5 points, 7.0 boards, 2.5 assists, 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals in 23.3 minutes while shooting 70.0 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Gafford produced seven points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists and two blocks over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 120-96 victory over the Thunder.
items.story: The 11 boards led Dallas on the night, although Gafford didn't see enough offensive opportunities to produce his first double-double of the season. The 28-year-old center hasn't seen a significant increase in his workload to begin the season even with Dereck Lively (foot) and Santi Aldama (knee) still waiting to make their 2026-27 debuts. In 22.4 minutes over five games, Gafford is averaging 6.6 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 2.0 blocks and 1.0 steals while shooting 65.2 percent from the floor. Wednesday's three-pointer was also the first of his career, and his second-ever attempt from beyond the arc. The other came in 2021-22, when he was playing for the Wizards.

items.headline: Gafford could have the green light to attempt occasional three-pointers this season, with head coach Dusty May encouraging the center to expand his offensive game, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: May said the Mavericks want Gafford to become more of a playmaking decision-maker on the perimeter and indicated that he'll be allowed to take rhythm threes as long as he earns those opportunities. Gafford has attempted just one three-pointer across his seven NBA regular seasons and has yet to make one, so any development of a perimeter shot would represent a significant change to his offensive profile. He averaged 9.5 points, 6.9 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 21.7 minutes across 55 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. With Dereck Lively (knee) not cleared for the start of training camp, Gafford could be in line for major minutes out of the gate in 2026-27.

items.headline: Gafford will face increased competition for minutes during the 2026-27 season after Dallas selected Morez Johnson with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Gafford started 44 of the 55 games he appeared in last season, but there's a new head coach in Dallas, and the Mavericks just drafted one of his favorite prospects. items.headline: Philon faces plenty of competition for minutes and an uncertain role heading into his rookie campaign, per Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com.
items.story: Selected with the No. 22 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Philon will likely have to impress to take on a steady role after the 76ers added Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Anfernee Simons, Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (finger) this offseason. Philon will need to prove he can be effective off the ball to see meaningful burn on a nightly basis during his rookie season, as the 76ers have plenty of ball-handlers ahead of him. The 20-year-old's off-ball movement and ability to hit catch-and-shoot threes could play a large part in his playing time, considering the Sixers also have Simons to handle the rock off the bench. Philon will also have to hold his own defensively to stay on the court. He earned All-SEC First Team honors with Alabama in 2025-26, averaging 22.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.2 steals while shooting 50.1 percent from the field and 39.9 percent from beyond the arc in 30.9 minutes per game.

items.story: Irving is sitting out this exhibition Wednesday. Friday's game against the Hawks marks his last chance for a tune-up.

items.headline: Irving recorded 17 points (6-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds and three assists across 22 minutes in Sunday's 132-115 preseason win over the Rockets in China.
items.story: Making his first appearance since suffering a torn ACL in March 2025, Irving led Dallas in scoring while shooting a respectable 46.2 percent from the field and knocking down two three-pointers. The veteran guard also distributed three assists without committing a turnover, demonstrating his usual composure as a ballhandler. Irving's 22-minute workload gave him a chance to build rhythm ahead of the regular season, and the goal is to have him as healthy and ready as possible for Opening Night against the Rockets on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Irving is scheduled to play in Sunday's preseason rematch against Houston, Kevin Gray Jr. of AllDLLS.com reports.
items.story: Irving's anticipated appearance would give Dallas an opportunity to evaluate its backcourt rotation alongside Cooper Flagg and the rest of the Mavericks' young core. The veteran guard's workload remains uncertain, but Sunday's contest could provide valuable preseason minutes as Dallas prepares for the 2026-27 regular season.

items.headline: Irving (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason game against the Rockets.
items.story: While Irving will miss the preseason opener in China, the veteran point guard is expected to play at some point during the exhibition schedule, with his next chance coming during Sunday's rematch against the Rockets. When Irving is cleared to suit up, he'll likely face major restrictions after a 19-month recovery from an ACL tear.

items.headline: Irving is fully cleared after a 19-month recovery from an ACL tear, and he will suit up for the Mavericks during the preseason, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: It sounds like Irving will be good to go for Friday's exhibition against the Rockets in China, although he'll likely have his minutes heavily monitored during the preseason. Irving offers first-round upside, but he's had trouble staying on the court throughout his career.

items.headline: Mavericks president Masai Ujiri offered an encouraging update on Irving's recovery from his knee injury Friday, saying the veteran guard is "right there" as he works toward returning to game action, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.story: Irving missed the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from surgery to repair a torn ACL in his left knee, but he has been participating in pickup games during his ramp-up process. The 34-year-old last played in 2024-25, when he averaged 24.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.3 steals in 36.1 minutes across 50 regular-season appearances. Ujiri's comments provide another positive sign that Irving is closing in on his return, though Dallas has yet to announce a definitive timeline.

items.headline: Irving (knee) has been playing in pickup games this offseason in an effort to ramp up toward his return to the court in 2026-27, Tim MacMahon of ESPN reports.
items.story: Irving suffered a torn ACL in his left knee in March 2025 and did not play in the 2025-26 campaign. The veteran point guard has had plenty of time to recover and will enter training camp having played in pickup games this summer. It wouldn't be surprising to see the 34-year-old enter the season on a minutes restriction, though it appears likely he'll be ready to play by Opening Night. Irving appeared in 50 regular-season games in 2024-25 before suffering the knee injury, averaging 24.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.8 combined steals-plus-blocks in 36.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Irving (knee) should be fully healthy by the end of the offseason, per Christian Clark of The New York Times.
items.story: Irving is close to a full recovery from ACL surgery, so he should be a full participant by the time training camp comes around in the fall. The star guard hasn't yet gotten the chance to take the floor since the Mavericks drafted Cooper Flagg last year, so it'll be interesting to see how the two mesh once they're sharing the backcourt duties.

items.headline: The Mavericks announced Wednesday that Irving (knee) won't play this season while he continues to recover from the ACL reconstruction surgery he underwent March 26.
items.story: Dallas sits at 19-35 on the season coming out of the All-Star break and is pivoting toward a rebuild, so the news that Irving won't play in 2025-26 comes as little surprise, especially after head coach Jason Kidd had been vague on the veteran guard's status in recent weeks. According to Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com, the Mavericks still have some optimism that Irving will be able to practice at some point before the end of the season, which will put him on track to be back to 100 percent well in advance of training camp next fall, when he would be 18 months removed from surgery. Irving will be entering the final year of his contract next season and holds a $42.42 million player option for 2027-28.

items.headline: George (rest) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
items.story: The star forward is good to go after sitting out Monday's loss in Houston. George is off to a fast start with his new team, having delivered at least 15 points in six straight games and seven dimes in three consecutive contests.

items.headline: George will be rested Monday against Houston.
items.story: There's no injury to report and this appears to be a planned maintenance day for the veteran. With George on the shelf, the Celtics will need guys like Payton Pritchard and Baylor Scheierman to absorb more minutes.

items.headline: George posted 17 points (6-14 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, eight assists, two steals and two blocks across 33 minutes in Sunday's 108-97 win over the Magic.
items.story: George didn't have his best shooting performance, but fantasy managers will gladly overlook it, given his excellent multi-category output. His eight assists and four combined defensive stats helped offset a relatively modest scoring total, while his 33-minute workload reinforced his importance alongside Jayson Tatum. George's versatility continues to provide a strong fantasy foundation even when his shot isn't falling consistently. In six appearances this season, George has averaged 20.7 points, 6.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 2.3 steals per contest.

items.headline: George produced 18 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, eight assists and three steals across 27 minutes during Friday's 125-111 win over Chicago.
items.story: George came out hot with eight points in the first quarter, and he ended the game a distant third on the Celtics in scoring behind Payton Pritchard (30 points) and Jayson Tatum (26 points). George also led the Celtics in assists, and Friday's game was the fourth time that the veteran forward has logged at least two steals. He has fit in seamlessly into head coach Joe Mazzulla's gameplan early on, and George is averaging 21.4 points, 6.0 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 2.4 steals over 30.4 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: George registered 20 points (8-16 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 36 minutes in Tuesday's 125-124 overtime win over the Nets.
items.story: George delivered a well-rounded fantasy performance in a bounce-back effort after his 16-point output (5-14 FG) against the Bulls on Monday. His 36-minute workload and 16 field-goal attempts highlight his continued involvement in Boston's offense alongside Jayson Tatum. While his scoring may fluctuate, George's ability to contribute across multiple categories gives him a relatively stable fantasy floor. George has established himself as a reliable scoring weapon for Boston with at least 15 points in each of his four appearances so far.

items.headline: George amassed 16 points (5-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 25 minutes during Monday's 134-99 win over the Bulls.
items.story: George struggled inside the arc but connected on three triples as Boston cruised to a comfortable victory. His playing time was limited by the lopsided score, and he committed four turnovers. The veteran forward has scored between 15 and 16 points in consecutive outings following his 38-point season opener.

items.headline: George had 15 points (6-15 FG, 3-7 3Pt), seven rebounds, two assists and two steals across 34 minutes during Friday's 107-103 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: George came back to earth a bit after dropping 38 points in his season debut, but he still delivered a strong all-around performance Friday. The Celtics have their first back-to-back set of the season on tap for Monday against the Bulls and Tuesday versus the Nets, and it'll be interesting to see if the 36-year-old forward will play both ends after sitting out back-to-backs at times last year with the 76ers.

items.headline: George tallied 38 points (12-21 FG, 7-12 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, five steals and three assists across 31 minutes in Tuesday's 121-113 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: George turned in an efficient shooting performance, particularly from three-point range, en route to a game-high 38 points in his regular-season debut with the Celtics. The veteran forward provided a well-rounded stat line, leading all players in triples and steals while finishing as the Celtics' second-leading rebounder.

items.headline: George (rest) is expected to play Tuesday versus Detroit.
items.story: George didn't suit up for Friday's 125-120 preseason overtime win over Philadelphia to rest, though he is anticipated to be ready to go Tuesday versus the Pistons. The 36-year-old appeared in only 37 regular-season games for the 76ers in 2025-26, averaging 17.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.7 steals over 30.7 minutes per outing. Now paired with Jayson Tatum (rest), George still has All-Star upside, but he will need to figure out how to stay on the floor.

items.headline: George (rest) won't play in Friday's preseason finale against the 76ers, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: George and the rest of Boston's regulars won't suit up for the final exhibition but should be good to go for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Pistons. George registered 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists and five steals over 25 minutes during his Celtics debut against the 76ers last Saturday.

items.headline: George registered 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists and five steals over 25 minutes during the Celtics' 144-106 preseason win over the 76ers on Saturday.
items.story: George didn't have the most efficient night offensively, but he demonstrated his defensive chops during Saturday's win, with four of his game-high five steals taking place in the first half. The veteran forward was the Celtics' return for Jaylen Brown in the offseason, and it'll be interesting to see how George and Jayson Tatum fit together early on in the 2026-27 season. George is expected to have his preseason reps limited before the Celtics' regular-season opener against the Pistons on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

items.headline: George (rest) is in the Celtics' starting lineup against the 76ers on Saturday, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: George will suit up in a Celtics uniform for the first time and face his former team in Saturday's exhibition contest. His playing time figures to be limited until the Celtics' regular-season opener against the Pistons on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

items.headline: George (rest) isn't in line to play Thursday versus Cleveland, Zack Cox of the Boston Herald reports.
items.story: The Celtics are holding several key contributors out of the starting lineup Thursday. Jordan Walsh is drawing the start at power forward.

items.headline: Head coach Joe Mazzulla praised George's experience Tuesday, per Justin Turpin of WEEI.com.
items.story: George has big shoes to fill in Boston this season, stepping into the role as one of Jayson Tatum's running mates following Jaylen Brown's exit. Staying on the court has been a major concern for George, who has made at least 70 regular-season appearances just once in his past seven seasons. However, he should push for mid-round fantasy value when healthy after averaging at least 16.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.5 steals per game in back-to-back years for the 76ers.

items.headline: The Celtics traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers on Wednesday in exchange for George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After two injury-filled years with the 76ers, the star forward will join the Celtics. The star forward has reached the 70-game mark just once over his last seven regular seasons, but he'll now get the opportunity to function as Jayson Tatum's running mate in a big role for the Celtics. George averaged 17.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.7 steals in 30.7 minutes per contest over 37 regular-season games in 2025-26.

items.headline: George could be in line for a larger workload after Philadelphia lost both Kelly Oubre and Quentin Grimes this offseason, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.
items.story: With two key wing contributors no longer on the roster, the veteran forward should be asked to shoulder more of the scoring and playmaking responsibilities alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. Assuming he stays healthy, George could be positioned for a bounce-back fantasy campaign with an expanded role on the wing.

items.headline: George contributed seven points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and two assists over 27 minutes during Sunday's 144-114 loss to the Knicks in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: George went out with a whimper, turning in easily his worst game of the postseason. In fact, his seven points matched his season low, summing up what was a rough night for the 76ers. With the season coming to an end, discussions regarding George's immediate future will undoubtedly begin to bubble. Through 49 appearances in both the regular season and the playoffs, George averaged 17.1 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.6 steals and 2.8 three-pointers.

items.headline: George had 19 points (7-18 FG, 5-13 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two steals over 43 minutes during Wednesday's 108-102 loss to the Knicks in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: George got off to a hot start, drilling his first four shots and racking up 11 points in his first five minutes of action. However, the Knicks did an excellent job shutting him down in the second half, holding him to just six points on 2-for-9 shooting after the break. The 76ers will look to climb out of their 0-2 hole with the series shifting to Philadelphia on Friday.

items.headline: George supplied 17 points (6-11 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 26 minutes in Monday's 137-98 loss to the Knicks in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: George turned in an efficient performance Monday, knocking down a game-high four triples while leading Philadelphia in scoring despite a blowout loss that kept him off the floor in the fourth quarter. The veteran forward also paced the first unit in assists. He has now hit at least three three-pointers in six straight games, scoring 16-plus points in five of them. George will look to remain productive in Game 2 on Wednesday as the Sixers try to steal a game at Madison Square Garden.

items.headline: George (illness) will play in Saturday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference first-round series against the Celtics, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: George was a late addition to the injury report due to an illness, though he'll give it a go in this win-or-go-home matchup. Through six first-round outings, the star forward has averaged 18.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.7 steals in 36.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Post (ankle) has been downgraded to out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Post is set for a second consecutive absence while tending to a right ankle sprain. His next chance to return will arrive Wednesday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Post (ankle) is questionable to suit up for Monday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Post missed Saturday's 136-105 victory over Sacramento with a sprained right ankle, and he's now in jeopardy of missing a second straight contest with the injury. If he's unable to play, Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks will split the backup center minutes.

items.headline: Post (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game versus Sacramento, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
items.story: Post was listed as doubtful, and now we have official confirmation that he'll be on the inactive list Saturday night. His minutes will likely be divvied up amongst Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks.

items.headline: Post (ankle) is doubtful for Saturday's game against the Kings.
items.story: A right ankle sprain is expected to cost Post at least one contest. Assuming he's eventually downgraded to out, more playing time should fall into the hands of Isaiah Stewart as the No. 2 center Saturday.

items.headline: Post (ankle) didn't return to Thursday's game against Portland. He recorded 10 points (3-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and four rebounds in seven minutes before exiting.
items.story: Post was off to a great start to Thursday's clash, and he may have had a significant opportunity to do damage in the second half if he hadn't tweaked his ankle, considering Zach Edey picked up four fouls before halftime. The severity of Post's injury isn't known at this time, and he can be considered day-to-day leading up to Saturday's game against Sacramento.

items.headline: Post is doubtful to return to Thursday's game against the Trail Blazers due to a right ankle injury.
items.story: Post appeared to step on an opposing player's foot and had to hobble off the court after the play. Zach Edey had four fouls in the first half, which likely means Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks will see more minutes down the stretch, assuming Post is unable to return.

items.headline: Post finished with seven points (3-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist across 17 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 win over the Kings.
items.story: Despite the absence of the resting Zach Edey at center, Post didn't see a bump in playing time Sunday. Post appears to be stuck in the backup center role and could continue to struggle for fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Post won't start Wednesday's preseason game against the Magic.
items.story: Zach Edey (ankle) will return to action Wednesday, pushing Post to the second unit. The big man got the starting nod in Monday's preseason-opening win over Atlanta, contributing eight points (3-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt) and four rebounds in 12 minutes.

items.headline: Post will start Monday's preseason game against the Hawks, Damichael Cole of The Memphis Commercial Appeal reports.
items.story: Zach Edey (ankle) isn't expected to play Monday, opening the door for Post to step into the starting five. The big man figures to compete with Isaiah Stewart for playing time behind Edey ahead of the regular season.

items.headline: The Warriors did not match the Grizzlies' three-year, $30 million offer sheet for Post on Tuesday, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Post is now officially a member of the Grizzlies after spending the first two seasons of his career with the Warriors. The big man appeared in 67 regular-season games (35 starts) in 2025-26, averaging 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 17.3 minutes per contest. While he could carve out a more significant role with the rebuilding Grizzlies, Post will still likely have to compete for playing time with the likes of Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks behind Zach Edey (ankle).

items.headline: Post (foot) agreed to a three-year, $30 million contract with the Grizzlies on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Post is a restricted free agent, so the Warriors can still match this offer sheet. Including the Play-In Tournament, the big man missed the Warriors' final nine games of the 2025-26 campaign due to a right foot injury, and he finished the regular season with averages of 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.4 steals in 17.3 minutes per game across 67 outings (35 starts). Golden State has until 11:59 p.m. ET on Tuesday to match the Grizzlies' offer.

items.headline: Post (foot) averaged 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.5 blocks and 0.4 steals in 17.3 minutes per game across 67 regular-season appearances (35 starts) in 2025-26.
items.story: Even as a member of the starting five, Post saw inconsistent playing time for the injury-plagued Warriors this season. The big man produced numbers similar to his rookie campaign but saw a dip in his three-point efficiency, shooting 33.6 percent from downtown. He still appeared in 25 more regular-season games than in 2024-25, though he missed the final seven outings of the regular season and both Play-In Tournament games due to a right foot injury. The 26-year-old's future in Golden State is uncertain, with the club holding a team option for 2026-27.

items.headline: Post (foot) is out for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Suns.
items.story: Post is in line for a ninth consecutive absence while on the mend from a right foot injury. If the Warriors are able to emerge victorious Friday, his next opportunity to take the court would arrive in Game 1 of the first round against Oklahoma City on Sunday.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Clippers.
items.story: Post will miss an eighth consecutive contest due to a right foot injury. However, his absence shouldn't affect the rotation with Kristaps Porzingis, Al Horford and Draymond Green all healthy.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Post will miss a seventh straight game due to a right foot injury, and his next opportunity to suit up will come Wednesday during the Play-In Tournament. The big man will finish the regular season with averages of 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 17.3 minutes per showing across 67 outings (35 starts).

items.headline: The Warriors announced Saturday that Post (foot) will be re-evaluated next week.
items.story: Post is working his way back from right foot soreness, which has already cost him Golden State's past three contests. With Post and Al Horford (calf) both sidelined, the lion's share of the center minutes should fall onto Kristaps Porzingis and Draymond Green for the time being.

items.headline: Post is out for Thursday's game against the Cavaliers due to right foot injury management.
items.story: Thursday will mark a second consecutive absence for Post, who left Sunday's loss to Denver early. Kristaps Porzingis and Draymond Green should share the center minutes for the Warriors versus Cleveland.

items.headline: Post has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to right foot injury management.
items.story: Post departed Sunday's matchup against Denver due to right foot soreness, though it's worth noting that he's been ruled out Wednesday due to right foot injury management, so this appears to be a precautionary decision. Draymond Green and Omer Yurtseven should be in line for increased opportunities at center with Post, Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) all out.

items.headline: Post won't return to Sunday's game due to right foot soreness, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Post left the game in the second half and will not return. He saw limited action before exiting, totaling two rebounds and a steal in four minutes. The injury puts his status for Wednesday's game against the Spurs in question.

items.headline: Post exited Sunday's game against the Nuggets for the locker room due to an apparent right lower leg injury, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Post came into Sunday's contest dealing with a right foot issue, and it appeared as if he rolled his right ankle before exiting the game. He should be considered questionable at best to return until any further update is given.

items.headline: Post (foot) is available for Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Post missed the last three games due to right foot injury management, but he will return to the lineup Sunday. In his last five games, he posted averages of 10.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 21.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Post (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Denver.
items.story: Post has missed three straight games due to right foot injury management, though the questionable tag is a step in the right direction. If Post is able to play, Omer Yurtseven and Malevy Leons could see fewer opportunities.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Post is slated for a third straight absence due to right foot injury management. Al Horford (calf) has also been downgraded to out Friday, which could once again open up more chances for Omer Yurtseven and Malevy Leons in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Post (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Post will miss a second consecutive contest due to right foot injury management. The 26-year-old big man's next opportunity to play will come Friday against the Wizards. With Al Horford (calf) also remaining out, Gui Santos and Malevy Leons are candidates to see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Post has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Mavericks due to right foot injury management.
items.story: Post has been working through a right foot issue as of late and will miss his fifth game since March 7, with his next chance to play being Wednesday against the Nets. He played 14 minutes in Saturday's loss to the Hawks, and those minutes should be absorbed by Kristaps Porzingis (back), the latter of whom is listed as probable for Monday's game.

items.headline: Post is part of the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the Hawks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.story: Post will start alongside Draymond Green in the frontcourt. In 34 starts this season, Post is averaging 9.5 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.6 assists across 20.6 minutes.

items.headline: Post (foot) is listed as available for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Post had been previously considered questionable due to a right foot issue. However, the second-year center has been given the green light to suit up Saturday. With Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (back) sidelined, Post and Draymond Green will handle most of the center duties.

items.headline: Post (foot) is questionable for Saturday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Post didn't play in Friday's loss to Detroit because of a nagging foot issue. The Warriors are already down Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (back) for this one. On top of that, Draymond Green (back) is also carrying a questionable designation. If Post can suit up, he could be looking at more action versus Atlanta. However, if Post and Green join Horford and Porzingis on the shelf, the Dubs should rely mostly on Gui Santos and Omer Yurtseven to handle the bulk of the work underneath the basket.

items.headline: Post (foot) is out for Friday's game versus Detroit.
items.story: Post will be sidelined for the first leg of this back-to-back set, joining Al Horford (calf) in street clothes. With this news, Omer Yurtseven could step into a larger role in the frontcourt behind Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis.

items.headline: Post (foot) is questionable for Friday's game in Detroit.
items.story: Friday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so there's a chance that Post will get hit with a maintenance day. If he is forced to the sidelines, Omer Yurtseven could see an expanded role in the rotation.

items.headline: Post (foot) is available for Wednesday's game against Boston.
items.story: Post missed Monday's contest, but he'll be back in action for Wednesday's contest. With Al Horford (calf) sidelined, Post will look to mix in behind Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Post (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Post was unable to take the floor Monday against Golden State due to a right foot injury. However, he's been upgraded to questionable ahead of Wednesday's clash, meaning he should at least have a chance to prove his health during shootaround and pregame warmups.

items.headline: Post (foot) won't play Monday against the Warriors.
items.story: Coach Steve Kerr mentioned in his pregame presser that Post was banged up after Sunday's game against the Knicks, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic, and the big man has since been downgraded to out. Look for Will Richard, Gary Payton and Malevy Leons to be candidates for an increase in playing time as a result.

items.headline: Post is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards due to right foot injury management.
items.story: After he posted a career-high 22 points (9-16 FG, 4-10 3Pt) and three blocks over 35 minutes during Sunday's 110-107 loss to the Knicks, the Warriors are thinking about holding Post out for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Draymond Green (back), who's expected to play Monday, and Kristaps Porzingis would be in line to share the center minutes if Post joins Al Horford (calf) on the sidelines.

items.headline: Post had 22 points (9-16 FG, 4-10 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists and three blocks over 35 minutes during Sunday's 110-107 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: With the Warriors extremely shorthanded, Post returned to the starting lineup Sunday after coming off the bench in Friday's loss to the Timberwolves. Even though he had the assignment of dealing with Karl-Anthony Towns, who posted a 17-point, 12-rebound double-double, Post still had a strong scoring line and delivered a new career-high mark in points while hitting the 20-point threshold for the first time this season. Post has scored in double digits in his last five starts. He could be a player worth keeping close tabs on, although his playing time will be tied to the availability of Draymond Green (back), Kristaps Porzingis (illness) and Al Horford (calf).

items.headline: Post will start Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Post enters the starting lineup due to Draymond Green (back), Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) being out of the lineup. In his last start, Post recorded 10 points, four rebounds, two assists and a steal in 25 minutes. He will be supplemented by recent addition Omer Yurtseven at the five Sunday.

items.headline: Post (ankle) is available for Sunday's game in New York.
items.story: Post will power through the ankle issue and make himself available for Sunday's game. Post and Omer Yurtseven will hold down the center spot Sunday with Draymond Green (back), Al Horford (calf) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) all unavailable.

items.headline: Post is questionable for Sunday's game versus the Knicks due to a sprained left ankle.
items.story: Post sustained the injury during Friday's loss to Minnesota, but it appears that he didn't come away with a high-grade sprain. The Warriors are already very thin down low, with Kristaps Porzingis (illness) and Al Horford (calf) both ruled out for Sunday, so they'd likely be left with Gui Santos and two-way player Malevy Leons to soak up the bulk of the center minutes if Post cannot play.

items.headline: Post won't return to Friday's game against Minnesota due to a left ankle sprain. He finished with seven points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 11 minutes.
items.story: Post will join fellow big men Draymond Green (back) and Al Horford (calf) on the sideline for the remainder of the contest, leaving Kristaps Porzingis and Gui Santos to pick up the slack. Post's next opportunity to play will come in New York on Sunday, but if available, he could be outside of the rotation so long as Green, Horford and Porzingis are able to suit up.

items.headline: Post (foot) is available for Friday's game against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Post was unable to play against the Bulls on Tuesday due to bilateral foot injury management, but the second-year pro has been given the green light to return for Friday's contest. Since the All-Star break, Post has averaged 6.9 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists over 19.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Post (foot) is questionable for Friday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Post is in danger of missing a second straight game while dealing with a foot injury. The team figures to monitor him closely during shootaround and leading up to warmups before issuing another update on his availability for Friday.

items.headline: Post has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Bulls due to bilateral foot soreness.
items.story: Post will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set, though his absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation with Al Horford and Kristaps Porzingis both available. Post's next chance to play will come Friday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Post is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Bulls due to bilateral foot soreness.
items.story: Post could sit out the second half of Golden State's back-to-back set Tuesday. Regardless of Post's status, Kristaps Porzingis and Al Horford are in line to share the center minutes Tuesday.

items.headline: Post will start Monday's game against the Jazz, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: After going unused off the bench in Saturday's loss to Oklahoma City, Post will step into the starting five Monday for the first time since Jan. 26. As a starter this season (32 games), the big man has averaged 9.1 points and 4.4 rebounds in 20.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Post (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Thursday in the Warriors' 121-110 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: After Post received single-digit minutes in three of his final four appearances before the All-Star break, the writing appeared to be on the wall for him to lose his rotation spot. The return of Kristaps Porzingis (Achilles) to action Thursday in what was his Warriors debut proved to be the final nail in the coffin for Post, who picked up his first DNP-CD of the season. So long as the Warriors have all of Al Horford, Draymond Green and Porzingis available in the frontcourt for a given game, Post looks like he'll face an uphill battle to find minutes.

items.headline: Youngblood supplied three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 3Pt) in seven minutes during Saturday's 112-90 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Youngblood earned his first minutes of the 2026-27 campaign after battling an ankle injury. Portland's backcourt is already loaded with Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson, but with Morant (hamstring) sidelined for an extended period, Youngblood could get some more run moving forward, although it shouldn't have much effect on the Blazers' rotation.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle) is available to play Saturday against the Jazz.
items.story: While Youngblood will be available for Saturday's game, that doesn't mean he'll get on the court. He's yet to log a single minute for Portland this season.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle) is questionable for Saturday's game against Utah.
items.story: Youngblood has yet to make his 2026-27 regular-season debut due to a left ankle injury. However, his potential absence wouldn't affect the rotation.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle/two-way player) is out for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: It's unclear at this time whether Youngblood is still dealing with an ankle injury, or if this decision is simply because he's on a two-way contract. Either way, he's yet to make his 2026-27 debut and will need to wait at least until Thursday against the Grizzlies to do so.

items.headline: Youngblood (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Youngblood will have to wait to make his 2026-27 season debut, and he'll miss a second consecutive game while dealing with left ankle soreness. His next chance to play will come against the Lakers on Tuesday, Nov. 27.

items.headline: Youngblood is out for Wednesday's regular-season opener against Phoenix due to left ankle soreness.
items.story: Youngblood missed Portland's final three preseason games due to left calf soreness, but now it's his left ankle that's giving him trouble. His next chance to play will come Friday in Sacramento.

items.headline: Youngblood (calf) won't play in Friday's preseason game versus the Warriors.
items.story: Youngblood will miss his third consecutive preseason contest due to lingering left calf soreness. It's unknown if he will be available for Opening Night versus Phoenix.

items.headline: Youngblood (calf) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Kings.
items.story: Youngblood will miss his second exhibition game in as many days due to left calf soreness. His final chance to play again in the preseason will come Friday against Golden State.

items.headline: Youngblood is out for Monday's exhibition against the London Lions with left calf soreness.
items.story: The two-way player is sitting out the first half of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play is Tuesday versus the Kings.

items.headline: Youngblood finished Monday's 111-84 Summer League win over the Timberwolves with 20 points (5-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and three assists across 19 minutes.
items.story: After shooting just 1-for-8 from deep in Sunday's overtime loss to Orlando, Youngblood was efficient from three-point range Monday en route to a team-high 20 points. He's scored at least 14 points in back-to-back contests after posting just eight points on 3-of-13 shooting in Friday's loss to the Suns. The 24-year-old guard is signed to a two-way contract and figures to spend most of his time with the G League's Rip City Remix in 2026-27.

items.headline: Youngblood totaled 14 points (5-14 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 29 minutes during Sunday's 112-105 Las Vegas Summer League overtime loss to the Magic.
items.story: Youngblood had a tough time getting his shot to drop, but that was true for most of his teammates, with Portland converting just 36.9 percent of its field goal attempts in the seven-point loss. Youngblood is on a two-way deal with the Trail Blazers, so he's expected to spend most of the 2026-27 season in the G League.

items.headline: Portland signed Youngblood to a two-way contract Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Youngblood has been a standout player for the Oklahoma City Blue in the G League. With this move, Youngblood is now likely to become a featured player for the Rip City Remix, but he may get some NBA looks with the Trail Blazers as well.

items.headline: Youngblood ended with five points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 116-106 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Youngblood played double-digit minutes for the first time this season, called upon to do more after Oklahoma City ruled out a number of players earlier in the day. Given his season averages of just 2.0 points in 5.4 minutes, there is no need to make any roster moves in fantasy based on this effort.

items.headline: Youngblood closed with three points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt), one rebound and one assist in 10 minutes during Wednesday's 138-89 victory over the Suns.
items.story: Youngblood continues to benefit from the fact that Oklahoma City is blowing opponents out on a regular basis. The majority of Youngblood's playing time has come during the final stretch of games, typically when the result has been decided. In 19 appearances, he has averaged 1.8 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Youngblood produced two points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds across four minutes during Tuesday's 126-107 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: The Thunder often blow out teams, allowing Youngblood and others to see a handful of minutes in garbage time. He's still pretty far off the fantasy radar, to be clear.

items.headline: Youngblood amassed three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt) over six minutes during Thursday's 141-135 double-overtime win over Indiana.
items.story: Youngblood didn't see any playing time during Tuesday's season-opening win over the Rockets in double overtime, but with the Thunder shorthanded Thursday, the two-way guard saw some action and scored his first NBA points. When Alex Caruso (concussion), Cason Wallace (knee), Isaiah Joe (knee) and Jalen Williams (wrist) return to action, Youngblood will likely be relegated to the G League.

items.headline: Youngblood signed a two-way contract with the Thunder on Saturday.
items.story: Youngblood played in six games for the Thunder during the preseason and averaged 11.0 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 20.7 minutes per game. He's likely to be a prominent player for the Oklahoma City Blue in the G League to open the 2025-26 season.

items.headline: Youngblood ended with five points (1-7 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT) across 25 minutes in Tuesday's 116-112 preseason win over the Bucks.
items.story: After posting an efficient 25 points in Saturday's loss to Indiana, Youngblood came back down to earth Tuesday. The undrafted 23-year-old out of Alabama signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Thunder in June and may receive consideration for the team's final two-way spot ahead of the 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Youngblood racked up 25 points (6-11 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 9-10 FT), five rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes during Saturday's 116-101 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: Youngblood was efficient in the shooting department while leading the way for his squad with major minutes off the bench. He shot 54.5 percent from the field and 44.4 percent from beyond the arc in a performance that will likely get the attention of the coaching staff.

items.headline: Youngblood produced 20 points (7-11 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one turnover in 21 minutes of Sunday's 135-114 preseason win over Charlotte.
items.story: Youngblood, who went undrafted in 2025, was a standout player at Alabama. The Thunder scooped him up on an Exhibit 10 deal, and he went on to make a strong impression at the Summer League. He's expected to suit up for the Oklahoma City Blue in the G League this season, but he's certainly making an impression on the coaching staff.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is available for Friday's game against Houston.
items.story: Marshall initially drew a questionable tag before being upgraded to probable Friday afternoon, and he's since been cleared to play following a two-game absence. The 28-year-old forward is averaging 13.7 points, 5.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals across 27.7 minutes per contest in three regular-season games (one start). With Marshall back in action, Caleb Martin and Zaccharie Risacher could see fewer minutes.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is probable for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Marshall is likely to return from a two-game absence Friday. Fewer minutes will likely be open for Zaccharie Risacher off the bench.

items.headline: Marshall is questionable for Friday's game against the Rockets due to an illness.
items.story: Marshall has a chance to return from a two-game absence Friday. Fewer minutes would be open for Zaccharie Risacher off the bench if Marshall is able to return.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) won't play in Wednesday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Marshall will now miss his second consecutive contest, meaning his next opportunity to suit up will come Friday against the Rockets. Without Marshall on the floor, Max Christie, Walter Clayton and Morez Johnson should each see a few extra minutes versus the Thunder.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is now doubtful for Wednesday against the Thunder.
items.story: Marshall was originally questionable, so he's trending in the wrong direction. With the Mavericks expected to hold him out, the team could rely more on Zaccharie Risacher.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Marshall is looking to return from an illness Wednesday. Zaccharie Risacher would likely play a larger role off the bench if Marshall remains sidelined.

items.headline: Marshall (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Marshall is under the weather and will be held out of Monday's road game, and his next chance to suit up will come when the Mavericks host the Thunder on Wednesday. With the 28-year-old forward unavailable, Zaccharie Risacher and Marcus Sasser could see increased burn.

items.headline: Marshall posted 10 points (4-8 FG, 1-1 3PT, 1-3 FT), five assists, four rebounds and one steal over 21 minutes during Saturday's 122-106 loss to the Spurs.
