items.headline: Reed notched 15 points (7-11 FG, 1-1 FT), nine rebounds, one block and one steal over 19 minutes during Saturday's 126-110 win over Chicago.
items.story: Reed shifted back to the bench with Jalen Duren returning from a two-game suspension. Despite the demotion, Reed still managed to put up a solid performance, continuing what has been a fantastic two-week period. In four games during that span, he has averaged 16.8 points, 6.0 rebounds and 3.3 combined steals and blocks, good enough for top 20 value in nine-category leagues.

items.headline: Reed won't start against the Bulls on Saturday.
items.story: With Jalen Duren (suspension) back in the lineup, Reed will retreat to the second unit. The big man has averaged 8.8 points and 4.5 rebounds across 16.5 minutes per game in four appearances off the bench this month.

items.headline: Reed registered 18 points (7-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 29 minutes during the Pistons' 126-111 win over the Knicks on Thursday.
items.story: Reed put together a nice stat line during Thursday's win, finishing as the Pistons' third-leading rebounder and second in points behind Cade Cunningham (42). Reed has started in each of the Pistons' last two games but will likely revert to a bench role against the Bulls on Saturday since Jalen Duren will be available to return after serving a two-game suspension. That said, Reed should see an elevated role off the bench in the short term as Isaiah Stewart (suspension) will not be eligible to return until March 3.

items.headline: Reed produced 22 points (10-17 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, three assists, four blocks and three steals across 33 minutes during Wednesday's 113-95 win over the Raptors.
items.story: With Jalen Duren and Isaiah Stewart both suspended in the wake of Monday's brawl with the Hornets, Reed made his first start since Jan. 10. He delivered a dominant defensive performance while producing his best scoring effort since Nov. 12, when he erupted for a season-high 28 against the Bulls. Duren is set to miss only one more game, but Stewart has been shelved until March 3, so Reed should see elevated usage into next month. The 26-year-old center has scored in double digits in three straight games, averaging 15.3 points, 4.7 boards, 2.7 assists, 2.0 steals, 2.0 blocks and 1.0 threes.

items.headline: Holiday tallied 17 points (7-11 FG, 3-4 3Pt), eight rebounds, 10 assists and a steal across 29 minutes in Monday's 118-110 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Holiday delivered an excellent all-around performance off the bench, finishing just two rebounds shy of a triple-double. His 10 assists highlighted his importance as a facilitator, while efficient perimeter shooting further boosted his fantasy production. Holiday's ability to contribute across several categories provides considerable value, although his reserve role could lead to occasional fluctuations in playing time and overall production. He should be fine as long as his minutes hover around the 25-30 range.

items.headline: Holiday registered 22 points (8-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Holiday gave Portland a big lift off the bench. The veteran guard's scoring and defensive versatility have given the Blazers one of the league's deepest backcourts. His role should stay prominent with Shaedon Sharpe (knee) out.

items.headline: Holiday (hand) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Holiday sat out Friday's preseason finale due to right hand soreness, though he'll return to action in Wednesday's regular-season opener. The veteran guard appears likely to begin the season with the second unit, and he faces competition for playing time from Scoot Henderson and Vit Krejci.

items.headline: Holiday is out for Friday's preseason finale against the Warriors due to right hand soreness.
items.story: The 36-year-old veteran will skip Portland's final exhibition game with some soreness in his shooting hand, but this shouldn't be anything that impacts his status for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Suns. With Holiday unavailable, expect more minutes for Scoot Henderson and Vit Krejci.

items.headline: Holiday supplied 11 points (4-11 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-3 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 110-98 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Holiday's shot wasn't cooperating, but he still reached double figures. It will be a close call between Holiday and Ja Morant in deciding who will run alongside Damian Lillard in the first unit, but most expect Morant to edge out Holiday to start the season.

items.headline: Holiday won't start Tuesday's preseason game against the Kings, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Holiday got the starting nod in Monday's blowout win over the London Lions, though he'll slide to the second unit in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Damian Lillard, Scoot Henderson, Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan will start against Sacramento.

items.headline: Holiday finished with six points (3-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds and three assists across 15 minutes in Monday's 119-66 preseason victory over the London Lions.
items.story: The veteran point guard got the start in place of the resting Damian Lillard on Monday. Holiday is expected to handle a reserve role once the regular season begins, but he could still push to play 30 minutes per game while Shaedon Sharpe (knee) is on the shelf.

items.headline: Holiday won't start Wednesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jason Quick of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Holiday has been a full-time starter for most of his career, though he isn't guaranteed to begin the 2026-27 campaign in a starting role. The Trail Blazers will start Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, Toumani Camara, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan in their preseason opener.

items.headline: Holiday is expected to spend more time on the wing this season, per Ramona Shelburne of ESPN.com.
items.story: The veteran point guard averaged 16.3 points and 6.1 assists per game last year, his most since 2022-23 with the Bucks, but Holiday is likely to see fewer ballhandling responsibilities now that Ja Morant and Damian Lillard are manning the backcourt. Toumani Camara is the favorite to start at small forward for Portland, but Holiday is positioned for a very significant role off the bench and is worthy of a late-round fantasy pick. He should remain a major threat from deep after hitting a career-high 2.6 three-pointers per game in 2025-26.

items.headline: Holiday is in danger of handling a lesser role in 2026-27 after Portland acquired Ja Morant in a trade this summer.
items.story: Additionally, it remains to be seen how the Trail Blazers will choose to deploy the returning Damian Lillard (Achilles) next year. Holiday is coming off a resurgent 2025-26 regular season, averaging 16.3 points, 6.1 assists, 4.6 rebounds and 1.0 steals per game in 53 appearances, so he at least appears to be the early favorite to start at shooting guard. Shaedon Sharpe and Scoot Henderson will also be battling for key roles, further making Holiday's fantasy forecast difficult to predict.

items.headline: Holiday supplied eight points (3-14 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds and seven assists across 40 minutes during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Holiday couldn't find the bottom of the basket in the Game 5 loss. He made a decent contribution in secondary categories, but the backcourt combo of Holiday and Scoot Henderson was anemic in the scoring column. Holiday is still under contract with Portland for another year, so he's expected to return to the team and continue with the first unit. Over 53 regular-season games, Holiday averaged 16.3 points, 6.1 assists, 4.6 rebounds and 1.0 steals.

items.headline: Holiday notched 29 points (12-18 FG, 5-9 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and four steals in 41 minutes during Friday's 120-108 loss to San Antonio in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: The veteran guard led the Blazers in scoring on the night, but it wasn't enough to pick up a win even with Victor Wembanyama (concussion) sidelined for the visitors. Holiday is averaging a whopping 38.7 minutes a game to begin the series, with the 35-year-old turning that workload into averages of 18.0 points, 8.3 assists, 5.0 boards, 2.7 threes and 2.0 steals per contest, and he'll likely be leaned on heavily again in Game 4 on Sunday.

items.headline: Holiday logged 16 points (6-17 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine assists, five rebounds, two blocks and one steal across 39 minutes in Tuesday's 106-103 Game 2 win over the Spurs in the first round of the playoffs.
items.story: The veteran guard struggled with efficiency in the win but still finished as Portland's second-leading scorer behind Scoot Henderson (31 points). Holiday has shot just 31.3 percent from the field through two first-round outings, though the 35-year-old led all players in assists Tuesday and has dished out 20 dimes in the series. He also tied the game-high mark in blocks in Game 2.

items.headline: Holiday posted nine points (4-15 FG, 1-7 3Pt), four rebounds, 11 assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Sunday's 111-98 loss to San Antonio in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: It's the second time in seven April contests that the veteran point guard has dished double-digit assists. Holiday's production has been inconsistent this month, and during that seven-game stretch, he's averaging 17.3 points, 6.9 assists, 5.6 boards and 2.9 threes while shooting just 38.3 percent from the floor and 31.7 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Holiday chipped in 23 points (8-18 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and one block in 33 minutes during Sunday's 122-110 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Holiday posted a strong stat line in the regular-season finale, and he's been one of the most consistent players for Portland all season long. The veteran floor general, who figures to play a big role for the Blazers in their postseason run as they'll attempt to get past the Play-In Tournament, averaged 16.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 6.1 assists per game in 53 appearances (51 starts) in the regular season. Those numbers are an upgrade compared to what he had done in his previous two seasons with the Celtics.

items.headline: Holiday chipped in 19 points (7-19 FG, 5-12 3Pt), six rebounds and 11 assists across 39 minutes during Monday's 137-132 overtime loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Although the team has adjusted the starting lineup to include Scoot Henderson in recent weeks, Holiday's numbers haven't suffered. He's averaged 21.8 points, 6.0 assists, and 4.5 rebounds since the recent adjustment, and it's a scenario that should stay in place as long as Shaedon Sharpe (calf) and Jerami Grant (calf) remain absent. Before Monday's loss, the new-look backcourt had generated three consecutive victories.

items.headline: Holiday ended with 27 points (10-22 FG, 7-15 3Pt), five rebounds, nine assists and one steal over 37 minutes during Thursday's 118-106 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: The 27 points led all scorers on the night as Holiday continues to fill up the bucket from downtown. The veteran guard has drained at least three three-pointers in five straight games, averaging 20.8 points, 4.8 assists, 4.8 threes, 4.2 boards and 1.0 steals over that surge while shooting 49.0 percent (24-for-49) from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Holiday totaled 30 points (10-21 FG, 7-15 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists and two steals in 32 minutes during Tuesday's 114-104 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Holiday took control on the offensive end and led the Blazers in scoring and made treys. He did so in an efficient manner by drilling 46.7 of his attempts from beyond the arc, and he fell one triple shy of tying his season high in three-point makes. Holiday isn't at the stage in his career where he's able to supply this type of pop on a nightly basis, but he still has a few elite performances in the tank.

items.headline: Holiday ended with 23 points (8-19 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 35 minutes during Friday's 100-93 loss to Dallas.
items.story: The 23 points led the Blazers on the night, as Holiday topped 20 points for the first time since March 13. The veteran point guard's usage has been a little inconsistent this month, but over his last 14 games he's drained multiple three-pointers nine times, averaging 16.2 points, 6.1 assists, 4.4 boards, 2.8 threes and 0.8 steals in March.

items.headline: Holiday provided 13 points (4-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 130-99 win over the Bucks.
items.story: The veteran guard has now failed to reach the 20-point marker in seven straight contests after accomplishing this feat in six of his prior seven outings. Over his past seven appearances, Holiday has averaged 10.9 points, 6.0 assists, 4.9 rebounds and 2.0 three-pointers in 28.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Holiday ended Friday's 108-104 victory over Minnesota with 12 points (5-17 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds and 12 assists across 32 minutes.
items.story: This was the fourth straight game in which Holiday was unable to surpass the 15-point mark, and the fifth time he's done that over the last six. The veteran floor general kicked off March in style with four straight outings with at least 20 points, but his numbers have plummeted since then. Over his last six appearances, Holiday is averaging 12.0 points, 6.7 assists and 4.2 boards per game while shooting 39.2 percent from the floor. That's a marked downgrade compared to the 24.8 points, 7.0 assists and 4.5 boards while shooting 58.7 percent from the floor in his first four outings of the month.

items.headline: Holiday closed Friday's 124-114 win over the Jazz with 25 points (10-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, eight assists, one block and one steal over 32 minutes.
items.story: Portland's backcourt led the way in the victory, as Holiday and Scoot Henderson each delivered a team-high 25 points. It was a reassuring bounce-back effort for Holiday after he managed only four points in Tuesday's loss to the Hornets, but that game was the only time so far in March that the veteran point guard has scored fewer than 20 points. Through six games this month, he's averaging 21.3 points, 6.8 assists, 4.0 boards, 3.7 threes and 0.8 steals while shooting 56.3 percent from the floor and a blistering 51.2 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Holiday finished Friday's 106-99 loss to Houston with 20 points (8-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 10 assists, four rebounds and one steal over 37 minutes.
items.story: Holiday finished as Friday's leader in assists and as the Trail Blazers' second-leading scorer behind Jerami Grant (21 points). Holiday has posted double-doubles in back-to-back games and is up to six on the season. He's also scored at least 20 points in five of his last six outings, and over that span he has averaged 22.5 points on 52.0 percent shooting, 6.7 assists, 4.3 rebounds, 3.0 threes and 1.2 steals over 32.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Karaban closed Tuesday's 130-103 loss to the Spurs with zero points (0-1 FG), one rebound and one assist across 11 minutes.
items.story: Karaban received his first meaningful rotation minutes of the season but failed to score on his lone field-goal attempt. The rookie forward entered the game during the first half as Sacramento searched for additional floor spacing, though he was unable to make much of an impact. Karaban remains outside the regular rotation and holds little fantasy value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Karaban finished with seven points (2-3 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal in 20 minutes during Thursday's 114-110 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Karaban made the most of his limited scoring opportunities, converting both attempts from beyond the arc while contributing in several other categories. The rookie forward also committed two turnovers but demonstrated the perimeter shooting ability that could help him compete for a reserve role in Sacramento. His regular-season fantasy appeal remains limited until he establishes consistent playing time.

items.headline: The Kings signed Ben Simmons to a one-year deal Friday, adding another bench option who will challenge Karaban for playing time.
items.story: Simmons will return to The Association after sitting out the 2025-26 campaign. With the three-time All-Star in the mix, Karaban faces increased competition for playing time off the bench. Karaban, the No. 29 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, could see increasingly steady minutes as the season progresses, though the UConn product isn't guaranteed a meaningful role early on, especially if Keegan Murray (ankle) is healthy to begin the campaign.

items.headline: Karaban finished Friday's 92-90 Summer League win over Charlotte with 14 points (6-12 FG, 2-8 3Pt), three assists and two rebounds over 35 minutes.
items.story: It was a bit of an inconsistent performance from Karaban, who scored seven points in both the first and third quarters but did not score in the other two frames. He still finished tied with Jonathan Mogbo as the Kings' second-leading scorer behind Emanuel Sharp (16 points). The Kings acquired Karaban from the Cavaliers after he was selected by Cleveland with the No. 29 pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, but the UConn product's playing time in his rookie season could be limited if he's behind De'Andre Hunter (eye) and Nique Clifford (rest) on the depth chart after the preseason.

items.headline: Karaban posted 21 points (7-15 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds and a steal across 27 minutes in Wednesday's 82-76 Summer League loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Karaban endured a slow start to the Summer League, scoring just seven points on 3-for-15 shooting across his first three appearances. However, he bounced back admirably here and showed a glimpse of what he can do on both ends of the court after ending just two boards shy of a double-double. The 29th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and former UConn star is expected to fight for a rotation spot during training camp.

items.headline: Karaban went scoreless (0-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt) with two rebounds, one assist and one block in 24 minutes during Thursday's 91-85 Summer League win over the Clippers.
items.story: Although the former UConn standout missed all six of his field-goal attempts, he finished with a team-best plus-12 and continued to provide solid positional defense. He wasn't even supposed to be ready in time for this game due to an ankle sprain, so it's not worth overreacting to his scoreless outing.

items.headline: Karaban (ankle) is available for Thursday's Summer League game against the Clippers, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Karaban was initially expected to miss this game, but he progressed quicker than anticipated. The No. 29 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft could be heavily featured during the Summer League.

items.headline: Karaban sustained a sprained right ankle in Thursday's practice and will be re-evaluated in one week, Kayla Anderson of Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Karaban won't play in the California Classic Summer League due to the ankle injury. His next chance to suit up will come in the NBA Summer League game against the Wizards on July 12.

items.headline: Karaban left Thursday's practice after suffering an ankle injury, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Karaban appeared to roll his ankle near the end of Thursday's practice, per Nunes, and he was unable to return. He can be considered day-to-day leading up to Sacramento's first Summer League game against Brooklyn on Saturday.

items.headline: The Cavaliers selected Karaban with the No. 29 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and traded his rights to the Kings, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: The Cavaliers received the No. 34 overall pick and future second-round picks in the deal. Karaban appeared in 151 regular-season games for UConn, averaging 12.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.0 blocks and 0.7 steals across 32.5 minutes per contest. The 23-year-old is a proven winner, helping the Huskies capture two NCAA championships. His athleticism is a concern, though his positive attributes make up for most of his shortcomings. It's unknown what the future holds for Sacramento's veterans, specifically, Domantas Sabonis (knee), De'Andre Hunter (eye) and DeMar DeRozan (hamstring). If those players aren't on the roster during the 2026-27 campaign, Karaban could see plenty of action. However, if they stay, it will be more difficult for Karaban to receive consistent minutes.

items.headline: Cissoko accumulated six points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and four assists across 20 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Cissoko provided a modest contribution off the bench, matching his scoring output with solid playmaking in 20 minutes. The 22-year-old wing has an opportunity to establish himself as a regular contributor in Portland's rotation, though his limited scoring opportunities and lack of defensive production Tuesday highlight his modest fantasy ceiling.

items.headline: Cissoko finished with 13 points (5-5 FG, 3-3 3Pt), three assists, two rebounds and two steals across 15 minutes in Monday's 119-66 preseason victory over the London Lions.
items.story: Cissoko maximized his minutes Monday, turning in a perfect shooting performance. He's auditioning for a spot in Portland's Opening Night rotation, contending mainly with Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan for playing time.

items.headline: Cissoko produced 11 points (4-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds and three steals across 20 minutes during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Cissoko began the season on a two-way contract before earning a two-year standard deal with the Trail Blazers. He appeared in 75 regular-season contests, posting averages of 5.1 points, 2.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.8 three-pointers in 19.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cissoko will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee.
items.story: Cissoko filled in for Jerami Grant last time out, but Grant is back in action, so Cissoko will come off the bench. Cissoko is averaging 4.6 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game as a reserve this season.

items.headline: Cissoko will start in Sunday's game against Denver.
items.story: Jerami Grant (foot) is unavailable, so Cissoko will occupy a spot in the starting lineup. The 21-year-old has averaged 7.4 points, 3.1 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.4 blocks and 0.8 steals in 24 starts this season.

items.headline: Cissoko tallied 14 points (6-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block across 17 minutes Friday in the Trail Blazers' 124-114 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Cissoko saw a streak of 10 consecutive appearances come to an end when he went unused off the bench in the Trail Blazers' two-point loss to the Hornets on Tuesday, but he was able to reclaim a spot in the rotation Friday while Robert Williams (knee) sat out. Cissoko fared well during his time on the court, but he may nonetheless find himself back outside of the rotation Sunday in Philadelphia if Williams is cleared to play.

items.headline: Cissoko (illness) is available for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Cissoko has been dealing with an illness of late, but he will continue to suit up despite the ailment. It should be noted that Cissoko was limited to just seven minutes during Saturday's loss to the Hornets despite averaging 21.6 minutes per game this season, which was likely a result of the illness.

items.headline: Cissoko (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Cissoko is in jeopardy of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set after recording zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT) and one assist over seven minutes during Saturday's loss to the Hornets. If the 21-year-old forward joins Deni Avdija (back) and Robert Williams (knee) on the sidelines, Kris Murray, Matisse Thybulle and Vit Krejci would be candidates to see increased minutes.

items.headline: Cissoko (illness) will play Saturday against the Hornets.
items.story: Cissoko will shake off a questionable tag for this contest. Over his last four games, he's averaging 2.0 points, 1.8 assists and 1.5 rebounds in 16.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cissoko (illness) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Cissoko is in danger of missing his second game in February while battling through an illness. The third-year pro is averaging 21.8 minutes per game this season, and those minutes would likely be absorbed by Matisse Thybulle and Kris Murray if Cissoko is unable to play.

items.headline: Cissoko will come off the bench for Friday's game versus the Nuggets.
items.story: Deni Avdija (back) is set to return after a one-game absence, so Cissoko will retreat to the second unit. As a reserve this season, Cissoko has posted averages of 5.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers signed Cissoko to a two-year contract Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Cissoko, who was previously on a two-way contract, quickly burned through his eligibility with some standout play on the defensive end. Across 50 appearances, he's played 22.3 minutes per contest with 6.5 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 0.8 steals.

items.headline: Cissoko will startin Thursday's game against Utah.
items.story: Cissoko will receive an opportunity to run with the starters Thursday after being a healthy inactive for Wednesday's loss to to the Timberwolves. The 21-year-old contributed across the board in his most recent start against the Grizzlies this past Saturday, when he finished with seven points, 10 rebounds, four assists and two steals in 33 minutes. With Cissoko set to be active for his 50th game of the season Thursday, he'll be ineligible to suit up for the Trail Blazers for the remainder of the campaign unless Portland upgrades him from a two-way deal to a standard NBA contract.

items.headline: Cissoko (two-way) was a healthy inactive Wednesday in the Trail Blazers' 133-109 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Cissoko has been a mainstay in the Portland rotation throughout the season, but because he's been active for 49 games this season, he's eligible to suit up just one more time this season while he remains signed to a two-way contract. Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland posits that Portland likely opted to keep Cissoko inactive Wednesday in order to use his final game of eligibility in its matchup with the Jazz on Thursday, when players such as Deni Avdija, Robert Williams and Scoot Henderson could be candidates to rest in the second leg of a back-to-back set. After Thursday's game, the Trail Blazers would then likely upgrade Cissoko to a standard contract to ensure he's available to play following the All-Star break.

items.headline: Cissoko isn't in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Cissoko will retreat to the bench with Deni Avdija (back) cleared to play Monday evening. Cissoko has managed to provide a decent scoring boost in his previous three appearances as a reserve, averaging 12.0 points in 24.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cissoko will start against the Grizzlies on Saturday.
items.story: With Deni Avdija (back) and Shaedon Sharpe (calf) sidelined, Cissoko will return to the starting five. As a starter this season (22 games), the two-way player has averaged 7.4 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists across 24.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cissoko is not in the Trail Blazers' starting lineup against the Suns on Tuesday.
items.story: Cissoko is coming off a 15-point performance in Sunday's loss against the Cavaliers in what was his 22nd start of the season (and 10th start in the Trail Blazers' last 13 games). However, the third-year pro will come off the bench for Tuesday's game due to the return of Jrue Holiday (personal).

items.headline: Cissoko supplied 15 points (5-9 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals across 32 minutes during Sunday's 130-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: The Trail Blazers put Cissoko back in the starting lineup after giving Deni Avdija (back) two opportunities to get back up to speed. Cissoko's role will decrease dramatically once Avdija is 100 percent, but Portland's All-Star forward may be hindered by a minute restriction once he returns and could sit occasionally leading up to the break. Cissoko's continued production is entirely dependent on Avdija's status.

items.headline: Cissoko will start Sunday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Cissoko will enter the starting lineup due to Jrue Holiday (personal) and Deni Avdija (back) being out. With the team shorthanded, he could be in line for increased usage, considering he is coming off his highest scoring game of the new year and has seen at least 25 minutes in each of his last four starts.

items.headline: Cissoko won't start against the Wizards on Tuesday.
items.story: With Deni Avdija (back) returning to the lineup, Cissoko will retreat to the second unit. In 21 games off the bench so far this season, the 21-year-old forward has averaged 5.3 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 18.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cissoko will start against the Raptors on Friday, Danny Marang of 1080 The Fan Portland reports.
items.story: With Deni Avdija (back) sidelined for the second leg of this back-to-back set, Cissoko will rejoin the starting lineup. As a starter this month (seven games), the two-way player has averaged 7.0 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 25.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cissoko isn't in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Cissoko will move to a bench role with the Blazers finally getting healthy. He was a solid contributor offensively in his last appearance as a reserve, dropping 14 points on 5-for-8 from the field Jan. 5 against Utah.

items.headline: Cissoko (illness) is available for Thursday's game against Miami, Danny Marang of 1080 The Fan Portland reports.
items.story: Cissoko was upgraded to probable a few hours before tipoff, and he's now been cleared to take the court despite dealing with an illness. He's drawn seven straight starts for the Blazers and is averaging 7.0 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 25.3 minutes during that stretch.

items.headline: Cissoko (illness) has been upgraded to probable for Thursday's game versus the Heat.
items.story: It sounds like Cissoko is feeling better and will get out there for Thursday's game. However, with Jerami Grant (Achilles) and Jrue Holiday (calf) also expected to play, there will be fewer minutes available for Cissoko.

items.headline: Cissoko is questionable for Thursday's game against the Heat due to an illness.
items.story: Cissoko is feeling under the weather, but the Trail Blazers should have a better idea whether he'll be able to play following morning shootaround Thursday. He's started in each of Portland's last seven games and is averaging 7.0 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.1 three-pointers, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 25.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cissoko finished Sunday's 117-110 victory over the Kings with eight points (2-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 34 minutes.
items.story: Cissoko drew another start Sunday with Jerami Grant (Achilles) downgraded to out shortly before tipoff. However, Cissoko wasn't all that sharp and was the only starter to be held to single figures in the scoring column. He added some production on the defensive end but has otherwise struggled, averaging 7.0 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals over his last seven games.

items.headline: Cissoko ended with six points (2-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 22 minutes during Thursday's 117-101 win over Atlanta.
items.story: Cissoko remained with the starters despite the return of Jerami Grant, as Deni Avdija (back) missed his second straight contest. Cissoko's fantasy appeal is limited to very deep leagues for the moment, as he's averaging 6.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 22.7 minutes over his last eight outings.

items.headline: Cissoko notched 13 points (4-4 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), one rebound, one assist and three steals in 22 minutes during Friday's 111-105 win over the Rockets.
items.story: Cissoko started his second straight game, and after going scoreless in his first opportunity Wednesday, he bounced back nicely in this contest. He's trending up in deeper formats, posting averages of 8.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.9 three-pointers in 22.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cissoko is in the Trail Blazers' starting lineup against the Rockets on Wednesday.
items.story: Cissoko will make his 13th start of the season Wednesday due to the absence of Kris Murray (back). Over his last five outings (two starts), Cissoko has averaged 10.2 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 2.6 threes, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks over 23.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cissoko is not in the Trail Blazers' starting lineup against the Pelicans on Friday.
items.story: Cissoko has started each of the Trail Blazers' last two games, but he'll cede his spot in the starting five to Kris Murray on Friday. Across 17 appearances off the bench this season, Cissoko has averaged 4.6 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 18.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cissoko closed with 19 points (7-10 FG, 5-7 3Pt), one rebound, two assists and one block in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 124-95 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Making his second straight start with both Jerami Grant (Achilles) and Matisse Thybulle (thumb) still missing from the Portland frontcourt, Cissoko led the team in scoring while setting a new career high in made three-pointers in a game. The third-year forward is seeing a consistent role in an NBA rotation for the first time, and through 14 contests (six starts) in December, he averaged 7.5 points, 2.4 boards, 1.6 assists, 1.4 threes and 1.0 combined steals and blocks in 23.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cissoko will start Monday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Cissoko is in line for his first start since Dec. 7 after Kris Murray (quadriceps) was ruled out for Monday's clash. Cissoko is averaging 6.6 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists in his last 10 appearances as a starter.

items.headline: Cissoko contributed 16 points (3-8 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 10-13 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Monday's 110-102 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Cissoko's offense comes and goes, but he saw more usage on that end with Jerami Grant (Achilles) sidelined Monday. Through nine December appearances, Cissoko holds averages of 7.3 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.5 three-pointers in 25.8 minutes.

items.headline: Cissoko closed Thursday's 143-120 loss to the Pelicans with 20 points (8-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one block in 32 minutes.
items.story: The Trail Blazers adjusted their starting lineup for this game, and Cissoko moved back to a bench role in favor of Shaedon Sharpe, who's been playing well since returning from injury. However, Cissoko responded by posting his best scoring output of the season. Cissoko has scored in double digits just three times in 2025-26, but he's worth a look in deeper formats as long as he's able to play around 25 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Cissoko will come off the bench Thursday night against New Orleans.
items.story: Cissoko will retreat to a bench role for the first time since Nov. 18 after making 10 straight starts for the Blazers. However, there may still be plenty of chances for Cissoko with Portland shorthanded in the frontcourt Thursday.

items.headline: Cissoko racked up six points (2-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt), four rebounds and one block in 24 minutes during Sunday's 119-96 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Sunday was another pedestrian effort by Cissoko, who's been unable to turn heads since joining the starting lineup in November. The forward is averaging just 6.6 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.3 three-pointers in 23.3 minutes per game across his last 10 contests, so fantasy managers can likely find more appealing streaming options on most waiver wires.

items.headline: Cissoko contributed five points (1-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block across 21 minutes during Sunday's 123-115 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Despite starting in his sixth consecutive game, Cissoko has turned in yet another relatively unproductive stat line. Cissoko is averaging 6.5 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.2 blocks when he starts, but he will look to bounce back offensively Tuesday against the Raptors.

items.headline: Cissoko supplied five points (2-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds and two steals in 22 minutes during Wednesday's 122-121 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Cissoko moved into the starting lineup due to absences to Jrue Holiday (calf) and Shaedon Sharpe (calf). However, it was Deni Avdija who shouldered the bulk of the responsibility, not the replacement guards. There is no reason to consider Cissoko a pickup in standard formats at this point.

items.headline: Cissoko is part of the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Cissoko will start for the first time in his three-year NBA career. The 21-year-old has logged double-digit minutes in six straight games, and he logged eight points, five assists and two steals across 28 minutes in his most recent outing.

items.headline: Cissoko posted eight points (2-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals in 28 minutes during Tuesday's 127-110 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Cissoko was likely in for a longer period of time due to the blowout nature of the game, and he is not expected to see anywhere near 28 minutes consistently in the future unless injury or blowouts occur. In his last eight games, Cissoko is averaging 3.4 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.5 steals across 14.5 minutes.

items.headline: Cissoko totaled five points (2-2 FG, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and two steals across 14 minutes during Monday's 123-115 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: With Blake Wesley suffering a fifth metatarsal fracture in his right foot, Cissoko is the next man up for Portland, at least while Scoot Henderson (hamstring) is out. Cissoko has just 36 career regular-season games under his belt, but he made a strong impression on the coaching staff Monday and could be worth monitoring in very deep formats.

items.headline: Cissoko racked up 20 points (7-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block across 27 minutes during Saturday's 96-86 Summer League loss against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Cissoko got it done on both ends of the floor Saturday, as he was one of two players to crack the 18-point mark while also recording a game-high three steals. The 20-year-old guard played in five regular-season games for Portland during the 2024-25 campaign, averaging 2.0 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists across 12 minutes per game.

items.headline: Cissoko closed with seven points (3-7 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four assists, two rebounds, one block and one steal over 29 minutes during Sunday's 109-81 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: Cissoko recorded season-high marks in points and minutes during the regular-season finale. The 21-year-old had a rollercoaster season, being traded twice before eventually being waived and signing a two-year, two-way contract with Portland. Cissoko appeared in 22 regular-season games between Portland and San Antonio this season, averaging 1.5 points, 1.0 rebounds and 0.7 assists across 5.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Kessler supplied 16 points (6-6 FG, 4-4 FT), 15 rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal over 31 minutes during Sunday's 131-125 win over the Raptors.
items.story: It was the fifth-year center's second straight double-double, and the fifth time in seven games to begin his Lakers tenure that Kessler recorded multiple blocks. He's been healthy and productive so far for his new team, averaging 14.3 points, 9.9 boards, 2.9 blocks, 1.1 assists and 1.0 steals in 30.6 minutes while shooting 75.4 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Kessler finished Friday's 112-95 loss to the Warriors with 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-3 FT), 13 rebounds, two assists and five blocks across 31 minutes.
items.story: Kessler had one of his best defensive efforts of the season, posting a double-double with 13 rebounds and five blocks. The center was one of the few Lakers to finish with a positive plus-minus, and his rim protection remains a key piece of the starting lineup. He'll look to build on that Sunday against the Raptors.

items.headline: Kessler registered 13 points (6-9 FG, 1-4 FT), eight rebounds, two blocks and one steal over 33 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Kessler was solid in the loss, scoring on six of nine shots over 33 minutes. The center's free-throw shooting was an issue again, but his rim protection remains key to the Lakers' starting lineup.

items.headline: Kessler racked up 22 points (10-14 FG, 2-5 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, six blocks and three steals across 35 minutes during Friday's 125-117 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Kessler followed up his perfect debut with another dominant showing, adding six blocks and three steals to his 22 points.  The Lakers gave up a bundle of draft picks to land the 7-foot-2 center from Utah, and he'll get a shot at his former team Sunday.

items.headline: Kessler delivered 26 points (12-12 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds, an assist and two blocks across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 127-105 win over the Warriors.
items.story: There was a lot of talk about how Luka Doncic and Kessler would thrive playing together, and while one game isn't enough to draw conclusions, this was an impressive performance from the big man. He made all 12 of his field-goal attempts, posting an unusually productive scoring performance for a player whose fantasy value typically centers on rebounds, blocks and efficiency. His 30-minute workload was particularly encouraging, suggesting a prominent role in Los Angeles' frontcourt. Although his scoring output is unlikely to be this high consistently, his combination of rebounding, rim protection and efficient finishing gives him a solid fantasy foundation, especially if he develops a rapport with the playmaking of Doncic and Austin Reaves.

items.headline: Kessler (finger) is available for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Kessler suffered a finger injury during training camp but was cleared to suit up in the preseason. The 25-year-old averaged a career-high 14.4 points along with 10.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.4 steals over 30.8 minutes per contest in 2025-26. However, he was limited to five regular-season games due to a shoulder injury.

items.headline: Kessler logged 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in 16 minutes during Tuesday's 101-89 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Kessler made an immediate impact in his Lakers debut after missing the first three exhibitions with a finger injury. Golden State grabbed only two offensive rebounds before halftime and 13 after the break, when Kessler was on the bench, which shows why the Lakers paid $130 million for him.

items.headline: Kessler (finger) will play in Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Kessler jammed his finger during training camp but has been cleared to make his 2026 preseason debut Tuesday. The big man appeared in just five regular-season games with Utah in 2025-26 due to a shoulder injury and will look to bounce back in his first year with the Lakers.

items.headline: Kessler (finger) was a full participant in Sunday's practice, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Kessler has yet to suit up in the preseason after jamming his finger during training camp, though the injury isn't viewed as a long-term concern. The big man can be considered questionable for Tuesday's exhibition against the Warriors until the Lakers provide an update on his status.

items.headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Kessler participated in Saturday's practice but didn't do live work, though the center might scrimmage Sunday, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: If Kessler scrimmages Sunday and everything goes according to plan, the big man could make his Lakers debut Tuesday against Golden State. Kessler jammed his finger early in training camp and has missed three straight games, but by all accounts, it's not a long-term issue.

items.headline: Kessler (finger) won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Kings, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Kessler will miss a third consecutive contest due to a finger injury, though head coach JJ Redick isn't concerned that it's a long-term issue, per Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com. The big man's next opportunity to play in the preseason will come Tuesday against the Warriors.

items.headline: Kessler (finger) won't play in Tuesday's exhibition game against the Warriors, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
items.story: Kessler will miss a second consecutive preseason game after jamming his finger during training camp. The big man will aim to make his preseason debut Thursday at home against the Kings, but the Lakers will take a cautious approach to keep the injury from lingering into the regular season.

items.headline: Kessler is out for Monday's exhibition against the Kings due to a finger injury, Dan Woike of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Kessler jammed his finger at camp and will now miss Monday's preseason opener, which will be the first game of a back-to-back set. There's a chance Kessler could be held out of Tuesday's game in Golden State as well, but it's unlikely that this will be something that lingers into the regular season.

items.headline: Kessler (shoulder) is fully healthy and has been cleared for the start of the season, according to Lakers president Rob Pelinka, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Kessler underwent shoulder surgery back in November, but Pelinka said the big man is looking forward to playing in a lot of games this year. The 25-year-old appears on track to enter training camp without restrictions and should have a prominent role in Los Angeles' frontcourt, with Luka Doncic setting him up with easy looks.

items.headline: Monk registered 24 points (9-14 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, seven assists and one block across 30 minutes during Monday's 115-100 win over Dallas.
items.story: Monk delivered one of Sacramento's best offensive performances, finishing one point behind Darius Acuff for the team lead while knocking down five triples. He also paced the Kings with seven assists and posted a game-high plus-27 rating. Monk's combination of perimeter scoring and playmaking makes him an intriguing fantasy option when he receives this level of playing time, although his production could fluctuate in Sacramento's crowded backcourt.

items.headline: Monk racked up three points (1-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt), two rebounds and six assists across 13 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Monk has yet to play more than 13 minutes in any game this season, leaving him well outside the top 350 in standard leagues. Despite a proven ability to be a solid contributor, it appears as though Sacramento has other ideas when it comes to allowing him to play meaningful basketball. He should remain on watchlists, just in case the tide turns at any point. For now, he can be safely ignored in all formats.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is available for Friday's game against Portland.
items.story: Monk is ready to make his season debut Friday. The veteran guard figures to cut into Emanuel Sharp's playing time off the bench in the Sacramento backcourt.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is probable for Friday's game against Portland.
items.story: Monk was downgraded to out for Sacramento's regular-season opener Wednesday against the Clippers due to an ankle issue. However, he appears on track to make his 2026-27 debut Friday. Expect confirmation on Monk's availability as tipoff nears.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) won't play Wednesday versus the Clippers.
items.story: Monk was initially listed as questionable. However, after being downgraded to doubtful, the veteran has officially been ruled out for the opener. With Monk unavailable, Nique Clifford, Emanuel Sharp and Daeqwon Plowden could each receive a few extra minutes.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) has been downgraded to doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Monk is not expected to suit up for Sacramento's regular-season opener due to left ankle soreness. If the veteran guard is ultimately ruled out, Nique Clifford, Emanuel Sharp and Daeqwon Plowden could all see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Monk is in danger of missing Wednesday's regular-season opener due to left ankle soreness. His absence would leave additional minutes available for the likes of Nique Clifford and Emanuel Sharp.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) could miss time to begin the 2026-27 campaign, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Monk has been dealing with left ankle soreness throughout training camp and the preseason. While he hasn't been ruled out for Opening Night against Los Angeles, his availability will hinge on "how the ankle responds" leading up to the contest. If Monk isn't available, Nique Clifford should be considered the favorite to see more minutes.

items.headline: Monk (rest) is out for Tuesday's preseason game against Portland, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: Monk is one of several Kings guards who will be unavailable Tuesday, joining Zach LaVine, Ben Simmons and Darius Acuff on the sidelines. His next chance to see preseason action will come Friday against San Antonio.

items.headline: Monk (rest) participated in Monday's practice, per James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento.
items.story: Monk is making progress and should make his preseason debut at some point in the near future. He'll try to do so Tuesday against Portland.

items.headline: Monk (rest) has been ruled out for Saturday's preseason game against the Warriors, Jason Anderson of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: Monk will be idle for a third consecutive preseason game. His next chance to play is Tuesday against the Trail Blazers, but it's possible that the Kings keep the veteran guard off the floor until the team's regular-season opener against the Clippers on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Monk (rest) is out for Thursday's preseason game against the Lakers, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: Monk didn't play in Monday's game against the Lakers, and he won't suit up for the rematch either. His next chance to feature will come against the Warriors on Saturday.

items.headline: Monk (rest) won't suit up for Monday's exhibition versus the Lakers, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports.
items.story: The Kings didn't list an injury for Monk, so this is likely just a rest day for the 28-year-old veteran. His next chance to play will come in a rematch with the Lakers on Thursday.

items.headline: The Kings signed Ben Simmons to a one-year deal Friday, adding another playmaker to Sacramento's second unit who could challenge Monk for playing time.
items.story: Simmons ended up sitting out the entire 2025-26 campaign but will return to The Association this season. He's a versatile defender who could take on a meaningful role thanks to his playmaking ability, though Simmons' arrival may result in fewer minutes for Monk. Monk averaged 12.5 points, 3.0 assists and 1.9 rebounds in 22.0 minutes per tilt across 62 regular-season games (three starts) last season, marking his fewest minutes per game since he played for the Hornets in the 2020-21 campaign. Aside from Simmons, Monk also faces competition for playing time from rookie No. 7 overall pick Darius Acuff, Nique Clifford and Emanuel Sharp. Monk has a $21.6 million player option for 2027-28 and remains a candidate to be traded after having been the subject of trade rumors throughout the 2025-26 season.

items.headline: Monk's (personal) role for 2026-27 is undetermined after Sacramento landed Darius Acuff with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: It was somewhat of a surprise that the Kings didn't trade Monk in 2025-26, as his 22.0 minutes per game were his lowest since 2020-21. The veteran guard is under contract for next year, but the selection of Acuff and emergence of Nique Clifford late last season appear to push Monk even further down the depth chart this summer. That said, Monk could also have a meaningful Opening Night role if Russell Westbrook leaves this offseason.

items.headline: Monk (personal) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Portland.
items.story: Monk will miss Sacramento's regular-season finale while attending to a personal matter. He will finish the 2025-26 campaign with averages of 12.5 points, 3.0 assists, 1.9 rebounds and 0.6 steals across 22.0 minutes per game in 62 regular-season appearances (three starts).

items.headline: Monk (personal) is available for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Monk is no longer on the injury report after missing Friday's game against the Pelicans. He's been hot over his last five games with averages of 16.0 points, 7.4 assists and 2.6 three-pointers.

items.headline: Monk is listed out for Friday's game against the Pelicans due to a personal matter.
items.story: The Kings initially listed Monk as questionable for the contest due to a sore right shoulder, but it's a personal issue that will ultimately keep him from playing Friday. His next chance to rejoin the Kings arrives Sunday, when Sacramento takes on the Clippers. Devin Carter and Nique Clifford should see enough playing time Friday to warrant streaming attention in all fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Monk (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Monk was held out of Sunday's loss to Brooklyn due to a right shoulder contusion and is in jeopardy of missing Friday's game with soreness in that same shoulder. If the 28-year-old guard isn't cleared to face the Pelicans, Daeqwon Plowden and Devin Carter would be candidates to see an uptick in playing time.

items.headline: Monk finished with 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 123-115 win over Toronto.
items.story: Monk returned from a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury and made his presence felt off the bench. This was the 27th time Monk scored at least 15 points as a reserve in 2025-26. That said, he's ending the season on a bit of a down note. Monk is shooting 32 percent from three since the All-Star break, compared to 42.6 percent from deep before the break.

items.headline: Monk (shoulder) is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Monk is set to return from a one-game absence with a shoulder injury that cost him Sunday's loss to the Nets. The veteran guard has averaged 13.2 points, 7.4 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 2.0 three-pointers in 27.0 minutes per tilt in his last five games.

items.headline: Monk (shoulder) is listed as out ahead of Sunday's game in Brooklyn.
items.story: Monk started in each of the Kings' last three contests, most recently finishing with 10 points, two rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Saturday's 123-113 loss to Atlanta. However, he won't suit up Sunday due to a right-shoulder contusion. With DeMar DeRozan (hamstring) and several other players also ruled out, DaQuan Jeffries, Nique Clifford, Daeqwon Plowden and Killian Hayes should all see more action, with two of them possibly moving into the starting lineup.

items.headline: Monk finished Thursday's 121-117 loss to Orlando with 13 points (5-12 FG, 3-9 3Pt), two rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal in 32 minutes.
items.story: With so many injuries in Sacramento, Monk started this contest and saw a healthy usage rate. Over his last four appearances, he's averaging 14.0 points, 7.5 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 2.5 three-pointers in 27.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Monk will start Tuesday's game against the Hornets, Sam Perley of the Hornets' official site reports.
items.story: After dropping a season-high 32 points in Sunday's win over Brooklyn, Monk will step into the starting five for the first time this season due to Sacramento being extremely shorthanded. The veteran guard has averaged 17.6 points and 4.0 assists across 23.6 minutes per contest in his last five appearances.

items.headline: Monk amassed 32 points (8-17 FG, 7-13 3Pt, 9-9 FT), six assists, two rebounds and one block across 30 minutes in Sunday's 126-122 win over the Nets.
items.story: With the Kings shorthanded Sunday, Monk saw an expanded role and made the most of the opportunity, tying his season high in triples en route to a season-best 32 points. The veteran guard also led the second unit in assists and has dished out at least five dimes in three of his last four outings. Killian Hayes (toe) and Nique Clifford (ankle) both exited Sunday's win early, so Monk would be in line for increased minutes in Charlotte on Tuesday if Hayes, Clifford or Russell Westbrook (foot) is sidelined.

items.headline: Monk (shoulder) is available for Sunday's game against the Nets.
items.story: After tweaking his shoulder Thursday against the 76ers, Monk is no longer on the injury report. He may see a bump in usage Sunday with Russell Westbrook (foot) sitting out.

items.headline: Monk won't return to Thursday's game against the 76ers due to a right shoulder injury. He finished with four points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five assists and one rebound in 16 minutes.
items.story: Monk returned from a four-game absence due to a sprained right ankle and logged 16 minutes in the first half. However, he won't return during the second due to the shoulder injury. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game against the Nets.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is available for Thursday's game versus the 76ers.
items.story: Monk is set to return from a four-game stint on the sidelines, and with Nique Clifford (hamstring) out, Monk could see increased minutes. The 28-year-old guard is averaging 12.6 points, 2.7 assists and 2.0 triples per game this season.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Monk is in danger of missing a fifth consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. If the 28-year-old guard is ultimately ruled out, Killian Hayes and Daeqwon Plowden would be candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Monk is in line for a fourth consecutive absence while nursing a right ankle sprain. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Thursday against Philadelphia.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Monk has missed three games since picking up a right ankle injury March 10 against the Pacers, but it's a positive sign that he's been upgraded to questionable ahead of Tuesday's matchup. The team should have another update on his availability closer to game time.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) won't play Sunday versus the Jazz.
items.story: This will be Monk's third straight missed game, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Tuesday's tilt with the Spurs. Killian Hayes and Nique Clifford will continue to pick up the slack in Monk's absence.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Monk injured his right ankle during the Kings' 114-109 win over the Pacers on Tuesday. The injury is severe enough for the veteran guard to be sidelined for a second consecutive game, and his next opportunity to play is Sunday against the Jazz in Sacramento. Killian Hayes will likely operate in an elevated role off the bench in Monk's absence.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Monk is in danger of missing his second straight game, but we'll have a better idea on his status based on his activity level at shootaround. If Monk can't give it a go, expect more minutes for Killian Hayes and Nique Clifford.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Monk left Tuesday's game against the Pacers early with this ankle issue. With Russell Westbrook (quadriceps) getting the night off, Nique Clifford and Killian Hayes could see extended minutes Wednesday.

items.headline: Monk won't return to Tuesday's game against the Pacers due to a right ankle injury, Sean Cunningham of Fox 40 Sacramento reports. Monk ended the night with four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt) in 11 minutes.
items.story: Monk suffered the injury at some point during the first half, and the team quickly announced that he's been shut down for the rest of the evening. Killian Hayes could see an increase in minutes with Monk sidelined, and the latter can be considered doubtful for Wednesday's game against Charlotte.

items.headline: Monk contributed 30 points (11-24 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one block in 31 minutes during Sunday's 126-110 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Monk had a brilliant outing during the decisive win, helping to fill the gap left by DeMar DeRozan's (illness) absence. Monk's 30-point effort was the best scoring result of the season for the ninth-year pro, who was at risk of fading into the woodwork as the team explored the bench for options as they look to the future. Monk ended that trend with 30 minutes against the Pelicans and a resounding tour de force against the shorthanded Bulls. Monk will probably be wearing another jersey next season, but nights like this will certainly drive his stock up in free agency.

items.headline: Monk ended with 13 points (5-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt), three rebounds and five assists in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 114-103 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Monk has logged fewer than 20 minutes in five consecutive games, limiting his fantasy appeal. During this stretch, the veteran swingman has averaged 9.6 points, 2.8 assists and 1.8 rebounds in 18.3 minutes per game while shooting just 36.2 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Monk (ankle) has been cleared to play Thursday against the Mavericks.
items.story: Monk was in danger of missing Thursday's matchup due to ankle soreness, but he's since been cleared to take the court. The Kentucky product is averaging 12.5 points, 1.5 rebounds and 3.3 assists in his last four outings.

items.headline: Monk has right ankle soreness and is questionable for Thursday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Thursday's game is the second leg of a back-to-back set, so the Kings may proceed with caution. Russell Westbrook (thigh) is also out, meaning Nique Clifford and Devin Carter could see expanded run.

items.headline: Monk finished Monday's 123-114 victory over the Grizzlies with 10 points (4-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two assists, one block and two steals in 19 minutes.
items.story: Monk scored in double digits for the fifth straight appearance, although his playing time was largely underwhelming. Despite the fact that Sacramento is looking to the future, it doesn't appear as though Monk is high on its list of priorities. In three games over the past week, he has averaged 14.3 points, 3.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.3 three-pointers in 22.4 minutes per game. At best, he should be viewed as a possible streaming candidate.

items.headline: Monk recorded 14 points (5-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-3 FT) and two assists across 20 minutes during Thursday's 131-94 loss to Orlando.
items.story: With Zach LaVine (hand) and Domantas Sabonis (knee) out for the season, Monk is a candidate to see increased usage down the stretch. An illness sidelined Monk for the Kings' final three games before the All-Star break, but he saw a modest workload Thursday with the team getting blown out by Orlando.

items.headline: Monk (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Thursday's game against the Magic.
items.story: An illness sidelined Monk for the Kings' final three games before the All-Star break, but the veteran guard has been given the green light to return Thursday against Orlando. Monk averaged 15.6 points, 3.1 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 3.2 threes over 24.0 minutes per game over his last nine outings prior to the ASB.

items.headline: Monk (illness) is out for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Monk has been listed as out for a third straight game while battling an illness. His next chance to return will arrive after the All-Star break against the Magic on Feb. 19.

items.headline: Monk (illness) didn't play in Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Monk has missed two straight games due to an illness, and his final chance to suit up before the All-Star break will come Wednesday in Utah. After the break, it's unclear what Monk's role will be, but that'll likely depend on the health of Zach LaVine (finger), Keegan Murray (ankle) and De'Andre Hunter (eye). From Jan. 9 through Feb. 6, Monk appeared in 14 of 16 games, averaging 14.4 points, 3.3 assists and 2.1 rebounds in 23.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Monk is out for Saturday's game against the Cavaliers due to an illness.
items.story: Monk is fresh off an 18-point performance in the loss to the Clippers on Friday, but he won't be able to suit up in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Monk, who has scored in double digits in all but one of his last nine appearances off the bench, will aim to return against the Pelicans on Monday.

items.headline: Wagner amassed 15 points (6-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and two steals in 22 minutes during Tuesday's 125-124 overtime loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Wagner delivered his best performance of the young season, establishing season highs in points, assists, steals and minutes. The veteran big man has now scored in double figures in consecutive games, shooting 11-for-17 from the field and 4-for-6 from beyond the arc during that stretch. Wagner remains a reserve behind Day'Ron Sharpe, but his recent offensive production could help him earn additional playing time in Brooklyn's frontcourt.

items.headline: Wagner finished with six points (1-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and one assist across 14 minutes during Saturday's 125-121 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Wagner struggled mightily with efficiency from inside the arc Saturday and is now shooting 22.2 percent from the field and 50.0 percent from deep through two regular-season appearances. The big man will likely continue operating as Day'Ron Sharpe's primary backup.

items.headline: Wagner played 22 minutes off the bench in Wednesday's 144-128 preseason loss to the Heat, delivering 15 points (6-7 FG, 3-3 3Pt) with three rebounds, two assists and a block.
items.story: Signed by the Nets to a two-year deal in July, Wagner is expected to be a key component of the team's second unit in 2026-27, provided he can stay healthy. The former Orlando big man was on the court for only 66 regular-season games across the prior two seasons, mainly due to an ACL tear, and in his return from the injury last season, he played just 11.9 minutes a contest while averaging a meager 6.9 points and 3.2 boards and shooting 42.6 percent from the field.

items.headline: Wagner finished with 13 points (4-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, an assist and two steals across 18 minutes off the bench in Monday's 131-122 preseason win over the Wizards.
items.story: Wagner provided energetic contributions off Brooklyn's bench, scoring efficiently inside the arc and converting five of six free-throw attempts. The veteran big man also collected five rebounds and two steals, giving him a well-rounded stat line despite playing fewer than 20 minutes. Wagner's combination of scoring, rebounding and defensive production could make him a useful contributor if he earns consistent minutes, but as of now, he's slated to open the 2026-27 season as the backup center behind Day'Ron Sharpe.

items.headline: Wagner is not in the starting lineup for Monday's preseason game against the Wizards.
items.story: With Day'Ron Sharpe (shoulder) back in action, Wagner will shift to a reserve role. As a starter Thursday against the 76ers, the veteran center totaled six points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four steals, three rebounds and one assist across 18 minutes.

items.headline: Wagner is in the starting lineup for Thursday's preseason game against the 76ers, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: The Nets will be without Day'Ron Sharpe (shoulder) for this preseason contest, meaning Wagner will get the nod at center. It will be an opportunity to see how Wagner plays alongside Julius Randle, who will get the nod at power forward.

items.headline: Wagner amassed five points (1-4 FG, 2-2 FT, 1-3 3Pt), five assists, four rebounds and one steal in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason win over Charlotte.
items.story: Wagner came off the bench in his first official game for the Nets, serving as the primary backup behind Day'Ron Sharpe. Though he scored only five points, Wagner flashed some playmaking upside, recording a team-high five assists. It appears Wagner could play a consistent, albeit modest, role for Brooklyn this season. Assuming Sharpe flirts with 27 minutes per game, expect to see Wagner's playing time in the mid-teens.

items.headline: Wagner did not participate in Germany's latest FIBA World Cup qualifying window as he turns his attention toward the upcoming NBA season.
items.story: Wagner appeared in 36 regular-season games for Orlando last campaign, averaging 6.9 points and 3.2 rebounds in 11.9 minutes per contest. The 29-year-old projects to be a reserve frontcourt option for the Nets in 2026-27 after signing a two-year deal with Brooklyn this offseason. His limited playing time makes consistent fantasy value unlikely. Wagner could become a streaming option in deeper formats if injuries create a larger role.

items.headline: Wagner agreed to a two-year, $19 million deal with the Nets on Wednesday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: Wagner will move on from Orlando after six seasons with the franchise. The deal is fully guaranteed and includes a second-year mutual option. During the 2025-26 regular season, after successfully recovering from an ACL injury, Wagner averaged 6.9 points and 3.2 rebounds in 11.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wagner posted five points (1-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and two rebounds across 10 minutes during Sunday's 116-94 loss to the Pistons in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: After beginning the season on the shelf amid his knee surgery recovery, Wagner never quite made his way into much fantasy relevance in 2025-26. Set for unrestricted free agency this offseason, the 29-year-old big man averaged 6.9 points, 3.2 rebounds and 0.8 assists in 11.9 minutes per contest across 36 regular-season games.

items.headline: Wagner (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Friday's 138-127 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Wagner had seen the court in each of the Magic's previous five games, but he played under 10 minutes in four of those outings, and two appearances came in blowouts. With Friday's contest proving to be more competitive throughout, head coach Jamahl Mosley leaned exclusively on Goga Bitadze (12 minutes) as the backup center when starter Wendell Carter (36 minutes) was off the court.

items.headline: Wagner (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the Magic's 128-126 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: After his season got off to a delayed start while he finished off his recovery from the ACL surgery he underwent in January 2025, Wagner has struggled to return to form since being cleared to make his debut just over two months ago. While Wagner had been an efficient scorer off the second unit over his previous four full seasons in Orlando, he's converted at a lowly 41.9 percent clip from the field and 32.8 percent rate from downtown through 29 appearances. Since Wagner doesn't offer much rim protection to make up for the lack of shooting efficiency, head coach Jamahl Mosley appears to have at least temporarily pulled the plug on the German big man. Goga Bitadze has now moved ahead of Wagner to serve as the backup to starting center Wendell Carter in each of the past two contests.

items.headline: Wagner recorded three points (0-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT) and nine rebounds over 18 minutes during Sunday's 130-91 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Wagner continues to play a minor role off the Orlando bench. Across 23 appearances, he's averaging 13.1 minutes per contest with 8.3 points, 3.4 rebounds and 0.9 assists on 45.3 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Wagner registered 12 points (4-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 17 minutes during Wednesday's 116-108 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Lines like these were the norm for Wagner before his ACL tear during the 2024-25 season. Wagner is instant offense off the bench, but his limited workloads combined with Orlando's crowded frontcourt limits his overall upside.

items.headline: Wagner chipped in 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and eight rebounds over 17 minutes during Saturday's 120-117 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Wagner scored in double digits for the second straight game, falling two rebounds short of what would have been his first double-double of the season. It appears as though Wagner has supplanted Goga Bitadze in the rotation, serving as the primary backup behind Wendell Carter. However, his role remains limited, as he is averaging just 7.4 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.3 three-pointers in 10.0 minutes per game over his past seven appearances.

items.headline: Wagner (rest) will be available for Thursday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: Wagner was held out of Sunday's game against the Grizzlies for injury management related to his previous knee injury. He's no longer appearing on the injury report, however, and he could see a handful of rotation minutes against Charlotte.

items.headline: Wagner has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Grizzlies in London due to left knee injury management.
items.story: Wagner missed the first 39 games of the season while recovering from a torn ACL that he suffered in December 2024. He was cleared to play in both of the Magic's last two games, but he'll be in street clothes for Sunday's tilt, with his next opportunity to play being Thursday against the Hornets. Goga Bitadze will operate as the Magic's primary backup center Sunday, while Wagner's absence should reopen a spot in the rotation for Jonathan Isaac.

items.headline: Wagner (knee) registered eight points (3-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and two assists across 10 minutes in Sunday's 128-118 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Wagner made his season debut Sunday, after he had been sidelined for the Magic's first 39 games of the campaign while completing his recovery from Jan. 8, 2025, surgery to repair a torn ACL in his left knee. Before he sustained the knee injury last season, Wagner had been regularly serving as the top backup to Wendell Carter, who missed Sunday's game due to a right hip strain. As a result, Goga Bitadze moved into the starting five Sunday, but it's unclear if the Magic will have room in the rotation for both Bitadze and Wagner once Carter is back to full health. Even if Wagner continues to maintain a regular role on the second unit, the Magic are likely to ramp him up slowly, given he's coming off the major knee injury.

items.headline: Wagner (knee) will make his 2025-26 regular-season debut against the Pelicans on Sunday.
items.story: Wagner was enjoying a career-best start to the 2024-25 regular season before tearing the ACL in his left knee in December 2024. He has progressed enough in his recovery to make his season debut Sunday, though he'll likely operate under a minutes restriction as he works his way into NBA-level shape. Goga Bitadze could revert to the Magic's No. 3 center once Wagner ramps up his minutes.

items.headline: Wagner (knee) is out for Friday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: The Magic had hoped Wagner would be able to make his season debut at some point this week, and his next chance to do so now arrives Sunday against the Pelicans. With the big man still recovering from ACL surgery, Goga Bitadze's minutes should remain solidified in the Orlando frontcourt.

items.headline: Wagner (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Wagner underwent surgery to repair a torn ACL in his left knee last January and has yet to make his 2025-26 debut. However, it was reported Friday that the big man is expected to return "within the next week," according to Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com. His next chance to play will come Friday against the 76ers.

items.headline: Wagner (knee) is out for Tuesday's game against the Wizards, per Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel.
items.story: The Magic are hoping that Wagner will be able to make his season debut at some point this week. Until then, Goga Bitadze is locked into the backup center role behind Wendell Carter.

items.headline: Wagner (knee) is expected to return "within the next week," Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com reports.
items.story: Wagner has yet to make his season debut after undergoing surgery to repair a torn ACL in his left knee last January, though he's inching closer to a return. The 28-year-old big man will likely be eased back into action whenever he's cleared to come back, and his next opportunity to play will come Tuesday against the Wizards. In 30 regular-season appearances (one start) in the 2024-25 campaign, Wagner averaged 12.9 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 18.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wagner (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nuggets.
