items.headline: Green supplied six points (2-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt), one rebound, two assists, one block and three steals in 21 minutes during Friday's 126-110 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Green moved into the starting lineup, replacing Tobias Harris, who was ruled out with a hip injury. As he has done for much of the season, Green made the most of his time on the floor, particularly on the defensive end, where he recorded three steals for the third straight game. Both Harris and Ausar Thompson (ankle) could return as soon as Sunday, meaning Green should be looked at for streaming purposes and nothing more.

items.headline: Green will start Friday's game against Memphis.
items.story: With Tobias Harris (hip) unavailable for the second leg of this back-to-back set, Green will enter the starting five for the first time since Jan. 10. As a starter this season (four games), the veteran forward has averaged 12.0 points, 7.8 rebounds, 3.3 combined steals-plus-blocks and 1.5 assists in 35.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Green totaled 17 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist and three steals in 19 minutes during Thursday's 131-109 victory over Philadelphia.
items.story: Green has been a key player for the second unit in Detroit this season, but he's still a bit too volatile to trust outside of very deep fantasy formats when the team is close to full strength. Across 65 appearances, he holds averages of 7.0 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 18.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green produced six points (2-5 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 15 minutes during Sunday's 121-110 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Despite the absence of Ausar Thompson (ankle) and Caris LeVert (wrist), Green hasn't been able to claim a more prominent role. As a result, Green remains off the radar in most fantasy leagues, averaging only 5.2 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.6 steals in 15.2 minutes per contest in his last nine games while shooting 37.2 percent from the floor during this stretch.

items.headline: Green had two points (1-1 FG), three rebounds and one assist in 17 minutes during Saturday's 126-110 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Green continues to put up modest production, logging no more than 20 minutes for the 17th straight game. With the Pistons rolling out a relatively healthy lineup, Green's role is simply that of a depth piece. At best, fantasy managers could consider him for streaming purposes when in desperate need of steals.

items.headline: Green chipped in two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 17 minutes during Friday's 111-104 loss to Houston.
items.story: Green scored just two points, failing to reach double digits for the fifth time in the past six games. After a brief run of relevance earlier in the season, Green has seen his role regress in recent times. In that recent six-game span, he has averaged just 6.8 points and 1.5 steals in 17.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green is not in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Suns.
items.story: With Isaiah Stewart (illness) and Tobias Harris (hip) both back in the mix, Green is reverting back to usual role off the bench. Green has averaged 8.8 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.1 steals in 21.1 minutes per tilt across his last 14 games off the bench, so the door remains open for him to offer streaming value in the steals category.

items.headline: Green will start against the Clippers on Saturday.
items.story: With Isaiah Stewart (illness) and Tobias Harris (hip) unavailable, Green will get the starting nod against Los Angeles. In three starts so far this season, the 32-year-old swingman has averaged 13.7 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.0 steals in 35.7 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Green totaled 17 points (6-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and three steals over 29 minutes during Monday's 121-90 win over New York.
items.story: Green has now scored in double figures in three straight games and has played at least 24 minutes in those contests with Tobias Harris (hip) sidelined. The 32-year-old forward drilled a season-high four threes and collected three swipes in the blowout win over the Knicks. He's now totalled six games with at least three steals this season, the second most in the league by a bench player. Green should continue to see healthy playing time while Harris is out and could offer some streaming appeal in the short term.

items.headline: Green ended with 11 points (3-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes during Sunday's 114-110 win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Tobias Harris (hip) is going to miss a couple of weeks, and Jalen Duren (ankle) is expected to miss at least one week as well. Ausar Thompson drew the start alongside Isaiah Stewart and Paul Reed in the frontcourt, but Green actually saw more minutes than Thompson. Green could offer some low-end streaming appeal for the next week or two.

items.headline: Green closed Tuesday's 128-106 victory over the Lakers with eight points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and two blocks in 31 minutes.
items.story: With Tobias Harris (hip) going down in the first quarter, Green logged his most minutes since Nov. 14. The 32-year-old forward struggled to find his rhythm from beyond the arc but was effective on the defensive end, chipping in a team-high two blocks. If Harris is forced to miss additional time, Green could step into a more prominent role.

items.headline: Green produced eight points (3-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and three steals over 14 minutes during Monday's 112-105 win over the Celtics.
items.story: With the Pistons at full strength, Green has seen his minutes take a hit. Over his last five outings, the 32-year-old forward has averaged 7.8 points, 0.6 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.4 three-pointers in 14.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Green closed with nine points (3-6 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, two assists and two steals in 16 minutes during Wednesday's 113-109 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Green's role has fluctuated due to the return of multiple key players from injuries, averaging just 3.3 points, 1.0 rebounds and 0.3 assists across 10.6 minutes in his last seven games after averaging 14.0 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists across 32.6 minutes in the five games (three starts) before. Green has shown that he can step up for Detroit when necessary, and if injuries occur to gash the team's wing depth again, he is a candidate to see heavy usage.

items.headline: Green registered zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one block across 10 minutes during Wednesday's 117-114 loss to Boston.
items.story: Green's role has regressed in recent times, having now played fewer than 15 minutes in three straight games. With Detroit now relatively healthy, Green is likely to serve as a depth piece on most nights. Over his last three games, Green has averaged just 3.0 points in 11.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Green won't start  Monday's game against Indiana.
items.story: A string of three straight starts for Green will be broken up Monday. He has averaged 7.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 22.6 minutes per contest over 13 games this season.

items.headline: Huerter provided seven points (3-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 0-2 FT), one rebound, one block and one steal across 16 minutes during Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Huerter shot efficiently from the field but missed both of his free-throw attempts. The veteran wing played a limited role despite Isaiah Joe (hip) being unavailable, which doesn't bode well for his fantasy outlook once Detroit's backcourt returns to full strength. Huerter remains a fringe option in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Huerter closed with three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists over 18 minutes during Tuesday's 121-113 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Huerter struggled to find his shooting touch in his Pistons regular-season debut, connecting on just one of four attempts from beyond the arc. He played fewer minutes than fellow perimeter reserves Isaiah Joe and Javonte Green, the latter of whom erupted for 19 points. With Duncan Robinson also starting and hitting five triples, Huerter faces considerable competition for minutes and perimeter opportunities in Detroit's rotation.

items.headline: Huerter registered 11 points (3-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal in 18 minutes during Saturday's 114-108 preseason loss to the Wizards in overtime.
items.story: Huerter delivered an efficient performance from downtown and was one of five Detroit players to score in double figures. He also tied for second in the second unit in assists. The veteran swingman is expected to compete for playing time off the bench with Isaiah Joe and Javonte Green.

items.headline: Huerter said Monday that he's healthy entering training camp after undergoing surgery during the offseason to address a groin injury, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Huerter said the injury initially occurred during his time with Chicago before he aggravated it during Detroit's first-round playoff series against Orlando. He underwent a cleanup procedure after the Pistons' postseason run ended and has since returned to full health, putting him on track to participate in training camp without limitations.

items.headline: Huerter intends to sign a three-year, $27 million contract with the Pistons, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Monday.
items.story: Huerter was traded from Chicago to Detroit before last season's deadline. He appeared in 25 regular-season games (three starts) with the Pistons, during which he averaged 8.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 20.5 minutes per game. However, the Pistons added Isaiah Joe via trade this offseason, so Huerter will likely have to compete for minutes with Joe, Daniss Jenkins, Caris LeVert and Marcus Sasser.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is available for Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter will shed his questionable tag due to a lingering left adductor strain and suit up in Sunday's do-or-die matchup. The 27-year-old swingman has appeared in just one game during the second round of the postseason, logging three minutes in Wednesday's Game 5 loss before aggravating the adductor injury.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is questionable for Sunday's Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Huerter is on the injury report again as he continues to manage a left adductor strain that has kept him sidelined for the majority of the second round. While he was cleared to play in Game 5, he saw just three minutes of action off the bench and did not see the floor at all during Friday's Game 6 victory. Given the "all hands on deck" nature of a Game 7, the 27-year-old sharpshooter will likely be active, but he may not see the floor, as he has yet to log meaningful minutes since the first round.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is available for Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers on Friday.
items.story: Huerter's presence Friday helps put the Pistons at full strength for a win-or-go-home contest. The 27-year-old, who missed time earlier this series with a left adductor strain, logged just three minutes in Detroit's Game 5 loss because he aggravated the injury, per Jamal Collier of ESPN.com. Collier also noted that Huerter received an injection to gain clearance for Game 6, so the sharpshooter's workload could depend on his pain tolerance.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) is questionable for Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the Cavaliers on Friday, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
items.story: Huerter managed to make his first appearance of the series Wednesday after missing time with a left adductor strain, but he logged only three minutes and recorded one assist. It's unclear how much the 27-year-old will be able to contribute if he's ultimately given the green light to suit up.

items.headline: Huerter (adductor) recorded one assist over three minutes off the bench Wednesday in the Pistons' 117-113 overtime loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Available to play for the first time since Game 4 of the Pistons' first-round playoff series versus the Magic, Huerter was a fringe member of head coach J.B. Bickerstaff's rotation. The veteran wing checked into the contest with 6:17 left in the first quarter and played a brief shift before heading back to the bench, where he remained for the rest of the game. Regardless of whether Duncan Robinson (back) plays in Friday's Game 6 after sitting out Wednesday, Huerter could find himself outside of Bickerstaff's rotation entirely.

items.headline: Huerter (thigh) is available for Wednesday's Game 5 matchup of the Eastern Conference Semifinals with Cleveland.

items.headline: Huerter finished Thursday's 113-108 win over the Timberwolves with 12 points (4-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists over 22 minutes.
items.story: Huerter regularly plays off the bench when Duncan Robinson is available, but the former has been a reliable option even if his minutes rarely go over 25. Huerter has scored in double digits in four of his last five games, and he's drained multiple threes four times over that stretch in which he's averaging 14.0 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game while shooting 44.4 percent from deep.

items.headline: Huerter isn't in the starting lineup for Tuesday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Huerter drew the start Monday with Detroit sitting multiple key starters, but he'll retreat to the bench for the second half of the team's back-to-back. The Maryland product has scored in double figures in two of his previous four matchups as a reserve.

items.headline: Huerter is starting Monday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Huerter will make his second start in three games due to another absence for Duncan Robinson (hip). Huerter scorched the nets in his last start Thursday against the Pelicans, when he finished with 22 points on 4-of-7 shooting from deep in 34 minutes of action.

items.headline: Huerter is not in the Pistons' starting lineup against the Timberwolves on Saturday.
items.story: Huerter made his first start of the season for the Pistons in Thursday's 129-108 win over the Pelicans, when he played 34 minutes and finished with 22 points, three rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers. He'll retreat to a bench role for Saturday's contest due to the return of Duncan Robinson (hip).

items.headline: Huerter chipped in 22 points (9-14 FG, 4-7 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and one steal over 34 minutes during Thursday's 129-108 win over New Orleans.
items.story: Huerter was penciled into the starting five Thursday after Duncan Robinson (hip/wrist) was downgraded to out, and he didn't disappoint. Huerter took advantage of his opportunities from behind the arc, where he added 12 of his 22 points. He finished second on his team in scoring and reached the 20-point threshold for just the fifth time this season.

items.headline: Huerter will start Thursday versus the Pelicans.
items.story: Huerter is getting the spot-start with Duncan Robinson (hip) out, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Ausar Thompson, Tobias Harris, Daniss Jenkins and Jalen Duren. As a starter this season, Huerter has averaged 11.1 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.2 triples per contest.

items.headline: Huerter (shoulder) has been removed from the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Huerter will be back in action Monday following a one-game stint on the sidelines, and he should be a bit more involved in the rotation with Cade Cunningham (lung) and Marcus Sasser (hip) out. Huerter can be viewed as a low-end streamer in deep leagues if you need some triples, dimes and steals.

items.headline: Huerter (shoulder) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Golden State, Keith Langlois of the Pistons' official site reports.
items.story: Huerter will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a right shoulder contusion, and his next chance to play will come Monday against the Lakers. With the 27-year-old swingman sidelined, Javonte Green and Ronald Holland are candidates to see a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Huerter is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors with a right shoulder contusion.
items.story: This is a new issue for Huerter, and the Pistons may be contemplating a maintenance day for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Huerter is coming off a strong showing Thursday, and he's someone who could be more involved offensively going forward, with Cade Cunningham (chest) sidelined indefinitely.

items.headline: Huerter provided four points (2-7 FG, 0-5 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists in 22 minutes during Tuesday's 130-117 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Huerter continues to play a very modest role off the Detroit bench. Over his last eight games, he's averaging 7.0 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.0 three-pointers in 20.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Doncic erupted for 42 points (14-24 FG, 6-15 3Pt, 8-10 FT), seven rebounds, 13 assists and two steals across 36 minutes in Monday's 138-117 victory over Miami.
items.story: Doncic has now eclipsed the 40-point mark in two straight games, totaling 87 points over that stretch. The Lakers superstar led all players in scoring, three-pointers, made field goals and assists in LA's second straight win. Doncic has topped 40-plus points in four of his seven regular-season outings, including a season-high 52 points in a win over the Jazz on Oct. 25. Over the past five games, he's averaging 43.4 points with 6.8 three-pointers, 8.4 rebounds and 8.6 assists in 36.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: Doncic posted 45 points (12-23 FG, 8-12 3Pt, 13-13 FT), 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals and one block over 35 minutes in a 131-125 win over the Raptors on Sunday.
items.story: Doncic set the tone early with a sensational first quarter, when he logged 16 points and four of his game-high six steals. He scored at least eight points in each of the next three quarters and also grabbed a season-high 15 boards en route to his second double-double of the 2026-27 campaign. Doncic has three games of 40-plus points this season and is averaging 37.7 points, 8.2 rebounds, 7.3 assists, 5.8 threes, 1.8 steals and 0.8 blocks over 35.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Doncic accumulated 37 points (12-27 FG, 6-16 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal in 37 minutes during Friday's 112-95 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Doncic was brilliant early, pouring in 21 points in the first quarter as Los Angeles built a 25-point lead, but he couldn't keep up the pace as the Warriors stormed back. He still led all scorers with 37 points, though he needed 27 shots and picked up a technical foul late in the third quarter. The Lakers will try to bounce back Sunday at home against the Raptors.

items.headline: Doncic (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Doncic was held out of Wednesday's game against the Clippers after logging 37 minutes in the first half of the back-to-back Tuesday. However, he'll be a full go for Friday's clash. The star guard has been on a tear to begin the 2026-27 season, averaging 36.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.3 steals in four regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Doncic (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Doncic is sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set. Quentin Grimes appears to be the most likely candidate to replace Doncic in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Doncic produced 41 points (12-22 FG, 6-15 3Pt, 11-13 FT), five rebounds, nine assists and one block in 37 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Doncic did everything he could to keep Los Angeles unbeaten, leading the scoring with 41 points and hitting six threes. It followed his 52-point outing at Utah over the weekend, and he brought a noticeably more engaged defensive effort. The Lakers will complete the back-to-back Wednesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Doncic posted 52 points (17-30 FG, 8-18 3Pt, 10-11 FT), eight rebounds, 10 assists and two steals over 38 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Doncic put on a masterclass during Sunday's matinee, helping the Lakers claw back from an early 18-point deficit as he notched his first 50-point performance of the season. It was the 10th 50-point game of Doncic's career, and he became just the third Laker in franchise history to tally 50-plus points and 10 assists in a game, joining Elgin Baylor and Jerry West.

items.headline: Doncic notched 23 points (8-21 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), six rebounds, seven assists and one block in 37 minutes during Friday's 125-117 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Doncic had an uneven night in the win. He finished third on the team in scoring and committed a career-high 11 turnovers. He played much better in Wednesday's opener, scoring 28 points in three quarters against Golden State. With LeBron James gone to Philadelphia, last season's scoring champion is the centerpiece in Los Angeles, and he'll look to bounce back Sunday in Utah.

items.headline: Doncic produced 28 points (7-18 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 9-9 FT), eight rebounds, seven assists and three steals across 30 minutes in Wednesday's 127-105 win over the Warriors.
items.story: Doncic opened the regular season with a strong all-around performance, and while his shooting line wasn't entirely efficient, he caused damage from three while filling out the stat sheet as he often does. Scoring prowess aside, his rebounding and playmaking reinforce his elite fantasy ceiling. The six turnovers were a drawback, but his high usage should keep him among the league's most productive fantasy options every time he steps on the hardwood.

items.headline: LaVine (elbow) is available for Monday's game against the Mavericks, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: LaVine will shed the questionable tag ahead of Sacramento's matchup with Dallas. He is dealing with soreness in his right elbow after playing a season-low 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis, but he'll fight through the issue and reprise his starting role for the 0-6 Kings.

items.headline: LaVine (elbow) is questionable to play in Monday's game against Dallas.
items.story: LaVine played a season-low 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis, but it's unclear if that was due to the elbow soreness or the game being out of reach for the Kings. Either way, his status will bear monitoring ahead of Monday's clash with the Mavericks. If he's unable to play, Darius Acuff Jr.'s usage would skyrocket, while Malik Monk, Emanuel Sharp and Nique Clifford could all see increased opportunities in the backcourt.

items.headline: LaVine chipped in 11 points (4-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT) and one assist over 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Saturday was the first time this season that LaVine attempted less than 10 field goals, and his performance broke a five-game streak of 20-plus-point tallies. Part of that lack of production was due to him playing only one minute in the fourth quarter, when the game was well out of reach for the Kings. The veteran wing will finish the month of October having averaged 23.5 points, 3.2 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 1.2 steals and 2.5 threes over 34.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: LaVine tallied 21 points (7-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds, five assists and three steals across 39 minutes in Thursday's 132-120 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: LaVine struggled with perimeter efficiency, connecting on just three of 10 attempts, but made up for it with five assists and three steals while going 4-for-7 from inside the arc. LaVine is off to an excellent start this season, scoring at least 20 points in every game and averaging 26.0 points per game. He's also shooting at an efficient rate, making 50 percent of his attempts and 35.7 percent of his three-pointers.

items.headline: LaVine supplied 22 points (7-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: LaVine delivered an efficient offensive performance, shooting 70.0 percent from the field while connecting on three triples. The veteran guard was one of three Sacramento players to score at least 20 points, joining De'Andre Hunter (24) and Domantas Sabonis (20). Despite LaVine's strong shooting, the Kings fell to 0-4 to begin the season.

items.headline: LaVine recorded 37 points (13-25 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 8-8 FT), five assists, two rebounds and two steals in 40 minutes during Sunday's 123-112 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: LaVine continued his run of strong play to begin the season, exploding for a game-high 37 points on solid efficiency. The 31-year-old pro has totaled at least 20 points and three three-pointers made in each of the team's first three games. He figures to maintain a high level of usage alongside rookie guard Darius Acuff this season.

items.headline: LaVine accumulated 22 points (6-15 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals in 39 minutes during Friday's 128-120 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: LaVine finished second on the team in scoring for the second straight game, though his outside shot was off. The veteran has led the Kings' perimeter attack early on, and he'll continue to play a lot of minutes as Sacramento searches for its first win. He'll next face the Grizzlies on Sunday.

items.headline: LaVine recorded 28 points (10-19 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-8 FT), four rebounds and four assists over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: The veteran guard had twice as many points as any other Sacramento starter, and only three of LaVine's teammates even scored in double digits in the rout. LaVine figures to see heavy usage on a roster lacking in established offensive options as long as he can stay healthy -- he played just 39 regular-season games in 2025-26 due to a hand injury that required surgery, but LaVine looks fully recovered to begin the current campaign.

items.headline: aVine generated 20 points (6-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 7-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Friday's 126-97 preseason loss to the Spurs.
items.story: LaVine led the Kings in scoring and posted his best preseason outing, nearly doubling his previous high of 11 points. The Kings went winless in the preseason, and they'll need LaVine's veteran production to get off to a good start against the Clippers in the season opener.

items.headline: LaVine (rest) will play in Friday's preseason game against San Antonio, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
items.story: LaVine didn't play in Tuesday's exhibition versus Portland. However, he will suit up for the Kings' final preseason game before Opening Night. The 31-year-old will be looking to bounce back during the 2026-27 campaign after averaging 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists over 31.4 minutes in just 39 regular-season games in 2025-26.

items.headline: LaVine (rest) will not play in Tuesday's preseason matchup against Portland, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: LaVine is among eight Kings players ruled out for Tuesday's contest. His next opportunity to play will come Friday against San Antonio in the preseason finale.

items.headline: LaVine posted 11 points (5-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt), two assists, one rebound and three steals in 23 minutes during Saturday's 111-106 preseason loss to the Warriors.
items.story: LaVine didn't have the most productive offensive showing. However, the veteran shined defensively, finishing two steals behind Jonathan Mogbo, who had a game-high five. LaVine is coming off one of least productive seasons in recent memory, averaging 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists over 31.4 minutes per contest in 39 regular-season games during the 2025-26 campaign. The 31-year-old has flashed All-Star upside in previous seasons, though it's unknown if those days are well behind him.

items.headline: LaVine finished with nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT) and one rebound in 15 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason loss to the Lakers.
items.story: LaVine started at shooting guard but played only during the first half as Sacramento limited the workload of its veterans. The 31-year-old remains one of the Kings' primary scoring options after averaging 19.2 points during the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: LaVine is healthy entering training camp, Kings general manager Scott Perry said Monday, Frankie Cartoscelli of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
items.story: LaVine underwent season-ending surgery in February to repair a torn tendon in his right fifth finger, an injury that limited him to 39 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. He averaged 19.2 points per game while shooting 47.9 percent from the field and 39.0 percent from three, and his healthy status entering camp puts him on track to resume a prominent role in Sacramento's backcourt.

items.headline: LaVine (hand) exercised his $49 million player option for 2026-27 on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: LaVine underwent season-ending surgery on his right hand before the 2025-26 All-Star break. He averaged 19.2 points in 39 regular-season games last season and was a two-time All-Star before being traded to the Kings in February of 2025. The Kings are listening to trade offers for LaVine and Domantas Sabonis (knee), but their hefty contracts are making things difficult. If LaVine stays in Sacramento, he would likely take a back seat as the Kings try to develop 2026 No. 7 overall pick Darius Acuff.

items.headline: LaVine (hand) is projected to have a new backcourt partner after the Kings selected Darius Acuff with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: LaVine primarily worked alongside Russell Westbrook in 2024-25, the latter of whom is an unrestricted free agent this offseason. LaVine, on the other hand, has a player option worth over $48 million for 2026-27 and figures to exercise it after averaging 19.2 points per game over 39 regular-season appearances last year, his lowest output since 2017-18. Assuming he remains with the Kings, LaVine should have a good chance of having a bounce-back season.

items.headline: LaVine will undergo season-ending surgery on his right hand after the All-Star break, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
items.story: After missing Sacramento's final three outings before the All-Star break due to right finger soreness, LaVine is scheduled to undergo season-ending hand surgery. The veteran swingman will finish the 2025-26 season with averages of 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists while shooting 47.9 percent from the field and 39.0 percent from downtown across 31.4 minutes per contest in 39 regular-season games (37 starts). He holds a $48.97 million player option for the 2026-27 campaign. With LaVine sidelined, Nique Clifford should continue to see an expanded role, while Malik Monk (illness) and Devin Carter are also candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: LaVine (finger) is out for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: LaVine will miss a third straight game due to finger soreness. His next chance to play won't come until after the All-Star break, so he'll have over a week to rest and recover. In the meantime, look for Nique Clifford and Devin Carter to see more minutes.

items.headline: LaVine (finger) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: LaVine will be sidelined for a second consecutive game due to right finger soreness, and his last opportunity to suit up before the All-Star break is Wednesday against the Jazz. Nique Clifford and Devin Carter should see more minutes in LaVine's absence.

items.headline: LaVine (finger) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: LaVine is dealing with right finger soreness and won't suit up in the second half of this back-to-back set. The veteran swingman's absence should open up more minutes for Nique Clifford, Malik Monk and Devin Carter. LaVine's next chance to play will come on the road against the Pelicans on Monday.

items.headline: LaVine finished Sunday's 116-112 loss to Washington with 35 points (13-26 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal in 35 minutes.
items.story: LaVine led the way in scoring for the Kings and combined with DeMar DeRozan for 67 points, but it wasn't enough to secure a victory. Sunday marked LaVine's best scoring performance since Dec. 6, when he dropped 42 points against the Heat. He's now averaging 19.6 points, 2.4 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.0 steals over his last five appearances.

items.headline: LaVine is in the Kings' starting lineup against the Celtics on Friday, Sean Grande of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.story: LaVine came off the bench during Thursday's loss to the 76ers, but the veteran wing will return to the starting lineup Friday while Nique Clifford reverts to a reserve role. LaVine has averaged 17.9 points, 2.5 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 2.6 threes over 31.0 minutes per game over his last 12 outings (10 starts).

items.headline: LaVine logged 17 points (5-16 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three assists, one rebound and two steals over 29 minutes during the Kings' 113-111 loss to the 76ers on Thursday.
items.story: LaVine was cleared to return Thursday from a two-game absence due to lower-back soreness. He ended up finishing as the Kings' third-leading scorer behind Dennis Schroder (27 points) and DeMar DeRozan (25 points), though LaVine connected on just 31.3 percent of his field-goal attempts during the loss. The Kings play the Celtics on Friday, so it's possible that LaVine is rested for the second leg of the back-to-back set.

items.headline: LaVine will come off the bench Thursday against the 76ers, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
items.story: LaVine was removed from the injury report ahead of Thursday's matchup, but it appears the club will ease him back into action following a two-game absence due to lower-back soreness. Nique Clifford will remain in the starting lineup for the time being, though he hasn't been all that effective in two starting opportunities.

items.headline: LaVine (back) is off the injury report for Thursday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: After sitting out two consecutive contests with lower-back soreness, LaVine is slated to return to the lineup Thursday and likely send Nique Clifford back to the bench. LaVine has averaged 17.8 points, 2.3 assists and 2.2 rebounds in 30.7 minutes per contest in his last 10 games.

items.headline: LaVine is out for Tuesday's game against the Knicks due to lower-back soreness.
items.story: Despite going through Tuesday's morning shootaround, LaVine isn't feeling well enough to play against New York. The star guard's next chance to play comes Thursday in Philadelphia. With Malik Monk (ankle) also sidelined, Keon Ellis could be thrust into a significant role.

items.headline: LaVine (back) participated in Tuesday's morning shootaround, Chris Biderman of The Sacramento Bee reports.
items.story: LaVine, who was unable to play Sunday against the Pistons, remains questionable on the injury report for Tuesday's game in New York. Malik Monk (ankle) is also questionable for the Kings, meaning players like Nique Clifford, Dennis Schroder and Keon Ellis may be asked to step up if the team ends up being shorthanded.

items.headline: LaVine (back) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: LaVine is in jeopardy of missing his second straight contest. Malik Monk (ankle) is also questionable, meaning the Kings may need to rely more on Nique Clifford, Dennis Schroder and Keon Ellis.

items.headline: LaVine (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: LaVine popped up on Saturday night's injury report as questionable due to low-back soreness. The Kings will hold the veteran wing out of Sunday's contest, and his next opportunity to play is Tuesday against the Knicks. Malik Monk, Dennis Schroder, Keon Ellis and Nique Clifford are candidates to enter Sacramento's starting lineup in LaVine's absence.

items.headline: LaVine is now questionable for Sunday's game against the Pistons due to low-back soreness.
items.story: LaVine wasn't part of the Kings' initial injury report, but the star guard was added late Saturday night due to back soreness. If he can't play in Sunday's game, Malik Monk or Dennis Schroder would likely enter the starting lineup.

items.headline: LaVine provided 18 points (7-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and five assists across 22 minutes during Tuesday's 130-117 loss to the Heat.
items.story: LaVine's numbers have been lower since his return from injury, but he's held a solid floor with no serious regression. He sank 70 percent of his shots during the loss, helping to pad a nine-game field-goal percentage of 49.6 percent. His shot volume has also been high since returning, averaging 13.0 attempts over the same nine-game span.

items.headline: Sexton ended Sunday's 131-125 victory over the Raptors with 14 points (6-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 19 minutes.
items.story: Sexton led the Lakers' reserves in scoring, making six of his 10 field-goal attempts in an efficient offensive showing. He remains a useful source of bench scoring, though his relatively limited playing time makes consistent fantasy production difficult to sustain.

items.headline: Sexton had 21 points (6-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 5-8 FT), four rebounds and two assists over 21 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 103-87 win over the Clippers.
items.story: The 21 points were a season high for Sexton, who remained on the second unit even with Luka Doncic (back) held out of the lineup. Instead, Quentin Grimes moved into the starting five. Through four games this season, all off the bench, Sexton has averaged 12.0 points, 2.3 assists, 2.0 boards, 1.5 threes and 0.8 steals in 17.8 minutes.

items.headline: Sexton totaled nine points (4-11 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and four assists over 14 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Sexton has now made three straight appearances off the bench for the Lakers after missing the start of the year with a calf injury. His fantasy upside should remain capped while the team's backcourt is nearly fully healthy.

items.headline: Sexton (calf) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Sexton took a seat for Wednesday's 2026-27 season opener against the Warriors as a precaution, but he'll be ready to make his team debut Friday evening. He's expected to be utilized off the bench behind Luka Doncic and will be on a minutes restriction, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said that Sexton (calf) did not experience a setback, but the Lakers will sit him out of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors as a precaution, Daniel Starkland of Lakers Nation reports.
items.story: It sounds like Sexton is day-to-day, so for now, he should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Clippers. Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia and Sandro Mamukelashvili will help pick up the slack in Sexton's absence.

items.headline: Sexton (calf) won't play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors, per Khobi Price of The California Post.
items.story: Sexton isn't ready to make his Lakers debut Wednesday due to a calf strain. The veteran guard's absence should open the door to more playing time for Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia and Sandro Mamukelashvili.

items.headline: Sexton (calf) is questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.
items.story: Sexton did not play during the preseason due to a right soleus strain, but he was able to get through the Lakers' past two practices, so he's trending in the right direction. He'll likely have some minutes restrictions if he's cleared to play.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) fully practiced Monday, per Dan Woike of The Athletic.
items.story: Sexton missed the end of the preseason with a lower right leg injury, but he's trending in the right direction. His status remains uncertain for Wednesday's season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) has been ruled out for Friday's preseason game against the Nuggets, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sexton will end up missing the entire preseason due to a lower right leg injury. However, head coach JJ Redick said the veteran guard is trending in the right direction ahead of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) participated in Thursday's practice but didn't take part in any live action, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sexton is considered day-to-day with a lower-leg injury and didn't scrimmage Thursday. He can be viewed as questionable for Friday's preseason finale against Denver until the Lakers provide an update on his status.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Sexton remains day-to-day with a lower-leg injury. His final chance to suit up in the preseason will come Friday against the Nuggets.

items.headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Saturday that Sexton is day-to-day due to a lower-leg injury, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Sexton has missed multiple preseason games due to what was initially described as a lower-body injury, but Redick was more specific about the nature of Sexton's health concern Saturday. With two more exhibition games left on the schedule, the Lakers may keep Sexton sidelined until the team's regular-season opener against the Warriors on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Sexton (lower body) has been ruled out for Thursday's preseason game against Sacramento, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Sexton has been battling a lower-body injury and will miss his third matchup of the preseason. However, the team isn't overly concerned at this point for what coach JJ Redick is deeming a minor injury for the 27-year-old guard, per Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com.

items.headline: Sexton (lower body) won't play in Tuesday's preseason game against the Warriors, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
items.story: It's unknown if Sexton will be available to play during the preseason, though his next opportunity to get on the floor will come Thursday against Sacramento. The 27-year-old ended the 2025-26 campaign with the Bulls, averaging 17.5 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.5 steals over 26.0 minutes per contest in 26 regular-season games.

items.headline: Sexton has been ruled out for Monday's preseason game against the Kings due to a lower-body issue, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: It's unclear exactly what Sexton is dealing with, though he's considered day-to-day. His next chance to suit up in the preseason will come Tuesday against the Warriors.

items.headline: Sexton agreed to a two-year, $19 million contract with the Lakers on Wednesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: LeBron James is leaving Los Angeles, and the Lakers are retooling via free agency. After re-signing Austin Reaves to a massive extension, the Lakers have signed Sexton, Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili, while pulling off a sign-and-trade for Walker Kessler. As things stand, Sexton appears set for a backup role behind Luka Doncic and Reaves in 2026-27.

items.headline: Sexton had 19 points (8-16 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 149-128 loss to Dallas.
items.story: Sexton played well in the final game, but it might be the last time we see Sexton in a Bulls uniform. Sexton is an unrestricted free agent and can shop around for a contract with another club. Given a depth chart that's deep at the guard position, the Bulls may not be compelled to give him a better offer.

items.headline: Sexton (finger/elbow) is available for Sunday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Sexton popped up on the injury report with a right finger injury and a left elbow contusion, though he'll shake off his probable tag and suit up in Chicago's regular-season finale. The 26-year-old guard has started four straight games for the shorthanded Bulls, during which he has averaged 18.0 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 3.3 steals in 30.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sexton (finger, elbow) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Although the Bulls aren't going to the postseason, Sexton is expected to suit up for Chicago's final contest of the 2025-26 campaign. He is coming off a 12-point effort in Friday's 127-103 loss to Orlando. However, Sexton has an excellent chance to turn it around against one of the worst teams in the NBA.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is listed as available for Friday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Sexton was in danger of missing this contest, but he is officially cleared to suit up. The 27-year-old is coming off one of his best performances of the 2025-26 campaign, finishing with 27 points, three rebounds, two assists and three steals across 34 minutes in Thursday's 119-108 win over Washington.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is probable for Friday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Sexton racked up 27 points (12-21 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals in 34 minutes during Thursday's 119-108 victory over Washington and will likely be available for the second half of Chicago's back-to-back set. With Josh Giddey (hamstring) still sidelined, Sexton should continue to start and see elevated usage.

items.headline: Sexton racked up 27 points (12-21 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals in 34 minutes during Thursday's 119-108 victory over Washington.
items.story: Sexton was one of three Chicago starters to finish with 20-plus points, as Tre Jones led the way with 31 points while Leonard Miller chipped in 26 points. This marks the first time Sexton has reached the 20-point threshold since March 30, and he looked much more comfortable on the offensive end after hitting on 37.2 percent of his tries from the field in his previous three matchups leading up to Thursday.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is available for Thursday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Sexton is expectedly shedding a probable designation Thursday with a right finger injury. The veteran guard is playing at a high level, averaging 19.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.8 steals in 27.6 minutes per contest over his last nine games.

items.headline: Sexton is probable for Thursday's game against the Wizards due to a right finger injury.
items.story: The probable tag suggests Sexton will suit up Thursday despite not being 100 percent healthy. He's averaging 18.8 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game over his last 10 appearances, and Thursday's matchup looks like a favorable one on paper against a lackluster Washington team.

items.headline: Sexton recorded 15 points (5-16 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), nine rebounds, seven assists and four steals over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 129-98 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Sexton ripped away two steals within his first five minutes of play, and he finished with a season-high four swipes in the blowout win. He'll have another chance to take advantage of the Wizards' lackadaisical play in a rematch with Washington on Thursday.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is available for Tuesday's game versus the Wizards.
items.story: Josh Giddey (hamstring) is out, so Sexton should see quality minutes against the Wizards. Over his past six games, Sexton has averaged 20.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 3.3 triples and 1.3 steals per contest.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) is listed as probable for Tuesday's game against Washington.
items.story: Sexton logged 31 minutes in Sunday's 120-110 loss to Phoenix, finishing with 18 points, nine rebounds, one assist and three steals. Assuming the 27-year-old can suit up, he could be more productive than usual against one of the worst defensive squads in the league, especially with teammates Josh Giddey (hamstring) and Matas Buzelis (illness) already ruled out.

items.headline: Sexton (finger) will play Sunday against Phoenix, Will Gottlieb of AllCHGO.com reports.
items.story: Sexton will be able to fight through a minor finger injury to suit for Sunday's tilt. He's been playing at a high level on the offensive end lately, averaging 21.0 points while converting at a clip of 52.2 percent from the field in his previous five appearances. With Josh Giddey (hamstring) sidelined, Sexton will slide back into the starting lineup and should retain increased usage.

items.headline: Sexton is probable to play Sunday against the Suns due to a right finger injury.
items.story: Sexton is dealing with a minor injury to a finger on his shooting hand, but it's not expected to keep him out of Sunday's game. Josh Giddey (hamstring) is questionable to play, and if he gets ruled out, that would open up minutes and a potential starting role for Sexton.

items.headline: Sexton registered 19 points (6-12 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes during Friday's 136-96 loss to New York.
items.story: Sexton returned to the bench with Josh Giddey (hamstring) back in the starting lineup, but he produced another strong showing as a scoring weapon for a Bulls team that's already out of playoff contention. Sexton has scored 15-plus points in seven consecutive games and is clearly ending the season on a strong note, showing he remains a very viable option ahead of hitting the open market in the summer.

items.headline: Sexton won't start Friday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Sexton got the start in Wednesday's 145-126 loss to the Pacers. However, with Josh Giddey (hamstring) back from a one-game absence, Sexton will head back to the bench. With that said, the 27-year-old has remained a reliable contributor as a reserve, scoring at least 20 points in four of his five appearances heading into the meeting with Indiana.

items.headline: Sexton racked up 18 points (8-14 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes during Wednesday's 145-126 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Sexton continues to play a sizeable role for the Bulls, scoring at least 16 points for the sixth straight game. While Chicago's rotation doesn't always make a lot of sense, it appears as though Sexton is in good favor right now. In four appearances over the past week, he has been a top-45 fantasy player, averaging 21.5 points, 3.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 3.0 three-pointers. Josh Giddey (hamstring) was sidelined for Wednesday's contest.

items.headline: Sexton will start Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: After providing a massive offensive spark off the bench over his last five appearances, the 27-year-old guard will rejoin the first unit Wednesday due to Josh Giddey being unavailable. Sexton has been on an absolute tear recently, pouring in at least 20 points in four of his last five outings. He'll look to continue that production in the starting lineup Wednesday.

items.headline: Sexton finished Monday's 129-114 loss to the Spurs with 20 points (8-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 27 minutes.
items.story: Sexton continues to find ways to put up points even if he doesn't start regularly, and his scoring surge has been huge for managers who are trusting him down the stretch across all fantasy formats. Sexton is ending the regular season on a strong note and has scored at least 20 points in four of his last five outings while reaching the 25-point plateau twice in that span.

items.headline: Sexton accumulated 26 points (6-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 11-13 FT), one rebound, two assists and two steals across 30 minutes during Saturday's 125-124 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Sexton scored at least 20 points for the third time in his past four games, continuing to provide the Bulls with a nice offensive punch off the bench. Although his overall appeal is somewhat limited, Sexton has been doing more than enough to be rostered in most leagues. In 11 games over the past month, he has averaged 20.2 points, 1.2 steals and 2.8 three-pointers in 25.4 minutes per game, good enough for top-65 value in standard formats.

items.headline: Sexton closed with 25 points (6-14 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 9-10 FT), four rebounds, two assists and three steals in 26 minutes during Monday's 132-124 victory over Houston.
items.story: Sexton has now scored at least 20 points in five of his past seven appearances. Despite coming off the bench, he has been able to provide the Bulls with an offensive boost, while also managing to flirt with top-100 value in standard nine-category leagues. For those needing points and threes, he is worth considering as a potential stream option when the schedule lays out nicely.

items.headline: Sexton will start Thursday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Sexton will enter Chicago's starting five for the fourth time this season. Over three starts for the Bulls, the 27-year-old guard has averaged 18.3 points, 3.0 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 29.3 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Sexton (fibula) is available for Thursday's game against Cleveland, Will Gottlieb of AllCHGO.com reports.
items.story: As expected, Sexton has been cleared to suit up for a second consecutive contest following a four-game absence due to a left fibular head contusion. He logged 18 minutes in Wednesday's loss to Toronto, finishing with 14 points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five assists, two rebounds and one steal.

items.headline: Sexton (fibula) is probable for Thursday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: The veteran guard is expected to be available for the second part of this back-to-back set. Sexton has averaged 16.0 points, 2.3 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 24.5 minutes per tilt over 13 games for the Bulls, shooting 50.0 percent from the field during that span.

items.headline: Sexton (fibula) notched 14 points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 6-8 FT), five assists, two rebounds and one steal over 18 minutes during Wednesday's 139-109 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Sexton fared well in his return from a four-game absence due to a left fibular head contusion. He'll likely be a key part of the second unit going forward, but Sexton could struggle to reach the 20-minute mark with any regularity if the Bulls end up getting Anfernee Simons (wrist) back from injury at any point over the final few weeks of the season.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) will play in Wednesday's game against Toronto, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Sexton was initially listed as questionable for Wednesday's contest, though he'll shed that tag and return from a four-game absence. His return may result in Rob Dillingham seeing fewer minutes, though Jaden Ivey (knee) and Anfernee Simons (wrist) are both still out. Over four March appearances (one start), Sexton has averaged 25.0 points, 3.0 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 30.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Sexton (lower leg) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Sexton has a chance to end a four-game absence with a left lower-leg contusion. With Anfernee Simons (wrist) and Jaden Ivey (knee) both sidelined, Tre Jones is worth streaming in most fantasy leagues, and Rob Dillingham should be on the radaer in deeper formats until Sexton is cleared to return.

items.headline: Hansen accumulated six points (2-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal in 13 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 win over Utah.
items.story: Hansen earned a season-high 13 minutes with Donovan Clingan limited to just 15 minutes due to foul trouble against the Jazz. Hansen's playing time will continue to fluctuate between the Blazers and the Rip City Remix of the G League, and his opportunities should remain limited as long as Clingan and Robert Williams are both healthy.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers exercised their third-year team option on Hansen for the 2027-28 season, the team announced Thursday.
items.story: Portland's decision keeps the 2025 first-round pick under contract through the 2027-28 campaign. The 7-foot-1 center remains a developmental piece in the Trail Blazers' frontcourt, where Donovan Clingan currently occupies the starting role. The transaction has no immediate impact on Hansen's fantasy outlook, as his value will depend on his ability to carve out a consistent role in Portland's rotation.

items.headline: Hansen was assigned to the Rip City Remix on Wednesday, the Trail Blazers announced.
items.story: With Portland sending him to the G League, Hansen is set for additional developmental reps away from the NBA roster. The move suggests the center won't be part of the Trail Blazers' immediate rotation while he's with the Remix.

items.headline: Yang finished with 13 points (6-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt), four rebounds and four assists across 21 minutes off the bench in Monday's 119-66 preseason victory over the London Lions.
items.story: Yang delivered an efficient performance, converting six of his eight field-goal attempts while matching Deni Avdija for the second-most assists on the team. The second-year center also connected on his lone three-point attempt and played more minutes than any other Portland player. However, with Donovan Clingan and Robert Williams (rest) ahead of him in the frontcourt rotation, Yang may have difficulty carving out a substantial role during the regular season.

items.headline: Hansen registered 19 points (8-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one block in 25 minutes during China's 89-87 win over Lebanon in Monday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Hansen starred for China on Monday, leading the club in scoring and rebounding. Hansen, a 2025 first-rounder, is looking to carve out a more prominent role in his second season with Portland, but he'll likely need to overtake Robert Williams and Micah Potter for a rotation spot. With that in mind, Hansen's most likely pathway to steady playing time resides with the G League's Rip City Remix.

items.headline: Hansen recorded 15 points (7-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 20 minutes during China's 83-57 win over Qatar in Thursday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Hansen came off the bench but led China in both scoring and rebounding, continuing an encouraging offseason for the 21-year-old center. The 2025 first-round pick had a limited role as a rookie with Portland, averaging just 2.2 points and 1.5 rebounds per game during the regular season, but he'll have an opportunity to push for a larger role in his sophomore campaign.

items.headline: Hansen recorded nine points (3-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 24 minutes during Friday's 83-79 Summer League loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Hansen led the Blazers in rebounds and was one point shy from recording his second double-double over his last three Summer League games. The 2025 first-rounder is set to enter training camp battling with Robert Williams, Sidy Cissoko and Micah Potter for the backup center job behind Donovan Clingan for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Hansen finished with 13 points (6-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and four blocks across 26 minutes in Thursday's 108-101 Summer League victory over the Nuggets.
items.story: Hansen didn't have his most productive offensive showing Thursday, but he certainly got after it on the defensive end by finishing the evening with four blocks. The 21-year-old appeared in 43 regular-season games for the Trail Blazers in 2025-26, averaging 2.2 points and 1.5 rebounds over 7.0 minutes. Although Hansen's development is still a work in progress, it's reasonable to assume he will continue to improve throughout the 2026-27 campaign, especially if he gets more playing time.

items.headline: Hansen racked up 18 points (7-8 FG, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds and five assists across 21 minutes in Monday's 111-84 Summer League win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Hansen missed the front end of this back-to-back set with an illness but returned to action Monday. The big man turned in an extremely efficient performance and finished as Portland's second-leading scorer. He also grabbed a game-high 10 rebounds while leading the Trail Blazers in assists. Hansen has supplied at least nine boards and four dimes in both of his Las Vegas Summer League appearances.

items.headline: Hansen (illness) is available for Monday's Summer League game against Minnesota.
items.story: Hansen will return Monday, marking his second appearance of the Las Vegas Summer League. The 21-year-old last played in Friday's 81-79 loss to Phoenix, finishing with 12 points, nine rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes.

items.headline: Hansen (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game against the Magic.
items.story: Hansen is under the weather and will miss the front end of this back-to-back set. The big man's next chance to play will come Monday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Hansen finished Friday's 81-79 Summer League loss to the Suns with 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), nine rebounds and four assists over 26 minutes.
items.story: The second-year center led the Trail Blazers in rebounds, finishing one board shy of a double-double, while ending as the team's third-leading scorer behind DJ Steward (21 points) and Frankie Fidler (13 points). Hansen averaged just 7.0 minutes per game across 43 regular-season contests during the 2025-26 campaign, and he'll battle against Robert Williams for the backup center role behind Donovan Clingan for the upcoming season.

items.headline: Hansen is expected to play in the 2026 NBA Summer League, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: Hansen will join Portland's Summer League squad after he is done playing for China in the FIBA World Cup qualifier. The 2025 No. 16 overall pick is coming off a quiet inaugural campaign during which he averaged 2.2 points, 1.5 rebounds, 0.5 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.1 steals across 7.0 minutes in 43 regular-season appearances. With the Trail Blazers in need of depth behind Donovan Clingan, Hansen will need to impress during Summer League and throughout training camp if he hopes to earn a meaningful role for the team in the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Hansen contributed zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) in one minute during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hansen's role with Portland was sparse during his rookie year, as he also made 14 G League appearances for the Rip City Remix. Overall, the 2025 first-rounder averaged 2.2 points, 1.5 rebounds and 0.5 assists in 7.0 minutes per contest over 43 regular-season games with the Trail Blazers. Robert Williams is an impending unrestricted free agent this summer, however, so Hansen could have an opportunity during training camp to claim the top backup center role behind Donovan Clingan.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Saturday.
items.story: Hansen will rejoin the Trail Blazers after appearing in the Remix's last two contests and averaging 19.0 points, 8.0 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks in 33.0 minutes. Unless Portland is without at least one of Donovan Clingan and Robert Williams for Sunday's game against Washington, Hansen isn't expected to be featured in the rotation.

items.headline: Portland assigned Hansen to the G League's Rip City Remix on Tuesday.
items.story: Hansen logged nine minutes at the NBA level Monday against Brooklyn, finishing with four points and three rebounds. He'll continue to see the bulk of his minutes with Rip City in the short term.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Monday.
items.story: The Trail Blazers will play the second leg of a back-to-back set Monday, so Hansen will be summoned to provide further depth in the frontcourt in the event Robert Williams (knee) is rested. Even if Williams ends up sitting out, Hansen won't be assured a spot in the Portland rotation, as interim head coach Tiago Splitter could turn to Sidy Cissoko to serve as a small-ball center when starter Donovan Clingan is off the court.

items.headline: Hansen played the final 48.9 seconds of Friday's 124-114 win over the Jazz, finishing with no statistics during his time on the court.
items.story: Recalled from the G League's Rip City Remix prior to Friday's contest, Hansen was unable to crack the Portland rotation while the game was competitive. Even though the Trail Blazers were without their top backup center in Robert Williams (knee) on Friday, interim head coach Tiago Splitter opted to run out small-ball lineups when starting center Donovan Clingan was off the court. Hansen looks like he'll continue to receive limited run at the NBA level for the rest of the season while he's yet to gain full trust of the coaching staff.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers assigned Hansen to the G League's Rip City Remix on Tuesday.
items.story: As such, Hansen won't be available for Tuesday's game against the Hornets. The rookie first-rounder has bounced back and forth between the G League and NBA this season, but he has not played double-digit minutes for Portland since Jan. 27 against Washington. In his last G League outing against the Valley Suns on Saturday, Hansen finished with 15 points (6-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal over 23 minutes.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Saturday.
items.story: Hansen appeared in Rip City's wins over the Valley Suns on Friday and Saturday, totaling 36 points and 18 rebounds in those two outings. He hasn't logged double-digit minutes for the parent club since Jan. 27, a trend that is likely to continue Sunday versus the Pacers.

items.headline: Hansen (back) is available for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder will shed his questionable tag due to mid-back soreness and could see increased playing time Sunday due to Robert Williams (knee) being sidelined. Hansen appeared in eight outings in February, during which he averaged 1.8 points in 4.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Hansen is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Hawks due to mid-back soreness.
items.story: Hansen was able to play through the issue in Thursday's win over the Bulls, though he saw just two minutes of playing time. However, if he's cleared to play Sunday, Hansen would be in line for a larger role off the bench due to the absence of Robert Williams (knee).

items.headline: Hansen (back) is available for Thursday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Hansen popped up on the Blazers' injury report Wednesday due to mid-back soreness, but the rookie first-rounder has been given the green light to play Thursday. Donovan Clingan (illness) won't play, so Hansen and Robert Williams are slated for elevated roles in Clingan's absence.

items.headline: Hansen is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Bulls due to mid-back soreness.
items.story: Hansen may have picked up the injury during his most recent appearance in the G League with the Rip City Remix on Sunday, when he posted 11 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 29 minutes in a 118-113 loss to the Santa Cruz Warriors. Robert Williams (foot) is also listed as questionable, so if both Williams and Hansen aren't available Thursday, Portland could turn to Sidy Cissoko or Jerami Grant to play center when starter Donovan Clingan is off the court.

items.headline: Hansen totaled no counting stats in four minutes during Friday's 127-97 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Hansen appeared during garbage time, continuing what has been a disappointing rookie season thus far. Although he has been able to see the court on most nights over the past month, his playing time remains largely underwhelming. In his last 12 appearances, he has averaged 2.1 points and 1.8 rebounds in 8.6 minutes per game. Outside of dynasty formats, he holds no fantasy value at this point.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Tuesday.
items.story: The rookie first-round pick should be available for the Trail Blazers' next game Thursday versus the Heat but is unlikely to be included in the rotation.

items.headline: Portland recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Saturday.
items.story: Hansen will be available to play Saturday against the Lakers after being recalled. He last appeared for the Blazers on Tuesday, logging three points and two rebounds in 13 minutes.

items.headline: Hansen (coach's decision) didn't appear off the bench Thursday in the Trail Blazers' 117-101 win over the Hawks.
items.story: After making an appearance in the G League for the Rip City Remix on Wednesday and producing 22 points, seven rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal in 30 minutes in a 123-99 win over the Oklahoma City Blue, Hansen rejoined Portland ahead of its matchup with the Hawks. However, the rookie big man found himself outside of the rotation, as Portland went with Jerami Grant, Robert Williams and Duop Reath as its reserve big men before frontcourt starters Sidy Cissoko and Donovan Clingan. Hansen could have more G League assignments in his future if playing time remains hard to come by at the NBA level.

items.headline: Hansen collected 22 points (6-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and two blocks in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 123-99 G League win over the Oklahoma City Blue.
items.story: Hansen led the Rip City Remix in points Wednesday to go with a full stat line. The rookie first-rounder is averaging 17.2 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.0 steals per game over six G League appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Hansen provided two points (0-1 FG, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 11 minutes during Saturday's 115-110 win over the Spurs.
items.story: Hansen played at least 10 minutes for the fourth time in the past five games, although his production has not followed suit. During that time, the rookie has averaged just 1.6 points and 2.0 rebounds, highlighting just how far he has to go before he becomes a viable NBA center.

items.headline: The Trail Blazers recalled Hansen from the G League's Rip City Remix on Monday.
items.story: Hansen joined the Remix for Monday's 116-110 win over the Stockton Kings, recording 18 points (8-11 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 10 rebounds and four assists in 31 minutes. He hasn't seen the floor in each of Portland's last two games and isn't likely to play meaningful minutes unless there are injuries to multiple centers.

items.headline: Hansen was assigned to the G League's Rip City Remix on Monday.
items.story: Hansen has been splitting time between the Trail Blazers and the Remix all season. The Blazers got back Donovan Clingan (leg) and Robert Williams (illness) on Sunday.

items.headline: Hansen (face) is available for Sunday's game against the Warriors, Sean Highkin of Rip City Radio 620 Portland reports.
items.story: Hansen didn't play in Thursday's loss to the Pelicans due to a face injury, but the rookie first-rounder has been cleared to play Sunday. He started in his last outing, but he'll likely come off the bench due to the returns of Donovan Clingan (lower leg) and Robert Williams (illness).

items.headline: Hansen (face) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Hansen is in jeopardy of missing his second consecutive contest due to a facial contusion. However, if the rookie is cleared to play, he could see increased minutes if Donovan Clingan (lower leg) is downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Hansen (face) will not play Thursday against the Pelicans.
items.story: Portland is going to be very thin in the frontcourt Thursday with Donovan Clingan (leg) and Robert Williams (illness) both out as well. As a result, the team could lean on Duop Reath and Kris Murray.

items.headline: Camara ended Saturday's 112-90 victory over Utah with 14 points (4-9 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two steals in 31 minutes.
items.story: The fourth-year forward continues to fill up the bucket from long distance. Camara has drained at least three three-pointers in five straight games to open the season, averaging 15.2 points, 4.0 threes, 2.2 boards, 1.4 steals and 1.2 assists in 26.2 minutes and shooting a blistering 51.3 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Camara produced 13 points (5-10 FG, 3-8 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two steals across 26 minutes during Thursday's 124-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Camara scored double digits for the fourth straight game, adding four combined steals and blocks. He has been arguably Portland's most consistent performer, averaging 15.5 points, 1.3 steals, and 4.0 three-pointers in 25.0 minutes per game. He is currently shooting an impressive 61.1 percent from the field, well above what he has done throughout his career. Taking this into consideration, he could be viewed as a potential sell-high candidate.

items.headline: Camara closed with 12 points (4-5 FG, 4-5 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 24 minutes during Tuesday's 136-129 victory over the Lakers.
items.story: Portland went with the hot hand of Jrue Holiday over Camara down the stretch, but Camara was efficient in his own right. Camara should remain entrenched as a starter for the Trail Blazers going forward.

items.headline: Camara registered 19 points (7-12 FG, 5-10 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 27 minutes in Friday's 128-120 win over the Kings.
items.story: Camara has been shooting the lights out through the first two games of the season, converting 61.9 percent of his shot attempts, including 52.9 percent of those from behind the arc. Those numbers are naturally unsustainable over time, but for now, he is getting a ton of wide-open looks playing alongside Ja Morant, Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija.

items.headline: Camara recorded 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and three assists in 23 minutes during Wednesday's 124-83 win over the Suns.
items.story: Every Trail Blazers starter scored in double digits, and the team built a 21-0 lead in the first quarter before the visitors even got on the board. Camara will look to provide stable secondary scoring in an offense that flows through the veteran backcourt of Damian Lillard and Ja Morant, and the fourth-year forward is coming off a career-best 2025-26 campaign that saw him average 13.4 points, 5.1 boards, 2.7 threes, 2.4 assists and 1.1 steals in 33.3 minutes while playing all 82 regular-season games.

items.headline: Camara posted 14 points (4-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one steal across 15 minutes in Monday's 119-66 preseason victory over the London Lions.
items.story: Camara made the most of his limited playing time, tying Scoot Henderson for the team lead in points while shooting efficiently from the field and converting all four of his free-throw attempts. The 26-year-old forward started alongside Portland's other regulars and contributed across multiple categories. His combination of perimeter shooting and defensive versatility should help him maintain a significant role in the Trail Blazers' rotation.

items.headline: Camara finished with five points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and one steal over 19 minutes in Wednesday's 123-118 preseason win over the Warriors.
items.story: Camara made his preseason debut Wednesday. The fourth-year forward has been a full-time starter for Portland in back-to-back seasons and should retain that role in 2026-27, especially given that Shaedon Sharpe (knee) is likely to be sidelined until March.

items.headline: Camara should continue to play a major role following Portland's trade for Ja Morant, according to Robert Ohman of Willamette Week.
items.story: The Trail Blazers have been reluctant to include Camara in trade discussions because of his defensive value, and he'll remain an important complementary piece alongside Ja Morant, Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija. Camara's fantasy value should continue to be driven primarily by steals, rebounds and hustle stats in general.

items.headline: Camara chipped in seven points (2-10 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds and two assists in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 114-95 loss to the Spurs in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Camara appeared in all 82 regular-season games for Portland, playing a key role with 33.3 minutes per game. He averaged 13.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.7 three-pointers, but he struggled with efficiency, shooting 44.0 percent from the field and 70.8 percent from the line.

items.headline: Camara totaled 10 points (3-7 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, one assist, one block and three steals across 35 minutes during Tuesday's 106-103 win over the Spurs in Game 2 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Camara posted a well-rounded stat line as the Trail Blazers leveled the series at one win apiece. Through two games, Camara holds averages of 9.0 points, 5.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.0 blocks and  2.5 steals in 33.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Camara registered eight points (3-9 FG, 2-7 3Pt), four rebounds and four steals in 36 minutes during Tuesday's 114-110 Play-In Tournament win over the Suns.
items.story: Despite struggling on the offensive end, Camara did what he does best, accumulating a game-high four steals. After a slow start to the season, Camara has turned things around at the right time, putting up top-35 fantasy numbers over the past month. Portland will now face San Antonio in the first round of the playoffs, and Camara may need to be at his best if the Trail Blazers are to pull off an upset.

items.headline: Camara registered 30 points (10-16 FG, 8-13 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and one steal in 35 minutes before fouling out of Monday's 137-132 overtime loss to Denver.
items.story: Camara's explosive total wasn't enough to seal the deal for Portland, who desperately needed a win to keep pace with the Clippers in the playoff race.  Although postseason hopes looked bleak after Shaedon Sharpe's (calf) injury, Camara has made the issue a non-factor with standout totals over the past two months.
