Through six postseason games, Dosunmu has put in averages of 18.2 points, 3.3 assists and 2.0 triples per contest on 58.0/52.0/95.0 shooting splits.

items.headline: Dosunmu (heel) is questionable for Friday's Game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs.
items.story: Dosunmu was previously hampered by a right calf injury but exited Wednesday's Game 2 early due to right heel soreness. The guard was highly effective to begin the postseason before injuries surfaced, averaging 21.8 points, 4.0 assists and 2.8 rebounds across the first five games of the opening-round series against the Nuggets. If Dosunmu is unavailable, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon could see increased opportunities.

items.headline: Dosunmu (heel) won't return to Wednesday's Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals versus the Spurs, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
items.story: Dosunmu was cleared to return for this contest after missing the last two games because of a calf injury. However, he exited Wednesday night with a right heel issue. The 26-year-old finished without a point (0-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt), adding one steal across 10 minutes. The Spurs and Timberwolves will meet again for Game 3 on Friday night, although it's possible Dosunmu may not be cleared to suit up. If that's the case, Bones Hyland, Mike Conley and Terrence Shannon should see more action.

items.headline: Dosunmu is questionable to return to Wednesday's Game 2 matchup with the Spurs due to right heel pain.
items.story: Dosunmu just returned from a right calf injury, but now his right heel is giving him trouble. If he's not able to return, there will be more minutes available for Bones Hyland.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) won't have a minutes restriction for Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals against San Antonio, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletici reports.
items.story: Dosunmu will return after a two-game stint on the shelf. Although Anthony Edwards (knee) has also been cleared to suit up, Dosunmu should still get all the minutes he can handle. As a result, Terrence Shannon, Mike Conley and Bones Hyland are expected to spend more time on the bench.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is available for Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs on Wednesday.
items.story: Dosunmu is set to return following a two-game absence. As of now, it's unclear if he will face any restrictions for this game. With this news, Terrence Shannon may see a reduced role. However, Anthony Edwards (knee) remains questionable after he surprisingly returned to action in a reserve role during Game 1.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is questionable for Game 2 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs on Wednesday.
items.story: Dosunmu has a chance to end a two-game absence with right calf soreness Wednesday. Terrence Shannon, who has logged 35 minutes in back-to-back contests for the Timberwolves, would likely be pushed into a lesser role if Dosunmu is available for Game 2.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is out for Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs on Monday.
items.story: The swingman also missed Minnesota's Game 7 win over the Nuggets in Round 1 due to right calf soreness. The Timberwolves are planning to have Anthony Edwards (knee) back in the lineup Monday, which should lessen the blow of Dosunmu's absence. Dosunmu will try to return for Game 2 on Wednesday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is questionable for Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs on Monday.
items.story: Dosunmu was held out of Thursday's Game 6 win over the Nuggets in the first round due to right calf soreness, and he may miss a second consecutive contest. Terrence Shannon would likely continue seeing a significant bump in minutes if Dosunmu is ruled out, though Bones Hyland could also see increased playing time.

items.headline: Head coach Chris Finch told reporters Saturday that Dosunmu is considered "day-to-day" due to his right calf injury, Jace Frederick of St. Paul Pioneer Press reports.
items.story: Dosunmu's calf injury prevented him from playing in the Timberwolves' Game 6 victory against the Nuggets on Thursday. Game 1 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs kicks off Monday, and Dosunmu could join Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) and Anthony Edwards (knee) on the sidelines for that contest. If Dosunmu is not cleared to play, then Terrence Shannon, Bones Hyland and Jaylen Clark would be in line for expanded roles alongside Mike Conley and Jaden McDaniels.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is out for Game 6 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Nuggets on Thursday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: This is a devastating loss for the Timberwolves, who will also be without Anthony Edwards (knee), Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) and Kyle Anderson (illness) on Thursday. There should be plenty of minutes available in the backcourt for Terrence Shannon and Bones Hyland in Dosunmu's absence.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is a game-time decision for Thursday's Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs against Denver, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Dosunmu was added to the injury report earlier in the day after experiencing calf soreness. The Timberwolves will presumably wait to see how he feels during warmups before providing an update on his status.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is questionable for Thursday's Game 6 against the Nuggets.
items.story: Dosunmu is a late addition to the injury report, joining Bones Hyland (knee) as questionable. With Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) out, Dosunmu has stepped up and turned into a go-to player for Minnesota. If Dosunmu and Hyland are in street clothes Thursday, Terrence Shannon, Jaylen Clark and Julian Phillips would likely be thrust into expanded roles.

items.headline: Dosunmu closed Monday's 125-113 loss to Denver in Game 5 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with 18 points (7-14 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, four assists and one steal in 38 minutes.
items.story: Amid absences from Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles), the Timberwolves have relied heavily on Dosunmu, and his results have often been the difference between victory and defeat. Although he was accurate from the floor, the Nuggets were successful in defending him and curtailing his production. A better result from Dosunmu will be essential in closing out this series.

items.headline: Dosunmu is starting Monday's Game 5 of the Western Conference first-round series against Denver.
items.story: Dosunmu was clearly up for the challenge in Game 4 after Anthony Edwards went down with a knee injury. The Illinois product finished with a career-high 43 points in 42 minutes, leading the Timberwolves to a 3-1 series advantage. Minnesota will need more of the same in Game 5, as the Timberwolves will be without the services of Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles).

items.headline: Dosunmu posted 43 points (13-17 FG, 5-5 3Pt, 12-12 FT), four rebounds, an assist and a block across 42 minutes off the bench in Saturday's Game 4 win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Not only did Dosumnu post a career-high scoring mark, he also scored the second-most points off the bench in playoff history. The five-year veteran was coming off a 25-point performance in Game 3, and Dosumnu is pretty much locked into a bigger role, as Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) will miss the rest of the playoffs, while Anthony Edwards (knee) is uncertain to be available for Game 5 on Monday.

items.headline: Dosunmu ended with 25 points (10-15 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and nine assists over 32 minutes during Thursday's 113-96 win over the Nuggets in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Dosunmu earned his keep in the win, scoring a team-high 25 points and powering Minnesota to an important home victory. Despite continuing to come off the bench, Dosunmu has been a key piece for the Timberwolves ever since being acquired in a trade with the Bulls. Now leading the series 2-1, Minnesota will look to build on that advantage when the two teams meet again on Saturday.

items.headline: Dosunmu posted 14 points (5-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one assist and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 116-105 loss to the Nuggets in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Dosunmu helped the Timberwolves keep things close with nine points in the first half, and he finished Saturday's game as the bench's scoring leader. He has given the Timberwolves the scoring punch off the bench that they were hoping for when they acquired Dosunmu from the Bulls in early February. However, he may need to be leaned on even more heavily in the postseason, especially if the Nuggets' defense focus its efforts on slowing down Anthony Edwards.

items.headline: Dosunmu (calf) is off the injury report for Game 1 on Saturday versus Denver.
items.story: Dosunmu sat out Minnesota's regular-season finale, but he's good to go for the beginning of the postseason Saturday. The swingman averaged 14.4 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 28.9 minutes per contest over 24 games for the Timberwolves in 2025-26.

items.headline: Lovering signed a two-way contract with the Lakers on Wednesday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: After being waived by the Grizzlies ahead of training camp, Lovering will join the Lakers and provide frontcourt depth while on a two-way contract. In a corresponding move, the club waived AK Okereke. Lovering appeared in 30 G League games with the Memphis Hustle last season, averaging 7.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.3 blocks and 0.7 steals in 26.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Lovering was waived by the Grizzlies on Monday.
items.story: Lovering won't get the chance to compete for a spot on Memphis' regular-season roster during training camp, and he's now expected to report to the club's G League affiliate, the Memphis Hustle. In 30 appearances with the Hustle last season, the big man averaged 7.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.3 blocks and 0.7 steals in 26.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Lovering signed a contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday.
items.story: The exact terms of the contract are unclear, though this is likely an Exhibit 10 deal for the big man. Lovering appeared in two regular-season games (one start) with Memphis in 2025-26 while signed to a 10-day pact. Over 30 G League games with the Memphis Hustle last season, he averaged 7.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.3 blocks and 0.7 steals in 26.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Lovering is in the starting lineup for Friday's matchup with the Jazz.
items.story: This will be just the second game of the season for Lovering, who is getting the start with Santi Aldama (knee) unavailable. Joining Lovering in the starting five for Friday's game will be Jaylen Wells, GG Jackson, Jahmai Mashack and Taylor Hendricks.

items.headline: The Grizzlies are signing Lovering to a 10-day contract Monday, per Michael Scotto of USA Today.
items.story: Lovering gives Memphis an extra healthy body while it waits for Santi Aldama (knee), Brandon Clarke (calf) and Zach Edey (ankle) to return. Lovering is averaging 8.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.4 blocks per game with the Memphis Hustle during the G League regular season.

items.headline: Lovering is not in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason game against the Hawks.
items.story: Lovering is battling for a roster spot with the Grizzlies. While he started against Boston on Oct. 8, he will have to wait for an opportunity off the bench in this one.

items.headline: Lovering is part of the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Boston.
items.story: Lovering, a 7-foot-1 undrafted free agent out of Utah, is battling for a spot on the Grizzlies roster. While he faces an uphill climb to do so, he'll have a chance to show his talents Wednesday. In all likelihood, Lovering will wind up playing for the G League's Memphis Hustle.

items.headline: Murphy (knee) is probable for Wednesday's game versus the Jazz.
items.story: Murphy played through the knee issues and logged 40 minutes in Monday's 135-134 win over the Grizzlies, so it clearly didn't impact his playing time. It appears he'll continue to push through the pain Wednesday.

items.headline: Murphy (knee) will play Monday against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Murphy is no longer on the injury report after previously carrying a probable tag. Through six regular-season games, he's averaging 14.3 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3.2 dimes.

items.headline: Murphy (knee) is listed as probable for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Murphy is dealing with bilateral patella tendinopathy, leaving him probable to suit up versus the 6-0 Grizzlies. If he's forced to sit out Monday, Saddiq Bey would stand to be the primary beneficiary alongside Trendon Watford, with Bey the likely candidate to join the starting lineup.

items.headline: Murphy finished with 19 points (6-12 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-8 FT), five rebounds, three assists and a steal across 32 minutes in Thursday's 132-120 win over the Kings.
items.story: Murphy delivered a balanced offensive performance, contributing as both a perimeter scorer and secondary facilitator. His seven three-point attempts reinforced his importance as a floor-spacing option alongside Zion Williamson, although Murphy's shooting efficiency from deep remained inconsistent. His established scoring role and steady playing time provide a useful fantasy foundation, with additional upside when his perimeter shot is falling. The lack of consistency has been an issue so far, but the upside is there. He has scored in double digits in three of his five appearances to date and is shooting 46.4 percent from the field.

items.headline: Murphy amassed six points (2-7 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 0-1 FT), one rebound, three assists and two steals across 30 minutes during Wednesday's 104-91 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Murphy scored a season-low six points Wednesday. Better days are ahead for the star forward, who just dropped 26 points against Denver on Oct. 24 and remains one of the focal points of the New Orleans offense alongside Dejounte Murray and Zion Williamson.

items.headline: Murphy notched 26 points (10-17 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, four assists and one steal across 37 minutes during Saturday's 141-135 overtime loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Murphy had scored just 20 points total in the two games prior, but he did a much better job of asserting himself offensively Saturday night. However, the Pelicans couldn't capitalize on his performance, surrendering a 23-point lead to fall to 0-3 to begin the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Murphy closed with 11 points (4-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds and one assist across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 123-120 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Murphy took a back seat to both Dejounte Murray and Zion Williamson on Wednesday. Despite a fairly quiet season debut, Murphy should still be able to deliver early-round fantasy numbers this season.

items.headline: Murphy supplied 11 points (5-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and two steals across 21 minutes in Friday's 107-106 preseason win over the Wizards.
items.story: Murphy bounced back from a five-point showing against Dallas, reaching double figures for the third time in four preseason games.  The forward should see a heavy workload this season as one of the Pelicans' top multi-category producers.

items.headline: Murphy finished with five points (2-8 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 19 minutes in Wednesday's 101-97 preseason win over Dallas.
items.story: Murphy came off the bench after starting in two of the Pelicans' exhibitions, though he had another inefficient shooting night, which has been a theme during the preseason. However, the 26-year-old has shot 45.9 percent from the field and 38.2 percent from deep throughout his career, so he could turn it around at some point early in the regular season.

items.headline: Murphy posted 11 points (4-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals across 19 minutes in Tuesday's 116-110 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: Murphy was one of five New Orleans players who scored in double digits in this comeback win, and he also made his presence felt with two steals. Expect the veteran forward to be a steady contributor for the Pelicans on both ends of the court when the regular season begins in late October.

items.headline: Murphy has been working alongside Zion Williamson during three-point shooting drills at training camp, offering advice as his teammate attempts to expand his offensive game, Jim Eichenhofer of the Pelicans' official site reports.
items.story: Murphy said he's been giving Williamson pointers during the drills and praised the forward for being willing to listen and put in the work. This highlights Murphy's growing leadership role in New Orleans as he enters his sixth NBA season, while his established perimeter shooting makes him a natural resource for Williamson as the latter works to become a more consistent threat from outside. Murphy is poised to have a considerable role on both ends of the court in 2026-27.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) continued his emergence as one of New Orleans' top offensive weapons before injuries interrupted another strong campaign.
items.story: Murphy's combination of three-point shooting, athleticism and secondary shot creation should once again make him a featured option alongside Zion Williamson. Murphy has averaged at least 21 points, five rebounds, three assists and one steal in back-to-back seasons, but he's made more than 66 regular-season appearances only once in his past five years.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is listed as out for Friday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Murphy will miss a fourth consecutive contest. With Dejounte Murray (hand) also ruled out, Jeremiah Fears and Jordan Poole will likely be the starting options out of the backcourt against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Murphy will miss a third straight game while dealing with a right ankle sprain. He'll have one more opportunity to return for the regular-season finale Sunday in Minnesota.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: The star forward is out for a second consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. Jeremiah Fears looks like the prime candidate to replace Murphy in the starting lineup at shooting guard Tuesday.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Murphy has been downgraded from questionable to out and will be back on the sidelines Sunday after making two straight appearances following a three-game absence. With Dejounte Murray (hand) also sidelined, Jeremiah Fears should see increased usage in New Orleans' backcourt.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Murphy missed three consecutive games because of a sprained right ankle, although he managed to suit up for the Pelicans' last two contests. However, he's back on the injury report for the meeting with Orlando. New Orleans has only four games remaining before the team calls it a season, so it's unknown how much action Murphy will see moving forward. If he doesn't suit up Sunday, Yves Missi will likely re-enter the starting lineup.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is available for Friday's game in Sacramento.
items.story: As expected, Murphy will suit up for a second consecutive contest following a three-game absence due to a right ankle sprain. Over 13 appearances since March 1, the 25-year-old wing has averaged 19.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.6 steals in 35.2 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is probable for Friday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Murphy just returned from a three-game absence with a right ankle sprain during Thursday's loss to the Trail Blazers, and he is expected to play the second half of this back-to-back set. Over his last five appearances, the star forward has averaged 19.0 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.4 steals in 37.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Murphy recorded 19 points (7-17 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and one steal across 36 minutes during Thursday's 118-106 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: After missing the prior three games with a right ankle sprain, Murphy rejoined the lineup and delivered solid production. However, his scoring output came on poor efficiency, and Murphy has now converted on 41.5 percent of his field-goal attempts and 31.8 percent of his three-point tries over his last seven games. With Thursday's contest marking the front end of a back-to-back set, Murphy could be a candidate to sit Friday in Sacramento, though the Pelicans have yet to release an injury report for that game.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) will play Thursday against Portland.
items.story: Murphy has missed his team's last three matchups while tending to a right ankle sprain, but he's been cleared to play Thursday. He'll presumably slot right back into the starting five in his return, which would likely bump Yves Missi back to the bench.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Murphy is in danger of missing his fourth consecutive contest due to a lingering right ankle sprain. With New Orleans already eliminated from postseason contention, the team has little incentive to rush the 25-year-old wing back to the floor. If Murphy remains sidelined Thursday, look for Jeremiah Fears and Jordan Hawkins to continue logging increased minutes.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is out for Sunday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Murphy will miss a third straight game due to a right ankle sprain. Jeremiah Fears and Jordan Hawkins will likely maintain expanded roles with Murphy sidelined. His next chance to suit up comes Thursday against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Houston.
items.story: Murphy is in danger of missing a third consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. If the 25-year-old wing remains sidelined, Jeremiah Fears and Jordan Hawkins could continue seeing increased playing time.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Murphy will miss his second game in a row, but he remains day-to-day. The Pelicans are out of the playoff hunt, so the team may be cautious going forward. Jeremiah Fears and Jordan Hawkins could be more involved as a result Friday.

items.headline: Murphy (ankle) is out for Thursday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Murphy will miss his first action since Feb. 28 after picking up a right ankle injury. In the past, the Pelicans have elected to start both Herbert Jones and Yves Missi when without Murphy, though Jeremiah Fears could also be more heavily involved in the rotation with Murphy sidelined Thursday.

items.headline: Murphy is questionable for Thursday's game against the Pistons with right ankle soreness.
items.story: Thursday's game is the front end of a back-to-back set, and with the Pelicans no longer in the mix for a playoff spot, a maintenance day is surely on the table. If he's held out Thursday, Jeremiah Fears and Jordan Poole could take on larger roles.

items.headline: Murphy ended Tuesday's 121-116 loss to the Knicks with 16 points (6-15 FG, 4-12 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists and one steal in 36 minutes.
items.story: With the Pelicans eliminated from the playoffs with this loss, it will be interesting to see how the team handles Murphy's minutes and usage the rest of the way. Through 64 appearances this season, Murphy holds averages of 21.7 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.5 steals and 3.3 three-pointers.

items.headline: Murphy notched 27 points (9-17 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal across 35 minutes in Thursday's 105-99 win over the Clippers.
items.story: After averaging 18.0 points per game on 40.4 percent shooting from the field over his previous three outings, Murphy turned in an efficient performance in the second leg of this back-to-back set. The 25-year-old wing led all players in scoring and knocked down five triples for the second time this month, during which he has made at least four triples seven times. He has also reached the 20-point mark in back-to-back outings and in seven of 10 March games.

items.headline: Murphy generated 23 points (7-17 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block across 40 minutes of Wednesday's 124-109 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Murphy had a strong all-around performance, racking up multiple steals for the seventh time in the last nine games and posting at least five rebounds and five assists for a third straight outing. The 25-year-old is averaging career highs in points (21.9), rebounds (5.7), assists (3.9) and steals (1.6) across 61 appearances this season.

items.headline: Murphy recorded 14 points (5-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds and seven assists across 37 minutes during Friday's 107-105 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Murphy had a rough shooting performance, needing 15 shots to score 14 points. This outing snapped a five-game stretch in which Murphy scored at least 21 points each time, but he regularly attempts around 15 shots per game, so the expectation is that this was just a bad shooting performance for the fifth-year forward. After all, Murphy is shooting 45.1 percent from the floor and 47.4 percent from three-point range since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Murphy generated 28 points (8-12 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and three steals across 34 minutes of Wednesday's 122-111 win over the Raptors.
items.story: Murphy hit the 25-point milestone for the 16th time this season, and his 12 field-goal attempts were the fewest he's taken to get there. The sharpshooting wing has now knocked down at least four three-pointers in five of his last six games, and he's generated a total of 12 steals during that stretch. He'll look to extend his streak of 20-point games to six when the Pelicans face Houston on Friday.

items.headline: Murphy racked up 22 points (6-17 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 6-7 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals over 41 minutes during Friday's 118-116 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Despite dealing with minor neck spasms earlier in the week, Murphy looked just fine Friday as he logged a massive 41-minute workload. While his efficiency from the floor was slightly down, he made his presence felt by getting to the line and connecting on four triples for the second consecutive night. The fifth-year wing has been highly productive since returning from a shoulder injury, averaging 21.3 points, 3.7 triples and 2.0 steals over his last three appearances.

items.headline: Murphy closed with 21 points (7-14 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals across 32 minutes during Thursday's 133-123 win over Sacramento.
items.story: The fifth-year wing has been locked in from long range since missing the first five games after the All-Star break due to a shoulder issue. Over three games since getting back onto the court, Murphy is averaging 19.3 points, 5.7 boards, 3.7 assists, 3.7 threes and 2.0 steals while shooting 47.8 percent (11-for-23) from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Carter ended with six points (2-6 FG, 2-6 3Pt) and three assists across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Carter attempted all six of his shots from beyond the arc, connecting twice while failing to register a rebound or defensive statistic. The veteran guard saw a reasonable amount of playing time off the bench but struggled to make a meaningful impact. His fantasy appeal remains limited to deeper formats where three-point shooting is at a premium, even with Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) sidelined indefinitely.

items.headline: Carter (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 132-125 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Carter wasn't called upon in Orlando's season opener, suggesting he'll primarily serve as backcourt depth. The veteran guard will likely need an injury or a rotation adjustment to receive consistent playing time.

items.headline: Carter finished with two points (1-5 FG, 0-3 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists and one steal in 19 minutes during Sunday's 119-105 preseason loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Carter struggled to find his shooting touch but contributed as a facilitator, recording four assists without committing a turnover. The veteran guard continues to compete for backcourt minutes, though his limited offensive production and Orlando's guard depth could restrict his fantasy value heading into the regular season.

items.headline: Carter will sign a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Magic, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Wednesday.
items.story: Carter will be penciled in as the third-string point guard ahead of Opening Night, behind Jalen Suggs and Anthony Black. During the 2025-26 regular season, Carter appeared in 53 contests between the Bulls and Magic, posting averages of 6.4 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.6 assists.

items.headline: Carter had zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one assist in 11 minutes during Sunday's 116-94 loss to Detroit in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: After being waived by the Bulls ahead of a busy trade deadline in February, Carter signed a one-year contract with the Magic and was a veteran presence for a young club. He wound up playing a fairly decent role for Orlando, closing with averages of 7.2 points, 2.3 assists, 2.1 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 20.4 minutes per contest across 30 regular-season games for the Magic.

items.headline: Carter (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Wednesday in the Magic's 109-97 loss to the 76ers in the Play-In Tournament.
items.story: Carter had appeared in all 29 of the Magic's games following the All-Star break and averaged 7.4 points, 2.3 assists, 2.1 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 21.0 minutes, but he ended up being the odd man out Wednesday with head coach Jamahl Mosley cutting his rotation down to nine men for the playoff opener. With Jalen Suggs logging heavy minutes Wednesday as the Magic's starting point guard and with Franz Wagner and Anthony Black also beginning to see more playing time after having their minutes monitored carefully late in the regular season following their returns from extended absences, Carter will likely struggle to see the court for the duration of Orlando's playoff run.

items.headline: Carter totaled three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two assists and one steal across 16 minutes during Wednesday's 130-101 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: The Magic used a deep rotation in this blowout loss, but Carter was unable to make much of an impact in this one. Over his last eight games, he's averaging 7.3 points, 1.8 assists and 1.6 rebounds in 20.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Carter won't start Tuesday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Carter got the starting nod in place of Jalen Suggs (illness) during Monday's loss to Indiana, but Jamal Cain will enter the starting five for Suggs in the second leg of this back-to-back. Carter has averaged 11.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.2 steals across 18.8 minutes per game over his last five outings off the bench.

items.headline: Carter posted two points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal in 24 minutes during Monday's 128-126 loss to Indiana.
items.story: Carter was elevated into the starting lineup after Jalen Suggs was ruled out due to an illness. Having scored in double digits in four straight games coming into Monday, the hope was that Carter would make for an interesting stream option. However, those who took a chance on him were met with nothing but disappointment, as Carter recorded arguably his worst performance since joining the Magic. At this point, he should only be on the radar for streaming purposes, if and when the schedule works in his favor.

items.headline: Carter will start Monday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: With Jalen Suggs (illness) joining Anthony Black (abdomen) and Franz Wagner (ankle) on the sidelines, Carter will get the starting nod for the first time this season. Over 12 appearances in March, the 30-year-old guard has averaged 8.4 points, 2.8 assists and 2.4 rebounds in 21.4 minutes per contest, though he'll likely see an uptick in minutes with the first unit.

items.headline: Carter finished Thursday's 130-111 loss to the Hornets with 11 points (4-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and two steals in 19 minutes.
items.story: Carter provided a scoring spark for Orlando's second unit Thursday, reaching double-digit points for the third consecutive game. It is a notable turnaround for the veteran guard, who had failed to reach that mark in each of his previous six appearances before this stretch. Carter has maintained a consistent role in the rotation following the return of Jalen Suggs, appearing for at least 16 minutes in 16 straight outings with the Magic. Since joining the Magic in mid-February, Carter is averaging 8.2 points and 2.8 assists across 21.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Carter finished with nine points (3-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists, one block and one steal over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 128-122 victory over the Cavaliers.
items.story: With Anthony Black (abdomen) and Franz Wagner (ankle) still sidelined, Carter continues to soak up additional minutes in the second unit. Over his last seven games, he's averaging 23.5 minutes with 7.7 points, 3.4 assists and 2.0 rebounds.

items.headline: Carter racked up 10 points (3-9 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and six assists over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 126-109 win over Washington.
items.story: The six assists were a season-high output for Carter, but overall, it's very hard to trust him as a bench option on a game-to-game basis. He has scored in double digits in two of his last five outings, but in the other three, he's scored a combined two points. The inconsistencies in production and playing time limit his upside considerably across all formats, making him valuable only as a streaming option in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Carter totaled 14 points (5-10 FG, 4-9 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal over 22 minutes during Thursday's 113-108 loss to Houston.
items.story: Carter has been a hit-or-miss fantasy asset off the bench in Orlando, but he continues to see increased reps in the backcourt. Jalen Suggs returned to action Thursday and logged just 13 minutes, but once he's up to full speed, Carter is likely to see a reduced role.

items.headline: Carter totaled 15 points (6-14 FG, 3-11 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals in 33 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 113-110 double-overtime loss to the Suns.
items.story: The Magic leaned heavily on their starting lineup over four-plus quarters, and Carter was the only member of the second unit to play more than 19 minutes or score in double digits. The veteran guard struggled to break into the rotation with Chicago before being waived at the end of January, but in two games for Orlando since the All-Star break he's had a prominent role in the backcourt, averaging 14.5 points, 3.0 assists, 3.0 threes, 2.5 boards, 1.5 steals and 1.0 blocks in 28.0 minutes.

items.headline: The Magic signed Carter for the remainder of the season on Friday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Carter, who was previously waived by the Bulls, is being brought in to provide emergency backcourt depth for Orlando. With the Magic moving on from Tyus Jones, Carter could be the third-string point guard on the depth chart moving forward.

items.headline: Carter ended Tuesday's 138-110 victory over the Clippers with three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and one steal over four minutes.
items.story: Carter played four minutes during garbage time, continuing what has been a season with very little fanfare. Having only appeared in 21 regular-season games, Carter currently sits well outside the top 300 in standard leagues, averaging 5.4 points and 1.4 three-pointers in 11.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Carter registered six points (2-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt), one rebound and one assist over 12 minutes during Monday's 115-101 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Carter saw playing time for the first time in the past three games and for just the third time in the past 13 games. It's been another disappointing season for the veteran, who has been used only in emergencies. In 17 appearances, he has averaged 6.2 points and 1.6 three-pointers in 13.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Carter ended with 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, two assists and three steals over 22 minutes during Sunday's 123-91 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: The Bulls are still dealing with plenty of injuries, but they seem comfortable with Carter playing a strict reserve role amid Tre Jones' (ankle) absence. The veteran point guard has averaged 6.9 points, 1.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 14.3 minutes per contest over 14 games, failing to reach the 25-minute threshold in any outing.

items.headline: Carter logged six points (2-8 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 16 minutes during Wednesday's 113-103 loss to the Nets.
items.story: The Bulls have been hit pretty hard by injuries, but Carter is still being used quite sparingly. Over his last four appearances, he's seen 10.5 minutes per contest with 2.8 points and 1.3 assists per game.

items.headline: Carter accumulated 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal over 18 minutes during Monday's 143-130 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Carter's offensive production has been very inconsistent, as he has logged duds every other game after turning in a solid shooting performance. He remains buried on the depth chart behind Josh Giddey, Coby White and Tre Jones, but Carter still finds himself in the rotation due to a slew of injuries on the wing.

items.headline: Carter posted 15 points (5-13 FG, 5-10 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist in 18 minutes off the bench during Monday's 130-127 victory over the Nuggets.
items.story: The five threes were a season high for Carter, albeit in only his fourth game, and it was his best showing from beyond the arc since March 31 of last season. The journeyman guard seems to have found a home as a depth option in the Chicago backcourt after playing for four different teams in his first five years in the NBA, but with Coby White (calf) getting close to resuming a full workload, Carter will likely head back to the end of the bench in short order.

items.headline: Carter finished with 11 points (3-4 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two steals over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 124-113 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Carter had arguably his best game in the past 12 months, an indication of how muted his role has become. Chicago was once again without Josh Giddey (ankle), allowing Cater to move into a somewhat meaningful role. While it was great to see the veteran holding his own, this is likely nothing more than an outlier, based on what we have seen from him recently.

items.headline: Carter produced zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and two assists across 12 minutes during Sunday's 128-116 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Carter made his season debut Sunday against New York, and while he was unable to produce in his first game, it is worth noting that he is probably getting back to speed after not playing since the preseason. Carter will likely continue backing up Tre Jones until Coby White (calf) returns.

items.headline: Carter logged 17 points (7-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists in 22 minutes of Tuesday's 124-117 preseason loss to Denver.
items.story: Despite some very modest workloads, Carter has been an obvious standout during the preseason. Through four games, he's averaging 13.3 points, 2.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.8 steals and 3.0 three-pointers in just 16.4 minutes per contest. He's firmly behind Josh Giddey and Tre Jones at point guard, but Carter is proving that he'll be ready when his name is called.

items.headline: Carter delivered 14 points (5-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal in 12 minutes during Thursday's 119-112 preseason win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Carter has been used sparingly in the preseason so far, though he's made the most of his minutes. Through two games, he's seeing 11.8 minutes per contest with averages of 12.0 points, 1.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 3.0 three-pointers on 64.3 percent shooting from the field. He's not guaranteed a role for Opening Night, but he's doing everything he can on his end.

items.headline: Carter will exercise his $6.8 million player option for the 2025-26 season, NBA reporter Jake Fischer reports.
items.story: This was always the expectation for Carter. The veteran guard made a total of 36 regular-season appearances in 2024-25, posting averages of 4.3 points, 1.1 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 8.9 minutes per contest. He could struggle to land a rotation role in 2025-26.

items.headline: Carter will come off the bench during Wednesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: After being a starter for the first time for Chicago in the loss to the Cavaliers on Tuesday, Carter will return to the second unit Wednesday against Miami. In 33 games off the bench this season, Carter has averaged 7.6 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game while shooting 41.1 percent from the field.

items.headline: Carter is in the starting five for Tuesday's game versus the Cavaliers.
items.story: Carter will replace Josh Giddey (forearm) in the starting lineup Tuesday. Carter has played more than 20 minutes in only two games this season, so it's unclear how much playing time he will receive.

items.headline: Carter (shoulder) is available for Friday's game versus the Trail Blazers, Cody Westerlund of 670TheScore.com reports.
items.story: Carter has been upgraded from questionable to available Friday after missing Chicago's previous contest due to a right shoulder contusion. Carter has averaged 5.2 points, 1.9 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 10.6 minutes across his previous 10 outings.

items.headline: Carter (shoulder) has been listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Carter has missed 11 of the Bulls' last 14 games due to a bruised right shoulder and is in danger of missing another game on Friday against Portland. Talen Horton-Tucker could see a boost in minutes off the bench for Chicago if Carter is ruled out.

items.headline: Carter (shoulder) won't play in Tuesday's game versus the Raptors.
items.story: Carter has been downgraded from questionable to out Tuesday due to a right shoulder injury. The 29-year-old guard's next chance to suit up is Friday's matchup with Portland.

items.headline: Carter (shoulder) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Carter picked up some rare minutes in garbage time during Monday's 145-117 loss to Oklahoma City, finishing with 17 points (6-14 FG, 5-11 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists across 18 minutes. If Carter is unable to go, Talen Horton-Tucker could see increased run with the Bulls submitting a very lengthy injury report.

items.headline: Carter posted 17 points (6-14 FG, 5-11 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists across 18 minutes during Monday's 145-117 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: The Bulls were blown out of this contest, allowing Carter to see rare reps in garbage time. He's been used sparingly in recent contests, playing just five times in March for an average of 10.8 minutes. This performance will likely go down as an outlier.

items.headline: Carter accumulated 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds, six assists and one steal over 23 minutes during Wednesday's 127-108 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Carter played an expanded role, logging double-digit minutes for just the second time in the past 10 games in which he has appeared. It's been another disappointing season for Carter, currently averaging 3.8 points in 7.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Carter (illness) isn't included on the Bulls' injury report for Thursday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Carter had missed Chicago's previous two games while recovering from an illness, but he'll be available off the bench for the final contest of the Bulls' road trip. The veteran guard hasn't been a regular in the rotation this season, appearing in 19 games while averaging 6.5 minutes.

items.headline: Carter (illness) won't play Monday against the Clippers.
items.story: This news doesn't carry many fantasy implications, as Carter has been unable to consistently crack Chicago's rotation.

items.headline: Carter (illness) won't play Sunday against Portland.
items.story: Carter isn't typically in Chicago's rotation, so his absence doesn't carry many fantasy implications.

items.headline: Carter is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game versus the Trail Blazers due to an illness.
items.story: Carter has appeared in only four of Chicago's last 10 outings, even when available. Therefore, Carter's expected absence shouldn't impact the team's rotation.

items.headline: Carter provided zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) in four minutes during Wednesday's 110-94 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Carter played four minutes in the loss, suiting up for just the third time in the past seven games. The Bulls have several options at the guard position, with Carter well and truly buried on the depth chart. Outside of injuries to multiple players, it is unlikely we will see Carter playing significant minutes any time soon.

items.headline: Carter closed Thursday's 141-133 loss to Atlanta with 26 points (9-15 FG, 7-11 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal in 36 minutes.
items.story: Entering Thursday's contest, Carter had appeared in just 13 games off the bench for Chicago and averaged just 4.7 minutes per game. However, the veteran guard got extended run Thursday due to the absences of Lonzo Ball (illness), Ayo Dosunmu (Achilles), Josh Giddey (ankle) and Matas Buzelis (illness). Carter took advantage of the opportunity, and his 26 points were a season high and the third-most of his career. His performance could warrant additional playing time off the bench moving forward, starting with Saturday's game against the Bucks.

items.headline: Carter notched five points (2-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and two rebounds in six minutes during Wednesday's 119-99 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Carter suited up for just the second time this season, playing six minutes in garbage time. It's been an underwhelming 12 months for Carter, who has struggled to carve out a consistent role in the Chicago rotation. Based on what we have seen across the first six games, it appears he is going to be utilized as nothing more than a depth piece.

items.headline: Miller contributed four points (2-3 FG), seven rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 103-87 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Miller saw some garbage-time action on a night when none of the Clippers' starters reached the 30-minute mark. The rookie second-rounder could carve out a larger role in the frontcourt at some point down the line, but Isaiah Jackson and Brook Lopez should dominate the center minutes for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Miller amassed 15 points (5-6 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds and one assist over 21 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Miller was a bright spot off the bench Wednesday, pacing the second unit in scoring. The rookie second-rounder is expected to start the season as frontcourt depth for the Clippers.

items.headline: Miller totaled 10 points (3-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, two steals and one block in 16 minutes during Saturday's 114-106 preseason loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Miller averaged 13.0 points, 10.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.2 blocks per game on 53/19/66 shooting splits during his senior season as a Bearcat, and he was expected to be brought along slowly. However, with all of the Clippers' preseason injuries, Miller may get extended opportunities during his rookie campaign.

items.headline: Miller ended with four points (2-5 FG, 0-1 FT), five rebounds and one steal in 17 minutes during Spain's 108-106 loss to Greece in Tuesday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: Miller has remained active this offseason, as he participated in the Las Vegas Summer League with the Clippers before playing for Spain in the FIBA World Cup qualifiers. The rookie second-rounder could have a hard time cracking Los Angeles' Opening Night rotation, as Isaiah Jackson, Rui Hachimura and Max Strus are all well-positioned for reserve roles.

items.headline: Miller registered 15 points (5-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 26 minutes during Sunday's 104-82 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Jazz.
items.story: Miller scored with remarkable efficiency, missing just two shots in 26 minutes while knocking down both of his free throws. The second-round pick is an intriguing seven-foot playmaker, but it may be difficult for him to carve out meaningful minutes in Los Angeles while Rui Hachimura, Brandon Ingram and Derrick Jones are healthy.

items.headline: Miller totaled 12 points (3-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, one assist and three blocks in 27 minutes during Thursday's 91-85 Summer League loss to Sacramento.
items.story: The rookie second-round forward showcased his intriguing two-way upside, finishing efficiently while swatting a game-high three shots. There is a lot of competition for minutes in the frontcourt in Los Angeles, but Miller certainly has the talent to carve out a role.

items.headline: Miller was selected by the Clippers with the No. 36 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Miller is an intriguing prospect as a seven-footer who can handle the rock and operate as a playmaker, although his jump shot remains a work in progress. He made collegiate stops at Florida State, Florida Atlantic and Cincinnati. Miller averaged 13.0 points, 10.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.2 blocks per game on 53/19/66 shooting splits during his senior season as a Bearcat. He'll likely be brought along slowly in Los Angeles, though that'll depend on what happens with Kawhi Leonard.

items.headline: Beringer will not start Monday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: As expected, with Rudy Gobert (back) returning to the lineup Monday, Beringer will shift back to the bench.

items.headline: Beringer will start Saturday against the Spurs, Jack Borman of Lockedon Wolves reports.
items.story: Beringer will draw the start with Rudy Gobert (back) out, making him an intriguing plug-and-play option in daily fantasy leagues. Beringer can struggle with foul trouble, and he'll have a tough matchup against San Antonio, but he can rack up the rebounds and defensive stats when given the opportunity.

items.headline: Minnesota exercised Beringer's contract option for next season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Minnesota locking in Beringer for another season, the young center's roster spot and long-term frontcourt role are more secure. Beringer remains a developmental piece for the Timberwolves, but he's been thrust into a larger role in the middle now that Naz Reid is in Charlotte.

items.headline: Beringer provided seven points (3-3 FG, 1-3 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and one block across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 119-114 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Beringer pulled down a season-high 10 rebounds Wednesday. Now that Naz Reid is in Charlotte, Beringer carries plenty of contingent upside as the No. 2 center behind Rudy Gobert but doesn't hold particularly stable standalone value outside of boards.

items.headline: Beringer ended Friday's 115-93 win over the Magic with nine points (4-8 FG, 1-2 FT) and nine rebounds over 15 minutes.
items.story: Beringer came within a whisker of his first double-double of the season, providing Minnesota with serviceable production as the backup center. It's been a modest start to Beringer's sophomore NBA campaign as he fills the role of primary backup behind Rudy Gobert. Assuming Gobert remains healthy, Beringer should be considered nothing more than a rebound-and-blocks streamer.

items.headline: Beringer won't start Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Heat.
items.story: Beringer started Friday's preseason finale with Rudy Gobert (rest) receiving a maintenance day, though the veteran big man is back in his usual starting role for the regular-season opener. Beringer figures to operate as Gobert's primary backup to begin the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Beringer will start Friday's preseason finale against the Bulls.
items.story: With Minnesota resting all of its regulars, Beringer will start alongside Zyon Pullin, Terrence Shannon, Jaylen Clark and Cody Williams. Beringer recorded 10 points (3-4 FG, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, one block and one steal across 18 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to Detroit.

items.headline: Beringer recorded 10 points (3-4 FG, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds, one block and one steal across 18 minutes in Wednesday's 128-106 preseason loss to Detroit.
items.story: Beringer made a nice impression on the coaching staff ahead of a critical second season in the league. After dominating at the G League level in 2025-26, the 2025 first-rounder is slotting in as Minnesota's No. 2 center behind Rudy Gobert now that Naz Reid is in Charlotte and out of the frontcourt mix.

items.headline: Beringer is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason matchup with Miami.
items.story: Rudy Gobert (rest) won't play Saturday, so Beringer will get some time to shine as a starter. He has elite defensive instincts, but he also has a tendency to find himself in foul trouble.

items.headline: Beringer amassed two points (1-3 FG), eight rebounds and one block in 19 minutes during Wednesday's 123-112 preseason loss to Indiana.
items.story: Beringer was the first big man off the bench once again, a role that he will presumably retain beyond the preseason. Although his production to this point has been modest, he should at least be on the radar as a speculative last-round pick for anyone needing boards and blocks. Should Rudy Gobert suffer an injury at any point during the season, Beringer could be a popular addition across all formats.

items.headline: Beringer supplied 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-4 FT), seven rebounds and one block across 15 minutes in Monday's 116-97 preseason win over the Bucks.
items.story: Beringer led the second unit in rebounding Monday in Minnesota's preseason opener. The second-year big man is slotting in as the team's No. 2 center behind Rudy Gobert now that Naz Reid is out of the frontcourt mix, so Beringer should have an Opening Night role.

items.headline: Beringer could play an expanded role in 2026-27 after the Timberwolves sent Naz Reid to the Hornets as part of the LaMelo Ball trade.
items.story: After logging just 7.9 minutes per game last regular season, the 2025 first-rounder is now slotting in as Minnesota's No. 2 center behind Rudy Gobert now that Reid is out of the frontcourt mix. Beringer dominated at times during the 2025-26 G League regular season, averaging 15.3 points, 11.3 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game while shooting 64.0 percent from the field.

items.headline: Beringer (back) has been ruled out for Friday's Summer League game against the Clippers.
items.story: Beringer will end up missing the Timberwolves' final four games of the Summer League due to lower-back tightness. The 2025 first-rounder averaged just 7.9 minutes per game across 40 regular-season contests during his rookie campaign. However, with Naz Reid now in Charlotte, Beringer figures to operate as Minnesota's backup center behind Rudy Gobert for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Beringer (back) is out for Wednesday's Summer League game against the Pacers.
items.story: Beringer is sidelined for a third consecutive contest due to back tightness. The 2025 first-rounder's next chance to play will come Friday against the Clippers, but it wouldn't be surprising if the Timberwolves proceeded with caution.

items.headline: Beringer (back) won't play in Monday's Summer League game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Beringer will miss a second consecutive contest due to back tightness. The 19-year-old center's next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Beringer has been ruled out for Saturday's Summer League game against the Nuggets due to back tightness.
items.story: Beringer will miss Minnesota's second Las Vegas Summer League outing with the back issue. His next opportunity to play will come Monday against Portland.

items.headline: Beringer produced 18 points (7-15 FG, 3-3 FT), 12 rebounds, four blocks, one assist and one steal across 25 minutes in Thursday's 105-92 Summer League win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Beringer started at power forward and turned in a solid all-around performance in Minnesota's Las Vegas Summer League opener. The 19-year-old big man finished third on the Timberwolves in scoring while leading all players in rebounds and blocks. With Julius Randle and Naz Reid out of the picture, Beringer has the opportunity to carve out a much more significant role in his second season in the Association.

items.headline: Beringer produced four points (2-3 FG), two rebounds, one block and one steal over eight minutes during Friday's 139-109 loss to the Spurs in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: The 2025 17th overall pick spent the postseason as a deep reserve behind Rudy Gobert and Naz Reid, but Beringer's regular-season finale provided a massive glimpse into his future potential. Filling in for a resting Gobert on April 12, Beringer exploded for 24 points, 13 rebounds and a staggering seven blocks in 31 minutes against New Orleans. While he averaged just 3.9 points across 40 regular-season appearances as a rookie, his combination of interior scoring and elite rim protection suggests he is ready for a consistent rotation role. With rumors swirling that the Timberwolves may look to move Gobert's $36.5 million salary this offseason to reshape the roster around Anthony Edwards, Beringer would be the primary beneficiary of such a trade. If Gobert is moved, Beringer would likely compete for significant minutes, offering a much higher offensive ceiling than the incumbent starter.

items.headline: Beringer is not in Minnesota's starting lineup against Denver in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs Saturday.
items.story: Beringer started in the final two games of the regular season, and in this past Sunday's 132-126 win over the Pelicans, he finished with 24 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and a whopping seven blocks over 31 minutes. He'll revert to a bench role for Game 1 and provide depth at center behind Rudy Gobert and Naz Reid.

items.headline: Beringer produced 24 points (9-12 FG, 6-9 FT), 13 rebounds, seven blocks and two assists across 31 minutes during Sunday's 132-126 win over New Orleans.
items.story: With Rudy Gobert (rest) and Naz Reid (shoulder) inactive, Beringer turned in the most impressive performance of his young career, recording his first double-double of the season while adding a staggering seven blocks. The rookie didn't see consistent playing time throughout the year, averaging 7.9 minutes across 40 regular-season appearances, though he did display flashes of potential when called upon. Heading into the postseason, Beringer isn't likely to see much action with Gobert and Reid back in the lineup.

items.headline: Beringer recorded 14 points (5-5 FG, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 26 minutes during Friday's 136-132 win over the Rockets.
items.story: With the sixth seed in the Western Conference sealed up, the Timberwolves have begun to empty the bench. Rudy Gobert (rest) was a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game, giving Beringer, a 2025 first-round pick, additional opportunities. The Florida product has appeared in 39 games with the parent club this season.

items.headline: Beringer is in the Timberwolves' starting lineup against the Rockets on Friday, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
items.story: With Rudy Gobert (rest) and Naz Reid (shoulder) both ruled out, Beringer will be in the Timberwolves' starting lineup for the second time this season. The rookie first-rounder made his first career start Feb. 22 against the 76ers, when he played 17 minutes and finished with seven points and three rebounds in a 135-108 loss.

items.headline: Beringer posted nine points (4-10 FG, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 23 minutes during Wednesday's 132-120 loss to the Magic.
items.story: The Timberwolves rested multiple players, including Rudy Gobert. Naz Reid started and saw 24 minutes, while Beringer soaked up the backup center minutes and made the most of his rare opportunity.

items.headline: The Timberwolves recalled Beringer from the G League's Iowa Wolves on Wednesday, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
items.story: Beringer has logged just seven minutes over two appearances with Minnesota on the month. However, the rookie first-rounder is likely to see meaningful playing time in Wednesday's game against Utah due to Naz Reid (ankle) being sidelined.

items.headline: Beringer has been recalled from the G League's Iowa Wolves and is available for the Timberwolves' game against the Lakers on Tuesday.
items.story: Minnesota is halting Beringer's G League assignment, summoning the rookie first-rounder from Iowa.  Beringer has averaged 3.0 points, 1.9 rebounds and 0.4 blocks in 6.8 minutes per contest through 30 NBA games this season, and he's unlikely to see meaningful playing time Tuesday on a healthy Timberwolves squad.

items.headline: Beringer is in the starting lineup for Sunday's matchup with the 76ers.
items.story: Beringer will draw the first start of his NBA career due to both Rudy Gobert (suspension) and Naz Reid (shoulder) being unavailable, and it'll be Donte DiVincenzo, Anthony Edwards, Jaden McDaniels and Julius Randle joining him in the first unit. Beringer is a solid rebounder and defender, so he could be someone to consider streaming in deep leagues if you need some big man stats.

items.headline: Beringer provided two points (1-1 FG, 0-1 FT) and two rebounds across five minutes during Friday's 119-115 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Beringer continues to be deployed minimally, having only appeared in two of the past four games. While he does possess an interesting fantasy game, the opportunities simply aren't there at the moment. As long as both Rudy Gobert and Naz Reid are healthy, expect to see Beringer spending a lot of his time on the sideline rather than on the court.

items.headline: Beringer closed Saturday's 126-123 loss to the Spurs with 10 points (5-6 FG), eight rebounds, three assists and two blocks across 23 minutes.
items.story: Beringer flirted with his first career double-double while also matching his career high in blocks. After it was announced that Rudy Gobert would miss the game due to a hip injury, Naz Reid lasted just five minutes before leaving the game with a shoulder concern. If both are forced to miss additional time, Beringer could be an intriguing short-term pickup, even in standard leagues.

items.headline: Beringer amassed 13 points (6-7 FG, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 30 minutes during Tuesday's 139-106 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Beringer assumed the role of backup center with Rudy Gobert sidelined due to a one-game suspension. Following an impressive Summer League, Beringer has struggled to play a consistent role for the Timberwolves, suiting up on just 16 occasions. He has played single-digit minutes in 15 of those games, with his one standout performance coming in this one. Despite the impressive display, there is almost no way he will play a similar role anytime soon, barring injuries to other players.

items.headline: Minnesota recalled Beringer from the G League's Iowa Wolves on Monday.
items.story: Beringer will return to the parent team after making a couple of G League appearances, during which he averaged 13.0 points and 10.5 rebounds per game. The young center has seen little action at the NBA level, logging less than 10 minutes in each of his 12 games played this season, and that may continue to be the case in the future.

items.headline: Minnesota recalled Beringer from the G League's Iowa Wolves on Tuesday.
items.story: After he put up 12 points (5-12 FG, 1-1 FT), four rebounds, an assist and four blocks across 27 minutes in Monday's 132-104 G League win over the Westchester Knicks, Beringer will provide depth for the NBA team. He has not appeared in an NBA game since Nov. 17 but will be available for Minnesota against the Knicks on Tuesday. Beringer will likely split time between the two clubs throughout the season.

items.headline: Minnesota assigned Beringer to the G League's Iowa Wolves on Tuesday.
items.story: Minnesota's rookie is heading to Iowa to get some live reps. He will be available to play in Friday's G League game against the Motor City Cruise, and he'll likely be recalled shortly after.

items.headline: Beringer supplied six points (2-4 FG, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and one block across eight minutes during Monday's 120-96 victory over the Mavericks.
items.story: This game was over in a hurry, allowing Beringer to see some extra run in garbage time. Across nine regular-season appearances, Beringer holds averages of 2.0 points and 1.3 rebounds in 4.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Beringer closed Sunday's 144-117 victory over the Kings with two points (1-1 FG) and one steal in six minutes.
items.story: Beringer made his seventh appearance of his rookie season Sunday, with this being his second-highest minute total. As long as the frontcourt in Minnesota is healthy, Beringer is likely to just get the scraps off the bench.

items.headline: Simons finished with 19 points (6-12 FG, 5-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists and three steals across 25 minutes in Saturday's 109-104 victory over Charlotte.
items.story: LeBron James (rest) and Joel Embiid (foot) did not suit up for this contest, so there were extra scoring opportunities up for grabs. While Simons couldn't hit the 20-point mark for the third consecutive game, he still shined on both ends of the floor. The 27-year-old is now averaging 12.0 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.3 assists while shooting a career-best 43.8 percent from deep over 24.7 minutes per contest in seven regular-season games in 2026-27. With the 76ers loaded with All-Stars, Simons likely won't be as productive as he was during his time in Portland, though he should continue to get plenty of playing time off the bench.

items.headline: Simons accumulated 21 points (7-11 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist over 31 minutes during Friday's 98-93 victory over New York.
items.story: Simons scored 20-plus points while connecting on five or more three-pointers for a second consecutive game, and he was the 76ers' second-leading scorer Friday behind Tyrese Maxey (21 points). Simons played a season-high 31 minutes due to the absence of Jaylen Brown (knee), and the former will have opportunities this season to operate in an expanded role in games that one of Maxey, Brown or LeBron James sit out.

items.headline: Simons notched 20 points (7-11 FG, 6-10 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 114-109 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Simons produced his best game of the season, scoring 20 points, including six triples. It appears as though Nick Nurse is comfortable running a shallow rotation, meaning Simons should at least be playing meaningful minutes on most nights. While this was certainly a strong performance, he had scored a total of just 11 points in his previous three games.

items.headline: Simons closed with 13 points (5-10 FG, 3-8 3Pt) and two rebounds in 25 minutes during Tuesday's 106-100 victory over the Knicks.
items.story: Simons made his regular-season debut for Philadelphia after dealing with hamstring tightness during the preseason. The veteran guard provided an immediate scoring boost, finishing as the 76ers' fourth-leading scorer while committing no turnovers. His eight three-point attempts highlight his role as a perimeter scoring option, though the absence of assists or defensive statistics limits his fantasy appeal beyond points and triples.

items.headline: Simons (hamstring) is available for Tuesday's regular-season opener in New York.
items.story: Simons is set to debut for Philadelphia after signing with the organization as a free agent in the offseason. Between the Celtics and Bulls in 2025-26, Simons averaged 14.3 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.4 assists while connecting on 38.5 percent of his three-point attempts across 55 regular-season appearances. He'll operate as a scoring spark for the Sixers' second unit behind starters Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe when they visit the Knicks on Opening Night

items.headline: Simons (hamstring) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Simons managed to log a full practice Sunday, but the team isn't yet ready to commit to his availability for the regular-season opener. The Sixers should have an update on his status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Simons (hamstring) was a full participant in Sunday's practice, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: Simons didn't play in the preseason due to a hamstring injury. However, the 27-year-old guard is trending in the right direction ahead of Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Knicks in New York.

items.headline: Simons (hamstring) is out for Friday's preseason game against the Celtics, Kyle Neubeck of AllPHLY.com reports.
items.story: Simons is trending in the right direction and was able to practice in full Thursday. The 76ers will take a cautious approach for the final exhibition, however.

items.headline: Simons (hamstring) was limited at Monday's practice, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
items.story: Simons continues to deal with tightness in his hamstring, though he's trending in the right direction. For now, he's questionable at best for the next preseason game Oct. 16 against the Celtics.

items.headline: Simons (right hamstring) isn't expected to play in either of Philadelphia's next two preseason games against Brooklyn and Boston, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Simons also missed Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks due to the injury. His next opportunity to make his preseason debut will come Oct. 16 against Boston.

items.headline: Simons won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Knicks due to undisclosed muscle tightness, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Simons will join Joel Embiid, LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey on the sidelines for the preseason opener. Head coach Nick Nurse said Simons has been "in and out" over the last few days, so it wouldn't be surprising if the team continues to exercise caution before the regular season.

items.headline: Simons is set to play a pivotal reserve role for the 76ers, per Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com.
items.story: Simons ended 2025-26 on the shelf with the Bulls due to a fractured wrist, but he's prepping for a significant bench role with his new team. The sharpshooter made a grand total of five starts all of last year, and he's likely to play a similar role in 2026-27 behind VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey. Simons has never averaged more than four rebounds or one steal in a season and has averaged more than five assists just once, so his style of play remains more conducive to points leagues.

items.headline: Simons (elbow) will join the 76ers on a two-year, $12.3 million deal, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The 76ers continue to round out their roster after acquiring Jaylen Brown on Wednesday. The second year of this deal is a player option, which will allow Simons to bet on himself if he puts together a strong campaign. Simons could be positioned to be the first guard off the bench for the 76ers ahead of Opening Night.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) will not play in Chicago's final two games of the regular season, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.
items.story: Simons' season will officially come to an end as he continues to recover from a fractured left wrist that has kept him sidelined since Feb. 21. Head coach Billy Donovan confirmed Friday that Simons, Josh Giddey (hamstring), Guerschon Yabusele (shoulder/elbow), Nick Richards (elbow) and Jalen Smith (calf) will be held out for the Bulls' final two matchups against the Magic and Mavericks. With Simons officially shut down, Collin Sexton (finger) and Rob Dillingham will continue to handle increased workloads in the backcourt to close out the campaign.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Friday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Simons hasn't played since Feb. 21, and there's been no indication he's close to a return. He can be considered doubtful at best for the season finale Sunday.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Thursday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Simons hasn't played since Feb. 21 due to a fractured left wrist, and it seems unlikely he'll return this season. His next chance to return comes Friday against the Magic.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Tuesday's game against Washington.
items.story: Simons hasn't played since Feb. 21 with a fractured left wrist, and it's becoming increasingly less likely he'll suit up again this year. Collin Sexton (finger) is probable for Tuesday and should continue to start at shooting guard for the Bulls if he's cleared to play.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) remains out for Sunday's game against Phoenix.
items.story: Simons hasn't played since the 126-110 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Feb. 21. With only five games remaining before the Bulls wrap up the 2025-26 campaign, Simons may have already played his final game of the season. While the 26-year-old remains on the shelf, Collin Sexton and Rob Dillingham should continue to absorb most of the backcourt minutes from off the bench.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Friday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: The combo guard has no timetable for a return due to a fractured left wrist. Simons can be tentatively considered doubtful for Sunday's matchup against the Suns.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Simons remains sidelined while on the mend from a fractured left wrist. He can be considered doubtful for Chicago's next matchup Friday in New York.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Simons hasn't played since Feb. 21 due to a fractured left wrist and is without a clear timetable for a return. He should be considered doubtful for future contests until the Bulls offer an update on his progress.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) won't play in Saturday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Simons has missed over a month due to a fractured left wrist, and his return won't come Saturday. As a result, Rob Dillingham and Collin Sexton should continue to absorb most of the minutes off the bench behind Josh Giddey and Tre Jones.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Simons was previously listed as doubtful and hasn't seen the floor since Feb. 21. His next chance to play comes Saturday against Memphis.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is doubtful for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Simons hasn't take the court since Feb. 21 while recovering from a fractured left wrist. His next opportunity to suit up will arrive Saturday in Memphis.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: This will be Simons' 15th consecutive game on the sidelines, and with Friday's match in Oklahoma City being the first of a back-to-back, it seems unlikely he'll be able to return for that one. Tre Jones should continue to see quality minutes with Simons unavailable.

items.headline: Simons is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the 76ers with a fractured left wrist.
items.story: It doesn't appear Simons, who has been sidelined since Feb. 21, is quite yet ready to return to the floor. His expected absence should continue to allow Tre Jones to play a prominent role in the Chicago backcourt Wednesday.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Monday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Simons, who has been out since Feb. 21 with a fractured left wrist, will not return for this contest, but he's getting closer and is officially considered day-to-day. His next chance to return comes Wednesday against the 76ers.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Simons has been out of action since Feb. 21 due to a fractured left wrist. The fact that he's been given the questionable tag for Monday's game indicates that he is progressing in his recovery, but whether he'll be cleared to return is unlikely to be known until closer to the 8:00 p.m. ET tip-off. Simons would likely operate under a minutes restriction if cleared to play, which would mean less playing time for Collin Sexton and Rob Dillingham.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) will be re-evaluated in 10 days, the Bulls announced Monday.
items.story: Simons is making progress since suffering a wrist fracture back on Feb. 24. Based on this update, the earliest possible return for Simons would be March 27 against the Thunder. Meanwhile, Jaden Ivey (knee) will be re-evaluated in one week.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Monday marks the 11th game in a row that Simons will miss while recovering from a fracture in his left wrist. His next opportunity to play is Wednesday against the Raptors, but there is no clear timeline for his return, so he can be considered doubtful for that contest.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) is out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Simons will be sidelined for a 10th straight game and remains without a timetable to return. His next chance to play comes Monday against the Grizzlies, but he should be considered doubtful for future contests until the Bulls provide an update on his status.

items.headline: Simons (wrist) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Simons will miss a ninth consecutive contest due to a left wrist fracture. His next chance to play will come Friday against the Clippers, though it doesn't seem like a return is imminent.
