His next chance to suit up will come Sunday against the Knicks.

items.headline: Cain (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Cain was a late scratch ahead of Wednesday's loss to the Raptors and may miss another game. He's one of four Pelicans listed as questionable for Friday's game.

items.headline: Cain has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Raptors due to a right ankle sprain.
items.story: Cain was a late scratch. His next chance to suit up will come Friday in Memphis. He hadn't seen playing time in back-to-back games, so his absence shouldn't impact the rotation.

items.headline: Cain racked up two points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds and one block in 12 minutes during Monday's 118-100 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: With injuries to CJ McCollum (thigh), Dejounte Murray (hand), Zion Williamson (thigh), Jordan Hawkins (back), Herbert Jones (shoulder) and Trey Murphy (hamstring), Cain has received depth minutes in New Orleans' forward rotation. Across his five appearances in 2024-25, Cain is averaging 5.2 points and 2.0 rebounds in 13.2 minutes.

items.headline: The Pelicans signed Cain to a two-way contract Friday, Adrian Wojnarowski of ESPN reports.
items.story: Cain spent last season with the Heat on a two-way deal, averaging 3.7 points and 1.4 rebounds in 10.0 minutes across 26 regular-season NBA appearances. In 2024-25, Cain is set to split time between the Pelicans and their G League affiliate, the Birmingham Squadron.

items.headline: Cain closed Friday's 111-88 loss to New Orleans with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one assist across four minutes.
items.story: Cain's playing time all came while the outcome was assured and marked just his second appearance of the month. Even if Duncan Robinson (back) continues to miss more time along with Tyler Herro (foot), Cain doesn't look as though he'll factor into head coach Erik Spoelstra's rotation plans.

items.headline: The Heat recalled Cain from the G League's Sioux Falls Skyforce on Friday, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Cain hasn't appeared in an NBA game since before the All-Star break, but he'll be available for Friday's matchup in Detroit. With Bam Adebayo dealing with a back issue, Cain will likely serve as emergency frontcourt depth. On Thursday, Cain suited up in the G League for the Sioux Falls Skyforce and posted 16 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists, four steals and two blocks during a win over the Mexico City Capitanes.

items.headline: The Heat recalled Cain from the G League's Sioux Falls Skyforce on Friday, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Cain hasn't appeared in an NBA game since before the All-Star break, but he'll be available for Friday's matchup in Detroit. With Bam Adebayo dealing with a back issue, Cain will likely serve as emergency frontcourt depth.

items.headline: Braun finished with 14 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals across 36 minutes in Monday's 118-110 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Braun delivered efficient scoring while continuing to impact the game defensively, as this was his fifth straight outing with at least two steals. His 36-minute workload reinforced his established role in Denver's starting lineup, although his limited rebounding and playmaking restrict his overall ceiling. Braun's steady playing time and defensive contributions support his fantasy relevance, particularly in category-based formats, even when scoring isn't his strongest suit. That said, he has scored at least 14 points in four of his last five games, so he's putting up consistent numbers in that regard as well.

items.headline: Braun registered 31 points (11-16 FG, 7-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and three steals in 37 minutes during Friday's 127-120 win over the Suns.
items.story: Braun was on fire in the win, hitting seven of his nine three-point attempts, including all six in the first half. The wing gave Denver a huge second scoring punch alongside Jamal Murray, who had 39, as the Nuggets knocked down 20 threes as a team. Performances like this make Braun an essential part of the starting five, and he'll look to stay hot Monday at home against Portland.

items.headline: Braun tallied 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt), four assists, three steals and a block across 36 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Braun matched his previous season-high scoring mark and delivered multiple steals for the third straight game. The main issue with Braun early in the season has been a lack of consistency. He's failed to hit double-digit points in two of his four games, and while he had a strong defensive outing in this one, he also failed to record a single rebound. His playing time and steady role as a starter will give him a decent floor, but the lack of consistency hurts his upside.

items.headline: Braun recorded seven points (3-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt), six rebounds, one assist and one steal over 33 minutes during Thursday's 96-84 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Braun struggled to find his shooting touch, particularly from beyond the arc, but maintained a substantial workload in Denver's starting lineup. His playing time remains encouraging for fantasy purposes, though he'll need to improve his offensive efficiency to provide more consistent production.

items.headline: Braun delivered 16 points (5-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, an assist and two steals across 28 minutes in Friday's 121-106 preseason win over the Lakers.
items.story: Braun delivered a well-rounded performance, shooting 50 percent from the field and contributing six rebounds. The versatile wing also recorded two steals without committing a turnover, showcasing his ability to impact the game on both ends of the floor while posting a plus-18 rating. Braun's combination of efficient scoring, rebounding and defensive activity should make him a useful multi-category fantasy contributor if he maintains a substantial role in Denver's rotation. He averaged 12.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 0.7 steals per game in 44 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Braun finished with two points (1-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks in 23 minutes during Sunday's 133-128 preseason win over Chicago.
items.story: Braun struggled to find his shooting touch but contributed defensively, recording three combined steals and blocks while avoiding turnovers. The 25-year-old guard started alongside Denver's projected first unit, and his ability to contribute across multiple categories should help offset occasional poor shooting performances during the regular season.

items.headline: Braun said Monday that increasing both his three-point volume and efficiency was his biggest developmental focus during the offseason, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: "Shoot more. Make more. Don't hesitate to shoot, just let it go," Braun said. The 25-year-old connected on just 30.1 percent of his three-pointers across 44 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 after shooting 39.7 percent from deep the previous season. A return to form from beyond the arc would help Braun provide more reliable floor spacing alongside Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray.

items.headline: Braun appears cemented as a starter for the Nuggets in 2026-27 after Peyton Watson was traded to Cleveland.
items.story: Despite playing a career-low 44 regular-season games, Braun was a full-time starter last year and should be locked into a similar role this season. The swingman is searching for a bounce-back campaign, closing last regular season with averages of 12.0 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.7 assists in 31.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Braun posted three points (1-4 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and three blocks in 28 minutes during Thursday's 110-98 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Braun scored in single digits for the fourth straight game, closing out what was an underwhelming end to a disappointing season. Despite having homecourt advantage, Denver simply couldn't match Minnesota's intensity. Injuries limited Braun to just 50 appearances across the season (including playoffs), during which he averaged 11.5 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Braun ended Saturday's 112-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs with eight points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal across 34 minutes.
items.story: Braun only took four shot attempts in the loss, ceding most of the backcourt output to Jamal Murray in the Game 4 defeat. Now facing an elimination game, the Nuggets desperately need more production from the supporting cast, and Braun could be set up for an easier task with Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) and Anthony Edwards (knee) shelved.

items.headline: Braun racked up two points (0-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-4 FT), two rebounds and one block over 24 minutes during Thursday's 113-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: After a relatively strong start to the series, Braun came up empty Thursday, contributing to what was an ugly loss on the road. After winning the first game at home, Denver has now lost back-to-back games, handing Minnesota the upper hand. Game 4 will take place in Minnesota on Saturday, when Braun may need to increase his production if Denver hopes to avoid a 3-1 deficit.

items.headline: Braun logged 12 points (4-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds and one assist over 36 minutes during Saturday's 116-105 victory over the Timberwolves in Game 1 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Braun logged 36 minutes in Game 1, finishing behind Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, who were out there for 39 and 40, respectively. While the 25-year-old went 4-for-10 from the field, he missed only one of his three tries from deep while falling two rebounds shy of a double-double. Braun averaged 11.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.0 steals while shooting 20.0 percent from behind the three-point line in two meetings with the Timberwolves during the regular season. He will look to increase his statistical contributions when these clubs meet Monday night for Game 2.

items.headline: Braun (ankle/hip) is available for Game 1 on Saturday against Minnesota.
items.story: Braun is set to return from a two-game absence due to ankle and hip injuries Saturday. The fourth-year swingman averaged 12.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 0.7 steals in 31.8 minutes per contest across 44 regular-season games.

items.headline: Braun (ankle/hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Braun will miss a second consecutive contest to end the regular season due to left ankle injury management and a right hip flexor strain. He'll finish the 2025-26 regular season with averages of 12.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 0.7 steals in 31.8 minutes per tilt across 44 games.

items.headline: Braun (ankle) won't play in Friday's game against Oklahoma City, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Braun and the rest of Denver's starters won't suit up against Oklahoma City, so they will have one more chance to play during the regular season before the playoffs commence. Without Braun on the floor, Tim Hardaway will likely enter the starting lineup for the first time since the 147-123 loss to Miami on Dec. 29.

items.headline: Braun (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Denver's entire starting lineup is now carrying questionable tags as the team considers some maintenance days. Tim Hardaway and Julian Strawther could pick up more run if Braun is held out.

items.headline: Braun accumulated 21 points (7-16 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one block over 39 minutes during Saturday's 136-134 overtime victory over the Spurs.
items.story: The fourth-year wing topped 20 points for the first time since March 18, when he hit for 26 points against the Grizzlies, while the five made three-pointers were a season high. Braun has scored in double digits in 12 of the last 13 contests, averaging 15.3 points, 4.7 boards, 2.5 assists and 1.6 threes over that span.

items.headline: Braun recorded 18 points (7-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds and four assists in 31 minutes during Wednesday's 130-117 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: It was Braun's best scoring effort since March 18, when he dropped 26 points on the Grizzlies. The fourth-year wing has also seen his defensive contributions evaporate of late. He hasn't produced a steal since that contest, averaging 12.4 points, 3.9 boards, 1.9 assists and 0.9 threes over the last seven games.

items.headline: Braun racked up 13 points (6-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist across 32 minutes during Tuesday's 125-123 win over Phoenix.
items.story: While Braun has been limited to just 37 games in 2025-26, he's finding his footing down the stretch for the Nuggets with eight straight outings with at least 11 points. Over these last eight contests, the swingman has averaged 16.1 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.5 three-pointers in 32.5 minutes per game while shooting 40.0 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Braun racked up 11 points (5-9 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four rebounds and two assists over 33 minutes during Friday's 121-115 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Braun was unable to keep his foot on the gas, providing modest scoring numbers while contributing nothing on the defensive end. With that said, Braun had been playing well prior to this performance and has been a top-50 talent in seven games over the past two weeks, averaging 15.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.4 three-pointers.

items.headline: Braun totaled 26 points (11-19 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and four steals over 41 minutes during Wednesday's 125-118 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Braun stepped up in a game where the Nuggets' go-to scoring options, Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, weren't as sharp as they usually are. Braun has missed considerable time due to injury this season but has been healthy of late, averaging 14.2 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game since the beginning of March. He's scored at least 19 points in three of his last five outings, including 20-plus points in the last two.

items.headline: Braun totaled a game-high 22 points (7-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal across 27 minutes during Tuesday's 124-96 win over Philadelphia.
items.story: The Nuggets didn't face much of a challenge on their home court from a shorthanded Sixers lineup, and Braun's 27 minutes led the starting five as Denver emptied the bench in the second half. It was Braun's best scoring effort in March, and through nine games this month, the fourth-year guard is averaging 12.9 points, 5.4 boards, 3.0 assists and 1.2 threes while shooting 52.5 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Braun racked up 19 points (8-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 129-93 win over Houston.
items.story: After missing a big chunk of the year with an ankle sprain, Braun is finally starting to gain a rhythm. The swingman has averaged 13.4 points, 6.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.4 three-pointers in 35.7 minutes per game across his last seven contests, shooting 50.7 percent from the floor during this period.

items.headline: Braun finished Friday's 142-103 loss to the Knicks with seven points (2-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds and five assists.
items.story: Braun notably logged 31 minutes Friday despite sitting out the entire fourth quarter of the blowout loss. He has been a total ironman for the Nuggets since returning from an ankle injury Feb. 3, having played and started in 14 straight games. During that stretch, he has averaged 34.4 minutes per game, serving as a durable fixture for a rotation dealing with various frontcourt absences. While his overall production has been somewhat mediocre -- he's averaging 12.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists per contest -- his availability remains vital for Denver's depth.

items.headline: Braun supplied 23 points (8-18 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 4-5 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal in 45 minutes during Friday's 127-121 overtime loss to the Thunder.
items.story: The 23 points were a season high for Braun, who appears to be rounding into form after ankle issues cost him more than two months of action. Over the last eight games, the fourth-year wing is averaging 13.6 points, 5.8 boards, 3.3 assists, 1.5 threes and 0.9 steals in 34.0 minutes while shooting 56.2 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Braun ended with six points (2-5 FG, 2-5 3Pt), seven rebounds and two assists in 28 minutes during Wednesday's 103-84 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Braun tallied just six points, unable to maintain his double-digit scoring streak. Since returning from injury, Braun has struggled to be anything more than a role player, averaging 10.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers in nine appearances over the past month. At best, managers should view him as a schedule play, if and when the Nuggets are tabled with some favorable matchups.

items.headline: Braun closed Sunday's 128-117 loss to the Warriors with 18 points (7-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: Braun has struggled with injuries this season and has been inconsistent for the most part, but he's suddenly trending up in a big way. Over his last five outings, he's seeing 33.5 minutes per contest with 14.0 points, 5.4 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.4 three-pointers.

items.headline: Braun (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Braun will shed a probable tag in time to suit up Wednesday. He's fresh off his third 20-point game of the season, as he logged 20 points, five rebounds and two assists in Monday's loss to Cleveland.

items.headline: Braun is probable for Wednesday's game against Memphis due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: Braun also carried a probable designation leading up to Monday's game against the Cavs and was ultimately able to suit up, so he'll presumably have a good chance to take the court Wednesday in his team's final game before the All-Star break. Braun is averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists in four showings since returning from a 12-game absence due to the ankle injury.

items.headline: Braun amassed 20 points (7-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 32 minutes during Monday's 119-117 loss to Cleveland.
items.story: Braun got his stat line to acceptable levels after struggling through his first three appearances following a 12-game absence. He's showing no ill effects from the ankle injury that sidelined him, and Monday's effort was a positive indicator that he'll return to his usual level of production heading into the All-Star break.

items.headline: Braun (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Braun will shed his probable tag and suit up for Monday's matchup. After missing 12 games due to a sprained left ankle, the Kansas product has averaged 7.3 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.3 assists across 33.7 minutes in three games since returning to the lineup.

items.headline: New Orleans recalled Johnson from the G League's Laketown Squadron on Sunday.
items.story: Johnson has recorded just three minutes of NBA play this campaign as he continues to be constantly assigned to the G League side. Still, he may have an opportunity to add backup behind the primary options Dejounte Murray and Jeremiah Fears in upcoming contests. While his value is limited in his current role, Johnson may be more active for the Squadron if he's assigned again when they open their G League season Nov. 8.

items.headline: The Pelicans recalled Johnson from the G League's Laketown Squadron on Friday.
items.story: New Orleans has some injuries on the roster, so the team presumably recalled Johnson to add depth. However, even if he remains with the Pelicans for a limited time, he likely won't be on the floor much.

items.headline: The Pelicans assigned Johnson to the G League's Laketown Squadron on Friday.
items.story: Johnson has yet to suit up for the Pelicans this season. He'll look to get some much-needed reps with the Squadron in the meantime.

items.headline: The Pelicans declined Johnson's team option Tuesday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: As a result, Johnson is now set to become an unrestricted free agent after the 2026-27 season. A 2024 first-rounder by the Bucks, he's looking for a fresh start in New Orleans following multiple offseason trades but is unlikely to begin the year in the rotation.

items.headline: Johnson was traded from the Grizzlies to the Pelicans on Tuesday along with Taj Gibson in exchange for Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a future second-round pick swap, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Johnson is already headed to his fifth organization since being selected 23rd overall in the 2024 NBA Draft. The 21-year-old has averaged 4.9 points across 77 career regular-season appearances and remains a developmental project despite his first-round pedigree. Johnson figures to compete for a depth role in New Orleans and is unlikely to have much fantasy relevance unless injuries open up additional playing time.

items.headline: The Grizzlies traded Santi Aldama (knee) to the Mavericks on Wednesday in exchange for Johnson, a protected 2030 Warriors first-round pick and two future second-round picks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After dealing Ja Morant (elbow) earlier this week, Memphis is continuing its rebuilding efforts. Johnson, who was part of last year's Anthony Davis (finger) trade to the Wizards, will have a chance at a fresh start with a young Grizzlies club, though Johnson will face plenty of competition for playing time on the wing. The 2024 first-rounder averaged only 9.5 minutes per game over 48 regular-season appearances between Dallas and Washington last season.

items.headline: Johnson ended Sunday's 149-128 win over the Bulls with 20 points (6-12 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 8-9 FT), one rebound and one assist in 25 minutes.
items.story: The second-year guard came over from Washington as part of the trade that sent Anthony Davis (finger) to the Wizards, but Johnson still struggled for regular action at the NBA level with Dallas. Johnson averaged 3.9 points, 1.1 assists and 1.0 rebounds in 10.4 minutes per tilt through 23 games for the Mavericks this season. All signs point toward Dallas exercising Johnson's team option for 2026-27, and perhaps he'll have a clearer path to minutes if the Mavs don't re-sign Khris Middleton.

items.headline: Johnson totaled 13 points (4-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), one rebound, two assists and one block across 20 minutes during Friday's 139-120 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Johnson recorded double-digit points for the first time in his past 15 games, shouldering a little more on the offensive end as Dallas continues to roll with some interesting lineups. Although he has flashed some upside on the offensive end, Johnson's lack of supporting stats remains an issue. At this stage, there is no reason to think he will be a relevant piece next season.

items.headline: Johnson (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Monday in the Mavericks' 137-131 overtime loss to the Warriors.
items.story: After a brief stint with the G League's Texas Legends, Johnson was recalled by the Mavericks ahead of Monday's game but was unable to crack head coach Jason Kidd's 11-man rotation. Rather than turning to Johnson to fill out the second unit, Kidd inserted two-way player John Poulakidas (12 minutes) into the rotation.

items.headline: The Mavericks recalled Johnson from the G League on Saturday.
items.story: Johnson will rejoin the NBA club ahead of the Mavericks' matchup with the Clippers on Saturday night.  Johnson has appeared in 15 games since being traded to Dallas in February, averaging 2.8 points, 1.0 rebounds and 0.9 assists across 9.3 minutes.

items.headline: The Mavericks recalled Johnson from the G League's Texas Legends on Wednesday.
items.story: The 2024 first-rounder is expected to serve as emergency depth for Dallas' matchup versus the Hawks on Wednesday, with Brandon Williams being in the league's concussion protocol. Since coming over from the Wizards as part of the Anthony Davis (finger) trade, Johnson has averaged 2.8 points, 1.1 rebounds and 0.9 assists in 9.3 minutes per tilt through 14 games for the Mavericks.

items.headline: The Mavericks recalled Johnson from the G League's Texas Legends on Sunday.
items.story: Johnson joined the Legends for Saturday's 112-105 loss to the Valley Suns, finishing the game with 27 points (10-14 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in 36 minutes. Over six appearances with the parent club since being acquired from the Wizards ahead of the trade deadline, the second-year guard has averaged 4.2 points in 10.8 minutes per contest. He logged 34 minutes in Friday's loss to Memphis and may continue seeing significant minutes in Sunday's matchup with the Thunder with Naji Marshall (finger) and P.J. Washington (ankle) expected to join Cooper Flagg (foot) on the sideline.

items.headline: Johnson had 11 points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist in 15 minutes during Thursday's 130-121 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Johnson logged substantial minutes for the first time since being dealt to the Mavericks. He didn't see many opportunities on the offensive end, but he went perfect from the field and scored in double digits for the first time since Feb. 3. Johnson still faces plenty of competition for playing time in the backcourt, but it's worth noting that Tyus Jones has played 12 minutes or fewer in three straight games, which could open up chances for Johnson and others.

items.headline: Johnson (recently traded) will be available for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Just because Johnson is available, that doesn't mean he will actually see the floor. The second-year guard was unable to carve out a role in Washington, and he's facing an uphill battle for playing time in Dallas too.

items.headline: Johnson (recently traded) is listed as probable for Saturday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Johnson was shipped off by the Wizards to the Mavericks on Wednesday, a trade highlighted by Anthony Davis (finger) being dealt to Washington. Johnson was not available for Thursday's loss to the Spurs but is trending toward playing in Saturday's rematch. The second-year pro is averaging just 8.6 minutes per game this season, and he faces an uphill battle for playing time with his new team.

items.headline: Johnson (recently traded) won't play Thursday against the Spurs.
items.story: Johnson was dealt from the Wizards to the Mavs on Wednesday, but he won't be available Thursday since the trade isn't yet official. His next chance to make his Dallas debut will arrive Saturday in San Antonio.

items.headline: Johnson is being sent to the Mavericks on Wednesday as part of the Anthony Davis (finger) deal, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Khris Middleton, Malaki Branham and Marvin Bagley will join Johnson in Dallas, while Davis, D'Angelo Russell (illness), Jaden Hardy and Dante Exum (knee) move to Washington. The Mavericks also received two first-round picks and three second-round picks.
items.story: Johnson will add some depth to Dallas' backcourt, where he'll compete for minutes with the likes of Branham, Max Christie, Caleb Martin and Klay Thompson. Johnson has shown some flashes this season, but it's unclear how he'll factor into Jason Kidd's rotation, so managers in most leagues can watch this situation develop from the waiver wire. Johnson can be considered doubtful for Thursday's game against the Spurs while the trade finalizes.

items.headline: Johnson supplied 17 points (7-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, four assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 116-112 victory over Sacramento.
items.story: Johnson saw his first action since Jan. 16 and didn't disappoint on the offensive end. He set a new season high by dropping 17 points, and he did so in an efficient manner. Johnson has yet to see this type of usage on a nightly basis, so while it's nice to see him have a breakout game, he's yet to carve out a consistent role in the team's rotation to this point.

items.headline: Johnson (illness) is off the injury report for Tuesday's game against Portland.
items.story: After missing Saturday's road loss to Charlotte, Johnson is ready to suit back up for the Wizards on Tuesday. However, the second-year guard was available off the bench in Washington's prior three contests before becoming ill and didn't see the floor in any of them.

items.headline: Johnson (illness) will not play Saturday against the Hornets.
items.story: Johnson was available to play Thursday against the Nuggets despite his illness, but he never saw the floor. He remains miles off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Johnson (illness) is available  for Thursday's game against Denver.
items.story: Johnson is available off the bench Thursday despite fighting through an illness. However, the 2024 first-rounder hasn't seen any action in Washington's past two contests, so Johnson doesn't figure to mix into the backcourt rotation in a meaningful capacity.

items.headline: Johnson is questionable for Thursday's game against the Nuggets with an illness.
items.story: Three members of the Wizards are questionable with an illness for Thursday, so an ailment appears to be spreading around the team. Johnson hasn't appeared in Washington's past two games and may not do so even if he's available against Denver.

items.headline: Johnson (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Saturday's 121-115 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Prior to Saturday, Johnson had appeared in 10 straight games for the Wizards, though he averaged just 11.0 minutes per contest while shooting 30.4 percent from the field over that stretch. Even though the Wizards were without Bilal Coulibaly (back) in the second leg of the back-to-back set, head coach Brian Keefe opted to keep both Johnson and Malaki Branham on the bench throughout the day while two-way player Jamir Watkins (21 minutes), Justin Champagnie (26 minutes) and Will Riley (16 minutes) operated as the backup wings/forwards in Washington's nine-man rotation. Keefe could opt to shake up the second unit in Monday's game against the Clippers, but Johnson's chances of regaining a role won't improve if Coulibaly is cleared to play in that contest.

items.headline: Johnson notched three points (1-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt), one assist and one steal across 14 minutes during Friday's 119-99 win over Brooklyn.
items.story: Johnson played at least 14 minutes for the second straight game, although he offered very little in terms of tangible production. On the whole, Johnson has been a non-factor this season, averaging just 1.1 points in 5.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Washington recalled Johnson from the G League's Capital City Go-Go on Monday.
items.story: Johnson has seen very limited run with the Wizards, but he's a young and polarizing prospect that Washington wants to develop. He will likely split time between the two clubs for the rest of the season.

items.headline: Washington recalled Johnson from the G League's Capital City Go-Go on Wednesday.
items.story: This move was done following Tuesday's 120-110 loss to the Delaware Blue Coats, where Johnson put up 23 points (7-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds, an assist and a steal across 32 minutes before fouling out. Johnson will now return to the Wizards, where he has appeared in just 10 games so far this season.

items.headline: Johnson was assigned to the G League's Capital City Go-Go on Saturday.
items.story: Johnson continues to bounce between the NBA club and the G League, as he was just recalled Friday. He should see the majority of his playing time for the Go-Go, where he's scored in double figures in all three of his appearances so far this season.

items.headline: The Wizards recalled Johnson from the G League's Capital City Go-Go on Friday.
items.story: Johnson is joining a banged-up Washington team as emergency depth ahead of Friday's game against the Cavaliers. The 2024 first-rounder is averaging just 4.5 minutes per game over 10 appearances in the NBA this year, so he'll be a candidate to head back to the G League following Friday's action.

items.headline: Washington assigned Johnson to the G League's Capital City Go-Go on Monday.
items.story: Johnson has been unable to break through Washington's rotation. Across 10 NBA appearances, he's averaging 4.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Johnson recorded zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound across six minutes during Friday's 119-86 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: Johnson appeared for the first time in the past five games, bringing his total number of garbage time appearances to nine. Despite the fact that Washington clearly has nothing to play for, it doesn't appear as though Johnson is high on the priority list. He is a name to watch as the season progresses, but for now, he can be safely ignored in all redraft fantasy formats.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is not on the injury report ahead of Tuesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Johnson has missed Washington's last two games due to a right ankle contusion but is off the injury report, indicating he'll be available Tuesday. Even if healthy, the young guard isn't guaranteed meaningful playing time, as he's averaged just 4.8 minutes per game across eight appearances this season.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Chicago.
items.story: Johnson will miss a second consecutive game due to a right ankle contusion, but he'll have extra time to recover ahead of Washington's next contest Tuesday against Atlanta. The second-year guard has averaged just 4.8 minutes per game across eight appearances off the bench, so his absence won't impact the Wizards' backcourt rotation too much.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Johnson is a late scratch with an ankle contusion. His next chance to play is Saturday in Chicago. Johnson's absence doesn't seem to open up a clear number of minutes for other members of the Wizards.

items.headline: Johnson's rookie option was exercised by the Wizards for the 2026-27 season Thursday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: While Johnson and Cam Whitmore were acquired by the Wizards via trade, the front office has grouped them along with young players Alex Sarr, Bilal Coulibaly, Bub Carrington and Kyshawn George to be their stars of the future. Johnson has also yet to play in a game this season for longer than four minutes, but this move by the front office instills confidence that they want him on the roster for the long haul.

items.headline: Johnson (leg) has been cleared to play in Wednesday's opener against the Bucks, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Johnson was able to get some contact work in Sunday after missing the entire preseason with a leg bruise. Due to his injury setback, Johnson will be facing an uphill battle for playing time early on this season. There certainly is a path to minutes for him if he finds the form he showed late in the 2024-25 season.

items.headline: Johnson (leg) was a limited participant in practice Saturday, Varun Shankar of The Washington Post reports.
items.story: Johnson participated in some contact work during practice as he continues to manage a lingering leg bruise that sidelined him for the entire preseason. His availability for Opening Night on Wednesday against the Bucks remains uncertain, and even if cleared, the guard is projected to have a limited role in the rotation.

items.headline: Johnson (leg) didn't play in Thursday's 119-98 preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Johnson missed the final three matchups of the preseason while dealing with a bruised leg. His next chance to take the court will arrive in the regular-season opener Wednesday against Milwaukee, his former team. However, Johnson is not expected to be much of a factor in the Wizards' rotation to begin the year.

items.headline: Johnson (leg) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Knicks, Tim Bontemps of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Johnson will miss his second consecutive game due to a leg bruise. His last chance to suit up ahead of the regular season will come in Thursday's matchup versus the Pistons.

items.headline: Johnson (leg) didn't play in Sunday's 113-112 preseason loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Johnson was limited during training camp due to a leg bruise, and he didn't take the floor during the Wizards' preseason opener. After being traded to Washington from Milwaukee last season, Johnson saw extended run down the stretch of the regular season. However, he may have a more difficult path to consistent minutes during the 2025-26 season. His next chance to play will come Monday against New York.

items.headline: Wizards general manager Will Dawkins said Johnson will be limited for the start of training camp with a leg bruise, Chase Hughes of Monumental Sports Network reports.
items.story: This sounds like a minor issue for Johnson that is unlikely to impact his availability for Opening Night. Johnson showed some flashes late in the 2024-25 regular season and will be a player to monitor closely in deeper formats during the preseason.

items.headline: Johnson generated 25 points (10-16 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), with five rebounds and three assists over 35 minutes of Wednesday's 86-76 Summer League loss to Utah.
items.story: Johnson dropped 20 points Tuesday and followed up the performance with a Summer-League high in the category. Entering his second NBA season, Johnson will have a tough time cracking the Wizards' rotation, but at age 20, he has shown plenty of promise as a long-term project.

items.headline: Johnson recorded 20 points (7-20 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 31 minutes in Tuesday's 74-58 Summer League loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Johnson struggled from beyond the arc but still led the Wizards with 20 points in Tuesday's loss. Acquired in February in the trade that sent Kyle Kuzma to the Bucks, the young guard will look to earn a spot in a crowded backcourt that now includes CJ McCollum, Tre Johnson and others.

items.headline: Johnson recorded 14 points (6-16 FG, 2-5 3Pt), one rebound, eight assists and one steal in 48 minutes during Sunday's 119-118 win over the Heat.
items.story: Since a mid-season trade with the Bucks, Johnson's career took off with the Wizards. In 22 regular-season appearances with Washington, Johnson produced averages of 9.1 points, 3.1 assists, 2.4 rebounds, 0.5 steals and 1.0 three-pointers with plenty of highlight-worthy dunks and energy plays. However, his efficiency wasn't great, as he shot 38.1 percent from the field and 24.7 percent from beyond the arc. Johnson could find himself in the Opening Night rotation in 2025-26 if he has a strong offseason.

items.headline: Johnson is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game against the 76ers, Sam DiGiovanni of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Johnson returns to the starting lineup due to the absence of Jordan Poole (elbow). Johnson is averaging 12.4 points, 2.9 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 0.5 steals per game in his previous eight starts this season.

items.headline: Johnson won't start in Tuesday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Kyshawn George will return from a seven-game absence due to an ankle sprain, pushing Johnson to the second unit. The 20-year-old has recorded double-digit points in four of his last five appearances (all starts), averaging 14.0 points, 3.4 assists and 2.0 rebounds across 35.8 minutes per contest in that five-game span.

items.headline: Johnson contributed 19 points (7-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, six assists and one steal across 37 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 116-111 win over the Kings.
items.story: Johnson fouled out in the final quarter, but his contributions were pivotal in the Wizards' victory, and the California-born rookie has been making the most of the expanded role he's enjoyed in recent weeks. He's scored in double digits in five of his last nine outings, a span in which he's averaging 12.2 points, 2.8 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 0.7 steals and 1.6 turnovers across 31.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Clippers recalled Niederhauser (foot) from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Sunday.
items.story: Niederhauser remains unlikely to play a meaningful role in the short term following a seven-month recovery from foot surgery. The 23-year-old might instead make a phased return to action, possibly seeing limited minutes at some point in upcoming weeks and making some appearances in the G League. Last season, he averaged 4.3 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.3 assists per regular-season game during his rookie year.

items.headline: Niederhauser (foot) had his third-year team option picked up Thursday by the Clippers, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: With Niederhauser still working back from a foot injury, this move is more about the Clippers' long-term roster planning than any immediate status change. It keeps the young center under team control beyond this season, which was the expectation after Los Angeles spent a first-round pick on Niederhauser a year ago.

items.headline: Niederhauser (foot) remains out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers. He also won't travel with the team for the upcoming two-game road trip in Minnesota and Golden State, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Niederhauser hasn't played this season and is working his way back from surgery in March. He's "making progress," though it's unknown when he will be back on the floor. The 2025 No. 30 overall pick appeared in 41 regular-season games as a rookie, averaging 4.3 points and 2.9 rebounds. Niederhauser will presumably be eased back into action once he's cleared to suit up, but until that happens, Isaiah Jackson and Brook Lopez should handle most of the work in the middle.

items.headline: Niederhauser (foot) won't be ready for the start of the season, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Niederhauser is progressing from March surgery but won't be able to suit up to begin the year. The Clippers are likely to take a cautious approach with the 2025 first-rounder. Isaiah Jackson should occupy the backup center spot behind Brook Lopez early in the campaign.

items.headline: Niederhauser has been diagnosed with a Lisfranc injury in his right foot and will require surgery. He's been ruled out for the remainder of the 2025-26 season, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: This is a tough blow for Niederhauser, who suffered the injury during Wednesday's matchup against the Pacers. It's still too early to talk about whether the big man will be available for the start of next season, though the team could provide an estimate following the procedure.

items.headline: The Clippers announced after Wednesday's 130-107 win over the Pacers that Niederhauser will remain in Los Angeles to undergo further evaluation for his right foot injury and won't travel with the team for its upcoming two-game road trip, Farbod Esnaashari of SI.com reports.
items.story: The rookie first-round pick will sit out Friday in San Antonio and Saturday in Memphis after playing just eight minutes and recording six points (2-2 FG, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two blocks before exiting Wednesday's win with the injury. A clearer timeline for Niederhauer's return should become available once the Clippers return to Los Angeles. In the meantime, the Clippers could lean on Nicolas Batum and Isaiah Jackson to play backup minutes at center when starter Brook Lopez is off the court.

items.headline: Niederhauser won't return to Wednesday's game against the Pacers due to a right foot injury, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports. He will finish with six points (2-2 FG, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and two blocks across eight minutes.
items.story: Niederhauser landed awkwardly on his right foot after blocking a shot and required assistance getting back to the locker room. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game in San Antonio. If the rookie big man is forced to miss time, Isaiah Jackson would likely see a bump in minutes behind Brook Lopez.

items.headline: Niederhauser exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Wednesday's game against the Pacers due to an apparent lower right leg injury, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Niederhauser came down awkwardly after blocking a shot and required assistance getting back to the locker room. If the rookie big man is unable to return, Brook Lopez and Isaiah Jackson should pick up the slack the rest of the way.

items.headline: Niederhauser finished with 11 points (3-6 FG, 5-6 FT), nine rebounds, four blocks and two steals across 21 minutes during Monday's 114-101 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder matched a season high in swats Monday. With Ivica Zubac (ankle) out of the picture, Niederhauser is starting to push for a larger role behind Brook Lopez at center. Niederhauser has averaged 8.8 points, 6.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks in 20.7 minutes per game over his last four contests.

items.headline: Niederhauser registered seven points (3-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt), eight rebounds and four blocks across 26 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 111-109 loss to the Magic.
items.story: With Ivica Zubac (ankle) now in Indiana, Niederhauser has seen a more consistent role in the Clippers frontcourt rotation, and he's beginning to make an impact -- Sunday's four rejections were a new career high. Over the last eight games, the rookie center is averaging 5.9 points, 4.5 boards and 1.4 blocks in 15.4 minutes with the second unit.

items.headline: Niederhauser tallied 11 points (5-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one block across 10 minutes in Team Austin's 40-34 Rising Stars loss to Team Melo on Friday.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder suited up for the G League Rising Stars on Friday and led all players in scoring, albeit in a losing effort. Niederhauser also knocked down a three-pointer, which he has yet to do for the Clippers this season. The 22-year-old center out of Penn State has averaged 3.7 points and 2.3 rebounds in just 9.0 minutes per game across 34 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. However, he has logged double-digit minutes in four of Los Angeles' last five outings and may continue seeing increased burn with Ivica Zubac (ankle) having been traded to the Pacers on Feb. 5.

items.headline: Niederhauser notched three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and two blocks across 13 minutes during Tuesday's 102-95 loss to Houston.
items.story: Niederhauser was limited to just 13 minutes, potentially putting pause on what many had hoped would be a late-season breakout. Isaiah Jackson made his debut for the Clippers, adding another wrinkle to the center rotation. While Niederhauser is still someone worth watching, it appears his short-term value could fluctuate from game to game.

items.headline: Niederhauser posted 15 points (5-5 FG, 5-7 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one block over 17 minutes before fouling out of Sunday's 115-96 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Niederhauser provided an unexpected scoring boost in limited opportunities by going perfect from the field. He fell one point shy of tying his best mark of the season and has now scored in double digits in two of his last three games. However, Niederhauser's minutes are expected to take a hit once Isaiah Jackson (trade pending) is ready for his team debut.

items.headline: Niederhauser (illness) isn't on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Timberwolves, Janis Carr of the OC Register reports.
items.story: Niederhauser left Friday's game early due to an illness, but the issue won't prevent him from suiting up Sunday. With Ivica Zubac having been traded to the Pacers, Niederhauser is left to compete with Isaiah Jackson (recently traded) and Brook Lopez for center minutes.

items.headline: Niederhauser won't return to Friday's game against the Kings due to an illness, NBA writer Justin Russo reports. He'll finish with two points (1-1 FG) in six minutes.
items.story: Niederhauser wasn't listed on the injury report ahead of Friday's contest, though he's under the weather and won't play in the second half. The rookie big man's next opportunity to suit up will come Sunday against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Niederhauser closed Wednesday's 124-91 loss to the Cavaliers with 10 points (4-4 FG, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds and two blocks over 25 minutes.
items.story: Niederhauser played a good chunk of the second half Wednesday with the Cavs fully in control. The Clippers elected to pull Brook Lopez early given the score, and with Ivica Zubac (personal) sidelined, Niederhauser received plenty of looks. The big man took full advantage of the blowout by turning in his best scoring performance since Jan. 14 and his best rebounding night since Jan. 1. He also set a new season high in swats.

items.headline: The Clippers recalled Niederhauser from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Saturday.
items.story: Niederhauser is back with the Clippers ahead of Sunday's game versus the Nets, but he's unlikely to be part of the rotation since LA will have Ivica Zubac and Brook Lopez available at center. The rookie first-round pick will likely be headed back to the G League in the near future to see extended playing time.

items.headline: Niederhauser ended with 16 points (7-7 FG, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two blocks across 23 minutes during Wednesday's 119-105 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Niederhauser played through an illness and logged 23 minutes during the victory. With Ivica Zubac (ankle) sidelined, the Clippers needed support in the frontcourt, and Niederhauser platooned under the basket with Brook Lopez. The rookie proved to be the more effective option, and while Lopez's backup role is likely safe, Niederhauser is making a strong case for more time.

items.headline: Niederhauser (illness) has been cleared to play Monday against the Warriors.
items.story: Niederhauser was upgraded to probable a few hours before tipoff, and he's now been officially cleared to suit up. He saw only six minutes in his last appearance Saturday against Boston with Ivica Zubac back in action, and Niederhauser will likely have a hard time finding opportunities again Monday.

items.headline: Niederhauser (illness) is probable for Monday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Niederhauser was initially added to the injury report as questionable, so the fact that he's since been listed as probable is a strong indication that he'll be ready to suit up. Expect official word from the team closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Niederhauser (illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Niederhauser is under the weather and could miss his first game since Dec. 20. However, the rookie big man's potential absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation with Ivica Zubac back in action following a five-game absence due to a sprained ankle.

items.headline: Niederhauser amassed six points (3-7 FG), 10 rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 27 minutes during Thursday's 118-101 win over Utah.
items.story: Niederhauser has taken on a larger role with Ivica Zubac (ankle) sidelined, logging 25 and 27 minutes over the past two games. The 2025 first-round pick finished second on the team in rebounds, with six of them being offensive boards, and tied for the team lead with two blocks. The rookie center is averaging 11.0 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.5 blocks in 26 minutes over the past two games.

items.headline: Niederhauser provided 16 points (6-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-6 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one block across 25 minutes during Tuesday's 131-90 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Although John Collins made an appearance despite an injury tag, the team elected to sit him midway through the third quarter. Niederhauser stepped in and scored 11 of his 16 points in cleanup duty. Ivica Zubac's (ankle) absence has affected the depth chart, and it's given the 2025 first-round pick a bit of a minute boost. The Penn State product isn't relevant in fantasy at the moment, but he could see more time if injuries mount in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Niederhauser (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Tuesday's game against the Rockets, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Niederhauser has missed LA's last two games with a knee injury but has received the green light to suit up Tuesday. He hasn't had much of a role this season for the parent club and has appeared in only three games since Dec. 1, averaging 2.7 points and 1.3 rebounds in 6.3 minutes over that stretch.

items.headline: Niederhauser (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Niederhauser will miss his second consecutive contest due to left knee soreness, though his absence shouldn't cause any major waves in the Clippers rotation. The rookie's next opportunity to suit up will come Tuesday against the Rockets.

items.headline: Los Angeles recalled Niederhauser (knee) from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Wednesday, but he is out for Thursday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Niederhauser has returned to the NBA following a productive stretch in the G League, but he is dealing with a knee injury that will sideline him at least for Thursday's contest. However, his absence will not impact the Clippers' rotation, as he is buried on the depth chart.

items.headline: Niederhauser played the final 3:40 of Monday's 121-103 loss to the Grizzlies, finishing with two points (0-1 FG, 2-2 FT) and one rebound.
items.story: After being recalled from the G League's San Diego Clippers earlier in the day, Niederhauser suited up for the parent club Monday but once again found himself outside of the rotation, with his playing time coming well after the Grizzlies had the game in hand. Though the 6-20 Clippers don't appear to view Niederhauser as an NBA-ready contributor just yet, the rookie first-round pick could nonetheless be in the mix for more meaningful run in competitive games behind top center Ivica Zubac once the team fades from playoff contention.

items.headline: Niederhauser produced 18 points (5-7 FG, 4-4 FT), 17 rebounds, three assists and two blocks in 36 minutes of Tuesday's 124-116 G League win over the Valley Suns. Los Angeles recalled him back to the NBA on Wednesday.
items.story: Niederhauser continues to feast at the G League level, but he's yet to see many opportunities in the NBA. Across 11 NBA appearances, Niederhauser is averaging 5.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Los Angeles assigned Niederhauser to the G League's San Diego Clippers on Sunday.
items.story: Niederhauser continues to bounce back and forth between the two teams. The rookie has made 11 appearances at the NBA level for an average of 5.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: The Clippers recalled Niederhauser from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Saturday.
items.story: Niederhauser joined the Clippers' G League affiliate for Friday's win over the Salt Lake City Stars, notching 12 points (3-3 FG, 3-3 FT), four rebounds and two blocks in 13 minutes. The rookie has appeared in all three of San Diego's games thus far and will likely continue to spend time in the G League this season.

items.headline: Los Angeles recalled Niederhauser from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Monday.
items.story: Along with Cam Christie, Niederhauser was assigned and recalled on the same day. Most of Niederhauser's minutes will likely come at the G League level to open his career.

items.headline: The Clippers assigned Niederhauser to the G League's San Diego Clippers on Monday.
items.story: Niederhauser has been unable to crack the rotation thus far, with an average of 4.4 minutes in three appearances. Expect him to get plenty of reps in the G League to open his rookie season.

items.headline: Niederhauser (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Heat, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Niederhauser missed Friday's game against the Pelicans due to a left ankle sprain, but he will be available for Monday's bout. Niederhauser hasn't seen much of a role to this point, so his availability likely doesn't impact the rotation.

items.headline: Niederhauser (ankle) won't play Friday against the Pelicans.
items.story: Niederhauser's absence is unlikely to have a big impact on the rotation. The No. 30 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, Niederhauser has averaged 4.3 minutes across three appearances thus far.

items.headline: Niederhauser notched 13 points (5-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists and two blocks across 26 minutes in Friday's 106-103 preseason win over the Warriors.
items.story: Niederhauser finished as the Clippers' third-leading scorer and was one of four Los Angeles players to reach double figures. The rookie big man also grabbed a game-high mark in rebounds. The No. 30 overall pick in the 2025 Draft is expected to provide center depth for the club in 2025-26, though he could see increased playing time if Ivica Zubac or Brook Lopez (rest) misses time.

items.headline: Niederhauser (back) is set to be available for Thursday's preseason opener against the Guangzhou Loong Lions, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Niederhauser sat out the end of the Las Vegas Summer League with a back injury, but he's healthy for the beginning of exhibition play. That said, the rookie first-rounder would likely need one of Ivica Zubac or Brook Lopez to go down with an injury in order to realistically carve out a meaningful role from the second unit during his first season.

items.headline: Green was ejected from Monday's game against Phoenix after being assessed two technical fouls, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports. He'll end with four points (1-2 FG, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 17 minutes.
items.story: Green was involved in an altercation early in the third quarter, resulting in a review and ultimate ejection from the matchup. Al Horford (rest) isn't available Monday, likely opening up minutes for Georges Niang, Charles Bassey and Graham Ike.

items.headline: Green (back) is available Monday against the Suns.
items.story: Green is no longer on the injury report after sitting out the front end of this back-to-back set. In his most recent outing against the Timberwolves, Green compiled three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, six assists and two blocks across 32 minutes.

items.headline: Green (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Green will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game against the Suns. Graham Ike, Al Horford and Charles Bassey will help pick up the slack with Green inactive Sunday.

items.headline: Green posted three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, six assists and two blocks across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 119-114 win over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Green attempted just three shots but remained productive as a rebounder, facilitator and defensive presence. His nine boards and six assists helped offset the minimal scoring contribution, while two blocks added further fantasy value. Green's limited offensive involvement continues to restrict his scoring ceiling, but his consistent playing time and ability to contribute across multiple categories make him a useful option in category-based formats.

items.headline: Green (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against Denver.
items.story: Green sat out Saturday's loss to Phoenix in the second leg of a back-to-back set, though he'll return to action Monday. In the first two games of the regular season, the veteran big man averaged 3.5 points, 7.0 assists, 4.5 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 26.0 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Green (back) won't play Saturday in Phoenix.
items.story: Green is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's meeting in Denver. Graham Ike, Georges Niang and Gui Santos will help pick up the slack with Green inactive.

items.headline: Green is doubtful to play Saturday against the Suns due to bilateral low back soreness.
items.story: It's not surprising to see the Warriors take a cautious approach with Green on the second leg of a back-to-back set, and they'll make a final call on his availability closer to Saturday's 10 p.m. ET tipoff. If Green doesn't suit up against Phoenix, then Georges Niang could be in line for a bigger role in a depleted frontcourt that will also be without Al Horford (back injury management) while having Charles Bassey (knee) questionable.

items.headline: Green closed Wednesday's 127-105 loss to the Lakers with two points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt), four rebounds, eight assists, one block and one steal over 21 minutes.
items.story: Green played the role of point guard Wednesday, handing out a team-high eight assists. The veteran forward's best fantasy days are behind him, but Green showed in the season opener that he's still capable of chipping in across the board and could provide late-round fantasy appeal this season.

items.headline: Green posted seven points (2-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 assists, eight rebounds and three steals over 24 minutes during Friday's 128-118 preseason win over Portland.
items.story: Green did a little bit of everything during Friday's exhibition contest, with five of his team-high 10 assists coming in the third quarter as he flirted with a triple-double. His box score production rarely matches his real-life importance on the floor, but Green's ability to contribute in multiple stats makes him a solid depth option on fantasy rosters.

items.headline: Green (rest) is available and will start in Friday's preseason game versus Portland, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Green didn't play in Tuesday's 101-89 preseason win over the Lakers. He will be on the floor for the preseason finale and is expected to log 25-30 minutes.

items.headline: Green (rest) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason game against the Lakers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The veteran big man will be held out of Tuesday's contest, with his last chance to suit up in the preseason coming Friday against Portland. Charles Bassey will get the starting nod in Green's absence.

items.headline: Green (rest) will start in Saturday's exhibition against the Kings, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Green did not play in Wednesday's exhibition for maintenance reasons, but he's back and starting Saturday. Charles Bassey will return to the second unit with Green active.

items.headline: Green will be limited to around 20 minutes in Tuesday's preseason contest against the Lakers and won't travel to Portland for Wednesday's back-to-back against the Trail Blazers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: The Warriors are being cautious with Green's workload in the preseason, so he'll be limited to around 20 minutes Tuesday and won't suit up Wednesday. This is part of a long-term picture, as the idea is to have Green as healthy as possible for the start of the regular season against the Lakers on Oct. 21.

items.headline: Green will play in Sunday's preseason game against the Clippers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Head coach Steve Kerr stated Green, Stephen Curry and Al Horford would all be available for the preseason opener. However, all three will play only in the first half and be on the floor "around 12-16 minutes." Green most recently averaged 8.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.5 assists over 27.5 minutes in 68 regular-season games in 2025-26. While his production has remained the same for the most part in the last few seasons, his numbers could improve, considering Jimmy Butler (knee) will miss the start of the 2026-27 campaign. In addition, it's unknown if Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed) will be ready to go for Opening Night.

items.headline: Head coach Steve Kerr wants Green to shoot more open three-pointers this season, per Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com.
items.story: Green already took a career-high 4.6 three-point attempts per game last regular season, and it sounds like there's room for growth in that area. The veteran forward is worthy of a late-round pick in most fantasy leagues this fall, but he'll likely need the playmaking threats of Jimmy Butler (knee) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) to be in the lineup to maximize his efficiency.

items.headline: Green agreed to re-sign with the Warriors on a one-year, $27.7 million deal Tuesday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: After declining the player option on his previous contract earlier this summer, the longtime Warrior is now set for his 15th season with Golden State in 2026-27 following the negotiation of a new pact. Green is entering his age-36 campaign this coming season and appears to be in a state of decline, but he still showed the ability to chip in across the board in 2025-26. He started all 68 of his regular-season appearances, averaging 8.4 points, 5.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 0.9 steals in 27.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Green will decline his $27.7 million player option, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Green is now scheduled to become a free agent. There will almost certainly be mutual interest in a return, but this gives the Warriors flexibility to pursue LeBron James in free agency and Anthony Davis via trade. Green, who is 36 years old, holds career regular-season averages of 8.7 points, 6.8 rebounds, 5.6 assists, 1.0 blocks and 1.3 steals.

items.headline: Green was ejected with 1:04 remaining in the fourth quarter of Friday's 111-96 Play-In Tournament loss to the Suns after fouling out at the 1:06 mark. He closed with five points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six assists, two rebounds and one steal across 36 minutes.
items.story: Both Devin Booker and Green, who was on the bench, were ejected late in the fourth quarter. The veteran big man and the Warriors will now look ahead to next season, though Green does hold a $27.7 million player option for the 2026-27 campaign. He finished the regular season with averages of 8.4 points, 5.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 0.9 steals across 27.5 minutes per game in 68 outings.

items.headline: Brazile won't start Friday's game against the Suns.
items.story: The rookie got the starting nod in Wednesday's win over the Pelicans, but he'll slide back to the second unit Friday with Cameron Johnson (ankle) back in action. Brazile has averaged 9.0 points, 7.3 rebounds and 0.7 blocks across 21.0 minutes per game in three outings off the bench this season.

items.headline: Brazile will start Wednesday against the Pelicans.
items.story: Brazile will replace Bryce Hopkins in the starting lineup for Wednesday's game, and he'll be joined by Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic in the first unit. Brazile scored 17 points over 28 minutes in Saturday's 134-114 overtime win over the Pelicans, so it'll be interesting to see what he can do in a starting role in this rematch.

items.headline: Brazile notched 17 points (6-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds, two blocks and one steal over 28 minutes during Saturday's 141-135 overtime win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Brazile fell one rebound short of his first career double-double, playing a key role for Denver down the stretch. He continues to impress with his energy on both ends of the floor and may have just put himself on the radar in standard fantasy leagues. With Cameron Johnson (ankle) set to miss time, it appears as though Brazile is going to be utilized as a sixth-man option. Keeping in mind that he is a rookie, expect to see fluctuations in his production. With that said, the upside is intriguing, and his ability to rebound the basketball makes him a viable stream consideration.

items.headline: Brazile contributed four points (1-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and 12 rebounds over 18 minutes during Thursday's 96-84 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Brazile made an immediate impact on the glass in Denver's season opener, collecting three offensive rebounds and nine defensive boards despite limited playing time. His shooting was inefficient, but the strong rebounding performance could help him earn additional opportunities in the frontcourt rotation.

items.headline: Brazile won't start Thursday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Brazile got the starting nod in Friday's preseason finale but will slide to the second unit in Denver's regular-season opener. The rookie forward is a candidate to enter the rotation Thursday due to Spencer Jones (hamstring) being sidelined.

items.headline: Brazile will start in Friday's preseason game against the Lakers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Aaron Gordon (rest) will get the night off, so Brazile will move into the starting lineup for the Nuggets' final exhibition. The 23-year-old is coming off a big showing, amassing 22 points, two rebounds, one steal and one block over 25 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason loss to the Clippers.

items.headline: Brazile registered 22 points (8-10 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-5 FT), four rebounds and one steal over 25 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Brazile exploded off the bench, pouring in a game-high 22 points after combining for just 14 points across his previous three preseason appearances. The rookie second-round pick faces an uphill battle for a consistent role in the regular-season rotation, though performances like Wednesday's could improve his chances of earning more playing time.

items.headline: Brazile (undisclosed) recorded seven points (3-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds and two blocks in 20 minutes during Sunday's 109-97 preseason loss to the Jazz.
items.story: Brazile missed the final game of Summer League for undisclosed reasons, but he was able to suit up for the preseason opener. Brazile showed flashes of upside in Sunday's loss, connecting on a three-pointer and adding two blocks. The Arkansas product brings a unique skill set to Denver and could work his way into playing time if he continues to connect on jump shots, given his clear athletic tools and motor.

items.headline: Brazile is out for Sunday's Summer League finale against the Raptors for undisclosed reasons, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Brazile is likely just getting a rest day for the team's final Summer League game. The No. 35 pick showed clear upside during his time in Las Vegas, averaging 25.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and 1.0 assists in 28.0 minutes per contest across two appearances.

items.headline: Brazile collected 19 points (7-17 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and three blocks in 29 minutes during Thursday's 108-101 Summer League loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Brazile put together a strong all-around showing, but it wasn't enough to propel the Nuggets to a victory. He's been on a tear offensively over his last two appearances, totaling 51 points while drilling 50.0 percent of his tries from the field during this brief stretch.

items.headline: Brazile (shoulder) registered 32 points (11-19 FG, 6-12 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, one steal and one block over 27 minutes during Tuesday's 106-103 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: Brazile sat out Saturday's win over the Timberwolves due to a shoulder issue but returned Tuesday with a game-high 32 points, suggesting the injury won't be a concern moving forward. He'll look to keep rolling in Tuesday's rematch against the Thunder.

items.headline: Brazile (shoulder) won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against Minnesota, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
items.story: Brazile is managing a right shoulder strain that will keep him sidelined Saturday. It remains to be seen whether the injury will sideline him beyond the weekend, though the rookie's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against Oklahoma City.

items.headline: The Spurs selected Brazile with the No. 35 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and traded his rights to the Nuggets, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: The Spurs traded the No. 35 pick and two additional second-round picks to the Nuggets in exchange for the 26th overall pick, which San Antonio used to select Tarris Reed. Brazile will head to Denver and provide frontcourt depth. If the team is unable to secure a new deal with restricted free agent Peyton Watson (hamstring), Brazile could have an opportunity to see rotational minutes early in his career, though a consistent role is far from guaranteed. Over 36 outings (35 starts) for Arkansas in 2025-26, the big man averaged 13.1 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.6 blocks, 1.5 assists and 1.5 steals in 31.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Wagner posted 24 points (10-18 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, six assists and one steal across 38 minutes in Monday's 103-94 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: After struggling with his shot in Sunday's 108-97 loss to the Celtics, Wagner bounced back with his most efficient outing from the field in seven regular-season appearances this year. He led Orlando in assists for the third consecutive game, a welcome addition for his fantasy managers. As long as Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) remain sidelined, Wagner is likely to continue operating as the focal point on offense for the Magic.

items.headline: Wagner finished with 14 points (5-20 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds and 12 assists across 40 minutes in Sunday's 108-97 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Wagner endured a difficult shooting performance but compensated with a career-high 12 assists, demonstrating his ability to generate fantasy value through playmaking while getting his teammates involved. His 40-minute workload and 20 field-goal attempts highlighted his substantial offensive responsibilities with Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) unavailable. Wagner's expanded facilitating role provides considerable upside, although his efficiency remains an important factor in his overall fantasy production. Through six games, he's shooting just 39.6 percent from the field and 19.4 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Wagner ended with 26 points (8-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 8-9 FT), five rebounds, 11 assists and one steal across 39 minutes in Friday's 121-114 win over Toronto.
items.story: With Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) sidelined, Wagner stepped up to lead the Magic to their second win of the year. The 25-year-old finished with a season high in scoring. Through five regular-season games in 2026-27, Wagner is now averaging 20.8 points and 1.0 steals over 34.6 minutes per contest. He's also posting career highs in rebounds (6.8) and assists (7.0), though he's shot a rough 18.5 percent from deep and is averaging 4.6 turnovers per game.

items.headline: Wagner supplied 15 points (4-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 7-8 FT), four rebounds, five assists and two steals over 34 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Wagner led the Magic in assists and finished second on the team in points behind Tristan da Silva (20). However, Wagner was also responsible for a season-high seven turnovers, although he's expected to have the ball in his hands more for as long as Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) are sidelined.

items.headline: Wagner produced 23 points (9-23 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 5-5 FT), 13 rebounds, nine assists and three turnovers across 38 minutes in Sunday's 111-102 win over the Knicks.
items.story: Wagner went to work on the glass, pulling down a career-high 13 rebounds while notching his first double-double of the season. Paolo Banchero is expected to miss the next 4-6 weeks with an ankle injury, and Jalen Suggs exited Sunday's game with what appeared to be a significant knee injury. As a result, Wagner figures to be extremely busy on offense moving forward.

items.headline: Wagner accumulated 22 points (9-20 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists and one steal over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 132-125 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Wagner picked up three early fouls, ultimately limiting him to 29 minutes. However, he made the most of his time on the floor, ending as one of three Magic players to score at least 20 points. Wagner, along with Paolo Banchero, will be looking to put last season in the rearview mirror, as both players dealt with relatively significant injuries. Assuming he can stay on the floor, expect Wagner to flirt with top-50 value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Wagner (shoulder) is off the injury report for Wednesday's season opener against the Hawks.
items.story: Wagner dealt with a brief bout of shoulder soreness to end the preseason, but the issue proved to be of minimal concern. The star forward should be able to handle a normal workload in his season debut.

items.headline: Wagner (shoulder) practiced in full Tuesday and is planning to play in Wednesday's game against the Hawks, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Orlando will release its injury report Tuesday evening ahead of Opening Night, and this update suggests Wagner may not be listed. For now, fantasy managers can pencil him into lineups.

items.headline: Head coach Sean Sweeney said the team will continue to evaluate Wagner's right shoulder, and he was limited to "light work" in Sunday's practice, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Wagner exited Friday's preseason finale due to right shoulder soreness and did not return. The severity of the issue is unclear, though the 25-year-old forward can be considered questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Hawks. If he's forced to miss time, Anthony Black (ankle), Jamal Cain and Tristan da Silva would all be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Wagner exited Friday's 136-115 preseason win over the Heat with right shoulder soreness and did not return, Cody Taylor of USA Today reports.
items.story: Per Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel, head coach Sean Sweeney did not provide an update after the game, simply saying that Wagner would be "re-evaluated." For what it's worth, Wagner did return to the bench after getting ruled out for the remainder of the game, but for now, he should be considered questionable for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Hawks.

items.headline: Wagner recorded 20 points (7-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 22 minutes in Tuesday's 132-116 preseason win over the Cavaliers.
items.story: Wagner delivered an efficient offensive performance, finishing second on Orlando in scoring behind Paolo Banchero, who ended with 24 points.
