However, he appeared in less than 58 regular-season games for the third consecutive year. Regardless of what the future holds for Barrett, he will need to remain healthy. His three-point shooting also needs work, especially since he shot a career-high 40.1 percent from downtown in 2020-21, his second season in the NBA.

items.headline: Barrett wants to stay with the Raptors, per Sam Amico of HoopsWire.com.
items.story: Barrett is set for unrestricted free agency next summer following the expiration of his rookie contract extension, originally signed as a member of the Knicks in 2022. The 26-year-old swingman tends to be a better fantasy investment in points leagues. He's never shot at least 75 percent from the free-throw line and has averaged at least one steal just once in his career.

items.headline: Barrett did not participate in Canada's latest FIBA World Cup qualifying window as he gears up for the 2026-27 NBA season.
items.story: Barrett averaged 19.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists across 57 starts for Toronto during the 2025-26 regular season while shooting 49.1 percent from the field. The 26-year-old remains an important part of a Raptors offense that is expected to feature Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley. That collection of scoring options could limit Barrett's overall usage, but he should remain a steady source of points and rebounds in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Barrett amassed 23 points (9-25 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds, six assists and three steals in 43 minutes during Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett played a huge role during Toronto's seven-game playoff run, scoring at least 18 points in each contest. The star forward put together another productive campaign in 2025-26, averaging 19.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.7 three-pointers in 30.3 minutes per contest over 57 regular-season games. With most of the Raptors' core players under contract for 2026-27, Barrett is likely to handle a similar role next year.

items.headline: Barrett produced 24 points (8-21 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 4-5 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal over 43 minutes during Friday's 112-110 overtime victory over the Cavaliers in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett landed a three-pointer with just 1.2 seconds remaining in overtime, sealing an emphatic victory at home. The shot was reminiscent of Kawhi Leonard's game-winner back in 2019, with the ball skying off the back of the rim before dropping into the basket. It continues what has been a strong series for Barrett, who's averaged 24.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.7 three-pointers thus far. Toronto will now head back to Cleveland for Game 7, where Barrett will look to lead his team into the second round of the playoffs.

items.headline: Barrett tallied 25 points (9-19 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-9 FT), 12 rebounds and five assists in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 125-120 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 5 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett was relatively efficient in this one, though he did struggle at the charity stripe. Still, the 25-year-old forward led the Raptors in scoring and has now reached the 20-point threshold in four of five first-round outings. He also recorded his first double-double of the season with a game- and season-best 12 rebounds. Barrett and the Raptors will aim to stave off elimination in Friday's Game 6 in Toronto, though they could be without Brandon Ingram, who left Wednesday's loss early due to right heel inflammation.

items.headline: Barrett finished Thursday's 126-104 victory over the Cavaliers in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 33 points (12-19 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 3-7 FT), five rebounds, five assists, one block and two steals in 39 minutes.
items.story: Barrett showed up for the Raptors in a big way on the offensive end. He combined with Scottie Barnes for 66 points, though it was Barrett who drilled a team-high six triples. The 25-year-old's production on the offensive end proved to be one of the key difference makers in Game 3 to keep his squad's playoff hopes alive. Barrett is averaging 26.3 points while hitting at a clip of 64.4 percent from the field through the first three games of the first round.

items.headline: Barrett recorded 22 points (10-13 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and five assists over 38 minutes during Toronto's 115-105 Game 2 loss against the Cavaliers on Monday in the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Barrett was rebound shy from logging a double-double and had another efficient performance from the floor Monday, finishing as the Raptors' second-leading scorer behind Scottie Barnes (26 points). Barrett has gone 17-for-26 (65.4 percent) from the field over the first two games of the series, and the Raptors will need that efficiency in Game 3 on Thursday if the team wishes to avoid going down 3-0 in the series.

items.headline: Barrett logged 24 points (7-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 7-9 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal over 32 minutes during the Raptors' 126-113 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the first round of the playoffs Saturday.
items.story: Barrett was quiet in the first quarter with just two points, but he responded by scoring nine points in the second frame and 13 in the second half to lead the Raptors in scoring. He's carrying some momentum from the tail end of the regular season, when he averaged 21.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.4 threes in 31.5 minutes across his eight games prior to the start of the playoffs.

items.headline: Barrett chipped in 26 points (9-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 6-9 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 29 minutes during Sunday's 136-101 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Barrett's status was up in the air earlier in the day, but he took the court and helped the Raptors clinch a playoff berth in the lopsided victory. The Raptors have made the playoffs despite a slew of injuries throughout the regular season. Barrett endured a whopping 25 games lost to injury, and the lengthy absences of Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) and Jakob Poeltl also posed challenges. Although Quickley left the game with a hamstring issue, Barrett and the rest of the first unit are healthy as they prepare to take on the Cavaliers in the first round of the playoffs.

items.headline: Barrett (knee) is available for Sunday's game against the Nets, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Barrett was unable to play against the Knicks on Friday due to right knee soreness, but he has been given the green light to suit up in Sunday's regular-season finale. In five outings since April 1, Barrett has averaged 19.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.4 threes and 0.8 blocks over 33.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Barrett (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Brooklyn, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Barrett was ruled out shortly ahead of Friday's 112-95 loss to the Knicks, his former team. While the Raptors are fighting to stay out of the Play-In Tournament, Toronto may still be able to allow Barrett to remain off the floor versus one of the defensively vulnerable teams in the league. If that happens, Ja'Kobe Walter could remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Barrett is out for Friday's game against the Knicks due to right knee soreness, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Barrett is a late scratch from the lineup Friday, and the Raptors may proceed with caution ahead of the postseason. With the star forward sidelined against New York, the likes of Ja'Kobe Walter, A.J. Lawson and Jamal Shead should be more involved.

items.headline: Barrett finished Thursday's 128-114 win over Miami with 22 points (6-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 9-10 FT), six rebounds, three assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
items.story: Barrett didn't have a great night from three-point range, but he was better inside the arc and was aggressive, resulting in double-digit free-throw attempts for the third time this season (and second in six games since March 31). Barrett has scored at least 20 points in five of his last seven outings, and over that span he has averaged 20.9 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.3 threes and 0.9 steals over 32.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Barrett registered 25 points (9-17 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds, four assists, one block and two turnovers across 29 minutes during Friday's 128-96 victory over Memphis.
items.story: Barrett has been in a nice rhythm over the past four games, scoring 23.3 points per game on 51.6 percent shooting from the field and 81.5 percent at the line to go with 4.3 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.8 triples, 1.0 steals and 0.5 blocks per contest. He'll aim to keep it rolling Sunday in Boston.

items.headline: Barrett ended Wednesday's 123-115 loss to the Kings with 20 points (8-19 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-5 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one block in 36 minutes.
items.story: Barrett didn't have his best shooting performance, but fantasy managers will gladly overlook the lack of efficiency if he continues to produce counting stats. Barrett has scored at least 20 points in three straight games and four of the last five, a stretch in which he's averaging a solid line of 20.8 points, 4.7 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game while shooting 48.4 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Barrett finished Tuesday's 127-116 loss to Detroit with 24 points (7-12 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 8-10 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal over 31 minutes.
items.story: Barrett was listed on the injury report due to a left shoulder injury he sustained during Sunday's blowout win against Orlando. He was cleared to play Tuesday, and his shoulder didn't appear to bother him in an efficient night from both the field and charity stripe. Barrett will wrap up the month of March having averaged 21.7 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.7 threes and 0.7 steals over 31.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Barrett (shoulder) will play Tuesday against the Pistons.
items.story: Barrett will shed his probable tag for this contest. The wing is averaging 20.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 30.3 minutes per contest in his last nine games.

items.headline: Barrett (shoulder) is probable for Tuesday's game versus Detroit.
items.story: Barrett is expected to play through left shoulder stiffness Tuesday. The star swingman has averaged 20.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 30.3 minutes per contest in his last nine games, shooting an efficient 53.0 percent from the field during this period.

items.headline: Agbaji will sign a deal with the Thunder, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: With so many injuries in Oklahoma City, the Thunder will quickly move to add some veteran depth to their bench. It remains to be seen what type of role Agbaji will play, but fantasy managers can monitor him from the wire for the time being.

items.headline: The Knicks will waive Agbaji on Wednesday, Stefan Bondy of The New York Post reports.
items.story: Agbaji was on a non-guaranteed contract for training camp and will now be free to seek opportunities elsewhere. The wing holds career regular-season averages of 7.2 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.1 assists.

items.headline: Agbaji (coach's decision) won't play in Thursday's preseason game against Washington, Stefan Bondy of The New York Post reports.
items.story: The Knicks are holding out some of their players on non-guaranteed deals Thursday. According to Bondy, Agbaji will play in Monday's preseason game against the Timberwolves.

items.headline: Agbaji signed an Exhibit 9 contract with the Knicks on Wednesday.
items.story: This will be a training camp invitation for Agbaji with injury protections. The Knicks have two roster spots open and Agbaji will compete with the likes of John Konchar, Bruce Brown and Drew Eubanks.

items.headline: The Nets declined to tender a qualifying offer to Agbaji, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports Monday.
items.story: Agbaji will hit the open market after being traded from Toronto to Brooklyn in February. Across 20 regular-season appearances with the Nets, the 26-year-old forward averaged 6.7 points and 2.3 rebounds in 16.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is available for Sunday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: As expected, Agbaji has been upgraded from probable to available and will suit up for the regular-season finale. He's made only one appearance in April, posting 12 points, four rebounds, two assists and a steal in 18 minutes during a 121-115 win over Washington on April 5. He figures to see increased usage Sunday, with most of Brooklyn's regulars resting.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: Agbaji is dealing with lower-back soreness but will likely suit up for Brooklyn's regular-season finale. However, he isn't guaranteed to see significant burn if he's cleared to suit up.

items.headline: Agbaji notched 18 points (6-11 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and one rebound across 25 minutes during Sunday's 116-99 victory over the Kings.
items.story: This was certainly an outlier performance from Agbaji, as the Nets continue to give different roles on almost a nightly basis. Over his last seven games, Agbaji is averaging 18.5 minutes with 7.0 points, 2.4 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 1.0 three-pointers on 38.6 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Agbaji (ankle) is available for Saturday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: As expected, Agbaji has been upgraded from probable to available, and despite being left out of the rotation the past two games, he could reclaim minutes versus Philadelphia. Egor Demin (foot) and Day'Ron Sharpe (thumb) were recently ruled out for the season, while Nic Claxton (rest), Michael Porter (ankle) and Drake Powell (knee) are all unavailable Saturday, opening up potential minutes for Agbaji.

items.headline: The Nets list Agbaji as probable for Saturday's game against the 76ers due to left ankle sporeness, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Agbaji has been left out of the Brooklyn rotation for the past two games in coach's decisions, but assuming his ankle injury doesn't keep him from playing Saturday, he could have a chance at reclaiming some minutes. In addition to Egor Demin (foot) and Day'Ron Sharpe (thumb) being out for the season, the Nets will be without Nic Claxton (rest), Michael Porter (ankle) and Drake Powell (knee) on Saturday.

items.headline: Agbaji closed with 18 points (8-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 22 minutes during Monday's 126-115 win over Memphis.
items.story: Agbaji had his best game since arriving in Brooklyn, taking advantage of what was a favorable matchup. The 18 points represented a season-high for Agbaji, who to this point, has not even been an every-night part of the rotation for the Nets. We would need to see more of this before declaring him a viable standard league asset.

items.headline: Agbaji (recently traded) is off the injury report for Saturday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Agbaji appears ready to make his Nets debut Saturday. The forward should be available off the bench, but it's perhaps too early in his Brooklyn tenure to tell if he'll take the court in a meaningful way against Washington.

items.headline: Agbaji (not with team) has been ruled out for Thursday's game in Orlando.
items.story: Agbaji was traded to the Nets on Wednesday, but he has yet to join his new team, and thus, will be unavailable for Thursday's game. Agbaji's next chance to make his Brooklyn debut will be Saturday versus the Wizards.

items.headline: The Raptors traded Agbaji to Brooklyn on Tuesday in a three-team trade, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. The Clippers flipped Chris Paul to Toronto, while a 2032 second-round pick and cash were sent to Brooklyn.
items.story: Agbaji was frequently mentioned in the rumor mill prior to this move. The 25-year-old wing made 42 appearances in Toronto, averaging 4.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 0.4 steals in 15.5 minutes per contest. It remains to be seen what type of role he'll be able to carve out in Brooklyn, and he can be considered doubtful to debut Thursday against Orlando while the deal finalizes.

items.headline: Agbaji won't start against the Warriors on Tuesday.
items.story: Agbaji started Toronto's last two games but will revert to a bench role Tuesday. The 25-year-old forward has averaged 3.0 points and 2.2 rebounds in 10.5 minutes per contest across six appearances off the bench so far this month.

items.headline: Agbaji will start against the Clippers on Friday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: With multiple key contributors sidelined, Agbaji will step into the starting five. In 11 starts so far this season, the 25-year-old forward has averaged 6.0 points and 3.1 rebounds in 20.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Agbaji (coach's decision) went unused off the bench in Friday's 125-117 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Even though Toronto was without three rotation players in Scottie Barnes (knee), Brandon Ingram (thumb) and Jakob Poeltl (back), Agbaji couldn't maintain his grasp on a spot in the Raptors' second unit. After playing 12 minutes or fewer in each of his previous four appearances, Agbaji had already been starting to see his role trend down, and his outlook won't improve as Toronto gets healthier.

items.headline: Agbaji will come off the bench for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: The Raptors will shake things up Saturday with Collin Murray-Boyles getting the starting nod. Over Agbaji's last six appearances, he has produced 7.0 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 19.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Agbaji closed Sunday's 141-127 overtime win over the Warriors with 10 points (4-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and one assist in 20 minutes.
items.story: Agbaji has been in and out of Toronto's rotation this season, but he's drawn starts in eight straight contests. During that stretch, his fantasy value has been lacking with 6.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 0.9 assists on 44.7 percent shooting from the field in 22.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Agbaji finished Thursday's 111-105 win over the Bucks with 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal over 20 minutes.
items.story: Agbaji has logged at least 20 minutes over his last four appearances, but he reached double-digit points in just two of those. His upside isn't the greatest due to a low usage rate, and his minutes will be in serious danger with RJ Barrett (knee) due back soon.

items.headline: Agbaji will start against the Knicks on Tuesday, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The 25-year-old forward will get the starting nod for just the second time this season, pushing Ja'Kobe Walter to the bench. In his last five outings, Agbaji has averaged 4.2 points and 2.2 rebounds in 14.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Agbaji (personal) will be available for Sunday's game against the Celtics, Vivek Jacob of the Raptors' official site reports.
items.story: Agbaji is no longer appearing on the injury report after missing the past two games for Toronto. Over his last six appearances, the forward has been a fringe rotation player, averaging 12.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Agbaji (personal) won't play in Friday's game against the Hornets, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Agbaji will miss a second straight game due to personal reasons. The 25-year-old wing's absence could mean a few extra minutes for Jamison Battle, Gradey Dick or Ja'Kobe Walter, especially with RJ Barrett (knee) sidelined indefinitely. Agbaji's next chance to play will come Sunday against the Celtics.

items.headline: Agbaji (personal reasons) will not play Thursday against the Lakers.
items.story: Agbaji is a fringe rotation player for the Raptors, so his absence doesn't have many fantasy implications. His status for Friday's game against the Hornets is currently in the air.

items.headline: Agbaji logged zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) in five minutes during Wednesday's 97-95 win over the Pacers.
items.story: Agbaji is yet to record double-digit scoring this season, continuing to play a limited role off the bench. Unlike previous seasons, Toronto has put together a strong start to the season and likely has visions of making the playoffs. With a deeper roster, Agbaji has moved down the pecking order, making him a non-factor in most fantasy formats, even with RJ Barrett (knee) sidelined.

items.headline: Agbaji finished Friday's 140-110 win over the Wizards with four points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one rebound in 16 minutes.
items.story: Agbaji wasn't included in the rotation during Wednesday's 121-112 win over the 76ers after missing the previous four contests due to a lumbar strain, but he was the fifth man off the bench Friday and was able to see some minutes before the game turned into a blowout. Toronto was still without rookie Collin Murray-Boyles (knee) in Friday's game, and once he returns to action, Agbaji could find himself as the odd man out of head coach Darko Rajakovic's rotation.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is available for Wednesday's game against the 76ers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Agbaji is suiting up after sitting out Toronto's past four contests with a back issue. The 2022 first-rounder could see some playing time off the bench, but he's not a lock for a significant role. Agbaji has averaged 2.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.7 assists in 13.9 minutes per contest through nine games this season, shooting 36.0 percent from the field.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is probable for Wednesday's game against the 76ers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Agbaji appears likely to return from a four-game absence. He was a fringe rotation player prior to his injury absence, so he's not a lock to see minutes if he gets the green light.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hornets, Coty Wiles of RaptorsRepublic.com reports.
items.story: After initially being listed as questionable to play Monday, Agbaji will miss his fourth consecutive contest due to a back strain. His next opportunity to suit up will come Wednesday against the 76ers. With the 25-year-old forward sidelined, Gradey Dick and Ja'Kobe Walter are candidates for a slight bump in minutes.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is doubtful for Monday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Agbaji had been initially considered questionable to return from a three-game absence with a lumbar strain, but it looks like he's going to need at least one more contest to recover. His likely absence might open up a few extra minutes for Gradey Dick and Collin Murray-Boyles.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Hornets, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Agbaji is in jeopardy of missing his fourth consecutive contest due to a back strain. If the 25-year-old forward is ultimately ruled out, Ja'Kobe Walter and Gradey Dick are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Pacers, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.story: Agbaji will miss a third consecutive game due to a back injury, and his next opportunity to play is Monday against the Hornets. Gradey Dick, Ja'Kobe Walter and Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) are likely to absorb Agbaji's rotational minutes for Saturday's Eastern Conference tilt.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Pacers, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Agbaji has missed the past two games for Toronto but remains day-to-day. Prior to his injury, Agbaji was a fringe rotation player on the wings with very low workloads.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) has been officially ruled out for Thursday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: Agbaji has already missed Tuesday's game against Brooklyn and will now miss two consecutive games and three of his last four. Jamison Battle will likely inherit more minutes as a result, and Agbaji's next opportunity to suit up will be Saturday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Agbaji (back) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Agbaji's minutes were trending in the wrong direction prior to his latest back issue. His status won't have a big impact in fantasy hoops, though it's worth mentioning that Collin Murray-Boyles is now questionable with an illness.

items.headline: Agbaji won't play Tuesday against the Nets due to lower back spasms.
items.story: Agbaji was a late addition to the injury report and will miss at least one game with this new issue. Agbaji has been an afterthought in the rotation thus far, with an average of 13.9 minutes across nine regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Agbaji finished Saturday's 130-120 loss to the 76ers with zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and two rebounds over 15 minutes.
items.story: With Jakob Poeltl (back) ruled out for Saturday's game, Agbaji got the starting nod for the first time this season as the Raptors opted to go with a small-ball lineup. Despite entering the starting five, Agbaji was primarily used as a defender and ended up seeing less playing time than Sandro Mamukelashvili (17 minutes). The Raptors have two days of rest before their next game against the Nets on Tuesday, so Agbaji will likely revert to a reserve role assuming Poeltl is cleared to play.

items.headline: Agbaji will be in the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the 76ers, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Jakob Poeltl (back) will be unavailable for Saturday's game, so Agbaji will get the start as the Raptors decide to go with a small-ball approach to counter Joel Embiid and the 76ers. Joining Agbaji in the first unit will be Immanuel Quickley, RJ Barrett, Brandon Ingram and Scottie Barnes.

items.headline: Agbaji supplied four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and two rebounds across 16 minutes during Sunday's 117-104 victory over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Agbaji continues to back up Brandon Ingram but has not been able to produce meaningfully, as he has not eclipsed five points yet this season. However, despite being in competition with Ja'Kobe Walter and Jamison Battle for minutes, Agbaji does not seem to be in danger of losing his spot in the rotation.

items.headline: Agbaji dropped three points (1-1 FG, 1-2 FT), a rebound and an assist across 12 minutes in Friday's 122-116 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Agbaji has not been an effective contributor among Toronto's second unit, primarily due to a lack of volume and playing time. His next chance to perform would be Sunday against Dallas, but Agbaji should not be considered as a fantasy option moving forward.

items.headline: Agbaji pulled down 11 rebounds during Sunday's preseason win over Washington, adding five points (2-8 FG, 1-2 FT) and one steal in 17 minutes off the bench.
items.story: With Scottie Barnes back in action Sunday, Agbaji returned to the second unit. Agbaji has proven he can provide impactful stats when given spot starts, but it'll be tough for him to make an impact in standard leagues when he's working with the second unit.

items.headline: Portis notched 11 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt), nine rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals across 23 minutes during Wednesday's 129-117 victory over the Hawks.
items.story: Portis made his presence felt across several categories despite struggling from beyond the arc. The veteran forward finished one rebound shy of a double-double while contributing three defensive statistics, making this a productive outing in limited minutes. His ability to provide rebounding and complementary scoring off the bench should help maintain his fantasy appeal, though Miami's crowded frontcourt could limit his ceiling.

items.headline: Portis notched 10 points (3-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 12 rebounds, two assists and two blocks across 24 minutes off the bench in Monday's 113-109 loss to the Mavericks.
items.story: Portis recorded his first double-double of the season and scored in double digits for a third straight game. While he continues to struggle from the floor, Portis remains a valuable two-way asset for the Heat, and his rapport with Giannis Antetokounmpo has been valuable for a Heat team still searching for its first win of the season. Portis is providing useful production across multiple fantasy categories off the bench, but his role should remain somewhat limited as long as both Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo remain healthy.

items.headline: Portis contributed 11 points (4-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 0-0 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and a steal across 21 minutes off the bench in Friday's 128-111 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Portis provided useful scoring and rebounding production in limited minutes, connecting on three triples while finishing second on the team in rebounds. He's filling the same role he had over the last few years in Milwaukee, and Portis will remain valuable in fantasy as long as he has a steady bench role, thanks to his encouraging per-minute production and long-range shooting. Portis should remain a viable source of rebounds and three-pointers, but his ceiling is capped due to his bench role and somewhat limited playing time.

items.headline: Portis won't start Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves, Zachary Weinberger of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Portis drew the start in Friday's preseason finale but will return to the second unit Wednesday. The veteran big man is expected to play a sizable role off the Heat's bench this season.

items.headline: Portis will start Friday's preseason finale against Orlando, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: With Giannis Antetokounmpo (rest) and Bam Adebayo (groin) sidelined, Portis will enter the starting five. He's expected to operate as one of the Heat's first men off the bench in the regular season.

items.headline: Portis finished with 11 points (4-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block in 20 minutes during Thursday's 128-118 preseason victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Portis struggled with his shot but contributed across several categories, particularly on the glass and defensively. The veteran forward received a relatively substantial workload in his first preseason appearance with Miami, though his role alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo could limit his opportunities compared to previous seasons. Portis should remain a capable source of points and rebounds when given sufficient playing time.

items.headline: The Bucks traded Portis (wrist) and Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) to the Heat on Monday in exchange for Tyler Herro (foot), Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez, Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks, a pick swap and a second-round pick, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Portis spent six years in Milwaukee, winning a championship with Antetokounmpo in 2020-21 while playing a steady role off the bench throughout his tenure. He's averaged at least 10 points and five rebounds per game while shooting at least 35 percent from deep in each of his past nine seasons. Portis figures to be a key part of the new-look Heat, who lost most of their depth while acquiring a two-time MVP to pair with Bam Adebayo.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) will remain on the inactive list for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.
items.story: Expect major minutes for Jericho Sims and Ousmane Dieng on Sunday evening as the last men standing in Milwaukee's frontcourt. Portis will end his 2025-26 season with averages of 13.7 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 2.0 three-pointers per game.

items.headline: Portis is listed as out for Friday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Portis has already missed the last nine games. With only one more chance to suit up after Friday's contest, it looks like the 31-year-old won't be back on the floor again this season. While Portis remains sidelined, Pete Nance and Jericho Sims could continue to see more work.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Portis will miss a ninth straight game due to a left wrist sprain. It remains to be seen whether he'll return to the court before the end of the regular season since the Bucks have nothing to play for. With Portis out, Pete Nance and Andre Jackson figure to see more minutes in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Portis will miss an eighth consecutive contest due to a left wrist sprain. The veteran big man should be considered doubtful for Milwaukee's final three regular-season games after Tuesday until the team offers an update on his progress.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) won't play in Sunday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Portis has missed the Bucks' last six games because of a sprained right wrist. At this point, it's possible he may have already played his final game of the 2025-26 campaign. While Portis remains on the shelf, Jericho Sims should continue to see more action.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) is out for Friday's game against Boston.
items.story: Portis is slated for his sixth consecutive absence while rehabbing from a left wrist sprain. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Sunday against Memphis.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) is out for Wednesday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Portis will be sidelined for a fifth straight game Wednesday and remains without a timetable to return. Ousmane Dieng will likely continue to shoulder a big workload for the Bucks.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Portis will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left wrist sprain. His next opportunity to play will come in the second leg of this back-to-back set Wednesday against the Rockets. With the veteran forward out, Pete Nance, Jericho Sims and Ousmane Dieng are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Portis will miss a third straight game, including both halves of Milwaukee's weekend back-to-back set. In his absence, Pete Nance, Jericho Sims and Ousmane Dieng are candidates for increased roles. Portis' next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against Dallas, but with the Bucks eliminated from playoff contention, it's unlikely they'll rush the veteran back into action.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) won't play in Saturday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Portis is included on an extensive list of players who aren't available for Milwaukee. While Myles Turner (calf) is back after missing a game, which will certainly help lessen the blow, the Bucks will still need more minutes from Pete Nance, Jericho Sims and Ousmane Dieng.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Portis is in jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest due to a left wrist sprain. With Myles Turner (calf) also listed as questionable, there could be plenty of additional minutes available for Jericho Sims and Pete Nance.

items.headline: Portis (wrist) won't play Wednesday against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Kyle Kuzma (Achilles) is also out for Wednesday's game, so Pete Nance, Taurean Prince and Ousmane Dieng will have the opportunity for some extended minutes. For now, Portis should be considered questionable for Saturday's game versus the Spurs, which will be the first of a back-to-back set.

items.headline: Portis is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Trail Blazers with a right wrist sprain.
items.story: Portis had just put a rib injury behind him, but he's now dealing with a wrist issue that has him in danger of missing Wednesday's contest. Kyle Kuzma (Achilles) is also questionable, so the Bucks could be a bit thin in the frontcourt if one or both players are unable to go.

items.headline: Portis (rib) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Portis was a late scratch ahead of Saturday's win over the Suns due to left rib costochondritis, though he's set to return to action Monday. Over his last five outings, the veteran big man has averaged 18.4 points, 7.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.4 steals across 27.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Portis has been ruled out ahead of Saturday's game against the Suns due to left rib costochondritis.
items.story: Portis hadn't been included on the Bucks' injury report before surprisingly being ruled out about a half hour prior to the 10 p.m. ET tipoff. With Portis, Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Kevin Porter (knee) all sidelined Saturday, the Bucks will have plenty of usage and minutes up for grabs.

items.headline: Portis registered 19 points (8-19 FG, 3-7 3Pt), nine rebounds, four assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Tuesday's 123-116 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Portis is expected to continue playing off the bench even if Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) remains sidelined, as the veteran big man has proven to be very effective as a second-unit member. Portis has scored in double digits in his last 12 games, a span in which he's averaging 16.6 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.5 assists across 24.3 minutes per game off the bench.

items.headline: Portis registered 29 points (11-21 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and two steals in 27 minutes during Sunday's 134-123 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Portis has been dealing with a back injury but ended up playing both legs of this back-to-back set, and the veteran forward posted an impressive stat line as the Bucks snapped a four-game losing skid. Portis has been an outstanding contributor off the bench, as this was his 11th consecutive game with double-digit points, and he's also posted two double-doubles in his last four appearances. Portis is averaging 15.6 points per game off the bench since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Portis (back) will play Sunday versus the Pacers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Portis will power through the back issues and make himself available for the second leg of this back-to-back set. He's averaging 13.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.0 triples per game this season.

items.headline: Portis is questionable for Sunday's game against the Pacers due to a back strain.
items.story: Portis was sidelined Tuesday against Phoenix due to a back injury, but he's suited up in two straight games, totaling 33 points, 11 rebounds, two assists and two steals in 53 minutes. With Giannis Antetokounmpo (calf), Myles Turner (knee) and Ousmane Dieng (illness) also questionable, Milwaukee's frontcourt could be extremely shorthanded versus Indiana.

items.headline: Portis provided 19 points (8-14 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal over 26 minutes during Thursday's 112-105 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Portis returned to action Thursday following a one-game absence due to a back contusion. He served as a much-needed spark for Milwaukee's bench, finishing as the team's second-leading scorer behind Giannis Antetokounmpo. Portis has been highly efficient in March, averaging 15.3 points per game while shooting over 56.5 percent from the field across six outings. With Milwaukee's frontcourt finally reaching full health, Portis has settled back into his signature high-usage reserve role, where he continues to be a reliable source of points and triples.

items.headline: Portis (back) is available for Thursday's game against the Heat, Stephen Watson of ESPN Milwaukee reports.
items.story: Portis sat out of Tuesday's game against Phoenix while nursing a back issue, but he's received the green light to suit up Thursday. He's gotten off to a solid start to March and is averaging 14.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists in five outings.

items.headline: Portis (back) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Portis remains day-to-day after missing Tuesday's game against the Suns. If the veteran forward is unable to shake this questionable tag, the Bucks could utilize Kyle Kuzma and Pete Nance a bit more.

items.headline: Portis (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Portis was a late addition to Tuesday's injury report due to a back contusion, and the injury is severe enough for the veteran big man to sit out of Tuesday's contest. With Jericho Sims (knee) also out, the Bucks will lean more heavily on Kyle Kuzma and Pete Nance to provide depth behind Giannis Antetokounmpo and Myles Turner.

items.headline: Portis is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Suns due to a back contusion.
items.story: Portis wasn't listed on Milwaukee's initial injury report, suggesting the issue popped up overnight. Jericho Sims (knee) is also questionable, while Taurean Prince (neck) could make his long-awaited return to game action. If Portis is sidelined, Pete Nance and Kyle Kuzma could see more action.

items.headline: Portis logged 18 points (7-11 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal over 28 minutes during Sunday's 130-91 loss to Orlando.
items.story: With Giannis Antetokounmpo getting a maintenance day, Portis took on a larger role for the Bucks and was one of the few bright spots for the team in this blowout defeat. He's been solid lately with averages of 14.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 2.8 three-pointers over his last eight outings.

items.headline: Portis finished with 18 points (7-14 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds and one block across 24 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 120-97 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: The veteran big led the Bucks in scoring on the afternoon, as none of the team's starters managed more than 13 points. Portis has scored in double digits in four straight games and eight of the last 10, averaging 13.6 points, 5.2 boards, 2.1 threes and 0.8 assists in 21.9 minutes as one of the key pieces of Milwaukee's second unit.

items.headline: Portis had 17 points (8-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt), 11 rebounds, one assist and one block over 27 minutes off the bench during Friday's 139-118 victory over New Orleans.
items.story: The veteran forward produced his second straight double-double and his ninth of the season. Portis has looked good in five games since returning from a bruised hip, averaging 13.4 points, 6.2 boards, 1.8 threes, 1.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 23.0 minutes while shooting 53.8 percent from the floor and 42.9 percent from beyond the arc over that stretch.

items.headline: Portis collected 15 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt), 12 rebounds, three assists and four steals in 29 minutes during Thursday's 110-93 win over the Thunder.
items.story: Portis bounced back from a dud Wednesday against the Magic, as he was held to four points, two rebounds and one steal in 16 minutes. He looked rejuvenated Thursday night by leading the Milwaukee bench in scoring. Portis also paced the team on the defensive end with four steals, his best effort through 51 games this season.

items.headline: Portis posted 21 points (9-18 FG, 3-7 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist in 26 minutes during Friday's 105-99 win over Indiana.
items.story: Portis returned from a two-game absence due to a right hip contusion and was one of three Bucks players to score 20-plus points. The veteran big man reached the 20-point threshold for the first time since Jan. 2, though he has scored at least 15 in five of his last seven appearances. He was also effective from beyond the arc after having shot just 20.0 percent from downtown over his previous three appearances (all starts), during which he averaged 14.7 points in 36.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: Portis (hip) is available for Friday's game against the Pacers but is not in the starting lineup.
items.story: Portis started each of his last three appearances prior to his two-game absence due to a right hip contusion. However, he'll come off the bench Friday. Over his last 10 appearances off the bench, the veteran big man has averaged 13.1 points, 6.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists across 23.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Portis (hip) will play in Friday's game against the Pacers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
items.story: Portis is returning from a two-game absence with a bruised right hip. Jericho Sims now has a major obstacle to overcome for minutes Friday, though Kyle Kuzma (calf) is out. Portis has scored in double figures in nine of his last 10 outings, averaging 14.1 points, 7.6 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 29.1 minutes per game during that span.

items.headline: Portis (hip) is questionable for Friday's game versus the Pacers.
items.story: Portis has missed the past two games, but it looks like there's a chance he could return Friday. If Portis can get back on the court, there would be fewer minutes available for Andre Jackson and Pete Nance.

items.headline: Portis (hip) will not play Wednesday against the Pelicans.
items.story: Portis will be sidelined for his second straight game, with his next chance to return coming Friday against the Pacers. Portis' name has surfaced in the rumor mill, but it's unclear if the Bucks are simply being cautious with this injury.

items.headline: Portis (hip) is out  for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Portis is up against a quick turnaround if he wants to return to action Wednesday versus the Pelicans. Pete Nance should be thrust into a more sizable role in the frontcourt Tuesday, with Gary Trent also being an option for increased playing time.

items.headline: Castle produced 16 points (7-16 FG, 2-7 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists and one block over 26 minutes during Monday's 119-97 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Castle got back on track Monday after being held scoreless his last time out versus Minnesota. The third-year guard is off to a solid start overall, averaging 14.7 points, 5.6 rebounds and 5.0 assists per contest through seven games this season.

items.headline: Castle (illness) is listed as available for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Castle popped up on the injury report due to migraines, but he is good to go for Saturday's meeting with the Timberwolves. He has had a quality year thus far, averaging 17.4 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals (all career highs) along with 5.4 assists over 31.0 minutes per contest in five regular-season games in 2026-27.

items.headline: Castle (migraine) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
items.story: Castle is a late addition to the injury report, so his status will be worth monitoring closely ahead of Saturday's 8:00 p.m. ET tipoff. Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson figure to be the top candidates to enter the Spurs' starting lineup if Castle is not cleared to play.

items.headline: Castle is questionable for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves due to a migraine.
items.story: The Spurs will likely want Castle to get through his pregame routine before an official decision is made on his status for Saturday's game, so he'll likely be a game-time call. If Castle is out, Julian Champagnie would likely draw the start, and both De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper would see an uptick in usage.

items.headline: Castle supplied 14 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, eight assists, one block and two steals over 38 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime win over the Jazz.
items.story: Castle delivered a well-rounded performance, finishing two assists shy of a double-double while contributing three combined steals and blocks. The third-year guard played 38 minutes and continued to showcase his versatility as a scorer, facilitator and defender. His ability to contribute across multiple categories makes him a valuable fantasy option even when his scoring output is modest.

items.headline: Castle totaled 15 points (4-11 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, five assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 win over the Kings.
items.story: Castle has not been shy from beyond the arc this season, as he's attempted a career-high 9.3 three-pointers through four outings so far. He's converting them at a career-best clip (37.8 percent), too, making 3.5 triples a night to go along with 18.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.3 steals in 29.2 minutes. Castle's ability to stuff the stat sheet, coupled with his improved outside shooting, is a great sign for fantasy managers going forward.

items.headline: Castle tallied 19 points (8-18 FG, 3-8 3Pt), eight assists, four rebounds and three steals over 28 minutes during the Spurs' 122-106 win over the Mavericks on Saturday.
items.story: Castle set the tone early for the Spurs with nine points in the first quarter before adding another eight points in the third. He finished tied for the third-most points on San Antonio, and his eight dimes were second behind De'Aaron Fox (nine). Castle is averaging 19.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.3 steals through the first three games of the regular season.

items.headline: Castle ended with 24 points (9-21 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds and one assist over 28 minutes in Tuesday's 116-104 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: With Victor Wembanyama shooting 1-for-13 from the field and finishing with only 12 points, Castle took over as the top option offensively for the Spurs. However, his efforts weren't enough, as San Antonio couldn't earn the win to begin the year. The 2024 No. 4 overall pick finished the 2025-26 campaign by averaging 16.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 1.1 steals, all career highs, across 30.0 minutes per contest in 68 regular-season games. Castle is expected to have an even better season, and while his 12 attempts from deep Tuesday were considerably higher than usual, an improved three-point shot could help him earn a spot on the All-Star team for the first time in his career.

items.headline: The Spurs exercised the team option on Castle for the 2027-28 season Saturday, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
items.story: In an unsurprising move, San Antonio picked up Castle's team option for the 2027-28 season. After that time, he will be a restricted free agent. However, there's a good chance both sides will agree on an extension before it gets to that point, though it can't happen until next offseason. The 2024 No. 4 overall pick has appeared in 149 regular-season games for the Spurs since entering the NBA, averaging 15.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, 5.6 assists and 1.0 steals over 28.2 minutes per contest. Castle's three-point shooting needs some work, but he makes up for it with all-around contributions on both sides of the ball.

items.headline: Castle recorded 18 points (2-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 14-15 FT), four rebounds and three assists over 24 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Castle was aggressive on offense and was rewarded at the charity stripe, with eight of his 14 made free throws taking place in the second quarter. The third-year guard was a key piece to the Spurs' run to the NBA Finals last season, and while he's cemented as a backcourt starter, it remains to be seen whether he'll be joined by Dylan Harper or De'Aaron Fox. The Spurs wrap up their preseason schedule Friday against the Kings.

items.headline: Castle (rest) will play Wednesday against the Suns, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Castle is returning to the starting lineup after missing the Spurs' last preseason tilt for rest purposes. He's in line for some first-half action Wednesday.

items.headline: Castle (rest) will not play in Monday's preseason matchup against Utah, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: The Spurs planned to rest several regulars for Monday's contest before the preseason began, so Castle's absence is not believed to be injury-related. Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell are also among the players sitting out. Castle's next opportunity to suit up will come Wednesday against the Suns.

items.headline: Castle registered 13 points (5-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one steal in 21 minutes during Saturday's 102-98 preseason loss to the Suns.
items.story: The 21-year-old guard turned in a respectable performance from the field and tied Victor Wembanyama for second on the Spurs in scoring. Castle delivered a productive all-around performance, as he finished second on the team in assists and was one of three Spurs players to grab at least seven rebounds. He's scored in double figures in both of San Antonio's preseason games while shooting 10-for-18 from the field.

items.headline: Castle finished with 14 points (5-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists, a steal and a block across 18 minutes in Thursday's 123-116 preseason loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Castle delivered an efficient offensive performance, connecting on five of eight field-goal attempts while contributing across multiple statistical categories. With De'Aaron Fox sidelined by soreness, Castle shared the backcourt with Dylan Harper, offering an early glimpse of San Antonio's potential guard combinations. Castle is cemented as the starting shooting guard ahead of the regular-season opener against the Thunder on Oct. 20, so fantasy managers shouldn't read much into his lack of minutes in the preseason.

items.headline: Castle appears to be locked into a starting role at shooting guard, per Jared Weiss of the New York Times.
items.story: There's some discourse surrounding whether or not Dylan Harper should start over veteran De'Aaron Fox in 2026-27, but Castle seems to be safe from that debate. Castle was instrumental to the Spurs' deep playoff run last year, averaging 18.2 points, 6.1 assists, 5.0 rebounds, 0.9 steals and 1.5 three-pointers per game across 23 postseason appearances.

items.headline: Castle registered six points (1-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Saturday's 94-90 loss to the Knicks in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Castle was nowhere to be seen, particularly on the offensive end, where he scored a career playoff-low six points. It highlighted the fact that San Antonio was running with a highly inexperienced lineup, although one that will certainly be better for the loss. It was an unfortunate end to what was a dynamic postseason for the sophomore, who averaged 18.2 points, 5.0 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 0.9 steals and 1.5 three-pointers through 23 appearances.

items.headline: Castle provided 23 points (8-14 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal over 38 minutes during Monday's 115-111 victory over the Knicks in Game 3 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Castle delivered on the biggest stage, turning in his best performance of the NBA Finals and helping the Spurs wrestle back some of the momentum. Despite his relative inexperience, Castle has remained upbeat, even after what was a disappointing effort in Game 2. Now trailing the series 2-1, San Antonio will look to secure a second straight road victory when the two teams meet again on Wednesday.

items.headline: Castle closed with 14 points (5-14 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Friday's 105-104 loss to the Knicks in Game 2 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Castle was benched down the stretch, although he did return to the court for the final few plays. Despite solid production, Castle's performance was littered with lapses in judgment, primarily on the offensive end. On more than one occasion, he appeared to attack the basket without knowing what he was going to do. Both he and Victor Wembanyama were guilty of making errors, highlighting the fact that San Antonio is significantly outmatched when it comes to experience. Now trailing the series 2-0, Castle and his teammates will be looking to turn things around when the two teams meet again in New York on Monday.

items.headline: Fontecchio (illness) is available for Friday's game against the Pacers, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Fontecchio will return from a one-game absence due to an illness. However, he isn't guaranteed to see meaningful playing time.

items.headline: Fontecchio (illness) is probable for Friday's against the Pacers.
items.story: Fontecchio is expected to be available off the bench Friday. However, he may not see a meaningful role.

items.headline: Fontecchio (illness) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Fontecchio is still under the weather and could hit the inactive list for a second straight game. However, his potential absence wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

items.headline: Fontecchio (illness) is out for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: The veteran sharpshooter was previously listed as doubtful. His next chance to play comes Friday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Fontecchio is doubtful for Wednesday's game in Atlanta due to an illness, per Tim Reynolds of Associated Press.
items.story: Fontecchio is unlikely to be available off the bench for the first time this season. His expected absence should have little impact on the Miami rotation.

items.headline: Fontecchio is not listed in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Brooklyn.
items.story: Fontecchio came off the bench in the first two preseason contests but got the start in Saturday's loss to Minnesota. In three preseason games in 2026, the 30-year-old has averaged 8.0 points and 2.0 rebounds over 16.4 minutes per contest. His final opportunity to play before the start of the 2026-27 campaign will come Friday in Orlando.

items.headline: Fontecchio mustered 14 points (4-12 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one rebound in 24 minutes during Saturday's 125-124 preseason loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Fontecchio got the starting nod with several key contributors sidelined Saturday. The 30-year-old forward struggled mightily from two-point range but caught fire from downtown, finishing as one of five Heat players to score at least 14 points. He also led the club in three-pointers made.

items.headline: Fontecchio will start in Saturday's preseason game against the Timberwolves, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: Fontecchio is getting a spot start, with all the usual Miami starters receiving a rest day. Over nine starts last season, Fontecchio averaged 11.9 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.4 triples per contest.

items.headline: Fontecchio finished with six points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and one assist in 14 minutes during Thursday's 128-118 preseason victory over New Orleans.
items.story: Fontecchio struggled from beyond the arc, connecting on just one of his four attempts. The veteran forward will look to provide Miami with perimeter shooting and frontcourt depth, although competition for minutes could limit his fantasy relevance heading into the regular season.

items.headline: Fontecchio recorded 14 points (5-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, one steal and one block in 30 minutes during Italy's 78-76 loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina in Friday's FIBA World Cup qualifier.
items.story: The 30-year-old re-signed with Miami on a one-year deal this offseason after averaging 8.5 points and 3.0 rebounds while shooting 37.5 percent from three-point range across 70 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. Miami's offseason additions have created considerably more competition for minutes, and Fontecchio will have to contend with a deep group of forwards that includes Giannis Antetokounmpo, Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis.

items.headline: Fontecchio will return to the Heat on a one-year deal, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Miami will secure some additional shooting to spread the floor for Giannis Antetokounmpo. During 70 regular-season games in 2025-26, Fontecchio averaged 8.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 16.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Fontecchio racked up zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one block in six minutes during Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Game loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Fontecchio was used sparingly as the Heat were knocked out of the postseason. Across 70 regular-season games, Fontecchio played a relatively minor role with 8.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.8 three-pointers in 16.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Fontecchio (ankle) is available for Tuesday's Play-In Tournament matchup against the Hornets.
items.story: After sitting out Sunday's regular-season finale due to left ankle soreness, Fontecchio is ready to suit back up Tuesday. Unless Pelle Larsson (leg) winds up being unavailable, Fontecchio might not see a meaningful role in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Fontecchio (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Fontecchio drew the probable tag for Sunday's game, but his left ankle injury is more severe than initially though and will prevent him from playing against Atlanta. Myron Gardner, Kel'el Ware and Keshad Johnson are all in line for more minutes Sunday in Fontecchio's absence. Fontecchio will end his fourth NBA regular season averaging 8.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.8 threes over 16.8 minutes per game in 70 outings (nine starts). He will work on being cleared to return for Wednesday's Play-In Tournament clash against the Hornets.

items.headline: Fontecchio (ankle) has been downgraded from probable to questionable for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Fontecchio is trending in the wrong direction when it comes to being available for Sunday's regular-season finale. If he's unable to play, then Myron Gardner, Kel'el Ware and Pelle Larsson would each be in line to see a bump in their minutes.

items.headline: Fontecchio is probable for Sunday's game against the Hawks despite left ankle soreness.
items.story: Fontecchio is dealing with some minor soreness in his left ankle, but it's not expected to keep him out of Sunday's regular-season finale. Check back for official confirmation on his status closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Fontecchio totaled 24 points (8-10 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Friday's 140-117 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Fontecchio not only led the way for the Heat in this blowout win over the Wizards, but he also notched a new season-high mark in points -- his previous best tally was 23 points in a loss to the Magic on Jan. 28. Fontecchio can be a productive player when given enough minutes, and if the Heat decide to rest their starters again Sunday against the Hawks, Fontecchio could be in line for another big role. If he retreats to the bench, however, his fantasy upside would be severely limited.

items.headline: Fontecchio will start in Friday's game against Washington, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.story: The Heat are down three starters, so Fontecchio will operate with the first five for Friday's meeting with the Wizards. In eight starts during the 2025-26 campaign, the 30-year-old has averaged 10.4 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 0.3 blocks and 0.6 steals across 25.0 minutes.

items.headline: Fontecchio won't start Tuesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: Fontecchio got the start in Saturday's 152-136 win over the Wizards, finishing with eight points, one rebound, four assists and one steal in 19 minutes. However, with Tyler Herro (personal) back in the lineup, Fontecchio will head back to the bench.

items.headline: Fontecchio is starting Saturday against the Wizards.
items.story: The sharpshooter is a very late addition to the starting lineup after the Heat ruled out Tyler Herro for personal reasons moments before Saturday's tipoff. It's likely to only be a spot start for Fontecchio.

items.headline: Fontecchio is not in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Spurs, Zachary Weinberger of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Fontecchio started each of the past two contests, pouring in an efficient 21 points against the Rockets on Saturday. However, he'll shift back to the bench Monday as the Heat roll out a starting lineup of Davion Mitchell, Tyler Herro, Pelle Larsson, Andrew Wiggins and Bam Adebayo. In 56 games as a reserve this season, Fontecchio is averaging 8.4 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 16.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Fontecchio (back) is available for Saturday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Fontecchio popped up on the injury report due to a back issue, but the fourth-year pro has been cleared to play in Saturday's game. He'll likely start against Houston due to the absence of Andrew Wiggins (toe).

items.headline: Fontecchio (back) is questionable for Saturday's game versus Houston.
items.story: With Andrew Wiggins (toe) ruled out, Fontecchio would likely be squandering an opportunity to start if he's unable to play. Kel'el Ware could be in line for an expanded role Saturday.

items.headline: Fontecchio is in the starting lineup for Thursday's matchup with the Lakers, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Fontecchio is replacing Norman Powell in the starting lineup for Thursday's game, and it'll be Davion Mitchell, Tyler Herro, Pelle Larsson and Bam Adebayo joining Fontecchio in the first unit. Through five starts this season, the 30-year-old forward has averaged 9.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.6 treys per game.

items.headline: Fontecchio had 10 points (3-9 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 24 minutes during Tuesday's 136-106 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: The Heat were a little shorthanded Tuesday, allowing Fontecchio to see an expanded role. It's worth noting, however, that Keshad Johnson made a really strong impression on the coaching staff, and he could be a threat to Fontecchio's minutes going forward.

items.headline: Fontecchio closed with 18 points (6-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal across 22 minutes during Tuesday's 150-129 win over Washington.
items.story: Fontecchio made his return to the rotation after a three-game absence and took full advantage of the extended opportunity he saw due to the absences of Tyler Herro (quadriceps), Norman Powell (groin) and Andrew Wiggins (toe). Fontecchio's 22 minutes were the most he's played since Feb. 11, but the inconsistent and limited role doesn't bode well for his fantasy prospects moving forward.

items.headline: Fontecchio (groin) is available for Tuesday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Following a three-game absence, Fontecchio will be back in action Tuesday. With Kel'el Ware (shoulder) sitting out, Fontecchio may absorb a few extra minutes.

items.headline: Fontecchio is probable for Tuesday's game against the Wizards with a left groin strain.
items.story: The sharpshooter is expected to be available off the bench after missing Miami's last three contests, but he's not guaranteed to play a meaningful role. Before getting injured, Fontecchio had logged at least 20 minutes in just one of his prior five appearances.

items.headline: Fontecchio (groin) will not play Sunday against Detroit.
items.story: Fontecchio will be sidelined for a third straight game Sunday and remains without a timetable to return. The Heat will likely continue to lean more on Kel'el Ware and Pelle Larsson in the meantime.

items.headline: Fontecchio (groin) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Fontecchio will miss a second straight game due to a left groin strain. The Heat's wing rotation is currently depleted with Norman Powell (groin) and Nikola Jovic (back) also sidelined, which should lead to expanded roles for Pelle Larsson and Kel'el Ware. Fontecchio's next opportunity to suit up will come Sunday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Fontecchio has a left groin strain and will not play Thursday against the Nets.
items.story: This is a new issue for Fontecchio for the front end of this back-to-back set. With this news, the Heat could rely more on Pelle Larsson and Kel'el Ware.

items.headline: Fontecchio racked up 12 points (3-6 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 20 minutes during Tuesday's 124-98 win over the Nets.
items.story: With the Heat fairly healthy, Fontecchio is falling out of favor with head coach Erik Spoelstra. The 20 minutes were Fontecchio's first time in double digits since Feb. 11, and the enhanced workload likely had more to do with the blowout nature of Tuesday's contest.

items.headline: Fontecchio is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Jazz, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Fontecchio will step into the starting lineup with Myron Gardner moving to the bench and Norman Powell (back) inactive. In three starts this season, Fontecchio is averaging 7.7 points, 5.7 rebounds and 2.7 assists in 26.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Fontecchio amassed 12 points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and three steals across 19 minutes during Sunday's 132-101 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Fontecchio is carving out a solid role for himself in the Miami rotation recently. The sharpshooter has averaged 9.3 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 20.8 minutes per contest in his last seven games, while the Heat have dealt with several absences.

items.headline: Fontecchio is not in the Heat's starting lineup against the Celtics on Friday.
items.story: Fontecchio is coming off an 18-point performance against the Hawks on Tuesday. He has started each of Miami's last two games, but he'll return to the bench for Friday's contest due to the return of Andrew Wiggins.

items.headline: Fontecchio closed with 18 points (7-15 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one block in 34 minutes during Tuesday's 127-115 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Fontechhio scored 18 points, tallying double-digit points for just the second time in the past six games. Starting for the second straight game, Fontecchio also logged a season-high 34 minutes, highlighting the current struggles in Miami. While this was an encouraging performance, there is no need to overreact here. He should continue to be looked at as nothing more than a potential streaming candidate in fantasy.

items.headline: Fontecchio is in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Fontecchio will step into the starting lineup Sunday in place of Norman Powell (personal), drawing the nod over Myron Gardner and Kasparas Jakucionis. Fontecchio's lone start of the season came Dec. 15 against the Raptors, when he totaled three points (1-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and one block across 26 minutes.

items.headline: Fontecchio notched 23 points (7-11 FG, 6-9 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block across 19 minutes during Wednesday's 133-124 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Fontecchio posted his best scoring output of the season Wednesday and was deadly from three-point range, with his six threes made also representing a season-high output for the four-year veteran. Fontecchio has been enduring a tough season in Miami, but he has shown signs of turning things around of late. He has scored in double digits in six of his last seven contests, averaging 13.7 points per game and shooting 48.9 percent from deep in that span.

items.headline: Fontecchio had 17 points (7-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt), four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 25 minutes during Thursday's 127-110 loss to Portland.
items.story: Fontecchio saw an uptick in opportunities Thursday night and took full advantage. He led the Miami reserves with 17 points and looked strong once again from downtown. The 30-year-old has been on a heater from three over his last two appearances, knocking down eight of 15 attempts. It wouldn't be a shock to see Fontecchio continue to get looks off the bench while Tyler Herro (ribs) and Kel'el Ware (hamstring) are sidelined.

items.headline: Fontecchio notched 13 points (5-11 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals across 27 minutes during Monday's 135-112 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: The eight boards were a season high for Fontecchio on Monday. The sharpshooter is working his way back into the favor of head coach Erik Spoelstra, as Fontecchio has played at least 17 minutes in three consecutive games after falling out of the rotation in the Jan. 13 win over the Suns. Fontecchio's increased playing time has coincided with Tyler Herro (ribs) being unavailable again.

items.headline: Fontecchio (ankle) will play Thursday against Detroit.
items.story: Fontecchio was able to shake off a questionable tag for this contest. The forward has played a minor role recently with 14.3 minutes per game over his last six appearances.

items.headline: Poeltl logged two points (1-1 FG, 0-2 FT) and two rebounds during Wednesday's 129-99 win over the Magic.
items.story: Poeltl barely saw the floor Wednesday due to foul trouble, and he finished with less playing time than backup big men Collin Murray-Boyles (15 minutes) and Trayce Jackson-Davis (20 minutes). Poeltl is off to an incredibly slow start to the regular season, with the veteran center averaging 2.8 points and 4.5 rebounds over 19.5 minutes per game. He seems to merely be a placeholder in the starting five, as the Raptors appear to be more content with Murray-Boyles, especially in high-pressure points during the game.

items.headline: Poeltl ended with zero points (0-2 FG) and one rebound in 19 minutes during Sunday's 117-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Poeltl recorded a single rebound and no other stats, turning in what is likely his worst performance of the season. A modest start to the season has raised a lot of questions, particularly around his standard league fantasy value. Although it appears as though he will be the starter moving forward, his playing time and production have both been less than ideal. He remains a hold for now but could certainly be considered a drop in certain situations.

items.headline: Poeltl ended Wednesday's 135-92 win over the Bulls with three points (1-1 FG, 1-3 FT), six rebounds, one block and one steal over 22 minutes.
items.story: Four of the five Raptors starters scored 20 or more points during Wednesday's regular-season opener, but Poeltl was a non-factor on the offensive side of the floor. Collin Murray-Boyles came off the bench and made arguably a bigger impact on both ends of the floor, so the big-man duo could be looking at an even split in playing time to open the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Poeltl (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against Chicago.
items.story: Poeltl sat out Friday's preseason finale but should be back in action Wednesday. Across four preseason outings in 2026, he averaged 7.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 1.3 assists in 20.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Poeltl (rest) has been ruled out for Friday's preseason game against the Pistons, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Poeltl will get the night off in the second half of this back-to-back set, though he should be good to go for Wednesday's regular-season opener against Chicago. With the big man out Friday, Trayce Jackson-Davis will likely see increased burn.

items.headline: Poeltl closed with six points (2-2 FG, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and one steal in 19 minutes during Tuesday's 148-98 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Poeltl didn't offer much in the victory, although perhaps the fact that he continues to play serviceable minutes should be the biggest positive for fantasy managers. Assuming he is healthy come Opening Night, the assumption is that he will be the starting center. However, given his role last season, there is a chance his playing time is not what we would expect to see from a typical starting center. Those considering him in drafts should brace for a 25-minute per-night role.

items.headline: Poeltl finished with nine points (3-3 FG, 3-4 FT), one rebound, one assist, two steals and one block in 18 minutes during Saturday's 129-105 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Poeltl's production on the glass was limited, but the bigger takeaway was his health, as back issues restricted him to 46 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. The veteran center overhauled his strength and conditioning routine during the offseason in hopes of putting the lingering issue behind him, and he's reportedly moving much better entering the new campaign.

items.headline: Poeltl is moving well and "looks good" ahead of training camp, Raptors general manager Bobby Webster said, according to Ryan Wolstat of the Toronto Sun.
items.story: Webster added that spending time at home helped Poeltl reset ahead of the upcoming campaign. The positive update suggests the veteran center is in good shape entering camp, though his workload and status will be worth monitoring as Toronto begins preseason preparations. Injuries limited Poeltl to 46 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Poeltl registered nine points (4-5 FG, 1-4 FT), seven rebounds and two steals over 22 minutes during Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Poeltl ended his season with another underwhelming performance, summing up what was basically a lost season for the veteran. An ongoing back injury was a major issue for the big man, limiting him both in terms of games and minutes played. In 53 appearances across the regular season and postseason, Poeltl averaged just 10.2 points, 6.9 rebounds and 0.7 blocks. He will likely come at a significant discount next season given the injury risk.

items.headline: Poeltl closed with two points (1-3 FG), four rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 22 minutes during Friday's 112-110 overtime victory over the Cavaliers in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Poeltl had very little impact outside of his three combined steals and blocks. Cleveland ran a lot of big lineups Friday, while Toronto opted to go in the other direction, limiting Poeltl's opportunities. Through the first six games of the series, Poeltl has averaged just 18.7 minutes per game, putting up 6.7 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.0 blocks.

items.headline: Poeltl closed Thursday's 126-104 victory over Cleveland in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with eight points (4-6 FG), six rebounds, two assists and one block across 18 minutes.
items.story: Poeltl continues to play limited minutes, resulting in what can only be described as modest production. Through three games, Poeltl has averaged just 4.7 points, 5.3 rebounds and 1.0 blocks per game. Despite Cleveland running with a sizeable lineup, Poeltl's apparent limitations have forced Toronto to counter with some small-ball looks.
