items.headline: Poeltl amassed four points (1-2 FG, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 21 minutes during Saturday's 126-113 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 1 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Poeltl logged 21 minutes in Game 1, putting him in line with the 21.9 he averaged in seven appearances in April to close out the regular season. However, the 30-year-old didn't do much offensively, recording only four points on two attempts, although he at least contributed to other statistical categories. Poeltl will look to be more productive offensively when these clubs meet Monday for Game 2.

items.headline: Poeltl registered 14 points (7-9 FG) and two rebounds across 20 minutes during Sunday's 115-101 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Poeltl had four fouls on the night which kept his minutes in check. He's been pretty solid over his last seven games, during which he has averaged 13.1 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.0 steals in 24.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poeltl closed with 18 points (9-11 FG), 11 rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal across 30 minutes during Friday's 119-106 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Poeltl  missed only two shots from the field in this win over the Pelicans. The veteran big man seems to have left his back issues in the rearview mirror and has missed just three games since the All-Star break. He's averaging 12.6 points, 8.1 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.1 blocks per game in 14 games in that span.

items.headline: Poeltl (face) is available to return to Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Kayla Grey of TSN reports.
items.story: Poeltl took an elbow to the face and had to receive five stitches above his right eye. After receiving the stitches, he's been cleared to return. That means Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Murray-Boyles will return to their typical reserve roles.

items.headline: Poeltl went back to the locker room during Wednesday's game against the Clippers after being hit in the face, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Poeltl looked to have taken an elbow to the face, and he exited the contest bloody. For now, the 30-year-old center can be considered questionable to return. While he's sidelined, look for Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Murray-Boyles to handle most of the center duties.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) is available for Wednesday's game against the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Poeltl will return from a one-game absence due to a lingering back injury. Since returning from a prolonged absence Feb. 11 due to the back issue, Poeltl has appeared in 14 games, averaging 11.4 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.1 blocks across 26.1 minutes.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Poeltl sat out Monday's matchup with Utah due to lower-back injury management, and he remains listed on the team's injury report ahead of Wednesday's tilt. The veteran center hasn't missed two straight games since returning from a back sprain in mid-February, but he'll likely still need to prove his health before gaining clearance to take the court in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) is out for Monday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Monday is the second half of Toronto's back-to-back set, and Poeltl is getting the night off for lower-back injury management. With Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) questionable to play, the Raptors could need Sandro Mamukelashvili to play a featured role at center.

items.headline: Poeltl produced 21 points (9-12 FG, 3-5 FT), 18 rebounds, five assists and one block over 36 minutes during Sunday's 119-108 win over the Pistons.
items.story: Poeltl established a season high in boards Sunday, also turning in his first 20-point, 10-rebound double-double of the year. After missing a big chunk of the season while sorting through a lingering back injury, Poeltl is rounding into form for the Raptors. Poetl has averaged 12.8 points, 8.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.5 blocks in 28.8 minutes per tilt in his last eight games, shooting a robust 71.0 percent from the field.

items.headline: Poeltl contributed eight points (4-7 FG), five rebounds and three blocks in 30 minutes during Wednesday's 122-111 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Poeltl had minimal production offensively in his return from a one-game absence due to an illness, but he contributed defensively with a game-high three blocks that also tied a season high. Since returning from an extended absence due to a back strain, Poeltl has averaged 10.2 points, 6.7 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.0 steals over 26.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Poeltl (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against New Orleans,  Vivek Jacob of the Raptors' official site reports.
items.story: Poeltl missed Tuesday's contest due to illness, but he'll be back in action Wednesday. Expect Poeltl to reclaim the starting center spot from Sandro Mamukelashvili. In his last five appearances, Poeltl is averaging 13.4 points, 8.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.6 blocks and 1.4 steals over 28.6 minutes.

items.headline: Poeltl (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the  Pelicans, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl remains day-to-day after missing the front end of this back-to-back set. If Poeltl is unable to give it a go, Sandro Mamukelashvili is likely to see another sizable workload for the Raptors, as Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) remains sidelined.

items.headline: Poeltl is out for Tuesday's game against the Rockets with an illness, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl faces a short turnaround if he hopes to suit up for Wednesday's matchup against the Pelicans. With Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) also sidelined, Sandro Mamukelashvili should get the spot start at center Tuesday and is worth streaming in most fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Poeltl is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Rockets due to illness.
items.story: Poeltl's availability for Tuesday is in jeopardy after he turned in a solid double-double Sunday against Dallas. The team should have a better idea of his availability closer to tipoff. Sandro Mamukelashvili would be in line for the start at center if Poeltl can't go.

items.headline: Poeltl finished with 16 points (8-9 FG), 10 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal across 30 minutes during Sunday's 122-92 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Poeltl is seemingly turning a corner with his back issue and is trending up in fantasy hoops. Over his last five games, he's been a second-round value in nine-category leagues with averages of 13.4 points, 8.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.6 blocks in  28.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poeltl racked up nine points (4-5 FG, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 29 minutes during Thursday's 115-107 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: This was a solid line for Poeltl as he continues to put his lingering back issue behind him. Over his last five games, he's producing third-round value in nine-category formats with averages of 11.4 points, 7.8 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.6 steals and 1.2 blocks in 27.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poeltl chipped in 18 points (7-7 FG, 4-5 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists, one block and three steals in 26 minutes before fouling out of Saturday's 134-125 victory over Washington.
items.story: Poeltl had arguably his best overall performance of the season, logging at least 26 minutes for the second straight game. The big man has dealt with back issues throughout the campaign, though he finally appears to be healthy. After being dropped in many leagues, and rightfully so, managers should check to see if he is somehow available. While the back could flare up again at any point, now is as good a time as ever to take a chance on a player who has been a proven top-70 asset in the past.

items.headline: Poeltl will start Saturday's game against the Wizards, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl is set to anchor the frontcourt Sunday after logging 28 minutes in Wednesday's loss to the Spurs -- his highest workload since returning from a 24-game absence due to a back strain. The veteran center finished that contest with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocks, showing no ill effects from the injury that required specialized treatment in January.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) is available for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Poeltl was held out for the front end of this back-to-back set for injury maintenance. With Poeltl back in the lineup, Collin Murray-Boyles will likely shift to the bench unless Scottie Barnes (quadriceps) is unable to play.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) is out for Tuesday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: With Tuesday being the first half of a back-to-back, the Raptors are holding Poeltl out for injury management. Collin Murray-Boyles and Sandro Mamukelashvili are expected to split the center minutes evenly in the absence of Poeltl.

items.headline: Poeltl will start Sunday in Milwaukee.
items.story: Poeltl came off the bench in Thursday's win over the Bulls, but he'll return to his starting role Sunday, and it'll be interesting to see how many minutes he's played. Over the past two games, Poeltl has logged a total of just 36 minutes, and he hasn't provided any defensive statistics in either of those outings.

items.headline: Poeltl contributed two points (1-1 FG) and one assist in 16 minutes during Thursday's 110-101 win over Chicago.
items.story: Poeltl was barely visible, scoring just two points in 16 minutes. It's been a disastrous season for Poeltl, having played just 23 games thus far, during which he has averaged 9.3 points and 7.3 rebounds. At this point, it may not be necessary to hold onto him outside of deeper fantasy formats. However, managers will want to keep a close eye on things in Toronto, just in case Poeltl is elevated back into the starting lineup, assuming his back injury continues to improve.

items.headline: Poeltl is not in the Raptors' starting lineup against the Bulls on Thursday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl missed 24 games spanning from late December to early February due to a back strain, but he was cleared to return for the Raptors' loss to the Pistons on Feb. 11, when he started and recorded nine points and six rebounds over 20 minutes. The veteran center will come off the bench for Thursday's contest while rookie first-rounder Collin Murray-Boyles enters the Raptors' starting five.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) finished with nine points (4-7 FG, 1-2 FT) and six rebounds in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 113-95 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Seeing his first game action since Dec. 21, Poeltl was on a tight minutes restriction but didn't seem hampered by the back issues that had kept him sidelined for 24 consecutive games. The veteran center will get the All-Star break to rest up further, but he may need more time after that to ramp up before he'll be allowed to handle a full workload.

items.headline: Poeltl (back/reconditioning) is available for Wednesday's game against the Pistons and will be on an unspecified minutes restriction, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Poeltl hasn't played since Dec. 21 due to a lower-back strain but will return to action in Toronto's final game before the All-Star break. It's unclear how many minutes he will be limited to, but his return will leave fewer minutes available for the likes of Sandro Mamukelashvili and Trayce Jackson-Davis. Per Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca, Poeltl is part of the starting lineup Wednesday. Over 21 regular-season appearances thus far, Poeltl has averaged 9.7 points, 7.7 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 25.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Detroit, per Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca.
items.story: Poeltl practiced Tuesday, and the Raptors are giving him a chance to return before the All-Star break. If the veteran center suits up for the first time since Dec. 21, the streaming appeal of both Sandro Mamukelashvili of Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) would likely take a big hit.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Pacers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: While Poeltl won't play Sunday, he's reportedly "very close" to getting back to the court. Per Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca, Poeltl went through a full practice Saturday, and at this stage, his main focus has been getting reconditioned after his back injury has kept him from playing since Dec. 21. Poeltl's next chance to play will come Wednesday versus the Pistons.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Pacers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl has been sidelined by a lower-back strain since Dec. 21, which has resulted in Sandro Mamukelashvili and rookie Collin Murray-Boyles stepping into larger roles for the Raptors. Poeltl drew the questionable tag for Sunday's contest after fully participating in Saturday's practice, but he would likely operate under a heavy minutes restriction if he's given the green light to return. The veteran center is averaging 9.7 points, 7.7 rebounds and 2.1 assists over 25.3 minutes per game across 21 regular-season appearances thus far.

items.headline: Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic said Thursday that Poeltl (back) has been "reacting really well" to his recent on-court work, and the Raptors are hopeful he can return before the All-Star break, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl has already been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bulls, but if he's able to increase his workload in practice Saturday, he may have a chance at playing as soon as Sunday's game versus the Pacers or next Wednesday's game against the Pistons. Given that he's been out since Dec. 21 due to a lower-back strain, Poeltl is likely to have some restrictions once he's cleared to play again, but he may be worth grabbing in certain leagues if he's sitting on a waiver wire. Collin Murray-Boyles and Sandro Mamukelashvili will both see their respective fantasy values take a hit once Poeltl is back in the mix and fully up to speed.

items.headline: The Raptors announced Sunday that Poeltl returned to Toronto to receive targeted pain relief treatment for his back injury and doesn't have an established timeline to return to the court, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl has been managing the back issue since the start of the season and hasn't played since suffering an aggravation of the injury Dec. 21. The Raptors noted that an update on Poeltl's status will be established once he resumes practicing, but at this point, he looks closer to week-to-week than day-to-day. Rookie first-rounder Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) and veteran Sandro Mamukelashvili should continue to handle expanded roles at center for as long as Poeltl is sidelined.

items.headline: Poeltl (back) isn't with the Raptors on their road trip and is seeing a specialist in Toronto on Thursday, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Poeltl has been sidelined since Dec. 21 due to a strained lower back, and he isn't traveling with the team on its West Coast road trip so he can see a specialist. Considering he is in Toronto and doesn't appear close to playing, it's probably safe to rule him out for the remainder of the road trip, which ends Sunday against Oklahoma City.

items.headline: Harper finished with 17 points (6-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-5 FT), seven rebounds, eight assists and two steals in 27 minutes during Monday's 119-97 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Harper led his team in scoring as part of a well-balanced attack from San Antonio. The Rutgers product continues to produce across the board and is averaging 17.0 points, 6.3 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.5 steals over his last four games.

items.headline: Harper racked up 13 points (4-17 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, eight assists and one steal in 37 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime victory over Utah.
items.story: Harper struggled with his shot, connecting on just four of 17 field-goal attempts, but compensated with a season-high eight assists. The second-year guard has started all five games this season and has scored at least 13 points in each contest. Harper's 37 minutes marked a season high, and his growing playmaking contributions are encouraging for his fantasy outlook.

items.headline: Harper logged 13 points (6-7 FG, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, six assists and two steals over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 victory over Sacramento.
items.story: Harper is settling in as a starter on the wing for the Spurs. The eventual return of Tobias Harris (calf) could complicate matters in the Spurs' first unit, but Harper should continue to enjoy an amplified role at least for the time being.

items.headline: Harper finished Saturday's 122-106 win over Dallas with 22 points (9-18 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, two assists and two steals over 28 minutes.
items.story: Harper scored 13 of his 22 points in the second half and finished as the Spurs' second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama (23 points). Harper has scored 20-plus points in back-to-back games and has gone 17-for-33 from the field in that span. He's started in each of the first three games of the regular season, but it's unclear whether he will stay in the starting five once Tobias Harris (calf) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Harper ended with 20 points (8-15 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 36 minutes during Friday's 114-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Harper scored an efficient 20 points despite the loss, although a lack of peripheral production was somewhat disappointing. Fantasy managers have to be thrilled with the fact that Harper has been inserted into the starting lineup. However, there is certainly a case to be made that sharing the floor with the likes of Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle could cut into the time he has his hands on the ball. With that said, he should still be able to flirt with mid-round value moving forward, even higher should he manage to add meaningful defensive contributions.

items.headline: Harper ended with 18 points (7-17 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds and five assists across 32 minutes during Tuesday's 116-104 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Harper had a busy night in the starting lineup, finishing second on the Spurs in scoring and tying De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle for second in rebounds. Harper's shooting was inconsistent, but he got to the line and contributed as a playmaker. The second-year guard appeared to suffer a lower-body injury after landing awkwardly on a floater attempt to start the fourth quarter, per Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com. Harper tried to play through it but eventually went to the bench for a few minutes before finishing the game with no issues.

items.headline: The Spurs exercised the team option on Harper for the 2027-28 season, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Harper had a quality 2025-26 campaign, averaging 11.8 points, 3.4 rebounds and 3.9 assists over 22.6 minutes per contest in 69 regular-season games, including four starts. The 2025 No. 2 overall pick has All-Star upside, though it may take him another year or two before he gets to that point. Harper will presumably continue to come off the bench behind De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle in 2026-27, but he should consistently see more minutes than some of the starters around the NBA.

items.headline: Harper logged 19 points (7-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four assists and a steal over 21 minutes during Friday's 126-97 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Harper led San Antonio in scoring in the rout, bouncing back nicely after managing just nine points against Phoenix on Wednesday. The No. 2 overall pick in 2025 Draft started Friday's finale and looks ready for a bigger role in his sophomore campaign.

items.headline: Harper tallied nine points (4-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist over 23 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: The Spurs continue to experiment with three-guard looks, which essentially feature De'Aaron Fox at point guard, Harper at shooting guard and Stephon Castle at small forward. While Harper may not work as a full-time starter this year, San Antonio appears early on to be committed to finding ways to get Harper in the lineup often.

items.headline: Harper (rest) is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Phoenix, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Harper is back in the starting lineup after missing Monday's game for rest purposes. The young guard should see a fair amount of playing time but may have his workload limited in the exhibition.

items.headline: Harper (rest) won't play in Monday's preseason game against Utah, per Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News.
items.story: Harper is joining the rest of the Spurs' regular starters on the sidelines Monday. His next chance to play comes Wednesday against the Suns.

items.headline: Harper posted 15 points (6-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block across 24 minutes in Saturday's 102-98 preseason loss to the Suns.
items.story: Harper led the Spurs in scoring despite playing slightly over 20 minutes, and he got the start in the backcourt due to the absence of De'Aaron Fox (undisclosed). If Fox is healthy for Opening Night against the Thunder on Oct. 20, Harper will move to a bench role, although that shouldn't stop him from seeing plenty of minutes on a regular basis.

items.headline: Harper scored 16 points (5-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT) while adding four rebounds, four assists and one steal across 19 minutes in Thursday's 123-116 preseason loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Harper was one of six players to score in double figures for the Spurs, and he led all San Antonio players in scoring. No player outside of Carter Bryant logged more than 20 minutes for the Spurs, and Harper doesn't need to log heavy minutes in the preseason since he's locked into a prominent role ahead of the 2026-27 season -- even if he's not listed as a starter in the backcourt.

items.headline: Harper is starting Thursday's game against the Hawks, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: The Spurs are getting a look at a three-guard lineup with De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle. It looks like Harper has a chance to start Opening Night with Tobias Harris (calf) injured.

items.headline: Jared Weiss of the New York Times believes coach Mitch Johnson needs to find ways to increase Harper's minutes this year.
items.story: Weiss thinks the optimal way to boost Harper's playing time would be to close games with all three of Harper, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle on the floor. It remains to be seen how willing the Spurs will be to deploy more frequent small-ball looks, as they would then have to squeeze either Devin Vassell or Tobias Harris from the lineup more often. Harper remains one of the favorites for the Sixth Man of the Year award heading into the new campaign.

items.headline: Harper finished with 25 points (10-19 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one block over 31 minutes during Saturday's 94-90 loss to New York in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Harper turned in another dynamic performance, leading the Spurs with 25 points off the bench. It was his second straight performance with at least 21 points, bringing to an end what was an impressive rookie campaign. After a solid regular season, Harper was able to increase his role during the postseason, averaging 14.1 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 three-pointers in 26.8 minutes per game through 23 appearances. Looking ahead to next season, it wouldn't be surprising to see Harper carve out a 30-minute per-night role, either off the bench or as a starter.

items.headline: Harper logged 21 points (8-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 107-106 loss to the Knicks in Game 4 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Harper continues to make a name for himself on the biggest stage, providing the Spurs with much-needed offensive production. It continues what has been a stellar postseason for the rookie, a fact that will certainly not be lost on fantasy managers heading into the 2026-27 campaign. Now trailing 3-1 in the series, the Spurs will head home for what is obviously a must-win game on Saturday.

items.headline: Hardaway provided 14 points (6-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 22 minutes during Wednesday's 129-117 victory over the Hawks.
items.story: Hardaway provided an efficient scoring punch off the bench, connecting on six of his 10 attempts while adding an unexpected pair of blocks. The veteran sharpshooter has a defined role as a perimeter scoring option for Miami, though his contributions outside of points and three-pointers are typically limited. His fantasy value is strongest in deeper leagues that need additional scoring and perimeter shooting.

items.headline: Hardaway logged five points (1-6 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two blocks and one steal in 21 minutes during Saturday's 115-110 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Hardaway struggled on the offensive end once again and is now shooting just 20.0 percent from the field and 17.6 percent from deep through three regular-season games. However, the veteran wing did tie the game-high mark in blocks.

items.headline: Hardaway contributed 14 points (4-10 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 20 minutes in Wednesday's 144-128 preseason victory over Brooklyn.
items.story: Hardaway led Miami's reserves in scoring despite connecting on just two of his eight attempts from beyond the arc. He supplemented his perimeter shooting with four points at the free-throw line and finished without a turnover. The veteran wing should provide another floor-spacing option for the Heat, although his fantasy value will likely depend heavily on three-point production.

items.headline: Hardaway finished with 14 points (4-4 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT) in 11 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 129-105 preseason win over Toronto.
items.story: Hardaway didn't miss a shot in his Heat preseason debut and finished tied for the team lead in scoring despite playing just 11 minutes. The veteran sharpshooter should provide Miami with valuable floor spacing off the bench after joining the club during the offseason, particularly alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

items.headline: Hardaway is expected to compete for the Heat's starting shooting guard job during the preseason, but Klay Thompson is considered the clear front-runner for the role, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Miami is prioritizing perimeter shooting around Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo, and Thompson's combination of size, volume and efficiency from beyond the arc gives him an edge entering camp. If Thompson claims the starting spot as expected, Hardaway would likely begin the season as one of Miami's primary perimeter options off the bench.

items.headline: Hardaway agreed to a one-year, $6.5 million deal with Miami on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After Miami acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in a blockbuster trade, the front office is adding Hardaway to bolster the team's depth and provide spacing. The 2013 No. 24 overall pick is coming off a quality 2025-26 campaign with the Nuggets, averaging 13.5 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.5 steals while shooting a career-high 40.7 percent from deep across 26.6 minutes in 80 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Hardaway registered 13 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal over 21 minutes during Thursday's 110-98 loss to Minnesota in Game 6 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: Hardaway's first season in Denver was a major success. He was a candidate for Sixth Man of the Year, appearing in 80 regular-season games. He played 26.6 minutes per contest with averages of 13.5 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.8 three-pointers while shooting 44.7 percent from the field and 40.7 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Hardaway produced 11 points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT) and five rebounds over 28 minutes during Thursday's 113-96 loss to the Timberwolves in Game 3 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: With Aaron Gordon (calf) out, Spencer Jones drew the start, but Hardaway matched his workload with 28 minutes. Through three postseason games, Hardaway is averaging 11.3 points and 3.7 rebounds on 39.1 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Hardaway (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's Game 1 against the Timberwolves.
items.story: Hardaway missed Denver's regular-season finale due to left knee soreness but will return to action Saturday. The veteran swingman averaged 10.7 points, 2.5 three-pointers, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 23.2 minutes per contest over his final 10 regular-season appearances (one start).

items.headline: Hardaway won't play Sunday against the Spurs due to left knee soreness.
items.story: Hardaway is one of several regular rotation members who will sit out Sunday's regular-season finale against the Spurs. The veteran sharpshooter enjoyed a strong regular season with Denver, averaging 13.5 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game while shooting a career-best 40.7 percent from three-point range in 80 regular-season contests (six starts).

items.headline: Hardaway will start Friday's game against the Thunder, Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman reports.
items.story: With the Nuggets holding out their usual starters, Hardaway will enter the first unit. As a starter this season (five games), the veteran swingman has averaged 17.2 points and 3.2 rebounds in 32.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hardaway is available for Saturday's game in San Antonio.
items.story: Hardaway was listed as probable, although he will now officially avoid his first absence since the 125-124 win over Philadelphia on January 5. The veteran has been a reliable contributor for Denver throughout the 2025-26 campaign,  averaging 13.7 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.1 blocks and 0.5 steals while shooting 45.0 percent from the field and 41.0 percent from deep across 26.7 minutes per contest, mostly while coming off the bench

items.headline: Hardaway (knee) is listed as probable for Saturday's game against San Antonio.
items.story: Hardaway exited Wednesday's 130-117 win over the Utah Jazz because of left-knee soreness and didn't return. Fortunately, it appears the 34-year-old avoided a serious injury, as he is expected to suit up Saturday versus San Antonio. Hardaway has been a reliable contributor for Denver throughout the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 13.7 points, 2.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 0.1 blocks and 0.5 steals while shooting 45.0 percent from the field and 41.0 percent from deep across 26.7 minutes per contest, mostly while coming off the bench.

items.headline: Hardaway exited Wednesday's 130-117 win over the Jazz in the second quarter due to left knee soreness and did not return, finishing with three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and one rebound in 10 minutes.
items.story: The veteran swingman exited Wednesday's victory with 8:40 remaining in the first half and never checked back in. Hardaway's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Saturday's game against the Spurs.

items.headline: Hardaway is questionable to return to Wednesday's game against the Jazz due to left knee soreness.
items.story: Hardaway logged just over 10 minutes in the first half before checking out with 8:40 remaining in the second quarter. If he's unable to return, he'll finish with three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and one rebound.

items.headline: Hardaway closed with 16 points (5-10 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals across 26 minutes during Sunday's 116-93 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Denver stormed back from a significant deficit in the second half, and Hardaway contributed 10 of his 16 points in the third quarter as the Nuggets erased the Warriors' lead. Hardway's numbers were also aided by premature exits from Cameron Johnson (back) and Spencer Jones (hamstring), who were both injured and failed to return.

items.headline: Hardaway totaled 21 points (5-12 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 6-7 FT) and one steal in 28 minutes during Friday's 135-129 victory over the Jazz.
items.story: Hardaway is one of the best long-range shooters in the NBA right now, and he showed that with an impressive performance in what turned out to be a tighter-than-expected win. Perhaps more importantly, Hardaway bounced back from the four-point dud he posted in the win over Dallas on Wednesday. The lack of consistency on a game-to-game basis limits Hardaway's potential from a fantasy perspective, but he's a player who can get hot at any moment. He has scored at least 20 points in four of his last eight games, but he's also produced single-digit outputs three times over that stretch. Still, as a player who's making a career-high 40.9 percent of his threes this season, Hardaway should be a player to roster even with his ups and downs.

items.headline: Hardaway ended Wednesday's 142-135 victory over the Mavericks with four points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound and two assists across 27 minutes.
items.story: Hardaway went cold from the floor, continuing a pattern of recent inconsistent performances. Although his role has remained relatively predictable, his shooting has been spotty, making him a tough player to hold in standard leagues. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he has been outside the top-250 players, averaging 11.5 points and 2.6 three-pointers in 24.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Hardaway registered 18 points (6-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds and two assists in 23 minutes during Tuesday's 125-123 victory over Phoenix.
items.story: Hardaway delivered another sharp bench performance thanks to continued success beyond the arc. After connecting on seven triples two games ago, Hardaway cooled down against Toronto but came soaring back with more shot volume Tuesday night. The veteran is on track for a career-high three-point conversion rate of 40.8 percent.

items.headline: Hardaway finished Friday's 121-115 win over the Raptors with 23 points (8-16 FG, 7-10 3Pt), four rebounds and one steal over 28 minutes.
items.story: Hardaway caught fire from the perimeter, connecting on seven three-pointers en route to 23 points. With many of the starters struggling, Hardaway filled the void on the offensive end, recording at least four triples for the fourth time in the past seven games. While this was certainly an encouraging performance, managers should view Hardaway as nothing more than a potential streaming option.

items.headline: Hardaway posted 14 points (5-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist over 21 minutes during Wednesday's 129-93 win over the Rockets.
items.story: Hardaway connected on four three-pointers, bringing his total to 12 in the past two games. As per usual, he added very little in terms of peripheral numbers, cementing his reputation as a three-point streaming option and nothing more.

items.headline: Hardaway totaled 28 points (10-16 FG, 8-12 3Pt, 0-2 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 33 minutes during Monday's 129-126 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Hardaway provided a scoring punch off the bench, trailing only Nikola Jokic in scoring for the Nuggets in a narrow defeat. The veteran wing's eight three-pointers marked a season high, with his previous best being seven treys on three occasions, most recently Jan. 29. Through 64 appearances this campaign, Hardaway has reached the 20-point mark 14 times.

items.headline: Hardaway finished with 17 points (5-6 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-7 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block across 34 minutes during Sunday's 117-108 loss to Minnesota.
items.story: Hardaway provided a much-needed spark off the bench and was the only member of Denver's second unit to score more than six points. The veteran swingman was the Nuggets' third-leading scorer and reached double figures for a third consecutive contest. Still, Hardaway doesn't offer much besides points and triples from a fantasy perspective, and he's been inconsistent from downtown of late.

items.headline: Hardaway finished with 19 points (7-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and two steals over 19 minutes off the bench during Friday's 157-103 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The veteran forward led the second unit in scoring and was one of seven Nuggets to score in double digits, as they set a new franchise record for points in a road game. Hardaway has drained at least three three-pointers in nine of the last 12 games, averaging 15.3 points, 3.6 boards, 3.2 threes and 1.2 assists in 27.5 minutes during that span while shooting 45.8 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Hardaway posted 21 points (7-8 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT) and three rebounds across 28 minutes during Wednesday's 122-116 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Hardaway is in the midst of a solid string of performances heading into the All-Star break. Over the past four games, he's averaged 18.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 0.8 assists. His scoring and rebounding averages during the stint are well above his seasonal averages in those categories. Absences from Aaron Gordon (hamstring) and Peyton Watson (hamstring) are probable reasons for the boost.

items.headline: Hardaway accumulated 23 points (6-11 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 8-12 FT), three rebounds and one assist in 28 minutes during Saturday's 136-120 win over the Bulls.
items.story: Hardaway led the Nuggets' bench in scoring and finished on the team in that category. It was his 12th game of at least 20 points, three of which have come over his last six outings. Hardaway has connected on 40.4 percent of his three-point attempts since the new year, and since then has averaged 15.6 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 3.1 threes over 29.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Hardaway produced 19 points (6-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one steal across 42 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 134-127 double-overtime loss to New York.
items.story: The veteran forward had scored just nine combined points in the prior two games while shooting just 1-for-13 from the floor, but Hardaway cranked up his efficiency Wednesday even though his usage didn't increase significantly with the extra court time. Hardaway has drained multiple three-pointers in five of the last seven contests, averaging 15.1 points, 4.6 boards, 3.4 threes and 1.4 assists in 29.4 minutes over that span while shooting 48.0 percent from beyond the arc.

items.headline: Hardaway (ankle) is not listed on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Hardaway tweaked his ankle during Friday's win over the Clippers, though he's set to play Sunday after being re-examined Saturday. The veteran swingman has scored in double figures in four straight games, averaging 19.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 27.8 minutes per tilt during that stretch.

items.headline: Nuggets head coach David Adelman said after Friday's 122-109 win over the Clippers that Hardaway tweaked his ankle during the contest and will be re-examined Saturday, Brendan Vogt of TheDNVR.com reports. Hardaway finished the game with 22 points (6-9 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT) and two rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench.
items.story: The 33-year-old wing continued his hot-shooting ways from downtown in the win, burying at least three three-pointers for the fourth game in a row en route to finishing second on the team in scoring behind Nikola Jokic (31 points). Hardaway was denied the opportunity to potentially add to his scoring haul, however, as he checked out of the game for good with 7:20 left in the fourth quarter to get his ankle checked out in the locker room. The Nuggets should provide an update on Hardaway's status when they release their next injury report later Saturday in advance of Sunday's game versus the Thunder.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Knueppel hasn't played this season, though it appears he will make his 2026-27 campaign debut versus Brooklyn. It may take him a few games to ramp up. However, Knueppel's return, even in a limited capacity, will presumably send Sion James back to the bench.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) is listed as out for Monday's game versus the Pistons.
items.story: While he is moving in the right direction, Knueppel will remain out for Monday's meeting with Detroit. For now, he should be considered week-to-week. Coby White (calf) is off the injury report, so his return will help lessen the blow, even if he plays limited minutes.

items.headline: The Hornets exercised Knueppel's (hamstring) third-year team option on Sunday.
items.story: Knueppel has yet to play in 2026-27 while dealing with a left hamstring injury, but it's clear he's one of Charlotte's foundational pieces going forward. Across 81 regualr-season games (80 starts) as a rookie, Knueppel averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 3.4 three-pointers in 31.5 minutes per contest helping him finish second in Rookie of the Year voting.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Friday. He remains out for Friday's contest against the Wizards.
items.story: Knueppel was able to log a practice with the Swarm on Thursday. While there's been no official update on his progress, it's safe to assume he's at least trending in the right direction. A timetable for his return has yet to be announced.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) will practice with the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Thursday, the Hornets announced.
items.story: Although the second-year sharpshooter hasn't been given an official timetable, this suggests that he's progressing toward a return. Knueppel will almost certainly be recalled shortly after practice, though an update on his progress may not be given immediately.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) is without a timetable for a return, Rod Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.story: Knueppel has yet to take the floor this season while on the mend from a left hamstring strain, and at this point in time, the team isn't ready to commit to a return date. Coach Charles Lee stated before Monday's game against Washington that he could have more clarity on the plan for Knueppel following the two-game road trip, which wraps up Friday in Washington.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Knueppel will miss a fourth straight outing due to a left hamstring strain, with his next chance to play coming Wednesday at Detroit. The second-year swingman's continued absence will leave additional playing time available for the likes of Sion James and Grayson Allen.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Knueppel will miss a third consecutive contest due to a left hamstring strain. The second-year swingman has been ramping up toward a return, and his next opportunity to play will come Monday against the Wizards.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) is out for Friday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Knueppel can be treated as day-to-day while he recovers from a preseason hamstring strain. He'll miss a second regular-season game Friday, but the sharpshooter has been ramping up and taking more contact at recent practices. With Knueppel sidelined, Grayson Allen should be rostered in the majority of fantasy formats as a high-end streaming option.

items.headline: Knueppel (hamstring) has returned to individual on-court activity but won't play in Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Knueppel didn't play in the preseason and will miss Wednesday's regular-season opener due to a left hamstring injury. However, he's trending in the right direction and can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Atlanta. With the 21-year-old swingman sidelined, Sion James, Grayson Allen (knee) and Royce O'Neale are candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Head coach Charles Lee said Sunday that Knueppel (hamstring) is still without a timetable for a return, though he's been ramping up and taking more contact in practice, Nick Carboni of WCNC Charlotte reports.
items.story: Knueppel missed the preseason with a left hamstring injury, though it's encouraging to see him ramping up his workload ahead of the regular season. Lee wouldn't comment on the second-year wing's status for Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Nets, so he can be considered highly questionable until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday that he "doesn't know" whether Knueppel (hamstring) will be available for the team's regular-season opener against the Nets, Owen Watterson of SI.com reports.
items.story: Knueppel's status for Opening Night remains uncertain as he continues to work his way back from his left hamstring injury. Peterson's comments suggest the Hornets aren't ready to rule out the second-year wing, though his availability will likely become clearer as training camp progresses. He has already been ruled out for the entire preseason.

items.headline: Knueppel will miss the preseason after suffering a left hamstring injury during an offseason workout, the Hornets announced Friday.
items.story: The Hornets say that Knueppel will be re-evaluated during the first week of the regular season, putting his status for Opening Night on Oct. 21 in jeopardy. Knueppel is coming off a dominant rookie campaign with regular-season averages of 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists on 47.5 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: LaMelo Ball's departure accelerates Charlotte's transition toward building around Knueppel and Brandon Miller, according to Cholo Magsino of Yahoo Sports.
items.story: The second-year wing could see increased offensive responsibilities immediately, particularly if the Hornets hand more playmaking duties to their young perimeter players. Knueppel's shooting and offensive versatility should make him a key part of Charlotte's long-term plans. Across 81 regular-season games in 2025-26, Knueppel averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists on 47.5 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Knueppel produced 11 points (3-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 29 minutes during Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic.
items.story: Knueppel was one of the deadliest shooters from three-point range during his rookie season, connecting on 42.5 percent of his attempts from beyond the arc (on 7.9 3PA/G). However, he struggled toward the tail end of the campaign, and over his last six outings (including both Play-In Tournament games), he connected on just 29.5 percent of his field-goal attempts (including 23.8 percent of three-point tries) while averaging 10.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 0.7 steals over 31.5 minutes per game. Knueppel's disappointing end to 2025-26 shouldn't take away from his historic season, as he and former Duke teammate Cooper Flagg are both frontrunners for the NBA's Rookie of the Year award.

items.headline: Knueppel finished Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Game victory over the Heat with six points (2-12 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist across 34 minutes.
items.story: Knueppel continued his recent struggles on the offensive end, shooting no better than 36 percent from the floor for the fifth straight game. While it has been a spectacular rookie season for Knueppel, his recent slump has come at arguably the worst time for the Hornets. Following Tuesday's victory, Charlotte will now face either the 76ers or the Magic for the final spot in the playoffs. Look for Knueppel to try and shoot his way back into form in what is another must-win game.

items.headline: Knueppel closed Friday's 118-100 loss to the Pistons with 10 points (4-12 FG, 2-8 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes.
items.story: Knueppel remains in a tight race with Cooper Flagg to see who will win the Rookie of the Year award, but it's safe to say the former Duke sharpshooter has cooled off lately. Knueppel has failed to reach the 15-point mark in three straight games and in six of his last eight. Furthermore, Knueppel has been limited to two or fewer three-pointers made four times during that eight-game stretch. That's below average for the rookie, who's shooting north of 42.5 percent from deep this season on nearly 8.0 attempts per game.

items.headline: Knueppel accumulated 20 points (7-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, four assists and two steals over 30 minutes during Friday's 129-108 win over the Pacers.
items.story: Knueppel has been shooting the lights out over the past two games, compiling a total of 40 points and seven triples on 14-of-26 shooting from the field and 7-of-16 shooting from beyond the arc. He'll look to keep the hot shooting going Sunday in Minnesota.

items.headline: Knueppel accumulated 20 points (7-14 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 33 minutes during Thursday's 127-107 win over Phoenix.
items.story: Knueppel reached the 20-point mark after not doing so in the past three games, but perhaps the most important thing out of this performance is that he bounced back from deep after going 1-for-9 over the past two games. Knueppel is averaging 16.0 points, 5.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game while shooting 36.8 percent from deep over his last 10 appearances.

items.headline: Knueppel recorded 13 points (5-13 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 32 minutes during Sunday's 114-99 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Knueppel has been struggling from distance over the past two games, going just 4-for-16 from three-point territory. However, he'll have an excellent chance of snapping out of his mini-slump Tuesday with a favorable matchup against the Nets in Brooklyn.

items.headline: Knueppel registered 11 points (3-14 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds and two assists over 36 minutes during Saturday's 118-114 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: That's now consecutive double-doubles for the rookie first-rounder and six on the campaign. Knueppel has scored in double figures in all but one of his past seven appearances, during which he's averaged 17.0 points, 6.1 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 3.3 three-pointers in 27.9 minutes per game.

items.headline: Knueppel registered 26 points (9-14 FG, 6-10 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 11 rebounds and eight assists over 37 minutes during the Hornets' 114-103 win over the Knicks on Thursday.
items.story: It was another strong performance out of the ROTY favorite, who connected on at least six triples for the ninth time this season and finished two assists short from registering the first triple-double of his NBA career. Knueppel's third three-pointer of the game was his 250th of the season, making him the only player age 22 or younger in NBA history to connect on 250 three-pointers in a season. The 20-year-old Duke product has been a key piece to the Hornets' resurgence this season, and since the All-Star break he has averaged 19.8 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 3.9 threes and 0.8 steals over 29.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Knueppel (back) is available for Tuesday's game against the Kings.
items.story: As expected, Knueppel will shake off his probable tag due to lower-back soreness and suit up against the injury-plagued Kings. The rookie first-rounder is coming off a lackluster shooting performance in Saturday's win over the Grizzlies and will look to bounce back Tuesday. Over 10 March appearances, he has averaged 18.2 points, 4.1 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 3.2 triples in 29.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Knueppel is listed as probable for Tuesday's game against Sacramento due to lower-back soreness.
items.story: Knueppel has been a steady presence for the Hornets in March, but he's evidently dealing with a minor back issue. He's expected to be able to play through the injury, barring any type of setback leading up to game time.

items.headline: Knueppel had 22 points (8-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 24 minutes during Tuesday's 136-106 victory over Miami.
items.story: Knueppel didn't have his best shooting performance from deep, but the rookie has shown he's more than just a spot-up shooter and has found ways to remain relevant on offense. Knueppel has drained multiple threes in seven games in a row while reaching the 20-point mark five times over that stretch. In those seven contests, the former Duke star is averaging 20.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game while shooting 44.8 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Knueppel totaled 24 points (7-13 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 5-5 FT), seven rebounds and three assists across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 117-109 win over Sacramento.
items.story: Knueppel continues to bolster his case in the Rookie of the Year Award race. The Hornets improved to 34-33 with this win, and Knueppel has been hot with 19.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 4.0 three-pointers over his last eight games.

items.headline: Knueppel totaled 27 points (9-14 FG, 6-10 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds and four assists over 34 minutes during Friday's 128-120 loss to the Heat.
items.story: Knueppel was quiet through the first half of Friday's game, but he caught fire after halftime and scored 19 of his 27 points on 6-for-10 shooting in the second half. This was the rookie's eighth game of the season with at least six treys, and it was nice to see him dish out some dimes after failing to do so in his previous outing.

items.headline: Herro had 23 points (9-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and one steal across 27 minutes in Wednesday's 132-100 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Herro didn't stuff the stat sheet in this one, though he turned in another efficient shooting performance and led Milwaukee in scoring. The star guard also connected on a game-high-tying four three-pointers and has made at least three triples in four of his five regular-season appearances. He's scored at least 23 points four times this season.

items.headline: Herro logged 23 points (7-14 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 6-10 FT), 10 rebounds, seven assists, one block and one steal across 32 minutes during Monday's 110-102 victory over Indiana.
items.story: Herro led Milwaukee in scoring while recording his first double-double of the season, helping the Bucks secure their first victory of the 2026-27 campaign. The veteran guard also contributed seven assists and three triples, delivering one of his most complete performances of the young season. Herro remains a focal point of Milwaukee's offense and should continue providing strong fantasy production.

items.headline: Herro finished with 13 points (6-14 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 0-0 FT), six rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes in Saturday's 127-116 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Herro logged the second-most minutes for the Bucks in this 11-point loss, but his contributions were subpar -- he didn't record a single defensive stat and only attempted three shots from beyond the arc. This was a step in the wrong direction for Herro, who opened the season scoring 58 points combined in his first two outings while shooting 9-for-21 from deep. Despite Saturday's subpar showing, Herro's role as one of the Bucks' go-to offensive options can't be overlooked.

items.headline: Herro recorded 34 points (12-24 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 5-7 FT), five rebounds, four assists and a steal across 32 minutes in Friday's 132-125 loss to the Bulls.
items.story: Herro posted his best scoring mark over his first two games, and he was the only Milwaukee player to score more than 20 points in this seven-point defeat. It's only been two games, but Herro looks comfortable operating as the Bucks' No. 1 option on offense. Through two contests, he has 58 points, seven rebounds and 13 assists while shooting 9-for-21 from three-point range.

items.headline: Herro ended with 24 points (9-21 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, nine assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 loss to Washington.
items.story: Herro looked great in his regular-season debut for the Bucks, and head coach Taylor Jenkins staggered his minutes with Ryan Rollins to allow Herro stretches to operate as the primary creator on offense. He appears primed for a big year as the main man in Milwaukee.

items.headline: Herro (rest) is available to play in Friday's preseason meeting with the Pacers.
items.story: Herro is back in the lineup for Milwaukee's preseason finale after getting the night off Wednesday. The star guard is coming off an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign and will look to bounce back in his first year with the Bucks.

items.headline: Herro (rest) won't play Wednesday against the Bulls, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: The star guard is receiving a rest day Wednesday. His last chance for exhibition reps arrives Friday against the Pacers.

items.headline: Herro recorded 18 points (6-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds and two assists in 23 minutes during Sunday's 105-90 preseason loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Herro led Milwaukee in scoring while tying for the team lead in rebounds, delivering an encouraging performance from beyond the arc. The veteran guard has the opportunity to play a prominent offensive role for the Bucks this season, and his combination of scoring and perimeter shooting should provide considerable fantasy value.

items.headline: Herro recorded 13 points (5-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists and a block across 23 minutes in Wednesday's 128-126 preseason win over the Thunder.
items.story: Herro bounced back from a relatively quiet preseason opener against Minnesota, connecting on three triples and shooting efficiently from the field. The guard started alongside Ryan Rollins and helped Milwaukee come back after the Bucks trailed by 18 points at halftime. Herro should remain a prominent perimeter scoring option for Milwaukee, and while the team's revamped rotation could require some adjustment as the regular season approaches, his role as one of the team's go-to scoring weapons shouldn't be at risk.

items.headline: Herro recorded 11 points (3-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds and three assists across 19 minutes in Monday's 116-97 preseason loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Herro struggled from the field overall but did connect on two of four attempts from beyond the arc, including back-to-back threes during the opening quarter. The veteran guard also chipped in three rebounds and three assists, though his four turnovers were a team high. Herro should have plenty of opportunities to handle the ball and create offense for Milwaukee, so his ability to establish chemistry with his new teammates will be one of the main storylines to monitor throughout the preseason. Even if Ryan Rollins or Kevin Porter start next to him in the backcourt once the regular season begins, Herro should handle a sizable playmaking role on a new-look Bucks team.

items.headline: Herro is participating in training camp after undergoing a foot procedure back in April.
items.story: Herro's availability at the start of camp is an encouraging sign after he dealt with injury issues during the 2025-26 campaign. The veteran guard should have an opportunity to ramp up his workload throughout the preseason as Milwaukee prepares for its regular-season opener.

items.headline: Herro (foot) was traded from the Heat to the Bucks on Monday along with Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez, Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks, a second-round pick and a swapped pick in exchange for Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Bobby Portis (wrist), Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Herro has spent his entire career with the Heat, averaging 19.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 0.2 blocks, 0.7 steals and 38.2 percent shooting from deep across 32.5 minutes in 394 regular-season appearances. Without question, the 26-year-old is a capable scorer, though his defensive limitations can be a problem. Herro has also had issues staying healthy over the years, most recently logging only 33 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 campaign. He underwent a minor foot procedure in April, but he should be ready to go for training camp. Herro is also set to hit free agency in the 2027 offseason, assuming he can't work out a long-term agreement with the Bucks.

items.headline: Herro is expected to undergo a minor procedure on his foot this week, according to Five Reasons Sports Network.
items.story: This is not expected to significantly inhibit his offseason program nor delay his next training camp, the report adds. This is to address an ongoing issue in his right foot, though it's not expected to sideline him for very long at all. Herro, who averaged 20.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.5 three-pointers in 31.3 minutes per contest across 33 regular-season games, is extension eligible this offseason.

items.headline: Herro recorded 23 points (7-18 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds and six assists across 34 minutes during Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Game loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Injuries limited Herro to 33 regular-season games in 2025-26, though he was productive during his time on the floor. Playing in his seventh NBA season, he posted averages of 20.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.5 three-pointers in 31.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Herro (foot) is available for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Hawks.
items.story: Herro was sidelined for Friday's 140-117 win over the Wizards due to a foot injury, but the veteran wing will be available for the last game of the regular season Sunday. In 16 games since March 3, Herro has averaged 21.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 2.9 threes over 32.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Herro (foot) is out for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Herro's last chance to make a regular-season appearance now comes Sunday against the Hawks. Simone Fontecchio could be in line for a spot start Friday, while Kasparas Jakucionis may also see more playing time.

items.headline: Herro (foot) is questionable for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: The Heat are contemplating a maintenance day for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Herro had 15 points, four rebounds and four assists in 28 minutes against the Raptors on Thursday.

items.headline: Herro closed Tuesday's 121-95 loss to Toronto with 14 points (5-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds and six assists over 30 minutes.
items.story: Herro returned to the court for Tuesday's game after missing Saturday's win over the Wizards while attending to a personal matter. His eight attempted field goals were a season low, but he still finished as the Heat's second-leading scorer while co-leading the team in assists with Davion Mitchell. Since the All-Star break, Herro has averaged 20.8 points, 4.7 assists, 4.6 rebounds and 2.8 steals over 31.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Herro (foot) is available for Tuesday's game versus Toronto.
items.story: Herro was listed as probable for this contest. However, he will officially suit up after missing Saturday's 152-136 win over the Wizards due to personal reasons. With Herro back in the lineup, Simone Fontecchio, who started against Washington, will likely move back to the bench.

items.headline: Herro (foot) is probable for Tuesday's game against Toronto.
items.story: The Heat removed Herro from the injury report after he missed Saturday's game for personal reasons, only to throw him right back on the report with foot soreness. The star guard is still expected to suit up despite this setback.

items.headline: Herro (personal) is available to play Tuesday against Toronto.
items.story: No surprise here as Herro shakes off a probable tag. With Herro set to return from a one-game absence, and Norman Powell (illness) healthy again, the Heat will be close to full strength Tuesday.

items.headline: Herro (personal) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Raptors, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports.
items.story: Herro was able to practice Monday after missing Saturday's game against Washington. All signs point to him returning to the court to face Toronto.

items.headline: Ament logged eight points (2-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, one block and one steal in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 132-100 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: While the rookie first-rounder's playing time may have been slightly inflated by Wednesday's blowout, it's encouraging to see the rebuilding Bucks already place an emphasis on getting Ament on the floor in some capacity. items.headline: Ament (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 128-116 loss to Washington.
items.story: The rookie forward was left out of Milwaukee's rotation after dealing with an ankle issue during the preseason. Although Ament was listed as probable entering the contest, the Bucks elected not to use him. His opportunities could remain inconsistent as he adjusts to the NBA.

items.headline: Ament (ankle) is available for Wednesday's season opener against the Wizards.

items.headline: Ament is probable for Wednesday's season opener against the Wizards with a right ankle sprain.
items.story: The rookie forward is expected to be available for his league debut Wednesday. However, Ament doesn't appear to be in line for a considerable role.

items.headline: Ament (ankle) didn't play in Friday's 128-127 preseason win over the Pacers in overtime.
items.story: Ament ended the preseason with a third straight absence due to a left ankle sprain. The rookie forward's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Wizards, though his absence likely wouldn't cause many waves in the rotation.

items.story: Ament will remain sidelined due to a left ankle sprain he sustained Oct. 7 against Oklahoma City. His availability for Friday's matchup against Indiana remains uncertain, though Milwaukee head coach Taylor Jenkins suggested the rookie should be ready for the regular season.

items.story: Ament landed awkwardly and grabbed at his left ankle. He remained in the game to shoot his free throws but headed back to the locker room shortly thereafter. It wouldn't be surprising to see the Bucks exercise caution the rest of the way.

items.story: The rookie forward made his preseason debut for the Bucks on Monday. Ament appears primed for an Opening Night role off the bench, but his fantasy appeal is likely to be limited in the early going while Milwaukee's frontcourt is healthy.

items.headline: Ament amassed 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 0-3 FT), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 27 minutes in Saturday's 96-94 Summer League win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Ament was unable to capitalize at the charity stripe Saturday, though he turned in an efficient performance from the field and tied for second on the team in scoring. The rookie No. 13 overall pick also finished second on the Bucks in rebounds. The Tennessee product scored in double figures in two of his five Las Vegas Summer League games, knocking down multiple triples in each of his last three appearances. He shot 38.9 percent from beyond the arc in Summer League play.

items.headline: Ament registered 23 points (7-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds, two steals and one assist across 25 minutes in Wednesday's 110-91 Summer League win over Charlotte.
items.story: Ament broke through offensively, leading Milwaukee in scoring during a double-digit victory. Wednesday's outing was an encouraging step forward for the No. 13 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft after he was held to single figures in each of his first three Summer League appearances. The Tennessee product is considered a raw prospect, but Ament figures to receive significant opportunities during his rookie campaign with a rebuilding Bucks squad.

items.headline: Ament accounted for seven points (3-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt), five rebounds and three turnovers in 25 minutes during Sunday's 90-80 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Ament has been relatively quiet through his first two games in Las Vegas, scoring in single digits with modest contributions elsewhere. It'll be interesting to see if he plays Monday against the Suns, with that game being the second in a back-to-back set.

items.headline: Ament (undisclosed) is in the starting lineup for Friday's Summer League game against the Heat, per Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
items.story: The Bucks held the rookie first-rounder out of California Classic Summer League play, but Ament is ready to roll Friday. He'll have a chance to showcase himself and play a featured role for as long as Milwaukee keeps him available this summer.

items.headline: Ament (undisclosed) didn't play in Monday's 95-89 California Classic Summer League loss to the Kings.
items.story: The Bucks' trade with the Heat involving Giannis Antetokounmpo (knee) and Ament was made official Monday, though the latter didn't suit up for Milwaukee in its California Classic finale. His next opportunity to make his Summer League debut will come in the Bucks' Las Vegas Summer League opener against the Heat on Friday.

items.headline: Ament (undisclosed) didn't play in Saturday's 97-83 California Classic Summer League win over the Warriors or Sunday's 89-69 California Classic Summer League loss to the Nets.
items.story: Ament, Brayden Burries and Malique Lewis all sat out Milwaukee's first two games of the California Classic. It's unclear if any of the Bucks' rookies will play Monday against the Kings, though they'll likely be available for the Las Vegas Summer League, which starts Thursday, with the Bucks' first game coming Friday against the Heat.

items.headline: Ament was selected by the Bucks with the No. 13 overall selection in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Ament appeared in 35 games for Tennessee in his lone college campaign, averaging 16.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.6 blocks while shooting 39.9 percent from the field in 29.7 minutes per tilt. The 6-foot-10 forward earned Second-Team All-SEC and SEC All-Freshman Team honors for the Volunteers. Ament will be competing with Jaime Jaquez and Kyle Kuzma for minutes in Milwaukee, so it'll be interesting to see how the rookie's role develops over training camp.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles chipped in 10 points (3-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 15 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 victory over the Magic.
items.story: Murray-Boyles provided an efficient offensive spark, connecting on two three-pointers while reaching double figures in scoring despite limited playing time. However, foul trouble restricted his involvement, as the second-year forward committed five personal fouls in just 15 minutes. His developing perimeter shooting is encouraging, but he will need a more consistent workload to become a dependable fantasy contributor.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles posted eight points (3-6 FG, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and three steals in 18 minutes during Friday's 112-102 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Murray-Boyles led the Raptors' bench in scoring Friday, and his three steals were tied with Kawhi Leonard for most on the team. Even though he's operating in a bench role, Murray-Boyles' versatility on defense and ability to switch matchups while playing alongside Leonard and Scottie Barnes will afford the second-year big man plenty of playing time. There's a scenario where Murray-Boyles enters the starting lineup this season in games when Jakob Poeltl is not available.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles racked up six points (2-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in 20 minutes during Wednesday's 135-92 win over the Bulls.
items.story: The second-year forward finished the 43-point victory as Toronto's leading rebounder despite coming off the bench. Jakob Poeltl tallied three points, six boards, one steal and one block as the starting center in 22 minutes, and it appears their playing time could be close to a 50-50 split, depending on the matchup.

items.headline: The Raptors exercised their third-year team option on Murray-Boyles' contract Tuesday, Vivek Jacob of the Raptors' official site reports.
items.story: Murray-Boyles is coming off a productive rookie campaign, averaging 8.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.8 combined steals-plus-blocks in 21.9 minutes per game across 57 regular-season appearances (22 starts). The 2025 No. 9 overall pick is set to play a sizable role as one of the first men off Toronto's bench in 2026-27, and he'll likely step into the starting lineup if Kawhi Leonard or Jakob Poeltl miss time.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Bulls.
items.story: Murray-Boyles got the night off Friday, though he should be back in action when the Raptors host the Bulls. The 21-year-old averaged 8.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.8 combined steals-plus-blocks in 21.9 minutes per game across 57 regular-season appearances (22 starts) in his rookie campaign, and he figures to see increased burn in 2026-27.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles is sitting out Friday's preseason game against the Pistons for rest, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Toronto is sitting regulars for the preseason finale, giving the main pieces of the rotation time to rest up for Wednesday's season opener against the Bulls.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles totaled 12 points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, three steals, two assists and one block in 22 minutes during Thursday's 122-120 preseason loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Murray-Boyles delivered yet another impressive performance, this time contributing on both ends of the floor. While his scoring has done most of the talking thus far during the preseason, he went to work on the defensive end Thursday, compiling four combined steals and blocks. Unsurprisingly, the hype around Murray-Boyles continues to grow, with fantasy managers now likely to have to spend a seventh- or eighth-round pick to secure his services.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles compiled 19 points (7-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and one steal in 16 minutes during Tuesday's 148-98 preseason win over New York.
items.story: Murray-Boyles put together another impressive performance, continuing what has been a strong preseason. Despite the fact that he is likely to assume a bench role come Opening Night, Murray-Boyles is seen as a potential breakout candidate this season. He should serve as the primary sixth man most nights, but there could certainly be situations in which he is inserted into the starting lineup.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles finished with 13 points (4-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 5-7 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and two blocks across 22 minutes off the bench in Saturday's 114-106 preseason win over the Clippers.
items.story: Murray-Boyles came within one rebound of a double-double, delivering an encouraging all-around performance in his reserve role. The young forward was a commanding presence defensively and made the most of his touches offensively. He's ticketed for a bigger role in his sophomore year after averaging 8.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.9 blocks in 21.9 minutes per tilt through 57 regular-season games as a rookie in 2025-26.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles finished with six points (3-10 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-1 FT), nine rebounds and one assist in 20 minutes during Saturday's 129-105 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Murray-Boyles was aggressive offensively despite struggling with his efficiency, with his 10 field-goal attempts ranking second on Toronto. The second-year forward also grabbed four offensive rebounds, and coach Darko Rajakovic recently praised his offseason development while indicating Murray-Boyles will see time at both power forward and center this season.

items.headline: Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic said Monday that Murray-Boyles will see time at both power forward and center this season, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Rajakovic added that Murray-Boyles could play alongside Jakob Poeltl at times, giving Toronto the option of using a bigger frontcourt. The second-year forward's ability to handle minutes at multiple positions could help him carve out a significant role in the Raptors' rotation, and he's likely to generate some buzz in fantasy drafts this year. There was also no mention of Murray-Boyles' sprained finger from Summer League action, suggesting he's 100 percent.

The rookie first-rounder carved out a significant role right away for the Raptors, averaging 8.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.9 blocks in 21.9 minutes per tilt through 57 regular-season games. Provided Sandro Mamukelashvili picks up his player option for 2026-27, Murray-Boyles could be in for a similar role next year unless Toronto finds a way to get off of Jakob Poeltl's gaudy contract.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles notched 17 points (6-10 FG, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, three blocks and two steals over 40 minutes during Friday's 112-110 overtime win over Cleveland in Game 6 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Murray-Boyles continues to be a difference-maker for the Raptors, having scored at least 14 points in all but one of his playoff appearances thus far. He has been able to get it done on both ends of the floor, as he's averaged 15.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.4 combined steals and blocks. With the series now tied at three games apiece, both teams will head to Cleveland for Game 7, looking to advance to the second round against either the Magic or the Pistons.

items.headline: Murray-Boyles amassed 15 points (5-11 FG, 5-7 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and two steals over 27 minutes during Sunday's 93-89 win over the Cavaliers in Game 4 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Murray-Boyles continues to play starter-level minutes despite coming off the bench, turning in another notable performance. Through the first four games of the series, the rookie is now averaging 17.0 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 25.4 minutes per contest, and he should continue to play a pivotal complementary role as the series shifts back to Cleveland.
