items.headline: Traore closed with nine points (4-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one block over 30 minutes during Thursday's 107-103 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Making his first start in the NBA with fellow rookie Egor Demin (foot) sidelined, Traore didn't look out of place, but he didn't make much of an impact, either. Traore missed the last two games himself due to an illness, and through 14 contests in January, the 19th overall pick in the 2025 Draft is averaging 7.9 points, 3.5 assists, 1.5 boards and 1.1 threes in 23.9 minutes.

items.headline: Traore is starting Thursday's game against the Nuggets, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Traore will draw the first start of his NBA career with Egor Demin (foot) sidelined. Traore sat out of Sunday's matchup against the Clippers due to illness and wasn't deployed off the bench despite being available Tuesday, but he'll be in line for his fair share of opportunities Thursday night.

items.headline: Traore (illness) is available for Tuesday's game against the Suns, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Traore missed Sunday's loss to the Clippers due to an illness but will shed his probable tag and suit up Tuesday. The rookie first-rounder has seen consistent burn across 13 appearances this month, averaging 7.8 points, 3.5 assists and 1.5 rebounds across 23.5 minutes per tilt during that span.

items.headline: Traore (illness) is listed as probable for Tuesday's game against the Suns.
items.story: Traore has been battling through an illness that prevented him from playing against the Clippers on Sunday, but the rookie first-rounder appears to be on track to play Tuesday. Friday's double-overtime loss to the Celtics was the most productive game of Traore's young career, during which he recorded 21 points, three rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block over 37 minutes.

items.headline: Traore has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Clippers due to illness.
items.story: Traore is feeling under the weather, and he'll be unavailable for Sunday's matchup with the Clippers. Cam Thomas (ankle) is also out, so Ben Saraf, Tyrese Martin and Terance Mann will handle most of the reserve guard minutes. Traore's next chance to play will come Tuesday at Phoenix.

items.headline: Traore ended Friday's 130-126 double-overtime loss to Boston with 21 points (7-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 37 minutes.
items.story: This was the performance that showed why Traore was a first-round pick for Brooklyn. He posted career highs in points, steals, and minutes played in the double-overtime loss while serving as Brooklyn's second-leading scorer on the night. Hopefully, the 19th overall pick in last year's draft builds off of this performance as the second half of his rookie season carries on.

items.headline: Williamson closed Monday's 135-134 overtime win over the Grizzlies with 25 points (9-15 FG, 7-9 FT), 11 rebounds and four assists across 35 minutes.
items.story: Williamson scorched the nets from inside the arc Monday, finishing with a team- and season-high-tying 25 points. The big man also grabbed a game-best 11 boards, securing his first double-double of the season. Williamson has been highly efficient to start the season and has scored at least 22 points in five of his seven regular-season outings. However, his streak of multi-steal games to begin the campaign ended at six Monday.

items.headline: Williamson chipped in 15 points (5-8 FG, 5-8 FT), six rebounds, four assists and three steals across 30 minutes during Saturday's 121-99 win over the Hawks.
items.story: Williamson scored 10 of his 15 points in the first half, and his three steals were second-most on the Pelicans behind Saddiq Bey (four). Williamson has opened the season shooting at a 64.4 percent rate, which as it stands would be a career high. He'll finish the month of October having averaged 20.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 3.2 steals over 31.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Williamson registered 22 points (10-12 FG, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, two assists, five steals and a block across 31 minutes in Thursday's 132-120 win over the Kings.
items.story: Williamson delivered another outstanding fantasy performance, shooting 83.3 percent from the field while recording six combined steals-plus-blocks. His defensive contributions were particularly notable, significantly boosting his value beyond scoring. Williamson has now scored at least 20 points in four of his five appearances this season while shooting an impressive, and likely unsustainable, 64.6 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Williamson delivered 25 points (10-14 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists and three steals across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 104-91 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Williamson was New Orleans' most efficient offensive contributor again and made his presence felt in a big way. The star forward has enjoyed an excellent start to the season and has surpassed the 20-point mark in three of his first four outings while recording multiple assists and steals each time. His rebounding numbers could use an uptick, but nonetheless, it's been a strong start to the campaign for Williamson, with averages of 21.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.8 steals per game while shooting 60.4 percent from the floor and 42.9 percent from deep.

items.headline: Williamson provided 23 points (8-12 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds, two assists and three steals across 33 minutes during Friday's 120-119 loss to the Jazz.
items.story: The 26-year-old forward topped 20 points for the second straight game to begin the season, but neither effort produced a win for the Pelicans. Williamson's main issue is always just to stay healthy and on the court, but so far New Orleans hasn't been limiting his workload -- after averaging 29.7 minutes across 62 regular-season games in 2025-26, he's played 32 and 33 minutes in the first two contests of the current campaign.

items.headline: Williamson notched 22 points (7-16 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 6-6 FT), three rebounds, three assists and three steals in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 123-120 loss to the Pacers.
items.story: The star forward turned in an excellent Opening Night performance, punctuated by a pair of three-pointers and a perfect display from the foul line. Williamson hit one three-pointer all of last season, so he could be preparing to add another dimension to his arsenal to boost his overall fantasy value.

items.headline: Williamson posted 11 points (5-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist over 22 minutes during Friday's 107-106 preseason win over the Wizards.
items.story: Williamson struggled with his shot, missing all four of his three-point attempts. Staying healthy has always been an issue for the 26-year-old forward, so a clean bill of health heading into the regular season is the biggest takeaway from his preseason workload.

items.headline: Williamson finished with 10 points (5-5 FG, 0-4 FT) and one assist across 18 minutes in Wednesday's 101-97 preseason win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Williamson came off the bench Wednesday after starting in two preseason contests. While free-throw shooting was an issue, he managed to drain all five of his attempts from the field. The 26-year-old ended the 2025-26 campaign by averaging 21.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.0 steals over 29.7 minutes per outing. Although Williamson certainly has the potential to make a few more All-Star appearances moving forward, his durability remains a significant concern.

items.headline: Williamson recorded eight points (3-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 16 minutes during Thursday's 128-118 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Williamson struggled to find his offensive rhythm, connecting on just three of his nine field-goal attempts while making minimal contributions elsewhere. The 26-year-old forward saw a limited workload in the exhibition contest, so his modest production isn't particularly concerning. Williamson remains a focal point of New Orleans' offense heading into the 2026-27 regular season, though his availability and durability will continue to be important considerations for fantasy managers.

items.headline: Williamson entered training camp in "impeccable condition," according to Pelicans executive Joe Dumars, who challenged the forward to prioritize his conditioning this offseason, according to New Orleans reporter Shamit Dua.
items.story: Dumars said Williamson accomplished that goal and has also been encouraged to expand his offensive game by taking more jumpers. Williamson is listed at 277 pounds, down from 284 last season, and improving his conditioning and perimeter game could help him remain productive while handling a significant role for New Orleans.

items.headline: Williamson (knee) bounced back with a productive campaign in 2025-26, reestablishing himself as the focal point of New Orleans' offense despite the team's 26-56 finish.
items.story: Williamson remains one of the league's most efficient interior scorers when healthy and should once again lead the Pelicans in usage entering 2026-27. With no major offseason additions threatening his role, Williamson is expected to remain the franchise centerpiece.

items.headline: Williamson (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Williamson has missed the last two games, and with New Orleans eliminated from postseason contention, it is easy to understand why he isn't suiting up for the final game of the 2025-26 campaign. Without Williamson in the lineup, Derik Queen will likely receive as many minutes as he can handle.

items.headline: Williamson is out for Friday's game against Boston due to right knee injury management.
items.story: It looks like the Pelicans are just about ready to shut down Williamson, though he'll have one more chance to appear during the regular season Sunday versus Minnesota. Derik Queen and Micah Peavy should see more playing time Friday for the depleted Pelicans.

items.headline: Williamson will dress for Tuesday's game against Utah, though he's unlikely to play, Erin Summers of the Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network reports.
items.story: Williamson will be available versus the Jazz. However, he will likely only see action if necessary. With Herbert Jones and Saddiq Bey also not expected to see the floor, and Trey Murphy (ankle), Yves Missi (hand) and Dejounte Murray (hand) ruled out, Derik Queen and DeAndre Jordan are the favorites to enter the starting lineup.

items.headline: Williamson closed Friday's 117-113 loss to the Kings with 13 points (5-11 FG, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists and one steal in 29 minutes.
items.story: Williamson's usual lines are essential to a productive night for the Pelicans, but he was unable to optimize his involvement in the offense during the loss. After a four-game stretch with totals of 20-plus points, he's failed to hit that milestone in four consecutive games, largely due to a slight reduction in minutes. With New Orleans having nothing to play for, we'll likely see more games in which Williamson will log less than 30 minutes as the season draws to a close.

items.headline: Williamson produced 18 points (6-8 FG, 6-8 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 25 minutes during Sunday's 134-102 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Williamson missed just two shots from the floor and two of his eight attempts from the free-throw line, but he didn't do much in other categories. The former Duke standout saw his streak of games with at least 20 points end at four contests, but he remains a reliable go-to option on offense for a Pelicans team that's no longer in the running for a playoff berth. Williamson is averaging 20.7 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game in 14 games since the beginning of March.

items.headline: Williamson posted 22 points (9-13 FG, 4-4 FT), seven rebounds and four assists across 31 minutes during Friday's 119-106 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Williamson has surpassed the 20-point plateau in four games in a row, and he's scored at least 20 in nine of his 13 appearances since the beginning of March. Williamson has managed to stay healthy throughout the majority of the campaign and has logged 58 regular-season appearances already. This could be his second-best season in terms of games played -- he's played more than 60 regular-season contests just twice in his career. Look for Williamson to remain a key piece on offense for the Pelicans as long as he's active -- he's averaging 20.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.1 steals per game since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Battle chipped in seven points (1-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), one assist and two steals across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 victory over the Magic.
items.story: Battle struggled to find his shooting touch but supplemented his scoring with a pair of steals. The reserve forward received 20 minutes in the lopsided victory, though he failed to grab a rebound and attempted just four shots. His inconsistent offensive involvement limits his fantasy appeal despite his ability to stretch the floor.

items.headline: Battle contributed 10 points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and three rebounds over 14 minutes in Thursday's 122-120 preseason loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Battle supplied instant offense off Toronto's bench, knocking down two three-pointers while finishing without a turnover. After dealing with a back injury earlier in the preseason, the forward's efficient outing was a welcome development. His ability to stretch the floor could help him compete for a spot in the Raptors' wing rotation.

items.headline: Battle (back) is expected to make his preseason debut Thursday against the Knicks, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Battle has yet to suit up this preseason while dealing with a back issue, but he appears to be nearing a return. Thursday's contest should give the Raptors an opportunity to evaluate the forward before the regular season, though it's unclear whether he'll face any minutes restrictions in his first appearance.

items.headline: Battle (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason matchup with the Knicks, Vivek Jacob of the Raptors' official site reports.
items.story: It's unclear exactly why Battle isn't playing Tuesday, though it's worth noting he previously dealt with a lower-back issue this preseason. His penultimate chance to play before the regular season will come Thursday against New York.

items.headline: Battle (lower back) isn't listed on the injury report for Saturday's preseason game against the Clippers, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Battle missed the preseason opener last weekend but returned to practice this past week and is slated to suit up Saturday. He's made 120 regular-season appearances over the past two seasons, but his path to playing time this year is muddled after the additions of Kawhi Leonard and Allen Graves.

items.headline: Battle (lower back) was a limited participant in Monday's practice, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The severity of the lower-back issue is unclear, though it kept Battle out of last Saturday's preseason-opening loss to the Heat. He'll look to continue making progress in practices ahead of Saturday's preseason matchup with the Clippers.

items.headline: Battle (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's preseason game against the Heat, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Battle was held out of Thursday's scrimmage due to a lower-back injury, and he'll remain sidelined for Toronto's preseason opener. His next chance to play in the preseason will come next Saturday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Battle was held out of Thursday's scrimmage due to a lower-back injury, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: This appears to be a precautionary move for the Raptors, who will take on the Heat in the preseason opener Saturday. Battle could be cleared to play Saturday, and he'll need to impress during the preseason to earn a role in the rotation.

items.headline: Battle racked up three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist across 14 minutes during Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: The second-year forward served mostly as frontcourt depth in 2025-26, so his fantasy impact was relatively limited. Battle averaged 4.2 points, 1.8 rebounds and 0.5 steals in 8.5 minutes per contest over 24 games during the regular season, shooting 51.0 percent from the field. If Sandro Mamukelashvili leaves this offseason, Battle could take on a larger role in 2026-27.

items.headline: Battle closed Thursday's 126-104 win over Cleveland in Game 3 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs with 14 points (5-5 FG, 4-4 3Pt) and two rebounds over 16 minutes.
items.story: Battle put together a strong line off the bench for Toronto. The Raptors quickly put this game on ice, allowing the team to go deep into their bench. Battle had logged three minutes in this series coming into Thursday.

items.headline: Battle (illness) played the final 4:31 of Friday's 128-96 win over the Grizzlies, finishing with two points (1-1 FG) and one rebound.
items.story: After missing Toronto's previous three games while recovering from an ailment, Battle was cleared to return to action but wasn't part of the rotation while the game was competitive. All of his playing time came in the fourth quarter, when Toronto had already built an insurmountable lead. Head coach Darko Rajakovic appears set to prioritize A.J. Lawson ahead of Battle for the ninth spot in his rotation while Immanuel Quickley (foot) remains sidelined indefinitely.

items.headline: Battle (illness) is available for Friday's game versus Memphis, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: After missing Toronto's past three contests due to an illness, Battle is ready to return to the floor Friday. With the Raptors' frontcourt completely healthy, Battle isn't a lock to see meaningful playing time.

items.headline: Battle (illness) is questionable for Friday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Battle has been upgraded to day-to-day after missing the past three games for Toronto. He's usually an emergency depth piece for the Raptors.

items.headline: Battle (illness) is out for Wednesday's game against the Kings.
items.story: Battle will be sidelined for a third straight contest, with his next chance to play coming Friday against Memphis. Even when available, Battle's playing time is inconsistent.

items.headline: Battle (not injury related) is out for Tuesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: After missing Sunday's win over Orlando due to an illness, Battle is now listed as out due to not being with the team. It's unknown if the forward will be able to rejoin the Raptors for Wednesday's game against the Kings. Battle has been a fringe rotation player when he's been available for Toronto, so his absence won't necessarily open up minutes for other players.

items.headline: Battle has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Orlando due to an illness, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: It looks like Battle came down with an illness over the weekend. It'll prevent him from playing Sunday, and he'll look to recover enough to be available for Tuesday's road contest against the Pistons. Gradey Dick and Ja'Kobe Walter should both see a slight uptick in minutes in Battle's absence.

items.headline: Battle produced 17 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and two assists over 23 minutes during Monday's 143-127 win over the Jazz.
items.story: Battle reached 17 points for just the second time this season, taking advantage of some extra minutes with the Raptors resting some key players. Over his last seven games, he's averaging 5.6 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.3 three-pointers in 12.7 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Battle registered two points (1-1 FG) over six minutes during Wednesday's 110-107 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Despite appearing in the box score on most nights, Battle continues to play very few minutes. In eight appearances over the past month, he has averaged just 1.4 points in 6.9 minutes, leaving him well outside the top 400 in nine-category fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Toronto recalled Battle from the G League's Raptors 905 on Saturday.
items.story: Battle will be back with the NBA squad following a brief stint in the G League. With Scottie Barnes (personal) sitting out Sunday's game in Milwaukee, Battle could end up entering the rotation, though he's unlikely to see major minutes.

items.headline: Battle ended Friday's 110-98 victory over Portland with three points (1-1 FG, 1-1 3Pt) across nine minutes.
items.story: Battle logged single-digit minutes for the third time in the past four games, continuing to serve as a depth piece for the Raptors. While he has been able to carve out a somewhat consistent role, his playing time is typically underwhelming, as he is averaging just 8.8 minutes per game through 34 appearances.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against the Lakers, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Battle didn't play against the Clippers on Friday due to a left ankle sprain, but the second-year pro has been cleared to play Sunday. He should enjoy an expanded role in the rotation due to the absences of RJ Barrett (ankle) and Ja'Kobe Walter (hip).

items.headline: Battle (ankle) has been upgraded to probable for Sunday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Battle was previously listed as questionable due to a left ankle sprain, though it now appears likely that he'll return to action after missing Friday's loss to the Clippers. Over five appearances this month (one start), the 24-year-old forward has averaged 3.4 points and 2.0 rebounds in 12.6 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Lakers, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Battle is still dealing with a left ankle sprain and could miss his second straight outing. If the 24-year-old forward joins RJ Barrett (ankle), Jakob Poeltl (back) and Ja'Kobe Walter (hip) on the sidelines, Gradey Dick, Ochai Agbaji and Collin Murray-Boyles would be candidates for increased playing time, while Alijah Martin could remain in the Toronto rotation.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: As expected, Battle has been downgraded from doubtful to out. With multiple players sidelined for Toronto, Battle started Wednesday's win in Indiana, posting five points, three rebounds and an assist in 20 minutes before leaving with a right ankle sprain. Gradey Dick has also stepped his game up recently, notching his first career double-double Wednesday, so he could see increased playing time with Battle joining the long list of unavailable Raptors.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) is doubtful for Friday's game against the Clippers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Battle, who is averaging 12.3 minutes over his last five appearances, picked up his right ankle sprain Wednesday, and it looks like it will force him to the shelf. That could open things up a bit more playing time for someone like Ochai Agbaji.

items.headline: Battle has been ruled out for the remainder of Wednesday's game against Indiana due to a right ankle sprain, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: It's unclear how exactly Battle picked up the injury, but he'll be held out the rest of the way because of it. He'll finish the game with five points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds, and one assist across 20 minutes. His absence should mean more opportunities for Gradey Dick and Ochai Agbaji. Battle's next chance to play will come Friday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Battle is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's matchup with the Pacers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Battle is getting a spot-start with Immanuel Quickley (back) unavailable, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Jamal Shead, Brandon Ingram, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles. In his previous start this season, Battle finished with four points, one rebound and one turnover in 11 minutes.

items.headline: Battle produced three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and two rebounds over eight minutes during Monday's 115-102 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Battle remained in the rotation, suiting up for the fourth straight game. Although he has been seeing the floor over the past week, his production leaves a lot to be desired, averaging 3.0 points and 1.8 rebounds during that time.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) recorded zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist across five minutes in Thursday's 111-105 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Battle saw his first action since Dec. 5, after a left ankle sprain had kept him out for two games before he was cleared to play Monday. He ultimately went unused in a coach's decision in the Raptors' eventual 106-96 win over the Heat that day, but Battle was able to get some light run in the rotation Thursday while Toronto was without Jakob Poeltl (back) and RJ Barrett (knee). One or both of those players could be ready to play in the Raptors' next game Saturday versus the Celtics, so Battle may soon find himself back outside of the rotation.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Heat, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: As expected, Battle will shed his probable tag and return from a two-game absence due to a sprained left ankle. Over his last five appearances (one start), the 24-year-old forward has averaged 4.4 points and 2.0 rebounds in 11.4 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against the Heat, Josh Lewenberg of TSN Sports reports.
items.story: Battle is on track to return from a two-game absence due to a sprained left ankle. The second-year wing has appeared in 17 games this season, averaging 3.9 points and 1.4 rebounds across 8.1 minutes.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: No surprise here, as Battle was previously listed as doubtful for Tuesday's contest due to a sprained left ankle. With the 24-year-old forward hitting the sidelines for a second straight game, Ochai Agbaji and Gradey Dick are candidates for a slight uptick in minutes.

items.headline: Battle is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Knicks due to a sprained left ankle, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Battle is in serious danger of missing back-to-back outings due to the ankle issue. His expected absence doesn't appear to free up very much playing time in the rotation, though it's possible Ochai Agbaji will see just enough minutes to warrant deep-league streaming consideration.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: Battle sprained his left ankle in Friday's loss to the Hornets and won't suit up Sunday. His next opportunity to play will come in Tuesday's NBA Cup matchup against the Knicks. Gradey Dick could see a slight bump in minutes with Battle sidelined.

items.headline: Battle (ankle) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Celtics, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Battle injured his ankle Friday and it looks like he'll be watching from the sidelines Sunday night. Jonathan Mogbo and Garrett Temple are candidates to split most of Battle's minimal minutes.

items.headline: Battle has been ruled out for the remainder of Friday's game against Charlotte due to a left ankle sprain, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Battle will finish the contest with three points (1-1 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist across 14 minutes. Although there's only a handful of minutes remaining in the contest, his absence could open up more minutes for Gradey Dick and Garrett Temple. Battle's next chance to play will come Sunday against Boston.

items.headline: Battle will come off the bench for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Battle got a spot start Sunday with Jakob Poeltl taking a rest day, but Poeltl is back and starting Tuesday, so Battle will return to a reserve role. As a reserve this season, Battle is averaging 3.6 points and 1.1 rebounds in 6.9 minutes a night.

items.headline: Battle accumulated four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and one rebound across 11 minutes during Sunday's 116-94 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Battle made his first start of the season Sunday due to the absences of RJ Barrett (knee) and Jakob Poeltl (back). However, Battle's 11 minutes of playing time were lower than five Raptors bench players, and the second-year pro was limited to just four field-goal attempts in the blowout loss. Battle will likely revert to a bench role Tuesday against the Trail Blazers, assuming Poeltl returns to the lineup after sitting out the second leg of a back-to-back set.

items.headline: Battle will start Sunday's game against the Knicks, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Battle will make his first start of the season due to Jakob Poeltl (back) being sidelined. Battle has struggled to crack the rotation this season, but he steps into a major opportunity Sunday. Over his last five appearances, he has seen just 5.8 minutes per game, averaging 2.2 points and 1.2 rebounds.

items.headline: Battle finished with two points (1-2 FG) and three rebounds in 14 minutes off the bench in Wednesday's 97-95 win over the Pacers.
items.story: After being recalled from the G League's Raptors 905 earlier in the day, Battle ended up cracking the rotation and saw his most minutes with Toronto since Nov. 3. Over 14 appearances on the season at the NBA level, Battle has averaged 3.6 points and 1.1 rebounds in 6.9 minutes.

items.headline: Battle (knee) is available for Monday's game against the Hornets, Coty Wiles of RaptorsRepublic.com reports.
items.story: Battle is active Monday after missing Saturday's win over Indiana due to a right knee contusion. The 24-year-old has averaged only 7.3 minutes across 10 appearances this season and has topped 10 minutes just three times, so his return is unlikely to impact the Raptors' rotation or elevate his fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Battle (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against Charlotte, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Battle is in jeopardy of missing his second game in a row with a knee contusion. He's been a fringe rotation player thus far, so his status doesn't carry a lot of fantasy implications.

items.headline: Battle (knee) won't play in Saturday's game against the Pacers, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.story: Battle is dealing with a right knee contusion and has been downgraded from questionable to out Saturday. The 24-year-old forward has averaged just 6.4 minutes per contest over his last five appearances, so his absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation. With Battle sidelined, Gradey Dick could see a slight bump in minutes.

items.headline: Battle tallied 20 points (7-7 FG, 6-6 3Pt), one rebound and one block over 15 minutes during the Raptors' 112-101 win over the Cavaliers on Friday.
items.story: Battle was a healthy scratch for each of the Raptors' two games prior to Friday's contest, but he was on the floor for a season-high 15 minutes and made the most of his opportunity. He was one of three Raptors players to score 20 points and was responsible for six of the team's 13 three-pointers while posting a game-high plus-28 point differential. Battle's performance Friday could help carve a consistent role for himself off the bench going into November.

items.headline: Battle put up nine points (3-3 FG, 3-3 3Pt), two rebounds and a steal in 11 minutes during Friday's 122-116 loss to the Bucks.
items.story: Battle led all bench players in scoring and made all three of his three-point attempts. While this type of production should not be expected, Battle has shown he has the ability to score given the opportunity, and may continue to see playing time while Collin Murray-Boyles (forearm) is out.

items.headline: Battle accumulated 25 points (9-19 FG, 7-15 3Pt), nine rebounds and three assists over 42 minutes during Sunday's 125-118 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Battle saved his best performance for last, finishing Sunday's contest with a season-high 25 points, which was second-most behind Scottie Barnes (35). Battle started in 10 of the Raptors' final 17 games of the regular season, and over that span he averaged 10.5 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists over 29.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Battle is in the Raptors' starting lineup against the Mavericks on Friday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Friday marks the ninth time Battle will be in the Raptors' starting five this season. The 23-year-old forward out of Ohio State has averaged 9.5 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 27.5 minutes per game over his last 15 outings.

items.headline: Quickley logged 16 points (5-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven assists, three rebounds and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 129-99 win over Orlando.
items.story: Quickley didn't have a great shooting night from the floor overall, but he had success from beyond the arc. He's averaging 2.8 threes per contest while connecting on 35.5 percent of his attempts from deep through the first four games of the regular season. Quickley can be inconsistent with his shot on a night-to-night basis, but his scoring output will be more valuable than ever given the extended absence of Kawhi Leonard (knee).

items.headline: Quickley totaled 19 points (7-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal over 28 minutes during Sunday's 117-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: With Kawhi Leonard (knee) sidelined, Quickley was one of Toronto's more effective offensive contributors, finishing third on the team in scoring while connecting on three shots from beyond the arc. However, he managed just two assists despite operating as a starting guard. Quickley's scoring and three-point production remain encouraging, but fantasy managers will want to see more consistent contributions as a facilitator.

items.headline: Quickley contributed 12 points (5-15 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), one rebound and six assists in 29 minutes during Friday's 112-102 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Quickley struggled from the field during Friday's win, failing to connect on any of his three-point attempts after going 4-for-9 from deep against the Bulls on Wednesday. However, his six assists were a team high. Quickley can be a streaky shooter, although he's connected on at least 37.0 percent of his three-point attempts in five of his six NBA regular seasons prior to 2026-27. He'll continue to command the offense and is capable of a big scoring performance on any given night.

items.headline: Quickley supplied 23 points (6-13 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 7-8 FT), four rebounds, seven assists and two steals in 28 minutes during Wednesday's 135-92 victory over the Bulls.
items.story: Quickley came out of the gate hot with 14 points in the first quarter, which included three triples. He joined the starters on the bench for most of the fourth quarter, and his 23 points were tied with Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes for most on the Raptors in Wednesday's regular-season opener. Leonard and Barnes figure to be the focal points for the Raptors on both ends of the floor, but Quickley will still be tasked with commanding the offense, as demonstrated by his game-high seven assists. Toronto will hit the road for Friday's game against Washington.

items.headline: Quickley (rest) is expected to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Bulls.
items.story: Quickley sat out Friday's preseason finale but should be able to suit up when the Raptors host the Bulls. In four appearances this preseason, he averaged 12.3 points, 5.0 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 0.8 steals in 20.2 minutes per showing.

items.headline: Quickley (rest) has been ruled out for Friday's preseason game against the Pistons, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Quickley will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set and end the preseason on the inactive list. The point guard should be cleared to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against Chicago.

items.headline: Quickley finished with 18 points (6-10 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), seven assists, five rebounds and one steal across 28 minutes in Thursday's 122-120 preseason loss to New York.
items.story: Quickley returned to Madison Square Garden and delivered an efficient scoring performance. His seven assists led Toronto, and he committed just two turnovers despite handling significant playmaking responsibilities. The guard appears comfortable directing an offense featuring several established scoring options.

items.headline: Quickley registered 18 points (6-8 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal across 19 minutes in Saturday's 114-106 preseason win over the Clippers.
items.story: Quickley was one of two starters who played less than 20 minutes in this game, with Ja'Kobe Walter being the other, but the former still ended as the Raptors' second-leading scorer behind RJ Barrett, who had 20 points. Quickley delivered an outstanding shooting performance, connecting on five of his six attempts from beyond the arc while missing just two shots from the field overall. The point guard also contributed four assists without committing a turnover, demonstrating efficiency as both a scorer and facilitator. Barring an injury between now and the start of the regular season, he'll be the Raptors' starting point guard against the Bulls on Opening Night.

items.headline: Quickley finished with five points (2-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), three assists, two rebounds and one steal in 12 minutes during Saturday's 129-105 preseason loss to Miami.
items.story: Quickley started at point guard and was held out after halftime along with the rest of Toronto's primary starters. The 27-year-old remains positioned for a significant role after averaging 16.4 points, 5.9 assists and 4.0 rebounds across 70 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, though the return of Kawhi Leonard adds another high-usage option to Toronto's offense.

items.headline: Quickley enters next season with pressure on him alongside RJ Barrett in the Raptors' backcourt, according to Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic.
items.story: Although expectations in Toronto are rising, the anticipated arrival of Kawhi Leonard should help alleviate some of the offensive burdens on Quickley at point guard. Quickley went down with a strained hamstring late last season, but not before he recorded a career-high 70 regular-season starts and averaged a career-best 5.9 assists and 1.3 steals in 31.9 minutes per game. The 27-year-old also ranked sixth in the league among qualified players in assist to turnover ratio (4.1) last year, so Quickley's ability to orchestrate the offense efficiently should help him maintain mid-round fantasy value even if he slots in as perhaps the fourth scoring option behind Leonard, Barrett and Scottie Barnes.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) is out for the remainder of Toronto's first-round series against Cleveland, per NBA reporter Marc Stein.
items.story: Quickley has suffered a setback with his right hamstring strain amid the rehab process and won't be available at any point during the quarterfinals. The sixth-year guard would now need the Raptors to advance to the second round of the playoffs in order to have a chance to return in 2025-26. With Quickley on the shelf, Jamal Shead should continue to start at point guard while Ja'Kobe Walter sees a boost in usage in the backcourt.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Game 3 against the Cavaliers on Thursday, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
items.story: Quickley has yet to play in this series, and he'll need to wait at least until Sunday's Game 4 to do so. Jamal Shead has started the first two games in Quickley's place and should be the favorite to do so again Thursday night, though Ja'Kobe Walter could also be heavily involved after dropping 14 points off the bench in Game 2.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) is questionable for Game 3 on Thursday against the Cavaliers, per Ryan Wolstat of the Toronto Sun.
items.story: The Raptors are giving Quickley a chance to return from a three-game absence with a right hamstring strain. His return would most significantly cut into the playing time of Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter, the latter of whom is also iffy for Thursday's pivotal contest due to an illness.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) won't play in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference first-round series on Monday against the Cavaliers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Quickley is unable to overcome a right hamstring strain, which will have cost him each of Toronto's first two playoff contests. The Raptors will hope to get him back in the lineup Thursday, when the series flips to Toronto for Game 3. Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter are both primed for more usage in the backcourt Monday.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) is questionable for Game 2 of the Eastern Conference first-round playoff series against the Knicks on Monday, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Quickley sustained a hamstring injury during the Raptors' regular-season finale against the Nets and has been listed as day-to-day ever since. If Quickley remains out, the Raptors will likely continue to lean on Jamal Shead.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Game 1 against the Cavaliers on Saturday, Spencer Davies of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Quickley sustained a hamstring injury during the Raptors' regular-season finale against the Nets this past Sunday. The injury is severe enough for him to miss Toronto's playoff opener, and his next opportunity to play is Game 2 on Monday. Jamal Shead figures to start for the Raptors on Saturday in Quickley's absence.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) is questionable for Game 1 against the Cavaliers on Saturday, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: For several days, the Raptors have said Quickley is day-to-day, so the questionable tag comes as no surprise. The Raptors may wait to see how he responds to warmups before a decision is made on his availability. Quickley appeared in three of Toronto's final four regular-season contests following an eight-game absence.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) was limited to an individual workout Tuesday, Ryan Wolstat of the Toronto Sun reports.
items.story: Quickley is battling a mild hamstring strain and continues to be considered day-to-day. For now, a questionable tag is being anticipated ahead of Toronto's playoff game against Cleveland on April 18.

items.headline: Quickley (hamstring) is considered day-to-day, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Quickley wasn't able to return to Sunday's game against the Nets due to right hamstring tightness, but an MRI revealed a mild strain. The Raptors are off until April 18 against the Cavaliers, and for the time being, he can be considered questionable for that contest.

items.headline: Quickley won't return to Sunday's game against the Nets due to right hamstring tightness, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports. He'll finish with four points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt), five assists, two rebounds and two steals across 17 minutes.
items.story: Quickley checked out of Toronto's regular-season finale late in the second quarter and won't return during the second half. Jamal Shead started the second half and should help pick up the slack the rest of the way.

items.headline: Quickley (rest) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game versus the Nets, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Quickley is set to return from a one-game absence Sunday, which should result in Jamal Shead heading back to the second unit. There will also be fewer minutes available for A.J. Lawson with Quickley active.

items.headline: Quickley won't play in Friday's game against the Knicks due to right foot injury management, Steve Popper of Newsday reports.
items.story: After missing eight consecutive contests while recovering from plantar fasciitis, Quickley has appeared in two straight games, including a 23-minute outing during Thursday's win over Miami. However, as expected, he'll take a seat for the second half of Toronto's back-to-back set for maintenance purposes. In Quickley's absence, Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter will be candidates to take on increased roles out of the backcourt.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) closed with three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt), four rebounds, four assists and two steals in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 121-95 win over the Heat.
items.story: Tuesday's game was Quickley's first appearance since March 22, with the sixth-year guard returning from an eight-game absence due to right foot plantar fasciitis. He ended up seeing less playing time than Jamal Shead (24 minutes), but that may have been more due to the Raptors' dominant lead through three quarters, resulting in the starters resting for the fourth frame. Quickley may have his minutes limited over the final few games of the regular season as the Raptors gear up for a postseason run.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) has been upgraded to available for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Quickley is ready to return from an eight-game absence due to plantar fasciitis in his right foot, which means fewer minutes will be free at point guard for Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter. However, Quickley could face a slight minutes restriction in his return to the floor Tuesday.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) has been upgraded to probable for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Quickley is trending toward suiting up Tuesday following an eight-game absence due to right foot plantar fasciitis. If the 26-year-old point guard is cleared to play, there would be fewer minutes available for the likes of Jamal Shead, Ja'Kobe Walter and A.J. Lawson.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Quickley has a chance to end an eight-game absence due to plantar fasciitis. His return would result in lesser roles at point guard for Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter on Tuesday.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) had his first workout without a boot Wednesday but remains without a timetable for a return to game action, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Quickley will miss a sixth straight game Wednesday due to right foot plantar fasciitis, though he's progressing in his recovery. The 26-year-old point guard can be considered doubtful for Friday's game in Memphis. With Quickley sidelined, Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter are candidates for increased roles, while A.J. Lawson could remain in the rotation.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Kings, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Quickley will be sidelined for a sixth straight contest, and it's unclear when he'll be able to return. His next chance to play comes Friday against the Grizzlies. In Quickley's absence, Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter should continue to see increased run.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game versus Detroit.
items.story: Quickley continues to battle right foot plantar fasciitis for a fifth straight contest, and he has a quick turnaround on tap for Wednesday against the Kings. Jamal Shead, who has averaged 11.7 points, 8.1 assists, 2.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals per contest in 10 games as a starter this season, should continue to ride with the first unit Tuesday.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Quickley will miss a fourth straight outing due to plantar fasciitis in his right foot, which means Jamal Shead will likely remain in the starting lineup. Quickley's next chance to play will come Tuesday at Detroit.

items.headline: Quickley won't play in Friday's game against the Pelicans, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Right foot plantar fasciitis is keeping the 2020 first-rounder out for a third consecutive contest. With Quickley sidelined, Jamal Shead has started two straight contests and should remain the top point guard for the Raptors on Friday.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) won't play Wednesday versus the Clippers, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: This will be Quickley's second straight game on the sidelines, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Pelicans. Jamal Shead should be looking at another start with Quickley unavailable, so he's on the radar as a potential deep-league streamer for managers seeking a boost in assists.

items.headline: Quickley is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: The 2020 first-rounder is expected to miss a second consecutive contest due to right foot plantar fasciitis. In Quickley's likely absence, Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter should both see additional ball-handling responsibilities in the backcourt Wednesday.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Quickley is dealing with right foot plantar fasciitis, which could cost him a second straight contest. With Brandon Ingram (heel) also questionable for Wednesday, the Raptors could need Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter to handle additional playmaking duties in the backcourt.

items.headline: Quickley (foot) is out for Monday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Monday's game is the second leg of a back-to-back set, so this absence may be maintenance-related. During Sunday's loss to the Suns, he finished with 11 points, three rebounds, one assist and two steals in 26 minutes. Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter could see increased reps with Quickley on the shelf.

items.headline: Quickley ended with 15 points (6-11 FG, 3-7 3Pt), four rebounds, eight assists and three steals in 34 minutes during Friday's 121-115 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Quickley got it done on both ends of the floor, although he remained somewhat passive on the offensive end. Although he has recorded eight steals in his past three games. Quickley's scoring has been less than ideal, averaging just 10.3 points per game during that time. With that said, he remains a top-50 player this season, providing a solid return on investment given he was typically available in the sixth or seventh rounds of fantasy drafts.

items.headline: Quickley chipped in 25 points (8-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds, three assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Wednesday's 122-111 loss to New Orleans.
items.story: The Raptors dropped to 36-29 despite a strong showing from Quickley. He's in the midst of a solid stretch for Toronto, posting averages of 17.5 points, 7.8 assists, 3.3 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 2.2 three-pointers on 46.1 percent shooting over his last six games.

items.headline: Quickley posted 12 points (3-9 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, six assists and one steal in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 113-99 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Quickley handed out at least six assists Tuesday in his fifth straight game. The star guard is on a roll as a playmaker, averaging 16.0 points, 8.8 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 2.0 three-pointers in 32.9 minutes per tilt in his last five games.

items.headline: Quickley registered 18 points (6-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), seven assists, three rebounds and one steal over 30 minutes during Toronto's 115-107 loss to Minnesota on Thursday.
items.story: Quickley went scoreless in the first quarter but was far more effective in the second half with 14 points (including nine in the third frame) to finish as the Raptors' second-leading scorer behind RJ Barrett (25 points). Quickley has been productive in the seven games since the All-Star break, having averaged 20.1 points, 6.6 assists, 2.9 rebounds, 2.7 threes and 1.0 steals over 33.4 minutes per game in that span.

items.headline: Quickley logged 13 points (4-14 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, 12 assists and two steals in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 111-95 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Quickley was a bright spot for the Raptors as the team dropped to 35-26 on the season. Toronto's starting point guard is in the midst of a hot stretch with averages of 20.5 points, 6.5 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 2.8 three-pointers over his last six games.

items.headline: Quickley had 27 points (10-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), two rebounds and 11 assists in 37 minutes during Saturday's 134-125 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: Quickley recorded just his sixth double-double of the season, taking full advantage of what was certainly a favorable matchup. He has now scored at least 20 points in three of his past four games, averaging 24.0 points, 6.0 assists and 3.5 three-pointers during that span. With Toronto looking to win as many games as possible down the stretch, Quickley should be able to flirt with top-50 value moving forward.

items.headline: Quickley closed Sunday's 122-94 win over Milwaukee with 32 points (11-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, nine assists and one steal in 31 minutes.
items.story: The 32 points led all scorers on the afternoon and represented Quickley's best offensive effort since he erupted for 40 points against the Warriors on Jan. 20. The 26-year-old guard has scored in double digits in all seven February games so far, averaging 20.1 points, 5.7 assists, 3.4 threes, 3.3 boards and 1.4 steals.

items.headline: Brooklyn recalled Powell from the G League's Long Island Nets on Friday.
items.story: Assuming he stays with the club for the day, Powell will be available to face the Pistons on Friday. He will remain an emergency depth option for the club going forward.

items.headline: The Nets exercised Powell's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
items.story: Powell remains part of Brooklyn's long-term plans as the organization continues developing its young talent. The second-year wing will have additional time to establish himself at the NBA level, though the contract decision doesn't guarantee a larger rotation role. His fantasy value remains limited without consistent playing time.

items.headline: The Nets assigned Powell to the G League's Long Island Nets on Monday.
items.story: Powell will continue his development with Long Island after struggling to carve out a consistent role in Brooklyn's rotation. The second-year wing could return to the NBA roster as needed, but he isn't currently positioned to provide meaningful fantasy production.

items.headline: Powell (coach's decision) did not play in Wednesday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: The second-year wing was excluded from Brooklyn's rotation to begin the campaign. Powell faces competition for perimeter minutes and will need to capitalize on future opportunities to establish a larger role.

items.headline: Powell finished with nine points (4-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 13 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason win over the Hornets.
items.story: Powell didn't commit a turnover and made the most of his limited opportunities, connecting on four of his six attempts from the field. The young wing will look to use the preseason to strengthen his case for a spot in Brooklyn's rotation after a tough 2025-26 campaign.

items.headline: Powell (rest) is looking to improve this season following a poor rookie campaign in 2025-26.
items.story: Powell struggled to make an impression on either end of the floor during his rookie year, averaging 6.5 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.6 steals per game while shooting just 40.2 percent from the floor over 63 regular-season appearances (24 starts) in 2025-26. While it appears unlikely he'll start the new year in the first unit, Powell should at least have a leg up on veterans Keon Ellis and Terance Mann for Brooklyn's backup role at shooting guard before training camp kicks off in September.

items.headline: Powell (rest) won't play in Sunday's Summer League game against the Thunder, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Powell will sit out the Nets' Summer League finale. The 2025 first-rounder struggled mightily with efficiency over four Las Vegas Summer League appearances, averaging 7.2 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.2 steals and 1.0 assists while shooting 25.9 percent from the field in 22.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Powell finished with 18 points (6-10 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, two steals and one block across 21 minutes in Tuesday's 115-83 Summer League win over the Kings.
items.story: Powell combined for just five points in his first two Las Vegas Summer League appearances. However, he turned it around Tuesday to finish second on the team in scoring behind Egor Demin, who ended with 22 points. Powell, the 2025 No. 22 overall pick, had a few quality performances in his 63 regular-season appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, though he was unproductive more often than not. While the 20-year-old is still adjusting to life at the NBA level, he will be expected to play better in 2026-27.

items.headline: Powell will be available for Monday's California Classic Summer League game against the Warriors Blue, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Powell skipped Sunday's win over the Bucks, but he'll be back in action for Monday's exhibition. John Ukomadu will likely return to the second unit with Powell active.

items.headline: Powell (undisclosed) won't play in Sunday's California Classic Summer League game against the Bucks, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: It's unclear exactly why Powell won't play Sunday, though the Nets have three games in as many days, so he may just be receiving a rest day. His next opportunity to play will come Monday against Warriors Blue.

items.headline: Powell finished with four points (0-9 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and one steal over 24 minutes in Saturday's 79-76 California Classic Summer League loss to the Kings.
items.story: Powell couldn't get anything going to begin the California version of Summer League. He went 0-for-9 from the field (0-for-5 from three-point range) while committing three turnovers. The 2025 No. 22 overall pick averaged 6.5 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.6 steals across 21.0 minutes in 63 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. Although his first year wasn't the worst, he has more work to do in order to carve out a routine spot in the rotation heading into the 2026-27 campaign. His odds of accomplishing that won't improve unless he turns it around this summer.

items.headline: Powell registered eight points (3-10 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one steal in 25 minutes during Sunday's 136-101 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: The rookie first-round pick had a mild effort to close out the regular season. Powell was used sparingly by the Nets, as he appeared in 63 games with averages of 6.5 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.8 three-pointers in 20.9 minutes. He was never close to being a consistent fantasy producer.

items.headline: Powell will start in Sunday's game against Toronto, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Powell didn't play in Friday's 125-108 loss to Milwaukee. However, he will return to  the starting lineup for the final game of the 2025-26 campaign. In 23 starts this season, the rookie has averaged 8.0 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 0.2 blocks and 0.7 steals across 25.3 minutes.

items.headline: Powell (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game in Toronto, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Powell is set to return from a one-game absence, and he could approximate the 40-minute threshold if Nolan Traore (illness) can't give it a go. Powell holds per-36 averages of 11.1 points, 2.5 assists, 1.4 triples and 1.0 steals per game.

items.headline: Powell is listed outfor Friday's game against the Bucks due to left knee injury management.
items.story: Powell will be in line for his first absence since March 23. With Powell among the 10 players the Nets have ruled out for Friday, extended minutes should be available for players like Trevon Scott, Malachi Smith and Tyson Etienne, among others.

items.headline: Powell won't start Thursday's game against the Pacers, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Tyson Etienne will step into the starting five in the front end of this back-to-back, pushing Powell to the second unit. The rookie first-rounder has averaged 3.8 points and 1.6 rebounds in 18.4 minutes per contest over his last five appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Powell finished with 11 points (4-16 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 40 minutes during Tuesday's 96-90 victory over the Bucks.
items.story: Powell had a woeful shooting performance, making just 25 percent of his attempts, and while his fantasy line was far from eye-popping, he managed to contribute in each of the five major categories. Powell has started every game he's been available for the Nets since March 9. However, his averages of 8.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game aren't particularly impressive, especially since he's also shooting 38.4 percent from the floor in that span.

items.headline: Powell finished with six points (2-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 29 minutes during Friday's 141-107 loss to Atlanta.
items.story: Powell played at least 28 minutes for the third straight game, seemingly earning himself a spot in the opening five. He has started 12 straight appearances, although during that stretch he has barely been a top-300 player. With averages of just 7.8 points and 1.3 three-pointers, fantasy managers are better off shifting their attention elsewhere.

items.headline: Powell logged 16 points (6-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 116-99 win over the Kings.
items.story: Powell and Nolan Traore combined for 33 points as the Nets improved to 18-57 on the season. Although this was a step in the right direction, Powell remains difficult to trust with averages of 6.9 points, 1.6 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 three-pointers in 24.5 minutes over his last seven games.

items.headline: Powell (knee) isn't listed on the team's injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against Golden State, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Powell took a seat for the second leg of Brooklyn's back-to-back Monday in Portland, but he'll be back in action for Wednesday's clash. He's made seven consecutive starts for the Nets and is averaging 6.4 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.4 assists over that stretch.

items.headline: Powell won't play in Monday's game versus Portland due to left knee injury management, per C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set, and the expectation is that he'll return for Wednesday's tilt against the Warriors. Powell's absence frees up a spot in the starting lineup Monday, with Ochai Agbaji, Malachi Smith and Jalen Wilson being candidates to join the first unit.

items.headline: Powell is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against Portland, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Powell is set to return from a one-game absence due to left knee injury management and will jump back into the starting five. The rookie had started the previous three games before being inactive Sunday and has made 12 starts this season, averaging 7.9 points, 1.7 assists and 1.4 rebounds in 23.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Powell (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Powell got the night off Saturday as he manages a left knee injury, but he will return to action Monday. Over his last three appearances, Powell has averaged 10.0 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 27.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Powell has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the 76ers due to left knee injury management, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Powell is getting hit with a rest day, and his minutes will be divvied up amongst Terance Mann, Nolan Traore and Ochai Agbaji. Powell should be back for Monday's matchup with the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Powell registered 10 points (3-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one rebound over 23 minutes during Tuesday's 138-100 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Powell reached double-digit points for the first time since Feb. 9. However, he's been mostly a bench option for a struggling Nets team, and his overall production hasn't stood out even when he's received more minutes. Thus, his fantasy upside should remain fairly low until further notice, even though he's drawn two straight starts.

items.headline: Powell is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against Memphis.
items.story: Powell, who hasn't seen NBA action since Feb. 26, will slide into the starting lineup for Monday's home contest. The rookie has made seven starts this season, averaging 8.4 points, 2.0 assists and 1.6 rebounds across 24.7 minutes per contest in that role, with his most recent start coming Jan. 25.

items.headline: Powell was recalled from the G League on Sunday, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Powell will be available for Monday's matchup with Memphis. The rookie is averaging 6.0 points and 1.5 assists per game this season.

items.headline: Brooklyn assigned Powell to the G League's Long Island Nets on Friday, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Long Island doesn't play its next game until Sunday, so Powell may just be sticking around in the G League to practice over the next couple of days. With Brooklyn playing a road game in Boston later Friday, Powell looks as though he won't be available for that contest. The Nets recalled Ben Saraf from the G League and could have him step into the rotation in place of Powell, who had appeared in each of the team's last 18 games and averaged 5.5 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 19.5 minutes per contest over that stretch.

items.headline: Powell ended Monday's 123-115 win over the Bulls with 14 points (4-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and five rebounds over 23 minutes.
items.story: This was one of Powell's best performances of the season, as he was able to take advantage of some maintenance days for Michael Porter and Egor Demin. While not a fantasy pickup yet, Powell may be worth keeping an eye on in deeper formats, with player development expected to be a focus for Brooklyn down the stretch.

items.headline: Powell logged 12 points (3-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds and one assist over 32 minutes during Sunday's 130-77 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Powell turned in one of his better scoring outings of the season in Brooklyn's lopsided loss to the Pistons. The first-round pick scored roughly twice his season average. He led his team in minutes played off the bench with Michael Porter sidelined for personal reasons. As the rest of the season plays out, it's worth monitoring if Powell can pick up his production on a consistent basis.

items.headline: Powell is not in the Nets' starting lineup against the Nuggets on Thursday, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.

The Nets will roll with a starting lineup of Nolan Traore, Terance Mann, Michael Porter, Danny Wolf and Nic Claxton for Thursday's contest.

items.headline: Powell had no counting stats over eight minutes during Tuesday's 106-102 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Ziaire Williams and Cam Thomas ended up playing the lion's share of the minutes at shooting guard Tuesday. Powell appears to have a tenuous hold on the starting role that he's had for the past eight games, during which the rookie first-rounder has averaged 7.1 points, 1.8 assists and 1.5 rebounds in 22.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Powell had 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound and three assists across 25 minutes during Monday's 126-117 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Powell started for a fourth straight appearance, ending with another serviceable line. Brooklyn has so many young pieces to choose from at the moment, knowing who is going to step up on any given night is anyone's guess. Even as a starter, Powell has fallen well short of the mark when it comes to standard league value, averaging just 10.0 points and 2.0 three-pointers in 24.5 minutes per tilt over the past three games.

items.headline: Powell (knee) is off the injury report for Monday's game against the Suns.

items.headline: Powell won't play in Sunday's game against Chicago due to left knee injury management, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports.
items.story: Powell was held to three points in 24 minutes Friday against the Bulls, and he'll now take a seat for Brooklyn's upcoming clash. He figures to have a decent chance to play Monday against Phoenix.

items.headline: Powell notched 16 points (6-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds and two assists in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 116-113 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Making his third career start, Powell scored a season-high 16 points Wednesday. The rookie first-rounder has averaged 7.9 points, 1.6 rebounds and 0.9 assists in 21.0 minutes per contest through seven games this month, so Powell appears to still have some work to do before commanding more fantasy attention.

items.headline: Powell will start against Dallas on Monday.

items.headline: Powell (knee) will be available for Monday's game against Dallas.

items.headline: Powell is not in the Nets' starting lineup against the Wizards on Friday.
items.story: Powell made his first NBA start against the Rockets on Thursday and finished with eight points, one assist, one steal and two turnovers over 25 minutes. The rookie first-rounder will revert to the bench Friday while Terance Mann and Egor Demin return to the starting lineup.

While Powell is out, there should be more minutes available for Jalen Wilson.

items.story: Powell seemed to tweak the same right ankle that has given him so much trouble this season, and he was sporting a serious limp as he was helped back to the locker room. For now, Powell should be considered questionable to return.

items.story: Jackson-Davis will start to close out the preseason. The 26-year-old most recently appeared in Tuesday's 148-98 preseason victory over New York, amassing nine points, three rebounds, one steal and two blocks over nine minutes of action.

items.story: With Sandro Mamukelashvili hitting free agency, Jackson-Davis could be in the mix for some backup center minutes going forward. During the 2025-26 regular season, he made 17 appearances with Toronto and averaged 3.4 points and 2.7 rebounds in 9.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Jackson-Davis did not see the floor during Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: Jackson-Davis' third NBA season was mostly a letdown throughout 2025-26. The big man got lost in the shuffle with Golden State before being traded to Toronto, where he averaged only 1.8 points, 1.9 rebounds and 0.4 assists in 5.0 minutes per tilt over 17 regular-season contests. With Sandro Mamukelashvili a potential departure this offseason, the Raptors could exercise Jackson-Davis' team option for 2026-27 to fortify their center depth.

items.story: Jackson-Davis will be available to return from a two-game absence due to an illness. However, he isn't guaranteed to see meaningful run while buried behind Jakob Poeltl, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Murray-Boyles.

items.story: Jackson-Davis is not a usual rotation player for Toronto, so his absence doesn't carry many fantasy implications. He's made 13 appearances since the All-Star break, playing double-digit minutes only once.

The third-year big man received some extended run Tuesday with the 905 in a 120-105 loss to the Motor City Cruise in the first round of the G League playoffs, playing 28 minutes and finishing with 18 points (5-10 FG, 4-5 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, three steals and three blocks.

items.headline: Jackson-Davis (knee) is available for Sunday's game versus the Magic, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.

However, he hasn't seen consistent minutes off the bench for the Raptors since being acquired by the team from the Warriors in early February. Jackson-Davis won't be a prominent member of Toronto's rotation for as long as Collin Murray-Boyles (back), Jakob Poeltl and Sandro Mamukelashvili are available.

He's unlikely to start seeing consistent minutes unless Jakob Poeltl or Sandro Mamukelashvili were to miss time along with Murray-Boyles.

items.headline: Jackson-Davis logged 10 points (2-4 FG, 6-10 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 16 minutes during the Raptors' 122-104 win over the Pacers on Sunday.
items.story: Jackson-Davis was cleared to make his Raptors four days after being acquired from the Warriors, and he saw meaningful minutes off the bench in the absence of Jakob Poeltl (back). Jackson-Davis gave the Pacers fits on the boards, logging a season-high eight offensive rebounds, which led to him attempting 10 free throws for the first time this season. With Collin Murray-Boyles and Sandro Mamukelashvili also on the roster, it's unclear what kind of playing time Jackson-Davis will see once Poeltl is cleared to return.

items.headline: Jackson-Davis (recently traded) is available for Sunday's game against the Pacers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Jackson-Davis was acquired by the Raptors from the Warriors on Wednesday in exchange for a second-round pick, and the third-year center is ready to make his debut with his new team Sunday. It'll be interesting to see what Jackson-Davis' role with the Raptors will be, especially with Jakob Poeltl (back) nearing a return from an extended absence, during which Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Murray-Boyles both took on expanded roles.
