items.story: Lively managed just 10 minutes in the loss, limited by early foul trouble. Matched up against Victor Wembanyama was never going to end well, something that could probably be said for a number of centers across the league. While this was a terrible night for Lively, managers should stick to their guns and hope for an improved performance against the Wizards on Friday.

items.headline: Dunn finished Sunday's 124-112 loss to the Warriors with 12 points (5-8 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four assists, two rebounds and seven steals over 27 minutes.
items.story: It was only the second time through six regular-season games that Dunn scored in double digits. However, the veteran guard once again made more of an impact defensively and set a new career high in steals, one more than his previous best that he set Feb. 20, 2025, against the Bucks. Dunn is averaging 8.5 points, 5.3 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 3.0 steals over 29.7 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Dunn tallied 15 points (6-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists, five steals, two blocks and two turnovers across 33 minutes in Sunday's 108-101 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Dunn cracked double digits in scoring for the first time this season, and he did so with remarkable efficiency, missing just two shots in 33 minutes of floor time. The scoring will come and go with Dunn, but as long as he's starting in Los Angeles, he should do enough with the assists and defensive stats to warrant a roster spot in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Dunn logged seven points (2-5 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and three steals over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 121-96 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Getting the start in the backcourt due to Bradley Beal (knee) being on the shelf, Dunn mainly left the scoring to Darius Garland while the former led the Clippers in assists and made a strong impact on defense. Dunn started 68 of 82 regular-season games last season and averaged a modest 7.3 points, 3.6 assists, 3.3 boards, 1.6 steals and 1.0 threes in 27.2 minutes, and his role doesn't seem likely to change much once the backcourt gets healthier.

The defensive-minded Dunn was essentially a full-time starter last regular season, making 68 starts over 82 games, so his status as the incumbent veteran could also work in his favor if Wagler struggles in Summer League or at camp.

items.headline: Dunn contributed seven points (3-5 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds, 10 assists and three steals across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game loss to the Warriors.

items.headline: Dunn will come off the bench for Wednesday's game in New Orleans, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Kawhi Leonard (ankle) is back and starting, so Dunn will shift to the second unit. As a reserve this season, Dunn owns averages of 7.3 points and 1.7 steals per game.

items.headline: Dunn contributed five points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt), seven rebounds, three assists and three steals in 29 minutes during Monday's 126-118 win over New York.
items.story: This was a modest line for Dunn, but his offense usually comes and goes. Overall this season, Dunn ranks just outside the top-150 players in nine-category formats with 7.8 points, 3.6 assists, 3.3 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 1.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Dunn totaled 16 points (7-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt), seven rebounds, seven assists and two steals across 26 minutes during Monday's 114-101 victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Dunn's time as a viable fantasy contributor may be running out soon, as Darius Garland returned to action and will be the starter at point guard once he reaches 100 percent. Fantasy managers who depend on Dunn's production will need to pivot quickly, as productive nights from Dunn could be limited to upcoming back-to-backs if Garland rests.

items.headline: Dunn (head) is off the injury report for Monday's game against the Warriors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn departed Sunday's game against the Pelicans due to an apparent head injury and did not return, but he's good to go Monday. The veteran guard has tallied at least one steal and four assists in six of his last seven outings and remains a strong streaming option for swipes and dimes.

items.headline: Dunn left Sunday's game against the Pelicans due to an apparent head injury and did not return.
items.story: Dunn exited the game for the locker room in the fourth quarter after appearing to get hit in the head by an inadvertent elbow, and he did not return. It should be noted that the game was all but over when Dunn exited and head coach Tyronn Lue stated postgame that Dunn was "good" following the injury, so it does not appear to be a concern going forward.

items.headline: Dunn went back to the locker room during Sunday's game against the Pelicans due to an apparent head injury, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn appeared to get hit with an inadvertent elbow from Pelicans player Karlo Matkovic before heading back to the locker room, grabbing at his head and neck area. Considering the injury occurred in the latter portion of a lopsided contest, it would be surprising if Dunn returns to the game, leaving extra minutes for Bennedict Mathurin.

items.headline: Dunn chipped in seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), five rebounds and two steals across 34 minutes during Sunday's 111-109 loss to the Magic.
items.story: Dunn remains a steady source of swipes without a whole lot else to be excited about in the box score. Over his last 12 appearances, the veteran guard has averaged 8.2 points, 5.2 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 29.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dunn had 16 points (6-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds, six assists and one steal over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 105-102 win over the Rockets.
items.story: The 16 points were Dunn's third-highest total on the year. The veteran guard has averaged 8.3 points, 4.6 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 27.3 minutes per contest in his last 10 games, so Dunn remains a decent fantasy streamer for dimes and swipes.

items.headline: Dunn was ejected from Sunday's game against the Timberwolves, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Dunn has been ejected from Sunday's game after getting into a scuffle with Julius Randle. He concludes the contest with nine points (3-6 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six assists, five rebounds and a steal in 28 minutes.

items.headline: Dunn had six points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds and six assists across 27 minutes during Monday's 128-113 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: The absence of James Harden (personal) didn't translate into a noticeable boost in usage for Dunn on Monday. Dunn remains strictly a fantasy streamer for swipes, averaging 6.1 points, 3.6 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 26.0 minutes per tilt in his last seven games.

items.headline: Dunn closed Tuesday's 115-103 win over the Jazz with 14 points (6-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and five steals in 31 minutes.
items.story: Dunn was very effective on defense, padding his fantasy totals with five steals. He also produced 14 points, marking his 15th game with 10 or more points. While his scoring average (7.9 points per game) is still low, decent secondary numbers will often offset a cold shooting night.

items.headline: Dunn (ankle) will play in Tuesday's game against the Jazz, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: The veteran guard left Sunday's 126-89 win over the Nets with a right ankle injury, but he's good to go Tuesday. Dunn has averaged 5.7 points, 3.2 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 27.7 minutes per contest in his last 10 games.

items.headline: Dunn (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Jazz, Janis Carr of the Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Dunn departed Sunday's game against the Nets after picking up a right ankle injury, and he's now in jeopardy of missing Tuesday's matchup. Jordan Miller and Cam Christie would be in line for more minutes if Dunn is ultimately unable to go.

items.headline: Dunn (ankle) didn't return to Sunday's 126-89 win over the Nets after exiting with 2:25 remaining in the second quarter. He finished the game with two points (1-3 FG), three rebounds and one steal in 13 minutes.
items.story: Dunn checked out of the game after he appeared to tweak his right ankle, and though the Clippers never officially ruled him out for the game, he remained on the bench for the entire second half while Kobe Sanders opened the third quarter with the starters. The Clippers took a 31-point lead into halftime, which may have played a part in the decision to hold Dunn out for the rest of the contest. The team should provide an update on Dunn's status when it releases its next injury report prior to Tuesday's game in Utah.

items.headline: Dunn (leg) left Sunday's game against the Nets for the locker room, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn appeared to roll his right ankle before going back to the locker room in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. If he is unable to return, Kobe Sanders figures to see extra minutes.

items.headline: Dunn posted 15 points (4-6 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds, four assists and four steals over 33 minutes during Friday's 121-117 overtime victory over the Raptors.
items.story: Dunn was a strong all-around presence in Friday's win, hitting key threes while also making his impact felt as a facilitator and on the defensive end. While his scoring can fluctuate, the veteran guard's ability to generate turnovers stands out, as he's recorded at least one steal in 33 of 41 games this season and has logged three or more in three of the past four contests.

items.headline: Dunn closed with zero points (0-6 FG, 0-6 3Pt) and two rebounds over 21 minutes during Monday's 117-109 victory over Charlotte.
items.story: Dunn missed all six of his shot attempts, continuing an awful run of production since the beginning of the year. Over the past seven games, Dunn has averaged only 6.6 points, 3.7 assists and 2.4 rebounds, and he logged a double-digit point total only once over that span. Dunn's subpar play may give way to Jordan Miller in the short term, and the eventual return of Bogdan Bogdanovic (hamstring) could give the starting lineup an upgrade.

items.headline: Dunn recorded seven points (2-9 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds and one assist across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 123-111 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Dunn was unable to follow up his strong performance against the Warriors on Monday, shooting poorly from the field and recording no defensive stats for just the fourth time this season. While Dunn has not been consistent in his shot efficiency, he is averaging 8.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.4 steals, 0.2 blocks and 1.2 threes across 28.0 minutes in 30 starts and continues to be an integral part of the Clippers' first unit.

items.headline: Dunn provided 16 points (5-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, six assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Monday's 103-102 win over the Warriors.
items.story: Dunn rarely shows out like this offensively, so this was a nice surprise for his fantasy managers. He continues to be a solid source of assists, defensive stats and three-pointers, posting averages of 8.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.6 three-pointers in 28.3 minutes over his last seven outings.

items.headline: Dunn provided five points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound, three assists, one block and two steals in 30 minutes during Sunday's 112-99 win over the Pistons.
items.story: Dunn's fantasy appeal remains almost entirely tied to his ability to rack up steals. The defensive-minded guard has averaged 8.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.8 steals in 28.6 minutes per contest through his last 13 games.

items.headline: Dunn supplied 17 points (6-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and five assists over 27 minutes during Monday's 121-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Dunn logged a double-digit scoring total for the first time in two weeks. He suffered through an abysmal four-game drought, during which he averaged only 6.3 points per game. Unfortunately, production gaps have been common for Dunn, who manages to hold onto a starting role due to his defensive skill set.

items.headline: Dunn closed Thursday's 115-113 loss to the Rockets with nine points (3-7 FG, 3-7 3Pt), one rebound, six assists and two steals over 26 minutes.
items.story: Dunn has been a full-time starter since the Nov. 7 loss to the Thunder, but his impact as a defender remains far more felt in real life than in fantasy. That said, the door is still open for the veteran guard to offer deep-league streaming appeal for swipes as long as Derrick Jones (knee) is sidelined. Over his last eight games, Dunn has averaged 9.1 points, 3.3 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 2.3 steals in 27.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Dunn posted zero points (0-1 FG), three rebounds, three assists and two steals across 21 minutes during Friday's 107-98 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: The veteran guard continues to see his role and minutes shrink as the struggling Clippers search for answers. While Dunn did make his 17th straight start as he helps to fill in for the absence of Bradley Beal (hip), he failed to see 30 minutes for a third straight game, and he's failed to score in double digits 13 times during those 17 contests -- although Friday's goose egg on just one shot attempt represented his worst production yet in 2025-26. Younger players like 2025 second-round pick Kobe Sanders and 2024 second-round pick Cam Christie could muscle Dunn out of the starting five at some point if coach Tyronn Lue decides his lineup needs a spark.

items.headline: Dunn notched 12 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal across 26 minutes during Monday's 140-123 loss to Miami.
items.story: The Clippers are a mess right now, but Dunn continues to start in the backcourt and remains a viable asset in deeper fantasy formats. Across 21 regular-season appearances, Dunn holds averages of 8.0 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.6 steals and 0.9 three-pointers in 26.4 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dunn was assessed two technical fouls and ejected in the fourth quarter of Tuesday's game against the Lakers, independent NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dunn got into an altercation with multiple Lakers players and was sent to the locker room early. He'll finish with 19 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three assists and one steal across 30 minutes. Despite leaving early, the 31-year-old posted a season-high mark in points after scoring in single digits in each of the Clippers' last seven games.

items.headline: Dunn totaled nine points (3-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal over 24 minutes during Sunday's 120-105 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Dunn has not been very productive on the offensive end, averaging just 6.9 points over 26.8 minutes in 11 starts, but he has been a reliable defensive anchor on the perimeter, averaging 1.3 steals and 0.4 blocks in that span. Dunn will likely remain in the starting lineup indefinitely since Bradley Beal (hip) will not return this season.

items.headline: Carr posted no counting stats in one minute during Sunday's 131-125 victory over the Raptors.
items.story: The rookie missed Los Angeles' first six games due to an oblique injury before making a brief appearance Sunday. His return to the floor is a positive development, though Carr remains outside the regular rotation and carries little immediate fantasy value.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the Raptors, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Carr, the No. 24 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, has been cleared to make his regular-season debut Sunday following his recovery from a right oblique strain that he picked up during the preseason. It's not clear what his role in the rotation will look like, but he could see most of his minutes in the G League.

items.headline: The Lakers assigned Carr (oblique) to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Friday, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: The rookie has yet to debut at the NBA level. He remains miles off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Carr has yet to make his NBA debut while tending to a right oblique strain. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Sunday against Toronto.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: The rookie first-rounder will need more time to recover from the oblique injury that's kept him sidelined for what will be his fifth consecutive contest. Carr's next chance to suit up will come against the Warriors on Friday in the first Emirates NBA Cup matchup, and while it's unclear if he'll be ready for that game, he has been ramping up his activity with practices in the G League.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) was assigned Wednesday to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
items.story: With the Lakers unlikely to have much practice time over their current back-to-back set, this assignment gives Carr a chance to continue his recovery work from an oblique injury. The rookie guard was recalled Tuesday and could be brought back to the parent club at some point soon.

items.headline: The Lakers recalled Carr (oblique) from the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Tuesday, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports.
items.story: According to Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times, Carr logged a full practice with the G League Lakers on Tuesday. He's working his way back from an oblique strain, and the rookie's next chance to play for the parent club will come Wednesday against the Clippers in the second leg of the Lakers' back-to-back set.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) was assigned to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Monday, Trevor Lane of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Carr is presumably getting some work in with LA's G League affiliate as he continues to battle his way back from an oblique strain. He's been ruled out for the Lakers' matchup against Portland on Tuesday but could have a chance to make his NBA debut Wednesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Carr will miss a fourth consecutive regular-season contest due to an oblique strain. The rookie's next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is out for Sunday's game in Utah, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: This will be Carr's third straight game on the inactive list. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Trail Blazers, the first game of a back-to-back set.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Carr isn't quite ready to make his NBA debut, but he can continue to be considered day-to-day. His next chance to take the court will arrive Sunday in Utah.

items.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said Carr (oblique), who is out for Wednesday's game against Golden State, is "ramping up" and can be considered day-to-day moving forward, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
items.story: Carr will miss the Lakers' regular-season opener, though he can be considered questionable for Friday's game against the Clippers until further notice. With the rookie sidelined, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams are candidates for a bump in minutes.

items.headline: Carr (oblique) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Carr has been dealing with an oblique injury. Considering the rookie hasn't been practicing, it appears his absence will extend beyond Opening Night. With Carr sidelined, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams are candidates for more playing time behind Quentin Grimes.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) didn't practice Tuesday, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
items.story: The rookie guard continues to nurse a contusion. His status remains in the dark for Wednesday's season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) didn't practice Monday, per Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times.
items.story: The rookie guard continues to tend to a contusion. His status is unknown for Wednesday's season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Friday's preseason game against Denver, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Carr will miss a third consecutive contest due to a contusion. His next chance to play will come in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) didn't practice Thursday, per Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times.
items.story: Carr continues to manage a minor contusion. His status is unknown for Friday's preseason finale versus Denver.

items.headline: Carr (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Tuesday's preseason matchup with the Warriors, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Carr remains day-to-day but will miss a second straight game due to an undisclosed injury. His final chance to play again in the preseason will come Friday against Denver.

items.headline: Carr won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Kings due to a contusion, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
items.story: Carr and several other players are reportedly dealing with minor injuries, per Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com, but the Lakers aren't concerned about him missing any regular-season action. His next chance to play will arrive Tuesday against the Warriors.

items.headline: Carr totaled 19 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and two steals in 23 minutes during Monday's 127-103 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Carr led the Lakers' reserves in scoring and continued to make a case for a rotation role after an impressive Summer League. Coach JJ Redick indicated during training camp that the rookie could earn opportunities this season, and Monday's performance was an encouraging first step.

items.headline: Carr could be part of the Lakers' rotation as a rookie, according to head coach JJ Redick, Ryan Ward of SI.com reports.
items.story: Redick indicated that Los Angeles plans to utilize a deeper rotation this season, which could create an opportunity for Carr to earn minutes. The rookie will still need to establish himself during training camp and the preseason, but he appears to have a path to a regular role. Keep an eye on him in deeper formats.

items.headline: Carr contributed 17 points (5-16 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 4-5 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 28 minutes in Saturday's 92-88 loss to the Warriors in the Las Vegas Summer League Semifinals.
items.story: Carr's and the Lakers' Summer League run came to an end Saturday, and the rookie first-rounder struggled mightily with efficiency. Still, he finished as Los Angeles' second-leading scorer, posting at least 14 points for the fourth time in as many Las Vegas Summer League outings. During that span, Carr averaged 18.0 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists per contest. He's in line to compete for meaningful playing time off the bench in his rookie season.

items.headline: Carr registered 14 points (5-12 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds and one steal in 22 minutes during Thursday's 105-82 Summer League win over the Bulls.
items.story: Carr put together a decent effort offensively, and while he couldn't get a shot to fall from beyond the arc, his production from the field helped the Lakers to a 4-0 Summer League record. The rookie has been putting together an impressive showing thus far in Summer League play, and assuming the Lakers don't shut him down, he'll have additional opportunities to get run over the weekend.

items.headline: Carr (thumb) tallied 23 points (8-18 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 3-5 FT), one rebound, two assists and one block over 29 minutes in Tuesday's 99-85 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Clippers.
items.story: Carr sat out Saturday's Summer League win over the Mavs with a minor thumb issue, but he returned Tuesday to pour in a game-high 23 points, suggesting the issue is behind him. The Lakers are 3-0 through their first three games in Las Vegas.

items.headline: Carr won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against Dallas due to a right thumb contusion, Khobi Price of The California Post reports.
items.story: Carr will be held out of Saturday's contest after scoring 18 points across 29 minutes in the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to suit up will come Tuesday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Carr finished with 18 points (7-13 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks across 29 minutes in Friday's 96-84 Summer League win over the Thunder.
items.story: After scoring just five points in Monday's 88-84 California Classic Summer League win over San Antonio, Carr turned it around Friday, finishing only two points behind Adou Thiero, who scored a game-high 20. The 21-year-old may not play in every game for the Lakers throughout the remainder of the team's time in Las Vegas. However, even if Carr suits up only a few more times, he is already in line for an expanded role heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Carr produced five points (2-7 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), one rebound, one assist, one steal and one block in 13 minutes of Monday's 88-84 Summer League win over the Spurs.
items.story: The Lakers relied heavily on their second unit in this contest, and Carr wasn't able to make much of an impact. He's been solid through three exhibitions, however, posting averages of 15.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 3.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: Carr logged 26 points (7-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-5 FT), eight rebounds and one assist in 31 minutes during Sunday's 93-91 double-overtime win over the Heat at the California Classic Summer League.
items.story: Carr did much of his work from beyond the arc again Sunday, knocking down a game-high four three-pointers en route to a game-high 26 points. The 24th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft has averaged 22.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 27.5 minutes per contest through two Summer League appearances. He figures to remain the Lakers' top option at Summer League for as long as he suits up.

items.headline: Carr finished with 19 points (7-15 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block over 24 minutes in Friday's 104-72 California Classic Summer League loss to Golden State.
items.story: Carr led the Lakers in scoring while tying Yaxel Lendeborg for a game-high 19 points. He also made five three-point shots, three more than the rest of the team combined. The 2026 No. 24 overall pick is coming off a sound 2025-26 campaign at Baylor, where he averaged 18.9 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.3 blocks and 0.9 steals on 49.4 percent shooting from the field and 37.4 percent shooting from deep across 33.7 minutes in 34 regular-season and postseason games. While Carr displayed flashes of promise in his Summer League debut, he faces an uphill battle for consistent playing time with the Lakers in 2026-27.

items.headline: The Knicks selected Carr with the No. 24 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and traded his rights to the Lakers, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After playing sparingly across two seasons with Tennessee, Carr broke out in his lone season at Baylor in 2025-26, averaging 18.9 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.3 blocks and 0.9 steals on 49.4 percent shooting from the field and 37.4 percent from deep in 33.7 minutes over 34 games, culminating in All-Big 12 Third Team honors. The Lakers' roster is far from set heading into the 2026-27 campaign, though LeBron James and Austin Reaves are expected to return, leaving Carr's path to consistent usage blocked.

items.headline: Payton accumulated five points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal over 15 minutes during Sunday's 124-112 victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Payton delivered his usual complementary production in a limited bench role, contributing a steal and a three-pointer without requiring much offensive involvement. His defensive activity can occasionally provide value in deeper leagues, but his modest minutes and scoring opportunities leave him with little appeal in standard formats.

items.headline: Payton ended Saturday's 131-122 loss to the Suns with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound in 17 minutes.
items.story: Payton logged double-digit minutes for a third straight game to open the regular season, though he didn't make much of an impact. The veteran guard is averaging 6.3 points and 1.3 rebounds in 15.3 minutes per tilt so far this season.

items.headline: Payton (rest) contributed zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal over 19 minutes in Saturday's 111-106 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Payton did not travel for Wednesday's exhibition in Portland, but he returned to the floor for Saturday's preseason game. With the offseason addition of Brandon Williams, Payton could have a tough time consistently getting into the rotation this season.

items.headline: Payton (rest) is out for Wednesday's preseason game against the Trail Blazers, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.story: Payton is among several rotation players Golden State is holding out Wednesday during a preseason back-to-back. The veteran guard remains in the mix for a reserve role after appearing in a career-high 73 games during the 2025-26 regular season.

items.headline: Payton finished with six points (3-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), two steals and one assist in 11 minutes during Sunday's 104-101 preseason loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Payton made his usual impact defensively in limited action, recording two steals without committing a turnover. The 33-year-old re-signed with Golden State on a one-year deal during the offseason and should remain a situational defensive option in a crowded Warriors backcourt.

items.headline: Payton agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Warriors on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Payton lingered on the open market, but he'll ultimately return to Golden State for his 11th NBA season. In 73 regular-season games last season, the 33-year-old averaged 7.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 15.6 minutes per contest. Payton isn't likely to see significant usage during the 2026-27 campaign but will provide valuable veteran depth in the Warriors' backcourt.

items.headline: Payton finished Friday's 111-96 Play-In Game loss to the Suns with four points (2-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three rebounds and three assists over 26 minutes.
items.story: Payton scored no more than six points for the third straight game, closing out what was an indifferent season. Although he was well outside the top 200, his efforts over the final month were far improved. In 14 games during that time, he averaged 10.9 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals, good enough for top-100 value.

items.headline: Payton was ejected in the fourth quarter of Friday's game against the Kings after being assessed his second technical foul, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area reports. He'll finish with 10 points (5-6 FG), three rebounds and one steal in 15 minutes.
items.story: Payton picked up his first technical foul in the third quarter and received another in the fourth. Although he played just 15 minutes, he scored in double figures for a fourth consecutive contest and for the 15th time over his last 16 appearances.

items.headline: Payton supplied eight points (4-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt), 12 rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals across 27 minutes during Thursday's 118-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: After missing Wednesday's game against the Spurs for injury maintenance, Payton responded with a terrific line Thursday. It's worth noting that Stephen Curry (knee) is targeting a return Sunday against Houston, so there's a chance Payton's workload decreases moving forward.

items.headline: Payton (knee) is available for Thursday's game against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Payton will be back in action after sitting out the front end of this back-to-back set for maintenance. With so many Warriors injured, Payton could see a sizable workload Thursday.

items.headline: Payton (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Payton will miss the front end of the Warriors' back-to-back set due to right knee injury management, but he should be available for Thursday's contest against the Cavaliers. Will Richard, Seth Curry and Nate Williams are all candidates to see a bump in minutes in Payton's absence.

items.headline: Payton is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to right knee injury management.
items.story: Payton could be held out of the front end of this back-to-back set, which would leave more minutes available for guys like Will Richard, Nate Williams and Seth Curry. Payton would likely see increased playing time if he's cleared to suit up due to De'Anthony Melton (thumb) being unavailable.

items.headline: Payton supplied 16 points (7-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds and one assist in 21 minutes during Sunday's 116-93 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: Payton has been a valuable role player for the Warriors over the last few seasons mainly due to his defensive versatility, but he's put himself on the fantasy radar of late thanks primarily to his increased production on the offensive end while Golden State has navigated numerous injuries. The 33-year-old has hit double figures in the scoring column in 11 straight games, averaging 14.3 points during that stretch while converting at an incredible 69 percent rate from the field. He's also chipping in 5.2 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.6 steals per game over that stretch.

items.headline: Payton finished with 17 points (8-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 0-1 FT), four rebounds, three assists and two steals in 21 minutes during Monday's 137-131 overtime win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Payton returned to play after resting one game for injury management and was perfect from the floor during the victory. The 10-year pro is averaging only 14.9 minutes per game, but he's seen a noticeable uptick to 22.3 minutes over his past 10 appearances. He's also averaged 13.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.9 steals over the span.

items.headline: Payton (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Payton did not play in the second leg of the Warriors' back-to-back set Saturday against the Hawks while managing a knee injury, but he will be back on the court for Monday's Western Conference tilt. The veteran guard has scored in double digits in each of his last seven outings, and over that span he has averaged 14.1 points on 61.8 percent shooting along with 5.1 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.0 steals over 23.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Payton (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: Payton will be sidelined Saturday for injury management purposes. His absence should leave more opportunities for Pat Spencer and Will Richard. Payton's next chance to play will come Monday at Dallas.

items.headline: Payton (knee) is questionable for Saturday's game against Atlanta.
items.story: Payton had 14 points in Friday's loss to Detroit. However, he's now in danger of missing Saturday's contest because of knee soreness. With De'Anthony Melton (knee) potentially taking the night off for injury management purposes, the Warriors may look to Pat Spencer and Will Richard to get more involved on both ends of the floor.

items.headline: Payton produced 14 points (7-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt), six rebounds, four assists and four steals over 21 minutes during Wednesday's 120-99 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Payton was a lone bright spot off the bench for the Warriors in Wednesday's blowout loss, and he finished with a new season high in steals. He's been shooting the lights out over the past five games, converting 63.3 percent of his shot attempts to go with averages of 14.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.4 steals per contest. Until the Warriors get the likes of Moses Moody (wrist) and Stephen Curry (knee) back in action, Payton should have a fairly clear path to a 20-plus-minute role in most games.

items.headline: Payton (lower leg) is available for Wednesday's game against the Celtics.
items.story: As expected, the swingman is shedding a probable designation with a left tibial contusion. Payton is handling a significant role recently, averaging 13.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.9 steals in 23.0 minutes per tilt over his last eight appearances.

items.headline: Payton is probable for Wednesday's game against the Celtics with a left tibial contusion.
items.story: The issue doesn't sound to be severe enough to stop Payton from playing Wednesday. The guard has moved into a more prominent role of late, averaging 13.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.9 steals in 23.0 minutes per contest over his last eight games.

items.headline: Payton closed Sunday's 110-107 loss to New York with 19 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt), six rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 28 minutes.
items.story: It was one of Payton's finest efforts of the campaign, tying a season high in scoring. The 33-year-old is worth streaming in most fantasy leagues until the Warriors get healthier, as Payton has averaged 13.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.9 steals in 22.9 minutes per tilt while shooting 56.5 percent from the floor in his last seven games.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) is available for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Payton has played through a lingering ankle injury that cost him the first two games of March, and the veteran guard has been given the green light to suit up for Tuesday's contest. Since the All-Star break, Payton has averaged 12.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.4 threes and 1.4 steals over 20.0 minutes per game.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Payton is dealing with a minor left ankle issue that he appears likely to play through. Over his last five games, he's averaging 11.0 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.4 steals.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) is good to go for Saturday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Payton will shed a probable tag to suit up for this contest. With De'Anthony Melton (knee) sidelined, Payton is a candidate to see a handful of extra minutes against the Thunder.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) is probable for Saturday's game in Oklahoma City.
items.story: Payton is on track to return from a two-game absence Saturday, which could result in fewer minutes for Pat Spencer and LJ Cryer. Check back for official confirmation on Payton's status closer to Saturday's tip.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) won't play Thursday against the Rockets.
items.story: Payton is set for a second straight absence due to a left ankle injury. Moses Moody (wrist) and Will Richard (ankle) are also out, so it'll presumably be up to Gui Santos, Nate Williams and Malevy Leons to step up in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) is questionable for Thursday's game against Houston.
items.story: The Warriors will be very thin Thursday and will be hoping Payton can give it a go -- Moses Moody (wrist) and Will Richard (ankle) have both been ruled out. De'Anthony Melton and Pat Spencer could have a lot on their plates Thursday.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) is out for Monday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Payton was considered a game-time call for Monday due to a left ankle issue, and the Warriors have since downgraded him to out. His absence should result in more opportunity for De'Anthony Melton and Pat Spencer in the backcourt.

items.headline: Payton (ankle) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Clippers.
items.story: Payton is in danger of missing his first game since Jan. 30 due to a left ankle impingement. If the veteran guard joins Stephen Curry (knee) and Will Richard (ankle) on the sidelines, Pat Spencer and De'Anthony Melton would be candidates for increased minutes, while Nate Williams could enter the rotation.

items.headline: Payton logged 19 points (8-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt), five rebounds, four assists and three steals in 28 minutes during Wednesday's 133-112 win over Memphis.
items.story: The Warriors were extremely shorthanded for the second leg of this back-to-back set, allowing Payton to step into an expanded role on the offensive side of things. Fantasy managers will not want to chase this line, however, as it has the makings of an obvious outlier.

items.headline: Payton registered 15 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt), eight rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 19 minutes off the bench during Thursday's 101-97 win over the Suns.
items.story: The 15 points represented Payton's best scoring effort since he dropped 19 points on the Pelicans back on Nov. 29, while the three made three-pointers were a season high. The veteran guard had gone 10 straight appearances without scoring in double digits prior to Thursday, however, and even with Stephen Curry (knee) spotting in and out of the lineup of late, there doesn't seem to be a consistent role for Payton.

items.headline: Horford will be rested Monday against the Suns.
items.story: As expected, Horford will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. Fortunately for the Warriors, Draymond Green (back) is set to return to the lineup.

items.headline: Horford had nine points (3-7 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 0-1 FT), five rebounds, two assists and one block across 22 minutes during Sunday's 124-112 win over the Clippers.
items.story: All three of Horford's field goals came from beyond the arc as the veteran provided floor spacing and modest contributions in several categories. His ability to generate three-pointers, rebounds and occasional blocks remains useful in deeper formats, though his reserve role limits his overall ceiling.

items.headline: Horford (back) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Horford was held out of Saturday's loss to Phoenix in the second half of a back-to-back set, though he'll be back in action Monday. His return will leave fewer minutes available for the likes of Graham Ike and Charles Bassey (knee), who is listed as probable.

items.headline: Horford (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Suns.
items.story: As expected, the veteran big man will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set due to lower-back injury management. With Draymond Green (back/rest) expected to join Horford on the inactive list, Graham Ike and Georges Niang are candidates for increased burn, especially if Charles Bassey (knee) is downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Horford posted 15 points (5-8 FG, 5-8 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist across 15 minutes in Friday's 128-118 preseason win over Portland.
items.story: Horford returned from a one-game absence and caught fire from downtown Friday. The veteran big man came off the bench in the Warriors' preseason finale and is expected to be a regular in the second unit during the regular season.

items.headline: Horford (rest) won't play in Tuesday's preseason game against the Lakers, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: The veteran center isn't making the trip to Las Vegas for this exhibition. He'll look to return for Friday's preseason finale versus Portland. Horford isn't expected to begin the season as a starter despite Kristaps Porzingis' (undisclosed) absence, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area.

items.headline: Horford (rest) is expected to play in Saturday's preseason game against the Kings, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
items.story: The veteran big man sat out Wednesday's exhibition versus Portland for rest purposes. Horford figures to receive some burn Saturday before the Warriors turn to some of their younger players in the second half.

items.headline: Horford (rest) is out for Wednesday's preseason game against Portland, per Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com.
items.story: The veteran center is getting a maintenance day Wednesday. His next chance to play comes Saturday against the Kings.

items.headline: Horford will come off the bench for Tuesday's preseason game against the Lakers, and he will not travel to Portland for Wednesday's exhibition, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: The Warriors will go with a small-ball starting lineup Tuesday, featuring Draymond Green and Yaxel Lendeborg in the post, with Horford shifting to the second unit. It's unlikely the 40-year-old veteran will earn enough consistent minutes in Golden State this season to warrant a roster spot in most fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Horford is in the starting lineup for Sunday's preseason matchup with the Clippers, Warriors' reporter Joseph Dycus reports.
items.story: Kristaps Porzingis (illness) is out indefinitely, so Horford could open the year as the Warriors' starting center. Joining him in the first unit for Sunday's exhibition will be Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green.

items.headline: Horford will play in Sunday's preseason game against the Clippers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: While Horford will be available for the preseason opener in Hawaii, head coach Steve Kerr said he will see action only in the first half and play "around 12-16 minutes." The 2007 No. 3 overall pick wasn't a routine contributor for the Warriors during the 2025-26 campaign, averaging 8.3 points and 4.9 rebounds, both career lows, along with 2.6 assists and 1.1 blocks over 21.5 minutes in 45 regular-season games. Although that is likely to remain the case in 2026-27, Horford could be tasked with an enhanced role right out of the gate, considering Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed) might miss time to begin the year.

items.headline: Horford could open the season as a starter if Kristaps Porzingis (undisclosed) isn't ready for Opening Night.
items.story: Horford's best fantasy days may be behind him at 40, but the opportunity for a larger role remains while Porzingis is on the mend. The veteran big man provided late-round fantasy numbers as a starter last regular season, averaging 10.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.4 blocks in 23.7 minutes per contest over 13 games in the first unit.

items.headline: Horford intends to sign a two-year, $14 million contract with the Warriors, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Horford will decline his player option in order to re-sign for another couple of years. The 40-year-old becomes the 13th player in NBA history to reach 20 seasons with this move. Just like 2025-26, it's likely that Horford plays a modest role with plenty of maintenance during the regular season. That includes sitting out one game of back-to-back sets.

items.headline: Horford finished with nine points (3-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and two assists over 26 minutes during Friday's 111-96 Play-In Game loss to Phoenix.
items.story: Horford played a key role in the Warriors' comeback victory against the Clippers on Wednesday, but the veteran big man was unable to replicate that success in Friday's elimination game. He was limited to just 45 regular-season games (13 starts) due to various injuries, including a right calf strain that cost him 14 consecutive games from March 15 to April 9. Horford will end his first regular season in Golden State averaging 8.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.1 blocks and 1.6 threes over 21.5 minutes per game. He holds a $5.97 million player option for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Horford supplied 14 points (5-8 FG, 4-7 3Pt) and three rebounds in 22 minutes during Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game victory over the Clippers.
items.story: Horford provided the Warriors with some unexpected offense late in the game, helping the team to an incredible come-from-behind victory. In only his third game back since returning from injury. Horford connected on three consecutive three-pointers down the stretch. Coupled with a vintage performance by Draymond Green and another shooting masterclass by Stephen Curry, Golden State will now play Phoenix for the right to face the Thunder in the playoffs.

items.headline: Horford won't start Wednesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Clippers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: The veteran big man got the starting nod with Draymond Green (back) sidelined in Sunday's regular-season finale -- a loss to the Clippers -- though Horford will retreat to the second unit in Wednesday's do-or-die matchup. The 39-year-old averaged 7.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.0 blocks in 20.6 minutes per game across 32 regular-season appearances off the bench.

items.headline: Horford amassed five points (2-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt), four rebounds and two assists over 19 minutes during Sunday's 115-110 loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Draymond Green (back) should be fine for Tuesday's rematch during the Play-In Tournament, and he will be an upgrade over Horford, who filled in for the feisty veteran. Horford's age is beginning to show, as the 39-year-old lacks the aggressiveness he's shown throughout his NBA career. The Warriors originally had grander plans for him, but the acquisition of Kristaps Porzingis and continued production from Green have limited Horford's production to a trickle.

items.headline: Horford will start Sunday's game against the Clippers, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Horford came off the bench during Friday's game against the Kings, but he will start Sunday. Over his last four completed starts, he has averaged 12.8 points, 6.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 2.0 blocks in 30.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Horford (calf) registered 10 points (4-8 FG, 2-4 3Pt), two assists and one block in 18 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Kings.
items.story: Just as head coach Steve Kerr had promised heading into Friday's contest, Horford was on a restriction of 15-to-20 minutes and fell right between that range while suiting up for the first time since March 13. Though Horford didn't appear to have any setbacks in his return from the right soleus strain that kept him sidelined for 14 straight games, the Warriors may not have much motivation to aggressively ramp up his workload during Sunday's regular-season finale versus the Clippers. Golden State is already locked into the No. 10 seed and may prefer to preserve Horford's health heading into next week's Western Conference Play-In Tournament.

items.headline: Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said that Horford (calf) will be limited to around 15-to-20 minutes in Friday's game against Sacramento, Sam Gordon of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
items.story: Horford will suit up after missing the Warriors' last 14 games due to a right soleus strain, but given the length of his absence along with the fact that Golden State is locked into the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference, the club will use him with caution. The return of Horford could still cut into the workload of fellow center Charles Bassey (ankle), who logged 30 minutes in the Warriors' 119-103 loss to the Lakers on Thursday.

items.headline: Horford (calf) is available for Friday's game against the Kings.
items.story: The veteran big man is set to return from a month-long absence with a calf strain, so his minutes could be limited Friday. That said, the recent rise in streaming appeal for Charles Bassey (ankle) could take a hit versus the Kings.

items.headline: Horford (calf) took part in a 5-on-5 scrimmage Thursday, and the Warriors are hopeful he'll play Friday against the Kings, Sam Gordon of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
items.story: Horford has already been ruled out for the first game of Golden State's back-to-back Thursday against the Lakers, but the team is optimistic about a Friday return. The veteran will presumably be re-evaluated Friday morning before another update is issued.

items.headline: Horford (calf) is "making good progress" toward a return and will be re-evaluated "early next week."
items.story: Horford has missed the Warriors' last 11 games while tending to a strained right soleus. Although the veteran's return date remains a mystery, he appears to be moving in a positive direction, participating in portions of Saturday's practice. The team indicated he will be re-evaluated "early next week," suggesting there is a chance he will return Tuesday versus Sacramento. With Quinten Post (foot) also sidelined, head coach Steve Kerr will presumably lean on Kristaps Porzingis and Draymond Green to handle most of the work in the middle.

items.headline: Horford is making good progress in his recovery from a right soleus strain and will be re-evaluated in one week, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Horford hasn't played since March 13 due to the calf injury and won't return until early April at the earliest. His next opportunity to play will come April 5 against the Rockets. With the veteran big man still on the shelf, Omer Yurtseven and Quinten Post (foot) are candidates for increased burn off the bench.

items.headline: Horford (calf) is out for Friday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: Horford is set to sit out his eighth straight game, but the Warriors are expected to release an update on his rehab Friday. Kristaps Porzingis, Draymond Green and Omer Yurtseven will continue to hold down the center spot while Horford is out.

items.headline: Horford (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: Horford will remain sidelined Wednesday with a right calf strain. Quinten Post (foot) is also out against the Nets, leaving plenty of opportunities for Kristaps Porzingis and Gui Santos in the frontcourt.

items.headline: Horford (calf) won't suit up for Monday's game against Dallas.
items.story: Horford was injured during a March 13 loss to the Timberwolves, and he's been unavailable for the Dubs' last five contests. The big man is due to be re-evaluated in coming days, although that doesn't mean he's close to returning. Kristaps Porzingis (back) is listed as probable for Monday's contest, and assuming he's available, he's expected to go a long way toward filling the void created by Horford's absence. Draymond Green and Gui Santos could also continue to see additional opportunities in the frontcourt.

items.headline: An MRI confirmed a minor right calf strain for Horford and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Danny Emerman of SFStandard.com reports.
items.story: Horford is set to miss at least the next five games, and it's important to note that while he'll be re-evaluated in one week, that doesn't mean he will return at that point. Quinten Post figures to be more involved in the rotation while Horford is sidelined.

items.headline: Horford (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Horford strained his right calf during the first quarter of Friday's loss to the Timberwolves. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr told reporters after the game that he expects Horford will miss time, per Anthony Slater of ESPN.com. It comes as no surprise seeing Horford scratched for Sunday's lineup, and the veteran big man will likely be sidelined for Monday's game against the Wizards. The Warriors will also be without Draymond Green (back) and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) on Sunday, so Golden State's frontcourt depth would be extremely depleted if Quinten Post (ankle) is also unable to play.

items.headline: Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said after Friday's 127-117 loss to the Timberwolves that Horford suffered a right calf strain during the contest and is expected to miss time, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports. "With a calf, we're not going to rush him back," Kerr said.
items.story: With Draymond Green (back) sitting out Friday, Horford picked up his 12th start of the season but played just five minutes before exiting with 7:05 remaining in the first quarter due to what the Warriors had labeled as right calf tightness. With Kerr confirming that the veteran big man strained his calf, Horford is expected to miss the Warriors' next game Sunday in New York and likely additional contests beyond that. The potential return of Green for Sunday's game could help offset Horford's absence, and Kristaps Porzingis and Quinten Post (ankle) could also move into larger roles in the Golden State frontcourt.

items.headline: Horford won't return to Friday's game against the Timberwolves due to right calf tightness. He finished with three points (1-3 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and one rebound in five minutes.
items.story: Horford entered the starting five in place of Draymond Green (back) but checked out of the game with just over seven minutes remaining in the first quarter and was ruled out for the rest of the game shortly thereafter. The absences of Green and Horford for the rest of the evening should open up more playing time for Kristaps Porzingis and Quinten Post in the frontcourt. The Warriors will likely send Horford in for further testing before deciding on his availability for Sunday's game against the Knicks, but the veteran big man would appear to be questionable -- at best -- for that contest.

items.headline: Horford accumulated 13 points (5-18 FG, 3-10 3Pt), nine rebounds, five assists and four blocks across 34 minutes during Tuesday's 130-124 overtime loss to the Bulls.
items.story: The fact that Horford needed 18 shots to score 13 points tells you all you need to know about his shooting performance. That said, the veteran big man still found a way to deliver strong numbers across the board due to his contributions in peripheral categories. He continues to sit out at least one half of back-to-back sets, but Horford's 34 minutes were a season-high mark, and he's played at least 29 minutes in three straight appearances.

items.headline: Horford (toe) will play Tuesday against the Bulls.
items.story: After missing the front end of this back-to-back set, Horford is all set to reprise his usual role. Quinten Post and Malevy Leons are expected to see reduced minutes as a result.

items.headline: Horford has been ruled out for Monday's game against Utah due to left toe injury management.
items.story: Horford will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set, though it appears likely he'll return Tuesday against Chicago. With the veteran big man and Kristaps Porzingis (illness) both sidelined, Quinten Post and Malevy Leons are candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Horford contributed 17 points (7-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal across 33 minutes during Thursday's 115-113 overtime victory over the Rockets.
items.story: Horford has alternated between the starting lineup and the bench most of the season, but he's been productive when handed a first-unit role. He has scored in double digits in his four starts since the All-Star break, averaging 16.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 4.5 assists across 28.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Horford is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Clippers, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Horford will return to the first unit Monday after coming off the bench Saturday against the Lakers. Gui Santos will be deployed off the bench in a corresponding move. Horford has scored in double figures in each of his previous four chances as a starter.

items.headline: Horford won't start Saturday's game against the Lakers, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Horford started Wednesday's win over the Grizzlies in place of Draymond Green (back), but the former will head back to the bench now that Green has been cleared to return. Horford has been productive when called upon and exploded for a season-high 22 points and six three-pointers in a start against the Nuggets last Sunday.

items.headline: Horford is in the Warriors' starting lineup against the Grizzlies on Wednesday.
items.story: Horford will be in the Warriors' starting five for the second time in three games due to the absence of Draymond Green (back). In his last start against the Nuggets on Sunday, Horford recorded 22 points, seven assists, one rebound, three steals and two blocks over 27 minutes in a 128-117 win.

items.headline: Horford (toe) is available for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Horford is no longer on the injury report after missing the front end of this back-to-back set Tuesday against the Pelicans. Even with Draymond Green (rest) questionable, Horford is likely going to see a modest workload Wednesday.

items.headline: Horford (toe) won't play Tuesday against the Pelicans.
items.story: Horford does not play in both games of back-to-back sets, so the Warriors will keep him on ice until Wednesday's game against Memphis. Quinten Post could be more involved as a result Tuesday.

items.headline: Horford is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Pelicans due to left toe injury management.
items.story: Horford hasn't appeared on the injury report lately for the Warriors, so this appears to be a precautionary listing. The club should have another update on his availability closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Horford logged 22 points (8-11 FG, 6-7 3Pt), seven assists, three steals, two blocks and one rebound across 27 minutes during Sunday's 128-117 win over Denver.
items.story: Horford drew the start with Draymond Green (back) sidelined and delivered in a big way, pouring in a season-high 22 points fueled by six three-pointers. Prior to Sunday, Horford had made just six total threes across six February games at a 23.1 percent clip, with his previous season high being four triples - a mark he hit twice, most recently Dec. 25 against Dallas. While it would be unwise to expect this level of production to become the norm for the 39-year-old, it's encouraging to see the veteran turn back the clock with a performance like this.

items.headline: Martinelli chipped in 10 points (4-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt) and three rebounds across six minutes during Sunday's 124-112 loss to the Warriors.
items.story: Martinelli made the most of his brief opportunity, scoring efficiently and knocking down two three-pointers during a late fourth-quarter push. Despite the impressive scoring burst, his minimal playing time leaves him well outside the fantasy radar unless his role expands considerably.

items.headline: Martinelli tallied nine points (2-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-4 FT) and one assist in 16 minutes during Saturday's 114-106 preseason loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Martinelli signed a two-way contract with the Clippers after he was selected with the No. 55 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. He'll likely spend most of his rookie campaign in the G League, but with all of the Clippers' injuries, they may have no choice but to let Martinelli learn on the fly.

items.headline: Martinelli posted 19 points (8-9 FG, 3-3 3Pt), five rebounds, two assists and two steals across 26 minutes in Wednesday's 108-94 Summer League win over the Wizards.
items.story: Martinelli missed just one of his nine shots from the floor, and this was his best performance of the current Summer League campaign.  The former Northwestern standout is playing on a two-way deal but is making his presence felt, scoring in double digits in each of his four SL appearances thus far while averaging 14.0 points per game.

items.headline: Martinelli signed a two-way contract with the Clippers on Monday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
items.story: The Clippers traded for Martinelli's draft rights in the 2026 NBA Draft and will now bring him on as a two-way player. The 22-year-old forward will likely spend most of his time with the club's G League affiliate, the San Diego Clippers. Over 33 starts at Northwestern in 2025-26, he averaged 23.0 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.0 assists while shooting 41.7 percent from deep in 35.6 minutes per game.

items.headline: The Knicks selected Martinelli with the No. 55 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and traded his rights to the Rockets, who then traded his rights to the Clippers for the No. 57 pick and cash considerations, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Martinelli will now head to Los Angeles after spending his college career at Northwestern. The 22-year-old logged 120 regular-season games for the Wildcats, though he averaged a career-best 23.0 points with 6.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.5 blocks, 0.8 steals and 41.7 percent shooting from deep across 35.6 minutes in 33 regular-season appearances in 2025-26. It's unknown what the roster will look like for the Clippers come the 2026-27 campaign. However, if there aren't significant changes made in the next few months, Martinelli could be in line for a prominent role right out of the gate.

items.headline: Lopez will start Monday's game against the Raptors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: The veteran big man will draw his first start of the season in the second leg of this back-to-back set, pushing Isaiah Jackson to the second unit. Lopez is averaging 12.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.0 blocks across 21.8 minutes per game through six regular-season outings thus far.

items.headline: Lopez racked up seven points (3-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds and two steals in 19 minutes during Sunday's 124-112 loss to Golden State.
items.story: Lopez failed to establish much offensive rhythm, connecting on just three of his eight attempts while contributing little on the glass. The veteran center did collect two steals, but his limited minutes and inconsistent production make him a difficult fantasy option in standard leagues.

items.headline: Lopez finished with 22 points (8-9 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and three blocks across 20 minutes during Friday's 125-117 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Lopez was the Clippers' most efficient bench scorer, missing only one of his nine shots and scoring 15 of his 22 points in the first half while adding three blocks. The 38-year-old backup center has opened the season with two productive games, following up a 17-point, 11-rebound effort in Wednesday's win over Sacramento. His veteran presence has been one of the bright spots on a young Clippers roster in the first week of the season.

items.headline: Lopez closed with 17 points (7-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 11 rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal over 27 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 121-96 win over Sacramento.
items.story: The 38-year-old managed only one double-double in 75 regular-season games last season, but Lopez wasted no time matching that total in 2026-27. He's been used mainly as a stretch big in recent years, hurting his rebounding numbers, but with only the unproven Isaiah Jackson ahead of him on the depth chart at center, Lopez could see more traditional usage near the basket and reverse that trend to some degree.

items.headline: Lopez amassed nine points (4-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds and one assist over eight minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Given preseason rotations, Isaiah Jackson, who started Wednesday, has overtaken Lopez for the Clippers' starting center job. Lopez looks to be positioned for a bench role to open 2026-27, and it's unclear what the veteran's role will look like when Yanic Konan Niederhauser is cleared to play again.

items.headline: Lopez is not listed in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Denver, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Lopez will come off the bench Wednesday after starting in Saturday's loss to the Raptors. The veteran has had a quiet preseason, averaging 3.5 points and 5.0 rebounds over 11.2 minutes per contest (two games).

items.headline: Lopez finished with six points (3-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), seven rebounds, one assist and one block across 15 minutes in Saturday's 114-106 preseason loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Lopez provided a solid presence on the glass, leading the Clippers' starters with seven rebounds despite playing just 15 minutes. The big man's abbreviated workload limited his scoring opportunities, but his rebounding production was encouraging. That said, he's expected to open the season as the No. 2 center behind Isaiah Jackson, though a strong showing in the final preseason games could change that. Lopez is still an imposing presence in the paint who can hit threes, so that should give him steady minutes regardless of whether he starts or comes off the bench.

items.headline: Lopez is in the starting lineup for Saturday's preseason matchup with the Raptors, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Head coach Tyronn Lue will use the preseason to find what groups mesh best, so a strong showing from Lopez on Saturday would help his case for a starting role. As a starter last season, Lopez averaged 10.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.8 triples and 1.3 blocks per contest on 45/37/74 shooting splits.

items.headline: Lopez won't start Sunday's preseason game against the Warriors, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: The veteran big man will come off the bench in favor of Isaiah Jackson. Lopez and Jackson are expected to compete for the starting center role ahead of the regular season, though it's worth noting that Jackson has spent time working with the first unit in training camp.

items.headline: Lopez is not guaranteed the Clippers' starting center role, as Isaiah Jackson has been working with the first team during training camp, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Lopez started 40 of his 75 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, averaging 8.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.2 blocks across 21.8 minutes per game on the campaign. The 38-year-old will face plenty of competition for minutes throughout the season, as Jackson could take Lopez's spot in the starting five. Additionally, Yanic Konan Niederhauser (foot) could fight for minutes once he's cleared to return.

items.headline: The Clippers are picking up the $9.2 million team option on Lopez's contract for the 2026-27 season, per Chris Haynes of NBA TV.
items.story: Lopez was thrust into a starting role following the Ivica Zubac trade last year, and he appears to be the early favorite for the top center gig once again in 2026-27. That said, the Clippers figure to try and upgrade the position this offseason. Lopez averaged 8.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 21.8 minutes per contest over 75 regular-season games in 2025-26.

items.headline: Lopez ended Wednesday's 126-121 Play-In Game loss to Golden State with 17 points (7-16 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals over 37 minutes.
items.story: Lopez ended his season with another serviceable performance, finishing what was a roller coaster campaign. Following the trade of Ivica Zubac, Lopez was thrust into a starting role, something that he was almost certainly not expecting coming into the season. While he was able to fill the role admirably, it is unlikely that the Clippers view him as a long-term solution. In 29 appearances over the final two months, Lopez averaged 11.4 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.3 blocks and 1.6 three-pointers in 27.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: Lopez notched 21 points (8-15 FG, 5-11 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist over 36 minutes during Friday's 116-97 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Lopez's 21 points marked his third-highest point total of the season and his second-highest total with the Clippers. Lopez bolstered his totals with five three-pointers, which matched his best result beyond the arc with his new team. The Clippers may need a couple of repeat nights from Lopez, as he could potentially line up against Kristaps Porzingis and Draymond Green twice in the coming week.

items.headline: Lopez logged nine points (4-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists and four blocks over 25 minutes during Tuesday's 116-103 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: Lopez grabbed double-digit rebounds for the first time since Feb. 20 but scored in single digits for a third straight game. Over his last 14 appearances, Lopez has averaged 10.0 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 2.2 blocks in 27.1 minutes.

items.headline: Lopez ended Sunday's 127-113 win over the Bucks with eight points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), seven rebounds, one assist, two blocks and four steals in 25 minutes.
items.story: With Ivica Zubac (ankle) off the roster down the stretch of the regular season, Lopez continues to provide some low-end fantasy appeal. Lopez has averaged 12.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 2.0 blocks and 1.0 steals in 28.6 minutes per contest in his last seven outings, shooting 50.0 percent from the floor and 41.9 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Lopez ended Monday's 129-96 victory over the Bucks with 19 points (7-9 FG, 5-6 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal in 22 minutes.
items.story: The five made three-pointers represented his best shooting effort from long range since Dec. 26, when he lit up Portland for a 9-for-14 performance from beyond the arc. Lopez continues to run hot and cold, sinking multiple three-pointers in five of 14 March games but also failing to hit one at all in five games. On the month, the veteran center is averaging 10.6 points, 4.0 boards, 2.0 assists, 1.6 threes and 1.1 blocks while shooting 51.8 percent from the floor and 41.5 percent from three-point range.

items.headline: Lopez racked up three points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt), one rebound, one assist, two blocks and one steal in 24 minutes during Monday's 119-115 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: This was a major dud for Lopez, but he's been solid enough to warrant another chance from his fantasy managers. Over his last eight games, he's producing ninth-round value in nine-category formats with averages of 10.0 points, 3.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 1.4 blocks and 1.4 three-pointers.

items.headline: Lopez amassed 26 points (11-19 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists and four steals across 34 minutes during Friday's 116-112 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: The 26 points represented Lopez's best scoring effort since Dec. 26, when he poured in 31 against the Trail Blazers, while the four steals tied his season high. The veteran center is still searching for some consistency since moving into the starting five in early February, but over the last 12 games Lopez is averaging 12.4 points, 5.0 boards, 1.8 assists, 1.7 threes, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks.

items.headline: Lopez contributed 17 points (7-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 21 minutes during Wednesday's 130-107 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Lopez didn't do much outside of scoring, but his contributions were enough to finish the game as the Clippers' third-best offensive weapon behind Kawhi Leonard and Bennedict Mathurin. Since moving to a permanent starting role Feb. 4, Lopez has scored in double digits in six of his last 12 outings. Consistency from game to game is lacking, but he should remain a secondary scoring option. He has decent fantasy upside, but he's more of a backup center rather than someone you'd want to have in your lineup every night.

items.headline: Lopez racked up 16 points (6-9 FG, 4-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, three assists and one steal over 26 minutes during Sunday's 137-117 victory over the Pelicans.
items.story: The 37-year-old center put together his best performance from three-point range since Dec. 26, when he erupted for 31 points on 9-for-14 shooting from beyond the arc against Portland. Since rejoining the starting five after the trade deadline, Lopez is averaging 10.5 points, 4.9 boards, 1.7 assists, 1.6 threes, 1.2 steals and 1.2 blocks in 29.7 minutes over the last 10 games.

items.headline: Lopez accumulated 16 points (7-12 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist, three blocks and two steals across 35 minutes during Friday's 125-122 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Lopez was forced to play a larger role on offense after John Collins (head) went down with an injury in the second quarter. Lopez recorded his third double-double of the season, and Ivica Zubac's (ankle) departure should allow Lopez to hit the milestone more frequently.

items.headline: Lopez registered 15 points (6-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt), one rebound, three assists, two blocks and two steals over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 105-102 win over the Rockets.
items.story: Fantasy managers can continue to treat Lopez as a low-end center option in the aftermath of the Ivica Zubac (ankle) trade. Lopez has averaged 9.4 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.6 blocks, 1.0 steals and 1.6 three-pointers in 30.4 minutes per game in his last five contests, shooting 42.1 percent from downtown.

items.headline: Lopez finished Tuesday's 102-95 loss to the Rockets with seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), two rebounds, one block and one steal across 29 minutes.
items.story: Lopez scored no more than seven points for the third time in the past four games, all of which have been starts. With Ivica Zubac traded to Indiana, Lopez assumed the starting role immediately. However, outside of a strong performance against the Kings, Lopez has been unable to deliver impactful standard-league production. During that four-game stretch, he has averaged just 8.0 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 28.7 minutes per contest. At best, he should be viewed as a blocks streamer.

items.headline: Lopez ended with 15 points (5-12 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal in 36 minutes during Friday's 114-111 victory over the Kings.
items.story: Making his second start since Ivica Zubac (ankle) was dealt to the Pacers, Lopez set a new season high in rebounds while posting his best scoring effort since a 31-point eruption in Portland on Dec. 26. The 37-year-old center may not have a lot left in the tank, but the Clippers will be counting on him to step up as part of the new supporting cast around Kawhi Leonard. Over nine starts this season, Lopez is averaging 10.1 points, 4.7 boards, 2.2 threes, 1.7 assists and 1.2 blocks in 25.8 minutes.

items.headline: Lopez closed Monday's 128-113 loss to Philadelphia with 13 points (5-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one block across 20 minutes.
items.story: Lopez continues to provide some value in deep category-driven leagues, but his upside is capped as long as Ivica Zubac is healthy at center. Over his last six appearances, Lopez has averaged 8.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.0 blocks and 1.7 three-pointers in 18.4 minutes per game.

items.headline: Vucevic racked up two points (1-2 FG), four rebounds, two assists and one block across seven minutes during Sunday's 108-97 loss to Boston.
items.story: Vucevic made little offensive impact in his brief appearance, attempting just two shots while playing a limited role in Orlando's frontcourt. His lack of playing time is concerning for fantasy managers, particularly with multiple big men competing for minutes.

items.headline: Vucevic racked up zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and two rebounds in four minutes during Friday's 115-93 loss to the Timberwolves.
