items.story: Conley saw less action than Bones Hyland (15 minutes), and that's been the case a lot recently. Over Conley's last six appearances, the veteran is averaging 4.0 points, 1.8 assists, 1.0 rebounds and 0.8 steals in 16.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Conley (rest) is available for Saturday's game against the Nets, Chris Hine of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.story: Conley was initially listed as questionable for rest purposes but will shed that tag Saturday. The veteran point guard is expected to come off the bench against Brooklyn, and he has averaged 3.0 points and 2.7 assists across 16.2 minutes per game over six appearances with the second unit in December.

items.headline: Conley (rest) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: The Timberwolves are considering giving the veteran floor general Saturday night off. If Conley sits out, Bones Hyland would likely see extra ballhandling duties and experience a boost in fantasy upside. Additionally, Rob Dillingham could join the Minnesota rotation to some extent in this case.

items.headline: Conley will start against the Knicks on Tuesday.
items.story: With Jaden McDaniels (hip) out, Conley will get the starting nod for the first time since Nov. 19. Over five starts so far this season, the veteran point guard has averaged 9.4 points, 5.8 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 26.8 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: Conley (Achilles) registered six points (2-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt), six assists, five rebounds, two blocks and one steal across 24 minutes in Sunday's 103-100 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Making his return from a four-game absence due to right Achilles tendinopathy, Conley ended up handling a prominent role off the bench and came through with a quality stat line during his time on the court. Conley is averaging 19.3 minutes per game on the season, but the Timberwolves had more playing time up for grabs after Jaden McDaniels (hip) missed the entire second half. Expect the Timberwolves to peel back Conley's minutes a bit if McDaniels is available to play Tuesday against the Knicks.

items.headline: The Nuggets declined Holmes' $5.55 million rookie-scale team option for the 2027-28 season, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: The decision puts Holmes, the 22nd overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, on track to become an unrestricted free agent in the summer of 2027. Denver's decision raises questions about the young big man's long-term future with the franchise, though it doesn't immediately affect his role or fantasy outlook for the current campaign.

items.headline: Holmes recorded three points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt), one rebound and one assist over two minutes during Thursday's 96-84 loss to the Thunder.
items.story: Holmes saw action only in the closing minutes of Denver's season opener, knocking down a three-pointer during his brief appearance. The limited playing time suggests the young big man remains outside the regular rotation, leaving him with little immediate fantasy value.

items.headline: Holmes finished with four points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block in eight minutes during Tuesday's 117-106 preseason win over the Jazz.
items.story: Holmes grabbed two offensive rebounds and didn't commit a turnover during his brief stint. The young big remains part of Denver's frontcourt depth and will look to carve out a consistent role during the preseason.

items.headline: Holmes finished Friday's 127-107 victory over the Thunder with two points (2-2 FT) and one steal across two minutes.
items.story: Nikola Jokic (wrist) didn't suit up in this contest. However, Holmes still didn't see much action from off the bench. While Jokic could be in the lineup for the season finale versus the Spurs in order to meet the 65-game threshold for awards eligibility purposes, it's unknown how much work the multi-time MVP will see. Still, even if Holmes manages to get on the floor more than usual Sunday, he likely won't be in the rotation during the playoffs.

items.headline: The Nuggets recalled Holmes from the G League's Grand Rapids Gold on Sunday.
items.story: Holmes will provide Denver with additional depth in the frontcourt for Sunday's game against the Trail Blazers, but he's unlikely to see any minutes outside of a garbage-time scenario. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in just four games for Denver since the All-Star break, averaging 4.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Holmes contributed five points (2-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt) and one rebound across three minutes during Wednesday's 103-84 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Holmes was in the rotation for just the fifth time in the past 13 games, all of which have been garbage-time appearances. With both Nikola Jokic and Jonas Valanciunas now healthy. Holmes is merely an emergency piece, providing little fantasy value.

items.headline: Holmes won't start against the Lakers on Tuesday, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
items.story: With Aaron Gordon (hamstring) back in the lineup following a one-game absence, Holmes will retreat to the second unit. During his last appearance off the bench in a win over Dallas on Wednesday, the 23-year-old center posted three points and two rebounds in only five minutes.

items.headline: Holmes is in the Nuggets' starting lineup against the Hornets on Sunday.
items.story: Holmes has not been a regular member of the Nuggets' rotation as of late. However, he'll have an opportunity for a solid role Sunday after being moved to the starting lineup due to the absence of Aaron Gordon (hamstring).

items.headline: Holmes (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Sunday in the Nuggets' 108-104 win over the Bucks.
items.story: In the absence of Nikola Jokic (knee) and Jonas Valanciunas (calf), Holmes had started in each of Denver's previous five contests, but he averaged just 17.6 minutes per game while shooting 34.8 percent from the field during that stretch. Head coach David Adelman opted to shake things up Sunday, deploying Aaron Gordon as a small-ball starting center while Zeke Nnaji served as the primary backup and Holmes was removed from the rotation entirely. The Nuggets may not necessarily stick with Gordon as their starting center in every matchup while both Jokic and Valanciunas are sidelined, but the instability of Holmes' role will make it difficult to rely on him in the majority of fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Holmes is not in the Nuggets' starting lineup against the Bucks on Sunday, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Holmes has started in each of the Nuggets' last five games due to the absences of Nikola Jokic (knee) and Jonas Valanciunas (calf). However, Holmes will come off the bench Sunday while Aaron Gordon enters the starting five.

items.headline: Holmes provided two points (1-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt), one rebound and four assists over 21 minutes during Monday's 125-124 overtime victory over the 76ers.
items.story: Holmes was soundly outplayed by Zeke Nnaji, who tied a career high with 21 points off the bench Monday. Holmes has mostly squandered the opportunity left behind by Nikola Jokic's (knee) absence so far, averaging 5.5 points, 3.0 assists and 2.3 rebounds in 20.5 minutes per game in his last four outings (three starts).

items.headline: Holmes produced three points (1-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), four rebounds and six assists across 24 minutes during Friday's 113-108 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Holmes picked up two fouls in his first three minutes, limiting him to just 24 minutes in the loss. While it wasn't the strongest performance, the fact that Holmes was given the starting nod was a real positive. With both Nikola Jokic (knee) and Jonas Valanciunas (calf) set to miss up to a month, it appears as though Holmes is going to have first crack at the starting job. If you added him in the past 24 hours, patience could be required.

items.headline: Holmes is in the Nuggets' starting lineup against the Cavaliers on Friday.
items.story: Holmes will make his first NBA start Friday due to the absences of Jonas Valanciunas (calf) and Nikola Jokic (knee). Holmes should remain in Denver's starting five for as long as Valanciunas and Jokic are sidelined, which could persist into late January/early February. Holmes played 22 minutes during the Nuggets' 106-103 win over the Raptors on Wednesday and finished with 11 points, three rebounds, one assist and one block.

items.headline: Holmes recorded 11 points (4-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block in 22 minutes Wednesday in the Nuggets' 106-103 win over the Raptors.
items.story: The No. 22 overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Holmes didn't make his professional debut last season after suffering a torn Achilles tendon in the Las Vegas Summer League. Though he's been fully healthy in 2025-26, Holmes has thus far received most of his minutes in the G League and had been limited to three garbage-time appearances at the NBA level before getting his first meaningful playing time Wednesday. Holmes' expanded role came after Jonas Valanciunas -- who was making his first start in place of superstar Nikola Jokic (knee) -- was forced out of the game with 4:03 left in the third quarter due to a right calf strain. While the severity of Valanciunas' injury isn't yet known, calf strains often entail multi-week recoveries, and with Jokic not set to be re-evaluated until late January or early February, Holmes could be poised for an extended run as the Nuggets' top center. Denver could also incorporate Zeke Nnaji into the rotation and make more use of small-ball lineups that would suppress Holmes' playing time, but at the very least, the 23-year-old rookie looks like a worthwhile speculative pickup in most leagues with the likelihood that Valanciunas misses time.

items.headline: Denver recalled Holmes from the G League's Grand Rapids Gold on Tuesday.
items.story: Holmes has appeared on an NBA court for just four total minutes this season and likely won't play Tuesday even though he has been recalled. Denver will continue to have Holmes split time with their G League affiliate.

items.headline: The Nuggets recalled Holmes from the G League's Grand Rapids Gold on Saturday.
items.story: After missing the entire 2024-25 campaign while recovering from a torn right Achilles tendon, Holmes has been healthy thus far during his rookie season but has nonetheless spent the majority of his time in the G League. He'll be available off the Nuggets' bench for Saturday's game against the Kings, though he's unlikely to be included in the rotation.

items.headline: Denver assigned Holmes to the G League's Grand Rapids Gold on Tuesday.

items.headline: Clark will sign a three-year, $10 million contract with the Timberwolves, Chris Hine of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports Friday.
items.story: The defensive-minded wing will re-sign with Minnesota after spending the first two years of his career with the club. He saw relatively consistent minutes before the Timberwolves traded for Ayo Dosunmu last season, though Clark could have a clearer path to consistent playing time in 2026-27 due to Naz Reid and Julius Randle no longer being in the picture. In addition, Donte DiVincenzo is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season after rupturing his Achilles in the first round of the playoffs. Over 68 regular-season appearances (one start) last season, Clark averaged 4.0 points, 1.8 rebounds and 0.7 steals in 13.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: Clark notched two points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and three rebounds in eight minutes during Friday's 139-109 loss to San Antonio in Game 6 of the Western Conference Semifinals.
items.story: The 2023 53rd overall pick proved his value as a defensive specialist throughout a 2025-26 campaign in which he appeared in 68 regular-season games, averaging 4.0 points, 1.8 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 0.7 steals in 13.1 minutes per contest. Known for his elite perimeter disruption, Clark was often deployed as a situational stopper against opposing lead guards during the regular season, but he saw his role vanish in the postseason, barely playing as rotations tightened. As the Timberwolves enter an offseason focused on reshaping the roster around Anthony Edwards, they face a key decision regarding Clark's restricted free agency. While his defensive advanced metrics and affordable price tag make him an attractive candidate for a qualifying offer, his limited offensive game and lack of a playoff role make him a potential casualty of a looming cap crunch and a necessary roster overhaul.

items.headline: Coach Dusty May has been impressed by Sasser's off-ball play during training camp, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
items.story: Sasser is competing for a bench role ahead of the 2026-27 season, and he's showing early on why he deserves a spot in the rotation. "Sass, first of all, I've been impressed with his cutting. He's been a real contributor when he wasn't even directly involved in the play," said May. "He's had a lot of those hidden plays that really make the team go. His shooting, his decision-making has been very sound, and defensively, he played at Houston, so we know we're going to get his best effort." Sasser averaged 5.2 points, 1.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 38 regular-season appearances a season ago in Detroit before joining Dallas in June as part of a six-team trade.

items.headline: Sasser will compete for playing time off the Mavericks' bench in 2026-27, and he could operate as the primary backup to Kyrie Irving (knee).
items.story: After spending the first three years of his career with the Pistons, Sasser will get a fresh start in Dallas. The 25-year-old logged several career lows in 2025-26, averaging 5.2 points, 2.0 assists, 1.0 rebounds and 0.5 steals in 12.0 minutes per showing across 38 regular-season outings (five starts). Although he shot a career-worst 39.0 percent from the field last season, Sasser connected on a career-high 41.5 percent of his three-point tries on 2.8 attempts per contest. He'll have a much clearer path to a consistent role with the Mavericks, as he'll presumably compete with rookie Sergio de Larrea for playing time off the bench behind Irving. While Cooper Flagg should continue to take on significant ball-handling duties, Sasser will likely have the opportunity to carve out a meaningful role, especially if he impresses during training camp and the preseason.

items.headline: The Mavericks officially acquired Sasser on Wednesday as part of an intricate six-team trade, per Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News.
items.story: After spending the first three years of his career with Detroit, Sasser is heading to Dallas. The 2023 first-rounder is searching for a fresh start as a backcourt reserve option with his new team, as he averaged a career-low 5.2 points, 2.0 assists and 1.0 rebounds in 12.0 minutes per game over 38 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

He finished with 20 points (7-16 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four assists and one steal in 23 minutes. It's unclear when he'll be involved with the NBA club.

items.headline: Detroit assigned Sasser (hip) to the G League's Motor City Cruise on Monday.
items.story: This is likely another rehab assignment for Sasser, as he's yet to make his regular-season debut for Detroit. On Monday, head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said that Sasser is trending in the right direction and has progressed to 3-on-3 work.

items.headline: Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Monday that Sasser (hip) is trending in the right direction and has progressed to 3-on-3 work, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.story: Sasser has yet to make his regular-season debut due to a lingering right hip issue, though he's seemingly nearing a return to the court. The 25-year-old guard has been getting practice reps in with the Pistons' G League affiliate, the Motor City Cruise, though he'll need to be cleared for 5-on-5 work before returning to game action with Detroit. He can still be considered week-to-week until the Pistons provide another update on his rehab.

items.headline: The Pistons recalled Sasser from the G League's Motor City Cruise on Saturday and assigned him back to the G League on Sunday.
items.story: Sasser will presumably join Motor City for practice again as he works his way back from a right hip impingement. While it's an encouraging sign that the 25-year-old guard is getting reps in, he still doesn't have a concrete timetable for his return to game action.

items.headline: Dick racked up 12 points (5-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and two steals in 29 minutes during Monday's 125-118 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Dick contributed across several categories against his former team, though he attempted just one three-pointer and failed to connect from beyond the arc. The 22-year-old has secured a starting role with the Clippers, but his fantasy upside remains tied to his perimeter shooting and offensive involvement. His two steals helped offset a relatively modest scoring performance.

items.headline: Dick will start Monday's game against the Raptors, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
items.story: Dick will get the nod at small forward due to Derrick Jones (knee) sitting out Monday. Dick got off to a strong start this season by dropping 12 points in the opener against the Kings, but he's been held to single digits in the scoring column in five games since.

items.headline: Dick closed Wednesday's 121-96 win over Sacramento with 12 points (3-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds and one block across 19 minutes.
items.story: With the rebuilding Clippers dealing with several injuries already, Dick stitched up an Opening Night rotation spot. A 2023 first-rounder, Dick remains worth monitoring on waiver wires until his role becomes more solidified.

items.headline: Dick amassed eight points (4-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three rebounds, two steals and four assists over 19 minutes in Wednesday's 122-110 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: Dick could see extra opportunities to start the season while Brandon Ingram recovers from a partially torn Achilles. His chances of claiming an Opening Night role increased when the Clippers announced Wednesday that Bradley Beal (knee) won't be ready to begin the year.

items.headline: Dick could see increased opportunities to begin the season while Brandon Ingram recovers from a partially torn Achilles and right heel surgery.
items.story: Dick arrived in Los Angeles alongside Ingram in the Kawhi Leonard trade and will compete for minutes on a Clippers team currently thin on the wing. Ingram's absence gives Dick an opportunity to earn a consistent rotation role, though he'll still face competition for playing time.

items.headline: The Clippers and Raptors mutually agreed Monday to complete the trade sending Leonard to Toronto in exchange for Brandon Ingram (heel), Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-rounders, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: The trade hit a snag in July when the league investigated Leonard and the Clippers for salary cap circumvention, but the deal is now official ahead of training camp. The 2023 first-rounder is searching for a fresh start in Los Angeles after averaging 6.0 points and 1.9 rebounds in 14.0 minutes per game across 76 regular-season appearances (one start) for the Raptors last year.

items.headline: The NBA has concluded its investigation into salary cap circumvention involving Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers, and the trade sending Dick to Los Angeles is expected to be finalized in the coming days, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Among other punishments, the Clippers were stripped of five first-round picks Wednesday. Furthermore, Leonard was fined $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits. With the findings and penalities being announced, Dick is now expected to officially join the Clippers after spending his first three seasons in the Association with Toronto. The 2023 No. 13 overall pick's production took a hit in 2025-26, during which he averaged 6.0 points and 1.9 rebounds in 14.0 minutes per game across 76 regular-season appearances (one start). The Clippers are set to acquire Dick, Brandon Ingram (heel), two first-round picks, two second-round picks and a first-round pick swap in exchange for Leonard. Dick figures to provide wing depth for Los Angeles in 2026-27, though he'll likely have to compete for playing time with Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal (hip) and Max Strus.

items.headline: The Raptors are expected to send Dick, Brandon Ingram, two first-round picks, a first-round pick swap and two second-round picks to the Clippers on Tuesday in exchange for Kawhi Leonard, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After a promising sophomore campaign, Dick took a major step back in Year 3 and will look for a fresh start with a change of scenery. The sharpshooter shot over 35 percent from three in each of his first two seasons but hit rock bottom in 2025-26, shooting 30.3 percent on 2.4 three-point attempts per game while playing only 14 minutes a night over 76 regular-season games. Dick will likely be competing with Kobe Sanders and Jordan Miller for reserve minutes in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Dick did not see the floor during Sunday's 114-102 loss to the Cavaliers in Game 7 of the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.
items.story: With Brandon Ingram (heel) joining the Raptors, Dick took a huge step back in 2025-26. Across 76 regular-season appearances, the third-year sharpshooter averaged a career-low 6.0 points, 1.9 rebounds and 0.7 assists in 14.0 minutes per game. Dick is set to return to Toronto in 2026-27, but it's concerning that he wasn't able to move into a more prominent role despite Ingram's absence in Game 7.

items.headline: Dick ended Sunday's 139-87 win over the Magic with 11 points (5-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist across 23 minutes.
items.story: Dick has been used sparingly in recent weeks, but he took advantage of some extra touches in this 52-point blowout win. Over his last six outings, he's averaging just 13.7 minutes per contest with 6.8 points, 1.5 assists and 1.5 rebounds on 40.0 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dick registered 10 points (2-4 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one steal over 15 minutes during Sunday's 120-98 loss to Phoenix.
items.story: The 2023 first-rounder has been part of Toronto's rotation for just two of the team's last five contests, implying he's not a major aspect of the mix for the time being. That said, Dick has an opportunity to remain in the lineup for Monday's matchup with the Jazz due to the absence of Immanuel Quickley (foot).

items.headline: Dick (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Friday in the Raptors' 122-115 win over the Suns.
items.story: Dick had appeared in each of Toronto's previous five contests while averaging 5.8 points in 6.8 minutes, but he ended up being the odd man out after head coach Darko Rajakovic condensed his rotation to nine Friday. The third-year wing's chances of re-emerging as a regular in the rotation will become even more difficult moving forward, as Collin Murray-Boyles (thumb) appears to be closing in on a return, which will bring the Toronto roster back to full strength.

items.headline: Dick finished with zero points (0-1 FG) in one minute during Tuesday's 111-95 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Dick moved back into the rotation after sitting out the previous two games, albeit for one minute during garbage time. Outside of a handful of encouraging performances, Dick has been a letdown this season, averaging just 6.2 points in 15.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dick (coach's decision) went unused off the bench Wednesday in the Raptors' 110-107 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Dick had appeared in each of the Raptors' first 58 games of the season, but after he was held under 10 minutes in two of the previous three contests, he was dropped from the rotation entirely. Rather than sticking with Dick on the second unit, head coach Darko Rajakovic went with Jamison Battle (six minutes) as the 10th man in the rotation. While Dick's removal from the rotation could prove to be a short-term arrangement, the Raptors still aren't expected to make the third-year wing a major priority when the team is at full strength.

items.headline: Dick will come off the bench for Wednesday's game against Sacramento.
items.story: Dick made his first start of the season Tuesday, logging 10 points and three rebounds across 23 minutes. However, he'll be replaced by Sandro Mamukelashvili in the first unit for Wednesday's matchup.

items.headline: Dick will start Tuesday versus the Warriors.
items.story: Dick will be earning his first start of the season Tuesday evening, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Jamal Shead, Immanuel Quickley, Brandon Ingram and Scottie Barnes. Per 36 minutes this season, Dick owns averages of 14.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.9 triples and 1.4 steals per game.

items.headline: Dick posted 21 points (9-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds and three assists over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-101 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Dick came from nowhere, recording the first double-double of his career, taking advantage of a depleted roster. Toronto was without Immanuel Quickley (back), RJ Barrett (ankle), Sandro Mamukelashvili (illness) and Ja'Kobe Walter (hip), as well as Jakob Poeltl, who continues to deal with a back issue. While this was a great performance, there is no need to prioritize Dick as a pickup, unless health continues to be an issue for others around him.

items.headline: Dick produced 11 points (4-4 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and two steals across 18 minutes during Monday's 118-100 win over the Hawks.
items.story: Dick continues to be used sparingly by the Raptors, making him a hit-or-miss fantasy asset in very deep formats. Over his last seven games, he's seen 15.1 minutes per night with 6.3 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 0.7 three-pointers on 43.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dick closed Sunday's 141-127 overtime win over the Warriors with four points (2-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 15 minutes.
items.story: Dick has mostly been an afterthought in Toronto's rotation lately. Over his last seven games, he's seen a mere 15.6 minutes per contest with 5.0 points, 1.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 three-pointers on 34.2 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Dick totaled 10 points (4-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), two rebounds and two steals in 15 minutes during Monday's 106-96 victory over Miami.
items.story: Dick bounced back from his last two scoreless appearances to reach double digits in points for just the eighth time this season, which included him breaking a three-game dry spell from beyond the arc. On the season, Dick averages 6.4 points, 1.9 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.7 steals, 0.1 blocks and 0.9 threes across 15.8 minutes.

items.headline: Dick posted zero points (0-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt) and one rebound across eight minutes during Tuesday's 117-101 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: Dick failed to score for the second straight game, another in a string of disappointing performances. After carving out a serviceable role for himself last season, Dick has been a non-factor thus far, averaging 6.3 points and 0.9 three-pointers in 15.8 minutes per game. He can be ignored in all but deeper leagues.

items.headline: Dick notched four points (2-7 FG, 0-3 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 21 minutes during Friday's 111-86 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Dick continues to be used sparingly, resulting in poor production across the board. He has scored double digits only six times thus far this season, averaging 6.8 points and 1.0 three-pointers in 16.4 minutes per contest. At this stage, he would need a lot of luck to force his way into a sizable role.

items.headline: Dick (head) is not listed on Friday's injury report and is on track to be available for Saturday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Dick sustained a head injury during the Raptors' win over the Pacers on Wednesday. The injury doesn't appear to be a serious issue for the third-year forward, and he should be available to play in the first leg of the Raptors' back-to-back set Saturday. Across 13 games since Nov. 2, Dick has averaged 6.8 points, 1.8 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 1.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 16.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Dick (head) has been ruled out for the remainder of Wednesday's game against the Pacers, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dick hit his head on the hardwood after taking a fall. He took a brief trip to the locker room before being ruled out. His next chance to play will come Saturday at Charlotte. Jamison Battle and Ochai Agbaji should see an uptick in minutes the rest of Wednesday's contest. Dick went scoreless (0-2 3Pt) with three rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block over seven minutes before departing.

items.headline: Dick went back to the locker room during Wednesday's game against Indiana after a hard fall, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.careports.
items.story: Dick took a hard fall while pursuing an offensive rebound, and according to Tony East of Forbes.com, Dick hit his head on the floor. The young wing stayed in the game briefly before departing and heading back to the locker room. Jamison Battle and Ochai Agbaji could see additional minutes while Dick is sidelined.

items.headline: Dick recorded 10 points (3-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and two assists in 19 minutes during Monday's 110-108 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Dick logged just his fifth appearance of the season with at least 10 points and his sixth time hitting multiple threes. The 2023 first-round pick has not seen enough volume or produced enough in other categories to warrant any value on any fantasy rosters yet. Still, he could be an intriguing add should one of the starters miss any time.

items.headline: Dick closed with six points (3-7 FG, 0-4 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 119-109 victory over the Nets.
items.story: Dick has not been as involved in the rotation as he was thought to be entering the season, averaging 7.6 points, 2.2 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.5 steals and 1.2 threes on a 35.1 percent clip in only 15.9 minutes. His role backing up Brandon Ingram is established, and he will likely only see extended playing time in the event of injury or blowout.

items.headline: Dick amassed 14 points (3-4 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 5-6 FT) and one rebound across 22 minutes during Tuesday's 128-100 win over the Bucks.
items.story: The Raptors ran away with this game early on, allowing Dick to see extended run off the bench. This was Dick's second-highest scoring performance of the season, with his best night coming Opening Night with 21 points. Dick remains mostly a deep-league fantasy asset with averages of 8.0 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.1 three-pointers in 16.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Dick notched zero points (0-2 FG, 0-2 3Pt) across eight minutes during Monday's 121-103 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Dick missed both of his shot attempts, continuing what has been a modest start to the season. Coming off a strong 2024-25 season, Dick's role has seemingly taken a sizeable hit. The addition of Brandon Ingram, as well as the arrival of rookie Collin Murray-Boyles, has seen Dick slide into a negotiable role, with his playing time fluctuating from one night to the next.

items.headline: Dick dropped five points (2-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt), four rebounds, an assist and a steal across 18 minutes in Friday's 122-116 loss to Milwaukee.
items.story: Dick was unable to follow up his stellar performance Wednesday against the Hawks. However, he led all bench players in minutes played and will continue in his role as the team's sixth man. Dick's next chance to make amends for his quiet showing will be Sunday against the Mavericks.

items.headline: Dick finished Wednesday's 138-118 victory over Atlanta with 21 points (6-10 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-8 FT), five rebounds and one steal in 24 minutes.
items.story: The third-year guard led the charge for the Raptors' second unit on a night when they out-scored the Hawks' bench 48-34. Dick saw his minutes and shooting volume increase in 2024-25 without it adversely affecting his efficiency, and the 21-year-old could be poised to take another step forward this season.

items.headline: Dick (back) is slated to play Friday in the preseason finale against Brooklyn, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Dick missed Wednesday's preseason game against the Celtics with back spasms. However, the sharpshooter looks to be good to go Friday and will enter the regular season with a bill of health.

items.headline: Dick (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's preseason game against the Celtics, Esfandiar Baraheni of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Dick will not suit up due to lower back spasms, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports. The next opportunity for the Kansas product to return to the floor will be Friday's preseason finale against the Nets.

items.headline: Dick finished with 22 points (8-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 3-6 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal across 24 minutes during Friday's 107-105 preseason win over the Celtics.
items.story: Dick had a strong all-around performance, coming four rebounds shy of a double-double in limited minutes on the floor. The Kansas product shot well, making 61.5 percent of his attempts from the field.

items.headline: Dick will start Friday's preseason game against the Celtics.
items.story: A number of the Raptors' usual starters are sitting Friday, giving Dick a shot with the first five. That said, the sharpshooter will likely begin the regular season in a reserve role.

items.headline: Dick racked up 14 points (6-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 15 minutes during Wednesday's 130-122 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Dick was incredibly efficient off the bench during his limited time on the floor. He shot 85.7 percent from the floor while showing his knack for scoring when he's the primary option for Toronto.

items.headline: Raptors general manager Bobby Webster said Friday that Dick (knee) is good to go for training camp, Ryan Wolstat of the Toronto Sun reports.
items.story: Dick was shut down for the 2024-25 regular season back on March 2 with a lingering right knee issue. However, it sounds like he'll be a full go for training camp with no reported restrictions. Dick averaged 14.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 29.4 minutes across 54 appearances in 2024-25, but he will have increased competition for touches as the Raptors integrate Brandon Ingram.

items.headline: Dick (knee) is out for the remainder of the 2024-25 regular season, Ryan Wolstat of the Toronto Sun reports.
items.story: Dick hasn't played since March 2 due to a right knee injury and will sit out the rest of the season with the Raptors sitting at 11th in the Eastern Conference standings. The second-year forward will end the 2024-25 campaign averaging 14.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 29.4 minutes across 54 appearances.

items.headline: Dick (knee) will not play Friday against the Pistons.
items.story: Dick will miss his 17th game in a row Friday, and his next chance to play comes Sunday against the Nets. At the beginning of March, the Raptors announced that Dick would be re-evaulated in two weeks after being diagnosed with a hyperextended right knee resulting in bone bruises. However, the team hasn't provided an update since, and the sharpshooter remains without a return timeline.

items.headline: Dick (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Trail Blazers, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports.
items.story: Dick will not be able to make his return to the floor Thursday against Portland, extending his absence to 16 straight games. The next opportunity for the second-year forward to play will be Friday against the Pistons.

items.headline: Dick (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Bulls, Coty Wiles of RaptorsRepublic.com reports.
items.story: Dick will miss his 15th consecutive contest due to a right knee contusion. There's no clear timetable for the second-year forward's return, though his next chance to suit up will come Thursday against Portland.

items.headline: Dick (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
items.story: Dick will miss a 14th straight game for the Raptors while nursing a right knee contusion. The next chance for the promising young forward to return to the floor will be Tuesday against the Bulls.

items.headline: Goodwin won't return to Monday's game against the Warriors due to a left calf injury, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports. He recorded four points (2-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and one steal in 10 minutes before exiting.
items.story: Rasheer Fleming and Ryan Dunn could see more opportunities in the second half with Goodwin shut down for the evening. The severity of his injury is unclear at this time.

items.headline: Goodwin ended with nine points (4-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt), four assists, three steals and two rebounds in 20 minutes during Saturday's 131-122 win over Golden State.
items.story: Goodwin logged 20-plus minutes for a second straight game and tied for the game-high mark in steals. He struggled from three-point range but didn't miss a shot from inside the arc. The versatile 28-year-old will likely continue playing a steady role off Phoenix's bench moving forward.

items.headline: Goodwin recorded five points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt) while adding six steals, three rebounds and two assists in 16 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's preseason loss to the Bulls.
items.story: The journeyman guard has been a terror on the defensive end during the exhibition schedule, snagging nine steals in two games so far. Goodwin is coming off a career-best season in 2025-26, producing 8.7 points, 4.9 boards, 2.1 assists, 1.6 threes and 1.5 steals in 22.5 minutes over 70 regular-season games for the Suns, and he should be a key part of the second unit once again in 2026-27.

items.headline: Goodwin recorded seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds, three steals and one assist in 11 minutes during Monday's preseason loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Goodwin made an immediate impact off the bench, grabbing three offensive rebounds and creating havoc defensively. His rebounding and defensive versatility should help him compete for a regular spot in Phoenix's rotation.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) agreed to a three-year, $19 million deal with the Suns on Sunday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Goodwin was claimed off waivers by Phoenix last July and made the regular-season roster before delivering a career-best year. Across 70 regular-season appearances (10 starts), the 27-year-old guard averaged 8.7 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals while shooting 37.0 percent from deep in 22.5 minutes per game. Goodwin missed the team's final three postseason games against Oklahoma City due to a left calf strain, though he'll likely be good to go by the time training camp rolls around. He receives added security with this new contract, which includes a player option for the third year.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) won't play in Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder on Monday.
items.story: Goodwin will miss his third game of this first-round series while tending to a left calf strain. His next opportunity to take the floor would arrive Wednesday if the Suns are able to extend the series with a win Monday.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is a game-time decision for Monday's Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against Oklahoma City, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Goodwin is on the brink of a return from a left calf injury, but he'll need to prove his health during warmups before receiving the green light from Phoenix's training staff. Expect another update on his availability closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is questionable for Game 4 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder on Monday, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Goodwin has missed the Suns' last two games due to a left calf injury that he sustained in Game 1 on April 19. Collin Gillespie would likely remain in the Suns' starting lineup Monday if Goodwin is not cleared to return.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is listed as out for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Goodwin will now miss a second consecutive contest, so his next chance to suit up will be Monday for Game 4. With Goodwin ruled out, Collin Gillespie is expected to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) will go through pregame warmups before Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against Oklahoma City, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Goodwin remains questionable for Game 3. However, head coach Jordan Ott stated that the 27-year-old will go through warmups before a decision is made regarding his availability. He suffered an ankle injury during the 119-84 loss to the Thunder to begin the series and was ruled out for Game 2. If Goodwin can't suit up, Collin Gillespie is the favorite to remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is listed as questionable for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder.
items.story: Goodwin is in danger of missing a second straight game due to left calf soreness. However, he was a full participant in Friday's practice, which bodes well for his chances of suiting up. If the 27-year-old isn't cleared to play, Ryan Dunn, Royce O'Neale and Collin Gillespie would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice, per Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic.
items.story: Goodwin missed Game 2 on Wednesday versus the Thunder with left calf soreness, which cropped up during Sunday's Game 1 loss in Oklahoma City. Phoenix's official injury report should shed more light on the swingman's chances of playing in Game 3, but Goodwin appears to be progressing well.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) has been ruled out for Wednesday's Game 2 against the Thunder.
items.story: Goodwin exited Sunday's Game 1 loss after logging just five minutes and did not return due to left calf soreness. He will now miss Wednesday's contest with the same issue, and his next chance to play will come in Game 3 on Saturday. With the 27-year-old out, Ryan Dunn, Royce O'Neale and Collin Gillespie are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Goodwin (calf) is listed as questionable for Game 2 against the Thunder on Wednesday.
items.story: Goodwin exited Sunday's Game 1 loss to the Thunder due to left calf soreness and is in danger of missing Game 2. If the 27-year-old is ultimately ruled out, Ryan Dunn, Royce O'Neale and Haywood Highsmith would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Goodwin has been ruled out for the rest of Game 1 of the Western Conference first-round playoff series against the Thunder on Sunday due to left calf soreness, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Goodwin tweaked his left calf in the second quarter, and medical staff determined that the injury was severe enough for the fifth-year forward to not return to Sunday's game. He'll finish with two points (1-4 FG, 0-3 3Pt) over five minutes. Royce O'Neale started in place of Goodwin to open the second half.

items.headline: Goodwin (undisclosed) went to the locker room during the second quarter of Game 1 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder on Sunday, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.story: It's not exactly clear what caused Goodwin to exit Sunday's game, but the team should have an update once he is evaluated by medical staff. Grayson Allen and Haywood Highsmith should see more minutes for as long as Goodwin is out of the game.

items.headline: Goodwin posted 19 points (7-11 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), nine rebounds, two assists and six steals in 34 minutes during Friday's 111-96 Play-In Game victory over the Warriors.
items.story: Goodwin played a significant role on both ends of the floor to help vault the Suns into the playoffs, where the Thunder awaits. Although Grayson Allen (hamstring) was cleared to play, the coaching staff opted to keep him on ice, allowing Goodwin to remain in the starting lineup. He finished the night just one rebound short of a double-double while also recording a season-high six steals.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) has been cleared to play in Tuesday's Play-In Game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Goodwin should be fresh for Tuesday's Play-In Game after sitting out the final two games of the regular season while tending to an ankle issue. He averaged 8.7 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals over 70 regular-season appearances.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) won't play in Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Goodwin started in three consecutive games before missing Friday's 101-73 loss to the Lakers. With Goodwin ruled out, Rasheer Fleming and Jamaree Bouyea should be in line for more work.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Goodwin is in danger of missing a second consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain. Jalen Green (knee) and Collin Gillespie (shoulder) are also questionable, while Devin Booker (ankle) and Grayson Allen (hamstring) have already been ruled out, so the Suns could be very thin in the backcourt.

items.headline: Goodwin (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Goodwin exited Wednesday's win over the Mavericks early and will now miss Friday's contest due to a sprained left ankle. His next chance to play will come in Sunday's regular-season finale in Oklahoma City. With Goodwin out, Grayson Allen, Ryan Dunn and Collin Gillespie are candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Goodwin exited Wednesday's game against the Mavericks in the second quarter with a left ankle injury and will not return. He'll finish with nine points (3-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 13 minutes.
items.story: With Goodwin out for the remainder of the contest, Rasheer Fleming and Ryan Dunn will likely help pick up the slack. The severity of the ankle injury is unclear, but for now, Goodwin can be considered questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.

items.headline: Goodwin (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Wednesday's game against the Mavericks, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Goodwin logged 13 minutes before exiting to the locker room with 4:53 remaining in the second quarter. He didn't start the second half and can be considered questionable to return until further notice.
