items.headline: Terry (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Trail Blazers, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Terry drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game due to a left shoulder injury. He is eligible to play in seven more regular-season games under his two-way contract, so he won't play against Portland but could be available for Tuesday's game against the Nuggets. MarJon Beauchamp and Trendon Watford will see more minutes in Terry's absence.

items.headline: Terry is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Trail Blazers due to a left shoulder impingement.
items.story: Terry may have suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Nets, when he fell to the floor hard after being inadvertently tripped mid-air by Ben Saraf. Terry has averaged 21.0 minutes per game over his last four outings, and if he's unable to play Sunday, then those minutes would be absorbed by MarJon Beauchamp, Trendon Watford and Kyle Lowry.

items.headline: Terry (undisclosed) checked in at the 3:48 mark of the third quarter of Saturday's game against the Nets, per the broadcast.
items.story: Terry exited to the locker room in the second quarter after being tripped mid-air by Ben Saraf, but the former was cleared by medical staff to return to Saturday's game. Terry is expected to see extended minutes for the 76ers due to the absences of Kelly Oubre (elbow), Tyrese Maxey (finger) and Paul George (suspension).

items.headline: Terry went to the locker room during the second quarter of Saturday's game against the Nets, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: Terry had a scary fall on a layup attempt after Ben Saraf inadvertently tripped him while in mid-air. Terry was able to shoot both of his free-throw attempts (making one) before being taken to the locker room, where he is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. MarJon Beauchamp would be slated for a larger role in the second half if Terry is unable to return.

items.headline: Terry finished Monday's 115-101 loss to the Cavaliers with nine points (4-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 19 minutes.
items.story: Terry made a strong impression on his new team Monday, and with so many injuries in Philadelphia, he's at least worth monitoring in deeper formats. Across five total appearances with the 76ers, Terry is averaging a mere 10.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Terry contributed two points (0-1 FG, 2-2 FT), one assist and one steal over five minutes during Tuesday's 135-114 victory over the Pacers.
items.story: Terry remained in the rotation, although he logged no more than seven minutes for the third straight game. Since arriving in Philadelphia, Terry has been nothing more than an afterthought, typically utilized during garbage time only. Despite the change of scenery, it appears that his fantasy value could remain almost nonexistent.

items.headline: Terry signed a two-way contract with the 76ers on Tuesday, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: The 76ers created an open roster slot by converting Dominick Barlow to a standard deal. Terry is a project for the 76ers to develop in the G League, and it's unlikely that he sees meaningful minutes at the NBA level in the near future.

items.headline: Terry (recently traded) is out for Friday's game against Minnesota.
items.story: Terry came over from the Knicks on Thursday via trade, but he has not yet joined his new team for action. His next chance to make his Pelicans debut comes Monday against the Kings. Given the uncertainty surrounding his role, Terry's absence doesn't seem to shake up the New Orleans rotation.

items.headline: The Knicks traded Terry and two second-round picks to the Pelicans on Thursday in exchange for Jose Alvarado, Ian Begley of SportsNet New York reports.
items.story: Just over 12 hours ago, Terry was traded to New York in exchange for Guerschon Yabusele, and now he's headed to New Orleans, where his role will likely be muted. He averaged at least 11 minutes per game in each of the past three seasons for Chicago, but his production has been lackluster. He can be considered questionable to suit up in Minnesota on Friday.

items.headline: The Bulls traded Terry to the Knicks on Wednesday in exchange for Guerschon Yabusele, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Terry's stint in Chicago will end after three-plus seasons. The versatile 23-year-old wing will get a fresh start with the Knicks after appearing in 34 games and averaging 3.5 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 11.1 minutes with the Bulls this season. He'll likely be competing with Landry Shamet, Jordan Clarkson and Mohamed Diawara for minutes off the bench.

items.headline: Terry recorded eight points (3-7 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 0-1 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal over 28 minutes during Sunday's 134-91 loss to the Heat.
items.story: With the Bulls shorthanded once again, Terry made another positive showing and eclipsed 28 minutes once again. He's averaging 8.5 points, 4.5 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.5 three-pointers over his last two outings, and with the franchise rumored to be sellers at the upcoming trade deadline, Terry could be a name to monitor closely in deeper formats.

items.headline: Terry finished with 11 points (4-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt), five rebounds, two blocks and three steals over 13 minutes off the bench during Wednesday's 128-126 win over the Jazz.
items.story: It was an incredibly productive performance from the fourth-year forward despite his limited minutes. It was the first time this season Terry has recorded multiple steals and blocks in the same game, while the points were a season high. The 18th overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft doesn't have a consistent enough role in the rotation to have any real fantasy value, but if the 19-21 Bulls decide to become sellers, Terry could wind up getting more court time after a roster shakeup.

items.headline: Terry contributed zero points (0-2 FG) over three minutes during Saturday's 125-107 victory over Dallas.
items.story: Terry delivered a donut once again, going scoreless for the sixth time in his past eight appearances. Even with recent injuries to the backcourt, Terry has been unable to produce anything of note. In seven appearances over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 1.1 points in 9.5 minutes.

items.headline: Terry accumulated five points (2-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt) over 13 minutes during Saturday's 112-99 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: With Josh Giddey (hamstring) and Coby White (calf) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Terry has been able to force his way into the rotation. With that said, he certainly hasn't made the most of his time on the floor, averaging just 1.3 points and 1.3 assists over the past four games.

items.headline: Terry (hand) will play Sunday versus the Pelicans.
items.story: Terry was being listed as probable, and now we have official confirmation that he'll be out there. Terry is averaging 3.0 points and 1.8 rebounds in 11.3 minutes per game this season.

items.headline: Terry (hand) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Terry is dealing with a left hand strain but is likely to suit up Sunday. With Ayo Dosunmu (thumb) unlikely to play, Terry could continue seeing meaningful minutes off the bench. The 23-year-old forward has appeared in four straight games, averaging 4.8 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.8 steals in 17.5 minutes per tilt during that span.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is available for Sunday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Terry has been dealing with a left calf strain lately, but he will be able to play through it again Sunday. Terry could see an expanded role due to Isaac Okoro (back) and Kevin Huerter (thigh) being out of the lineup.

items.headline: Terry is probable for Sunday's game against the Warriors with a left calf strain.
items.story: Terry remains day-to-day with a mild left calf strain. Over his last two appearances, the 23-year-old has averaged 6.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.5 steals in 18.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is available for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Terry will shed his probable tag due to a left calf issue and suit up in his second consecutive contest following a five-game absence. Over his last five appearances, the 23-year-old swingman has averaged 3.6 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.2 steals across 15.2 minutes per game. He could see a slight bump in minutes Friday with Tre Jones (ankle), Isaac Okoro (back), Ayo Dosunmu (thumb) and Kevin Huerter (hamstring) sidelined.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is listed as probable for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: Terry matched his season high in minutes last game with 18, and with the statuses of Ayo Dosunmu (thumb), Zach Collins (wrist), Tre Jones (ankle), Isaac Okoro (back), Jalen Smith (hamstring) and Coby White (calf) all up in the air, more playing time could be in store for Terry.

items.headline: Terry will play in Wednesday's game against Brooklyn, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: Terry will return from a five-game absence due to a left calf strain. In 10 games played, Terry is averaging 2.3 points, 1.5 assists and 1.3 rebounds across 9.0 minutes this season.

items.headline: The Bulls assigned Terry (calf) to the G League's Windy City Bulls on Tuesday before later recalling him. He's listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Terry presumably joined Windy City for practice as he ramps up following a five-game absence due to a left calf strain. It remains to be seen whether the 23-year-old forward will return Wednesday, and the Bulls will likely make a final decision on his availability closer to tipoff at 8:00 p.m. ET.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is questionable  for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Terry has a chance to end a five-game absence due to a left calf strain. The Bulls will re-evaluate him closer to Wednesday's tipoff, but he won't be guaranteed to see meaningful playing time even if the team clears him.

items.headline: Terry (calf) won't play Monday against the Magic.
items.story: No surprise here, as Terry was initially listed as doubtful. The forward will miss his fourth straight game, but his absence won't have many fantasy implications.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against the Magic.
items.story: Terry is expected to miss his fourth straight game due to a left calf strain. If he's ultimately ruled out, his next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against the Nets.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is out for Friday's game against the Hornets, Chuck Swirsky of the Bulls Radio Network reports.
items.story: Terry is missing a third consecutive game with a calf injury. His next chance to return is Saturday against the Pacers. Terry's absence may open up a few extra minutes for Ayo Dosunmu and Tre Jones.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is doubtful for Friday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: Terry was originally listed as questionable before this downgrade. Terry is a fringe rotation player for Chicago, so this news doesn't move the needle much in fantasy hoops.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is questionable for Friday's game against Charlotte.
items.story: Terry has missed the past two games for Chicago, but he remains day-to-day. He's been a fringe rotation player for Chicago, so his status doesn't carry many fantasy implications.

items.headline: Terry (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Terry will miss his second straight game due to a strained left calf, and his next chance to play will come Friday against the Hornets. With the 23-year-old forward and Isaac Okoro (back) both remaining on the shelf, Julian Phillips and Ayo Dosunmu are candidates for increased playing time, especially if Kevin Huerter (illness) or Patrick Williams (wrist) are downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is out for Saturday's game against the Wizards, Julia Poe of the Chicago Tribune reports.
items.story: Terry grabbed four rebounds, dished out two assists and finished scoreless across 13 minutes in Friday's loss to Miami. The veteran forward won't be an option here, meaning Julian Phillips, Jalen Smith and rookie Noa Essengue could be in line for more minutes in the frontcourt. Terry's next chance to play will come Monday at New Orleans.

items.headline: Terry (calf) is doubtful for Saturday's game against the Wizards.
items.story: After leaving Friday's loss to the Heat early and not returning, Terry will likely miss the second half of Chicago's back-to-back set. His next chance to return will come Monday in New Orleans, but given the current state of calf injuries in the NBA, it wouldn't be surprising if Terry is sidelined for the Bulls' upcoming four-game road trip.

items.headline: Terry will not return to Friday's game against the Heat due to a calf injury, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
items.story: With the Bulls set to play again Saturday against the Wizards, Terry won't have much time to recover. If he needs to sit out Saturday's match, that would open up some minutes for Patrick Williams. Terry will finish Friday's game with zero points (0-1 FG), four rebounds and two assists in 13 minutes.

items.headline: Terry supplied six points (3-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds, five assists, one block and three steals in 17 minutes during Wednesday's 122-121 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Terry saw meaningful minutes for the second straight game, scoring a season-high six points. While there is obviously very little to see here from a fantasy perspective, it is interesting that he played more minutes than both Patrick Williams and Jalen Smith, both of whom had been playing a consistent role.

items.headline: Terry posted one point (1-4 FT), one rebound, one assist and one steal over 10 minutes during Wednesday's 124-113 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Terry saw a handful of extra minutes, although he failed to make the most of his opportunity. He eclipsed 10 minutes for just the second time this season, highlighting how muted his role has been thus far. There is no indication he will be used as anything more than an emergency piece moving forward, negating any fantasy value he might have.

items.headline: Terry racked up two points (1-2 FG), one rebound, two assists and two blocks across 14 minutes during Tuesday's 113-111 win over Philadelphia.
items.story: Terry made his fourth appearance of the season in Tuesday's win. Overall, he's seeing a mere 5.8 minutes per contest, keeping him miles away from fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Terry finished with 11 points (3-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six assists, five rebounds and one steal across 21 minutes of Tuesday's 124-117 preseason loss to Denver.
items.story: Several projected rotation players sat out Tuesday, allowing Terry to get some rare run with the second unit. Terry has averaged a mere 11.1 minutes in the last three regular seasons combined for Chicago, and he's once again facing an uphill battle for regular playing time.

items.headline: Barlow (back) has been on the court "a little bit" and will be re-evaluated Tuesday, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: The Sixers are hoping for positive news so they can progress Barlow's workouts. The big man has yet to make his season debut due to a lumbar spine bone stress response.

items.headline: Barlow will miss at least the next two weeks due to a lumbar spine bone stress response, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: The back issue cost Barlow the entire preseason, and now he'll begin the regular season on the sidelines. The earliest we could see Barlow back on the court would be Nov. 2, but it wouldn't be shocking to see his absence extend beyond that two-week window.

items.headline: Barlow (back) did not participate in Monday's practice, according to 76ers reporter Paul Hudrick.
items.story: Barlow wasn't able to make any appearances during the preseason and remains without a timetable to return. The 76ers will release an injury report Monday evening ahead of Opening Night against the Knicks on Tuesday.

items.headline: Barlow (back) didn't participate in Sunday's practice, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow didn't play in the preseason and is in danger of missing time in the regular season. If the 23-year-old is ultimately ruled out for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Knicks, Adem Bona (foot), Jabari Walker and Justin Edwards could see increased burn.

items.headline: Barlow (back) didn't play in Friday's 125-120 preseason loss to Boston in overtime.
items.story: Barlow missed the entire preseason with a back injury. He can be considered questionable for Tuesday's regular-season opener against the Knicks until further notice.

items.headline: Barlow (back) was unable to practice Tuesday, Noah Levick of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.story: Barlow has missed the entire preseason so far and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered questionable at best for Friday's preseason finale against Boston.

items.headline: Barlow (back) isn't expected to play in either of Philadelphia's next two preseason games against Brooklyn and Boston, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
items.story: Barlow also missed Monday's preseason opener against New York due to the back issue. His next opportunity to make his preseason debut will come Oct. 16 in a rematch against Boston.

items.headline: Barlow won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Knicks due to a back issue, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow also didn't participate in Saturday's team scrimmage, and head coach Nick Nurse said he's been "in and out" over the last few days. With Philadelphia thin in the frontcourt due to injuries to Adem Bona (foot) and Tacko Fall (hip), Barlow could see opportunities at center once he's available.

items.headline: The 76ers picked up Barlow's team option Monday, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: This was a no-brainer for the 76ers for $3.42 million. Barlow is coming off a career-best season, posting averages of 7.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals in 23.8 minutes per game over 71 regular-season games (59 starts).

items.headline: Barlow produced five points (2-3 FG, 1-1 FT), one rebound and one assist in 15 minutes during Sunday's 144-114 loss to the Knicks in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Barlow put forth a quality campaign for the 76ers in 2025-26, averaging a career-high 7.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.9 steals in 23.8 minutes per tilt over 71 regular-season games (59 starts). His contract includes a $3.42 million team option for 2026-27, and it would make sense if Philadelphia brought Barlow back as a key reserve piece in the frontcourt for 2026-27.

items.headline: Barlow finished with six points (3-3 FG), two rebounds, one steal and two blocks across 16 minutes in Wednesday's 108-102 loss to New York in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
items.story: Joel Embiid (hip, ankle) didn't suit up Wednesday night, but Barlow logged only three more minutes than he did in Game 1. While the 22-year-old didn't do much on the offensive end, he still got involved defensively, amassing two blocks and one steal. With Embiid uncertain for Game 3 on Friday night, Barlow may have an opportunity to continue to see more action. However, even if Embiid misses another game, Barlow will still be tough to trust for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Barlow (coach's decision) didn't receive any playing time Thursday in the 76ers' 106-93 win over the Celtics in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Quarterfinals series.
items.story: A starter for Philadelphia for most of the campaign, Barlow shifted to the bench late in the regular season but didn't notice a dramatic drop in minutes. His playing time has fallen by the wayside in the playoffs, however, with Barlow being a casualty of head coach Nick Nurse trimming down his rotation to eight players. Barlow has now gone unused in two of the first six games of the series and has played single-digit minutes in two of his four appearances.

items.headline: Barlow is not in the starting lineup for Saturday's game against the Pistons, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Barlow will play off the bench for the first time since Jan. 29, as the Sixers have elected to go with Kelly Oubre and Paul George at the forward spots. Barlow is averaging 5.9 points and 4.1 rebounds per game when deployed off the bench this season, but he's been a regular starter throughout the campaign -- he's been part of the second unit in just seven of his 66 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

items.headline: Barlow finished with seven points (3-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, one assist and three blocks in 26 minutes during Friday's 115-103 victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Barlow grabbed double-digit rebounds for just the fourth time this season and also matched his season high in blocks. Although these numbers almost certainly helped fantasy managers, the excitement levels should remain tempered. In seven games over the past two weeks, he has averaged just 4.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 18.8 minutes per game.

items.headline: Barlow posted three points (1-1 FG, 1-2 FT) and two rebounds in 15 minutes during Saturday's 118-114 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Barlow hung onto the starting spot at power forward despite the return of Kelly Oubre on Saturday, though that could change once the latter becomes further removed from his elbow injury. Over his last 10 games, Barlow has averaged a modest 7.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.9 blocks in 23.9 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Barlow (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Barlow exited Saturday's contest early due to a left ankle sprain, and it initially looked unlikely he'd suit up Monday, though the forward has progressed well and has now been cleared to play. The 22-year-old was averaging 10.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.0 steals in 28.2 minutes over his previous five contests prior to Saturday's brief appearance. Barlow has started 53 of the 60 games he's played and hasn't come off the bench when healthy since January, so he figures to slot into the starting five as usual against the Thunder.

items.headline: Barlow (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Barlow was previously listed as doubtful, but he's trending in the right direction. With so many injuries in Philadelphia, Barlow could see a sizable workload if he's given the green light to play.

items.headline: Barlow (ankle) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against Oklahoma City.
items.story: Barlow exited Saturday's 126-116 win over Utah after only four minutes of work because of a sprained left ankle. If he can't suit up, Trendon Watford would be considered the favorite to start at power forward against one of the top defensive clubs in the Association.

items.headline: Barlow was diagnosed with a left ankle sprain and has been ruled out for the remainder of Saturday's game against the Jazz, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports. He finished with one point (1-2 FT) and two rebounds in four minutes.
items.story: Barlow checked out of the game with 8:19 remaining in the first quarter to get his ankle evaluated and was quickly shut down for the rest of the night. The severity of the ankle sprain won't be known until he undergoes further testing, but Barlow would appear to be at risk of missing the 76ers' next game Monday versus the Thunder.

items.headline: Barlow finished with 11 points (4-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, two assists and three steals across 21 minutes during Sunday's 109-103 victory over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: With Paul George still suspended until the March 25 matchup versus the Bulls, it looks like Barlow has a clear runway to a starting role for at least Philadelphia's next four games. Barlow has averaged 8.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 1.1 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.9 blocks in 26.5 minutes per tilt in his last seven games, shooting 52.1 percent from the field.

items.headline: Barlow racked up four points (2-5 FG), one rebound, two assists and one block over 26 minutes during Saturday's 125-116 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Barlow is holding down the fort at power forward for the suspended Paul George, but the former continues to see little usage in the starting lineup. Barlow has averaged 5.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.9 blocks in 24.8 minutes per game over his last nine contests, so fantasy managers may be able to find more appealing streaming options.

items.headline: Barlow (undisclosed) has checked back in to Tuesday's game against the Spurs, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow went to the locker room during the first quarter after picking up an undisclosed injury, but he's since been cleared by the medical staff to return. He shouldn't face any limitations the rest of the way.

items.headline: Barlow exited to the locker room during the first quarter of Tuesday's game against the Spurs with an undisclosed injury, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow was spotted walking down the tunnel to the locker room after picking up his second foul. The nature of his injury is unclear at this time. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Barlow finished with 14 points (4-7 FG, 6-8 FT), eight rebounds, one assist and three steals over 28 minutes during Sunday's 114-98 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: As long as Paul George remains suspended, Barlow appears to be locked into the starting position at power forward. However, the fourth-year forward is averaging just 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 0.9 blocks in 27.0 minutes per game over his last seven outings, so he's not seeing a lot of usage in the first unit.

items.headline: Barlow chipped in nine points (4-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal across 31 minutes during Thursday's 124-117 win over the Heat.
items.story: This was another quiet showing for Barlow, but the minutes were at least encouraging -- he's been playing more while Paul George is serving his suspension. Over his last five games, Barlow is averaging 5.4 points and 3.2 rebounds in 26.1 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Barlow finished Thursday's 117-107 loss to the Hawks with one point (0-3 FG, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, three blocks and one steal in 22 minutes.
items.story: Barlow had quite the dud Thursday, but Trendon Watford wasn't much better off the bench for the 76ers. With Joel Embiid (knee, shin) sidelined, it was Kelly Oubre, Andre Drummond and Adem Bona who stepped up the most for Philadelphia.

items.headline: Barlow produced 13 points (6-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt), four rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 138-89 loss to the Knicks.
items.story: With Paul George suspended until late March, Barlow has a clear runway to the starting job at power forward for the next month and a half or so. Barlow has delivered fairly quality numbers when part of the first unit, averaging 11.6 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 26.6 minutes per game while shooting 55.9 percent from the floor over his last eight contests as a starter.

items.headline: Barlow (illness) will play Wednesday versus the Knicks, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
items.story: Joel Embiid (knee) will skip Wednesday's game, so Barlow could see some more shots and minutes falling his way in his return from a one-game absence. Barlow is averaging 8.4 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.0 steals and 0.6 blocks per game this season.

items.headline: Barlow (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Barlow was a late addition to the injury report prior to Monday night's game against Portland, and he was ultimately downgraded to out. He's in jeopardy of missing a second straight game due to illness after being added to the injury report as questionable for Wednesday's clash.

items.headline: Barlow (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Portland, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Barlow was a late addition to the injury report and will ultimately sit out Monday due to an undisclosed illness. With both he and Joel Embiid (knee) inactive, Philadelphia will be without its usual frontcourt starting duo, leaving Trendon Watford, Adem Bona and Andre Drummond as candidates to step into the starting five. Barlow's next chance to play will come Wednesday against New York.

items.headline: Barlow is questionable for Monday's game against the Trail Blazers due to illness.
items.story: Barlow is a late addition to the injury report, so the team will presumably wait to see if he can make it through warmups before commenting further on his availability. Trendon Watford and Adem Bona could be in the mix for a start if Barlow ultimately can't go.

items.headline: Barlow agreed to a standard contract with Philadelphia prior to Thursday's game against the Lakers, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow's availability for Thursday was previously in question as the team scrambled to fill out a 15-man roster, which would have allowed him to play while remaining on a two-way contract. However, the big man will be eligible to suit up against LA after putting pen to paper on a standard deal. Barlow has made three straight starts for Philly, averaging 14.7 points, 8.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1.7 steals during that brief stretch.

items.headline: Barlow's availability for Thursday's game against the Lakers is in question while the 76ers work to piece together a 15-man roster prior to the 10 p.m. ET tipoff, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
items.story: Barlow has spent all season as one of the 76ers' three two-way players, even though he's been a staple in the Philadelphia rotation when healthy and has started in 33 of his 40 appearances. While two-way players are eligible to be active for 50 games at the NBA level, teams aren't able to keep their two-way players active for more than 90 combined games when they have fewer than 15 players signed to standard contracts. The 76ers have already exhausted their 90-game, under-15 limit, so neither Barlow nor their other two-way players (Jabari Walker and MarJon Beauchamp) will be eligible to play until the team has 15 players signed to standard deals. In the aftermath of Thursday's trade deadline and after inking Charles Bassey and Patrick Baldwin to 10-day deals, the 76ers currently have 14 players signed to standard contracts. The 76ers could still convert Barlow or one of the other two-way players to standard contracts or sign another player outside of the organization to ensure that he can suit up against the Lakers.

items.headline: Barlow registered 26 points (10-16 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 5-5 FT), 16 rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block in 35 minutes during Monday's 128-113 win over the Clippers.
items.story: Barlow was one of three starters to reach the 20-point threshold and combined with Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey for 79 total points. This marks Barlow's first double-double since Nov. 28 and his second of the season through 39 games. He also set a new season high in rebounds, beating his previous best of 14 boards Dec. 4 against Golden State. Barlow is expected to be one of several players who will benefit from Paul George's (suspension) 25-game absence.

items.headline: Wilson finished Monday's 126-107 loss to the 76ers with 24 points (9-17 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and four steals across 34 minutes.
items.story: Wilson turned in an efficient effort, particularly from three-point range, finishing as the Bulls' leading scorer. The rookie No. 4 overall pick also tied for the team lead in rebounds and paced all players in steals, supplying multiple swipes for the fourth time in seven regular-season games. The 20-year-old has been impressive on both ends of the floor to begin his NBA career, reaching the 20-point threshold five times while recording at least three combined steals-plus-blocks in all seven outings.

items.headline: Wilson finished Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics with 23 points (7-16 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 3-6 FT), five rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal across 31 minutes.
items.story: Wilson impressed in his first NBA Cup game, leading the Bulls in scoring while reaching the 20-point threshold for the fourth time across six regular-season appearances. The rookie No. 4 overall pick also doubled his previous career high in three-pointers made after shooting 22.2 percent from deep in his previous five appearances. He made an impact on the defensive end as well, matching the game-high mark in blocks. Wilson has yet to record fewer than three combined steals-plus-blocks in a game this season.

items.headline: Wilson finished with 20 points (7-18 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block over 38 minutes in Wednesday's 133-127 loss to New York.
items.story: Wilson's solid inaugural campaign continued Wednesday, with the rookie reaching the 20-point mark for the third time in his young career. While the 20-year-old has certainly been a steady offensive contributor, he's also shined defensively and now has nine steals in his first five professional appearances.

items.headline: Wilson closed with 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), five rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal across 32 minutes in Monday's 134-99 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Wilson didn't deliver his most efficient performance, particularly from three-point range, though he still finished as the Bulls' second-leading scorer. The rookie No. 4 overall pick also had a productive outing on the defensive end, racking up at least three combined steals-plus-blocks for the fourth time in as many regular-season appearances thus far. He also has yet to score fewer than 16 points and has reached the 20-point mark twice on the campaign.

items.headline: Wilson tallied 30 points (10-24 FG, 1-9 3Pt, 9-11 FT), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 38 minutes in Saturday's 124-120 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: After dropping 21 points in Friday's win over Milwaukee, Wilson erupted for a game-high 30 points in the second half of this back-to-back set, though he did struggle from beyond the arc. The rookie forward also tied for the game-high mark in rebounds. He's the first player since Terry Cummings in 1982-83 to record at least 30 points and 14 rebounds in one of his first three career games, per the broadcast.

items.headline: Wilson produced 21 points (7-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and three turnovers across 33 minutes in Friday's 132-125 win over the Bucks.
items.story: Wilson did a much better job of picking his spots offensively and limiting his turnovers in his second NBA game, while coming through with some game-saving plays on defense in the closing seconds of regulation. Additionally, after shooting just 33.3 percent from the free-throw line in Summer League, he's converted 75 percent of his freebies through the first two games of the regular season.

items.headline: Wilson recorded 16 points (7-21 FG, 1-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, three steals and one block over 32 minutes in Wednesday's 135-92 season-opening loss to the Raptors.
items.story: While the counting stats were nice, the rookie did not score efficiently and also finished with a game-high nine turnovers. Poor shooting and turnover issues tend to come with rookies, but Wilson will need to do a better job of taking care of the rock in Friday's game in Milwaukee.

items.headline: Wilson finished with 16 points (7-15 FG, 2-5 3Pt), seven rebounds, four assists and two blocks across 23 minutes in Friday's 133-116 preseason victory over the Timberwolves.
items.story: Wilson had another strong showing Friday, leading the Bulls in points while picking up his fifth consecutive preseason double-digit scoring performance. The 2026 No. 4 overall pick will be thrust into a meaningful role immediately, so his name could be mentioned often in Rookie of the Year conversations throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Wilson posted 10 points (4-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal over 24 minutes in Wednesday's 125-104 preseason victory against the Bucks.
items.story: Wilson received another opportunity to work with Chicago's starting unit but struggled with his outside shot, missing four of five attempts from beyond the arc. The rookie forward also committed four turnovers, highlighting some growing pains despite his contributions across several categories. He'll look to build on his preseason experience as he adjusts to the NBA level.

items.headline: Wilson played 25 minutes in Sunday's 133-128 preseason loss to the Nuggets, scoring 17 points (6-10 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-7 FT) and adding five assists, four rebounds and a block.
items.story: The rookie led Chicago's starting five in minutes and points, although he also committed a game-high five turnovers. Through three exhibition contests, Wilson is averaging 28.7 minutes, 17.7 points, 3.7 boards, 2.3 assists and 2.0 threes while shooting 47.6 percent from the floor and 31.6 percent from beyond the arc, as he prepares for a significant role in the rotation to begin his NBA career.

items.headline: Wilson finished Friday's 104-100 preseason loss to the Grizzlies with 21 points (7-17 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 2-6 FT), four rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes.
items.story: Wilson struggled to get going in the first half, during which he scored one point while shooting 0-for-2 from the field in 16 minutes. However, he erupted for 20 points and shot 5-for-10 from downtown in the second half, finishing with a game-high 21 points. The rookie No. 4 overall pick has led the Bulls in scoring in both of their preseason games, totaling 36 points, seven rebounds, two assists and two steals over 61 minutes.

items.headline: Wilson scored a team-high 15 points (6-15 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT) while contributing three rebounds, two assists and a steal over 29 minutes in Wednesday's preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: The Bulls got balanced scoring up and down the lineup, as six different players delivered 13 or more points, but Wilson's 15 led the way. The fourth overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft is set to be Chicago's starting power forward Opening Night, and while his willingness to chuck it up from long range is encouraging for his long-term fantasy outlook, it's likely to be a drag on his scoring efficiency as a rookie.

items.headline: Wilson is acclimating to NBA practices, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.
items.story: "Honestly, my first two days, it seemed like everything was moving so fast because you're going against NBA talent and everybody's athletic, and the gaps close really fast. But now, it's way more chill. [Friday] was a really good day for me," Wilson said. After Wilson was selected by the Bulls with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, the rookie forward is expected to be thrust into a big role immediately and is being treated as a mid-round player in most fantasy drafts.

items.headline: George produced seven points (3-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt) and seven rebounds over 22 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: George endured a frustrating performance, shooting just 25 percent from the field while failing to record an assist or defensive statistic. He also finished with a team-worst minus-30 rating as Utah dropped its fifth consecutive game. With rookie Darryn Peterson handling a significant share of the playmaking duties, George's offensive role and playing time warrant monitoring.

items.headline: George finished Wednesday's 117-111 overtime loss to San Antonio with 31 points (11-27 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 4-4 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 37 minutes.
items.story: George carried a substantial offensive workload, leading Utah in scoring while knocking down five three-pointers. Although he struggled with efficiency inside the arc and committed five turnovers, his willingness to shoulder significant scoring responsibilities remains promising for fantasy managers. His combination of scoring volume and perimeter shooting gives him considerable upside.

items.headline: George totaled 24 points (7-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 8-10 FT), nine rebounds, 10 assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: George fell just one rebound shy of nabbing his first career triple-double, and he's now dished out 10 assists in back-to-back games. However, he's also committed 12 turnovers over that two-game stretch.

items.headline: George accumulated 19 points (6-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-6 FT), one rebound, 10 assists and one steal over 32 minutes during Friday's 120-119 win over New Orleans.
items.story: The points and dimes were nice, but George also committed a game-high six turnovers and missed two of his free-throw attempts. Through the first two games of the season, George is shooting 61.5 percent at the charity stripe, but that number will assuredly improve for the 85.4 percent career free-throw shooter.

items.headline: George tallied 22 points (7-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 4-7 FT), five assists, three rebounds and one steal across 29 minutes in Wednesday's 123-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: George delivered an efficient shooting performance from beyond the arc, though it wasn't enough to help the Jazz secure a win in their regular-season opener. The 22-year-old point guard also led Utah in assists, finishing as the only Utah player to dish out more than three dimes. George is coming off a career year in 2025-26, and he should remain one of the team's top offensive options despite the addition of Darryn Peterson.

items.headline: George closed with 13 points (5-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three steals, two rebounds and one assist across 16 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over the Spurs.
items.story: George fared well in his limited action, finishing as one of seven Jazz players to score in double figures. After failing to record a steal in his first two preseason appearances, the 22-year-old made his presence felt defensively with three swipes Monday. George will look to take another step forward during the 2026-27 campaign after breaking out with averages of 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals across 54 games last season.

items.headline: George produced 15 points (5-8 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and three assists over 21 minutes in Sunday's 109-97 preseason win over the Nuggets.
items.story: George briefly exited the game after taking a blow to the face, but he returned a short while later and didn't seem any worse for the wear. George will look to take another step forward in Year 4 after breaking out with averages of 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, 2.5 triples and 1.1 steals per game last season.

items.headline: George and the Jazz agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million contract extension Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.
items.story: The writing was on the wall for this move a long time ago, as there was a lot of mutual interest to get this done quickly. George averaged 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 33.1 minutes per contest during the 2025-26 regular season, and moving forward he'll get to play alongside No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson in a new-look backcourt.

items.headline: The Jazz selected Darryn Peterson with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, adding another high-level creator to their backcourt that already includes George (hamstring).
items.story: George remains an important piece of Utah's rebuilding effort, but Peterson's arrival could reduce his on-ball responsibilities after he served as one of the team's primary playmakers last season. The additional talent should improve the quality of George's opportunities, though his fantasy value may become more dependent on efficiency than volume. The Jazz are also projected to be much more competitive in 2026-27, bolstering their late-season outlook.

items.headline: George (hamstring) will remain sidelined for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Lakers.
items.story: A hamstring injury caused George to miss 15 consecutive games to end the campaign. However, it was an excellent third season for the talented guard, as he averaged 23.6 points, 6.1 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 33.1 minutes per contest.

items.story: George went down with a hamstring injury during Wednesday's game against the Trail Blazers, and it'll cost him at least another two weeks. Isaiah Collier figures to hold down the starting point guard job until George returns to health.

items.story: George suffered a right hamstring strain during Wednesday's loss to the Knicks, so it's not surprising at all to see him hit the sidelines for Thursday's game. Given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries, partnered with Utah's desire to try and keep their top-8 protected pick in the upcoming draft, this is something that could turn into a multi-game absence for George. Isaiah Collier will be the primary beneficiary while George is out.

items.headline: George has been ruled out for the remainder of Wednesday's game against the Knicks due to a right hamstring injury. He recorded 14 points (6-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five assists, two rebounds and one steal over 20 minutes prior to departing.
items.story: George checked out of the game with 5:47 left in the third quarter and was quickly ruled out for the rest of the contest. Though the severity of George's injury won't be known until he undergoes further testing, even mild hamstring strains often result in multi-game absences for players. With that in mind, George should be viewed as unlikely to play in Utah's next contest Friday in Portland. Isaiah Collier would be the next man up to start at point guard if George misses time.

items.headline: George went back to the locker room during Wednesday's game against the Knicks with an apparent hamstring injury, Steve Popper of Newsday reports.
items.story: George went to block a shot by Karl-Anthony Towns and immediately grabbed at his hamstring area before departing the contest. While he's sidelined, look for Isaiah Collier to take over point guard duties, while Elijah Harkless could see some additional playing time.

items.story: George will play through an illness for a second straight game. The talented young guard played just 24 minutes last time out, so it's possible he'll have his minutes limited once again Wednesday. If that's the case, Isaiah Collier would likely see a bump in playing time.

items.headline: George has an illness and is questionable for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: George was a very late addition to the injury report, which is an ominous sign in fantasy hoops. Additionally, Isaiah Collier (illness) is also questionable. If the Jazz err on the side of caution, more minutes could be available for Elijah Harkless and Cody Williams.

items.headline: George finished with 22 points (4-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 12-13 FT), two rebounds and four assists over 29 minutes during Saturday's 113-99 loss to Milwaukee.
items.story: George had a woeful shooting performance in this game, but the fact that he went 12-for-13 from the charity stripe salvaged his outing from a scoring perspective. The electric floor general was returning from a one-game absence after sitting out the win over the Wizards on Thursday, and this was the third straight game in which he recorded at least 20 points.

items.headline: George (ankle) is off the injury report ahead of Saturday's game against the Bucks.

George has scored 30-plus points in back-to-back outings while connecting on 52.2 percent of his field-goal attempts (including 45.0 percent from three on 10.0 3PA/G).

items.headline: George is out for Thursday's game against the Wizards due to right ankle injury management.

Isaiah Collier should draw the start at point guard versus Washington, and he's averaging 14.5 points, 8.6 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 31.4 minutes per contest in 15 games as a starter this season.

items.headline: George finished Wednesday's 106-102 loss to the 76ers with 30 points (10-24 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), four rebounds, two assists and one steal over 30 minutes.
items.story: George propelled the Jazz's offense during Wednesday's loss, with 15 of his game-high 30 points coming in the third quarter. It was the eighth time this season that the third-year pro connected on at least five three-pointers. George has scored 30-plus points in back-to-back games and appears to be fully recovered from the right ankle sprain that cost him six straight games in February. That said, his playing time could be restricted for the second leg of the Jazz's back-to-back set against the Wizards on Thursday.

items.headline: George provided 36 points (14-22 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-5 FT), two rebounds, two assists and four steals in 30 minutes during Monday's 128-125 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: George enjoyed his 12th game of the year with at least 30 points Monday. The star guard's workload increased in his second contest back from an ankle sprain, which is an encouraging sign. Over his last 10 appearances, George has averaged 24.7 points, 4.6 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 31.4 minutes per game.

There is going to be a ramp-up period, which does limit his short-term upside. However, he is a clear must-roster player, given the fact that Charlotte will need him to play a major role following the offseason departure of LaMelo Ball.

Dennis Schroder and Christian Anderson will likely continue seeing increased burn until White returns.

items.headline: White said Monday that he wanted to return to the Hornets to take on the challenge of a new role, and he's "excited" for the road ahead, Owen O'Connor of SI.com reports.
items.story: After trading away LaMelo Ball, the Hornets signed White to a three-year, $74 million deal this offseason. The veteran guard was traded from Chicago to Charlotte last February and provided a spark off the bench for the Hornets in 2025-26, though he's now expected to step into a starting role. In 21 regular-season games with Charlotte last season, he averaged 15.6 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists across 19.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: White will sign a three-year, $74 million contract with the Hornets, Shams Charania of ESPN reports on Thursday.
items.story: The Hornets will quickly lock up White after trading away starting point guard LaMelo Ball to Minnesota earlier in the day. White becomes the starter by default in Charlotte and is likely to see a big uptick in fantasy appeal. In 21 regular-season appearances for Charlotte in 2025-26, White averaged 17.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.3 three-pointers in 25.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Retaining White will be a priority for the Hornets this offseason, Bobby Marks of ESPN reports.
items.story: White will be free to test the open market in the offseason, although Charlotte will look re-sign him. After trading for White ahead of the deadline, Charlotte inherited his Bird rights, enabling the team to exceed the salary cap to retain him. Considering the club will be operating well below the luxury tax while possessing three trade exceptions valued at a combined $17.5 million, Marks added that the franchise is in a "strong position" to keep the former Bull on the roster. White appeared in 21 regular-season contests for the Hornets after being acquired from Chicago -- all off the bench -- averaging 15.6 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists while shooting 39.1 percent from deep in those appearances. It's unknown what his role would be if he remained with the organization. However, his biggest issue in the last few seasons has been his inability to stay healthy.

items.headline: White finished Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to Orlando with four points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) over 17 minutes.
items.story: White had easily his worst game as a Hornet, contributing to what ended up being a blowout loss. Despite averaging 15.3 points, 2.9 assists and 2.1 three-pointers in 23 games after joining Charlotte, it's safe to say that White's overall fantasy appeal took a large hit following the trade. Looking ahead to next season, White could struggle to be more than a stream-level asset, assuming his role remains largely unchanged.

items.story: White is nursing left groin soreness, but the issue isn't expected to stop him from playing Tuesday. The combo guard has scored in double figures in 12 consecutive appearances, during which White has averaged 17.9 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.3 three-pointers in 20.3 minutes per game.

items.headline: White contributed 19 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 20 minutes during Thursday's 127-107 win over the Suns.
items.story: White continues to put up solid numbers off the bench for the Hornets, and this was his 10th consecutive game in which he scored in double digits. Over that 10-game stretch, White is averaging 18.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. White remains a valuable fantasy contributor in most formats due to his scoring prowess, and his involvement on offense is more important than how many minutes he plays.

items.headline: White supplied 16 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), two rebounds and five assists in 21 minutes during Tuesday's 117-86 win over the Nets.
items.story: Despite some inconsistent shooting, White continues to provide Charlotte with valuable production off the bench. He has scored in double digits in nine straight games while also chipping in across other categories, most notably assists and threes. While he isn't a must-roster player, he certainly isn't out of place on a standard-league roster.

items.headline: White logged 17 points (6-13 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 23 minutes during the Hornets' 114-103 win over the Knicks on Thursday.
items.story: White helped the Hornets establish a double-digit lead going into halftime by scoring 12 of his 17 points through the first two quarters of Thursday's game. The veteran guard has been a key contributor off the bench for Charlotte and has scored at least 17 points in five of his last six outings. Over that six-game span, White has averaged 20.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 3.0 threes over 21.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: White collected 27 points (9-12 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and one assist in 18 minutes during Tuesday's 134-90 victory over the Kings.
items.story: White scored 16 of his 27 points in the first half, which included four treys. He provided an undeniable spark off the bench on the way to a blowout win, leading the Hornets in scoring despite being held under 20 minutes. The 26-year-old is averaging 21.6 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 3.4 made triples per game over his last five appearances.

items.headline: White posted 27 points (7-13 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 8-8 FT), five assists and three rebounds over 23 minutes during the Hornets' 130-111 win over the Magic on Thursday.
items.story: White got extra run in the fourth quarter due to the Hornets' large lead, and the veteran guard took advantage of the extra playing time by scoring 12 of his team-high 27 points in the frame. He has scored 51 points over his last two games, connecting on 53.6 percent of his field-goal attempts while going 8-for-17 (47.1 percent) from three-point range in that span. White gives the Hornets a much-needed scoring punch off the bench, especially when LaMelo Ball, Kon Knueppel or Brandon Miller are off the floor.

items.headline: White supplied 24 points (8-15 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and three assists in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 136-106 win over the Heat.
items.story: White seems to have settled into a steady bench role with the Hornets, as he's logged at least 20 minutes with the second unit in six of his last seven appearances since the trade and after overcoming a nagging calf problem. He's averaging 15.4 points, 2.7 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game over that span, and while those aren't eye-popping numbers, they're certainly solid contributions considering he's averaging 20.6 minutes per game over that stretch.

items.headline: White accumulated 18 points (7-15 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal over 26 minutes during Saturday's 115-102 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: White chipped in across the board, providing the Hornets with solid contributions on both ends of the floor. This was arguably his best performance since returning from injury, scoring at least 15 points for just the second time in his past five outings while matching a season high with three combined steals-plus-blocks. Despite the effort, White remains a stream-level player in most standard formats, particularly for those needing points and threes.

items.headline: White (heel) is available for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: A bruised heel won't stop White from playing Saturday, but he remains difficult to trust in fantasy lineups with his workload limitations. Over his first seven games for the Hornets, the star guard has averaged 11.9 points, 3.6 assists and 2.3 rebounds in 18.6 minutes per contest.

items.headline: White (heel) is probable for Saturday's game in San Antonio.
items.story: White is dealing with a bruised heel, but it appears he plans to push through it. Check back for official confirmation on White's status closer to Saturday's tipoff.

items.headline: White logged nine points (3-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 117-109 win over Sacramento.
items.story: White was back in the rotation after missing the previous game as part of his injury management. It's been a tough slog for White since arriving in Charlotte, averaging 11.9 points, 3.6 assists and 1.4 three-pointers in seven games over the past month. At best, fantasy managers should view him as a potential streamer for both points and threes.

items.headline: White (calf) is cleared to play Wednesday against the Kings.
items.story: White missed the front end of the back-to-back set, but he's all set to return to the rotation. Through six appearances for Charlotte, he's averaging 12.3 points, 4.0 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 three-pointers in 18.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: White has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Trail Blazers due to left calf injury management.
items.story: White has played in three straight games for the Hornets, but he'll take a seat for the first half of Charlotte's back-to-back. Tre Mann could be in line for more chances in the backcourt in White's absence. If all goes according to plan, White should be a full go for Wednesday in Sacramento.

items.headline: George ended Monday's 103-94 victory over the Magic with 22 points (9-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 0-1 FT), four rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal in 37 minutes.
items.story: George delivered an efficient all-around performance, finishing second on Washington in scoring while leading the team with four three-pointers. His five assists and contributions in both defensive categories further enhanced his fantasy output. George's ability to produce alongside Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa is particularly encouraging, though the Wizards' crowded offensive hierarchy could lead to fluctuations in his scoring opportunities.

items.headline: The Wizards exercised the fourth-year team option on George on Sunday, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Washington selected George 24th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft. Since then, the 22-year-old has appeared in 122 regular-season games, averaging 11.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.8 blocks in 27.7 minutes per contest. Even with the Wizards' selection of AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick in 2026, George continues to start and remains a key piece of the organization's future.

items.headline: George racked up eight points (4-10 FG, 0-4 3Pt), two rebounds, 11 assists and one block in 38 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: George handed out a season-high 11 assists, making amends for what was a passive offensive night. Despite the debut of AJ Dybantsa, George logged a whopping 38 minutes, an encouraging sign for anyone rostering him. It appears as though Washington is fully invested in him moving forward, with foul issues seemingly his only stumbling block when it comes to playing time.

items.headline: George finished with 22 points (8-17 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 6-8 FT), nine rebounds, five assists and four blocks over 36 minutes in Saturday's 124-120 win over the Bulls.
items.story: After committing a career-high eight turnovers in Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors, George did a much better job of taking care of the rock Saturday, limiting his giveaways to three. He's gotten off to a solid start with averages of 17.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.7 blocks per game, although those numbers could dip once AJ Dybantsa (ankle) gets into the mix.

items.headline: George finished with 11 points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals over 26 minutes during Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: George couldn't take care of the basketball Friday, with the third-year pro responsible for eight of the Wizards' 20 turnovers. He also had a poor shooting night, although his work at the charity stripe was enough for him to finish in a tie with Bilal Coulibaly for the third-most points on Washington behind Trae Young (22) and Tre Johnson (20). George will have his off nights as the third option on the Wizards behind Young and Anthony Davis.

items.headline: George had 18 points (8-14 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal across 29 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 win over Milwaukee.
items.story: George was aggressive on offense, finishing second on the team in shot attempts behind Anthony Davis in the win. He also committed a team-high four turnovers, but overall, it was a solid debut for the third-year swingman. This was Washington's first season-opening win since 2022.

items.headline: George logged 14 points (5-7 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks over 27 minutes during Friday's 107-106 preseason loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: George put together another efficient night, making five of his seven shots while chipping in on the defensive end. His preseason numbers make a strong case for a full-time starting role for him when the regular season begins.

items.headline: George produced 21 points (6-7 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 6-6 FT), one rebound, four assists and three steals over 25 minutes in Monday's 131-119 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: George was dialed in, missing only one shot while he was out there, and he was one of the few Washington players to finish with a positive plus-minus rating. George showed some impressive flashes last season, but he may struggle to assert himself in the offense when working alongside Trae Young, Anthony Davis, AJ Dybantsa and Alex Sarr.

items.headline: George registered 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt), seven rebounds, five assists and a block across 22 minutes in Thursday's 111-109 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: George contributed across multiple categories, finishing tied for second on the team in rebounds and leading Washington in assists. George also showed his well-known ability to stretch the floor, and he was one of four Wizards who drained multiple threes in this win. The third-year guard looks penciled in to open the 2026-27 regular season as the Wizards' starting shooting guard, and his combination of playmaking, rebounding and perimeter shooting makes him an intriguing fantasy contributor.

items.headline: George (elbow) finished with nine points (4-8 FG, 1-5 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist in 21 minutes for Canada in Friday's 110-84 World Cup Qualifiers win over Puerto Rico.
items.story: George missed the end of the 2025-26 regular season with a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow, but he's since been deemed 100 percent. The Wizards are noticeably deeper heading into 2026-27, as Anthony Davis (finger) is expected to be healthy, and the team drafted AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

items.headline: George's (elbow) role becomes less certain after Washington added another high-upside wing prospect in AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: George displayed intriguing playmaking ability and positional versatility during his sophomore campaign. However, the Wizards now possess considerable depth on the wing, including fellow talented youngsters Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly. George is currently penciled into the starting lineup, but his offensive opportunities may fluctuate depending on lineup combinations. The Wizards also just re-signed Trae Young (quadriceps) and will be welcoming Anthony Davis (finger) to the mix.

items.headline: George (elbow) will miss the rest of the 2025-26 season, Chase Hughes of Monumental Sports Network reports.
items.story: George has been sidelined since March 2 due to a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow, and the Wizards had no incentive to rush him back to the court for the last couple of weeks. The forward appeared in 48 regular-season contests with averages of 14.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.1 three-pointers on 43.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: George (elbow) is out for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: George has been sidelined since March 2 due to a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow. The team has yet to provide much of an update on his timeline for a return, and there doesn't seem to be much sense in rushing him back for the final few games of the regular season. George can be considered doubtful for Saturday's game in Miami until further notice.

items.headline: The Wizards said Wednesday that George (elbow) will be re-evaluated in one week, at which point an update for his rest-of-season status will be provided, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: George is dealing with a Grade 2 distal UCL tear in his left elbow, an issue that has kept him sidelined since March 3.  The Wizards are planning to take a conservative approach with George, so it wouldn't be surprising for next week's update to rule George out for the season. While George has been out, Will Riley and Jamir Watkins have taken on larger roles. The Wizards have six regular-season games after George's set re-evaluation date of April 1.

items.headline: The Wizards announced Wednesday that George has been diagnosed with a partial tear of the UCL in his left elbow and will be re-evaluated in three weeks.
items.story: George sustained the injury in Monday's loss to Houston and won't return until late March at the very earliest. With the Wizards sitting at 16-45 on the season, it wouldn't be surprising to see the club exercise extreme caution with the second-year wing for the remainder of the season. With George sidelined, Will Riley, Jamir Watkins (ankle) and Justin Champagnie are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: George (elbow) is out for Thursday's game against Utah.
items.story: A sprained left elbow is resulting in a second consecutive absence for George. Will Riley should draw his fifth career start at small forward Thursday, making him a worthwhile streaming option in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: George (elbow) is listed out for Tuesday's game against Orlando.
items.story: George sprained his left elbow in the third quarter of Monday's loss to the Rockets and will need at least one game off to recover from the injury. With Jamir Watkins (ankle/foot) also sidelined for the second leg of the back-to-back, the Wizards are likely to lean on Will Riley, Tre Johnson, Jaden Hardy and Bilal Coulibaly as their primary options on the wing.

items.headline: George didn't return to Monday's 123-118 loss to the Rockets after exiting with 6:13 left in the third quarter due to a left elbow sprain. He finished with 16 points (5-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two assists, one rebound and one steal in 22 minutes.
items.story: George had been listed as questionable heading into Monday's contest due to a left knee contusion, but it was a new injury that knocked him out of the game early. The second-year wing was later spotted sitting on the bench following a trip to the locker room, but the Wizards didn't clear him to return to the contest. George can be considered questionable for Tuesday's game against the Magic until the team provides another update.

items.headline: George is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Rockets due to a left elbow sprain.
items.story: George was dealing with a knee injury leading up to tipoff, but he's now dealing with an elbow injury picked up at some point during Monday's clash. Will Riley would see more minutes down the stretch if George is unable to return.

items.headline: George (knee) is good to go for Monday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: George will shake off his questionable tag for the front end of this back-to-back set. His status for Tuesday against Orlando could be up in the air if the Wizards contemplate a maintenance day.

items.headline: George is questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets due to a left knee contusion.
items.story: George has been in and out of the lineup of late as he continues to nurse a left knee injury. He was limited to just 15 minutes during Saturday's loss to the Raptors and is officially listed as questionable for Monday's contest. If he is unable to go, Justin Champagnie and Will Riley could see increased minutes.

items.headline: Head coach Brian Keefe said George (knee) will operate under an unspecified minutes restriction in Saturday's game against the Raptors, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: George will return from a one-game absence due to a left knee contusion, though he isn't expected to see a full workload. The second-year swingman has yet to log more than 26 minutes in a game through eight February appearances, during which he has averaged 10.3 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 20.5 minutes per tilt.

items.headline: George (knee) is available for Saturday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: George was held out of Thursday's loss to the Hawks due to a left knee contusion, but the second-year pro has been cleared to return Saturday, which will likely result in Will Riley reverting to a bench role. George has averaged 10.3 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.0 threes and 0.8 blocks over 20.5 minutes per game in his last eight outings.

items.headline: George (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Raptors.
items.story: George is in jeopardy of missing a second straight outing due to a left knee contusion. He has appeared in five of Washington's last eight games, averaging 12.0 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 20.4 minutes per contest over that stretch. If he's ultimately ruled out, Will Riley (ankle), Jamir Watkins and Justin Champagnie would be candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: George (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Hawks.
items.story: George has frequently missed time for the Wizards, and his latest injury is a knee contusion. With George sidelined, the team is likely to lean more on Justin Champagnie and Will Riley.

items.headline: George is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Hawks due to a left knee contusion.
items.story: George may have picked up the injury during Washington's 119-98 loss to Atlanta on Tuesday, when he played 21 minutes and finished with 11 points (3-10 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds and two assists. Justin Champagnie figures to be the top candidate to enter the Wizards' starting lineup if George is unable to play in Thursday's rematch.

items.headline: George (toe) is available for Sunday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: George missed the second game of a back-to-back set Friday due to a toe injury, but he will return to the lineup Sunday. Over his last five appearances, George holds averages of 10.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 21.2 minutes per contest.

items.headline: George (toe) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Hornets.
items.story: George was held out of the Wizards' 131-118 win over the Pacers on Friday while managing a left toe sprain, but the second-year pro could be available for Washington on Sunday. He has averaged 15.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 1.7 threes, 1.1 steals and 0.9 blocks over 27.1 minutes per game over his last 15 outings.

items.headline: George has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Pacers due to a left big toe sprain.
items.story: After George finished with six points (3-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt), three rebounds, two blocks and one assist across 19 minutes during Thursday's 112-105 win over the Pacers, the Wizards will hold him out for the second leg of a back-to-back set. With George sidelined, Justin Champagnie and Will Riley could be more involved after they played a combined four minutes Thursday.

items.headline: George supplied six points (3-10 FG, 0-3 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two blocks across 19 minutes during Thursday's 112-105 win over the Pacers.
items.story: George logged fewer than 25 minutes for the fifth time in his past six appearances, raising some doubt as to his overall fantasy appeal. Despite putting together what could be considered a breakout campaign, it appears as though George's playing time could be limited for the run home. For now, he warrants a roster spot in most leagues. However, managers will want to keep an eye on his minutes moving forward, as he could eventually become a disposable asset.

items.headline: George registered 17 points (4-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 8-8 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 138-113 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: George tallied double digits for the second straight game, although his playing time remains underwhelming. With Washington clearly shifting into tank mode, it appears as though George is not only going to miss games moving forward, but his playing time could be limited on most nights. While he does remain a must-roster player, managers are going to have to be prepared for some uncertainty.

items.headline: George (ankle) will play Wednesday against the Cavaliers.
items.story: Both George and Bilal Coulibaly (heel) will shake off questionable tags for this contest. George has been quiet in his six most recent outings with 12.2 points, 3.7 assists, 2.7 rebounds, 1.0 blocks and 1.3 three-pointers in 24.1 minutes per game.

items.headline: George (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
items.story: George sprained his left ankle during Sunday's game, and the issue could prevent him from missing Wednesday's contest. With Bilal Coulibaly (heel) also listed as questionable, the Wizards may have to lean on Jamir Watkins, Will Riley and Jaden Hardy.

items.headline: George has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game versus the Heat due to a left ankle sprain.
items.story: George tweaked his ankle, and with the Wizards down by 30-plus points entering the fourth quarter, they'll opt to hold out George for the remainder of the game. He'll end his afternoon with 13 points (4-12 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists, one block and two turnovers in 19 minutes.

items.headline: George (knee) will play Sunday against the Heat.
items.story: George is back after a one-game stint on the sidelines, so he should see his usual minutes as a starter Sunday. His return will likely send Will Riley back to the bench, and Keshon Gilbert's minutes could dip.

items.headline: George (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Miami.
items.story: George remains day-to-day after missing the front end of this back-to-back set Saturday against Brooklyn. Over his last six games, George has averaged 13.2 points, 4.0 assists, 3.8 rebounds, 1.2 steals, 1.2 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers.

items.headline: George (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
items.story: George will miss the front end of this back-to-back set due to a right knee contusion. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Miami. The Wizards will be extremely shorthanded against Brooklyn, meaning Will Riley, Jamir Watkins and Sharife Cooper should see increased playing time.

items.headline: George is questionable for Saturday's game against the Nets with a bruised right knee.
items.story: The Wizards are considering holding out a number of key players for the first half of their back-to-back set. Depending on who's available for Saturday's contest, Bub Carrington, Will Riley and Justin Champagnie appear to be in a favorable situation when it comes to added playing time.

items.headline: George closed Sunday's 116-112 win over the Kings with six points (3-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound, two assists and one block in 19 minutes.
items.story: This was a bizarre game for Washington with the team benching all their starters for most of the second half to close this game out. Bub Carrington and Bilal Coulibaly were the only starters to eclipse 20 minutes, and they barely did that. With the Wizards not playing for much, this could become a trend.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is active for Monday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Awaka was probable to suit up versus Philadelphia with a sprained left ankle, but he's going to play through it for the second straight contest. He'll provide center depth on the bench behind starter Jalen Smith (finger), although Awaka isn't expected to see much playing time.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
items.story: Awaka played 12 minutes during Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics after missing one game with the ankle issue. The rookie big man will continue to provide depth off the bench for the Bulls behind Jalen Smith.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is available for Friday's game in Boston.
items.story: The rookie big man is available off the bench for the Bulls on Friday. Awaka may not see significant playing time, though.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game in Boston.
items.story: Awaka continues to battle a left ankle sprain. The rookie big man could go through morning shootaround and pregame warmups before the Bulls update his status.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Knicks, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Awaka will hit the sidelines after tweaking his ankle during Monday's 134-99 loss to the Celtics. For now, he should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting in Boston.

items.headline: Awaka (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
