items.headline: Collier (illness) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Collier was unable to play against the Warriors on Monday due to an illness, and he missed the Jazz's prior game against the Bucks on Saturday while attending to a personal matter. The 2024 first-rounder is on track to return Wednesday, and he could start against New York if Keyonte George (illness) is unable to play.

items.headline: Collier (illness) is out for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Collier was unable to shake his questionable tag for this contest. Meanwhile, Keyonte George (illness) remains questionable. With this news, Elijah Harkless, Cody Williams and Svi Mykhailiuk could step into larger roles.

items.headline: Collier (illness) is questionable for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Both Collier and Keyonte George were late additions to the injury report due to illness. The Jazz could be very shorthanded, meaning players like Elijah Harkless, Cody Williams and Svi Mykhailiuk could step into larger roles.

items.headline: Collier (personal) isn't listed on the injury report for Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Collier missed Saturday's loss to Milwaukee due to personal reasons, though he's set to return to action Monday. Over his last five games (two starts), the second-year point guard has averaged 17.4 points, 7.2 assists, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 27.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Collier (personal) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
items.story: Collier will miss his first game since Nov. 5 for personal reasons, and his next opportunity to play will come Monday against Golden State. Elijah Harkless, Brice Sensabaugh and Svi Mykhailiuk are candidates for increased minutes due to Collier being sidelined.

items.headline: Collier had 27 points (11-18 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 4-6 FT), three rebounds and 11 assists across 29 minutes during Thursday's 122-112 victory over Washington.
items.story: Collier moved to the starting lineup due to the absence of Keyonte George (right ankle management), and he made the most of the opportunity. Three of Collier's games with at least 20 points have come off the bench this season, but he stood out in more areas than just scoring. This was also his 10th game with double-digit assists in 2025-26.

items.headline: Collier is in the Jazz's starting lineup against the Wizards on Thursday.
items.story: Keyonte George has been ruled out for Thursday's game due to right ankle injury management, so Collier will enter the starting lineup for the 16th time this season. Collier started in nine of the Jazz's first 10 games of February, and over that span he averaged 17.3 points, 9.7 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 steals over 33.7 minutes per game.

items.headline: Collier provided 18 points (5-10 FG, 8-8 FT), five assists, one block and three steals in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 106-102 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Collier gave the Jazz the spark off the bench that they needed during Wednesday's close loss, with the second-year pro leading the team with five dimes while finishing as Utah's second-leading scorer behind Keyonte George (30 points). Collier has taken on a larger role as the season has progressed, and since Feb. 1 he has averaged 17.1 points, 8.8 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 2.2 steals over 32.0 minutes per game in 13 outings (nine starts).

items.headline: Collier won't start Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: With Keyonte George (ankle) back in action, Collier will slide to the second unit. The second-year point guard has averaged 9.3 points, 6.7 assists, 2.4 rebounds and 0.9 steals in 23.3 minutes per game across 36 outings off the bench so far this season.

items.headline: Collier finished with 11 points (5-11 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, seven assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Thursday's 129-118 loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: It doesn't sound like the Jazz are in a rush to bring Keyonte George (ankle) back, extending Collier's runway in the first unit. Collier has started nine of his last 10 outings, averaging 17.3 points, 9.7 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 steals in 33.7 minutes per game during this stretch.

items.headline: Collier recorded 24 points (9-16 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds, five assists, two blocks and four steals across 25 minutes during Friday's 123-114 loss to Memphis.
items.story: Collier wreaked havoc on the defensive end, tying career highs in steals and blocks, and this was the fourth game of his career with at least four steals. Collier has been flirting with top-40 value over the past eight games with averages of 18.1 points, 10.9 dimes and 2.5 swipes per contest.

items.headline: Collier contributed 15 points (3-8 FG, 9-12 FT), two rebounds, nine assists and three steals in 36 minutes before fouling out of Thursday's 135-119 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Making his third straight start and sixth in seven February games while Keyonte George (ankle) remains sidelined, Collier just missed picking up his 10th double-double of the season. Four of those nine double-doubles have come this month, and he's averaging 17.3 points, 11.7 assists, 3.4 boards and 2.3 steals in February. The Jazz haven't been rushing George back into the lineup as they try to stay near the bottom of the standings, and the top of the lottery, so Collier's role won't necessarily shrink on the other side of the All-Star break.

items.headline: Collier provided 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt), one rebound, 14 assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 121-93 win over the Kings.
items.story: Collier turned in an efficient shooting performance, resulting in his 10th straight game in double figures. He's also been distributing the ball at a high level lately and has tallied a double-double in four of his last five matchups. Collier will continue to run the Utah offense until Keyonte George (ankle) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Collier is in the starting lineup for Monday's game against the Heat.
items.story: Collier came off the bench in Saturday's contest but will return to the starting lineup Monday with Keyonte George (ankle) inactive. Collier has started four of the Jazz's past 10 games, averaging 15.6 points, 9.5 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 31.8 minutes per contest during that stretch.

items.headline: Collier is not in the Jazz's starting lineup against the Magic on Saturday, Andy Larsen of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Collier was the starting point guard in the Jazz's last three games and put together some strong performances, including a 22-assist game against the Pacers on Tuesday and a 25-point double-double Thursday against the Hawks. Keyonte George (ankle) was cleared to return from a three-game absence but will be restricted to approximately 24 minutes, so Collier should continue to operate in an expanded role despite his demotion to the bench.

items.headline: Collier produced 25 points (11-22 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, 11 assists and three steals in 48 minutes during Thursday's 121-119 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Collier continues to see elite usage with Keyonte George (ankle) sidelined. The 22-year-old didn't miss a second of game action for a second straight appearance, and he piled on the production across the board yet again. He's now recorded a double-double in back-to-back games and set a new season high in rebounds Thursday.

items.headline: Peterson amassed 14 points (5-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists, three blocks and three steals across 33 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Peterson struggled with his overall efficiency but delivered an impressive defensive performance, combining for six steals and blocks while leading Utah with six assists. The rookie also logged a team-high 33 minutes and committed just one turnover despite handling substantial playmaking responsibilities. His ability to contribute across the board gives him considerable fantasy upside even when his shot isn't falling.

items.headline: Peterson amassed 16 points (6-15 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal across 36 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The 16 points led the Jazz on the afternoon, as only two of his teammates even scored in double digits. Peterson is quickly getting the hang of this NBA thing after being the second overall pick in the 2026 Draft, scoring at least 14 points in four of the last five games while averaging 14.2 points, 4.4 boards, 2.8 assists, 2.0 threes and 1.2 steals, but his 35.2 percent shooting during that stretch indicates he still has plenty to work on.

items.headline: Peterson provided 18 points (4-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 7-7 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Peterson struggled to find his rhythm from the field but compensated with three triples and a perfect showing at the charity stripe. The rookie displayed his scoring potential despite playing considerably fewer minutes than fellow starters Keyonte George and Ace Bailey. Peterson's perimeter shooting and ability to draw fouls should help support his fantasy value as he develops.

items.headline: Peterson (nose) started the second quarter of Wednesday's game against the Spurs, per the broadcast.
items.story: Peterson took a shot to the head and exited to the locker room with a bloody nose in the first quarter. However, he returned to the bench shortly thereafter and started the second quarter.

items.headline: Peterson exited to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to an apparent head injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: The rookie guard took a shot to the head on a dunk attempt and appeared to have a bloody nose. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Peterson finished with eight points (4-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 30 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Peterson was the only Jazz starter to have a positive plus-minus, despite his shot not falling. The second overall pick in the 2026 draft added four combined steals and blocks, representing his first tallies in each statistical category to begin his career. Through three outings, Peterson is averaging 10.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals in 30.3 minutes.

items.headline: Peterson amassed nine points (3-7 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and three assists across 31 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 loss to Memphis.
items.story: The No. 2 overall pick started at shooting guard in his first regular-season appearance, receiving the third-most minutes among Utah's starters. Peterson attempted just seven shots and struggled to establish himself offensively, but his substantial workload suggests the Jazz intend to give him considerable opportunities to develop. His scoring volume should increase as he becomes more comfortable alongside Keyonte George, Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson.

items.headline: Peterson recorded 13 points (4-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, six assists and a steal across 29 minutes in Friday's 119-116 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Peterson struggled with his shooting efficiency but made meaningful contributions elsewhere. The young guard finished tied for the team lead with six assists while collecting six rebounds, the second-best mark on the team, showcasing his versatility despite an inconsistent offensive performance. He also committed just one turnover in a team-high 29 minutes, an encouraging sign for his decision-making. Peterson's ability to contribute across multiple categories could help him earn a significant role in Utah's backcourt as the regular season approaches, and as a rookie on a rebuilding team, he'll be given every opportunity to log heavy minutes. He's expected to be the Jazz's starting shooting guard come Opening Night against the Grizzlies on Wednesday.

items.headline: Peterson produced 14 points (5-10 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five assists, two rebounds and one steal across 24 minutes in Monday's 119-109 preseason win over San Antonio.
items.story: Peterson put together a solid offensive effort, finishing as Utah's leading scorer in a well-rounded team victory. After a quiet three-point performance in his preseason debut Oct. 4, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft has fared much better in his two most recent appearances. The Kansas product is penciled in as the Jazz's starting shooting guard for the 2026-27 campaign.

items.headline: Peterson tallied 23 points (10-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-4 FT), three rebounds and three assists over 30 minutes in Tuesday's 93-79 preseason loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: With Lauri Markkanen (neck) out and Keyonte George and Jaren Jackson having their minutes monitored, Peterson got some time to shine as the main man on offense for the Jazz. Despite going 1-for-6 from three-point range, he still converted over 50 percent of his shot attempts, and it was nice to see him take 18 shots after attempting just five field goals in the preseason opener.

items.headline: Peterson accumulated three points (1-5 FG, 1-2 FT, 0-2 3Pt), six rebounds, two assists and one steal in 22 minutes during Sunday's 109-97 preseason victory over Denver.
items.story: Petersen made his NBA debut, sliding straight into the starting lineup, as expected. Although he struggled with his efficiency, the fact that he played a team-high 22 minutes is an encouraging sign. He should open the regular season as a key piece in the rotation, putting him firmly on the fantasy radar. As a rookie point guard, managers should expect some ups and downs when it comes to his shooting splits. However, his role alone should lend itself to plenty of opportunities, making him a viable target in the 100 range of drafts.

items.headline: Peterson has impressed veteran teammate Jusuf Nurkic with his maturity and work ethic during training camp, according to Jazz reporter Chandler Holt.
items.story: Nurkic said that in 13 NBA seasons he hasn't seen a player enter the league with Peterson's level of maturity, adding that the rookie spends so much time working that Utah has nearly had to tell him to stay out of the gym. Peterson is preparing for his first NBA season after being selected No. 2 overall in the 2026 NBA Draft and should have an opportunity to take on a substantial role immediately.

items.headline: Peterson (rest) is set to compete for a starting role during training camp in the fall.
items.story: The rookie No. 2 overall pick has Ace Bailey to overcome for the top spot at shooting guard with the Jazz. Whether he starts or comes off the bench right off the bat, Peterson is certainly primed for a significant role for Utah in 2026-27. Over five Summer League appearances, the 19-year-old stood out with averages of 23.0 points, 5.2 assists, 3.2 rebounds, 1.2 blocks and 1.0 steals per game.

items.headline: Peterson (rest) is out for Friday's Summer League game against Portland, per Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City.
items.story: Peterson is sitting out Utah's Summer League finale Friday. The rookie first-rounder is primed for a significant role with the Jazz in 2026-27.

items.headline: Peterson ended with 15 points (4-16 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 4-5 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 29 minutes in Wednesday's 94-82 Summer League loss to the Spurs.
items.story: After resting Monday, Peterson returned to action Wednesday but struggled to find his shot, finishing with his lowest scoring output of the summer. In his previous four appearances between the Salt Lake City and Las Vegas portions of the Summer League, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft had scored at least 20 points in each contest. Peterson figures to play a significant role from the outset of the 2026-27 regular season.

items.headline: Peterson (rest) is available to play in Wednesday's Summer League game against the Spurs, Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City reports.
items.story: After getting a maintenance day Monday, Peterson will be back in action. The rookie is averaging 22.3 points and 5.5 assists through four exhibitions.

items.headline: Peterson (rest) has been ruled out for Monday's Las Vegas Summer League game against the Bulls, Sarah Todd of The Deseret News reports.
items.story: Peterson will skip the second leg of a back-to-back set, but he should be back in action for Wednesday's game against the Spurs. With Peterson on the sidelines, Bez Mbeng could get some time to shine in a starting role.

items.headline: Peterson finished with 23 points (6-18 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 6-8 FT), two rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks over 26 minutes during Sunday's 104-82 Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Clippers.
items.story: Peterson showcased his explosiveness with a vicious throwdown early in the game, and while he didn't have his most efficient outing, he did an excellent job drawing contact and getting to the free-throw line. He's been one of the standout performers at Summer League, elevating expectations for his already highly anticipated rookie season.

items.headline: Peterson finished with 24 points (6-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-8 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block over 30 minutes in Thursday's 92-88 Summer League loss to Washington.
items.story: Peterson was productive during the Salt Lake City Summer League. Although he kept it going on the scoring end Thursday, he was inefficient shooting the ball. Turnovers were also an issue once again, as the 2026 No. 2 overall pick committed eight on the night. It's unclear how much action Peterson will see throughout his time in Las Vegas, though it's reasonable to believe he will clean up some of those issues, especially once he adjusts to the speed of the professional level.

items.headline: Diabate closed with seven points (3-6 FG, 1-1 FT), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals in 24 minutes during Monday's 124-91 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: With a strong start to the year, Diabate seems to have pulled way ahead of Ryan Kalkbrenner for Charlotte's starting job at center. Diabate has come down with at least eight boards in seven of his first eight games, posting at least one steal or block each time out so far.

items.headline: Diabate contributed 10 points (5-11 FG), 12 rebounds, one assist and two steals in 31 minutes during Friday's 95-79 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Diabate continued his strong start to the season, recording his second double-double in the past three games. He appears to be firmly locked in as the starting center, averaging 9.3 points. 9.8 rebounds and 2.6 combined steals and blocks in 29.6 minutes per game over the first six contests of the season. Although his ceiling is somewhat limited, he remains a clear must-roster player, particularly for those needing steals from the center position.

items.headline: Diabate contributed 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-4 FT), 17 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal over 35 minutes during Monday's 110-103 win over Washington.
items.story: Diabate delivered his strongest rebounding performance of the young season while recording his first double-double of the campaign. The center also made a significant defensive impact with three blocks, providing valuable production across multiple categories. His limited offensive involvement caps his scoring upside, but his rebounding and defensive contributions give him considerable appeal in category-based fantasy formats.

items.headline: Diabate registered five points (2-2 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block across 21 minutes in Friday's 128-81 loss to the Hawks.
items.story: Diabate saw his playing time drop from 34 minutes in the season opener against the Nets on Wednesday to just 21 here, largely because of the lopsided score. He remained productive on the glass, but his scoring and defensive numbers weren't as notable as in the previous game. His rebounding and defensive contributions provide a useful fantasy foundation, although his limited offensive involvement makes consistent minutes particularly important to his value.

items.headline: Diabate registered 17 points (7-11 FG, 0-0 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and five steals across 34 minutes in Wednesday's 110-103 win over the Nets.
items.story: Diabate opened the regular season with an impressive two-way performance, with his five steals providing a significant fantasy boost while ending just two boards shy of a double-double. The 34-minute workload was particularly encouraging, suggesting he could maintain a substantial role in Charlotte's frontcourt. He can be even better defensively because of his blocking ability, but if Diabate gets enough playing time, he can be a double-double threat every time he steps on the court.

items.headline: Diabate (elbow) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Diabate missed the preseason finale due to a right elbow injury but is good to go for Opening Night. The 2022 second-round pick is expected to start at center but will face competition from second-year big man Ryan Kalkbrenner and rookie Hannes Steinbach.

items.headline: Diabate has been ruled out for Friday's preseason finale against the Grizzlies due to a right elbow injury.
items.story: Diabate can be considered day-to-day moving forward, and his status for Wednesday's regular-season opener in Brooklyn remains unclear. If he's sidelined, Ryan Kalkbrenner and rookie Hannes Steinbach would be candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Diabate closed with four points (1-1 FG, 2-4 FT), four rebounds, three steals, two blocks and one assist in 20 minutes during Tuesday's 124-90 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: Diabate assumed the starting center role ahead of both Ryan Kalkbrenner and Hannes Steinbach. Despite scoring only four points, Diabate did what he does best, providing the team with energy and effort on both ends of the floor. He finished with five combined steals and blocks, an element of his game that will need to stabilize should he hope to hold onto the starting role. Assuming that is the case, Diabate is worth a look late in fantasy drafts for those needing to add some center depth.

items.headline: Diabate was spotted working with the first unit in Friday's practice.
items.story: Although he began the 2025-26 season in a reserve role, Diabate started 47 of his 73 regular-season appearances, averaging 7.9 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.0 blocks and 0.8 steals across 26.0 minutes per contest. He faces added competition for playing time this year with Hannes Steinbach and Naz Reid now in the mix. However, it appears likely Reid will start at power forward, while Diabate battles for center minutes with Steinbach and Ryan Kalkbrenner.

items.headline: Diabate could face a more crowded path to playing time after Charlotte acquired additional frontcourt talent in the LaMelo Ball trade, Cholo Magsino of Yahoo Sports reports.
items.story: The young big man showed flashes as an energy player and rebounder last season, but the additions of Naz Reid and Hannes Steinbach, plus internal improvement of second-year center Ryan Kalkbrenner may create increased competition for minutes. Diabate's defensive activity and athleticism should still give him an opportunity to earn a role, though his playing time may be less secure entering 2026-27.

items.headline: Diabate had two points (1-4 FG), eight rebounds, two assists and three blocks across 18 minutes during Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic.
items.story: Diabate tallied at least three blocks for the seventh time this season, closing out what could be considered a breakout campaign. However, although he was able to establish himself as the starting center in Charlotte, there are certainly some questions when it comes to his overall impact, especially for a team with lofty ambitions. In 75 appearances, Diabate averaged 7.8 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.7 combined steals and blocks.

items.headline: Diabate (hip) is available for Friday's Play-In Tournament game versus the Magic.
items.story: Diabate should continue to start Friday, and with him active, there will be fewer minutes available for Ryan Kalkbrenner and Xavier Tillman. In Tuesday's Play-In Tournament win over Miami, Diabate finished with eight points, 14 rebounds, one assist and one block over 36 minutes.

items.headline: Diabate is questionable for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Magic due to left hip soreness.
items.story: It's not clear as to when Diabate picked up this injury, as he logged 36 minutes during Tuesday's overtime win over the Heat. The team will presumably monitor the injury closely leading up to tipoff and should have more information to share on his availability closer to game time.

items.headline: Diabate posted eight points (4-5 FG), 14 rebounds, one assist and one block in 36 minutes during Tuesday's 127-126 overtime Play-In Game victory over Miami.
items.story: Despite scoring in single digits for the sixth straight game, Diabate found other ways to impact the game, most notably on the boards, where he grabbed a team-high 14 rebounds. Charlotte will now face either Philadelphia or Orlando, with the winner going on to face the Pistons in the opening round of the playoffs.

items.headline: Diabate notched two points (1-3 FG), five rebounds, five assists and one steal over 33 minutes during Tuesday's 113-102 loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Diabate underwhelmed again, continuing a rough couple of weeks. In seven appearances during that time, he has averaged just 5.7 points, 8.3 rebounds and 1.1 steals. While his role as the starting center is safe, his lack of offensive upside could be an issue during the playoffs.

items.headline: Diabate (ankle) will play Sunday in Minnesota.
items.story: Diabate is back after a one-game stint on the sidelines, which could push Ryan Kalkbrenner back to the second unit, while Xavier Tillman might drop from the rotation entirely. Since the All-Star break, Diabate is averaging 7.5 points, 9.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.9 swats per contest.

items.headline: Diabate (ankle) is listed as probable for Sunday's game in Minnesota.
items.story: Diabate didn't suit up for Friday's 129-108 win over the Indiana Pacers. However, it appears he will miss only one contest. If that's the case, Ryan Kalkbrenner will likely head back to the bench.

items.headline: Diabate (ankle) won't play in Friday's game against Indiana.
items.story: Diabate was listed as questionable heading into this contest because of left-ankle soreness. However, he has since been downgraded to out, meaning his next chance to play will be Sunday in Minnesota. With Diabate unavailable, Ryan Kalkbrenner is considered the favorite to replace him in the rotation, which would mark his first start in over a month.

items.headline: Diabate has left ankle soreness and is questionable for Friday's game against the Pacers.
items.story: It sounds like the Hornets are contemplating a maintenance day for the second leg of this back-to-back set, and the inferior opponent may be factored into the decision. If Diabate is held out, Ryan Kalkbrenner could step into a larger role for Charlotte.

items.headline: Diabate registered 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists and one steal in 25 minutes during Saturday's 118-114 loss to the 76ers.
items.story: Diabate collected his 19th double-double of the season, and he's pulled away from rookie big man Ryan Kalkbrenner for the top center spot since late December. Diabate has averaged 8.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks in 27.3 minutes per game in his last five outings, shooting 68.0 percent from the field.

items.headline: Diabate closed Tuesday's 134-90 victory over the Kings with 17 points (6-7 FG, 5-7 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal in 24 minutes.
items.story: Diabate took advantage of yet another favorable matchup, recording his second straight double-double. In what has been a breakout season thus far, Diabate's role appears to be secure, having started every game since late December. In 35 appearances since then, he has averaged 8.4 points, 9.5 rebounds and 1.1 blocks, good enough for top-100 value in standard leagues.

items.headline: Diabate had 11 points (5-6 FG, 1-2 FT), 14 rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal in 33 minutes during Saturday's 124-101 win over the Grizzlies.
items.story: Diabate has started in every one of his 13 appearances since the All-Star break, and while the big man often plays a secondary role on offense, he was able to leave his mark this time around. That said, Diabate has scored in double digits just three times in that span, so it's hard to trust him for sustained production even if he has a steady role in the first unit. Diabate has excellent upside in category-based leagues, but in standard point-based formats, he's better suited to be a streaming, matchup-based alternative.

items.headline: Diabate (hand) isn't listed on the Hornets' injury report for Thursday's game against Orlando.
items.story: Diabate appeared to sustain a left hand injury late in Tuesday's win over Miami, but the issue won't prevent him from facing the Magic. He's averaging 7.4 points, 9.2 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.1 blocks across 29.2 minutes over his last 11 appearances.

items.headline: Diabate exited Tuesday's 136-106 win over the Heat with 4:19 remaining in the fourth quarter after suffering an apparent left hand injury, Sam Perley of the Hornets' official site reports. He finished with eight points (4-6 FG), 13 rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block across 31 minutes.
items.story: Diabate bounced back following a four-point, five-rebound performance during Saturday's loss to San Antonio, though he seemingly picked up a hand injury late in the contest. The Hornets were up by 28 points at the time of Diabate's departure, so while it's possible that he was lifted early as a precaution, his status will still be worth monitoring ahead of Thursday's game against the Magic. If Diabate is forced to miss time, Ryan Kalkbrenner would likely move into the starting five.

items.headline: Diabate exited to the locker room during the fourth quarter of Tuesday's game against the Heat with an apparent left hand injury, Sam Perley of the Hornets' official site reports.
items.story: Perley notes that Diabate looked to be grabbing his left hand as he walked into the locker room, though it's not clear when he suffered the injury. Given the score of the game and the fact that he went to the locker room with only a few minutes remaining, it would seem unlikely that he returns to this one.

items.headline: Diabate logged four points (2-7 FG), five rebounds and three assists in 21 minutes during Saturday's 115-102 loss to San Antonio.
items.story: Diabate was barely noticeable Saturday, picking up two early fouls that limited him to just 21 minutes. This was simply a case of being matched up against a superior opponent, with Victor Wembanyama having his way on both ends of the floor. Despite this performance, fantasy managers should feel relatively comfortable holding him, assuming you can deal with the light schedule.

items.headline: Diabate produced seven points (3-8 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, four assists, one block and three steals over 31 minutes during Tuesday's 103-101 victory over Portland.
items.story: Diabate continues to deliver important contributions on both ends of the floor. While his scoring remains modest, to say the least, his ability to rebound at a high rate while adding consistent defensive numbers makes him a clear must-roster player. In seven appearances over the past two weeks, he has put up top-75 value in standard leagues, averaging 8.3 points, 9.4 rebounds and 2.0 combined steals and blocks.

items.headline: Diabate notched two points (1-4 FG), four rebounds, two assists and four blocks in 27 minutes during Sunday's 111-99 loss to the Suns.
items.story: Diabate swatted four balls, but that was the highlight of his stat line. Ryan Kalkbrenner recorded 19 minutes and had a much better line than Diabate. It will be interesting to see which center the Hornets prefer more as they make a playoff push. The tight battle for playing time limits the fantasy viability of both players.

items.headline: Diabate finished with nine points (2-4 FG, 5-6 FT), nine rebounds, six assists and two steals in 29 minutes during Wednesday's 118-89 victory over the Celtics.
items.story: Diabate continues to shine as Charlotte's starting center. Meanwhile, rookie Ryan Kalkbrenner has had to settle for a role with minutes in the teens off the bench. With Charlotte eyeing a playoff spot, Diabate's role appears to be locked in.

items.headline: Davis contributed 27 points (12-17 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds, three steals and one assist across 34 minutes in Monday's 103-94 win over the Magic.
items.story: Davis turned in an efficient performance en route to a game-high scoring total Monday. The veteran big man also tied for the game-best mark in rebounds while finishing with a season high in steals. Davis has reached the 25-point mark while grabbing at least nine boards in three of his last four outings.

items.headline: Davis finished with 25 points (8-18 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 9-10 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block across 34 minutes in Friday's 95-79 victory over the Hornets.
items.story: Davis had a quality game Friday to begin NBA Cup group play. He surpassed the 20-point mark for the third time this season, and he's also had at least one steal in each of the Wizards' six regular-season games of the 2026-27 campaign. Davis has shot a career-low 44.1 percent from the field this season, though he is still averaging a productive 22.3 points, 9.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks over 33.3 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Davis logged 18 points (8-18 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 121-111 loss to the Cavaliers.
items.story: Davis contributed across the board despite an uneven shooting performance, finishing with three combined steals and blocks while committing no turnovers. The veteran big man also connected on two three-pointers, adding another dimension to his offensive production. Although his rebounding total was modest, his ability to contribute in multiple categories continues to make him a valuable fantasy asset.

items.headline: Davis finished with 29 points (11-22 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 10 rebounds and one steal in 36 minutes during Monday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Davis put together a strong all-around showing, resulting in his second double-double through four matchups this season. He was spotted grabbing his right hand during the final 30 seconds of Monday's game after getting bumped on a screen, but he joked after the matchup that his hand was simply hot from making too many shots, per Greg Finberg of Wizards Central, so fantasy managers can breathe a sigh of relief.

items.headline: Davis supplied 19 points (8-21 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-5 FT), six rebounds, four assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 win over Chicago.
items.story: The veteran forward bounced back from a nine-point effort against the Raptors on Friday, but Davis' six boards were still his lowest mark on the young season. Through his first three games for the Wizards, Davis is averaging 20.7 points, 9.0 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks, and he hasn't even found his rhythm on offense yet -- he's shooting just 41.5 percent from the floor on 17.7 FG attempts a contest.

items.headline: Davis finished with nine points (3-12 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, two blocks and one steal across 32 minutes during Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Davis had a big performance in Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Bucks, but the veteran big man was held in check Friday by a Raptors team with tough defenders in Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles. Even in an off night, Davis was sniffing at a second consecutive double-double and figures to have more productive nights than duds. He could see a dip in minutes on the second leg of the Wizards' back-to-back set Saturday against the Bulls in Chicago.

items.headline: Davis finished Wednesday's 128-116 win over Milwaukee with 34 points (11-20 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 11-14 FT), 12 rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals in 34 minutes.
items.story: Davis dominated in his Wizards' regular-season debut, leading his team in rebounding, shot attempts and scoring. At times, he brought the ball up the floor and operated in a point-center role when Trae Young was off the court, so he should see significant usage in head coach Brian Keefe's system. When healthy, Davis is a league-winning fantasy asset.

items.headline: Davis generated 14 points (6-14 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-4 FT), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks over 27 minutes during Friday's 107-106 preseason loss to the Pelicans.
items.story: Davis notched his second straight double-double, led Washington in rebounds and tied for the team lead in blocks. Washington acquired the veteran big man from Dallas in an eight-player trade in February. The All-Star's health will again be the key variable when Washington opens the regular season Wednesday against the Bucks.

items.headline: Davis (rest) will start in Friday's preseason finale against the Pelicans.
items.story: Davis sat out Monday's preseason loss to the Nets for rest, but he's back and starting for the Wizards' preseason finale. Joining him in the first unit will be Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa and Alex Sarr.

items.headline: Davis (rest) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Nets, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Davis logged 10 points (3-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-6 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal over 22 minutes during Saturday's 114-108 overtime win over the Pistons, but he'll take a seat Monday as the Wizards monitor his workload. The star big man's next chance to play is Friday against the Pelicans.

items.headline: Davis logged 10 points (3-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-6 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal over 22 minutes during Saturday's 114-108 overtime win over the Pistons.
items.story: All of Davis' production came in the first half, with the veteran big man observing the entire second half from the bench. He's scored in double digits in limited playing time across his first two preseason games, and Davis will likely continue to operate under a minutes restriction to keep him fresh ahead of the Wizards' regular-season opener against the Bucks on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

items.headline: Davis recorded 16 points (6-11 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists and one block in 17 minutes during Thursday's 111-109 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Davis knocked home a pair of triples and was efficient from the field on the way to a team-high 16 points. He also made an impact on the glass during his brief time on the court. Overall, this can be considered a successful 2026 preseason debut by Davis, who was limited to 20 regular-season games a year ago due to ligament damage in his left hand along with calf and groin injuries.

items.headline: Davis is healthy and participating in training camp after dealing with injury issues during the 2025-26 campaign, according to Wizards reporter Greg Finberg.
items.story: Davis was spotted going through on-court work alongside Trae Young during Wednesday's practice, providing further confirmation that he's healthy entering his first full season with Washington. The veteran big man should have the opportunity to ramp up throughout camp and the preseason without injury-related limitations.

items.headline: General manager Will Dawkins said during Thursday's press conference that Davis (finger) is "very much a motivated player" and that he expects the veteran big man to bounce back in 2026-27.
items.story: Davis was limited to only 20 regular-season appearances with Dallas last season due to health issues, but Dawkins said the 10-time All-Star is currently in a "great frame of mind." Washington also views Davis as a starting-caliber center in a revamped frontcourt featuring Alex Sarr and Deandre Ayton. Davis and the Wizards reportedly postponed contract extension discussions earlier this offseason, but Dawkins declined to specifically address those talks Thursday.

items.headline: The Wizards selected AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, adding another high-usage scorer to the roster alongside Davis (finger).
items.story: Davis remains a cornerstone of Washington's frontcourt and should be the team's primary interior presence when he makes his Wizards debut. However, playing with Dybantsa and Trae Young could slightly reduce Davis' offensive workload while improving the overall quality of his scoring opportunities. Assuming he stays healthy, and that's a big assumption, Davis still projects as one of the league's most productive fantasy big men.

items.headline: Young provided 15 points (5-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 3-5 FT), three rebounds, nine assists and one steal across 34 minutes during Monday's 103-94 win over Orlando.
items.story: Young took a backseat offensively to Anthony Davis, Kyshawn George and AJ Dybantsa, who combined for 70 points, but he remained Washington's primary facilitator. His nine assists helped offset a modest scoring total, and his established playmaking role should continue to provide a reliable fantasy floor even when his shot volume fluctuates.

items.headline: Young recorded 22 points (10-20 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds and 10 assists in 38 minutes during Monday's 110-103 loss to Charlotte.
items.story: Young put together another strong final line Monday, though it resulted in a loss. He's been facilitating at an elite level to kick off the 2026-27 campaign, registering three double-doubles in four appearances, and he's been almost as impressive as a scorer, putting up 20 or more points in all four games.

items.headline: Young totaled 25 points (6-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 9-9 FT), four rebounds and nine assists in 34 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 win over Chicago.
items.story: The 25 points led the Wizards on the night, as Young just missed extending his double-double streak to three games to begin the season. He's looking as productive as ever in his first full campaign for Washington, averaging 22.3 points, 11.3 assists, 2.7 threes, 1.7 boards and 1.0 steals so far in 2026-27 while launching 8.7 three-point attempts a game, volume comparable to his last couple years in Atlanta.

items.headline: Young posted 22 points (5-15 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 8-10 FT), one rebound, 12 assists and a steal across 37 minutes in Friday's 112-102 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Even though the Wizards suffered their first loss of the season, Young posted an impressive stat line and excelled as a playmaker. Young has posted at least 20 points and 12 assists in each of his first two games of the season, although it remains to be seen if he can keep it up for an extended stretch and remain healthy.

items.headline: Young closed with 20 points (4-13 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 12-16 FT), 13 assists and two steals over 38 minutes during Wednesday's 128-116 victory over Milwaukee.
items.story: Young had a tough time getting his shot to drop and missed all six of his three-point attempts, but he did a nice job of creating contact and getting to the line for easy buckets. He also finished with just one turnover in 38 minutes of floor time, an impressive feat given his game-high 13 dimes.

items.headline: Young finished with 11 points (1-5 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 8-8 FT), three rebounds, 11 assists and a steal across 28 minutes in Monday's 131-122 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: On one hand, Young struggled to find his shooting rhythm, making just one field goal and relying heavily on free throws for his scoring. However, the veteran point guard dazzled as a playmaker with 11 assists, even if the eight turnovers were concerning. Still, the fact that Young posted a double-double despite his offensive inefficiency is a great sign of him being ready for the start of the 2026-27 regular season. Young's passing volume remains an important fantasy asset, but his ball security and shooting efficiency will be worth monitoring. If he stays healthy, he should have a sizable role as the team's primary floor general in a dynamic lineup alongside AJ Dybantsa, Alex Sarr and Anthony Davis.

items.headline: Young finished with 15 points (4-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), four assists and two steals across 17 minutes in Thursday's 111-109 preseason win over the Knicks.
items.story: Young made the most of his abbreviated playing time and looked good orchestrating the offense alongside several projected starters in Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa and Anthony Davis. The veteran guard's combination of perimeter scoring and elite playmaking should remain central to Washington's offensive approach once the regular season begins.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been cleared for training camp and was spotted participating in on-court work during Wednesday's practice, according to Wizards reporter Greg Finberg.
items.story: Young's 2025-26 campaign ended with him sidelined by a right quadriceps contusion and lower-back irritation after appearing in just five games for Washington following his midseason arrival. His participation during the second day of camp indicates he's moved past those issues and enters the preseason healthy.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been doing sand-dune workouts during the offseason, and his trainer discussed the guard's outlook Monday, Mark Medina of RG reports.
items.story: With Young limited to 15 regular-season appearances in 2025-26 due to injuries, any sign of offseason rehab progress is notable. This report points to active conditioning work after his quadriceps issue, though it does not provide a return timeline or formal clearance update ahead of Washington's training camp. However, a previous report from ESPN indicated that he would be ready to roll.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) plans to sign a four-year, $212 million deal with the Wizards, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: Young declined his $49 million player option and was initially going to test the waters in free agency. The Wizards were always viewed as the favorites to sign him, however, and it's clear that they value him extremely highly based on this offer. Young was limited to 15 appearances during the 2025-26 regular season due to injuries, posting averages of 17.9 points and 8.0 assists on 45.8 percent shooting from the field.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) is expected to sign a three-year deal with the Wizards in free agency, according to ESPN's Brian Windhorst.
items.story: Young plans to decline his $48 million player option for the 2026-27 season, and while he's expected to meet with other teams, the Wizards are the clear favorites. Windhorst adds that the Wizards are preparing to offer him a very large contract, and it sounds like there's mutual interest in getting something done quickly.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps, back) isn't expected to play again in 2025-26, per Chase Hughes of Monumental Sports Network.
items.story: Young last appeared for the Wizards during the March 16 loss to the Warriors, and it sounds like Washington is finally ready to pull the plug on his campaign. It was an injury-ruined season for the star guard, who averaged 17.9 points, 8.0 assists, 2.0 rebounds and 1.8 three-pointers in 25.6 minutes per game over 15 outings with Atlanta and Washington. Bub Carrington should continue to serve as the Wizards' top point guard the rest of the way.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps/back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Young hasn't played since March 16 and will miss a 12th straight game while dealing with a right quadriceps contusion and lower-back pain. The star point guard should be considered doubtful for future contests until the Wizards provide an update on his status. However, it wouldn't be surprising if he doesn't play again this season, as Washington has just three regular-season games remaining after Tuesday.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Young hasn't played since March 16, and while the Wizards continue to treat him as day-to-day, it'd be surprising if the veteran point guard suited up during the final week of the regular season. In his absence, Bub Carrington, Jaden Hardy and Sharife Cooper remain candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) is out for Saturday's game versus Miami.
items.story: The star guard will be sidelined for a 10th consecutive game Saturday. With a lost regular season winding down for the Wizards, it's becoming increasingly more unlikely that Young will suit up again this year.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: Young isn't yet ready to return after suffering a right quadriceps injury. His next opportunity to suit up will arrive Saturday in Miami.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) is out for Monday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: The Wizards will keep Young on ice for the eighth straight game as they continue to take a cautious approach. His next chance to play comes Wednesday against the 76ers.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps/back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Young will miss a seventh consecutive contest due to a right quadriceps contusion, and he's also dealing with lower-back pain. The star point guard should be considered doubtful for future contests until the Wizards offer an update on his progress.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) is out for Friday's game against Golden State.
items.story: Young will remain sidelined Friday with a bruised right quadriceps. Bub Carrington should continue to see run as the team's starting point guard in Young's absence.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) is out for Wednesday's game against the Jazz.
items.story: Young is set for his fifth straight absence while on the mend from a right quadriceps bruise. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Friday against Golden State.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps/back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks.
items.story: Young is rehabbing from both a right quad contusion and lower-back injury. His next chance to play is Wednesday against the Jazz, but the Wizards have not communicated a clear timeline of return for the veteran point guard. Bub Carrington will continue to start at point guard for as long as Young is out of action.

items.headline: The Wizards announced Saturday that Young (quadriceps) is also working through lower-back irritation, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
items.story: Young re-injured his right quad during Monday's loss against the Warriors. Neither his quad nor his back injury require surgery at this time, but with the most recent injury report from the Wizards, there doesn't appear to be a clear timeline of return for the veteran point guard. Bub Carrington should continue to serve as the Wizards' starting point guard for as long as Young is sidelined.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) is out for Saturday's game against the Thunder.
items.story: Young will be sidelined for a third straight contest. At this point, it remains unclear if he will be able to return for the second leg of this back-to-back set Sunday against the Knicks. In the games that Young does play, he'll likely continue to see modest workloads.

items.headline: Young (quad) won't play Thursday versus the Pistons.
items.story: This will be Young's second straight game on the sidelines, and with Saturday's game versus the Thunder being the first of a back-to-back, it seems likely that Young will miss at least one more game. Bub Carrington should continue to start while Young is out, and there will be more minutes available for Jaden Hardy.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Pistons.
items.story: Young will be sidelined for the second half of Washington's back-to-back set after leaving Monday's loss to the Warriors early following a collision with Will Richard. Young was able to leave under his own power, but the Wizards are expected to be extremely cautious with their new point guard the rest of the way. His next chance to suit up will come Thursday in a rematch against Detroit.

items.headline: Young (quadriceps) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's game against the Warriors. He'll close with 21 points (7-10 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 4-5 FT), five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block across 21 minutes.
items.story: After a collision with Will Richard, Young hobbled off to the locker room at the 7:53 mark of the third quarter. The guard was able to walk off under his own power but will not return to Monday's contest due to a right quad contusion. His next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Pistons, though it's unlikely the 27-year-old suits up for the second half of the back-to-back.

items.headline: Young (undisclosed) is off the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Warriors.
items.story: Young exited Saturday's game in the third quarter and did not return due to undisclosed reasons, but he appears set to play in Monday's contest. In four appearances since joining the Wizards, Young is averaging 13.8 points, 6.5 assists and 3.3 rebounds in 20.5 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Fox totaled 12 points (5-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and one steal across 22 minutes during Monday's 119-97 win over Utah.
items.story: Fox converted five of his eight field-goal attempts but wasn't required to shoulder a heavy offensive workload as San Antonio cruised to its fifth consecutive victory. The veteran guard committed five fouls and played just 22 minutes, while rookie Dylan Harper paced the Spurs with 17 points and eight assists. Fox's efficiency was encouraging, but his limited playing time and modest playmaking numbers resulted in a relatively quiet fantasy outing.

items.headline: Fox accumulated 11 points (3-6 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds and six assists over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 130-103 win over Sacramento.
items.story: The 26 minutes were a season low for Fox, but that can primarily be attributed to the Spurs nursing a large lead for most of the contest. He's dished out at least six dimes in all four outings and has seven combined steals-plus-blocks, and that trend should continue as long as he remains healthy.

items.headline: Fox recorded 19 points (6-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, nine assists, three steals and one block over 28 minutes in Saturday's 122-106 win over the Mavs.
items.story: Fox has hit the ground running this season, pumping out top-30 value with averages of 17.3 points, 8.3 assists, 4.7 rebounds, 1.3 triples and 2.0 steals per game on 58.1 percent shooting from the field and 80.0 percent at the line. He'll look to maintain his strong play Tuesday against the Kings.

items.headline: Fox chipped in 19 points (6-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 5-5 FT), four rebounds, nine assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Friday's 114-110 loss to the Rockets.
items.story: Fox played through a wrist injury, falling one assist short of a double-double. Despite the apparent issue, Fox doesn't seem too bothered, chalking up meaningful stats on both ends of the floor. The injury is something for fantasy managers to monitor, though the fact that he has played in excess of 30 minutes in each of the first two games is a positive.

items.headline: Fox (wrist) is available for Friday's game against the Rockets, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Fox will power through the wrist issue and get out there for the second game of the season. He logged 32 minutes as a starter in the season opener and finished with 14 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and two turnovers in a 116-104 loss to the Thunder.

items.headline: Fox (wrist) participated in Friday's morning shootaround, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Fox appeared to get some extra shots up following practice as well. The point guard is officially listed as questionable and could end up being a game-time call.

items.headline: Fox (wrist) is questionable to play in Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Fox appears to have picked up a wrist injury that will leave his status for Friday's contest up in the air. He was efficient in the season-opening defeat Tuesday, tallying 14 points (6-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 32 minutes. If Fox is sidelined, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle will handle more of the playmaking duties, while Julian Champagnie would likely slide into the starting unit.

items.headline: Fox contributed 14 points (6-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Tuesday's 116-104 loss to Oklahoma City.
items.story: Fox ran the offense efficiently, leading San Antonio in assists. His night will be remembered more for the second-quarter flagrant foul, when he threw Chet Holmgren to the floor and set off a scuffle between the two teams. The veteran point guard did set up Victor Wembanyama's only field goal, an alley-oop at the end of the third quarter.

items.headline: Fox tallied 16 points (5-9 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds and three assists in 22 minutes in Friday's 126-97 preseason win over the Kings.
items.story: Fox was sharp against his former team, finishing second on the Spurs in scoring. The veteran point guard played in only two preseason games but was efficient in both outings. He'll be ready to go when San Antonio opens the regular season Tuesday against the Thunder.

items.headline: Fox tallied nine points (3-5 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds and four assists over 19 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: On the heels of his nightmarish NBA Finals run, fantasy managers are likely keeping a close eye on Fox's role this preseason. Even though youngsters Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper appear to be nipping at his heels for playmaking duties, Fox is set to open the season as San Antonio's top floor general.

items.headline: Fox (undisclosed) is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's preseason game against Phoenix, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Fox will make his preseason debut after missing the first three games with an undisclosed issue. While the guard is in the starting lineup, his workload may be limited in the exhibition.

items.headline: Fox (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Monday's preseason game against the Jazz, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: Fox was listed in the starting lineup for Thursday's game against the Hawks but was a late scratch and will miss a third straight exhibition Monday. The extent of his injury remains unclear, but the Spurs have given no indication the veteran point guard is in danger of missing Opening Night. For what it's worth, the Spurs are resting most of their regulars, including their expected starting lineup, for Monday's game.

items.headline: Fox (undisclosed) has been ruled out for Saturday's preseason game against the Suns, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
items.story: Fox will end up missing two consecutive preseason games due to general soreness, so his next chance to play is Monday against the Jazz. Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle will form the Spurs' starting backcourt for Saturday's exhibition contest.

items.headline: Fox (undisclosed) is considered a game-time decision for Saturday's preseason game against the Suns, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Contrary to a previous report, Fox now has a chance of being available for Saturday's exhibition contest, but his official status may not be known until about 30 minutes prior to the 10:30 p.m. ET tipoff. Fox was unable to play in the Spurs' preseason opener against the Hawks on Thursday due to soreness.

items.headline: Fox (undisclosed) won't play in Saturday's preseason game against the Suns, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Fox will miss a second straight exhibition after being a late scratch ahead of Thursday's preseason opener against the Hawks. The veteran point guard will have three more chances to suit up before the Spurs' regular-season opener against the Thunder on Oct. 20.

items.headline: Fox won't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Hawks due to soreness, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
items.story: It's unclear exactly what is bothering Fox, though he was a late scratch due to soreness. His next chance to play in the preseason will come Saturday against the Suns.

items.headline: Head coach Mitch Johnson said he expects Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and Fox to play together more during the regular season, per Raul Dominguez Jr. of the Associated Press.
items.story: Fox played through an ankle sprain for the Spurs during the NBA Finals, averaging only 12.8 points per game while shooting 34.4 percent from the field and 25.0 percent from deep across the five Finals contests. The emergence of Dylan Harper last postseason is a serious threat nipping at Fox's heels for more playing time at point guard, but it sounds like the Spurs are willing to deploy all three in the lineup at times to accommodate all their backcourt talent.

items.headline: Jared Weiss of the New York Times believes that Fox should start over Dylan Harper in 2026-27.
items.story: The calls for Harper to unseat Fox as the Spurs' starting point guard grew louder this past postseason, when the former soundly outperformed the latter, particularly during the NBA Finals. Fox appears to be in pole position to begin 2026-27 as the starter over Harper, but any kind of slow start could jeopardize his hold on the top spot if Harper carries his NBA Finals success into the new season.

items.headline: Fox closed with seven points (3-15 FG, 1-8 3Pt), five assists and two steals in 37 minutes during Saturday's 94-90 loss to the Knicks in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Fox wrapped up a brutal championship series with another dreadful shooting display, failing to crack 37.5 percent shooting from the field for a third straight game as San Antonio was eliminated. The 28-year-old guard was never able to recapture his pre-injury form after returning from a Western Conference Finals high-ankle sprain, averaging a meager 12.8 points while shooting 34.4 percent from the field and 25.0 percent from deep across the five Finals contests. Beyond the efficiency woes, Fox's decision-making plagued the Spurs at the worst possible moments and most notably in Game 4, when he inexplicably drove into a contested layup attempt instead of running out the clock and forcing New York to foul while up one with 12 seconds remaining. With San Antonio heading into the offseason, management will have to weigh whether Fox can adjust his game alongside rising stars Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper, or if his maximum contract will continue to clog the team's flexibility.

items.headline: Fox had seven points (3-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal across 38 minutes during Wednesday's 105-95 loss to the Knicks in Game 1 of the NBA Finals.
items.story: Fox scored single digits for the third time in his past four games, continuing what has been an underwhelming stretch of games since returning from an ankle injury. In those six appearances, he has averaged just 10.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.5 steals. If San Antonio is to wrestle back home-court advantage, Fox is going to have to figure things out in a hurry.

items.headline: Fox totaled five points (1-9 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds and seven assists across 26 minutes during Thursday's 118-91 victory over Oklahoma City in Game 6 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: Fox went 1-for-9 from the field, continuing what has been a lean run of production, particularly on the offensive end. In four games over the past week, he has averaged just 10.3 points, 6.5 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 1.3 steals, shooting 33.3 percent from the field and 71.4 percent from the line. Despite his struggles, San Antonio is now only one win away from advancing to the NBA Finals. A proven clutch performer, the hope is that Fox will turn things around when the two teams meet in Game 7 on Saturday.

items.headline: Fox amassed 12 points (5-13 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), 10 rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal across 31 minutes during Sunday's 103-82 victory over the Thunder in Game 4 of the Western Conference Finals.
items.story: Fox racked up his first double-double of the postseason, helping the Spurs to an impressive home victory. However, despite his efforts, it is clear that Fox is still hampered by an ankle injury that forced him to miss Games 1 and 2. items.headline: Swain was selected by the Bulls with the No. 15 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: Swain lands in Chicago after putting together a dominant junior season at Texas. The athletic forward was the engine of the Longhorns' offense, putting up a stellar line of 17.3 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game while displaying tremendous efficiency inside the arc with a 54.2 percent shooting mark from the field. Swain possesses a versatile, modern skill set, offering the size to impact the game on the glass alongside the playmaking chops to generate looks for others out of the frontcourt. A significant driver behind that high field-goal percentage is Swain's elite ability as a finisher at the rim. He excels at using his length and explosive athleticism to play through contact in the paint, frequently converting tough, contested looks and generating second-chance opportunities. While his perimeter shooting consistency remains a development point as he transitions to the NBA, his interior scoring prowess, defensive motor and elite athletic traits give him dynamic upside. He joins a Bulls squad looking to inject youthful length and playmaking into its core, positioning Swain to compete for immediate minutes during his rookie campaign.

items.story: The 21-year-old big man is currently recovering from foot surgery but is expected to be ready for training camp after averaging 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds and 2.0 blocks in 48 regular-season appearances last year. Sarr remains a major part of the franchise's long-term plans, although the additions of established veterans could reduce some offensive responsibilities. His defensive upside should continue to provide substantial fantasy value if he can stay healthy.

items.headline: Sarr underwent surgery to repair a fractured right foot Monday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
items.story: Despite the procedure, Sarr is expected to be ready for the start of the 2026-27 season. The 2024 No. 2 overall pick was limited to 48 regular-season appearances in 2025-26, averaging 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.0 blocks in 27.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) has been ruled out for Sunday's regular-season finale against Cleveland.
items.story: Sarr will end up missing 23 of the Wizards' final 30 games of the regular season, most recently due to left toe inflammation. The 2024 first overall pick will end his sophomore season averaging 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.0 threes, 2.0 blocks and 0.8 steals over 27.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Head coach Brian Keefe said Thursday that Sarr (toe) is unlikely to play again this season, Chase Hughes of Monumental Sports Network reports.
items.story: Sarr will miss a seventh consecutive contest Thursday due to a left big toe injury, and he should be considered doubtful for the Wizards' final two regular-season games until further notice. With the second-year big man on the shelf, Julian Reese and Anthony Gill will likely continue seeing increased burn.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) is listed as out for Thursday's game versus Chicago.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Bulls.
items.story: Sarr is out for a sixth consecutive contest with a left toe issue. Anthony Gill could start at center Tuesday and make for a viable streaming choice in most fantasy leagues, especially if Tristan Vukcevic (knee) is downgraded from questionable to out.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Sarr will miss a fifth straight game, including both halves of Washington's weekend back-to-back set. In his absence, Tristan Vukcevic (knee) is a candidate for increased playing time, but if he's also sidelined, Anthony Gill and Julian Reese would likely be thrust into expanded roles.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) is out for Saturday's game against Miami.
items.story: Sarr is sidelined for a fourth consecutive contest due to a left toe issue. With Tristan Vukcevic (knee) also out Saturday, Anthony Gill should be in for a massive role at center against the Heat.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) is questionable for Saturday's game against Miami.
items.story: Sarr is trying to end a three-game absence due to a left toe issue. With Tristan Vukcevic (knee) also questionable for Saturday, Anthony Gill could be in for a featured role at center against the Heat.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) is out for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
items.story: This is a tough blow for an injury-depleted Washington frontcourt. With Sarr out for a third straight contest, the Wizards will likely lean more on Tristan Vukcevic and Anthony Gill.

items.story: Sarr was also listed as questionable ahead of Monday's game against the Lakers before ultimately being downgraded to out, so it seems he's closing in on a return. The Wizards should have more to share on his status as tipoff approaches.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) is questionable for Monday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Sarr was initially left off the team's injury report, but he's since been added with a questionable tag after also sitting out Sunday due to left big toe injury management. Washington should have a better idea of whether he'll suit up closer to tipoff.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) isn't on the injury report for Monday's game versus the Lakers.
items.story: Sarr is available for the second part of this back-to-back set Monday. The Wizards are scaling back the second-year center's workload as of late -- Sarr has averaged 11.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.9 blocks in 21.2 minutes per tilt in his last seven games.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) won't play in Sunday's game against Portland.
items.story: Sarr will miss the front end of this back-to-back set due to left big toe injury management. His next opportunity to suit up will come Monday against the Lakers. With the second-year big man out, Tristan Vukcevic, Anthony Gill and Julian Reese are candidates to see expanded roles.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) will play Friday against the Warriors.
items.story: Sarr is set to return after a pair of games on the sidelines. Given how the Wizards have handled recent games, Sarr may see a modest workload in his first game back.

items.story: Sarr is in danger of missing his third straight game Friday. If he can't give it a go, Tristan Vukcevic (back), Anthony Gill and Julian Reese will help pick up the slack.

items.story: Sarr will miss a second straight game as a result of left toe inflammation. Tristan Vukcevic (back), Anthony Gill and Julian Reese could all factor into the mix at center in Sarr's absence.

items.story: Sarr has been able to play through inflammation in his left big toe in each of the Wizards' last two games, but he will sit for the second leg of the team's back-to-back set after playing 22 minutes in Saturday's 132-111 loss to the Thunder. Tristan Vukcevic, Anthony Gill and Julian Reese should all see a bump in minutes Sunday due to Sarr's absence. Sarr's next chance to play is Wednesday against the Jazz.

items.headline: Sarr (toe) is available to play Thursday against the Pistons.
items.story: After missing the Wizards' first two games of the week -- first due to right hamstring injury management, then due to left big toe capsulitis -- Sarr will make his return to action Thursday. Since returning to action March 8 following a month-long absence due to a right hamstring strain, Sarr has yet to clear 25 minutes in any of his four appearances. Expect the Wizards to keep his workload in check once again Thursday as he returns from a two-game absence.

items.headline: Markkanen supplied 22 points (8-16 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Markkanen bounced back from a dreadful shooting night in Saturday's 112-90 loss to Portland. His performance marked the first of the season in which he shot better than 47 percent from the field. He finished with game-high figures in scoring and three-pointers while tying Mo Bamba for the team lead in rebounds. Markkanen and the Jazz have struggled out of the gate to begin 2026-27, but there's still plenty of time for him to turn things around from a fantasy perspective.

items.headline: Markkanen finished with 13 points (3-14 FG, 2-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and two blocks over 29 minutes in Saturday's 112-90 loss to Portland.
items.story: Markkanen didn't play in Wednesday's 117-111 loss to San Antonio. He was back on the floor Saturday, though it wasn't his most efficient shooting performance. The 2017 No. 7 overall pick hasn't played the best in his five regular-season appearances in 2026-27, averaging just 15.4 points. However, Markkanen has proven he can be one of the most productive players in the league, so there's reason to believe he will get on track at some point.

items.headline: Markkanen (wrist) is available for Saturday's game against Portland.
items.story: Markkanen missed Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to a wrist injury, but the veteran forward has been cleared to return for Saturday's contest. He is averaging 16.0 points, 5.5 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 2.5 threes over 28.5 minutes per game to open the 2026-27 season. His return means Josh Green will likely revert to a rotational role off the bench.

items.headline: Markkanen (wrist) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Portland.
items.story: Markkanen suffered a right wrist sprain during the 110-105 loss to Memphis on Monday. As a result, he didn't play in Wednesday's meeting with the Spurs. While subsequent tests have been encouraging, the veteran should still be considered day-to-day. If Markkanen misses another contest, Josh Green could remain in the starting lineup.

items.headline: Markkanen (wrist) is out for Wednesday's tilt against the Spurs.
items.story: After being listed as questionable to suit up due to a right wrist sprain suffered in Utah's 110-105 loss to Memphis on Monday, Markkanen has been downgraded to out. With Jusuf Nurkic (toe) and Jaren Jackson (knee) both sidelined, Jaxson Hayes, Brice Sensabaugh, Kyle Filipowski and Svi Mykhailiuk are all candidates to earn more playing time.

items.headline: Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
items.story: Markkanen was forced out of Monday's 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies after spraining his wrist, but there's a chance he won't miss any additional game time. Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is also questionable for Wednesday's game, and if they both get cleared, Mo Bamba will lose some of his streaming appeal.

items.headline: Markkanen is day-to-day with a right wrist sprain, per NBA reporter Marc Stein.
items.story: Markkanen left Monday's loss to Memphis with the injury, and it doesn't sound initially that he's dealing with a significant setback. The star forward can be tentatively deemed questionable for Wednesday's tilt versus the Spurs.

items.headline: Markkanen (wrist) won't return to Monday's game against Memphis. He'll finish with two points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT) in six minutes.
items.story: Markkanen exited to the locker room in the first quarter and won't return due to a right wrist injury. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Wednesday's game against the Spurs. The Jazz noted after the game that Markkanen will be sent for imaging Tuesday, per Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune. If the veteran forward is forced to miss time, Kyle Filipowski, Ace Bailey and Brice Sensabaugh would likely see increased playing time.

items.headline: Markkanen is questionable to return to Monday's game against Memphis due to a right wrist injury.
items.story: Markkanen exited to the locker room in the opening quarter and is questionable to check back in. If the veteran forward doesn't return, Ace Bailey and Kyle Filipowski will likely see increased burn.

items.headline: Markkanen went to the locker room during the first quarter of Monday's game against the Grizzlies due to an apparent hand injury, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reports.
items.story: Markkanen checked out of the game with 5:58 remaining in the first quarter and was spotted walking to the locker room. He can be considered questionable to return until further notice.

items.headline: Markkanen ended Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers with 28 points (9-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt, 5-6 FT), six rebounds and one assist in 38 minutes.
items.story: Markkanen had failed to crack the 20-point plateau through his first two games of the season, but he got hot Sunday and finished as Utah's leading scorer. The 29-year-old forward scored efficiently and committed just one turnover in 38 minutes of floor time, but the Jazz couldn't capitalize on his effort, falling victim to a 52-point barrage from Luka Doncic.

items.headline: Markkanen ended Friday's 120-119 victory over the Pelicans with 16 points (6-13 FG, 4-9 3Pt), six rebounds, three assists and one steal in 34 minutes.
items.story: With the Jazz roster rapidly getting stronger around him, Markkanen's usage could be set to decline. The 29-year-old forward averaged 19.2 FG attempts over 42 regular-season games in 2025-26, but through two games to begin the current campaign he's attempted exactly 13 shots in each, with Jaren Jackson, Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson all seeing similar volume in Friday's win. Markkanen still figures to be busy from beyond the arc and grab his share of boards, but his overall scoring could dip well below the 23-25 PPG his fantasy investors have been used to getting from him since he arrived in Utah.

items.headline: Markkanen chipped in 18 points (4-13 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 9-10 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and one block across 36 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Markkanen struggled to find his shooting touch, particularly from beyond the arc, but his aggressiveness at the free-throw line helped salvage his scoring output.
