The Clippers had been cycling through several players as Zubac's primary backup, but the return of Bamba should bring some stability to the second unit. According to Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com, Bamba said before Sunday's contest that he doesn't anticipate being held out for one-half of back-to-back sets this season, though it wouldn't be surprising if the Clippers opted to take a cautious approach by resting him for Monday's contest versus the Warriors. If Bamba isn't available Monday, the Clippers could turn to Kobe Brown, Kai Jones and/or Nicolas Batum to handle the backup center role.

items.headline: Bamba (knee) is available to play Sunday against the Jazz, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Bamba has spent the past week in the G League with the San Diego Clippers while in the final stages of his rehab for his left knee. He managed to play in Thursday's game against the Valley Suns and finished with 13 points, 12 rebounds and one assist over 21 minutes. Bamba will serve as the Clippers' backup center Sunday behind starter Ivica Zubac, though the former will likely operate on a minutes restriction.

items.headline: The Clippers recalled Bamba (knee) from the San Diego Clippers of the G League on Friday.
items.story: Bamba has yet to suit up this season due to left knee soreness but spent a few days in the G League to continue his rehab program. The 25-year-old big man's next chance to return to action is Sunday's matchup with Utah.

items.headline: Bamba (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Rockets.
items.story: Bamba continues to deal with left knee soreness but will play in the G League with the San Diego Clippers during Thursday's game against the Valley Suns. As things stand now, the medical staff in Los Angeles hopes to have him ready to go for Sunday's contest against the Jazz, according to Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com.

items.headline: The Clippers announced Bamba (knee) is out for Wednesday's game versus the Rockets, and they have assigned him to the San Diego Clippers of the G League in order to progress in his rehab, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
items.story: Bamba has missed the beginning of the season while dealing with a left knee injury. However, Bamba's assignment to the G League indicates that he is nearing a return to action.

items.headline: Bamba (knee) is out for Monday's game against the Thunder, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Bamba has yet to appear in a game this season, but he is seemingly nearing a return as he has been a full go during 5-on-5 scrimmages during practice. Nonetheless, Bamba will be unavailable once again Monday.

items.headline: Coach Tyronn Lue said after Saturday's win over the Raptors that Bamba (knee) has been a full go during 5-on-5 scrimmages during recent practices, but the center's status for the Clippers' upcoming three-game road trip remains unclear, Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Bamba appears to be nearing his season debut, but even when he's cleared to suit up, his role will likely be minimal. For the most part, the Clippers have been going small with their second unit, but Kai Jones has received some playing time as Ivica Zubac's primary backup over the first few weeks of the season.

items.headline: Bamba (knee) is out for Saturday's game versus the Raptors, Justin Russo of the 'Clip & Roll' podcast reports.
items.story: Bamba will remain sidelined to begin the 2024-25 campaign due to left knee soreness. There is no official return timetable for the 26-year-old big man.

items.headline: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
items.story: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Beekman had his Exhibit 10 contract converted to a two-way deal by the Wizards on Saturday, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
items.story: Beekman signed with the Wizards for training camp and has done enough to earn himself a two-way contract. He last played in the NBA in the 2024-25 season and will likely spend most of his time with the G League's Capital City Go-Go in 2026-27.

items.headline: Beekman agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with the Wizards on Sunday.
items.story: Beekman went undrafted in 2024. Since then, he has spent the bulk of his career in the G League, appearing in 62 games between the Santa Cruz Warriors, Long Island Nets and Osceola Magic, averaging 11.7 points, 4.2 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 2.1 steals over 30.3 minutes per contest. He also logged 36 regular-season games between Brooklyn and Golden State in 2024-25.

items.headline: Beekman registered 13 points (5-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, 14 assists and one steal over 31 minutes in Saturday's 91-83 Las Vegas Summer League win over the Hawks.
items.story: Beekman finished his Summer League run strong, recording his first double-double in Las Vegas while leading the Wizards to a victory. His performance helped strengthen his case for a training camp invite with Washington.

items.headline: Beekman logged 11 points (4-4 FG, 3-3 FT) and two assists in eight minutes during Saturday's 126-118 preseason win over the Heat.
items.story: Beekman finished Saturday's exhibition contest as one of six Magic players to score in double digits, and he finished third on the team in the scoring category behind Jase Richardson (13) and Tristan da Silva (12). Beekman inked an Exhibit 10 contract with the Magic in early September after competing with the Nuggets in the Summer League, and he is competing for a permanent spot on Orlando's roster for the upcoming season.

items.headline: Beekman agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with Orlando on Tuesday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
items.story: Beekman will compete for a spot on Orlando's regular-season roster during training camp. The 23-year-old point guard joined the Warriors on a two-way contract before the 2024-25 season, though he was eventually traded to the Nets in December. He appeared in 36 regular-season games (four starts) between Golden State and Brooklyn, averaging 2.6 points and 1.8 assists across 13.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Beekman (calf) is listed in the starting lineup for Thursday's Summer League game against Milwaukee, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports.
items.story: Beekman battled a calf injury at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, but he's back at full strength for the start of Summer League play. He'll draw the start alongside Spencer Jones, Hunter Tyson, DaRon Holmes and Tyrell Harrison.

items.headline: Beekman (calf) signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Nuggets on Saturday, Bennett Durando of The Denver Post reports.
items.story: Beekman will join Denver on a non-guaranteed contract and compete for a roster spot. The 23-year-old guard signed a two-way contract with the Warriors last season before being traded to the Nets in December. He averaged 2.6 points, 1.8 assists and 1.1 rebounds across 13.0 minutes per game in 36 regular-season appearances (four starts) between Golden State and Brooklyn.

items.headline: Beekman (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
items.story: Beekman popped up on Saturday's injury report due to right calf soreness, and the injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for Sunday's regular-season finale. With Beekman and D'Angelo Russell (ankle) both sidelined, Tyson Etienne could be in line to make his first career NBA start. Over his last five outings (four starts), Beekman averaged 5.4 points, 4.8 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 2.6 steals over 26.0 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Beekman is listed as questionable for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Knicks due to right calf soreness, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
items.story: Beekman has started in the Nets' last four games, but he could miss Sunday's contest while working through a right calf issue. With D'Angelo Russell (ankle) already ruled out, Beekman's absence would open the door for Tyson Etienne to see more playing time, potentially in a starting role.

items.headline: Beekman racked up 11 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, three assists and three steals over 32 minutes during Friday's 117-91 loss to the Timberwolves.
items.story: Making his fourth straight start for the Nets, the undrafted rookie once again made his presence felt at the defensive end of the court. Beekman has recorded three steals in four of the last five games, and during his run in the starting five he's averaging 6.3 points, 5.5 assists, 2.8 boards and 2.5 steals in 28.0 minutes.

items.headline: Beekman ended with zero points (0-3 FG), four rebounds, 10 assists and three steals over 31 minutes during Tuesday's 119-114 win over the Pelicans.
items.story: Although Beekman was held scoreless Tuesday, he was able to dish out a game-high 10 assists while playing a passive role on offense. With the Nets missing several key contributors, it wouldn't be surprising to see Beekman remain in the starting lineup during the final week of the season. Beekman has registered at least five assists, four rebounds and three steals in both of his starting appearances thus far.

items.headline: Beekman contributed 14 points (6-13 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, five assists and three steals over 36 minutes during Sunday's 120-109 loss to Toronto.
items.story: Beekman got his first career start Sunday with D'Angelo Russell (ankle) out and Brooklyn shorthanded, lifting the Nets on both ends of the floor while leading all players in scoring, assists and steals in a losing effort. Beekman's points were a season-high figure, and he also matched season-best marks in rebounds, assists and steals.

items.headline: Beekman will start Sunday's game against the Raptors, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
items.story: Beekman has been a consistent part of Brooklyn's rotation but played 18 minutes against the Timberwolves on Thursday, posting two points, two rebounds, two assists and three steals. With the Nets shorthanded once again, including an absence to D'Angelo Russell (ankle), Beekman will draw his first career start and should handle a sizable role against the Raptors, who'll also be without multiple starters.

items.headline: Beekman logged three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 3Pt) and one rebound over nine minutes during Monday's 111-108 win over the Lakers.
items.story: Beekman was back in the rotation, albeit for just nine minutes. After playing a somewhat consistent role through the months of January and February, this was just the second time Beekman has suited up since the calendar flipped to March. In 28 games played this season, Beekman is averaging just 2.0 points and 1.2 assists.

items.headline: Beekman registered three points (1-5 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), one rebound, one assist and three steals in 27 minutes during Saturday's 115-94 loss to the Pistons.
items.story: Beekman played a career-high 27 minutes, although his numbers tell a different story. Despite the increased playing time, Beekman had no real impact, a worrying trend given he has failed to score double-digits all season. He does provide the Nets with a defensive presence, something that could at least keep him on the floor down the stretch of the season.

items.headline: Beekman amassed two points (1-4 FG, 0-1 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists and two steals over 22 minutes during Tuesday's 99-97 win over the Rockets.
items.story: Beekman played at least 20 minutes for the second time in his past four games. However, he has also been a DNP-CD in two of the past five games, as the Nets continue to shuffle their rotation on a nightly basis. While he could step into a consistent role at some point, Beekman is likely to remain on the fringe of the rotation, at least for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Beekman finished Monday's 110-96 loss to the Kings with zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and two assists across 12 minutes.
items.story: Beekman was back in the rotation, continuing a recent pattern not dissimilar to his teammates. The Nets are chopping and changing their rotation on a nightly basis, making it hard to know who will be playing and how much they will be playing. Unless we see a change in their mentality, Beekman is likely to remain on the fringes of the rotation until further notice.

items.headline: Beekman finished with one point (1-2 FT) and one assist across four minutes during Wednesday's 130-113 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Beekman moved back into the rotation, logging fewer than five minutes for the fourth time in six games since joining the Nets. Moved as part of the Dennis Schroder deal, Beekman has remained on the fringe of the rotation despite the change of location. At this point, there is no reason to think that his role will increase any time soon.

items.headline: The Warriors traded Beekman to the Nets on Sunday, along with De'Anthony Melton (knee) and three second-round picks, in exchange for Dennis Schroder and a second-round pick.
items.story: Beekman wasn't mentioned in the initial trade reports but will ultimately take Yongxi Cui's (knee) spot on the roster. Beekman has made two NBA appearances during his rookie season, totaling only four minutes. However, there may be more playing time available in Brooklyn, especially if the Nets remain active in the trade market. Beekman (trade pending) won't play in Monday's game against the Cavaliers, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.

items.headline: Allen ended Monday's 124-91 loss to Detroit with 11 points (3-7 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one rebound over 19 minutes.
items.story: Allen finished with an empty 11 points, logging just 19 minutes, coming off a season-high 27 points during a loss to the 76ers. With Coby White returning from a calf injury, there are simply more mouths to feed in the backcourt. Assuming Kon Knueppel's return from a hamstring injury is getting closer, playing time for Allen is going to be even harder to come by. Looking ahead, there is a chance he moves from being a must-roster player to more of a streaming candidate.

items.headline: Allen ended with 27 points (9-12 FG, 7-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block over 30 minutes in Saturday's 109-104 loss to Philadelphia.
items.story: Allen scored only five points in Friday's loss to the Wizards. However, he showed up in a big way Saturday by finishing the night with a new season high in scoring. The 2018 No. 21 overall pick is now averaging 15.4 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.9 assists while shooting a career-best 47.1 percent from deep over 27.3 minutes per contest in his first seven regular-season games with the Hornets.

items.headline: Allen recorded five points (2-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists over 21 minutes during Friday's 95-79 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Allen continued to struggle with his shot, having now failed to exceed 40 percent from the field in four of his past five games. Despite playing a relatively significant role, Allen has averaged just 13.5 points, 2.8 assists and 2.8 three-pointers in 26.9 minutes per game through six appearances. While he is probably worth holding for now, once Charlotte starts to get healthy, he could very well trend towards becoming a three-point streaming option.

items.headline: Allen racked up 15 points (3-8 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 7-7 FT), two rebounds and one assist in 28 minutes during Monday's 110-103 win over the Wizards.
items.story: Allen provided another scoring boost off Charlotte's bench, reaching double figures for the third time in four games to open the season. Although he struggled from the field, the veteran guard was perfect on seven free-throw attempts and connected on two triples. Allen should remain a useful source of points and three-pointers while Coby White (calf) and Kon Knueppel (hamstring) are sidelined.

items.headline: Allen supplied 21 points (6-9 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and four assists across 29 minutes off the bench in Wednesday's 110-103 win over the Nets.
items.story: Allen made an immediate impact as Charlotte's sixth man, leading the team in scoring while connecting on five three-pointers in an extremely efficient shooting display. It's only one game, and he's not expected to play 29 minutes on a regular basis, but he should have a steady workload regardless of whether he starts or comes off the bench, particularly if the Hornets continue to rely on his perimeter shooting. His limited defensive contributions and dependence on three-point efficiency could make his fantasy production somewhat inconsistent, but there's no question this was an excellent start to his Hornets tenure.

items.headline: Allen (knee) isn't listed on the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
items.story: Allen missed three straight preseason games due to a nagging knee issue, but he'll be good to go for Opening Night. Depending on how his knee holds up, Allen could be in line for major usage, as Coby White (calf) and Kon Knueppel (hamstring) will be sidelined for the regular-season opener.

items.headline: Allen (knee) didn't play in Friday's 117-98 preseason loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Allen missed a third consecutive contest due to right knee soreness. If he's unable to play in Wednesday's regular-season opener against Atlanta, Sion James and Royce O'Neale could see increased minutes.

items.headline: Allen (knee) did not play in Wednesday's 114-93 preseason loss to the Celtics.
items.story: Allen missed Sunday's game due to right knee soreness and remained sidelined for Wednesday's defeat. His final chance to suit up during the preseason will come Friday against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: Allen will not play in Sunday's preseason game against the Bucks due to right knee soreness.
items.story: Allen performed well in the Hornets' opening preseason game, posting 13 points in 14 minutes, but he will miss Sunday's contest with a knee injury. Sion James and Royce O'Neale could see extra action with Allen out of the lineup.

items.headline: Allen contributed 13 points (4-6 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist over 14 minutes in Tuesday's 124-90 preseason loss to the Nets.
items.story: Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (calf) won't play during the preseason, and if their injuries linger into the regular season, that could result in major minutes and a starting role for Allen. As a starter in Phoenix last season, Allen averaged 17.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 3.3 triples and 1.4 steals per game on 42/37/84 shooting splits.

items.headline: Allen is starting Tuesday's preseason opener against the Nets.
items.story: Allen is filling in for the injured Kon Knueppel (hamstring) on Tuesday. He's also auditioning for a starting job in the event that Knueppel can't suit up for Opening Night.

items.headline: Allen could open the season as a starter if Kon Knueppel (hamstring) isn't ready for Opening Night.
items.story: Knueppel has already been ruled out for the preseason, and his absence could extend into the regular season. Allen would likely see a sizable boost in streaming appeal if Knueppel isn't available for the start of the season, having averaged 17.6 points, 4.1 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.4 steals per contest in 27 games as a starter for the Suns in 2025-26.

items.headline: The Suns traded Allen, Royce O'Neale and a 2033 first-round pick to the Hornets on Sunday in exchange for Miles Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
items.story: After spending the past three years in Phoenix, Allen will join a retooling Charlotte squad that has now traded away LaMelo Ball and Bridges this offseason. Allen is coming off arguably the best year of his career, averaging 16.5 points, 3.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 28.8 minutes per game across 51 outings (27 starts). However, he shot just 40.3 percent from the field and 34.9 percent from deep, a significant dip from the 2024-25 campaign. He figures to play a significant role off the bench for Charlotte and will likely compete for minutes with Sion James and Tre Mann.

items.headline: Allen ended with 12 points (4-5 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two blocks across 21 minutes during Monday's 131-122 loss to Oklahoma City in Game 4 of the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.
items.story: A hamstring injury might have plagued him during Phoenix's brief playoff run, but there's no question that Allen was a particularly effective nine-category fantasy asset when healthy in 2025-26. Across 51 regular-season contests, the veteran swingman averaged a career-high 16.5 points, 3.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 3.1 three-pointers in 28.8 minutes per game. With a club option for 2027-28, Allen is set to remain with the Suns for at least one more year.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is available for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
items.story: Allen has been upgraded from questionable to available for a fourth straight game, though he didn't see minutes in any of Phoenix's last three contests. The veteran wing isn't guaranteed to see the floor Saturday and may be used only in case of an emergency.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) will go through pregame warmups before a final decision is made on his availability for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder, Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com reports.
items.story: Allen was upgraded from questionable to available ahead of each of Phoenix's last three games, though he didn't see the floor in any of them. He may be used only in an emergency Saturday if he's active.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Saturday's Game 3 of the Western Conference first-round series against the Thunder.
items.story: Allen was upgraded from questionable to available ahead of each of Phoenix's last three games but didn't see the floor in any of them. He may only be used in an emergency if active, though he was a full participant in Friday's practice.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) was a full participant in Friday's practice, per Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic.
items.story: Allen was available only for emergencies in Games 1 and 2 of Phoenix's first-round series against the Thunder due to a hamstring injury. All signs point toward the sharpshooter suiting up for Game 3 on Saturday, but it's unknown if the Suns are ready to get Allen back on the floor.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is available for Wednesday's Game 2 against the Thunder.
items.story: Allen will shed his questionable tag and be available for a third straight game, though he didn't appear in either of the last two. The veteran wing could see increased playing time Wednesday due to Jordan Goodwin (calf) being sidelined.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Game 2 against the Thunder on Wednesday.
items.story: Allen was also listed as questionable ahead of each of Phoenix's last two matchups before being upgraded to available, though he didn't see the floor in either contest. Even if the veteran wing is cleared to play Wednesday, it's not guaranteed he'll see significant minutes.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is available for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.story: Allen missed the Suns' last three games. It's unknown if the veteran wing will see fewer minutes than usual following the layoff, so the door remains open for expanded roles from Ryan Dunn and Royce O'Neale.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is considered a game-time decision for Sunday's Game 1 against the Thunder, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
items.story: Allen has missed the Suns' last three games due to a left hamstring injury. He's coming off a career year, averaging 16.5 points, 3.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds, 3.1 threes and 1.4 steals over 28.8 minutes per game during the regular season. That production would need to be replaced by Haywood Highsmith, Royce O'Neale and Ryan Dunn if Allen is unable to play in Game 1.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's Game 1 against the Thunder.
items.story: Questionable tags have been par for the course for Allen. He was available for Friday's Play-In Tournament game, but he did not leave the bench.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is available for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Warriors.
items.story: Allen missed Phoenix's regular-season finale and Tuesday's Play-In Tournament loss to the Trail Blazers due to a left hamstring injury, though he'll return to action in Friday's win-or-go-home matchup. Over 51 regular-season appearances (27 starts), the veteran wing averaged 16.5 points, 3.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 28.8 minutes per contest.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is questionable for Friday's Play-In Tournament game against the Warriors.
items.story: Allen is in danger of missing a third straight matchup while dealing with hamstring soreness. He'll likely test the injury in shootaround and warmups to see if he can suit up for Friday's clash.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) has been ruled out for Tuesday's Play-In Tournament game against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Allen will miss a second straight outing due to left hamstring soreness. With the veteran wing sidelined, Collin Gillespie, Jordan Goodwin and Ryan Dunn are all candidates to see increased playing time.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) is questionable for Tuesday's Play-In Tournament matchup against the Trail Blazers.
items.story: Allen is the lone Suns player on the injury report ahead of Tuesday's matchup, as he deals with left hamstring soreness. The 30-year-old emerged as a key scoring contributor this season, averaging 16.5 points in 28.8 minutes across 51 regular-season appearances. He has primarily operated off the bench but retained a consistent workload of late, so an absence on his part would likely place more responsibility on Jordan Goodwin against the Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Allen has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder due to left hamstring soreness.
items.story: Allen exited Friday's loss to the Lakers due to the hamstring issue and won't suit up in Sunday's regular-season finale. He will end the 2025-26 regular season with averages of 16.5 points, 3.8 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 28.8 minutes per contest across 51 outings (27 starts). His next chance to play will come in Tuesday's Play-In Tournament matchup against the higher-seeded team between the Clippers and Trail Blazers.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) won't return to Friday's game against the Lakers. He'll finish with eight points (2-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 13 minutes.
items.story: Allen exited to the locker room with 8:22 remaining in the second quarter and will not return during the second half. With Jalen Green (knee), Devin Booker (ankle) and Jordan Goodwin (ankle) also out, Jamaree Bouyea, Amir Coffey and Rasheer Fleming will likely help pick up the slack the rest of the way.

items.headline: Allen exited to the locker room in the second quarter of Friday's game against the Lakers due to an apparent left hamstring injury, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Allen grabbed at his hamstring before heading back to the locker room with 8:22 remaining in the first half. He can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

items.headline: Allen is in the Suns' starting lineup against the Lakers on Friday.
items.story: Allen will make his 27th start of the season Friday, but it'll be his first appearance in Phoenix's lineup since Feb. 5 against the Warriors. Over his last six outings, Allen has averaged 12.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 2.3 threes and 1.2 steals over 23.8 minutes per game. He should operate in an expanded role against the Lakers due to the absences of Devin Booker (ankle), Jalen Green (knee) and Jordan Goodwin (ankle).

items.headline: Allen (quadriceps) isn't listed on the injury report for Friday's game against the Lakers.
items.story: Allen missed Wednesday's win over Dallas due to a right quadriceps contusion, but he's set to return to action Friday. With Jordan Goodwin (ankle) and Devin Booker (ankle) out, Allen will likely see an uptick in playing time against the Lakers.  He has averaged 11.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.2 steals in 24.0 minutes per game over his last five appearances.

items.headline: Allen (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Allen will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a right quadriceps contusion. His next opportunity to play will come Friday against the Lakers. With the veteran wing out, Jordan Goodwin, Ryan Dunn and Rasheer Fleming are candidates to see increased minutes.

items.headline: Allen (quadriceps) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Mavericks.
items.story: Allen has a contusion and may be held out for the second leg of this back-to-back set. If he's held out by the Suns, Jordan Goodwin and Rasheer Fleming could see a bump in minutes on the wings.

items.headline: Allen closed with 13 points (4-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 3-5 FT), two rebounds and one assist across 25 minutes during Thursday's 127-107 loss to the Hornets.
items.story: Allen has played exclusively off the bench since the All-Star break, but he's been extremely consistent, and he retains fantasy value despite the change in role. He has scored in double digits in every one of his 13 appearances since the All-Star break, averaging 17.2 points, 2.8 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.1 steals across 27.2 minutes per game.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is off the injury report for Tuesday's game versus Orlando.
items.story: Allen is returning to action after sitting out Monday's win over Memphis. The sharpshooter has averaged 16.1 points, 4.7 assists, 2.6 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 3.0 three-pointers in 26.1 minutes per tilt in his last seven games.

items.headline: Allen (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies, Amanda Pflugrad of 3TV Phoenix reports.
items.story: Allen will be held out of the front end of this back-to-back set due to left knee injury management. His next chance to play will come in Orlando on Tuesday. With the veteran wing out, Jordan Goodwin, Ryan Dunn and Rasheer Fleming are candidates for increased minutes.

items.headline: Allen (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Monday's game is the front end of a back-to-back set, and Allen is likely to get a maintenance day for one of these. If the Suns hold out the sharpshooter Monday, the team could rely more on Jordan Goodwin with the second unit.

items.headline: Allen registered 19 points (7-16 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals across 21 minutes during Saturday's 134-109 victory over Utah.
items.story: Allen's opportunities increased as the Suns built an insurmountable lead. He spearheaded the bench-clearing effort in the second half and posted the solid total after logging 21 points during the heartbreaking loss to Denver earlier in the week. Allen's recent knee injury didn't appear to be an issue in the game, but he may be on a slight minute restriction Monday night against the Grizzlies.

items.headline: The Jazz have exercised Bailey's $9.98 million rookie-scale team option for the 2027-28 season, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
items.story: The move keeps Bailey under contract with Utah through the 2027-28 campaign as the franchise continues investing in the young forward's development. The fifth overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft remains an important part of the Jazz's long-term plans, and the decision has no immediate impact on his fantasy outlook for the current season.

items.headline: Bailey registered nine points (4-10 FG, 1-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, one assist, three blocks and two steals across 37 minutes during Saturday's 112-90 loss to the Trail Blazers.
items.story: The second-year forward collected his first steals of the season while posting three blocks for the third time in six games to begin the campaign. Bailey's skills are growing quickly, and so far in 2026-27 the fifth overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft is averaging 13.3 points, 7.8 boards, 2.2 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 threes in 31.0 minutes while shooting an impressive 50.0 percent from the floor.

items.headline: Bailey accumulated 19 points (9-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt), six rebounds and one block in 39 minutes during Wednesday's 117-111 overtime loss to the Spurs.
items.story: Bailey was efficient inside the arc, converting eight of his 12 two-point attempts, though his perimeter shooting remained inconsistent. The second-year forward played a team-high 39 minutes, giving him ample opportunities to contribute offensively and on the glass. His substantial workload is encouraging for fantasy purposes, but improved three-point efficiency and more consistent contributions in other categories would strengthen his overall value.

items.headline: Bailey closed Monday's 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies with 17 points (6-10 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 34 minutes.
items.story: Bailey recorded his second straight double-double, logging a season-high 34 minutes in the process. Both Jaren Jackson (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (wrist) left this game early and did not return. Should they miss additional time, Bailey will likely be tasked with doing a lot more on both ends of the floor. In four appearances to begin the season, Bailey has been a top-50 player, averaging 13.0 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.8 three-pointers.

items.headline: Bailey registered 17 points (8-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt), 12 rebounds, four assists and one block in 29 minutes during Sunday's 132-123 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: This was a nice bounce-back game for Bailey following Friday's six-point, 2-for-8 shooting performance, and he set a new career high in rebounds while recording the second double-double of his career. Bailey has shown flashes before, but he's struggled to put it all together consistently to this point in his career. However, he should continue to get plenty of opportunities while Jusuf Nurkic (foot) is sidelined.

items.headline: Bailey is in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Pelicans.
items.story: Bailey was productive coming off the bench in Wednesday's loss to the Grizzlies, posting 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and three blocks in 24 minutes. He's moving to a first-unit role, sending Jaxson Hayes to the bench. In 61 starts in the 2025-26 season, Bailey averaged 15.3 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists per contest.

items.headline: Bailey closed with 12 points (5-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists and three blocks in 24 minutes during Wednesday's 123-103 loss to the Grizzlies.
items.story: Even with Jusuf Nurkic (foot) on the shelf, Bailey wasn't able to beat out Jaxson Hayes at training camp for an Opening Night start. Hayes swatted six shots Wednesday, so he likely extended his lead as a member of the first unit in Nurkic's stead for now.

items.headline: Bailey delivered 12 points (3-3 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, a steal and two blocks across 21 minutes in Friday's 119-116 preseason win over the Suns.
items.story: Bailey delivered an exceptionally efficient scoring performance, making all three of his field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone three-pointer, and he also added defensive contributions with three stocks. Bailey was aggressive driving to the basket, and while he came off the bench in this contest, he's expected to be a starter in the regular season. His two-way impact will be pivotal for a Utah team looking to make noise in the 2026-27 regular season.

items.headline: Bailey will come off the bench in Monday's exhibition against the Spurs, Jazz digital reporter Eric Spyropoulos reports.
items.story: Lauri Markkanen (neck) is back after a one-game stint on the sidelines, so Bailey will return to a reserve role. In his previous game off the bench this preseason, Bailey finished with 10 points, four rebounds, one steal and one block over 16 minutes.

items.headline: Bailey logged 10 points (4-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, three assists and a steal across 27 minutes in Tuesday's 117-106 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: With Lauri Markkanen (neck) and Brice Sensabaugh (hip) sidelined, Bailey earned a spot in the first unit during the Jazz's second preseason game. New acquisitions like Jaren Jackson and Darryn Peterson are expected to log meaningful minutes right away, leaving the former first-round pick in an uncertain spot after starting 61 games for the Jazz during his rookie campaign. Markkanen's struggles to stay on the court made an uptick for Bailey necessary, and his 2026-27 participation hinges on Markkanen becoming a more consistent contributor.

items.headline: Bailey will start in Tuesday's preseason game against the Nuggets.
items.story: Bailey will get the start with Lauri Markkanen (neck) unavailable, and he'll be joined in the first unit by Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Jaren Jackson and Jaxson Hayes. It'll be interesting to see what Bailey's usage rate looks like in the first unit.

items.headline: Bailey finished with 10 points (5-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt), five rebounds, one steal and one block in 20 minutes during Sunday's 109-97 preseason win over Denver.
items.story: Bailey came off the bench behind rookie Darryn Peterson but entered the starting lineup for the second half and finished with a plus-11 rating. The second-year wing should remain firmly in Utah's rotation, and he could see heavy usage with the second unit.

items.headline: Bailey's (back) role is undetermined heading into the 2026-27 campaign.
items.story: The addition of No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson may leave Bailey without a spot in Utah's starting lineup to begin the new year. The Jazz are also getting Keyonte George and Lauri Markkanen back in the lineup after the two stars sat out the final stretch of a losing season in 2025-26. Bailey began to blossom late last year, averaging 18.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.1 blocks per game in 23 regular-season appearances (all starts) after the All-Star break, so he should have a chance to battle with Peterson for an Opening Night starting position.

items.headline: Bailey (back) won't play in Friday's Summer League game against Portland, per Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City.
items.story: The Jazz are giving Bailey Friday night off while he tends to right back spasms. Given the nature of the injury, the 2025 first-rounder should be fully recovered in time for training camp this fall.

items.headline: Bailey (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's Las Vegas Summer League game against the Spurs, per Ben Anderson of KSL News Salt Lake City.
items.story: Bailey is nursing right back spasms in the aftermath of Sunday's Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Clippers. His next chance to play will come Friday against Portland.

items.headline: Bailey exited Sunday's Las Vegas Summer League loss to the Clippers with back spasms and did not return, Sarah Todd of The Deseret News reports.
items.story: Bailey only managed to make it through eight minutes before aggravating his back, and it's already been announced he will miss Monday's meeting with the Bulls. The Jazz will likely be extra cautious with Bailey's back issue during these exhibition games, so for now, he should be considered doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.

items.headline: Bailey (back) is available for Sunday's Summer League game against the Clippers, Chandler Holt of KSL Sports reports.
items.story: Bailey is available to return from a three-game absence due to back spasms. The 19-year-old wing has played in just one game this summer, posting 10 points (4-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, one steal and one block in 20 minutes during the July 4 overtime win over Atlanta.

items.headline: Bailey (back) didn't play in Thursday's 92-88 Summer League loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Bailey missed Utah's last two Salt Lake City Summer League games due to back spasms, and he didn't suit up for the club's Las Vegas Summer League opener. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Clippers.

items.headline: Bailey (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's Salt Lake City Summer League game against the Thunder, Travis Green of ABC4 Utah reports.
items.story: Bailey was held out of Monday's contest due to back spasms and will remain sidelined Tuesday as the Jazz opt to rest some of their top young players. His next chance to play will come Thursday against the Wizards in the Las Vegas Summer League.

items.headline: Bailey (back) won't play in Monday's Salt Lake City Summer League game against the Grizzlies, Sarah Todd of The Deseret News reports.
items.story: Bailey is dealing with back spasms and won't play in the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play will come Tuesday against the Thunder.

items.headline: Bailey finished with 10 points (4-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, one steal and one block in 20 minutes of Sunday's 103-102 Salt Lake City Summer League win over the Hawks.
items.story: This was Bailey's first look alongside Darryn Peterson, and it was immediately clear who the offense flowed through. Bailey is projected to come off the bench in his second season, and it's clear that he has a lot of work to do to move up fantasy draft boards.

items.headline: Bailey will enter his second NBA season playing alongside franchise guard Darryn Peterson, who Utah took with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.
items.story: The pairing gives the Jazz a dynamic young offensive core, with Peterson's playmaking potentially creating easier scoring opportunities for Bailey and Keyonte George. While usage distribution remains uncertain, Bailey still projects as one of Utah's foundational building blocks. After the All-Star break, Bailey averaged 18.3 points, 4.9 boards and 2.0 dimes in 23 regular-season games.

items.headline: Bailey accumulated 15 points (7-21 FG, 1-9 3Pt, 0-2 FT), three rebounds, one assist and one block across 29 minutes during Sunday's 131-107 loss to the Lakers.
items.story: Bailey endured a rough shooting performance in his final game of the 2025-26 season, but the rookie out of Rutgers showed a marked improvement as the campaign went on. He finishes his rookie with averages of 13.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game across 72 appearances, but those figures improve to 18.3 points, 4.9 boards and 2.0 dimes per game in 23 contests after the All-Star break. All things considered, it was a successful season for Bailey, who's expected to be a key player for the Jazz for years to come.

items.headline: Bailey (knee) is available for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
items.story: Bailey took a seat for Tuesday's game against the Pelicans due to a knee issue, but he'll be back on the court Friday. The rookie forward is averaging 16.0 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.2 blocks over his last five matchups.

items.story: Bailey was previously listed as doubtful, so this latest update isn't much of a surprise. His next opportunity to suit up will be Friday versus the Grizzlies. In the meantime, Cody Williams, Brice Sensabaugh and Kyle Filipowski are expected to do most of the heavy lifting on offense.

items.headline: Bailey (knee) is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Pelicans.

With Utah's injury list a mile long, John Konchar, Bez Mbeng and Svi Mykhailiuk are candidates for increased roles.

items.headline: Bailey (knee) is listed as questionable for Tuesday's game against New Orleans.
items.story: Utah's injury report continues to grow, with Bailey now making an appearance because of a bruised right knee. If he can't suit up, John Konchar could work his way back into the starting lineup.

items.headline: Bailey finished Sunday's 146-111 loss to Oklahoma City with 14 points (6-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal across 33 minutes.
items.story: Brice Sensabaugh and Kyle Filipowski led the way for Utah offensively. While Bailey didn't have his best performance, he still found a way to be relevant in fantasy and contributed in the five major categories. The rookie is averaging 20.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game over his last 10 games. He should be one of Utah's go-to offensive weapons in the final week of the regular season.

items.headline: Bailey recorded 22 points (9-17 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 2-3 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one block across 33 minutes during Friday's 140-106 loss to Houston.
items.story: Bailey reached the 20-point mark for the first time since scoring 37 in a loss to the Raptors on March 23. Even though his scoring numbers had been trending a bit downward of late, the rookie out of Rutgers has improved massively compared to his first month in the league, and he's ending the season on a strong note. If you drafted Bailey and trusted him throughout the entire season, you're clearly reaping the benefits of being a patient manager when it matters the most. Bailey has scored at least 15 points in eight of his last 10 appearances.

items.headline: Bailey registered 15 points (7-14 FG, 1-7 3Pt), seven rebounds and one assist across 27 minutes during Friday's 135-129 loss to the Nuggets.
items.story: The rookie out of Rutgers struggled with his three-point shot, but he was nearly automatic with his two-point attempts. Inconsistencies and ups and downs are going to be part of Bailey's game early on, but he has shown flashes of his scoring potential. He's reached the 15-point mark in six games in a row and is now averaging a solid line of 18.9 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.1 steals per game since the All-Star break.

items.headline: Bailey contributed 15 points (7-19 FG, 1-6 3Pt), five rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 133-110 loss to the Wizards.
items.story: Bailey started in the frontcourt alongside Cody Williams with Kyle Filipowski out with an illness. The Jazz have put together some really interesting rotations in recent weeks, but Bailey seems to be a safe fantasy play for the time being.

items.headline: Bailey closed with 37 points (11-21 FG, 7-10 3Pt, 8-8 FT), six rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 35 minutes during Monday's 143-127 loss to the Raptors.
items.story: Bailey continued his strong play on the offensive end of the court, as he set a new career high in scoring and reached the 30-point threshold for the second time in three games. He was particularly dialed in from beyond the arc Monday, which is where he tacked on 21 of his 37 points. Bailey is set for another appealing matchup Wednesday against the Wizards.

items.headline: Bailey ended Saturday's 126-116 loss to Philadelphia with 25 points (7-20 FG, 4-14 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and five blocks over 33 minutes.
items.story: Bailey was coming off posting a career-high 33 points in the win over the Bucks on Thursday, and while he fell short of reaching that mark in this loss, it was the first time in his career that he recorded at least 25 points in back-to-back contests. Bailey endured a slow start to his NBA career but has progressed steadily as the season has advanced. All signs point to him ending the season -- and therefore, the fantasy playoffs -- on a strong note as the Jazz's primary go-to option on offense. Bailey has scored at least 20 points six times since the All-Star break (13 games), compared to only seven during the rest of the season (49 contests).

items.headline: James logged 11 points (4-6 FG, 3-4 3Pt), four rebounds and three assists across 21 minutes during Monday's 124-91 loss to Detroit.
items.story: Although James continues to work with the first unit, he's essentially serving as a nominal starter for the Hornets while they wait for Kon Knueppel's (hamstring) season debut. The 11 points were a season-high figure for the second-year forward, who had previously been unable to score more than six points in any of his first seven appearances.

items.headline: James contributed five points (2-4 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds and three assists across 29 minutes during Monday's 110-103 victory over the Wizards.
items.story: James remained in Charlotte's starting lineup but played a limited offensive role, attempting just four shots. The second-year guard has scored five points or fewer in each of his first four appearances this season, though his playing time has remained relatively steady. His low usage makes him difficult to trust in standard fantasy formats.

items.headline: James will start in Wednesday's game against Brooklyn.
items.story: With Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (ankle) sidelined to begin the year, James will get an opportunity to start versus the Nets. The 23-year-old started 19 times in 2025-26, averaging 5.9 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists over 29.1 minutes per contest in those appearances.

items.headline: James will start in Friday's preseason finale against the Grizzlies.
items.story: This will be James' first start this preseason and he'll be joined in the first unit by Dennis Schroder, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid and Ryan Kalkbrenner. Across 19 starts last season, James averaged 5.9 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.1 triples per contest on 35/33/83 shooting splits.

items.headline: James finished with 11 points (3-4 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and four assists in 20 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 105-90 preseason win over Milwaukee.
items.story: James delivered an efficient performance, connecting on three triples while contributing as a rebounder and facilitator. The young guard made a strong case for additional opportunities in Charlotte's rotation, though the Hornets' backcourt depth could make consistent minutes difficult to secure once the regular season begins.

items.headline: James could see more playing time to begin the season if Kon Knueppel (hamstring) isn't ready for Opening Night.
items.story: If Knueppel is out for the start of the season, the Hornets have James, Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale as the most likely candidates to enter the first unit. James was more of a defensive stopper for Charlotte in his rookie campaign, having averaged just 5.9 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 29.0 minutes per contest across 19 games as a starter in 2025-26.

items.headline: James will have added competition for playing time after the Hornets added Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and Dorian Finney-Smith this offseason.
items.story: James saw a meaningful role in his rookie season, averaging 5.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.6 steals across 22.5 minutes per tilt in 82 regular-season games (19 starts). The Hornets took a significant step forward in 2025-26 and will look to continue building momentum behind Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller (shoulder). The club added several veteran swingmen, and while not all of them are guaranteed a steady role, they could challenge James for minutes.

items.headline: James amassed six points (2-5 FG, 2-5 3Pt), two rebounds and two assists across 18 minutes during Friday's 121-90 Play-In Game loss to the Magic.
items.story: The rookie second-rounder was a key contributor for the Hornets during the first half of the 2025-26 regular season, and he started 11 of Charlotte's 13 games from Oct. 30 to Nov. 23. He saw his playing time dip slightly in 2026, and in the 27 regular-season games since the All-Star break (one start), James averaged 4.9 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 19.4 minutes per contest. He figures to serve in a bench role for the 2026-27 season unless a path to more playing time opens up for the Duke product.

items.headline: James ended with 13 points (4-9 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, three assists and one steal in 23 minutes during Friday's 129-108 win over the Pacers.
items.story: James caught fire from downtown during Friday's comfortable victory and managed to score in double figures for just the second time since March 10 with the help of four made treys. He also led the Charlotte bench in scoring. James has seen more consistent usage lately after averaging 17.9 minutes through his first 13 outings of March, as he's logged 22.5 minutes per game over his last four appearances.

items.headline: James closed Thursday's 114-103 win over New York with zero points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal across 14 minutes.
items.story: James continues to be used sparingly by the Hornets at the edge of the rotation. Over his last six games, he's averaging 18.5 minutes per contest with 4.0 points, 2.7 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.0 three-pointers.

items.headline: James recorded zero points (0-1 FG, 0-1 3Pt), three rebounds and one assist in 14 minutes during Saturday's 115-102 loss to the Spurs.
items.story: James continues to play a modest role off the bench, typically resulting in limited production. Despite being a consistent part of the rotation, it's fair to say that James' impact on the court does not translate well when it comes to fantasy value. In 13 games over the past month, he has averaged just 4.5 points and 3.7 rebounds in 19.5 minutes per game.

items.headline: James contributed 11 points (2-3 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and one block over 24 minutes during Tuesday's 103-101 win over the Trail Blazers.
items.story: James put together a solid line Tuesday as the Hornets improved to 33-33 on the season. The rookie had scored a combined 12 points in his previous three games, so he's got some work to do to get back onto the fantasy radar.

items.headline: James accumulated 13 points (5-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt), eight rebounds, two steals and one assist in 24 minutes during Tuesday's 117-90 win over the Mavericks.
items.story: With Coby White (calf) unavailable for the front end of this back-to-back set, James saw a bump in minutes and led the second unit in scoring. James will likely see fewer minutes when White returns to action, as the former has yet to log more than 20 minutes when White is available.

items.headline: James will come off the bench for Thursday's game in Orlando.
